input: Terrace Lounge appears to want to have a great cocktail venue, but they fall short.  One bartender didn't even know there was a new cocktail menu.  The cocktail was weak and watery, and the liquors they have here and throughout Peppermill are the most unfortunate corporate types.  The service is also very spotty.  It confounded me how four bartenders could not seem to handle about 45 customers.  They didn't have any bar areas, so they all floated around the circle, but then they'd stop, often just short of me and go to the waitress stations to fill their orders.  You can't really build up any rapport with four bartenders floating around trying to serve everyone.  I also hated the people there.  Sorry, but many were your run-of-the-mill casino gamblers.  Why don't you just sit at a machine and play?  You didn't come here for the drinks or to smooze with the bartenders, so seriously, go sit at a machine.  One just sat next to me and lite up a cancer stick and the smoke just blew in my face.  Look, if I walk into a bar and sit next to someone, it's their turf.  They can smoke, fart, vomit on themselves, if I don't like it I can leave.  But if I'm there, it's my turf.  Don't come sit next to me and smoke, fart, or vomit all over yourself.  Or at least be frickin thoughtful and if you see your smoke wafting in my face, put your cancer stick and tray on the other side of the bar so it wafts in your face.  Oh, you don't like smoke in your face???  Me neither moron.  Your life revovles around throwing away your pension money in a mindless electronic game of cards and killing yourself with carcinogens and toxins, well go kill yourself in private, seriously.  You don't see me walking up to a bar and slitting my wrists and burning my money.  It's gross.  I probably just realized this, but I really enjoy Cin Cin not only because they have the best cocktails in town, but they have no machines at the bar.  Peppermill, if you want to create a cool cocktail bar, ditch the machines, train your staff, or hire bartenders with better service skills, and buy some independent liquors.
Revise this with your best effort:
Terrace Lounge's potential as a great cocktail venue falls short due to certain shortcomings. For instance, one of the bartenders seemed unaware of the newly introduced cocktail menu. Moreover, the cocktails served were weak and lacking in flavor, while the liquor selection throughout Peppermill, including Terrace Lounge, seemed limited to uninspiring corporate options. The service, unfortunately, was inconsistent, leaving me perplexed as to how four bartenders struggled to handle a moderate crowd of around 45 customers. The absence of designated bar areas meant the bartenders roamed around the circular space, frequently pausing just short of serving me to attend to orders at the waitress stations. This prevented any chance of building rapport with the staff, as they were constantly preoccupied with serving everyone.

Furthermore, the clientele at Terrace Lounge left much to be desired. Many patrons resembled typical casino gamblers with no apparent interest in the drinks or engaging with the bartenders. It would be more fitting for them to occupy a slot machine and play rather than taking up space in the bar. One individual even sat beside me, lighting up a cigarette and subjecting me to secondhand smoke. In my understanding, when entering a bar and sitting next to someone, it is their territory. They are permitted to smoke, pass gas, or even vomit on themselves, and I have the choice of leaving if I find it unpleasant. However, when I occupy a space, it becomes my domain. Therefore, it is inconsiderate for someone to sit next to me and expose me to their smoke, flatulence, or vomit. At the very least, they should demonstrate some thoughtfulness by relocating their cigarette and ashtray to the other side of the bar if they notice the smoke drifting towards me. I understand they may not appreciate smoke in their own face, just as I don't. 

The individuals who revolve their lives around squandering their pension money with mindless electronic card games and subjecting themselves to carcinogens and toxins should do so in private. It is indeed disgusting. It has only recently occurred to me that I genuinely enjoy Cin Cin, not only for their exceptional cocktails but also because they prohibit machines at their bar. If Peppermill desires to establish a trendy cocktail bar, I recommend eliminating the presence of machines, providing thorough training to staff, or hiring bartenders with better service skills, and investing in a diverse and independent selection of liquors.

input:
Thank you for a lovely morning!  I was in NJ early and decided to stop in for a delicious diner breakfast.  I got a taylor ham, egg, and cheese and a short stack of blueberry pancakes (I simply couldn't decide between sweet or savory, plus leftovers are never a bad thing).  

The egg sandwich was fantastic.  I was nervous when they said they didn't have kaiser rolls so I went with a hamburger roll.  It was an excellent decision.  The roll was excellent - not just an average cheap hamburger roll.  They layered the cheese on the sandwich, which to me is a must for a true egg sandwich.  It was served with home fries, which were sauteed with large slices of peppers and onions.  I'm not the biggest breakfast potatoes fan, but these were great and I appreciated that they didn't clearly just scoop some food from a huge pile of pre-cooked home fries.

The pancakes were great and fluffy.  My one gripe was their use of smuckers pre-packaged syrup.  I realize that if they put syrup in a container, it probably wouldn't be real maple syrup, but I sort of wish I didn't know that they were giving me sub-par syrup.

The server was friendly and very attentive.  The coffee refills were constant, and the coffee was actually good (so many diners fail at coffee).  Bonus points for the server agreeing not to judge my decision to get two breakfasts.

All around, I loved this place and hope to go back soon.  Long live the Jersey diners!
Revise this with your best effort:
I want to express my appreciation for the wonderful morning I had! Having arrived early in NJ, I spontaneously decided to indulge in a delectable breakfast at a local diner. After much contemplation, I settled on ordering a taylor ham, egg, and cheese sandwich along with a short stack of luscious blueberry pancakes, unable to resist the temptation of both sweet and savory options. Plus, having leftovers is always a welcome bonus.

The egg sandwich surpassed my expectations. Initially worried when I discovered they were out of kaiser rolls, I took a chance and opted for a hamburger roll instead. This turned out to be an excellent decision as the roll itself was far from ordinary; it had a delightful taste and a quality that surpassed an average, low-cost hamburger roll. The layering of cheese on the sandwich, in my opinion, is an essential component of a genuine egg sandwich. Accompanied by sautéed home fries generously mixed with large slices of peppers and onions, even though breakfast potatoes may not be my go-to, these were exceptional. I appreciated the effort they put into them instead of just scooping from a mass of pre-cooked home fries.

Moving on to the pancakes, they were simply delightful, fluffy, and satisfying. My only slight complaint was their choice of using pre-packaged syrup from Smuckers. While I understand that if they were to provide syrup in a container, it may not be genuine maple syrup, a part of me wishes I hadn't known they were serving me a somewhat subpar syrup.

In terms of service, I couldn't have been more pleased. The server was friendly and attentive, making sure my coffee cup was consistently replenished. Impressively, the coffee itself was actually good, which isn't always the case at many diners. Extra credit goes to the server for not criticizing or questioning my decision to order two breakfasts.

All in all, I absolutely adored this place and am already looking forward to visiting again soon. Here's to the enduring legacy of Jersey diners!

input:
The new Han Dynasty took over the spot where the old Mid-Atlantic restaurant (with the unchanging menu) was. I like the Han Dynasty here a lot more than the one in Olde City even if I give both 4*. Maybe I'm biased, because I love the service here. They've always been very nice, and came over to check in with me and just make some small conversation when they heard I had a peanut allergy (even though they had no peanuts in any of the dishes I ordered; I think it was Han's sister?). I've been to this Han Dynasty more times in a month than the number of times I've been to the other.

Note though, that the different branches have different specialties. I heard the dan dan mian in Olde City is the best, but the one in UC isn't so good (I wouldn't know since it has peanuts). Overall, I think it;s okay food wise, still not spicy enough as with the other branch. But I like the layout and atmosphere a lot more.

Next, if you go during lunch, you can ask for lunch portions, that are smaller than the dinner portions, and half the menu price! So it's a great lunch place too, alone, or in a group of 2 or 3.
Revise this with your best effort:
The new Han Dynasty has taken over the location previously occupied by the old Mid-Atlantic restaurant, renowned for its unchanging menu. Personally, I find that I prefer this particular Han Dynasty branch over the one in Olde City, even though I would still rate both establishments with four stars. Perhaps I am biased because of the exceptional service provided here. The staff has always been incredibly friendly, going the extra mile to check in with me and engage in small conversations upon learning about my peanut allergy (despite none of the dishes I ordered containing peanuts; I believe it was Han's sister who took care of me). In fact, I have frequented this Han Dynasty branch more times in a month than I have ever visited the other one.

It is important to note, however, that each branch has its own specialties. I have heard that the dan dan mian in Olde City is simply exceptional, although I cannot personally vouch for it since it includes peanuts. Overall, I find the food at this branch to be satisfactory, but lacking the desired level of spiciness found in the other location. Nevertheless, I greatly appreciate the layout and atmosphere, which significantly adds to the overall dining experience.

Furthermore, if you visit during lunch hours, you have the option of requesting lunch portions that are smaller in size compared to the dinner portions, and they come at half the price! This makes the Han Dynasty an excellent choice for a satisfying lunch, whether you prefer to dine alone or in a group of two or three.

input:
We went to Carisma Restaurante again tonight. It has become our "go to" spot. The food is excellent and the service was great. The owner Jose is very friendly and tries to visit every table to make sure everyone is satisfied.  Tonight we had 2 Paellas, salmon and a filet mignon. Everything was made to order, cooked to perfection and came out hot.  

The family also opened a cafe in front of the restaurant. Jose gave us a tour and introduced us to his daughter that runs the cafe. The baked goods and coffees at the cafe are just as good as the meals at Carisma. Good, fresh food prepared and served by nice people. Try Carisma, it's so much more than just the normal tacos and burritos. You wont be disappointed!
Revise this with your best effort:
We once again dined at Carisma Restaurante this evening, solidifying it as our utmost favorite spot. The culinary creations at this establishment truly surpass expectations, and the service we received was impeccable. The amiable owner, Jose, went above and beyond to ensure every guest's satisfaction, making it a point to personally visit each table. 

Choosing from an array of delectable options, we indulged in two perfectly executed Paellas, alongside a salmon dish and a succulent filet mignon. Each plate was meticulously crafted to order, exemplifying culinary expertise, and arrived at our table piping hot.

To our delight, we discovered that the family behind Carisma had recently expanded their offerings by opening a charming café adjacent to the restaurant. Led by Jose's daughter, the café amazed us with their heavenly baked goods and exceptional coffees, mirroring the high standards set by Carisma. 

At Carisma, not only can you relish in the pleasure of devouring good, fresh food, but you are also attended to by genuinely kind-hearted individuals. It is a culinary experience that transcends the ordinary realm of mere tacos and burritos. Trust us when we say, a visit to Carisma will leave you far from disappointed.

input: This is a small hole in the wall in the African section of Woodland Avenue.  Though it might not look like much, there is some good food coming out of its kitchen representing Senegal and West Africa.  I enjoyed the national dish of Senegal - Thiboudienne - although note that here they do a version without the usual tomato sauce.  I also took home a Jollof Rice which is often called the mother dish of Jambalaya.  There are a few hightop tables inside for dining or you can order the food to-go.  Either way, service is friendly.
Revise this with your best effort:
Located in the African section of Woodland Avenue, this hidden gem may appear unassuming, but don't let its modest facade deceive you. Behind its walls, a culinary journey awaits, showcasing the flavors of Senegal and West Africa. The kitchen churns out delectable dishes that exemplify the essence of these vibrant cultures.

One dish that particularly captivated my palate was the Thiboudienne, Senegal's national treasure. A slight departure from the traditional rendition, this rendition omits the customary tomato sauce, yet still manages to captivate with its rich and robust flavors. Additionally, I couldn't resist bringing home a serving of Jollof Rice, often hailed as the mother dish of Jambalaya. Each bite transported me to a realm of authentic African cuisine, leaving a lasting impression.

The cozy interior of this establishment offers a handful of hightop tables, inviting patrons to experience their gastronomic delights firsthand. Alternatively, the option to conveniently order the food to-go is also available. Regardless of your choice, expect a warm and amiable service that enhances the overall dining experience.

input: Had a falafel wrap here a few years ago. Not bad, so tried it again today. No flavor, except extreme saltiness! The falafels & pita = no flavor. I was hoping the tzatziki sauce would pull it all together, nope! It had no flavor either. It wasn't like the sauce you'd imagine, but more like a thin tasteless glue. Only good part about the wrap were the fresh diced cucumber & tomato, too bad that was underneath the icky white sauce that doesn't even deserve to be called tzatziki : (
Revise this with your best effort: I had a falafel wrap at this place a few years ago, and it was decent, so I decided to give it another try today. Unfortunately, I was quite disappointed as there was absolutely no flavor, except for an overpowering saltiness. Both the falafels and pita lacked any taste. I had high hopes that the tzatziki sauce would bring everything together, but it turned out to be a major letdown. It lacked any flavor, resembling more of a thin and tasteless glue than the sauce you would expect. The only redeeming aspect of the wrap was the fresh diced cucumber and tomato, but it was a shame that they were covered by the disappointing white sauce that hardly deserves to be called tzatziki :(

input:
Our group of 6 decided to try something different.  So,  we gave this place a shot.   Very happy with our decision. 

The wife and I shared the special,  which was a massive amount of food for the two of us.   It was a great sampling of all their food options. 

The chicken, steak and rice/beans were pretty amazing.  I could do without the egg,  but it was easy enough to push over to the side.   I'm not a fan of Yuca, but this wasn't bad.   The plantains were delicious.   I didn't try the salad... Just wasn't in the mood for it. 

All in all,  the place is a must visit if you are up for trying something new.
Revise this with your best effort:
Our group of six decided to step outside our comfort zone and give this place a chance. Needless to say, we were thoroughly satisfied with our decision. 

My wife and I opted to share the special, and boy, were we in for a treat! The generous portion size could have easily fed a small army. It allowed us to sample a wide array of their delectable offerings.

The chicken, steak, and rice/beans combination truly surpassed our expectations. The harmonious blend of flavors left us craving for more. Although I personally could have done without the egg, it was a minor issue as I simply pushed it to the side. As someone who isn't particularly fond of Yuca, I was pleasantly surprised that it wasn't as bad as I had anticipated. However, the undisputed star of the dish was the mouthwatering plantains. I regrettably skipped the salad, as it just didn't pique my interest at the time.

In conclusion, I highly recommend this gem of a place if you're adventurous and willing to try something new. It's a culinary experience that shouldn't be missed.

input: Out lunch today was pulled pork, smokehouse bowl, and delicious sides of sweet potato casserole and red beans and rice.   Red beans and rice was spicy but good. Sweet potato casserole yummy and meat was smoky juicy and plentiful. Definitely a must.

Meanwhile, the sweet potato casserole delighted our palates with its luscious flavor and perfect balance of sweetness. The meat itself was a true delight, boastfully smoky, juicy, and generously portioned. Without a doubt, this culinary experience is an absolute must-try for any food enthusiast.

Revise this with your best effort: Incredible detailing service! My car was in an appalling state, ridiculously dirty and neglected for months. However, I opted for the outstanding executive detailing package and the transformation is simply astounding.

input: Tried the pulled pork, green beans, Mac n cheese and cornbread. It was all pretty mediocre barbecue. Not bad, not great. The pork was a little overdone/dry, but had a nice smoky flavor. The original bbq sauce is pretty sweet/syrupy. Ill probably go back, but I wouldn't if there was a better option as close to my house.
Revise this with your best effort: I sampled the pulled pork, green beans, Mac n cheese, and cornbread, and found the overall barbecue experience to be decent but not exceptional. The pulled pork, although slightly overdone and dry, did offer a pleasant smoky undertone. The original BBQ sauce, on the other hand, leaned towards the sweeter side, almost syrupy in nature. While I would consider revisiting this establishment, the decision would ultimately hinge on the availability of a superior option in close proximity to my residence.

input: Husband and I made a mistake and came here on a Lenten Friday. The wait was forever. But since we were already there, might as well suck it up and see what's it all about. We ordered the blackened alligator and oysters for appetizers, the alligator came out within 15 minutes, and it was alright. A bit too greasy. Then another 15 minutes later, our raw oysters came out, I wanted mine char grilled but the waitress didn't mention they don't have char grilled oysters and still took my order, so I thought I was waiting for mine to be cooked the entire time. When she brought out the two half-dozen raw oyster trays, that's when she told me they only have raw oysters there. SMH. I have sensitive stomach so I only had 3 then gave the rest to my husband. Regardless, the oysters were really fresh. We waited for at least another 20 minutes later for our entrees to come out. At this point, I was really hungry and had hoped we were at home eating ramen noodles instead. My husband had the roast beef po-boy, and I had the tuna and shrimp kabob. My husband told me his roast beef was really salty and while ironically, my kabob was very bland. The kabob came with exactly 3 pieces of cubed tuna, 2 medium size shrimp with plenty of bell peppers and onions in between, and baby shrimp creole with rice. For the ok price, I shouldn't complain too much about this place. Didn't try their seafood boil, but it looked like that would have been a better choice.
Revise this with your best effort:
My husband and I made a regretful decision by coming here on a Lenten Friday. The wait seemed never-ending. However, since we were already there, we decided to endure it and see what all the fuss was about. As appetizers, we ordered the blackened alligator and oysters. The alligator arrived within 15 minutes, but it was just alright and a tad too greasy. After another 15 minutes, our raw oysters arrived. I had requested mine to be char-grilled, unaware that they didn't offer that option. The waitress took my order without mentioning this, leaving me waiting for my oysters to be cooked. It was only when she brought out the trays of raw oysters that she informed me they only served them raw. SMH. Due to my sensitive stomach, I could only handle three oysters and gave the rest to my husband. Nevertheless, the oysters were undeniably fresh.

We endured another 20 minutes before our entrees finally made their appearance. By this point, I was famished and yearning for a comforting bowl of ramen noodles at home. My husband opted for the roast beef po-boy, which he found overly salty. Ironically, my tuna and shrimp kabob lacked flavor. It consisted of a mere three pieces of cubed tuna, two medium-sized shrimp accompanied by an array of bell peppers and onions, and a side of baby shrimp creole with rice. Considering the fair price, I suppose I shouldn't complain excessively about this establishment. Unfortunately, we didn't have the chance to try their seafood boil, although it appeared to be a better choice.

input:
im going to have to give this place one star for its horrible customer service:

i called in to ask about the 50% off for tulane students they were advertising, the woman assured me if i came with an id it would be half off and made an appointment for me, only once i got there did they tell me it's only on certain days, "it says it right on the sign," i was perturbed by the inconvenience and said so you're not going to honor it even though you just made an appointment with me and told me it would be 50% off, they said no flat out at first even though the error was blatantly on their side, after my nagging, she eventually called john jay himself and he told the woman that he would not honor what i was told even though i had been inconvenienced by someone in HIS staff because it might cause a 'domino effect,' i said how will there be a domino effect unless you continue to give people incorrect information, there will be no other 'dominoes' as long as you remember what day it is from now on... they began to treat me somewhat patronizingly as i explained that usually businesses make concessions when they are the one at fault, that the customer is supposed to always be right, yadda yadda yadda, i left pretty upset and with ~45 minutes of my life having been wasted - empty handed but for a lame excuse from someone who owns at least 3 businesses over 10 dollars...

i have not received a haircut from them so if you're one of those people who ONLY cares about the product and you think you'll get a good cut go right on ahead, but if you're like me (principled) and you don't like handing profits to people who care nothing about their customers this is a good place to skip next time you need a cut
Revise this with your best effort: I have to give this place a one-star rating due to its extremely poor customer service. When I called in to inquire about their advertised 50% discount for Tulane students, a woman assured me that if I brought my ID, I would receive half off and even scheduled an appointment for me. However, upon arriving at the salon, I was informed that the discount only applied on certain days, which was clearly stated on their sign. I was frustrated by the inconvenience and expressed my disappointment, questioning why they wouldn't honor the agreement they made with me. Initially, they flat out refused, despite the fact that the mistake was clearly on their end. After persistently voicing my dissatisfaction, the woman finally contacted the owner, John Jay, who refused to honor what I had been promised, claiming it might cause a "domino effect." I challenged this statement, questioning how there could be a domino effect if they simply provided correct information going forward. Their attitude became condescending as I explained that it's common for businesses to make concessions when they are in the wrong and that the customer should always be valued. Ultimately, I left the salon feeling upset and having wasted around 45 minutes of my time, without receiving any service except for a weak excuse from a business owner who owns multiple establishments over a mere $10. Since I didn't actually experience their haircut services, if you solely prioritize the quality of the cut, you may still consider this place. However, if you value principles, like myself, and prefer not to support businesses that disregard their customers' satisfaction, I recommend skipping this place the next time you need a haircut.

input: Awesome food, great place to split a bunch of delicious spicy, ultra flavorful dishes with a large group. It's the Chinese restaurant a lot of people know about for good reason - I haven't had a single bad dish here, and it's always a crowd-pleaser.
Revise this with your best effort: This Chinese restaurant is renowned for its incredible food and is the perfect spot to share a wide array of delectable, spicy, and intensely flavorful dishes with a large group. It has earned its reputation for all the right reasons – every dish I have tried here has been outstanding, and it never fails to satisfy everyone's taste buds.

input:
My friend and I visited Tampa for a concert, and about ten minutes away from the Atlanta airport he realized that he had purchased tickets for the wrong day. We had already made hotel reservations and bought the concert tickets, so he just had to pay same-day price for airfare: all in all about $800 more. "It was totally worth it," he later told me, "Because I got to have the best sandwich of my entire life."

All because we randomly picked the Bricks of Ybor from Yelp. I can't vouch for the peanut butter or meatless menu, but the meat sandwiches that we bought were absolutely phenomenal. I had the pulled pork, which was flavored with ponzu and served on Hawaiian sweet bread. It was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. We spent a few hours hanging out and drinking, during which time Brian, the owner, came out and talked to us, comped us a drink, let us try new appetizers he was developing (all for free) and generally made us feel really welcome. 

I kept my eyes open to the kind of crowd that came in and out of the restaurant. It seemed to draw everything from hipsters to geriatrics and strait-laced families with young kids. I think it speaks to both the diversity of the menu and the pleasant environment. We went back for drinks before and after the concert. It got very crowded but we still received excellent food, drinks and service. I give this restaurant my strongest recommendation, and it's the first place I'm going when I next visit Tampa.
Revise this with your best effort:
During our visit to Tampa for a concert, my friend and I encountered an unexpected twist. Just ten minutes away from the Atlanta airport, my friend realized that he had mistakenly purchased tickets for the wrong day. Despite the setback, we were determined to make the most of our trip. We had already arranged hotel accommodations and bought concert tickets, so he reluctantly paid the same-day price for airfare, amounting to an extra $800. "It was completely worth it," he later confided in me, "Because I had the most incredible sandwich of my entire life."

This stroke of luck happened solely because we randomly stumbled upon the Bricks of Ybor through Yelp. While I cannot personally vouch for their peanut butter or meatless options, the meat sandwiches we feasted on were nothing short of extraordinary. Personally, I opted for the pulled pork, tantalizingly infused with ponzu and nestled within a delectable Hawaiian sweet bread. It easily ranks among the most memorable meals I've had in quite some time. Immersed in the atmosphere for a few hours, we indulged in drinks and delightful conversation, and to our surprise, the owner, Brian, joined us, treating us to a complimentary drink and samples of his latest appetizers – demonstrating his genuine warmth and hospitality.

Throughout our time there, I observed a diverse crowd frequenting the establishment, ranging from trendy hipsters to wise geriatrics and even traditional families with young children. This remarkable amalgamation is a testament not only to the menu's versatility but also to the overall welcoming ambiance. Prior to and after the concert, we returned to the Bricks of Ybor for more drinks, despite the bustling crowds. To our delight, we consistently received outstanding cuisine, beverages, and attentive service. With utmost conviction, I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant, as it will undoubtedly be my first stop on my next visit to Tampa.

input: So worth the wait! The crepes are amazing! I also loved the grits, which is rare. Tried my hubby's pancakes....awesome!
Revise this with your best effort: Absolutely worth the anticipation! The crepes here truly exceeded my expectations and left me in awe! Additionally, I was pleasantly surprised by how much I enjoyed the grits, a rarity for me. I couldn't resist sampling my beloved spouse's pancakes, and they were absolutely fantastic!

input: My sister-in-law and I visited this restaurant on 8/28/15 mid afternoon.  We were seated after requested 3 times that the hostess speak a little louder because we couldn't even hear her with the background music.  We were seated in a booth with a never ending Larry King vitamin commercial on the TV - really?  Our waitress introduced herself and a new trainee and then we never saw her again.  Two other wait staff seemed to be sharing our table, but no idea who was responsible for our table.  We got our drinks and ordered, but food took forever considering there was not more than 15-20 filled tables in the entire restaurant.  Burgers were not bad - I ordered the blue cheese burger and it would have been better with less blue cheese, way too much!  Fries and onion sticks were very good.  But no one came to see if we were satisfied, needing anything, etc and took two requests and waiting to get a carry out box.  There was a family seated across the aisle from us when we arrived and we assumed they had finished their meal and were "hanging out".  Only after we received our food did we understand they had already ordered and still did not have their food!  I doubt I will return to this restaurant in the future.
Revise this with your best effort:
On 8/28/15, my sister-in-law and I decided to visit this restaurant in the mid-afternoon. However, we encountered some issues right from the beginning. We had to request multiple times for the hostess to speak louder as we couldn't hear her over the background music. Finally, we were seated in a booth with a never-ending Larry King vitamin commercial playing on the TV. It was quite unexpected and distracting.

Our waitress introduced herself along with a new trainee, but unfortunately, we hardly saw her for the rest of our visit. Throughout our time there, we noticed that two other wait staff members seemed to be attending to our table, but it was unclear who was actually responsible for serving us. This lack of clarity in service was disappointing.

Although we eventually received our drinks and placed our orders, we found that the food took an unusually long time to arrive. Surprisingly, the restaurant was not crowded, with only 15-20 tables occupied. Nonetheless, the delay in serving the food didn't leave a good impression.

When our burgers finally arrived, we found them to be decent, although I had ordered a blue cheese burger which had an excessive amount of blue cheese. It would have been much better with a lesser quantity. On a positive note, the fries and onion sticks were delicious.

However, what truly disappointed us was the lack of attentive service. No one bothered to check if we were satisfied or needed anything throughout our meal. We had to make multiple requests just to get a carry-out box, indicating a lack of attention from the staff.

Furthermore, we noticed a family seated across the aisle from us who had arrived before us and still hadn't received their food. It was quite concerning to witness such a delay, and it gave us little confidence in the restaurant's efficiency.

Given these experiences, it is safe to say that I do not anticipate returning to this restaurant in the future.

input:
In short, the food was decently good, but completely overpriced.  The guacamole and my Mojito were probably the highlight of the meal. I had the peach pork medallions, which were nicely cooked, but lacked flavor. I tried the corn cakes with Barbacoa and that was pretty good.  

The atmosphere was inviting with a hip feel if that's what you're looking for.  What was really annoying was the parking situation. For a place with price points such as these and limited parking spaces, a valet service should be provided either at a cost or complimentary.  Don't even try and park in the back of the building, it's tight and dangerous even getting there and back.  I ended up parking three blocks away and broke a sweat walking in the dead of summer to the front entrance.
Revise this with your best effort:
In summary, the food at this restaurant was decently good, albeit overly expensive. The guacamole and Mojito stood out as the highlights of the meal. While the peach pork medallions were cooked well, they lacked flavor. On the other hand, the corn cakes with Barbacoa were quite enjoyable.

The inviting atmosphere of the restaurant exuded a trendy vibe, perfect for those seeking such an ambiance. However, the parking situation was highly inconvenient. Considering the high prices and limited parking spaces, it would be beneficial if the establishment offered either a valet service, at a cost or complimentary. Attempting to park at the back of the building proved to be challenging and hazardous. In my case, I had to park three blocks away and endured a sweaty walk in the scorching summer heat just to reach the front entrance.

input: Had dinner Saturday night for the first time at rusty pelican. Called ahead and made a reservation and requested a table next to the window overlooking the water. Hostess went to seat us away from the window, when we questioned her she huffed off and left us staying in the middle of the dining room!! She did return and sat us by the window. The rest of the evening was great, drinks, food and wait staff was excellent. Liz was our server and went above and beyond. Still have to say the hostess was very disappointing!
Revise this with your best effort: On Saturday night, I had the opportunity to dine at the Rusty Pelican for the first time. Prior to my visit, I had made a reservation and specifically requested a table by the window, offering a picturesque view of the water. However, upon arrival, the hostess attempted to seat us away from the window, disregarding our request. When we politely questioned her decision, she responded with an unprofessional attitude and left us standing awkwardly in the middle of the dining room. Fortunately, she eventually returned and assigned us a table by the window, allowing us to fully enjoy the rest of the evening. The evening was otherwise exceptional, with great drinks, delicious food, and an attentive wait staff. Our server, Liz, truly impressed us with her exceptional service, going above and beyond to ensure our satisfaction. Despite a disappointing experience with the hostess, our overall dining experience at the Rusty Pelican was highly enjoyable.

input:
This was a tough one!   On the merits of the wine, fairly average... I understand that the winery has more than one lable and other label is their premium wines.  I look forward to when that is available (I went two weeks ago so maybe it already is)     Location..   what's not to like?  On the pier!  A wonderful outdoor patio,  couldn't have a nicer setting to enjoy your tasting....   The staff were super, super nice,  I would give them an A+!  

So why only three stars?  It is because of the wine club!  Very expensive for the quality of the wines and stingy as HELL with the benefits to the members..   Most wine clubs will give you a free tasting every time you come in (after all, we are your best customers... we are the ones who buy your wine time and time again).  Some wineries will give their members a complimentary glass in leau of a tasting (Carr).   Most wineries allow you to bring guests which is how you get new wine club members.   This system works folks!  The way this wine club works is that you are given a very limited number of passes per quarter, five as I recall.   If I come with my wife once a month we wouldn't even be covered... let alone if we bring a guest!   

So go to this winery if you want to enjoy a tasting in one of the most beautiful settings on earth.   But avoid the wine club!  For that you can pretty much go to any of the other wine tasting rooms on the Urban wine trail.
Revise this with your best effort:
This was a challenging experience! In terms of the wine itself, it was quite average. I understand that the winery offers different labels, with their premium wines being highly anticipated. I am looking forward to trying them when they become available (as I visited two weeks ago, they might already be). 

As for the location, what's not to love? Situated on the pier, it provides a wonderful outdoor patio where you can enjoy your tasting in a picturesque setting. The staff were incredibly friendly and deserve an A+ rating!

However, despite these positive aspects, I can only give this place three stars due to the wine club. It is excessively expensive given the quality of the wines, and they are extremely stingy with member benefits. Most other wine clubs offer a complimentary tasting each visit as a token of appreciation to their loyal customers. Some wineries even offer a complimentary glass instead of a tasting (like Carr). Additionally, many wineries allow members to bring guests, which helps attract new wine club members. This system proves to be effective. 

Unfortunately, this winery's wine club only provides a very limited number of passes per quarter, if my memory serves me right, it's five. This is far from sufficient if I were to visit with my wife once a month, let alone if we were to bring a guest along. 

So, if you want to relish a tasting experience in one of the most breathtaking settings on earth, I highly recommend this winery. However, if you're considering joining the wine club, I suggest exploring the other wine tasting rooms on the Urban wine trail instead.

input:
I got a cheap haircut in NY for next to nothing and what do you know. it looks like some crazy chimp chewed up my hair and spat  it back on my raw scalp.

Since I'm going for job interviews, I needed to look better and went to Domenick's. The guys were great, Robert cut my hair and did a clean job. Bill came out to $35. I'd give it a 4, but it was a little pricy for my taste, but I look human again. Don't know what you guys in Philly normally pay for a haircut.
Revise this with your best effort:
I recently had a budget-friendly haircut in NY and unfortunately, it turned out to be quite disastrous. It felt as though my hair had been tampered with by a wild chimp and then carelessly placed back on my scalp.

However, due to upcoming job interviews, I was in dire need of a better appearance. I decided to visit Domenick's, where I had the pleasure of being serviced by Robert, who skillfully transformed my hair into a clean and presentable style. The final bill tallied up to $35, which, in my opinion, seemed a tad expensive for my liking. Nevertheless, I must admit that I am once again satisfied with my appearance, looking much more human. I'm curious to know what the average haircut price is in Philly, as it differs from my previous experience.

input: Very unhappy, you lost a valued customer. We had a problem where Monro Muffler underfilled our engine by 3 quarts of oil and caused damage to the engine. Monro's insurance company said they would pay for damages if we brought to the dealer, we were frequent customers of Bergeys so we brought it here. They discovered the timing chain needed to be replaced, a chain that lasts the life of the car unless you don't change the oil or have low oil pressure the tensioner can lock and stretch the chain. Joe the service associate that took the car in specifically said I told the insurance company as little as possible and told them he couldn't tell if it was from the oil and there was no way to tell. And on top of that, was extremely rude and unprofessional to my wife bringing her to tears the way he spoke to her. My wife and I just bought a house in the area, only 26 years old and you lost a life long customer. Over the past year we spent about $7000 in repairs here, and Joe went out of his way to be unhelpful and leave us in a terrible spot. I brought it to another mechanic who was able to help us prove more it was from the oil and do what Joe told us and the insurance company they could not do. So on top of losing a service customer, I'm on the market for a new car and can tell you for sure where I will not be getting it.
Revise this with your best effort:
I am extremely dissatisfied to inform you that I have made the difficult decision to discontinue my patronage as a valued customer. This unfortunate choice stems from a distressing incident involving Monro Muffler. They negligently underfilled our engine with three quarts of oil, resulting in significant damage to the engine itself. Subsequently, Monro's insurance company agreed to cover the expenses if we had the repairs done at the dealer, and as loyal customers of Bergeys, we chose to bring our car to your establishment.

During the inspection, it was revealed that the timing chain, typically known to last the entire lifespan of the vehicle unless issues such as lack of proper oil changes or low oil pressure occur, needed to be replaced. To my dismay, Joe, the service associate who handled our case, deliberately disclosed as little information as possible to the insurance company, emphasizing that there was no conclusive way to determine whether the damage was attributable to the oil issue. His demeanor was not only unprofessional but also deeply offensive, reducing my wife to tears with his disrespectful tone and behavior.

It pains me to share that my wife and I, who recently purchased a house in this vicinity and are merely 26 years old, have decided to sever our long-standing relationship with your establishment. In the past year alone, we have entrusted you with approximately $7,000 worth of repairs. Regrettably, Joe, in his efforts to be uncooperative, has left us in an extremely unpleasant situation. It was necessary for us to seek assistance from another mechanic who went above and beyond to help us gather the evidence required to substantiate the connection between the oil issue and the damage caused – a task that Joe informed us and the insurance company was impossible.

At this juncture, I feel obliged to inform you that not only have you lost a devoted customer for your services, but I am also now actively in the market for a new vehicle. Rest assured, I will be exploring alternative options for this purchase, given the disheartening experience I have undergone with your establishment.

input:

Revise this with your best effort:
Experience the allure of a stunning and immaculate shop that will leave you speechless. Indulge in the delectable homemade breakfast tarts and savory chicken pot pies that will surely tickle your taste buds. Each exquisitely crafted sweet treat is a visual masterpiece and an absolute delight to consume.

While some may argue that the prices of certain items are slightly steep considering their smaller portions, it is important to acknowledge the undeniable fact that superior quality often comes with a higher price tag. Furthermore, the amiable and engaging nature of the counter staff adds to the overall pleasant experience. With such positive encounters, I eagerly anticipate returning to this wondrous place, and wholeheartedly recommend it to others seeking an exceptional culinary adventure.

input: Definitely get in line before 8:30am. We waited about 30 minutes. Pancakes were fine. My friends got the raspberry pancakes, the sweet potato pancakes and the san antonio. I got the sugar and spice pancakes. All were well and fine, a bit dry. I don't understand the hype, but if the line isn't too long it's not bad for normal breakfast food. If the line is longer I would highly recommend skipping this place and heading down the street to Fido - insanely good coffee and great breakfast food.
Revise this with your best effort: For the best experience, it is highly advisable to join the line before 8:30am. Although we had to wait approximately 30 minutes, the pancakes were decent. My companions opted for the raspberry, sweet potato, and San Antonio pancakes, while I tried the sugar and spice variety. All of them were satisfactory, albeit slightly dry. Personally, I fail to comprehend the excessive praise surrounding this place. However, if the queue isn't too lengthy, it's an acceptable option for a standard breakfast. Conversely, if the line stretches far, I highly recommend bypassing this establishment and instead heading towards Fido just down the street, where the coffee is exceptionally good and breakfast fare is superb.

input: They have the WORST service advisors! Used to be good before Kelly and her team left. Unfortunately, it's convenient to work if I need oil change before I can make it to another Honda dealer.
Revise this with your best effort: The service advisors at this place are absolutely terrible! It used to be much better when Kelly and her team were here. Unfortunately, it's the only convenient option when I require an oil change before I can get to a different Honda dealer.

input:
The best soon-dubu in the city!  This place is tucked away and once you walk in, it's like you've stepped into a Korean home.  Very welcoming, warm and inviting.

It's very vegetarian friendly!  The soft tofu is stewed and put into the dol sot pots which each and every stew feels like it's custom made for you. 

You can select from beef, seafood or mixed meats (seafood & beef), mushroom, and just plain.  They can adjust the spice as needed too.  I always get the extra hot with the hot temperature, can't beat it.  The rice also comes in a dol-sot which is great if you leave it in for a while, it burns the rice into a nice crispy shell.  DROOL.

Just thinking about this place makes my mouth salivate!  

If you're not into tofu, they also offer korean bbq meats (cooked in the back), with other soup/stew items.

Love this place!!!
Revise this with your best effort:
Experience the pinnacle of soon-dubu at this hidden gem in the city! As you step inside, you are transported to a cozy Korean home, radiating a welcoming and homely atmosphere.

For vegetarians, this place is a haven! The stewed soft tofu is served in dol sot pots, ensuring each delightful concoction feels tailor-made for you. Choose between beef, seafood, mixed meats, mushroom, or go for the classic plain option. Spice levels can also be customized to your preference. Personally, I can't resist the extra hot with the steaming temperature – a match made in culinary heaven. Additionally, the dol-sot rice adds another layer of deliciousness; let it linger and witness the creation of a delectable crispy shell. The mere thought of it has my mouth watering!

But fret not if tofu isn't your cup of tea, as this place also offers Korean BBQ meats, meticulously prepared in the back, along with a variety of other soup and stew items.

To put it simply, I am head over heels for this place!

input:
As motels go this one is very nice for the rate. Clean, comfortable and well-managed. You get what you pay for so the breakfast buffet is just OK. The pool is too small to swim laps (disappointing). The lobby area is spacious and comportable. 

If you are looking for a moderately priced place to sleep that is clean and comforable this will suit you just fine.
Revise this with your best effort: This motel stands out among others for its affordable rate, boasting a pleasant and inviting atmosphere. Immaculate, cozy, and efficiently run, it exceeds expectations in terms of cleanliness and comfort. The breakfast buffet, while adequate, reflects its price point. Regrettably, the pool falls short for those seeking to swim laps, leaving room for disappointment. Nonetheless, the lobby area impresses with its generous space and remarkable comfort. Should you be searching for a reasonably priced sanctuary to rest, offering a clean and comfortable experience, this establishment will undoubtedly meet your needs seamlessly.

input:

That older area that is out of sight has been that way for years but we finally got tired of it and complained.  He never admitted it could be cleaned up. If there was empathy, I did not hear it.

Regrettably, I did not perceive any empathy being expressed during our interaction.

input:
From the second you walk in the door, you're greeted by the adorable woman at the counter. It seems if you come in here more than once a week, she'll know you're name but I haven't been so lucky since my visits are a bit more sporadic.

My most recent discovery are the vegetarian breakfast sandwiches, which are served all day! I particularly enjoy veg. sausage w/ havarti on an everything bagel. I could actually go for one right about now... I've also had the veggie club sandwich and my other half has enjoyed the chicken cheesesteak hoagie and the chicken salad on a croissant. Everything always taste fresh, they are priced really well  (I think my favorite bagel sandwich I mentioned is $2.09-2.99- cheaper than wawa!). The people at the deli are super helpful, offering menus if you can't read the one on the wall and will make great suggestions and accommodations to your needs and want.

Don't forget to grab a really great snack too while you're there- they have amazing chocolate bars, an incredible drink case, tons of chip varieties and those addictive hi-chew candies in every flavor.

I know i'll be back here, who doesn't like fast / delicious / attentive service?
Revise this with your best effort:
Upon entering the door, you are immediately greeted by an enchanting woman behind the counter. It appears that regulars are fortunate enough to have their names remembered, but unfortunately, my infrequent visits have left me nameless thus far.

During my most recent visit, I stumbled upon the delightful discovery of vegetarian breakfast sandwiches, which are available all day. My personal favorite is the delectable combination of veggie sausage and havarti on an everything bagel. The mere thought of it has me craving one at this very moment... Additionally, I've indulged in their veggie club sandwich, while my partner has savored the flavors of the chicken cheesesteak hoagie and the chicken salad on a perfectly flaky croissant. The freshness of their ingredients always shines through, and what's even better is that their prices are quite reasonable. In fact, the beloved bagel sandwich I mentioned earlier is priced at a mere $2.09-2.99, which is actually cheaper than what you'd find at Wawa! The deli staff goes above and beyond, providing exceptional assistance such as offering alternative menus if the one on the wall proves difficult to read. They also offer great suggestions tailored to your specific cravings and dietary needs.

Oh, and don't leave without treating yourself to an extraordinary snack. Their collection of chocolate bars is truly exceptional, their drink case is beyond incredible, and their vast array of chip varieties is nothing short of impressive. Let's not forget about the irresistible hi-chew candies, available in every mouthwatering flavor imaginable!

Rest assured, I will definitely be returning to this delightful establishment. After all, who can resist the allure of prompt, scrumptious, and attentive service?

input: We stopped in for brunch and we weren't expecting the food to be so delicious.  The 3 meat hash was amazing, as was the turkey sandwich and bagel/salmon.  The employees were very friendly and accommodating.  A little pricey, but well worth.  We will visit again if in the area.
Revise this with your best effort: We decided to try their brunch and were pleasantly surprised by how incredibly delicious the food was. The three meat hash, turkey sandwich, and bagel with salmon were all outstanding. Furthermore, the staff members were exceptionally friendly and accommodating, ensuring a pleasant dining experience. Although the prices were slightly higher, the quality and taste of the food made every penny worth it. If we find ourselves in the area again, we would definitely make a point to visit this place again.

input: Nice little bar located at the very far end of Terminal E and Tampa International. The airport recently added several new restaurants with a "local vibe" and this is one of them. There isn't a ton of seating but it also isn't close to the TSA area so it's a bit hidden. Hey have TVs if you wanna catch a game while you wait for your flight. Food is very reasonably price for the portion size. Appetizers run from $5-$10 and majority of sandwiches are $12. I didn't order any food but it looked amazing! Drinks are tasty and Prices are not terrible. Think 22oz Jai Alai for $8.50. You cannot take alcoholic beverages into the terminal (Columbia does this I think). I had a Manhattan for $11 and it was very tasty. Staff is attentive and friendly. I know my new spot when I'm waiting on a Delta flight!
Revise this with your best effort:
Located at the very far end of Terminal E in Tampa International, this cozy little bar fits right in with the airport's new "local vibe" theme. Despite its limited seating, this hidden gem is far enough from the TSA area to offer a more relaxed atmosphere. With TVs available, you can catch a game while waiting for your flight.

One of the highlights of this bar is its reasonably priced food. From appetizers priced between $5 and $10 to sandwiches averaging at $12, the portion sizes are generous. Although I didn't personally try any food, the presentation was impressive. 

When it comes to drinks, you won't be disappointed either. The prices are fair, with a 22oz Jai Alai costing $8.50. However, it's important to note that you cannot bring alcoholic beverages into the terminal, which is a common practice at other bars like Columbia. For those looking for a classic cocktail, I highly recommend their Manhattan for $11 — it was delicious.

Beyond the food and drinks, the staff is attentive and friendly, making the overall experience even more enjoyable. Whenever I find myself waiting for a Delta flight, I know exactly where to go.

input: The depot burger is so delicious along with the shishito peppers! Perfect food, perfect atmosphere, perfect drinks!
Revise this with your best effort: The Depot Burger is absolutely scrumptious, especially when paired with the delightful Shishito Peppers! It's a match made in culinary heaven - the flavors are simply impeccable. Moreover, the ambiance at this place is beyond compare, setting the stage for a truly perfect dining experience. And let's not forget about the drinks - they are second to none! This combination of delectable food, inviting atmosphere, and sensational beverages creates an unparalleled culinary delight.

input: Quality of this store has gone downhill over the past few years. In the past,  I was able to easily choose from a wide selection of food at reasonable prices any time of day. I have noticed recently that the produce is not as fresh, but more expensive,  and the prices of the organic foods are more expensive than Whole Foods. This morning I debated on going to Wegmans or going to this store. I only had to get a few items so I decided on this Giant since it was closer. Big mistake. I have seen on average at least 3 or 4 people shopping around 5 a.m. In the past but today just me. They had all of the store roped off where it was impossible to get to certain aisles and very difficult to get to the register. In my frustration I went under a rope to get soup.  I was then berated by a number of people who were supposed to be cleaning the floors but some were just standing around doing nothing. I couldn't even walk out of the closest door because that was blocked off. If they needed to clean the floor they should have closed the store for a few hours. It would have taken less time at Wegmans which is where I will shop for now on.
Revise this with your best effort:
The quality of this store has significantly declined in recent years. Previously, I could effortlessly select from a wide variety of food options offered at reasonable prices throughout the day. However, I have recently observed that the produce is not as fresh and has become more expensive. Additionally, the prices of organic foods here are even higher than those at Whole Foods. 

This morning, I found myself contemplating between going to Wegmans or this store. Since I only needed a few items and this Giant was closer, I made the regrettable decision to come here. To my dismay, I was the only customer present, whereas in the past I would typically see three or four people shopping around 5 a.m. Furthermore, the entire store was sectioned off, preventing easy access to certain aisles and making it extremely challenging to reach the checkout counter. Frustrated, I decided to go under one of the ropes to retrieve some soup. This action led to me being scolded by several individuals who were supposedly cleaning the floors, although some were simply standing idly by. 

Notably, even exiting through the nearest door was impossible as it was also blocked off. If the intention was to clean the floors, they should have considered closing the store for a few hours. I am convinced that it would have been more efficient to shop at Wegmans, which is where I will be directing my shopping endeavors from now on.

input: This place is a hidden gem.  It is located in a strip mall, but this restaurant is anything but a strip mall restaurant.   My husband took me here for my birthday and I was blown away with the whole experience.  It's a very modern, romantic atmosphere.  The food is excellent.  I was shocked by the Fois gras-amazing.  I had the prix fixe menu and I loved ordering 3 courses.  The short ribs were great, but I want to try something new next time.  The desserts were awesome.  I usually take caramel, but there was a caramel tart that was to die for.  Can't wait to go back!!!!
Revise this with your best effort: This place truly is a hidden gem, tucked away in a strip mall, but don't let its location fool you - this restaurant surpasses all expectations. My husband surprised me with a birthday dinner here, and I was utterly captivated by the entire experience. From the moment we stepped inside, the modern and romantic ambiance engulfed us. The food itself was nothing short of exceptional, with one dish in particular leaving me in awe - the Fois gras was absolutely phenomenal. Opting for the prix fixe menu allowed me to indulge in three delightful courses, and while the short ribs were undeniably delicious, my adventurous spirit craves something new on our next visit. Now, let me tell you about the desserts - they were simply mind-blowing. As someone who typically gravitates towards caramel, I was delightfully surprised by the caramel tart that was nothing short of heavenly. Needless to say, I am eagerly anticipating our return to this extraordinary place!

input:
--------DINNER REVIEW----------

I rarely write reviews, but this honestly was one of the worst group dining experiences I've ever had. It was objectively a horrible experience, even without comparing it to the hype it receives, and ruined what was supposed to be a nice birthday dinner celebration. 

We had a group of 8 that had a reservation made well in advance. Short wait, but not too bad. Keep in mind, it seemed like a normal Friday night, but weren't super busy or at-capacity.

It was a birthday dinner, so I told the hostesses that it was her birthday, and asked if they could bring out something for her at the end of the meal, which was acknowledged. Pretty standard stuff, whether at a Applebee's or the French Laundry. We were sat at a booth right next to the Maitre D' stand, and next to all the wait staff's home base, so pretty much no excuse for not getting any attention. 

After getting us waters, it took them a LONG time to even come by and acknowledge us. After ordering wine, it took them another good 15-20 minutes to even bring us our wine, and no one even checked in on us! (hint: if you're running a restaurant, wine is your profit center and doesn't take any work other than taking a bottle off a shelf and opening it. bring it out ASAP...). 

After ordering food, it was more of the same...a long wait for food to start coming out and no one checking in on us AT ALL. We drank the bottles we ordered and had to get up and flag someone down to get another wine order. A couple of us even got up during the meal to remind them to bring out something for birthday girl at the end of the meal. 

Once our meal was done and taken away, we were given dessert menus and the server disappeared for 10-15 minutes... AGAIN. After coming back, he asked what dessert we wanted, so we ordered some coffees... and waited... and waited. Eventually we got up and asked him what was going on and if they were going to bring anything out like we asked multiple times. 

They finally brought out a couple of cookies with a candle...

In summary, the food was pretty hit or miss, pretty mediocre for this price point. Whipped feta, like other reviews have said, was amazing, and the Braised Lamb was really good. But the Sirloin was chewy and bland and the Grilled Caesar tasted like a soggy, luke-warm, wilted mess (two orders were left untouched by a group of 8). Atmosphere was nice and trendy. But the service, which is a huge reason to spend your hard-earned $ at a restaurant, was absolutely horrendous. 

I really love going to cool, popular restaurants and having a great time, and I hate writing such a negative review, but I had to share my experience, especially for a restaurant that is getting an awful lot of (undeserved) hype.
Revise this with your best effort:
--------DINNER REVIEW----------

Typically, I don't write reviews, but I feel compelled to share my recent dining experience, which unfortunately falls under the category of one of the worst group dinners I've ever had. Even without considering the excessive hype surrounding this establishment, it was objectively a horrible experience that overshadowed what was meant to be a memorable birthday celebration.

We had made a reservation well in advance for our party of 8. Although the wait wasn't excessively long, it should be noted that it was just a typical Friday night, and the restaurant wasn't exceptionally busy or at full capacity.

Since it was a birthday dinner, I informed the hostesses about the occasion and requested something special for the birthday celebrant at the end of our meal. They acknowledged the request, a standard practice whether dining at a casual restaurant like Applebee's or an upscale place like the French Laundry. Interestingly, we were seated at a booth right beside the Maitre D' stand and in close proximity to the wait staff's home base. With such convenience, there was no excuse for the lack of attention we received.

After serving us water, it took an exceptionally long time for anyone to even acknowledge our presence. Ordering wine was another ordeal, as it took an additional 15-20 minutes for them to bring it to our table, all while neglecting to check on us. (Hint: A restaurant's profit center often lies within its wine selection, which requires minimal effort other than retrieving a bottle and opening it. Therefore, it should be promptly served.) 

Even after placing our food orders, the situation persisted with long waiting periods and complete absence of any staff member checking on us. We finished the bottles of wine we ordered and had to go out of our way to flag someone down for another round. Throughout the meal, a few of us had to remind them multiple times about bringing out something special for the birthday girl.

Once our main course was cleared, we were finally presented with dessert menus, but our server vanished yet again for another 10-15 minutes. When he eventually returned, it required us to specify our dessert choices, including coffee. Regrettably, we found ourselves waiting indefinitely. At this point, we had no choice but to inquire about the delay and remind them, once more, about the special request we had previously made.

Eventually, they brought out a couple of cookies with a solitary candle...

In summary, the food offered a mixed experience, falling somewhat short of expectations given its price point. The whipped feta, as mentioned in other reviews, was commendable, and the braised lamb was enjoyable. However, the sirloin was disappointing, being both chewy and lacking flavor, and the grilled Caesar salad resembled a damp, lukewarm, and wilted mess (so unappealing that two orders remained untouched by our group of eight). The ambiance of the restaurant was trendy and pleasing. Unfortunately, the service, a crucial aspect when investing one's hard-earned money in dining out, was absolutely horrendous.

I genuinely adore visiting popular and trendy restaurants, creating incredible memories, so it truly pains me to write such a negative review. However, I felt compelled to share this experience, especially considering the excessive and, in my opinion, undeserved hype surrounding this particular establishment.

input:
Great food for the price. 
Tender steak and perfectly cooked shrimp. 
Would certainly come back.

input:
We stopped at Tako due to the positive reviews on yelp. We brought a bottle of white wine with us, the staff did not bring a ice or a chill bucket for us. It took 45 minutes for our appetizers to come out. The edamame was over cooked and mushy while the spring roll did not look appetizing almost like it was frozen. I could buy better spring rolls from trader joes.
Next we moved on to our sushi which was sat on the sushi bar for 15 minutes before it was brought to us. The sushi it self was good, but not the best I have ever had,
If I came here again I would not buy any appetizers. The service was slow
Revise this with your best effort:
We chose to dine at Tako based on its positive reviews on Yelp. However, upon arrival, we were disappointed with the lack of attention to detail. Bringing our own bottle of white wine, we expected the staff to provide an ice or chill bucket, but unfortunately, they did not. Additionally, we waited 45 minutes for our appetizers to be served, only to be disappointed with the quality. The edamame was overcooked and mushy, while the spring roll looked unappetizing and almost as if it had been frozen. Frankly, I have had better spring rolls from Trader Joe's.

Moving on to the sushi, it was left sitting on the sushi bar for 15 minutes before being brought to our table. While the taste was satisfactory, it was not the best I have ever had.

If I were to visit Tako again, I would avoid ordering any appetizers. The slow service was a significant drawback to our overall dining experience.

input: The catfish, chicken, gumbo and mac &a cheese are all to die for. We are the lunch buffet and everything was piping hot and fresh. This place was recommended by a local in the neighborhood we are staying in and it was so worth it!
Revise this with your best effort: The catfish, chicken, gumbo, and mac & cheese at this place are absolutely irresistible. As we indulged in the lunch buffet, everything was served piping hot and delightfully fresh. We discovered this hidden gem thanks to a local in the neighborhood we are staying in, and we couldn't be happier with their recommendation. This dining experience was truly worth it!

input:
See's candies is California base bakery reach Florida. I know about this candies when my wife living in California. Their chocolate is very soft and tasty. 

In Tampa, the International Plaza Mall has this temporary store from Thanksgiving to Easter. They located very close to H&M clothing store. You can have samples before you buy it. I got the lollipop candies. I also bought one assorted chocolate candies. They are very good. The store clerk was kind enough to let us try their assorted chocolate other their typical sample candies. 

You can go with chocolate with nut, mint, toffee, milk, white or dark chocolate. All are good. Guilty pleasure with a touch at sweet side. Mail order through the web also available. If you close to the mall, just go to buy one without shipping.
Revise this with your best effort:
See's Candies, a California-based bakery, has expanded its reach to Florida, including Tampa. I first discovered these delectable treats when my wife lived in California, and ever since, I have become enamored with their soft and delicious chocolates.

Located in the International Plaza Mall from Thanksgiving to Easter, See's Candies sets up a temporary store conveniently close to the H&M clothing store. What sets them apart is their generosity in allowing customers to sample their creations before making a purchase. During my visit, I indulged in their lollipop candies and couldn't resist buying an assorted box of chocolates. They did not disappoint.

The store clerk went above and beyond, granting us the opportunity to taste their assorted chocolates, going beyond their typical sample candies. With options ranging from chocolate with nuts, mint, toffee, milk, white, and dark chocolate, it was difficult to choose just one. Each flavor was a guilty pleasure with a satisfying touch of sweetness.

For those unable to visit the mall, you can conveniently order these delectable treats online through their website. However, if you find yourself in close proximity to the mall, I highly recommend stopping by to experience the joy of purchasing these mouthwatering chocolates without the need for shipping.

input:
Second stop for Center City Restaurant Week:  R2L, dinner for $35 each. 

On the 37th floor of Two Liberty Place is a very fancy-cool restaurant/lounge where you can get a bird's eye view of the city! Group of us went to dinner here together after a day of meetings. Didn't get one of the tables facing the windows, but still had great views of the sunset and city by night. Again, multiple choices for the three courses, but I chose to start with the crisp peas/ham/garlic risotto [balls]. Main course was the Butcher's Filet (braised short rib + Steuben bean chili, potato/farm veg slaw and basil), which was quite heavy since there was also meat in the chili as well. The dazzling dessert to finish it off was the milk chocolate + hazelnut pudding served with salted caramel and coffee to melt the chocolate, and candied almonds on the side. A bottle of wine for the table as well. Food was great, waiter was awesome (making sure to warn me that the risotto came in ball form rather than a bowl, for instance), very classy experience.
Revise this with your best effort:
Our second stop for Center City Restaurant Week was R2L, located on the 37th floor of Two Liberty Place. This upscale restaurant/lounge offers stunning views of the city, providing a bird's eye perspective. After a long day of meetings, our group decided to dine here together. While we didn't secure a table by the windows, we still enjoyed a marvelous view of the sunset and the city lights at night.

The menu at R2L provided multiple options for each of the three courses. I opted to begin with the delicious crisp peas/ham/garlic risotto balls. They were a fantastic starter that left me wanting more. For the main course, I indulged in the Butcher's Filet, which consisted of braised short rib and Steuben bean chili, accompanied by potato and farm vegetable slaw with a touch of basil. The dish was satisfyingly hearty, especially due to the presence of meat in the chili. A delightful finale awaited us in the form of a milk chocolate and hazelnut pudding served with salted caramel, coffee-infused melted chocolate, and candied almonds on the side. To complement our meal, we also savored a bottle of wine shared amongst the table.

Not only was the food at R2L exceptional, but the waiter provided outstanding service. He made sure to inform me that the risotto came in the form of tasty balls rather than a traditional bowl presentation, displaying attention to detail and thoughtfulness. The entire experience at R2L exuded class and sophistication, contributing to a memorable evening.

input: Becca is an awesome bartender. They have awesome happy hour specials including land shark. The food menu is somewhat limited but the service at the bar is great. We hope they can keep up the business and attract more locals.
Revise this with your best effort: Becca is an exceptional bartender, known for her exceptional skills and service. With her dedication and expertise, we have high hopes that Becca will continue to foster a thriving business and attract an ever-growing number of local patrons.

input: Bummer, just moved to this area and this was my first visit to this location. input: They have great prices if you order family style. We tried the pot roast and it was just as good carry out as it would have been at the restaurant. input: Ordered Caramel frappe at Drive thru, BIG MISTAKE! Took 30 min and there were only 2 cars in front of me.

input:

We tried the Peanut butter pizza cookie and the Oreo cookies, and both were perfection. I'm very eager to try other flavors. Also, being open until 3am is the smartest decision of any bakery in America. 

The only reason I'm not giving a 5 is because of the prices. But, to be honest, those late nights when all I want is a fresh baked cookie pizza, I'd be willing to pay $50.
Revise this with your best effort:

We indulged in the Peanut Butter pizza cookie as well as the Oreo cookies, and let me tell you, both were sheer perfection. The combination of flavors in each bite left us craving more, and we simply cannot wait to explore the other delectable options available.
