input:
I moved from Chicago to Philadelphia over a year ago.  Everybody here raves about the restaurants, but I have yet to find many that deserve five stars, or even four.  This is the best restaurant I have eaten in in Philadelphia.  

Tahini and bread  arrived at the table, and I thought, hum, plain but I'm hungry.  They must put crack in that Tahini.  I wanted to lap it out of the bowl like an uncouth dog.  The bread is excellent too.

I love a menu with many organic meat choices.  How often can you order an organic beef shishkabob?  It was superb.  The meat done perfectly, the onions nearly caramelized but not quite so they still had some substantive crunch.  The purslane salad tasted like I was eating a plant in the middle of a garden.  It is not often that I dream about a salad but I do dream about this one

My husband had a chicken dish with black eyed peas and green peas and fantastic rice.  I won't begin to describe the flavoring; it is beyond my culinary vocabulary.  We asked what spices they use, and in addition to traditional zatar, they use their own blend of spices.  I don't even need to know what is in it just so long as we can keep coming back and ordering it again and again.

I was so full but ate dessert none the less, which I usually don't do.  But when a diner is this good, I had a feeling the desserts would be too and I just needed to find out.  Pistachio creme brulee.  It could have come out over the top, but no indeed.  It was pure pistachio heaven in s super light yet rich custard.  Heaven. Heaven.

Our service was superb.  The squeezed us into a last minute Friday night reservation with the caveat that we would need to get through our dinner in an hour and 15 minutes in order to accommodate a reservation made prior to us.  Given the time constraints they never made us feel rushed and timed the meal perfectly.  Then my husband left to go to the restroom, the waiter picked up his napkin and refolded it nicely on the table.  Do I care about the napkin placement in the middle of a meal?  Not really, but it is a sign that the waitstaff is incredibly attentive and extremely well trained.  

My eating out plan for Philly might just be to skip eating most everywhere most of the time so I can frequent this expensive, though appropriately priced restaurant.  Kudos to the chef.
Revise this with your best effort:
I relocated from Chicago to Philadelphia more than a year ago, and while everyone here boasts about the restaurants, I have struggled to come across many that truly deserve a five-star or even a four-star rating. However, I must admit that this particular restaurant has surpassed all expectations and stands as the best dining experience I have had in Philadelphia thus far.

As I sat at the table and observed the tahini and bread before me, my first impression was that it appeared rather plain. Yet, as I indulged in the tahini, I couldn't help but feel an incredible, addicting taste that left me yearning for more. In fact, I found myself tempted to savor every last bit of it straight from the bowl, much like an uncivilized dog. The bread, too, was exceptional in its own right.

One aspect that truly captivated me was the extensive selection of organic meat options on the menu. When was the last time I could order an organic beef shishkabob? The flavors were absolutely superb, with the meat cooked to perfection and the onions skillfully caramelized, retaining a delightful crunch. The purslane salad transported me to a serene garden, providing a unique freshness that I rarely associate with a mere salad. This particular dish has even made its way into my dreams on multiple occasions.

My husband opted for a chicken entree accompanying black-eyed peas, green peas, and delectable rice. Describing the flavoring would be an arduous task as it goes beyond the limits of my culinary vocabulary. Upon inquiring about the spices used, we were informed that in addition to the traditional zatar, the restaurant uses its own exclusive mix of spices. It matters not whether I am aware of the precise ingredients; all that matters is that we have the privilege of returning to this establishment to relish this remarkable dish repeatedly.

Despite already being thoroughly satiated, I couldn't resist indulging in a dessert, a rarity for me. However, being within the walls of this remarkable eatery, I harbored a strong conviction that the desserts would be equally exceptional, and I simply had to experience them firsthand. The pistachio creme brulee surpassed all expectations; devoid of any excessive flamboyance, it delivered a taste of pistachio heaven within an exquisitely light and simultaneously rich custard. A truly heavenly experience indeed.

The service was nothing short of exceptional. Despite squeezing us into a last-minute reservation on a bustling Friday night, with the caveat that we would need to finish our meal within an hour and fifteen minutes to accommodate a prior booking, we never felt hurried or pressured. The timing of the meal was impeccable, ensuring a seamless dining experience. Furthermore, when my husband briefly excused himself to visit the restroom, the attentive waiter took the time to neatly refold his napkin on the table. While such a gesture may seem insignificant in the grand scheme of a meal, it speaks volumes about the remarkable level of attentiveness and training of the staff.

Upon reflection, as I plan future dining experiences in Philadelphia, my inclination may very well be to forgo dining at various establishments and instead frequent this slightly pricier, yet appropriately priced gem of a restaurant. My heartfelt commendations extend to the talented chef behind these exceptional culinary creations.

input: They served me a frozen pizza and skunked beer.  'Nuff said.

input:
This is the place for authentic Indian street food. I've been here multiple times ordering different things ranging from bhel puri, pav bhaji, vada pav, deconstructed samosa and aloo tikki, dabeli, kulfi and more. Everything was made exceptionally well.

I regret not having found this place sooner.
Revise this with your best effort:

Not to mention the heavenly deconstructed samosa and aloo tikki, as well as the delectable dabeli, kulfi, and many more delights. Impeccably prepared, each dish surpassed my expectations.

I can't help but feel a pang of regret for not stumbling upon this incredible place earlier.

input:

input: I was told this place is a must for a Sonoran hot dog. I was visiting from out of town and had never had one. Revise this with your best effort: I was informed that this place was a must-visit for Sonoran hot dogs, so as someone from out of town who had never tried one before, I decided to give it a shot. While I can't say it was my personal favorite due to its multitude of components, it was still enjoyable. However, what truly impressed me was the delicious guacamole. Additionally, I ordered the taco combo which included chicken, carne asada, and cabeza. Something commendable about this place is the salsa bar at BK, where you have the freedom to add your desired toppings. The service was prompt and attentive, with the food arriving promptly as well. input:
I stopped by Bell Meade during a recent visit to Nashville. The best way for me to describe my experience is to say that the next time I go to Nashville I will go out of my way to make sure I return to Bell Meade.

On my travels, I tend to stop from time to time to see if I can find specific bourbons that may be out locally. At this time of year, I did not expect any great finds because many of the items for which I look have their annual release later in the year so it's a surprise to find any of them on the shelf. For example, Elmer T Lee is a favorite of mine so it was one that I asked about.

Despite the fact that I walked away without Elmer T, I still had a great time. I enjoyed a few tastes at the tasting bar and even better I had a great conversation with Max. He is one of the reasons I will return.

I did walk out with a bottle of Tennessee whiskey cream that is not sold locally and there was a bottle on the shelf that I have not seen locally that I need to investigate. As I said I will return and a five star rating from me should say at all.
Revise this with your best effort:
During my recent trip to Nashville, I made a stop at Bell Meade and I must say, it left such a lasting impression that I am determined to visit again on my next trip to the city.

Whenever I travel, I like to take a break and explore different places in search of specific bourbons that may not be readily available locally. Naturally, I didn't have high expectations of finding any rare gems during this time of year, as most of the sought-after releases typically happen later in the year. Nonetheless, to my surprise, I stumbled upon Bell Meade and decided to give it a try. Among the bourbons I inquired about was Elmer T Lee, a personal favorite of mine.

Although I left without securing a bottle of Elmer T, I had an absolutely splendid time during my visit. I had the opportunity to indulge in a few samples at their tasting bar, but what made the experience even more enjoyable was my delightful conversation with Max. His knowledge and friendly demeanor truly left an impression and convinced me I had to return.

While I may not have found Elmer T, I did manage to get my hands on a bottle of Tennessee whiskey cream, a rarity that isn't easily found in local stores. Furthermore, I spotted another unique bottle on their shelf that requires further investigation. With all these positive experiences in mind, it is safe to say that I will be back at Bell Meade, and a well-deserved five-star rating is definitely warranted.

input:
I love trying fresh seafood on piers, wharfs and seaside markets. Most of the time, it is a disappointing experience but this place is not. The food is legitimately fresh and prepared well. The gorgeous view is just a cherry on top of nature's beautiful sundae. I have been here before but ordered the "wrong" thing (cioppino). That wasn't very good when I had it a couple of years ago here. 

We came for a late lunch/early dinner on a Monday. Even at 4pm,  there was a wait! We waited about 25 minutes and got a table outdoor. While it wasn't ideal that we sat right in the sun with no shelter other than our sunscreen and sunglasses, the view was worth it. 

We got the local crab special which was a steamed 3-lb. crab served with a salad and soup for $26. I thought this was quite the steal because the crab was huge, delicious and meaty. The garden salad was fresh as simple as it was. The lobster bisque we got was pretty good. (The other options were Caesar salad and clam chowder). They topped off the crab with a couple of onion rings and cups of cocktail sauce and drawn butter. Yum!

We also got the fried platter of shrimp, oysters, calamari and scallops for $12.95. It came with cole slaw, onion rings, tartar sauce and cocktail sauce. As greasy of a meal as this made, it was one of the better fried platters I've had anywhere. The seafood was just really fresh including the sometimes-feared fried oyster. :)

The ice in our iced teas melted away in the sun. Our waitress was so cool and brought us lots of extra ice and an extra iced tea in case we needed it (we did because it was hot out!). She was just friendly and good at her job - five stars for her!

By the time we left at about 6, there were so many people waiting. Make sure you sign up for a seat on the clipboard right when you get there. The restaurant is the last one at the very end of the pier. Parking on the pier is free for 90 minutes but it looks like a drive that will upset tires. I parked in the large lot south of the pier and walked 15 minutes up and onto the pier. It was free on a Monday late afternoon.
Revise this with your best effort:
I absolutely adore indulging in fresh seafood from piers, wharfs, and seaside markets. More often than not, my experiences end up being disappointing, but this particular place defied my expectations. The food here is genuinely fresh and impeccably prepared, and the stunning view is the perfect accompaniment to nature's beautiful spread. I have visited this place before, but unfortunately, I made a poor choice with the cioppino, which didn't taste great when I had it a couple of years ago.

We arrived for a late lunch/early dinner on a Monday, and surprisingly, even at 4pm, there was a wait! After waiting for about 25 minutes, we were seated outdoors. Though it wasn't ideal to be sitting under the blazing sun without any shelter except for our sunscreen and sunglasses, the awe-inspiring view made it all worthwhile.

We decided to try the local crab special, which consisted of a steamed 3-lb. crab served with a salad and soup, all for the price of $26. I found this to be an absolute steal because the crab was massive, delectable, and packed with meat. The garden salad was delightfully fresh and simple. The lobster bisque we ordered was pretty good as well. (Alternatively, we could have chosen Caesar salad or clam chowder). To complement the crab, they garnished it with a couple of onion rings and provided cups of cocktail sauce and drawn butter. Simply divine!

Additionally, we opted for the fried platter of shrimp, oysters, calamari, and scallops, priced at $12.95. It was accompanied by cole slaw, onion rings, tartar sauce, and cocktail sauce. Despite the indulgent and greasy nature of this meal, it was one of the best fried platters I've had anywhere. The seafood was exceptionally fresh, even the oft-dreaded fried oyster proved to be delightful. :)

As we sat in the sun, the ice in our iced teas inevitably melted away. However, our waitress was incredibly considerate, promptly bringing us an abundance of extra ice and an additional iced tea in case we needed it (which we certainly did, given how scorching it was outside!). Her friendly and efficient service truly deserved five stars!

By the time we concluded our meal at around 6 o'clock, the waiting area was bustling with numerous people. I highly recommend signing up for a seat on the clipboard as soon as you arrive. The restaurant is located at the very end of the pier, and while parking on the pier is free for 90 minutes, the drive might be rough on your tires. Personally, I parked in the large lot south of the pier and enjoyed a leisurely 15-minute walk on to the pier. Plus, parking was free on a late Monday afternoon.

input:
What a disappointment. This place was not good I would suggest you think twice before selecting this option. The manager and wait staff may possibly be the worst I have ever encountered, rude and definitely not focused on customer service.  The manager is a very angry hostile fella I asked if I could get brown rice instead of white and he blasted me...I offered to pay extra and he stormed off? Do not know what the deal was but this is just plain unprofessional and creepy behavior. The waitresses will smack into you while you are eating...man what a mess this place is from top to bottom.
The food just OK at best! I am seriously complimenting them here... you can do better at home than here. Seriously I am not going to go into you have been warned just yuk...OK? these other folks with the positive reviews for this place must burn off their taste buds with adult beverages. (Didn't try the sake it may be the high point of the joint...but why would I want to expose my taste buds to a substandard meal to enjoy some rice wine? I can do this at home.
 Here is something I am not sure of, I have only lived here a few months now, is it customary to charge for each soda every time you get a refill here? I was charged for each I asked why they said "This is how we do it here." So at $2 bucks per 6-8 ounces of beverage you may want to go with water at this place...but smarter yet! Go elsewhere.
I will not be returning to this establishment.

Worst yet.
Revise this with your best effort:
What a disappointment. This place was extremely disappointing and I strongly advise against choosing this option. The manager and wait staff were absolutely terrible, displaying rudeness and a complete disregard for customer service. The manager's angry and hostile demeanor was shocking when all I did was ask for brown rice instead of white, even offering to pay extra. Their unprofessional and unsettling behavior was beyond comprehension. To make matters worse, the waitresses would carelessly bump into me while I was trying to eat, creating a chaotic dining experience.

As for the food, it was just mediocre at best. I'm giving them a generous compliment here by saying it was only okay. Honestly, you can make better food at home. Seriously, I can't emphasize enough how strongly I recommend avoiding this place. It seems those with positive reviews must have numbed their taste buds with alcohol because there is no other explanation.

I didn't try the sake, but it might be the only redeeming aspect of this establishment. However, subjecting my taste buds to substandard food just to enjoy some rice wine doesn't make any sense. I can have a better meal at home.

Here's something I'm not sure about, as I've only lived here for a few months. Is it normal for this place to charge for each soda refill? I was charged for each refill and when I asked why, they simply responded with, "This is how we do it here." Charging $2 for 6-8 ounces of beverage is absurd. It might be best to stick with water at this place, or even better, go somewhere else entirely.

I have absolutely no intention of ever returning to this establishment.

It was the worst experience yet.

input:
I stayed at the Orange St location from Friday to Monday.

Arrival: I already read plenty of reviews about no signs marking the location therefore, I looked for Starbucks. I parked in a spot in front of the multi business complex. I went inside to find a guard at a desk that said we have been contracted to hand guests their keys and room number and nothing more. He advised me there was a phone that was on the wall that I could make a call to someone if I needed to. He also stated that the very few parking spots in front were free* only on the weekend.

The Room: This wasn't a room, this was an apartment and I absolutely loved it. It was very spacious and had everything I sought* after for that weekend, such as: fully stocked kitchen, a desk, lots of space, king bed, huge table, nice living room, lots of closets. My only complaint is that I could not open any windows for fresh air...they are nailed/screwed shut. There was also a small welcome bag w cookies and water and papers letting you know where all the food delivery locations and numbers.
There wasn't maid service knocking loudly or trying to barge in early in the morning. This place is more of a long term setting and I'm sure the maids come around during the week Monday-Friday if you desire. I was only here for 3 days and I was fine with that. I went shopping at Shoprite and filled my fridge with water and breakfast to cook.

Overall: This place is awesome, I had a huge living room to entertain my guests when they visited, and a nice desk to study my Anatomy notes. I forgot to mention how quiet** this place is. I loved it. I felt as if no one was there except me. Very quiet* which worked for me on Sunday bc I had lots of studying to do and two TV's to watch The Walking Dead on. Lol!  I would most definitely stay here again. Very spacious and updated. Loved it!
Revise this with your best effort:
During my stay from Friday to Monday, I chose the Orange St location based on several reviews I had read. Upon arrival, I immediately noticed the absence of signs marking the location, so I relied on the nearby Starbucks as a landmark. Parking was available in front of the multi-business complex, although I later discovered that the limited spots were only free on weekends. Inside, I found a guard at the front desk who informed me that their role was solely to hand out keys and room numbers. He pointed out a wall-mounted phone for any additional assistance I might need.

Upon entering my room, I was pleasantly surprised to find that it was more like an apartment rather than a standard hotel room. The spacious layout included a fully stocked kitchen, a comfortable desk, ample storage space, a king-sized bed, a large dining table, and a cozy living room. It had everything I had hoped for during my weekend stay. The only downside was that the windows were securely sealed shut, preventing me from enjoying any fresh air. However, I did appreciate the small welcome bag filled with cookies, water, and helpful information about nearby food delivery options.

What stood out about this accommodation was the lack of intrusive maid service. Since it caters more towards long-term stays, I understand that the maids would typically visit on weekdays. However, during my three-day stay, I didn't encounter any disruptive knocks on the door or early morning disturbances. This suited me well as I was able to go shopping at Shoprite and stock my fridge with water and breakfast items to cook at my convenience.

Overall, I had a fantastic experience at this Orange St location. The spacious living room provided a great space for entertaining my guests, and the well-appointed desk allowed me to focus on studying my Anatomy notes. I must also mention how incredibly quiet the place was. It truly felt like I was the only one there, which was perfect for my Sunday of intensive studying and catching up on episodes of The Walking Dead with the two TVs available. I would not hesitate to stay here again in the future. The modern updates and spaciousness made it a truly enjoyable stay.

input: Awesome location, good service is why I have been eating there for the past 15 years off and on. Mostly the excuses about the steak is why I have to write the review. I am happy to pay more for good quality steak but don't blame the poor guy that sold it to you !
Revise this with your best effort: I have been a patron of this establishment for the past 15 years, and it continues to impress me with its exceptional location and commendable service. input: I had the worst experience of my life and it's not over yet.  I made a mistake in purchasing a vehicle that is out of my budget on a Friday afternoon.  By Sunday after review of my budget I realized I was unable to afford the car.  I called the salesman and tried to explain my situation at 11:30am.  He stated he would speak with his manager and call me back.  At 3:30 after no return call, I called him again, no answer. I left a voicemail and still no call at closing time.  Monday morning I arrived at the dealership as they were opening.  I asked Stephen, the salesman what they determined.  He instructed me to have a seat and he would talk to his management team.  One hour + later, I was called into a cubicle and told my loan had been funded and the title had been changed.  Therefore, I would have to sell the car back to the dealership as a used car.  I would lose a lot of money in doing this.  This morning, Bill head of finance advised that the bank had questions about funding the loan.  I received a call from the bank stating the loan had NOT been funded and they would be unable to okay the loan.  I have left numerous messages with the dealership and have yet to receive a callback.  I contacted an attorney and per his review I again called the dealership and asked for a time to return the vehicle and take back my trade.  Still no response!  These people will lie to your face, avoid this dealership!!
Revise this with your best effort:
My recent experience at the dealership has been absolutely awful, and it seems like there's no end in sight. It all started on a Friday afternoon when I made the regrettable mistake of purchasing a vehicle that was way out of my budget. It wasn't until Sunday, after carefully reviewing my finances, that I realized I couldn't afford the car at all.

Panicking, I immediately called the salesman at 11:30am to explain my situation. He assured me that he would speak with his manager and get back to me as soon as possible. But as the hours ticked by without a call, I grew increasingly frustrated. At 3:30pm, I decided to call him again, only to be met with a ringing phone and no answer. Left with no other choice, I left a voicemail and hoped for a response by closing time. Sadly, that response never came.

Determined to resolve this matter, I showed up at the dealership first thing Monday morning. I sought out Stephen, the salesman, and asked about the progress with his management team. He told me to wait and promised that he would discuss the matter with them. Little did I know that waiting would consume more than an hour of my time.

Finally, I was called into a cubicle, only to receive devastating news. The loan had already been funded, and the title was changed, meaning that I would have to sell the car back to the dealership as a used vehicle. This would result in a significant financial loss for me. It was a blow I wasn't expecting, and it left me feeling utterly defeated.

As if things couldn't get any worse, this morning the head of finance, Bill, informed me that the bank had raised concerns about funding the loan. I received a call from the bank, confirming that the loan had not, in fact, been funded, and therefore they were unable to provide approval. Frustrated by this rollercoaster of emotions, I have left countless messages for the dealership, desperately seeking a response. Unfortunately, my calls have gone unanswered.

Having reached my wit's end, I contacted an attorney for assistance. Following their advice, I once again called the dealership, this time requesting a scheduled time to return the vehicle and reclaim my trade. But to my disappointment, there has been no response from them whatsoever. It is beyond frustrating to deal with a dealership that not only lies to your face but also avoids any form of communication.

Save yourself the trouble and avoid this dealership at all costs. Their deceptive practices and lack of professionalism are not worth the headache.

input:

We were skeptical having also tried Mood Cafe (owned by the W.Philly folks), and it wasn't as good. But the KOP location is actually very comparable to the West Philly location.  

There is no ambiance or atmosphere here.  The strip mall where it's located is pretty depressing.  Desi Village may be the only active store in it.  And its decor is tired and old.  It is a big space and it appears they do a big lunch buffet but I'm curious if it's ever full.  So don't go for the ambiance.

But the food is good.  We ordered some Keema Naan, Samosas, Saag Paneer, and Lamb Biryani.  All of it was really good.  Perfectly seasoned, not too oily, and appropriately spicy.  I have a nut allergy and made them aware of that and they did not screw it up (most Indian restaurants do).  So we'll definitely be back.  It would be great if they moved into nicer digs but the food is what is most important.
Revise this with your best effort:
For years, I have been a loyal patron of Desi Village in West Philly. Recently, after moving to the suburbs, my curiosity drove me to try the KOP Desi Village. Although I had my reservations, especially after my disappointing experience at Mood Cafe (also owned by the W. Philly folks), I was pleasantly surprised to find that the KOP location was just as good as its West Philly counterpart.

Regrettably, the ambiance in the strip mall where Desi Village is situated leaves much to be desired. It is a rather dreary location with Desi Village being the only active store. The outdated decor reflects an undeniable tiredness. While the space is large and seems to cater to a busy lunch buffet, I do wonder if it ever fills up. Thus, if ambiance is a priority for you, this may not be the ideal spot.

However, when it comes to the food, Desi Village truly shines. Our order of Keema Naan, Samosas, Saag Paneer, and Lamb Biryani proved to be exceptional. The dishes were delightfully seasoned, not excessively oily, and provided the right amount of spice. I have a serious nut allergy, and I appreciate that Desi Village took my allergy seriously, as many Indian restaurants tend to overlook this. As a result, we will definitely be returning. It would be even better if the restaurant relocated to a more inviting space, but ultimately, the quality of the food is what matters most.

input:
What an AMAZING occurrence that we ended up here after another barbecue place ran out of food!

So yeah, we started out at another spot and they were out of food when we got there. Super bummed and still in the mood for barbecue, we started wandering around Mid City and my trusty Yelp app guided me to this place. We were greeted by the super nice woman working the counter and she explained the whole process.

I decided to get the one-meat plate with "wet" pulled pork, grits and potato salad, I also got a medium mac and cheese, because I can. My boyfriend got the two-meat plate with brisket and pulled chicken with potato salad and fries. The food blew us both away! It was delicious from beginning to end. The pulled pork was perfect and had the perfect amount of sauce without being drenched. I could tell that if I hadn't ordered it wet it still would have been able to stand on it's own. The mac and cheese was incredible, and after the pork, was my favorite part of the meal. The stone ground grits had a different type of flavor (almost smoky) that I enjoyed and the potato salad was served cold and had that nice crunch that I like in potato salad,

We both agreed that the food was excellent, and a good deal to boot, and that we would both make the trip back out to Earhart, just to have more of this delicious food. The owner himself was bringing the food out to folks and he was really friendly and made sure that we were happy with everything. I like when the owners take the time to make sure that everything is okay. The atmosphere is casual and comfortable and the entire process was a breeze. I will definitely return to LA Smokehouse and I'll be adding it to my "BBQ Favorites" list for future reference.
Revise this with your best effort:
What an incredible turn of events to stumble upon this hidden gem after our previous barbecue joint had already sold out! Initially disappointed but still craving barbecue, we decided to explore Mid City and thank goodness for Yelp leading us to this fantastic place. Upon entering, we were warmly greeted by a friendly woman behind the counter who eagerly explained the ordering process.

Opting for the one-meat plate, I chose the "wet" pulled pork along with sides of creamy grits and tangy potato salad. To indulge my taste buds even further, I couldn't resist ordering a side of their medium mac and cheese. My boyfriend, on the other hand, went for the two-meat plate, selecting both the flavorful brisket and succulent pulled chicken, accompanied by potato salad and crispy fries. The food took us by storm! Each bite was absolute perfection, from the tender and well-seasoned pulled pork to the mac and cheese that easily surpassed all expectations. The stone ground grits possessed a distinctive smoky undertone that delighted my palate, while the chilled potato salad boasted a satisfying crunch.

We both agreed that not only was the food excellent, but it was also a great value for the quality provided. We were so impressed that we decided we would definitely make the journey back to Earhart just to savor more of their delectable offerings. The owner himself personally delivered our food to us, showcasing his friendliness and genuine dedication to ensuring our satisfaction. I truly appreciate when owners take the time to check on their customers. The relaxed and comfortable atmosphere added to the overall enjoyable experience, making the entire process effortless. Without a doubt, I will be returning to LA Smokehouse and adding it to my list of favorite barbecue joints for future reference.

input:
After today's lunch, Iris has moved to the top of my New Orleans favorites lists--no small feat in a city where restaurants are numerous and culinary competition is fierce. Iris excels in every area: food, drinks, service, atmosphere, location, music and overall graciousness. I made the reservation for 10-15 people, not knowing exactly how many in my party would show up. Iris pulled out all the stops to make sure everyone had comfortable seating and even prepared an overflow table for us. At no time did we feel jostled or rushed, which is a common fine dining concern. 

The layout of the restaurant allowed diners to move freely to and from the table and to exchange seats as needed. The music selection was fun and unique, ranging from the Magnetic Fields to Johnny Cash. It was also quiet enough to be enjoyed while allowing conversation to flow unimpeded. Our waiter had excellent timing and anticipated our every need. 

Though they don't have a full drink menu for lunch (I hear they have an amazing mixologist for the dinner hour) they do offer a selection of martinis and wines. One of the guests has accounts with several high-end bars in the Quarter, and the drink list passed his muster. Our table settled for Chardonnays, Perseco and chilled shots of Chartreuse, though I hear they have several types of absinthe as well. 

Our group began with slices of warm, heavenly bread that Iris bakes in house. We continued with an assortment of salads--I had the Hollygrove arugula with warm goat cheese, niçoise olives and balsamic vinaigrette. It was fresh perfection. A few of us opted for the mussels, which I heard were delicious. For my main course, I had a wonderful drum with onions prepared in a tangy soy reduction, which was an elegant complement for the fish. I also heard rave reviews about the gnocci and chicken. 

All the entrees were creatively arranged and selected, and at no point did I feel overwhelmed or that any fuss or pretense had gone into the food. I also appreciated that the portions were European-sized (it always makes me laugh when other Americans list too-small portion size as a complaint even when the food is well-prepared!). Iris prepares a lot of their basic ingredients in-house, and I appreciate that the kitchen makes a point of incorporating gulf fish and produce purchased from local, farmer-friendly markets. 

We settled on the prix fixe menu, which was $20 a person for appetizer, main course and the dessert of the day (the best strawberry sorbet I have had yet). With the added drinks and tip it came out to under $35 a person, which is an excellent price for such a delicious white-linen lunch. No matter the size of my group, I will definitely be returning!
Revise this with your best effort:
Iris has truly earned its place at the top of my list of favorite restaurants in New Orleans. In a city where culinary competition is fierce and dining options are plentiful, this is no small feat. Iris excels in every aspect: the food, drinks, service, atmosphere, location, music, and overall graciousness are all top-notch.

When I made a reservation for a group of 10-15 people, unsure of the exact number that would show up, Iris went above and beyond to ensure our comfort. They prepared additional seating and an overflow table, making sure everyone had a place to sit without feeling cramped or rushed, as can often be the case in fine dining establishments.

The layout of the restaurant allowed for easy movement and seat exchanges, giving our group flexibility and a relaxed atmosphere. The music selection was enjoyable and diverse, ranging from Magnetic Fields to Johnny Cash. It was at just the right volume to be enjoyed without impeding conversation.

Our waiter displayed excellent timing and anticipated our needs perfectly. Despite only offering a limited drink menu during lunch, their selection of martinis and wines was impressive. Even one of our guests, who frequents high-end bars in the Quarter, was impressed by the drink list. We settled on Chardonnays, Prosecco, and chilled shots of Chartreuse, but I also heard they have various types of absinthe available.

Our meal began with slices of warm, homemade bread that were simply heavenly. We then enjoyed a variety of delicious salads. I opted for the Hollygrove arugula with warm goat cheese, Niçoise olives, and balsamic vinaigrette, which was a fresh and perfect combination. Some of our group chose the mussels, which came highly recommended. For my main course, I savored a delicious drum dish with onions, prepared in a tangy soy reduction that truly elevated the flavors of the fish. I also heard rave reviews about the gnocchi and chicken dishes.

All of the entrees were creatively presented and carefully selected. There was no sense of overwhelming or excessive fuss in the preparation. I also appreciated the European-sized portions, finding it amusing when people complain about portion sizes despite the food being well-prepared. Iris takes pride in making many of their key ingredients in-house and sourcing Gulf fish and produce from local, farmer-friendly markets.

We opted for the prix fixe menu, which offered an appetizer, main course, and the dessert of the day (a delightful strawberry sorbet). With drinks and tip, the cost came to under $35 per person, which I consider to be an excellent value for such a delicious white-linen lunch. I am already looking forward to returning to Iris, regardless of the size of my group.

input:
Great atmosphere and decor. Super friendly staff seat you right away. I stopped once for lunch and one time for dinner. They have some lunch specials one of which was Pad Thai. I order with chicken as the protein but they have the typical options for this .  The portion was good for lunch and had good flavor.

For dinner I ordered the chicken satay to start and the Panang Curry with chicken for main course. I was very disappointed in the satay being that you only get two small skewers. The flavor and peanut dipping sauce were very good but they give a few more skewers.  The Panang was good and you get a good size portion of rice.

On a side note, I was disappointed they do not have Pad See Ew. Still some other options on the menu I will return to try.

The staff and manager really know customer service.  Look forward to returning soon!
Revise this with your best effort:
The atmosphere and decor of this place are fantastic. The staff is incredibly friendly and seated me right away. I had the pleasure of dining here for both lunch and dinner. During lunch, they had a few specials, one of which was Pad Thai. I opted for chicken as my protein, but they had the typical options available. The portion size was perfect for a satisfying lunch, and it had a great flavor.

For dinner, I started with the chicken satay and followed it up with the Panang Curry, also with chicken. Unfortunately, I was a bit disappointed with the satay as they only served two small skewers. However, the flavor and the peanut dipping sauce were delicious, but it would have been better if they gave a few more skewers. On the other hand, the Panang Curry was really good, and they served a generous portion of rice.

On a side note, I was a bit let down that they didn't offer Pad See Ew. Nevertheless, there are still plenty of other options on the menu that I plan on returning to try.

The staff and manager displayed excellent customer service and made the dining experience even more enjoyable. I'm eagerly looking forward to my next visit!

input: We randomly decided to look for middle eastern food. Came up with Petra Restaurant near our home. Tried it with my family and liked it quite a bit. Try their Friday and Saturday special rice (it actually test like Indian fried rice) with lamb. Really tasty. Other things are very good too. Don't be discouraged with the location of the place, but food is good and inside of the restaurant is quite nice. Service is good too.
Revise this with your best effort: We spontaneously embarked on a quest for Middle Eastern cuisine and stumbled upon Petra Restaurant conveniently situated near our residence. Venturing inside with my family, we were pleasantly surprised by our dining experience. Particularly noteworthy was their Friday and Saturday special rice, resembling delectable Indian fried rice, impeccably paired with tender lamb. Every bite was a burst of flavors that tantalized our taste buds. Additionally, the menu showcases an array of equally exceptional dishes. Although the restaurant's exterior may not be awe-inspiring, its interior exudes a pleasant ambiance that complements the culinary delights served. Furthermore, the service provided was prompt and friendly, enhancing our overall enjoyment of the meal.

input: I went to the pearl for my birthday and every detail of the experience was awesome!  The food, the wine and the service were all impeccable!  We didn't realize the time and were chatting away after closing time and the staff never made us feel rushed.
Revise this with your best effort: For my birthday celebration, I decided to visit The Pearl, and without a doubt, it turned out to be an absolutely extraordinary experience! Every single aspect of the evening, including the delectable food, exquisite wine selection, and flawless service, exceeded all expectations. In the midst of engaging conversation, time somehow escaped our notice, and even after closing hours, the remarkable staff graciously accommodated us without ever conveying any sense of hurriedness.

input: I stopped in because I was hungry for some snacks.  Browsed the store since I had some spare time and found it to be clean and well stocked.  Wide isles, good selection of bakery stuff, flowers and all your usual groceries. I like that they had some locally made snacks too like California Kettle Corn and Taco Works (out of SLO).  Found the semi-unusual chips I wanted that other stores don't always carry, grabbed a Diet Coke by the checkout and I was happy.  Convenient parking lot and the staff was friendly and helpful.  Thanks Albertsons!
Revise this with your best effort:
I visited the store out of sheer hunger and craving for snacks, and was pleasantly surprised by what I found. As I roamed the aisles during my leisurely browse, it became evident that the store was not only well-maintained but also excellently stocked. The wide aisles allowed for easy navigation, and their impressive bakery selection, along with beautiful flowers, were accompanied by all the regular grocery items one could desire.

What caught my attention and further fueled my satisfaction was the inclusion of locally made snacks like California Kettle Corn and Taco Works from SLO. It's always delightful to support local businesses, and finding my desired semi-unusual chips, which other stores often neglect to carry, was a definite win. Adding a Diet Coke to my cart at the checkout concluded my shopping experience on a high note. Additionally, the convenience of a well-located parking lot further enhanced my visit, and the staff's friendly and helpful demeanor truly made my day.

I express my sincere gratitude to Albertsons for delivering an exceptional shopping experience.

input: New owners turned it into a double threat: Bad food AND bad service. Shame. I loved this place.
Revise this with your best effort: Sadly, under new ownership, this beloved place has tragically become a double-edged sword, encompassing both poor quality cuisine and woeful service. It's truly disheartening as I used to hold it dear to my heart.

input:
We see Dr. Gloudemans, and she's a wonderful doctor. Friendly, upbeat, up on the most recent research, and pro-vaxx (hooray!!). She's proactive about problems after making sure things are worth worrying about-- "let's keep an eye on this, and if there's still a problem in a month or two, come back in and we'll see about a referral to a specialist."

As others have mentioned, we've had a few billing hiccups. We received a bill saying we were past due on 3 appointments' fees, despite paying all copays in the office. Luckily it was all straightened out after a phone call, but it's been frustrating on that front.
Revise this with your best effort:
We had the pleasure of meeting Dr. Gloudemans, and she exceeded our expectations as a remarkable doctor. She radiates friendliness, maintains an upbeat demeanor, and stays updated on the most recent research, making her a vocal advocate for vaccinations (hooray!). We greatly appreciate her proactive approach when it comes to potential issues, ensuring that we only worry when there is a genuine concern. Her suggestion of monitoring a situation and considering a referral to a specialist if necessary demonstrates her commitment to comprehensive care.

However, as mentioned by others, we did encounter a few difficulties with billing. Despite diligently paying all copays during our visits, we unexpectedly received a bill claiming that we were overdue for fees related to three appointments. Thankfully, a simple phone call resolved the issue, but the frustration arising from this situation is undeniable.

input: I attended a meeting for the homebuilders Association of New Orleans here. The food was good and they took good care of the patrons. I had a mimosa which was good. I had a small cup of corn and crab soup which is fantastic but the portion was quite small. I had the grits and grillades and it was fantastic! The portion same grade on this one. The price was around $10. I've included a photo of the menu for your convenience. I didn't get a chance to test the Wi-Fi but I would say given the ambience and the quality of the food it's a repeat
Revise this with your best effort:
I recently attended a meeting for the homebuilders Association of New Orleans, and it was an enjoyable experience. The event staff provided excellent service and took great care of the attendees. As for the refreshments, I treated myself to a delicious mimosa, which was delightful. Additionally, I had the pleasure of trying a small cup of their outstanding corn and crab soup, although the portion size left me wanting more. I also opted for the grits and grillades, and I must say, it was absolutely fantastic. However, similar to the soup, I felt the portion could have been a bit more generous. The dish was priced at around $10, which I found reasonable. I have attached a photo of the menu for your reference.

Unfortunately, I didn't have the opportunity to test the Wi-Fi during my visit. Nevertheless, based on the overall ambience and the high quality of food, I would definitely consider returning to this establishment in the future.

input: I work at the Frist and I don't eat at the cafe much, since I like to leave the building and go home for lunch. But once in a blue moon on a really dreary day like today, I stay in and have the Cobb Salad. It's a go-to for gluten free noshers like me. Add an extra egg for extra protein punch (as if all the meat wasn't enough already) and oil and vinegar dressing and i'm doing ok. A lot of museum visitors and local employees come for the cheap prices and quick bites. Beware of Senior Mondays (every 3rd Monday of the month) and weekends at lunchtime- it's usually busiest at 1130-noon.
Revise this with your best effort: I work at the Frist, although I don't often eat at the cafe. I prefer to leave the building and go home for lunch. However, on rare occasions like today when the weather is dreary, I choose to stay in and indulge in the Cobb Salad. It's a favorite among those who follow a gluten-free diet, like me. To give it an extra boost of protein, I add an additional egg to the already meat-filled salad. Topped off with oil and vinegar dressing, it satisfies my cravings perfectly. Many museum visitors and local employees flock to the cafe due to its affordable prices and quick service. It's important to note that the cafe tends to get quite crowded on Senior Mondays (every 3rd Monday of the month) and during lunch hours on weekends, particularly between 11:30 am and noon.

input:
The food at Ghini's is just delicious. Everything for French breakfast imaginable, and more. I highly recommend the eggs provencale, not something you can get anywhere else. Two eggs basted with a sliced hot house tomato, thyme, garlic and herbs de provance. Get the baguette toast and add the great hashbrowns for a mere dollar.
My personal favorite are all the crepes, both sweet and savory. Especially recommend the spinach and swiss.
Revise this with your best effort: The culinary offerings at Ghini's are simply delightful, providing an array of delectable options for a fulfilling French breakfast experience and beyond. Among the assortment of tantalizing dishes, I eagerly advocate for indulging in the remarkable eggs provencale, a unique delicacy exclusive to this esteemed establishment. This exquisite creation entails two perfectly basted eggs accompanied by a luscious hot house tomato, harmoniously infused with the flavors of thyme, garlic, and the fragrant herbs de provance. As an additional treat, I urge you to savor the baguette toast while incorporating the magnificent hashbrowns into your order, requiring only a nominal fee of one dollar. Among the multitude of temptations, my personal preference inevitably gravitates towards the magnificent crepes, whether in their sweet or savory renditions. With utmost enthusiasm, I particularly urge you to sample the sublime spinach and Swiss crepes, an impeccable fusion of flavors that will surely leave a lasting impression.

input: This was such a unique spot, from the graffiti style art on the walls to the delicious food options and special hummus flavors. Good prices, great portion size. I had the greek steak pita with guac hummus. Will definitely be back!
Revise this with your best effort: I was amazed by the distinctiveness of this place, from the captivating graffiti-style art adorning the walls to the incredibly mouthwatering array of food choices and the extraordinary variety of hummus flavors. The prices were quite reasonable, and the portion sizes were generous. For my meal, I savored the delectable Greek steak pita accompanied by a delightful guacamole-infused hummus. Undoubtedly, I will make it a point to return in the future!

input:
I really like Prep & Pastry - we have been twice in the last two months on a Sunday.  The best trick I learned is to put your name on the waitlist BEFORE YOU ARRIVE.  As long as you are within 5 miles of the restaurant, you can be added.  It is a great service.

I have tried a number of things for brunch and all have been excellent - even their sweets. I think my favorite is the breakfast sandwich.  I am not a big drinker, so I usually order the ice team and it really is better than almost anything else I have tried. 

Staff is really, really nice.  I highly recommend a visit if you are in town.
Revise this with your best effort:
Prep & Pastry has quickly become one of my favorite brunch spots - I can't stop raving about it. In the last two months, my friends and I have visited twice on Sundays, and each time has been a delightful experience. One phenomenal trick I discovered is to add your name to the waitlist beforehand, even before you arrive. The best part? As long as you're within a 5-mile radius of the restaurant, they gladly accommodate your request. I must say, their prompt and efficient service truly impressed me.

When it comes to their brunch offerings, I've tried a number of dishes, and I can confidently say that everything has been excellent, including their delectable sweets. However, if I had to pick a personal favorite, it would definitely be their mouthwatering breakfast sandwich. The flavor combination is simply unforgettable. As for beverages, I don't fancy alcohol much, so I usually opt for their iced tea. Let me tell you, their refreshing iced tea surpasses any other I've ever tasted - it's truly a cut above the rest.

Furthermore, the staff at Prep & Pastry deserves a special mention. Not only are they genuinely friendly, but they also go above and beyond to ensure your visit is worth every penny. Their warm and welcoming nature creates a pleasant and comfortable ambiance that adds to the overall dining experience. Trust me, if you ever find yourself in town, I highly recommend paying a visit to this exceptional establishment. You won't be disappointed.

input:
Another great annual festival Edmonton has to offer.

The Fringe is over two weekends and the joining week full of performances. There's a variety of venues and plays to watch, street performers and musicians. There's a schedule online to find show times, buy tickets and learn more about the artists. 

Half of 104th closes down to add space for a variety of food vendors and artisan vendors (art, jewelry, clothing, etc.).

Good tip: there's a gourmet mini donut truck off behind the farmers market a bit tucked away. Amazing!

It's nice to take an hour or two before or after a show to walk around and casually stumble on other street performances. Or even go without seeing a play just to snack and shop at the vendors.

The location is absolutely fabulous.
Revise this with your best effort:
Edmonton's annual Fringe Festival is a remarkable event that spans over two weekends, accompanied by an entire week filled with captivating performances. With a multitude of venues and an array of plays to choose from, attendees are guaranteed an unforgettable experience. The festival also boasts an impressive lineup of street performers and musicians, adding to the vibrant atmosphere. Show times, ticket purchases, and artist information can easily be accessed through the festival's comprehensive online schedule.

One extraordinary feature of the Fringe Festival is the closure of half of 104th street, allowing for an expanded space that accommodates a diverse assortment of food vendors and artisan sellers. From delectable treats to unique handmade products such as art, jewelry, and clothing, this vibrant marketplace offers a truly unforgettable shopping experience. Keep an eye out for a hidden gem - a gourmet mini donut truck tucked away behind the farmers market, offering an unparalleled delight.

While attending a play is undoubtedly the main attraction, it is highly recommended to allocate some time before or after the show to leisurely explore the festival grounds. Stumbling upon unexpected street performances or indulging in delectable snacks from the vendors is a delightful way to enhance the overall experience. Even without catching a play, simply meandering through the festival and immersing oneself in the lively ambiance is incredibly rewarding.

Lastly, the festival's location itself is nothing short of exceptional. With its picturesque setting and convenient accessibility, attendees are treated to an enchanting experience that further elevates the allure of the Fringe Festival.

input:
Wow have things changed at this location. I used to come here on a regular basis with a friend. I haven't been back in over a year and so couldn't wait to have lunch today. I was surprised at the deterioration in customer service...,.our server didn't smile, was unwilling to give a recommendation and didn't offer us a tea to go. When I used to come, every server was friendly, gave suggestions and always offered a tea to go. 

The food was okay and probably would have been better if we had been treated better.  I noticed there was tape on the benches where the leather/vinyl is wearing out; this looks tacky.

This used to be my favorite lunch spot; this is no longer the case. I will not be back.
Revise this with your best effort:
I was filled with anticipation as I returned to this location after over a year, reminiscing about the countless times I used to visit with a dear friend. However, upon stepping foot inside, the changes that greeted me were astonishing. The deterioration in customer service left me taken aback. Our server wore a disinterested expression, unwilling to offer any recommendations or even a simple smile. Gone were the days when every server would warmly welcome us, provide thoughtful suggestions, and graciously offer us a tea to savor on our way. 

While the food itself was passable, the experience would have undoubtedly been enhanced had we been treated with more care. Furthermore, my eyes couldn't help but notice the evident signs of wear and tear as I glanced upon the benches. Tape, haphazardly placed to patch the crumbling leather or vinyl, marred the once inviting appearance. This cheap attempt at a quick fix appeared rather tacky.

Regrettably, this once cherished lunch spot has lost its magic. My fond memories of delightful meals and genuine hospitality will no longer be associated with this place. It pains me to declare that I shall not be returning, as the essence that once made it my favorite haunt has vanished.

input:
Got an estimate but went with another plumber as this was the highest quote of the 3 plumbers we interviewed for the job.
Very prompt communication though.

Will re-consider for future jobs.  Seems reliable (and often you get what you pay for!)
Revise this with your best effort: Although we received an estimate from this plumber, we ultimately decided to choose another one because their quote was the highest among the three plumbers we interviewed for the job. However, it is worth mentioning that their communication was consistently prompt and efficient. We will certainly keep them in mind for future plumbing projects, as they appear to be a reliable and professional service provider. As the saying goes, you often get what you pay for.

input: Only the best Mexican food in Florida!!!!  Since the first day I tried it I love it I keep coming back!!!
Revise this with your best effort: Experience the absolute best Mexican food in all of Florida! From the very first bite, I instantly fell in love and I just can't stay away.

input: Real Thai food and they'll make it spicy if you ask for it pet pet. I really like both their soups. The curries have excellent flavor but they can seem runny if you're not used to Thai curries. I'm not super thrilled with the eggrolls but my girlfriend always gets the veggie ones. Perhaps the meat ones are better.
Revise this with your best effort: If you're craving authentic Thai cuisine, look no further as they serve the real deal, and to add some heat, just request it, pet pet. Personally, I find their soups utterly delightful. The curries are bursting with incredible flavors, though they might appear thin to those unaccustomed to Thai curries. While I'm not particularly impressed by the eggrolls, my girlfriend always opts for the veggie ones and seems to enjoy them. It's possible that the meat-filled ones could be more to my liking.

input:
Last May, my wife and I used Jump on the School Bus to take our wedding guests on a winery and brewery tour. They were just amazing, the perfect choice for our pre-wedding wine and beer tour and for wedding transportation between Goleta and the Circle Bar-B Ranch for our guests who stayed in town. Darin and Sierra did a wonderful job communicating with us in Washington, DC as we planned our wedding itinerary. They were flexible about trip times and made last minute adjustments when the number of in-town guests changed suddenly. 

Darin and Sierra have such attention to detail and quality that Darin even stopped by one of the wineries to meet us and to ensure that everything was as expected. Our driver was also extremely knowledgeable about the area and had many good suggestions throughout the day.

We couldn't have picked a better choice for a winery, brewery day tour and wedding day transportation than Jump on the School Bus! I highly recommend them to everyone!
Revise this with your best effort:
My wife and I had the pleasure of using Jump on the School Bus last May for our wedding guests' winery and brewery tour. It was an absolute delight and the perfect choice for our pre-wedding wine and beer excursion, as well as for transporting our guests between Goleta and the Circle Bar-B Ranch for those staying in town. Throughout the entire process, Darin and Sierra impressed us with their exceptional communication skills, even though we were planning our wedding from Washington, DC. They were incredibly accommodating with our trip times and readily adjusted when the number of in-town guests unexpectedly changed.

The level of attention to detail and commitment to excellence from Darin and Sierra was truly remarkable. To ensure everything went smoothly, Darin personally visited one of the wineries to meet us and confirm that everything was as expected. Moreover, our driver possessed a wealth of knowledge about the area and provided us with numerous insightful suggestions throughout the day.

Choosing Jump on the School Bus for our winery and brewery tour, as well as wedding day transportation, was undoubtedly the best decision we made. I highly recommend them to anyone in need of such services.

input:
A great spot to take out-of-town guests. I take all my Chicago friends here and they fall in love. The burgers are incredible and the boozy shakes are like no other. The first time I had horchata shake I honestly had dreams about it for like a week. It's also super centrally located, a quick walk from Wash Ave and other downtown attractions. Great vibe, although I always prefer to get a table upstairs than sit at the community tables on the ground floor.

The burger selection is really, really great. You can pretty much get whatever your heart desires. I've had mac n cheese patties on my burger, you can get a bison burger, turkey burger, literally anything. I have tried a ton and have never been let down by the flavor combinations. The waiters are always super honest, in a good way. If you ask them what's better, X or Y, they're not going to jerk you around and say they're equally good. They'll give you their honest opinion. LOVE that. 

Another unique aspect about Bailey's Range is that they have a burger showdown (can't remember their technical term for it) where last week's featured burger goes up against a new burger recipe. It's a cool call-out that you don't see at a lot of other restaurants. 

The only reason I gave it a 4/5 star instead of 5/5 is because I've had a couple of instances (out of MANY visits, so it's really not alarming or anything) where I requested my burger medium or medium-rare and it turned out a little well done. I still ate it, but it wasn't really what I expected.
Revise this with your best effort:
Bailey's Range is my favorite spot to take out-of-town guests. Every time I bring my Chicago friends here, they instantly fall in love. The burgers are beyond incredible, and the boozy shakes are simply unparalleled. In fact, the first time I tried their horchata shake, I couldn't stop dreaming about it for a whole week. 

Located centrally, a quick stroll from Wash Ave and other downtown attractions, this place offers a fantastic ambiance. Although the community tables on the ground floor are alright, I personally prefer getting a table upstairs for a more intimate experience.

Now, let me tell you about their burger selection. It is absolutely remarkable. You can customize your burger to your heart's content. From mac n cheese patties to bison and turkey burgers, they have it all. I've explored various combinations and I have never been disappointed with the flavors. One thing I truly appreciate is that the waiters are incredibly honest. If you're torn between two choices, they won't shy away from giving you their genuine opinion. And that, my friends, is something I absolutely adore about this place.

Bailey's Range offers a unique burger showdown where they pit last week's featured burger against a new recipe. It's an exciting highlight that sets them apart from other restaurants in town.

Now, I must confess that I gave Bailey's Range a 4 out of 5 stars instead of a perfect score. The reason behind this is a few instances (out of the many times I've visited) where my burger, despite requesting it medium or medium-rare, turned out a bit overcooked. Although it was still enjoyable, it didn't quite meet my expectations. However, let me assure you that it was a rare occurrence and shouldn't alarm anyone.

It will be run through, and you will be charged an overdraft fee."
OH THANK YOU FOR TELLING ME NOW, JERK.

input:
We stayed at the Four Points for 3 nights in November, while here on business.  Nice hotel, and a good experience. 

Check in was a breeze.  We had a good price on the room via my Sheraton/SPG member and AAA discount, which included the free breakfast.  The hotel is literally 5 minutes from the airport, and there are several other hotels right on the same block.

Staff was friendly and helpful.  Room was fine, parking easy, quiet at night.
Revise this with your best effort:
During our business trip in November, my colleagues and I had the pleasure of staying at the Four Points hotel for a total of three nights. Overall, our experience was quite pleasant.

The check-in process was incredibly smooth, allowing us to swiftly settle into our rooms. Thanks to my membership with Sheraton/SPG and the AAA discount, we were able to secure a great price for our accommodations, which also included a complimentary breakfast. Additionally, the hotel's convenient location, a mere five-minute drive from the airport, made our arrival and departure hassle-free. Moreover, there were several other neighboring hotels in the same vicinity.

The hotel staff were attentive, approachable, and always ready to assist us with any queries or requests we had. Our room was comfortable and met our needs perfectly. Parking was a breeze, and we were pleased to find that the hotel maintained a peaceful atmosphere throughout the night, allowing for a restful sleep.

input: Located right at the Union Station Metro stop (walking distance to all of downtown but metro-able too), this place was a good deal on the weekend.  Prices spike during the week when business-peeps fly in and their companies are paying the bill.  The room was clean, the bed was super comfy with TONS of pillows (one sure way to my heart).  The bathroom was large with a tub and too many white towels for two people.  Subtracted one star cause the coffee machine in our room sucked and the door was thin so you could hear people/children in the hall at WAY too early in the morning.  The main lobby is really a cool place tho.  Definitely worth checking out if you're in the area.
Revise this with your best effort: Located conveniently right at the Union Station Metro stop and within walking distance of downtown, this place offers great value for a weekend stay. However, it's important to note that prices tend to increase during the week when business professionals fly in and their companies foot the bill. Nevertheless, the room itself was clean and the bed was incredibly comfortable, adorned with an abundance of plush pillows (a sure way to win my affection). Adding to its appeal, the bathroom was spacious and featured a bathtub, accompanied by an overwhelming supply of white towels (almost too many for just two people). Deducting one star for a disappointing coffee machine in our room and the lack of soundproofing on the door, which unfortunately allowed for early morning disturbances from fellow guests or noisy children in the corridors. On a brighter note, the main lobby exudes a unique and appealing ambiance, making it a must-see if you happen to be in the area.

input:
Super lunch option
Watch out for the yoga mats
You won't miss the meat

Lunch has been very strange for me since HipCity opened. Because here's the thing: I am a meat eater. I mean like my last meal on earth would be a burger. Or, just maybe, the fajita wrap. Because it's that good.

Haven't had everything on the menu yet, but everything I have had has been great. The buffalo bella and crispy hipcity ranch are amazing sandwich alternatives, especially paired with the green lemonade. The groothie is also delicious, and can stand on its own to get you through an afternoon if you only want to spend a few bucks.

Okay suffice it to say that the food is great. The staff is also very friendly, and when they get busy someone will come out along the line and take orders so congestion doesn't get too bad at the register itself.

My only issue with HipCity is that it is at times nearly impossible to figure out where to stand when you're waiting to order or waiting for your food. People kind of convene everywhere and it can get awkward when there's a line out the door. In such a small space it's hard to rectify, but if I see a line out the door I tend to walk on by not because it's a long wait (they're really efficient), it's just difficult to navigate the interior.
Revise this with your best effort:
Upgrade Your Lunch with HipCity: Vegetarian Delights Await!

If you're on the hunt for a satisfying lunch spot, look no further than HipCity. As a self-proclaimed dedicated meat eater, I was initially skeptical. But boy, was I wrong! From the moment I took my first bite, I knew I wouldn't miss the meat.

With every visit, I find myself discovering new favorites on their menu. The buffalo bella and crispy HipCity ranch sandwiches are delightful alternatives to traditional meat options. And when paired with their refreshing green lemonade, it's a match made in lunch heaven. If you're looking for a quick pick-me-up, their groothie is a tasty and budget-friendly option.

What sets HipCity apart, aside from the incredible food, is their friendly staff. Even when they're bustling with customers, they go the extra mile to ensure everyone is taken care of. They'll even come out along the line to take orders, keeping the waiting time minimal.

While there's no denying the quality of their food and service, the only downside is the limited space. Navigating the interior and finding the right place to stand during peak hours can be a challenge. It's not uncommon to see a line stretching out the door. But don't let that deter you - their efficiency means the wait is never as long as it seems.

So, if you're in need of a lunchtime adventure that will delight your taste buds and open your mind to vegetarian options, HipCity is the place to be. Don't miss out on this super lunch option. Just be prepared to watch out for those yoga mats!

input:
This place's posted hours include a 10PM closing time. 

I walked in at 8:30 and, as soon as I got to the counter, the guy said to me "kitchen's closed." The grill, fryers, etc were all being covered up. 

First of all, if your kitchen is closed, why is the door to your restaurant unlocked? 

Secondly, I could see this being the case if I walked in at, say, 9:55PM. But 8:30? That's ridiculous.
Revise this with your best effort:
The posted hours of this establishment indicate a closing time of 10PM. However, upon entering at 8:30, I was promptly informed by the employee behind the counter that the kitchen was closed. To my surprise, I noticed that various cooking appliances such as the grill and fryers were already being covered up. 

My first concern is why the door of the restaurant was unlocked if the kitchen was closed. This seems contradictory and raises questions about the establishment's practices. 

Furthermore, it would have been understandable if I had arrived at the establishment close to the closing time, perhaps around 9:55PM. However, being turned away at 8:30, a good hour and a half before the posted closing time, is highly unreasonable and unexpected.

input:
Rosemary's Grill is my favorite resaurant.  My wife and I take my Mother in law to Rosemary's Grill often for many reasons.  Their menu is extensive.  You can get Classic American food in many categories prepared fresh and delicious with great care and attention to detail that is lacking in common chain restaurants.  You can also get traditional Turkish cuisine that is the very best kebab that I ever had.  Rosemary's is a family owned business and they treat you like you are part of that family.  We are making Rosemary's our Saturday night place.  last weekend my wife and I took my. Mother in law to Rosemary's Grill for dinner.  It was even better that the time before.  I tried the Mixed grill kebab platter.  Lamb, Chicken, Adana, and gyro kebab meats, so tender and expertly spiced and grilled, along with a shepherds salad, grilled half tomatoes, rice, and of course flat bread.  The Adana kebab was particularly tender, juicy, and tasty.  I had never had Adana kebab before and will be ordering it again.  I shared a taste with my Mother in law and she loved it too!  mom in law had crab cakes and she enjoyed them very much.  My wife had the French onion soup, which she raves about and always orders.  She also had the roast turkey, mashed potatoes, cranberry sauce, and corn.  She loved everything on that platter.  She commented that the gravy was especially good.  The portion sizes are huge and we love to have the left overs again at home.  I have honestly not been to a restaurant in the area that has such good quality in all there entrees, sides, salad bar, and drinks, and you have to try the rice pudding.  We have eaten a few times here for breakfast, lunch, and dinner and it continues to be our very favorite place.  The waitstaff and owners make you feel right at home and are warm, welcoming, and friendly.  I can not say enough good things.  

Sent from my iPad
Revise this with your best effort:
Rosemary's Grill is without a doubt my absolute favorite restaurant. Not only do my wife and I frequent this establishment, but we often bring my mother-in-law along for the remarkable dining experience. Because Rosemary's Grill is a family-owned business, you are treated like part of their extended family. It has quickly become our go-to place for a fantastic Saturday night outing. In fact, just last weekend, my wife and I took my mother-in-law to Rosemary's Grill for dinner, and the experience was even better than our previous visits.

On this particular occasion, I decided to indulge in the Mixed Grill Kebab Platter, which featured an assortment of tender lamb, chicken, Adana, and gyro kebab meats, impeccably seasoned and grilled. Along with this delectable assortment, the platter came with a refreshing shepherd's salad, grilled half tomatoes, fragrant rice, and, of course, the essential flatbread. I couldn't help but rave about the tenderness and juiciness of the Adana kebab - a culinary delight I had never experienced before. I even shared a taste with my mother-in-law, who adored it as much as I did.

Meanwhile, my mother-in-law opted for the crab cakes, and they left a lasting impression on her taste buds. As for my wife, she is always enthralled by the French onion soup, a dish she consistently orders. She made sure to mention the exceptional quality of the gravy as well. The waitstaff and owners at Rosemary's Grill truly know how to create a welcoming and homely atmosphere. Their warmth, friendliness, and genuine hospitality truly make all the difference. I simply cannot stress enough how incredible our experiences have been at Rosemary's Grill.

input: If not for the pretentious, haughty, superior attitude of our waiter, I would have given this place four stars or possibly more... Seriously. Revise this with your best effort: If it weren't for the arrogant and disdainful demeanor of our waiter, I would have easily given this place a solid four stars, if not more. I mean, seriously?
