Personally, I indulged in the fried green tomatoes, which were flawlessly seasoned and accompanied by a scrumptious sauce. Regrettably, they arrived after everyone else had already been served. Among my companions, they savored the chicken salad, the fried bologna sandwich, and a mouthwatering cheeseburger. To conclude our delightful dining adventure, we decided to share the peach cobbler dessert, and we were astounded by its delectable taste. I highly recommend savoring it paired with a scoop of ice cream for a truly heavenly experience.

input: Food is good, but the cafe itself is extremely dirty. I will probably not return unless they clean the place up.
Revise this with your best effort: While the food is enjoyable, the cleanliness of the cafe leaves much to be desired. Unless they improve the condition of the establishment, it is unlikely that I will choose to revisit.

input: We really liked this place. Everything we had was delicious. Portions were big. Chicken parm was so yummy. Can't wait to go back and try more stuff !
Revise this with your best effort: We absolutely loved this place! Every single dish we had was beyond delicious. The portions were incredibly generous, and the chicken parm in particular was undeniably yummy. We are already eagerly looking forward to our next visit, as we can't wait to explore and indulge in more of their delectable offerings!

input: not a bad little burger joint. i got the bacon cheeseburger. bacon was cooked perfect and had the perfect thickness. bun had a really great toasted crust. fries were good, as well as the chocolate shake I had. 3 complaints, i wish the burger was more juicy, I wish I wasn't paying so much for the tiny burger portion I was served, and I wish I didn't leave the place smelling like burger grease.
Revise this with your best effort:
This burger joint is actually quite decent. I decided to go for the bacon cheeseburger, and I must say, the bacon was cooked to perfection with just the right thickness. The bun had a wonderfully toasted crust that added a delightful touch to the overall experience. Additionally, the fries were tasty, and the chocolate shake I had was satisfying.

However, I do have a few minor complaints. Firstly, I wish the burger itself was more juicy, as this would have elevated the taste even further. Secondly, I couldn't help but feel slightly disappointed by the relatively small portion size of the burger, especially considering the price I paid. Lastly, I left the place with an unfortunate lingering smell of burger grease, which was not exactly pleasant.

Overall, while not without its flaws, this burger joint offers a delightful experience with its perfectly cooked bacon, crispy bun, and satisfactory sides.

input: So I decided to give this place a shot after reading all the reviews on yelp. The place was dead but I have it a shot. The food was okay at best. I actually left there and went across the street to Charlie's. The place was packed and one bite of the redtop pizza and I cursed myself for not coming here first. If you want a sit down meal this place is nice. If you want good pizza go to Charlie's.
Revise this with your best effort: After carefully analyzing the reviews on Yelp, I made the spontaneous decision to try out this place. Upon arrival, I couldn't help but notice the lack of customers, but I decided to give it a chance nonetheless. The food, while adequate, did not exceed my expectations. That being said, I soon found myself leaving and heading across the street to Charlie's. The bustling atmosphere and the very first bite of their remarkable redtop pizza made me regret not choosing it initially. If you're seeking a comfortable sit-down dining experience, this place would suffice. However, for truly exceptional pizza, I highly recommend Charlie's.

input:
We've been shopping here since this location was a Wild Oats. Perhaps I'm just imagining things, but I'd swear it has gotten better since the merger of these two chains.

I love the produce, seafood and cheese here. But it's the personal care section with tons o' natural cosmetics, handmade soaps and the like that brings us in most often. Well, that and the salad bar. In the cooler months, nothing beats hitting Whole Foods for a post-yoga lunch of soup and salad or the deli salad sampler plate. The Carrot Ginger, Split Pea and Corn Chowder soups are the best! Other sure bets: the curried tofu salad (or pretty much any of the deli-made tofu items), sushi to-go boxes and the everything cookies. My most recent find: lavender soda - kinda' dry and really does relax you :-)
Revise this with your best effort:
We have been loyal customers of this store since before it was known as Wild Oats. It may just be in my head, but I could swear that the quality has improved ever since the merger of these two chains.

What I absolutely adore about this place are their fresh produce, seafood, and cheese. However, what truly entices us to visit frequently is their personal care section, filled with a wide variety of natural cosmetics and handmade soaps. And of course, I can't forget to mention the irresistible salad bar. During the cooler months, there is nothing more satisfying than stopping by Whole Foods for a refreshing post-yoga lunch consisting of soup and salad, or even their delightful deli salad sampler plate. Trust me when I say that the Carrot Ginger, Split Pea, and Corn Chowder soups are absolutely divine. If you're looking for reliable choices, you can never go wrong with their curried tofu salad, any of their deli-made tofu items, sushi to-go boxes, or their delectable everything cookies.

Recently, I made a delightful discovery - lavender soda. It has a slightly dry taste to it and genuinely helps with relaxation.

input: OMG the Mediterranean chicken quesadillas what awesome sauce. Definitely recommend to anyone who enjoys fresh Greek food
Revise this with your best effort: OMG, the Mediterranean chicken quesadillas are simply incredible! They are packed with flavors and the combination of ingredients is like magic. These quesadillas are a must-try for anyone who appreciates the vibrant and delicious taste of Greek cuisine. Trust me, you won't be disappointed!

input: So so in love with this place & it is gorgeous. A very spacious & modern design & most of all CLEAN!!!! Love Will, Amanda & Sal! I have made several purchases to include some mods and atty's and being a newbie I have issues from time to time with the devices. Not because the devices aren't working but I may take something apart and can't figure out how to put it back together (newbie ish) lol They always help me and get me back to vaping!!! They have a wide variety of juices, mods, atty's and i'm always in there tasting something. You've got to try it! You will not be sorry! In love with this spot!
Revise this with your best effort: I am absolutely infatuated with this place; it is undeniably stunning. The design is incredibly spacious and modern, and above all else, it is meticulously clean! Will, Amanda, and Sal, you guys are amazing! I have made numerous purchases here, including modifications and atomizers. As a newcomer to the vaping world, I occasionally struggle with operating my devices, not because they are faulty, but because I sometimes take them apart and struggle to put them back together (still getting the hang of it, haha). However, the staff always comes to my rescue and swiftly gets me back to vaping smoothly. Their selection of juices, mods, and atomizers is extensive, and I find myself consistently exploring new flavors in their shop. Trust me, you absolutely have to give it a try! You won't regret it. I am head over heels for this place!

input: So this is what you need to know. Everything taste great, well at least what I had. I practically tried everything for breakfast and have come to the conclusion that this is the spot for breakfast. I have one gripe though, the monte cisto is not worth the price and is way over priced. I know truffle oil is used but that should not be the reason its so damn expensive. one egg, one piece of toast and some sauce. Don't ever order it, not worth it unless they drop the price $5. everything else is worth it taste great. Jebbs open face and the huevos rancheros are my favs. Enjoy. oh and the coffee is addicting. Also there are no reservations, so get there early or go about 30 min before u think u may be hungry.
Revise this with your best effort:
Here is my revised version:

Let me give you the lowdown. The food here is absolutely delicious, well, at least in my experience. I've tried nearly everything on their breakfast menu and, hands down, this place is the go-to spot for breakfast. However, there's one thing that leaves me dissatisfied – the Monte Cristo. It simply isn't worth the steep price tag, even with the fancy truffle oil. Seriously, it's just one egg, a piece of toast, and some sauce. I suggest avoiding it unless they decide to slash the price by $5. On the bright side, everything else on the menu is worth every penny and tastes amazing. Personally, I adore the Jebbs open face and the huevos rancheros. Make sure to indulge in their addicting coffee too. Just a heads up, this place doesn't take reservations, so either arrive early or allow yourself a 30-minute cushion before hunger strikes. Enjoy your meal!

input: Only had one experience with this place and it will be my last. I called in the night before to ask if they sell deboned duck and the man on the phone said they could but I would have to request it the day of. I called the following morning to ask to pick up a plain deboned duck and whoever the incompetent girl who answered had trouble getting my order clear. I picked up my order and came home to find that not only did they gave a whole duck with stuffing I never asked for. I called the place back and thy never offered any compensation of any sort except a trade in right as it's a hour before dinner time and the butcher shop is more than thirty minutes away for me. Shame that food from this place is overshadowed by their terrible customer service.
Revise this with your best effort:
My only interaction with this establishment left me extremely dissatisfied, to the point where I have no intention of returning. Initially, I called the night before to inquire about the availability of deboned duck. The man who answered assured me they had it, but mentioned that I would need to make the request on the day of my visit. The following morning, I called again to place an order for a plain deboned duck. Unfortunately, the individual who answered the phone seemed completely inept, as they struggled to understand and process my order correctly. Despite this, I decided to go ahead and pick up the duck.

To my dismay, when I arrived home, I discovered that they had given me a whole duck with stuffing, even though I had specifically requested a plain deboned duck. Frustrated with the mix-up, I promptly contacted the establishment to voice my concern. However, their response was far from satisfactory. They neither offered compensation nor attempted to make amends for their mistake. Instead, they simply suggested a trade-in. This was highly inconvenient, as it happened to be just an hour before dinner, and their butcher shop was over thirty minutes away from my location.

It is truly unfortunate that the poor customer service overshadowed the quality of their food.

input:
Visited the preserve today based on reviews and was VERY pleased.  

The hikes are great! Lots of wildlife and nature to see on clearly marked paths. 
The birds of prey aviary is wonderful and the learning center not only presents educational information in a beautiful manner, but the AC was a nice break after the hike.  

If you make your way over in the mid afternoon you may be lucky enough to see the birds up close with the handlers. 

All the staff and volunteers are friendly and helpful.
Revise this with your best effort:
Today, I had the pleasure of visiting the preserve, and I must say, I was thoroughly impressed. The positive reviews I had come across were certainly well-deserved.

The hiking trails provided a fantastic experience, boasting an abundance of captivating wildlife and picturesque scenery. I was particularly delighted by the meticulously marked paths, which made navigating through the preserve a breeze.

One of the highlights of my visit was the birds of prey aviary. It was truly a sight to behold, offering an incredible opportunity to closely observe these magnificent creatures. Additionally, the learning center exceeded my expectations, not only imparting valuable educational information but also enveloping visitors in a visually stunning environment. As an added bonus, the air conditioning in the learning center provided a much-needed reprieve after a long hike.

For those fortunate enough to visit in the mid-afternoon, there is a chance to witness the birds up close during interactive sessions with the skilled handlers. It is an experience that should not be missed.

Lastly, I cannot praise the staff and volunteers enough for their warmth and helpfulness. Their friendly demeanor and willingness to assist enhanced my overall experience at the preserve.

All in all, the preserve offers a memorable and enriching outing, where nature and wildlife truly come alive.

input: One of the few diners in North Wilmington, and the only one that probably isn't really bad. I've had totally ordinary diner fare here, and used to come by after swim meets. Nothing particularly good or bad about this place.
Revise this with your best effort: Located in North Wilmington, this diner stands out as one of the rare options in the area that consistently delivers decent food. While it might not wow you with exceptional flavors, it remains a reliable choice for satisfying diner fare. In the past, I would often swing by after swim meets, appreciating its standard offerings that neither exceeded nor disappointed my expectations. Overall, this place lacks any outstanding features, but it also manages to avoid any glaring shortcomings.

input: We loved the food, service and decor! The minute we walked in for a late lunch we were greeted with a huge smile and a warm welcome from the manager. Our server, Christina (i think that was her name) was delightful. The beer selection was great. We had the chicken rabe sandwhich and pepperoni pizza. The sandwhich was very good, on tasty foccacia bread. The pizza was superb!  We love the "well done" taste. We will definately be back. One problem we may have is our 7 year old is very picky and we didn't see a chidren's menu.
Revise this with your best effort:
We were absolutely impressed with our dining experience at your establishment. From the moment we stepped foot inside for a late lunch, we were met with exemplary hospitality, captivating decor, and mouthwatering cuisine. The manager warmly greeted us with a beaming smile, instantly making us feel valued and appreciated. Our server, Christina (apologies if we misremembered her name), was an absolute delight throughout our meal.

The beer selection was exceptional, providing us with a wide variety of options to choose from. Our taste buds were truly tantalized as we savored every bite of our delectable chicken rabe sandwich and pepperoni pizza. The sandwich, served on a scrumptious focaccia bread, was bursting with flavors that left us thoroughly satisfied. As for the pizza, it was nothing short of superb! The "well done" taste truly elevated our dining experience to new heights.

We were so enamored with our visit that we most certainly plan on returning again in the future. However, we do have one minor concern that we would like to bring to your attention. Our 7-year-old daughter tends to be quite selective when it comes to her meals, and regrettably, we did not observe a children's menu during our visit.

In conclusion, we cannot express enough how much we appreciated the remarkable food, exceptional service, and captivating ambiance of your establishment. It is truly a hidden gem that we are excited to revisit. We kindly request that you consider incorporating a children's menu option to cater to families like ours. Thank you once again for providing us with an unforgettable dining experience.

input:
I regularly go to student salons for hair cuts and styling. 

I have long, fine, mostly straight Asian hair, and have had mixed results from the Aveda Institute -- to be expected considering I had a different stylist in every case.

Just know that if you haven't had a student stylist before, don't expect perfection. Do expect the cut to take an inordinately long time compared to a seasoned professional -- most of my cuts/styles have taken around 2 hours. The basic cut price includes massaging wash, cut, and blowdry style, plus the stylists do take the time to check in with their teachers and make sure the cut is going the way you want it to. Another plus: all of the stylists I've had at the Aveda Institute have been professional and committed to their service, which isn't always the case at other schools. And the prices are right.
Revise this with your best effort:
I frequently visit student salons for my haircuts and styling needs. As someone with long, fine, predominantly straight Asian hair, my experiences at the Aveda Institute have been a mixed bag, simply because I've had different stylists each time.

It's important to keep in mind that perfection shouldn't be expected when dealing with student stylists. However, what you can expect is an unusually long duration for your cut compared to a seasoned professional. Most of my cuts and styles have taken approximately 2 hours. The basic cut price includes a luxurious massaging wash, cut, and blowdry style. Additionally, the stylists make sure to consult their teachers and ensure that the cut is progressing to your liking. 

On a positive note, all of the stylists I've encountered at the Aveda Institute have displayed professionalism and a dedicated attitude towards their craft, which is not always the case at other educational institutions. Moreover, the prices for the services provided are quite reasonable.

input:

input: Great food and friendly service. I will definitely be back. Menu variety is great.  I had the Monte Cristo crepes, absolutely amazing

input:
A nice alternative to Cafe du Monde, the beignets were as good if not better. But the real kicker was NO line! 

It was a calm little oasis on Bourbon St. Granted at 8:30 am the street is empty besides garbage men & street washers.

We were there early on a holiday, so we didn't get to experience any live music, sadly.

We did have a full breakfast as well, sharing a crawfish omelet & Cajun hashbrowns. Neither was anything to write home about, but really when your name has Beignet in it, does the other stuff really matter?
Revise this with your best effort:
A delightful alternative to Cafe du Monde, the beignets at this place were just as exceptional, if not better. What made it even more impressive was the absence of any lines! Located on Bourbon St., it provided a serene and peaceful escape amidst the hustle and bustle. Of course, the early hour of 8:30 am meant the street was practically deserted, except for a few dedicated garbage collectors and street cleaners.

Unfortunately, due to visiting on a holiday, we missed out on the chance to enjoy live music, which was a bit of a letdown.

Nevertheless, we made the most of our visit by indulging in a fulfilling breakfast. We decided to share a scrumptious crawfish omelet and some flavorful Cajun hashbrowns. While they were nothing extraordinary, it's fair to say that when a place's name includes "Beignet," does anything else really matter?

input: Not the best prepared sushi inthe city by a longshot, but for quick (and I mean quick), cheap sushi with a long menu, Mixx is great.
Revise this with your best effort: While it may not claim the title of being the finest prepared sushi in the city, Mixx undeniably excels in offering prompt and affordable sushi options with an extensive menu selection.

input: Completely unprofessional and pathetic. I called last week to get price quotes on a battery and brakes. I spoke to someone very nice- he gave me two quotes, fairly low but close to other shops. Then I told him I'd like to speak to someone else and he says "no, we won't do a battery for that price, so bye-bye" and he HUNG up the phone. NEVER NEVER call these people. Revise this with your best effort: Completely unprofessional and disappointing. I reached out last week to inquire about pricing for a battery and brakes. The person I initially spoke with was pleasant and provided me with two quotes that were slightly lower but comparable to other shops. Today, when I called to schedule an appointment, an individual who identified himself as either Mike or Nick (although I have no interest in his name) rudely informed me that there was no battery available at the price previously quoted. Instead of taking responsibility, he immediately shifted blame to me, stating, "I have no idea how you arrived at that price." Upon expressing my desire to speak with someone else, he abruptly replied, "No, we can't provide a battery at that price. Goodbye," and promptly ended the call. I strongly advise against contacting this establishment. I would rather go to Walmart than have any dealings with these individuals.

input:
I would NOT recommend this place to anyone. Their biggest mistake is not having a customer service department. They rely on their sales team to provide customer service meaning every time you call in to try and get something done, you get put into a voicemail because the sales guy is out selling - which should be their only job. This left me on numerous occassions incredibly frustrated that I could not get an answer. I even left the manager a voicemail (big surprise I couldn't get them to answer) and they never had the decency to call me back - Just made my sales person call me back.

I purchased my car last July and was promised numerous things would be done to the car before I purchased it. One of which being the tint on the rear window would be removed as the view out of the back was blurry. Somehow, that passed thru inspection and when I came to sign the papers, I noticed that it was still on the back windshield. I was told that they would have it removed by the time we were done the paperwork. Also, I was told that the price was going to be higher than the original agreement because the sales manager did the math wrong the previous day when we ran numbers. I told him that wasn't my fault and I would only pay the agreed upon amount and he spoke with the manager and got it sorted out. 

After sitting in the office for 2.5 hours, they finally told me that they were unable to even start taking off the tint and I would have to bring the car back. I dropped it off that Friday and let them keep it for the weekend. My sales guy called me on Saturday night to tell me that they never got to finish it and I would have to bring it back again and leave it. I live 45 minutes from the dealership so this isn't something I can easily do. I insisted on them giving me a loaner car for whatever day they would do this as I was sure this wouldn't be a one day process from my previous experience. 2.5 weeks later they were able to provide me with said car and I dropped off my vehicle. When I went to pick up my "finished car" there was still tint left on the bottom of the windshield. 

After all of that I knew I would never bring my car back for service there if that's the kind of service they provide. Now with all the rain we've been having, my trunk is leaking and when I called to check with the service department to see if it would be covered under warranty, I got the same run around with the service department who just said "I don't know" - OK well give me someone who will be able to tell me. Once they forwarded me to the correct person, I again got "I don't know". We need you to bring it in and look at it then submit to our warranty company to see if it gets accepted. No thanks after my previous experience of bringing my car in there to get "serviced". 

Invest in a customer service department to handle complaints in a professional and timely matter. This should not in any way be left upon the sales department to do. My sales guy did the best he could and I appreciated the help he gave me, but no one else would help me throughout the entire process. Not a good look on managements part.
Revise this with your best effort:
I would strongly discourage recommending this establishment to anyone. Their lack of a customer service department is their biggest flaw. Instead, they rely on their sales team to handle customer inquiries, resulting in voicemails and frustration when attempting to get assistance. Even leaving a voicemail for the manager yielded no response, forcing them to make my salesperson contact me.

When I purchased my car last July, I was assured that certain things would be taken care of before the purchase. One such promise was the removal of tint from the rear window, as it obstructed the view. However, despite this concern passing inspection, the tint remained on the windshield when I came in to sign the papers. I was informed that it would be removed during the paperwork process, but after spending 2.5 hours in the office, they informed me that they were unable to start the removal and I would have to return with the car. I left the vehicle at the dealership for the weekend, only for them to inform me that it still hadn't been finished and I needed to bring it back again. Since I live 45 minutes away, this was quite inconvenient. I insisted on receiving a loaner car for the duration of this process, as my prior experience indicated it wouldn't be a one-day task. Eventually, after 2.5 weeks, they provided me with a loaner car and I dropped off my vehicle. However, when I collected my "finished car," there was still leftover tint on the bottom of the windshield.

Given this experience, I decided to never return to their service department. When I contacted them to inquire about potential warranty coverage for a leaking trunk caused by the recent rain, I received the same unhelpful responses from the service department, with a simple "I don't know." I requested to speak to someone who could provide more information, but even then, I was met with another "I don't know." Their proposal was for me to bring in the car for inspection and then submit it to the warranty company for consideration. Considering my previous experience with their service, I declined this offer.

It is crucial for them to invest in a dedicated customer service department to address complaints professionally and promptly. This responsibility should not fall to the sales department. While I appreciate the efforts made by my salesperson, no one else offered any assistance throughout the entire process. This lack of support reflects poorly on the management.

input: I love this restaurant. The owners are the nicest family. The food is delicious!!. My favorite is bacon pizza. I love that there is a play room for my kids to play while we wait for our food.
Revise this with your best effort: I absolutely adore this restaurant! The owners, who happen to be the friendliest family, create such a welcoming atmosphere. Moreover, the food is beyond delicious! What's even better is that they have a splendid play room where my kids can have a blast while we patiently await our scrumptious meal.

input: Omg this is sooooo good, the fried rice is gorgeous,   Good price good food, one of the best Asian restaurant on the town.

input:
Harry's blue bell is a nice spot. We stopped a few days ago for a quick dinner. It's tucked in the corner of a shopping center and it's very easy to miss. It was packed and seemed like the place to be for locals. The inside is nice but small, only a few tables in the entire place. The service was just okay. 

The beer selection is very good as are the prices on the beer. The food menu was a bit limited with you're basic bar food. The wife went with the bbq pulled pork and I went with the chicken and honey mustard wrap. The bbq pork was good, the bun was nicely toasted but the sauce was overly sweet for our liking. The wrap was fresh and good but nothing spectacular. The fries were hot and crispy. The kale slaw was fantastic but a very small portion.

Overall it was a decent meal. I wouldn't go out of my way to go back. If I were in the area I'd stop though. Solid 3 stars.
Revise this with your best effort:
Harry's blue bell is a delightful gem that we stumbled upon during a recent outing. Nestled discreetly in a corner of a shopping center, this hidden locale exudes an understated charm that is easily overlooked. However, its popularity among the locals was immediately evident as the restaurant was filled to the brim. 

With its cozy interior, Harry's blue bell offers only a handful of tables, creating an intimate atmosphere. While the service was satisfactory, it didn't quite exceed our expectations. 

One aspect that left a lasting impression was the remarkable beer selection, boasting a variety that would appease even the most discerning palate. Moreover, the prices on the beer were quite reasonable, making it even more appealing.

On the culinary front, the food menu was slightly limited, offering your typical bar food options. My wife opted for the bbq pulled pork, which was accompanied by a beautifully toasted bun. However, the sauce, while flavorful, leaned towards an overwhelming sweetness that wasn't to our taste. As for myself, I indulged in the chicken and honey mustard wrap, which was fresh and satisfying, albeit lacking a wow factor. The fries served alongside were perfectly crispy and piping hot. Additionally, the kale slaw was a standout, albeit it arrived in a disappointingly meager portion.

In summary, our dining experience at Harry's blue bell was decent, although it didn't quite compel us to make a special trip back. However, were we in the vicinity, we would certainly consider stopping by again. All in all, a solid three-star establishment.

input: Just an update regarding the only complaint in my first review of Kajuns: the smoke. They've since installed a couple of smoke eaters that have made the air extremely breathable for people who, like me, have sensitivities to cigarette smoke. I previously would get headaches because of the smoke if I stayed at Kajuns too long, as I am wont to do, but now I can hardly notice that people are smoking while I'm sitting inside the bar! (When I leave, it's a different story as my clothes still smell like smoke, but that's a compromise I am willing to make.) Just goes to show you how dedicated the Kajuns staff is to improving the experiences of their customers. Thank you Kajuns!
Revise this with your best effort:
I wanted to provide an update regarding the one complaint I mentioned in my initial review of Kajuns: the smoke. I'm pleased to share that they have taken steps to address this issue by installing a couple of smoke eaters. These devices have greatly improved the air quality, making it much more breathable for individuals like me who are sensitive to cigarette smoke.

Previously, I would often develop headaches if I stayed at Kajuns for an extended period, which is something I tend to do. However, I am now pleasantly surprised by how minimal the presence of smoke is while sitting inside the bar. It's almost as if people are not smoking at all! I do need to mention that when I leave, my clothes still retain some lingering smoke smell, but I can understand and accept this compromise.

This update demonstrates the dedication of the Kajuns staff to enhancing the overall experience for their customers. I sincerely appreciate their efforts in addressing the smoke issue and thank you, Kajuns, for taking this step towards creating a more enjoyable environment.

input: My friends at work (connoisseurs of good food in the St. Louis area) introduced me to yet another very nice restaurant and that's Brio's!! input: One of the worst places in Tucson!  Cold food , rude service. They have the right idea but fail to deliver
Revise this with your best effort: This is one of the most disappointing establishments in Tucson. The food is consistently served cold, and the service is incredibly rude. Although they seem to have a promising concept, their execution falls drastically short.

input:
I am a huge fan of Gennaro's. It's got a thin crust, sweet and rich tomato sauce along w fresh mozzarella cheese. Also, the meatballs are excellent. Can't say enough about how much I love it here. Also, the decor is vintage and adorable. 

I have yet to be disappointed with Gennaro's
Revise this with your best effort: I am an avid admirer of Gennaro's. The thin crust, adorned with a splendid combination of sweet and delectable tomato sauce, paired with fresh mozzarella cheese, never fails to impress me. Additionally, the meatballs offered at this establishment are truly outstanding. Words cannot express the deep affection I have for this place. Furthermore, the vintage and charming decor only adds to its allure. Without a doubt, Gennaro's has continuously exceeded my expectations, leaving me eagerly anticipating my next visit.

input:
Stopped in on a Monday around 7pm and the place was pretty full.  The bartender was friendly and attentive.  The bar seemed well stocked, not a drinker so take that as you will.  Now the food...THE FOOD was fantastic!  I ordered the Pear Gorgonzola Melt.  How they fit all that amazingness on one plate is impressive.  The clientele is all ages and backgrounds, which is great.

Nutshell:  Definitely check this place out for a good sandwich at a good price (~$10) and to catch up on the footy games.
Revise this with your best effort:
I visited this place on a bustling Monday evening at around 7pm and was pleased to see it filled with customers. The bartender was cordial and provided attentive service throughout my visit. From my observations, the bar was well-stocked, although I cannot personally attest to the quality of the alcoholic beverages. 

Now, let's talk about the real highlight - the food. It was absolutely remarkable! I opted for the Pear Gorgonzola Melt, and I must applaud the kitchen for fitting such an incredible combination of flavors onto one plate. It was truly impressive. One thing worth noting is the diverse clientele that frequents this establishment. People of all ages and backgrounds can be found here, which adds a welcoming and inclusive atmosphere.

To summarize, I highly recommend checking out this place for a delicious sandwich priced at around $10. It's also an ideal spot to catch up on the latest footy games.

input: Great atmosphere, service was very friendly and prices were very reasonable however I found the food a bit bland, not bad just bland. My husband and I were starving after a long drive to Philly and this filled the spot but it wasn't overly enjoyable and we most likely won't be back.
Revise this with your best effort: The restaurant had a pleasant ambiance, with a friendly and attentive service team. Additionally, their prices were quite reasonable. However, I must admit that I found the food to be somewhat lacking in flavor. Not necessarily terrible, just lacking that extra punch of taste. Considering our famished state after a long drive to Philadelphia, this meal did satisfy our hunger to some extent. However, it didn't leave us overly satisfied or particularly eager to return in the future.

input: Great place for a drink, nice friendly staff.  Didn't eat there though and would be hesitant to as it doesn't look to be the cleanest place.
Revise this with your best effort: This place is a gem for grabbing a drink, thanks to its wonderful atmosphere and incredibly friendly staff. However, I must admit that I didn't have a chance to try their food, and I would approach with caution as the cleanliness of the establishment doesn't seem to be top-notch.

input:
Freedom toast = check, freedom fries = check, awesome breakfast food = check.

The is a greek owned pancake house (hence the over doing it on naming the food) and is a great alternative to your larger chain pancake houses such as Robert Evans, IHopity hop, and Mr. Dennys. 

We eat here every new years day, typically around 2 pm when we drag ourselves out of a drunken slumber to brave the bitter cold. They never have a problem seating our group of about 12-15 and are pleasant and quick service. 

The energetic owner likes to roam around making sure everything is going well. In my opinion, the food is also better than the chains. The secret ingredient is love.
Revise this with your best effort:
This Greek-owned pancake house goes above and beyond when it comes to naming their food, offering not only Freedom toast and Freedom fries, but also an array of awesome breakfast options. If you're tired of the typical chain pancake houses like Robert Evans, IHopity hop, and Mr. Dennys, this place is a fantastic alternative.

Our go-to spot every New Year's Day, we stumble in around 2 pm, still recovering from a night of indulgence and facing the harsh cold. Despite our large group of 12-15, the staff never has a problem seating us, providing pleasant and speedy service.

The owner, full of energy, can often be found ensuring everything is running smoothly. And in my opinion, the food here surpasses that of the chain restaurants. There's a secret ingredient in every dish - love.

input:
After going there several times going to Fresh I am sad to report my last visit was not up to par.  I went with a group of people and the service / product was not how it used to be and the price was outrageous to say the least.  I entered and was not greet by the staff  and I do understand that the group I was meeting with was taking up most the inside of Fresh, but a little acknowledgement would have went a long way. After realizing the price for the drink I was put off by ordering any products.

Revise this with your best effort: Unfortunately, my most recent visit to Fresh was disappointing. Despite being a frequent patron, the service and quality of the products fell short this time, and the exorbitant price was hard to overlook. Upon entering, I was not greeted by the staff. While I understand that my group was occupying most of the space, a small acknowledgment would have made a difference. Additionally, I ordered a Vienna Latte with an extra shot, which turned out to be one of the worst espresso-based drinks I have ever tasted. The price, at over $7 for a coffee, was exasperating. The realization of the high cost left me hesitant to order any further items. It saddens me to recount this negative experience at a place I genuinely love, as my previous comments have attested. However, this time was one of the worst encounters I have had at Fresh.

input:
We have big group of 12 for the office outing lunch. I would said for the number of people we have, the service is not the best but good enough. Only one of our members get the food late. The close out may need to work on it. Tip was added since we have large group which may my bill easy. 

I have order the lamb kebab (Shish Kebab) plate. It come with two choices of side. I got the rice and the babaghanoush. The rice was well cook and nice aroma. The babaghanoush was well prepared and great with extra olive oil. The presentation of the dish is pleasant. However, the meat did not measured up. It was too dry and the marinated is not over the top. They need to improve on this area. 

I have been here several time. My previous experience is better. During the month of Ramadan, they serve the buffet that are plenty of choices and attractive. I would said try them during this time. The buffet of Ramadan usually start at 8:30. Go early because is a lot of customers.
Revise this with your best effort:
We have a large group of 12 for our office outing lunch. Considering the number of people, the service was decent, although one member of our group did have a delay receiving their food. The close out process could use some improvement as well. We appreciated the added tip since we were a large group, which made the bill easier to handle. 

I decided to order the lamb kebab (Shish Kebab) plate, which came with two side choices. I chose the rice and babaghanoush. The rice was cooked perfectly and had a delightful aroma. The babaghanoush was well-prepared and tasted excellent with the additional olive oil. The presentation of the dish was also quite appealing. However, the meat fell short. It was dry and lacked the strong marinade flavors. This is an area they should focus on improving.

I have visited this restaurant several times before, and my previous experiences were better. During the month of Ramadan, they offer a buffet with plenty of choices that are quite appealing. I would recommend trying them during this time. The Ramadan buffet usually begins at 8:30, but make sure to arrive early due to the high volume of customers.

input:
This was a cool place to stop by and check out the birds on a Sunday morning.

If you're a bird person this is the place to go.

input: So it's an old club and I think it still maybe a club at night but me and my family including our 5 year old went there for dinner! Revise this with your best effort: So it's an old establishment, and although it may still function as a club at night, my family and I, including our 5-year-old, decided to try it out for dinner. The food exceeded our expectations, particularly the sashimi plate which left us extremely satisfied. My son opted for a classic burger and fries, and he thoroughly enjoyed his meal as well. However, I must address the abysmal service we experienced. It was truly disappointing. I found myself having to fetch our own plates, sauce bowls, and napkins, and to make matters worse, they only brought out two glasses, neglecting to provide my son with one. I had to specifically request a glass for him, as if they were oblivious to his presence. Despite all this, thanks to a groupon certificate, we were able to enjoy a pleasant dinner. However, I would only consider returning if the service improved significantly.

input:
This review is mainly chicken talk as Cuenelli's Peruvian Style Rotisserie Chicken brings to the table. Pollo a la brasa.... Rotisserie chicken.... Whatever you wanna call it.... I call it a technique done here with love and pride. Lets be clear, you will find no comparison coming from your grocer deli section or at the checkout isle.

Why do I think this chicken have some TLC put into it? On biting down of this chicken you can note seasoning flavors down to the bone. This is an inclination that prior to even getting into the rotisserie oven, these birds spend some time in some form of marinating process. Building flavor, the chicken also has a seasoning rub all over the skin.

Lets go to this rotisserie oven. Another unique element is this oven has a charcoal or grill like component. This gives the chicken a smoky element in the flavor build. As these birds turn in this oven, they keep moist from the natural drippings dropping from bird to bird as they rotate through this oven. In turn, this a reason why some people may note some pieces the skin end up dry and crispy and others get moist or soggy skin on their chicken In the end, you end up with this tender, smoky, well seasoned, fall off the bone goodness. Wait.... how can they add more flavor? Cuenelli's serves it with two dipping sauces, a chimichurri  which gives a herbaceous and slightly spicy flavor, and an aioli which has a garlicky - lemony element.

Round out this meal with some solid sides. Must haves for me would be the cilantro rice. Another herbaceous addition that works well with this meal. I got to use the word herbaceous a few times in this review, it has reflects such great imagery for food talk:) Must have beans with rice no? I pick the spicy pinto beans over the black beans at this establishment but lets be clear these beans are pretty spicy. I also love the maduros here. These sweet plantatains are cooked to perfection where the outsides has this caramelization from the natural sugar of the sweet plantain, leaving you with this toffee-like, stick to your tooth exterior and soft and sweet interior. 

Wash all down with Inca cola or a bottle of chicha limena.  Inca cola is almost like a cola champagne or a cream soda type of drink. Chicha Limena I say is Christmas in a bottle. This juice has a floral base blended with cinnamon and cloves.

Though Cuenelli's Peruvian Style Rotisserie Chicken have many other notable Latin dishes, the one thing that comes to mind to me is this chicken made with love. This chicken gives new meaning to all who thought they knew what rotisserie chicken is. I say, go to Cuenelli's and taste again for the very first time.
Revise this with your best effort:
Let's dive into Cuenelli's Peruvian Style Rotisserie Chicken, a true chicken masterpiece. Whether you refer to it as pollo a la brasa or rotisserie chicken, one thing is certain - this technique is executed with passion and pride. Prepare yourself, as a trip to your grocer's deli section or the checkout aisle simply cannot rival this culinary experience.

Why do I believe this chicken receives tender loving care? With each bite, you can taste the intricate flavors that penetrate every inch, down to the bone. It's evident that these birds have undergone a meticulous marinating process before reaching the rotisserie oven. Not only that, but the chicken is coated in a delightful seasoning rub, enhancing its already seasoned profile.

Enter the rotisserie oven, boasting a unique charcoal or grill component. This ingenious addition infuses the chicken with a hint of smokiness that elevates its flavor profile. As these juicy birds rotate within the oven, the natural drippings cascade from one to another, ensuring their moistness. Consequently, some may find certain pieces with crispy, dry skin while others are blessed with tender, moist skin. Ultimately, you're left with succulent, well-seasoned chicken that falls off the bone effortlessly. But wait, there's more! Cuenelli's serves their culinary masterpiece with two delectable dipping sauces - a herbaceous and slightly spicy chimichurri and a garlic-lemon infused aioli.

Now, let's complement this outstanding dish with some remarkable sides. A must-have for me is their cilantro rice, which perfectly harmonizes with the chicken. I can't help but emphasize the herbaceous nature of this rice; it truly brings you into a vivid world of flavors. Of course, no meal is complete without beans and rice. At Cuenelli's, I gravitate towards the spicy pinto beans, although it's important to note that they pack quite a fiery punch. Additionally, I highly recommend indulging in their maduros. These caramelized sweet plantains boast a divine toffee-like exterior and a tender, sweet interior.

Quench your thirst with Inca cola or a bottle of chicha limena. Inca cola can only be described as a cola champagne or a cream soda-like elixir. On the other hand, chicha limena is akin to a bottled Christmas. This juice enchants your senses with its floral base, infused with hints of cinnamon and cloves.

Although Cuenelli's Peruvian Style Rotisserie Chicken offers a myriad of remarkable Latin dishes, it is undoubtedly the chicken that steals the show. This extraordinary creation redefines what rotisserie chicken can be. I implore you to visit Cuenelli's and rediscover the true essence of this beloved dish. Prepare to embark on an unforgettable culinary journey.

input: fuck yes. meat, bourbon libations, and a salad (to round things out aka make myself feel better about ingesting the aforementioned two items.) i took myself on an early birthday date with myself and was not disappointed (neither in the food nor the company). i had a medium rare plain burger to see if it was worth all the fuss...no cheese, bacon, dressing, etc to disguise the quality of the meat. (of course, no bread either since i'm gluten free.) the burger was great - perfectly cooked and seasoned... though, i felt like a bit of a freak sitting at the bar eating my burger with a knife and a fork. i'd like to come back to try a fancypants burger since the extras look pretty tasty.  the salad was so-so; it was no frills with the perfect amount of dressing. the bartender-cum-waiter was super attentive but not cloyingly so. he made delicious sazeracs to accompany my repast.
Revise this with your best effort: Absolutely! I couldn't agree more - indulging in delectable meat, sipping on bourbon libations, and even accompanying it all with a refreshing salad (which helps me maintain balance and guilt-free enjoyment). I decided to treat myself to an early birthday date, and let me assure you, it was everything I hoped for and more. To truly savor the quality of the meat, I opted for a simple, perfectly cooked, medium rare burger, without any distractions like cheese, bacon, or dressings. And since I follow a gluten-free diet, I enjoyed it without the bun. The burger exceeded my expectations with its divine seasoning and flawless preparation. Although I felt slightly unconventional eating it with a knife and fork at the bar, the taste made it worth every moment. Next time, I look forward to exploring the menu further and trying one of their fancypants burgers which seem incredibly tantalizing. As for the salad, it was decent enough, straightforward, and dressed just right. The bartender, who doubled as a friendly and attentive waiter, skillfully crafted sazeracs that perfectly complemented my meal.

input: Came here on a Monday at lunch time. I sat at the bar and received fast service. Ordered their carne asada taco lunch special which were better than average. More than pleased with this place
Revise this with your best effort: I decided to visit this establishment on a bustling Monday afternoon during lunchtime. Taking a seat at the inviting bar area, I was promptly attended to by the attentive staff. Opting for their much-recommended carne asada taco lunch special, my taste buds were met with delight as the flavors surpassed my expectations. input:

input: Here's an update for my further Comcast experience. Our bill was increased to 250.00 a month. We called and removed some luxery items which brought our bill to 225.00 a month. Called 4 time a to see how we could get our bill lowered, as we have been a loyal customer for 14 years. "Nothing we can do" was all I heard. We decided to no longer be raped by this company and set up service with Verizon. Called Comcast to cancel once we got hooked up with Verizon. All of a sudden, they can do better and reduce my bill to 140.00 a month....which I would have been extremely happy with. Unfortunately, it should have been offered the four previous times I called.  I have Verizon now and have been quite happy with the installation, customer service, and overall product.  I wish Comcast would go under because they don't care about quality customer service. They could offer me a years free of service, yet I wouldn't take it on principle. Screw you Comcast!
Revise this with your best effort: I wanted to provide an update on my recent experience with Comcast. Our monthly bill unexpectedly increased to $250.00, prompting us to call and remove some luxury items in an effort to lower it to $225.00. Despite being loyal customers for 14 years, we were repeatedly told by customer service representatives that there was nothing they could do to lower our bill. Feeling frustrated, we decided to switch to Verizon for our service and called Comcast to cancel our subscription. Suddenly, they were able to offer us a reduced rate of $140.00 per month, which would have made us quite happy. input:
This place is a little harder to find but worth the hunt. B's Diner is a little hole-in-the-wall joint populated by neat antiques, funny posters, and the warmth and personality of their staff. They do incredible work in the community and they are worth supporting.

If you are looking for an affordable meal or are looking to have a hearty bite at somewhere chill- this is your spot. It's got that great diner feel and the personality is all in the food.

I think part of the fun is the people-watching at this joint. Whyte ave bar staff the morning after, hipsters, musicians- never a dull moment.

I've heard the Elk sausage and perogie poutine is amazing, but I've yet to try it.
Revise this with your best effort:
This hidden gem, known as B's Diner, may require a little extra effort to locate, but the search is truly rewarded. Tucked away in a charming space adorned with antique treasures and amusing posters, the atmosphere is made even more delightful by the welcoming and friendly staff. Not only does this eatery excel in providing exceptional food, but they also make a significant impact in the community, making it all the more worthwhile to lend them our support.

Whether you are seeking an affordable meal or craving a hearty and satisfying bite in a relaxed setting, B's Diner is the place to be. Its authentic diner ambiance perfectly captures that nostalgic charm, and the true essence of the establishment emanates through their delectable dishes.

While indulging in their scrumptious offerings, part of the enchantment lies in observing the diverse clientele that frequents the joint. From the tired yet spirited bar staff of Whyte Ave from the night before, to the stylish hipsters, and even talented musicians, there is never a dull moment at B's Diner.

Although I haven't had the pleasure of experiencing it myself, I've heard rave reviews about their Elk sausage and perogie poutine, with many considering it to be an absolute culinary masterpiece.

input:
I'm not sure what changed over the last year at this restaurant, but now it's just terrible food. Before, when I first started coming, it was decent: nothing fancy, but filling and palatable. Now, though, the food is disgusting. 90% of their buffet offerings are WAY too salty. The pulled turkey was tough, the fish tasted like licking a bottle of meat tenderizer, and the vegetables cooked to a putty-like state. The only thing vaguely edible was the corn pudding and mashed potatoes. The desserts are ok, almost store-bought quality. 

The service at least was good. Our waitress refilled our drinks promptly and removed plates often. The only good I saw all night.
Revise this with your best effort:
I'm uncertain about the changes that have taken place at this restaurant in the past year, but the quality of their food has significantly declined. Initially, when I first began frequenting this establishment, the meals were satisfactory - not extravagant, but substantial and enjoyable. However, presently, the food has become unappetizing. A staggering 90% of the items on their buffet are excessively salty, rendering them almost inedible. The pulled turkey is tough, the fish is akin to the taste of meat tenderizer, and the vegetables are overcooked and mushy. The only vaguely palatable dishes were the corn pudding and mashed potatoes. As for desserts, they are passable, resembling store-bought quality.

Remarkably, the service was the one redeeming aspect of the evening. Our waitress was attentive, promptly refilling our drinks and regularly collecting empty plates. It was the only positive element I observed throughout the night.

input:

input:
The long and the short of it: A romantic little BYOB in Newtown Square that hits the mark in several areas. Big portions at decent prices. You won't leave hungry!

And now for a full review:

I have been to this Fellini's Cafe and the one in Bryn Mawr several times and each time I've visited there have been some memorable moments...and there have been speed bumps that keep this place from reaching its full potential.

On my latest visit this past Friday night, I made reservations for 730. My beautiful wife and I arrived right at 730. Although there were two vacant tables available, it took them at least 10 minutes or so to seat us. And when they did, they broke up a table for 6 instead of putting us at the 2 seater. Odd.

Being out and away from the kids for a few hours, we wanted at least a little bit of privacy, instead of sitting next to (pretty much connected to) a table of four. We asked the manager if we could be moved to the 2 seater...he said fine. Another 5-10 minutes (too long!) later a member of the wait staff came and, without any indication as to his intentions, whisked up our bottle of wine and silverware and ran off to the other table. Not a problem, but some eye contact and a simple 'follow me please' with even a hint of a smile would have been lovely. We shrugged and just rolled with it.

The interior is quaint, and the lighting is dim. It's a nice place for a romantic meal. But it is LOUD. So loud I would say this place is kid friendly despite being in such close quarters with your neighbors. Not sure if we'd ever try taking our four kids there (actually I'm certain we won't) but one or two can be done without much trouble.

Our waitress was extremely polite and offered the energy and enthusiasm that our other friend lacked.

For dinner, we ordered a caesar salad to share and for our main courses my wife opted for her usual tagliatelli with mushroom cream sauce and i had what i always have, the tortellini pasticiatti.

Complimentary with the meal were two pieces of bruschetta (very nice) and a small loaf of crusty Italian bread, which is served with butter packets (which perhaps only I find strange for an Italian restaurant?). 

Overall the food was delicious, except for a few somewhat minor hiccups: 

1. The caesar salad was served on a warm plate. The salad was excellent and would have been legendary had it been served on a chilled (or at least not warm!) plate.

2. I am pretty sure they used frozen peas in the tortellini dish, which is fine with me as long as you make sure the peas are thawed before you serve it! Only a few peas were not quite thawed, but it marred what was otherwise a perfectly crafted masterpiece of a dish.

When we paid, the manager allowed us to use an expired gift card. That was a very nice gesture and one that required no push from us to induce.

All in all, I'll keep visiting Fellini because it's relatively inexpensive and they do most everything well.
Revise this with your best effort:
The long and short of it: Fellini's Cafe in Newtown Square is a charming BYOB spot that excels in several aspects. With generous portions at reasonable prices, you won't leave feeling hungry!

Now, let's dive into a comprehensive review of this restaurant:

I have frequented both the Fellini's Cafe in Newtown Square and Bryn Mawr multiple times, and my visits have been a mix of memorable moments and occasional shortcomings that prevent it from reaching its full potential.

During my recent visit on a Friday night, my wife and I had made reservations for 7:30. We arrived promptly at the designated time, but despite having two vacant tables available, it took them at least 10 minutes to seat us. Strangely, instead of placing us at a two-seater table, they broke up a table meant for six. This arrangement didn't provide the privacy we desired as a couple, with us being seated almost attached to a table of four. When we requested to be moved to a two-seater, the manager obliged. However, it took another 5-10 minutes (which felt too long!) for a member of the wait staff to approach us silently, grab our bottle of wine and silverware, and rush off to the other table. Although it wasn't a major issue, a little eye contact accompanied by a simple "follow me, please" and even a faint smile would have been appreciated. Nevertheless, we simply shrugged it off and made the best of it.

The interior of Fellini's Cafe exudes quaintness, complemented by dim lighting, making it an ideal setting for a romantic meal. However, one drawback is that the noise level is quite high, making it less suitable for a quiet dining experience. Despite this, I would say the place is still kid-friendly, as there is space for families, although I doubt we would ever bring our four kids there (in fact, I'm certain we won't). However, having one or two children shouldn't pose much trouble.

Fortunately, our waitress was extremely polite and brought the energy and enthusiasm that our previous encounter lacked.

For our dinner, we decided to share a Caesar salad followed by our respective main courses. My wife went with her usual choice of tagliatelle with mushroom cream sauce, while I opted for my go-to dish, the tortellini pasticiatti.

As a pleasant bonus, the meal included two pieces of delectable bruschetta and a small loaf of crusty Italian bread, served with butter packets (although I found this slightly strange for an Italian restaurant).

Overall, the food at Fellini's Cafe was delightful, except for a few minor hiccups:

1. The Caesar salad was served on a warm plate, which was regrettable as it would have been outstanding if presented on a chilled or at least room temperature plate.

2. In the tortellini dish, I suspect they utilized frozen peas. While this doesn't bother me, it would have been preferable if they had ensured that the peas were fully thawed before serving. Only a few peas remained slightly frozen, but it slightly detracted from an otherwise masterfully prepared dish.

When settling our bill, the manager kindly allowed us to utilize an expired gift card, displaying a thoughtful gesture that required no prompting from us.

All in all, I will continue to visit Fellini's Cafe because it offers a relatively affordable dining experience, and they excel in most aspects of their service and cuisine.

input:
Pretty bummed I didn't try out the Catbird Seat, because this place was totes underwhelming. When you enter, there is a large, awkward entrance and you have to go upstairs to be seated. It was probably only half full, but since it was strange weather, we decided to sit indoors. I'll just say again, walking up towards the hostess as she watches you approach just feels....weird. 

Our server was nice, and we joked with him about the silly flower in a very knock-over-able vase. We got two drinks--julep and one of their other ones with gin, both of which were utterly average to bad. 

The crowd was sort of stuffy. The bread was blah. The food was pretty forgettable. The tenderloin was good because it was a good cut of meat. The Amish chicken was pretty average, with a not so flavorful and slightly MSG-y twang jus. Their signature grits was underwhelming as well. 

All in all, stuffy and so overpriced. Bummed out!
Revise this with your best effort:
I'm extremely disappointed that I missed out on the Catbird Seat experience, as it turned out to be quite underwhelming. The entrance itself was rather awkward and overly large, requiring patrons to climb upstairs to reach their tables. Despite the fact that the place was only about half full, we opted to sit indoors due to the peculiar weather. I must admit, approaching the hostess as she waited for us felt quite uncomfortable.

Fortunately, our server was pleasant, and we shared a few jokes about the ridiculous flower placed in a precarious, easily toppled vase. We tried two drinks, a julep and another gin-based concoction, and unfortunately, they were both thoroughly average at best.

The atmosphere of the restaurant was rather snobbish, and the bread served was unremarkable. As for the food itself, it failed to leave a lasting impression. The only saving grace was the decent quality of the tenderloin, thanks to its cut of meat. However, the Amish chicken dish was disappointingly average, accompanied by a lackluster and somewhat MSG-infused jus. Even their highly praised signature grits fell short of expectations.

All in all, the overall vibe of the Catbird Seat was pretentious and outrageously overpriced. I can't help but feel let down by the entire experience.

input:
This review is LONG overdue!  I visited Stitch-It in June 2013

In brief: Stitch it did an EXCELLENT job on my dress and I was extremely pleased.  I needed it done in a rush and they were able to accommodate me.  Given the tight turnaround, and the work that needed to be done, I didn't mind paying a premium.  The service and results far exceeded my expectations.

Complete Experience: I was attending a convention in Nashville, TN and had ordered an evening gown online a week before (admitted procrastinator tendencies).  The gown was a navy blue Tadashi Shoji evening gown with sequins and an intricately designed lace and sheer layered bodice. The gown was a tad bit too long and there was a bulge in the back. The dress arrived a few days before I was scheduled to fly out to Nashville and I knew I wouldn't have time to get it tailored before leaving.  I found a few Nashville area tailor shops on Yelp, read the reviews and decided I might try Stitch-It.  I also saw a few cleaners that advertised they performed tailoring services, but they (quite frankly) didn't give me the warm and fuzzies.  

Stitch-It was about a 30 minute drive from the Gaylord Hotel where I was staying, so before taking a taxi that far, I decided to check with the hotel to see if they had an in-house tailor.  When I took the dress to the Gaylord tailor/seamstress (who was the nicest lady ever), she looked at the gown and said "I can hem the bottom....I'd have to do it by hand.  The top part though....I won't touch that with a 10ft. pole!"  I laughed, but appreciated her honesty in not being able to handle the work that I needed done.  

I contacted Stitch-It and sent pictures of the dress via text message to a nice young man who's name I can't remember (I think it was Cameron...I could be wrong).  They assured me that they should be able to accommodate me, so I hopped a cab and visited Stitch-It.  When I arrived I was greeted by courteous and professional staff.  I was shown to the dressing room and changed into my gown.  My personal tailor was Maggie O'Neill and she was AWESOME!  After the fitting and pinning, I left the gown and picked it up in two days.  It fit perfectly and was well worth the fee.  If I lived in Nashville, I would DEFINITELY use Stitch-It on a regular basis.

input:
If you're looking for a great brunch place in New Orleans, definitely come here!

My boyfriend and I had brunch here on Sunday, and we loved it! We both started with the Brandy Milk Punch, which was divine.  If you are of age, order this drink!  It is an alcoholic milkshake, and I could literally go here just to drink that because it is so good.  

They bring out fresh bread and butter, and then my boyfriend and I ordered the trio of appetizers.  The trio is quite small, but it includes a duck springroll, fried chicken livers and a fried oyster.  The duck springroll came with a wonderful tangy sauce, which I greatly enjoyed.  My boyfriend enjoyed the fried chicken livers and the fried oyster, but those are not two of my favorite things.

For my entree, I ordered the shrimp and grits.  Oh my goodness... so good! The shrimp are bacon-wrapped, and the grits are true Southern grits.  I will definitely order this dish again when I get the chance to return.  My boyfriend ordered the fish of the day, which was blackened Mahi Mahi, and he loved it.  

Definitely go to Mr. B's!

I highly recommend you give it a try if you're of legal drinking age. It's like an alcoholic milkshake that I could easily come back for just to savor its incredible flavor.

Upon being seated, we were promptly served some fresh bread and butter. As for our appetizers, we opted for the trio, which featured a duck spring roll, fried chicken livers, and a fried oyster. While the portion size was quite small, I must admit that the tangy sauce served with the duck spring roll was a delight for my taste buds. While my boyfriend thoroughly enjoyed the fried chicken livers and fried oyster, they're not exactly my personal favorites.

Moving on to our main courses, I made a fantastic choice with the shrimp and grits. The shrimp were perfectly wrapped in bacon, and the grits were authentically Southern. I absolutely must have this dish again whenever I have the opportunity to return. On the other hand, my boyfriend went for the fish of the day, which happened to be blackened Mahi Mahi, and he was more than pleased with his selection.

Trust me when I say, a visit to Mr. B's is an absolute must!

We went to this restaurant after running in the Philadelphia marathon.  We had a large group (12) with us including kids (ages 10-14), parents and grandparents.   The place is very clean and looks fairly new or at least newly decorated.  The service was excellent and friendly.  The food was very good for the parents but everything was on the spicy side which was not so great for the kids and grandparents.  The lighting was very dim which was an issue for the grandparents reading the menu.  

The Veggie wings were great as were the cactus and sweet potato burritos.   The guacamole was very good although the spicy chips were a little too much.

They offer pitchers of margaritas which was great for our large group.

After completing the Philadelphia marathon, our group of twelve, consisting of children (ages 10-14), parents, and grandparents, decided to dine at this restaurant. Upon arrival, we were pleased to find that the establishment was immaculate and had a modern, newly-decorated appearance. The service provided was outstanding and the staff was genuinely amiable.

While the food was of high quality and greatly satisfied the parents' palates, it leaned toward the spicy side, much to the disappointment of both the kids and grandparents. Additionally, the dim lighting posed difficulties for the grandparents when perusing the menu, which could be improved.

On a positive note, the veggie wings, cactus, and sweet potato burritos were absolutely delicious. The guacamole, although flavorful, had a slight drawback with the spicy chips being a bit overwhelming.

To accommodate our large group, we were delighted to discover that they offer pitchers of margaritas, a feature which greatly enhanced our dining experience.

input:
First of all, I think this might be my first Yelp review about "fast food." It's not a genre I ever eat unless I'm forced to on a road trip.  However, I am from Buffalo, NY, and am a chicken-finger connoisseur, so I decided to give this place a chance.  Additionally, it was on a road trip of sorts.  We had been at the beach all day and were halfway back home to central Tampa.

The service is amazing!  I have never seen fast-food workers who take so much pride in their jobs.  These people were drinking the Zaxby's cool-aid!  They seemed more like Disney employees than fast-food workers.  Both a female counter gal and a male (possible the manager/franchisee) went out of their way to make sure we liked everything.  

The food was a solid 4 stars, but my review overall is rounded up for the above mentioned points.  We had the chicken finger sandwiches on Texas toast.  While the chicken fingers themselves were super juicy and moist, the Texas toast was too greasy to eat them on.  I love sauce and enjoyed the variety.  We tried the Zax, hot honey mustard, insane hot and ranch.  What is missing from the sauce variety, for me, is a spicy bbq and blue cheese.  Serving ranch with hot sauce is an insult to the folks in Buffalo that created the cuisine.  Aside from the bread and sauce small issues, I really enjoyed our meal.  Additionally, it was so cheap!!  $12 and change for 2 meals with drinks.  

I am a fan!  This place doesn't quite hit all the marks of Buffalo-Inspired food, but it does a pretty good job of putting a southern twist on chicken fingers!
Revise this with your best effort:
To begin, this may very well be my inaugural Yelp review regarding "fast food." It's not a culinary category I typically indulge in unless circumstances necessitate it, such as during a road trip. However, being a Buffalo, NY native, and a self-proclaimed aficionado of chicken fingers, I felt compelled to give this establishment a shot. Moreover, I found myself on a sort of impromptu road trip, having spent the entire day at the beach and finding ourselves halfway back home in central Tampa.

The service at this place is truly outstanding! I have never encountered fast-food employees who exhibit such genuine pride in their work. These individuals embody the true spirit of Zaxby's, akin to the enthusiasm of Disney employees rather than your typical fast-food workers. Both a gracious female counter attendant and a male, potentially the manager or franchisee, went above and beyond to ensure our satisfaction.

When it comes to the food, I'd rate it a solid 4 stars, but my overall review is slightly elevated due to the aforementioned points. We opted for the chicken finger sandwiches on delectable Texas toast. While the chicken fingers themselves were exceptionally juicy and moist, the Texas toast proved to be excessively greasy to enjoy alongside them. I relish in sauces and found great enjoyment in the array of options. We sampled the Zax, hot honey mustard, insane hot, and ranch varieties. In my humble opinion, the sauce assortment could benefit from the inclusion of a spicy barbecue and blue cheese option. It feels somewhat lacking to pair hot sauce solely with ranch, as it undermines the authenticity of Buffalo cuisine. Setting aside these minor qualms concerning the bread and sauce, I must say that I thoroughly relished our meal. Added to its appeal was the incredible affordability, with a total of merely $12 and some change securing two meals with beverages.

I am most certainly a fan! While this place may not fully embody the true essence of Buffalo-inspired fare, it commendably injects a southern twist into the world of chicken fingers.
