input: Love!! Our new favorite local spot. We've gone a few times since they opened and it's always a good ambiance, and great food. The drinks are great, the salsa is super yummy, and the salads are very much entree sized. Bring your friends, sit outside, grab a margarita and enjoy!
Revise this with your best effort: Love, our cherished go-to local spot, has truly captured our hearts. Since its grand opening, we have frequented this place multiple times and have never been disappointed. The atmosphere is consistently inviting, while the culinary delights are simply extraordinary. The drinks here are top-notch, the salsa is undeniably scrumptious, and the salads are generously portioned, easily doubling as entrées. Gather your friends, opt for outdoor seating, indulge in a tantalizing margarita, and relish in the wonderful experience Love has to offer!

input:
Great service, food was ok..  Wish the soups were served warmer, and my steak was cooked well done, when requested medium. 

However the service was excellent.
Revise this with your best effort: The service provided was absolutely outstanding. Unfortunately, the food had some room for improvement. While it was decent overall, I would have preferred if the soups were served warmer. Additionally, I requested my steak to be cooked medium, but it arrived well-done. Nonetheless, the impeccable service made up for these shortcomings.

input:
Despite it's great reviews by other Yelpers, I was not that blown away by Nippon Tei. 

My roommate and I were craving sushi and were recommended to come here by Yelp and a friend so we decided to give it a shot. 

First off, they get bonus points for serving FREE edemame as an appetizer. I usually pay $4 to $5 for it at other sushi restaurants. The mango sake drink I have was alright, but not worth the price I paid for it. 

On to the main event...SUSHI! We had the philly roll, tempura roll, tuna roll, and california roll. They were all yummy, but I would have to say I have had better. Actually, out of the hand-full of sushi restaurants I have tried, this was the worst sushi I have tried, but I cannot say the sushi was bad by any means. Don't get me wrong, it was still tasty. 

The other big thing was that the rolls were actually falling apart. I have never had this happen. Therefore, I can say that the presentation and the ability to get the sushi from the plate to my mouth without falling apart did make me unhappy. 

I am willing to come back to Nippon Tei, but I have to say I already have my other favorites. The prices were average compared to other sushi bars, so that won't really help them out either when it comes to bringing me back. We will see!
Revise this with your best effort:
In contrast to the glowing reviews from other Yelpers, my experience at Nippon Tei left me somewhat underwhelmed. Upon the recommendation of Yelp and a friend, my roommate and I decided to give this sushi restaurant a try.

One positive aspect worth mentioning is that they served complimentary edamame as an appetizer, which is a rarity considering I usually pay $4 to $5 for it at other sushi establishments. However, the mango sake drink I ordered was mediocre at best and didn't live up to its price.

Now, onto the main event – the sushi! We ordered the philly roll, tempura roll, tuna roll, and california roll. While they were all decently tasty, I must confess that I've had better elsewhere. In fact, out of the handful of sushi places I've tried, this was the least impressive. However, it's important to note that the sushi itself was not bad by any means; it just didn't exceed my expectations. 

One major issue was that the rolls tended to fall apart, something I've never experienced before. This compromised the presentation and made it difficult to enjoy the sushi without it disintegrating.

While I am open to giving Nippon Tei another chance, I already have my preferred go-to sushi spots. The prices were average for a sushi restaurant, so that alone won't be enough to entice me back. Only time will tell if I decide to return in the future.

input: Went to see Star Wars Rogue One yesterday in 3D.  Buying the tickets was a breeze, and the atmosphere was inviting.  Found the comfortable seats with no problem and ordered right away before the movie began.  I ordered pretzel sticks - food was hot, prompt & delicious.  I was excited for the movie to begin.  Once the advertisements were done and the movie started, that's when I noticed something wasn't right.  The entire screen was so dark that I was not able to make out the faces of the actors on the screen.  I kept lifting up the 3D glasses to see if it made a difference - nope.  The two people seated next to me were noticing the same and complaining.  I thought that maybe this is how the movie was filmed?  Then it got worse.  Even with the 3D glasses on, the shadows in the background on the screen were double and there was no discerning most actors' faces at all.  I got up and went to the lobby and asked for the manager.  The gentleman wore a blue shirt, middle age with a beard, said that this was the 3D experience, it was a "closed-system" and there was nothing he could do.  I simply asked him to come with me into the theater to see with his own eyes how dark it was.  He would not and did not.  I suspect this wasn't the first time he's heard this from a customer.  I've seen normal movies at this location before, but this was my first, and last experience with their 3D in room #1.
Revise this with your best effort:
Yesterday, I had the pleasure of watching Star Wars Rogue One in 3D. The ticket purchasing process was incredibly smooth, and the atmosphere in the theater was warm and welcoming. Locating comfortable seats was a breeze, and without hesitation, I placed my food order just before the movie commenced. Opting for the pretzel sticks, I was delighted to find that the food arrived promptly, steaming hot, and undoubtedly delicious. Anticipation filled the air as I eagerly awaited the start of the film.

However, as the advertisements concluded and the movie began, I couldn't help but notice that something was amiss. The entire screen appeared unusually dark, obscuring the facial features of the talented actors. I even attempted to lift up my 3D glasses, hoping for a quick fix, but to no avail. To my dismay, the individuals seated next to me seemed to share my frustration, expressing their dissatisfaction. Initially, I questioned whether this was an intended stylistic choice by the filmmakers. Unfortunately, matters took a turn for the worse.

Despite wearing the 3D glasses as recommended, the shadows lingering in the background became distorted and double, making it nearly impossible to discern the faces of most actors. Growing increasingly frustrated, I decided to take matters into my own hands. Venturing to the lobby, I approached the manager to address the issue. The manager, a gentleman of middle age adorned in a blue shirt and sporting a beard, explained that this immersive 3D experience was a "closed-system" and there was nothing he could do to rectify the situation.

Unsatisfied with his response, I politely requested his presence in the theater, urging him to witness the overwhelming darkness firsthand. However, much to my disappointment, he adamantly refused, implying that this wasn't the first time a customer had expressed similar concerns. It left me questioning the quality of customer care in this establishment. Although I had previously enjoyed regular movies at this venue, this ill-fated encounter would undeniably be my first and final experience with their 3D capabilities in room #1.

input: Overpriced for average food served warm (not hot) by servers who had trouble saying the names of the dishes and seemed in a rush to give us our bill when the place was more than half empty (on a Saturday night). When one of the servers came over to check on the $23 pork chop (which was not listed in the menu - $18 price was), my spouse commented there was a lot of fat....she seemed baffled by his comment, then walked away! The "ropa vieja" dish was good, but overpriced for being served in moderate portion. The menu prices did not reflect the ambiance (random plastic container boxes placed on a nearby table nor the sagging knitted item hanging over our table - it looks like there should've been a lamp in it).
Revise this with your best effort: The food at this establishment was disappointingly overpriced and average, served lukewarm instead of hot. Furthermore, the servers struggled with pronouncing the names of the dishes, and we noticed a lack of attentiveness as they hurriedly presented us with the bill despite the restaurant being mostly empty on a Saturday night. To make matters worse, when one of the servers checked on our $23 pork chop (which was not even listed on the menu, contrary to the $18 price mentioned), my spouse commented on the excessive amount of fat. Instead of addressing the concern, the server appeared bewildered and simply walked away. Although the "ropa vieja" dish was enjoyable, it fell short in terms of portion size compared to its inflated price. Additionally, the menu prices did not align with the overall aesthetic of the establishment, as we observed random plastic container boxes placed on a nearby table and a sagging knitted item hanging above our own table that seemed as if it should have held a lamp.

input: Should have listened to other reviews--we were kind of disappointed.  The layout of the restaurant is interesting in that it's made to look sort of like the inside of a chicken coop (made for people).  However, the food was overpriced and underwhelming.  We ate from the Sunday brunch menu--only decent value on the menu is the chicken strips and fries.  My wife ordered the seasonal salad, which was comically small and was way short on the actual lettuce (and not cheap either).  Chicken was good, but nothing better than Raising Canes in my opinion.  Service and food seemed on the slow side, especially with the small crowd.
Revise this with your best effort: After taking into account other reviews, we regretfully felt a sense of disappointment. The restaurant's layout was intriguing, resembling the interior of a chicken coop designed for humans. However, our culinary experience left much to be desired. We found the prices to be exorbitant while the dishes failed to impress. Opting for the Sunday brunch menu, we discovered that the sole item offering reasonable value was the chicken strips and fries. Regrettably, my wife's choice, the seasonal salad, was a comical disappointment. It arrived disproportionately minimal and lacking in sufficient lettuce, which was particularly frustrating considering its unjustifiable price. While the chicken was satisfactory, it failed to surpass the quality found at Raising Cane's, in my personal estimation. Moreover, both the service and food exhibited a sluggish pace, which was particularly noticeable given the sparse crowd present.

input: Wow. I am not a vegetarian, nor am I a health-food nut (except for my random "diet" binges) but this place is awesome. A co-worker talked me into trying it out one day (by going there and getting me something and putting it in front of me) and she created a monster. I may not order every day but I sure do think about them. And their delicious salads! Every time I go there I am greeted with a smile and there are tons of other people waiting for their food, as well. Good company =)
Revise this with your best effort: Wow, I must admit, I'm not normally one to embrace vegetarian or health-conscious options, save for my occasional "diet" splurges. However, I have to give credit where credit is due - this place is absolutely incredible. It all started when a persuasive co-worker convinced me to give it a shot, surprising me with a delectable treat right before my eyes. Ever since that moment, I've been hooked. While I may not indulge every single day, the mere thought of this place occupies my mind on a regular basis. And let's not forget about their mouthwatering salads! Each visit is a warm and inviting experience, with friendly smiles all around and a bustling crowd eagerly anticipating their own tantalizing meals. Truly, the company alone is worth cherishing.

input:

input: Perfect place for a date night. The sweet potato nachos and the "breakfast" we're to die for! Really everything we tried was delicious...I can't wait to go back again.
Revise this with your best effort: The ideal spot for a memorable date night, this place offers an exquisite dining experience. The sweet potato nachos were a taste sensation, while the "breakfast" option was simply to die for! Every dish we sampled was absolutely delicious, leaving us longing for our next visit.

input: We had dinner at Convivio right after it opened and we will definitely go back. There were a few minor quirks with the service and with wine being out of stock, but I'm chalking it up to the fact that it just opened and they were working out the kinks. The owner visited our table and he could not have been nicer or more gracious. The food was excellent...nothing to change there! I had the tortelloni pansotti, and i think it was the best pasta I've ever had. I'm sure we will be frequent diners .
Revise this with your best effort: After deciding to visit Convivio during its grand opening, we were pleasantly surprised by our experience and can confidently say that we will be returning. Although we encountered minor setbacks with the service and wine being unavailable, we believe these hiccups can be attributed to the restaurant's recent opening and their earnest efforts to iron out any issues. The owner, in particular, graciously attended to our table, displaying utmost hospitality. As for the food, it surpassed our expectations, leaving no room for improvement. Personally, I indulged in the tortelloni pansotti, which easily secured its position as the finest pasta I have ever savored. With such a remarkable dining experience, we anticipate becoming regular patrons of Convivio.

input: After driving pass all the seafood restaurants around Clearwater Beach, I knew wanted seafood right there and then. I wasn't familiar with the area and did not do any yelping before hand, so was pretty hesitant to just blindly pick a restaurant.  Finally, after a long day at the beach, we made a quick walk across the street to all the restaurants and thats when we stumbled into Crabby Bill's. We ordered the $25 bucket of steamed seafood. It was decent, not necessarily the best fresh seafood. This was just a quick snack that I shared with one other person to keep us going before our big dinner at Bern's Steak House that we had reservation for a couple hours later.
Revise this with your best effort: As I drove past the numerous seafood restaurants adorning Clearwater Beach, a sudden craving for seafood consumed me. However, being unfamiliar with the area and neglecting to research beforehand, I hesitated to simply select a restaurant at random. Eventually, after a tiring day spent at the beach, we decided to take a short stroll across the street to the various dining establishments. That's when fate led us to discover Crabby Bill's. Opting for their $25 bucket of steamed seafood, we indulged in a modest portion that unfortunately fell short of the finest, freshest flavors. Nevertheless, it served as a satisfying snack to sustain us until our highly anticipated dinner at Bern's Steak House, for which we had a reservation a few hours later.

input:
Just finished a State Street Kitchen, Grilled Chicken, Spinach, Swiss and Honey Mustard Sub.  To kick it up a notch I stuffed in Jalapeno Chips for a spicy crunch. 
It was great on an afternoon when autumn is starting to assert itself with bluster.  

This excellent local establishment continues to turn out first rate creative dishes thanks to the ever-present Micha, and her friendly staff.  It has become my most constant breakfast companion, and often my lunch date, as well.  

If you have not been in for a taste of home cooking with a Korean flare, you don't know what you are missing. 

Find a way to get there.  Sit down and become part of the family.
Revise this with your best effort:
I just devoured a mouthwatering State Street Kitchen creation: a Grilled Chicken, Spinach, Swiss, and Honey Mustard Sub. But of course, I couldn't resist taking it up a notch by adding some Jalapeno Chips for that extra spicy crunch. Truly a treat on this blustery autumn afternoon.

This remarkable local establishment, courtesy of the ever-present Micha and her friendly staff, never ceases to amaze with their innovative dishes. It has become my steadfast breakfast companion, and often my go-to spot for lunch as well.

If you haven't experienced the comforting taste of home cooking with a delightful Korean twist, you're truly missing out. Make it a priority to visit. Take a seat and become part of their welcoming family.

input: awesome place.  good food. nice people.  rotating specials.  all home made.  what else do you want?  Chicken salad is a great pickup to make sandwiches at home.
Revise this with your best effort: Experience the awesomeness of this remarkable establishment, boasting an inviting atmosphere, delectable cuisine, and a friendly staff. Indulge in our delectable rotating specials, meticulously crafted with homemade ingredients. This place truly has it all- amazing food, wonderful people, and an array of tantalizing options. Don't miss out on our exceptional chicken salad, perfect for creating scrumptious sandwiches in the comfort of your own home.

input: I'm rating this based on the service and not the food. I am a sales administrator at a hotel. Typically, many places offer a hospitality discount because we do refer guests different places. Front desk told me I should try this place as they give a decent discount. I called to place my order and wasn't really able to say what I liked b/c the girl who answered would cut me off to finish my statement.(she wasn't in the best mood) We get to the end of the order and she asks me am I a guest or an employee. I told her an employee. She asked my title. I told her. She gives me a total and I asked her about the discount. She says it's only for front desk. I'm shocked that this is a departmental thing 1 and 2 I'm thinking to myself, "I'm in sales. I get groups of people here. They ALWAYS asked for recommendations." I said well should I hang up and have front desk place my order? She huffed and puffed and then said "well i'll give it to you this time but please dont abuse it." I was so shocked at how rude she was. So when I finally got my food, I tipped the driver and gave him their menus back and said we will no longer be doing business with you guys. She didnt know SALES is in charge of who the front desk can recommend. Her name was Neisha.The food was good though.
Revise this with your best effort: As a sales administrator at a hotel, I would like to provide a review based solely on the service I experienced, excluding the food quality. Typically, we often receive hospitality discounts from various establishments, as we frequently refer guests to different places. The front desk recommended this particular restaurant to me, mentioning they offer a decent discount. So, I called to place my order, but unfortunately, the girl who answered the phone seemed to be in a rather unpleasant mood. She continuously cut me off while I was trying to express my preferences for the order. Nevertheless, we reached the end of the order, and she suddenly asked if I was a guest or an employee. I informed her that I was an employee and shared my job title. Surprisingly, she provided me with the total amount due without mentioning the discount. I politely inquired about the discount, to which she replied that it is only applicable for front desk staff. I was taken aback by this, as I couldn't believe it was a departmental policy. Additionally, I thought to myself, "I work in sales, and I frequently bring groups of people to this hotel. They always ask for recommendations." I suggested that I hang up and have the front desk place the order instead. In response, she seemed annoyed and begrudgingly agreed, stating, "Well, I'll give it to you this time, but please don't abuse it." I was genuinely shocked by her rudeness. Once I finally received my food, I tipped the driver and returned their menus, informing them that we would no longer be patronizing their establishment. It seems the girl, named Neisha, was unaware that the sales department is responsible for determining which places the front desk can recommend. On a positive note, the food itself was quite good.

input: Always the sweetest ladies! Appointments never take forever and barely any wait time!
Revise this with your best effort: They're always the sweetest ladies, providing exceptional service! Appointments are a breeze, taking hardly any time at all. Minimal waiting ensures a seamless experience!

input: We won't be back. We got the Brussel sprouts and they tasted like pure salt. Our server sent them back and we got another batch and they tasted exactly the same. My husband got the burger and it was okay but the fries that came with it tasted like pure salt also. Maybe the cook working this night was just a little heavy handed on the salt, I don't know. I got the flank steak and it was okay. I wouldn't rave about it or ever get it again. Our cocktails were good and the atmosphere was nice, but we were really disappointed with the food :(
Revise this with your best effort: We regret to inform you that we will not be returning to your establishment. Our experience was unsatisfactory, starting with the Brussel sprouts that were incredibly salty. Despite sending them back and receiving another batch, they tasted identical to the first. My husband ordered a burger which was decent, but unfortunately, the accompanying fries were also overwhelmingly salty. It is possible that the cook preparing our meal that evening was overly generous with the salt, but we cannot be certain. As for myself, I ordered the flank steak which was average at best, neither impressing me enough to rave about it nor tempting me to order it again. On a positive note, the cocktails we had were enjoyable and the atmosphere of your establishment was pleasant. Nevertheless, we left feeling extremely disappointed with the food.

input: I love going to Phillies games sooo much and this stadium definitely adds to the experience. I was never a big baseball fan until about a couple of years ago, when my bf introduced me to the wonder that is the Phils- instant love. Sure,my first Phils game was the 10, 000 loss but whatever. The places has a open feeling, and never feels clausterphobic. The only time i've felt that I had bad seats was when we sat right under neath the scoreboard, and I had to keep on looking up.  I like how you can wander about and watch the game from the lower levels, and that despite it's a sold out game, it never feels cramped or you're really aching to get around the stadium. They have a lot of great food (lots of variety) and the facilities are always clean- both are numerous, so I'm never waiting in line.  I am missing baseball season and I cannot wait until April! Go Phillies!
Revise this with your best effort:
I absolutely adore attending Phillies games, and the stadium itself truly enhances the entire experience. It's remarkable how my passion for baseball developed just a couple of years ago when my boyfriend introduced me to the magic of the Phils – it was love at first sight. Although my inaugural Phillies game happened to coincide with their 10,000th loss, I brushed it off because there's something about this place that exudes an open atmosphere and never feels suffocating. The only instance where I've encountered less than ideal seats was when we sat directly beneath the scoreboard, causing me to constantly crane my neck upwards.

One aspect that I appreciate is the ability to wander around and catch glimpses of the game from the lower levels. Even during sold out games, there's an absence of overcrowding or a desperate urge to navigate through the stadium. Moreover, they offer a wide variety of delectable food options, ensuring that there's something to please every palate. What's more, the facilities are consistently immaculate, and the abundance of amenities means I never have to wait in lengthy lines.

I can't help but feel a sense of longing for baseball season, eagerly anticipating its arrival in April. Go Phillies!

input: My boyfriend and I decided to stop by for lunch yesterday, and I am so glad we did. I ordered a side of beans, chips and salsa, and guacamole. He ordered two steak tacos and a side of rice. The beans are hands down my favorite I've had from a mexican restaurant.  My only complaint is that, unfortunately you do not get a very big portion. The salsa is so fresh tasting and delicious-very cilantro forward, and the chips were nice, thick and crunchy without being oily at all. Take note though, chips and salsa are not included with your purchase and must be bought separately. Now let me get to the best part-the made to order, chunky guacamole. The hardy chips would definitely withstand this heavy duty guac, but I opted instead for tortillas as my vessel to stuff it with along with my beans and salsa. The hot sauces were anything but, though admittedly my tolerance to spices may be higher than the average persons. While I had a great eating experience, my boyfriend did not. He said the meat was of low quality and quite flavorless. He did say he would give it another shot though!
Revise this with your best effort:
Yesterday, my boyfriend and I made the delightful decision to stop by for lunch, and I have to say, it was a wise choice. I indulged in a side of delectable beans, along with some chips and salsa, accompanied by a generous serving of guacamole. Meanwhile, he ordered two steak tacos paired with a side of flavorful rice. I can confidently proclaim that the beans at this Mexican restaurant are, without a doubt, the best I've ever had. However, my only gripe revolves around the portion size, which unfortunately falls a bit short.

Now, let me praise the salsa, as it boasts a refreshing and vibrant taste, with cilantro taking the lead. The chips provided a fulfilling crunch, without being excessively greasy. Nevertheless, it's important to note that chips and salsa are not included with your purchase, and must be acquired separately.

Now, onto the highlight of my meal - the chunky, made-to-order guacamole. Its texture and flavor were simply divine. Although the sturdy chips would have withstood the hearty guacamole, I opted to utilize tortillas as my vessel, allowing me to create mouthwatering bites filled with beans, salsa, and guacamole.

Unfortunately, the hot sauces failed to deliver the anticipated kick, though it is worth noting that my tolerance for spices may exceed that of the average individual. Despite my thoroughly enjoyable dining experience, my boyfriend did not share the same sentiment. According to him, the meat lacked quality and remained disappointingly bland. However, he expressed willingness to give this place another chance in the future.

input: I love this place. It's been in La Cumbre Plaza for I don't know how long now. If you are looking for a good sandwich look no further. All of the ingredients taste fresh, and their bread rolls are amazing. They are nice and soft, not with that cut the roof of your mouth crust. Being born and raise in Santa Barbara, actually just down the street, I have been coming here for some years now. I've tried probably over half of their sandwiches and all have been good, so good it's hard to pick a favorite.  In addition, I cannot forget to mention their awesome soda selection, so awesome I cannot hesitate to try something different with every visit. You won't find anything super fancy or exotic, like a roasted duck pastrami sandwich here, but if you're a local or just passing through and feel like having a great sandwich with good fresh ingredients swing by Plaza Deli and grab a bite.
Revise this with your best effort:
I absolutely adore this place. It's a hidden gem nestled in La Cumbre Plaza, and honestly, I've lost track of how long it's been there. When it comes to satisfying your cravings with a top-notch sandwich, trust me, there's no need to look any further. Every single ingredient used here tastes incredibly fresh, and the bread rolls? They are beyond amazing. Soft and heavenly, unlike those crusty ones that can leave your mouth in pain. 

Being a proud Santa Barbara native, and conveniently residing just down the street, I've been a loyal regular at this spot for years now. I've practically sampled more than half of their scrumptious sandwich menu, and I'm telling you, each one surpasses expectations. It's nearly impossible to choose a favorite when they're all bursting with flavor.

Oh, and let's not forget about their mind-blowing variety of sodas. It's honestly remarkable, and I find myself eagerly trying a different one on every visit. Now, don't expect any overly extravagant or exotic options like a roasted duck pastrami sandwich here. But if you're a local like me or simply passing through, and you're in the mood for an exceptionally delicious sandwich crafted with quality, fresh ingredients, then swing by Plaza Deli and treat yourself to a truly satisfying bite.

input: I think this Nordstrom's shoe department is better than other locations.  There was a lot of variety and they carry some higher end lines here.  The sales professionals were very good.  A gentleman named Erwin helped me locate two pairs of shoes throughout the Nordstrom's network AND price matched them to Bloomingdale's clearance sale price.  And no charge for shipping and handling.  Nordstrom's has won my loyalty due to the very high level of customer service!
Revise this with your best effort: In my opinion, the shoe department at Nordstrom exceeds the offerings of other locations. I was pleasantly surprised by the extensive variety and the presence of higher-end lines in this particular department. The sales professionals showcased exceptional expertise. Notably, a gentleman named Erwin went above and beyond, assisting me in finding two pairs of shoes across Nordstrom's network. What impressed me even more was his willingness to price match them to Bloomingdale's clearance sale price, while also waiving any shipping and handling fees. Such outstanding customer service has undoubtedly earned Nordstrom my unwavering loyalty.

input: A small aquarium that is interesting mainly for kids.  They have a shark feeding show and stingrays that you can pet and buy food to feed.  It is not the first place i would go in Tarpon Springa, but it is ok, small children seem to like it.
Revise this with your best effort: The aquarium, although primarily appealing to young children, offers an assortment of attractions. One of the show-stopping events is the thrilling shark feeding performance that captivates visitors of all ages. Moreover, there is an interactive opportunity to pet friendly stingrays, while also having the option to purchase food to feed them. While it may not be the top priority destination in Tarpon Springs, it still manages to amuse small children to a remarkable degree.

input: Nothing extraordinary, but if you want some simple Chinese takeout, this is the best place around. The food seems less greasy than you sometimes find and the people are super nice.
Revise this with your best effort: If you are in the mood for a straightforward Chinese takeout experience, this place is definitely worth a try. While it may not offer anything particularly unique, it stands out as one of the top choices in the area. The food is noticeably less greasy compared to other establishments, adding a touch of quality to the overall experience. Moreover, the staff members are exceptionally friendly and accommodating, ensuring a pleasant encounter.

input: Quaint place with great ambience, food and service. I had the Shrimp Po Boy. It was delicious. The fries and cole slaw were perfect side dishes. This was my first visit. Definitely not my last.
Revise this with your best effort: I thoroughly enjoyed my visit to this charming establishment that boasts a delightful atmosphere, exceptional culinary offerings, and impeccable service. Opting for their renowned Shrimp Po Boy, I was met with a mouthwatering dish that surpassed my expectations. Complemented perfectly by the delectable fries and cole slaw, it was a culinary triumph. This initial experience has undoubtedly left a lasting impression, and I am eagerly looking forward to returning in the future.

input: Broussard's was pretty good when I went there a few weeks ago. I had a Groupon that was about to expire so I took my parents out to dinner.  I knew going in that Broussards is a very old skool New Orleans restaurant, and it is very nice when you walk in to see the old tile on the walls in the foyer of the building. The courtyard is beautiful and I just had to turn into a tourist and take a picture in front of the fountain with my mom. We were seated and very promptly greeted by the drink guy.  He brought us our water and told us about the extensive wine list, but they were of course out of the Pinot Grigio that I ordered.  He successfully suggested a Chardonnay for me instead and I was happy. The head waiter came out and explained with great detail the specials for the night, but I went for menu regulars, the maytag blue cheese salad and the pecan crusted drum. I wanted more salad, it was so good, I ate it up so fast. The drum was excellent too. It had this soy butter sauce on it that was so good and topped with crawfish. I was definitely happy with my meal and glad I had the experience. What makes me knock off two stars is that though the foyer's vintage appeal is nice and the courtyard is beautiful, I feel like the dining room needs an upgrade.  The chandeliers on the walls in the main dining room are very reminiscent of the hallways of my grandmother's assisted living home. I think its just one of those places I am glad to say I've been to, but I don't think I will choose to go there again.
Revise this with your best effort:
When I recently visited Broussard's a few weeks ago, I was pleasantly surprised by the experience. To make use of a soon-to-expire Groupon, I decided to take my parents out for dinner. Being aware of Broussard's reputation as a classic New Orleans restaurant, I was delighted to see the vintage tile on the walls of the foyer upon entering. The courtyard added to the charm, and I couldn't resist acting like a tourist and snapping a photo in front of the beautiful fountain with my mom.

Once seated, we were promptly attended to by the beverage server, who provided us with water and presented an extensive wine list. Unfortunately, the Pinot Grigio I requested was unavailable, but he successfully recommended a satisfying Chardonnay alternative. The head waiter went above and beyond in explaining the night's specials in great detail, but I ultimately opted for my usual favorites from the regular menu: the Maytag blue cheese salad and the pecan-crusted drum.

The salad was so delectable that I devoured it rapidly, savoring every bite. The drum, too, was exceptional, featuring a delightful soy butter sauce and a generous topping of crawfish. My meal certainly left me fulfilled and content, and I felt fortunate to have had such an enjoyable dining experience.

Although the vintage allure of the foyer and the beauty of the courtyard were highlights, I must admit that the dining room itself could benefit from an upgrade. The chandeliers adorning the walls gave off a slightly outdated vibe, reminiscent of the halls in my grandmother's assisted living home. While I am glad to have had the opportunity to dine at Broussard's, I don't foresee myself choosing to return in the future, hence the deduction of two stars.

input:
Service is excellent. Atmosphere is great. The raw bar was fantastic. Those were the best Alaskan crab legs I've had. Well worth splurging for them. 

My friends were drawn in by the awesome looking burger they had, and indeed the burgers were all they hoped for. It came with a generous portion of crispy fries. But if you want anything else besides the $17 burgers, expect to spend over $30 for your entree. While the ambience feels and looks casual, it is fine dining.

Unfortunately, the waiter did sell the shrimp and grits with the additional crab as "heaven in his mouth", but that it was not. I've had better shrimp and grits in Atlanta, and there is no reasonable way you should be paying $30 for shrimp and GRITS. Without the crab, it was still over $20.

But everything else was great. Drinks were delicious. Everything came out pretty quickly. Oh, when we mentioned we were visiting from out of town, the waiter was nice enough to give us a complimentary appetizer of the cool pizza to start. It was great but the name is hard to say or remember. And the rabbit and chicken liver pate was super worth since it comes in a huge mason jar.

I recommend sticking to the drinks, appetizers, and burgers and you'll be a pretty happy camper.
Revise this with your best effort:
The service at this establishment is truly excellent, while the atmosphere is undeniably great. The raw bar exceeded all expectations, particularly the Alaskan crab legs which were the best I've ever had. They were definitely worth splurging on.

My friends were captivated by the burger options, and they were not disappointed. The burgers lived up to their expectations and were accompanied by a generous portion of crispy fries. However, if you're looking for something other than the $17 burgers, be prepared to spend over $30 for your entree. Despite the casual ambience, this place can be considered fine dining.

Unfortunately, the waiter oversold the shrimp and grits with the additional crab, claiming it would be "heaven in his mouth", but it fell short. I have experienced better shrimp and grits in Atlanta, and it seems unreasonable to pay $30 for a dish that typically costs much less. Even without the crab, it still exceeded $20.

On a positive note, everything else was exceptional. The drinks were delicious, and all the orders were served promptly. Furthermore, when we mentioned that we were visiting from out of town, the waiter kindly treated us to a complimentary appetizer of a unique and memorable pizza. The rabbit and chicken liver pate, served in a substantial mason jar, was definitely worth trying.

In conclusion, I would highly recommend sticking to the drinks, appetizers, and burgers at this establishment, as they are guaranteed to leave you satisfied and pleased.

input: I love Doan's. It's the kind of place you have a "usual" and every time you have it, it's just as good as the last time. They staff is friendly and speedy so if you don't have a long lunch it's a great place to go.
Revise this with your best effort: I absolutely adore Doan's! It's that kind of delightful establishment where you can establish your own "usual," and no matter how many times you indulge in it, the experience never fails to amaze. The staff is not only exceptionally friendly, but they also deliver prompt service, making it the perfect spot for those with limited lunch breaks.

input: This amazing brick oven pizza joint gets better every time I go. The last I time I went I got a Rotolo and a prosciutto pizza. The Rotolo is dough wrapped around mortadella and ricotta cheese and topped with pistachios and oil. It is so good. I order it every time. It's about the size of a bun and cost $5. The pizza was amazing. The prosciutto was incredibly tasty. The dough is divine. The service is always great and the beer selection is good. Definitely one of the best pizza places in Philly.
Revise this with your best effort:
I am consistently blown away by the continuous improvement of this extraordinary brick oven pizza establishment. During my most recent visit, I indulged in a delightful combination of the Rotolo and prosciutto pizzas. The Rotolo, an absolute delight, presents a heavenly marriage of dough hugging mortadella and ricotta cheese, then adorned with the perfect amount of crunchy pistachios and a drizzle of oil. This particular creation has become a steadfast preference of mine, with its bun-sized proportions and reasonable $5 price tag.

The pizza itself was an impeccable masterpiece. The prosciutto, bursting with incredible flavors, delivered a truly remarkable taste experience. Each bite into the divine dough was met with an explosion of delectable sensations that left me craving more. It's worth noting that the exceptional service consistently provided at this establishment further enhances the dining experience, and the assortment of beers available complements the pizza flawlessly.

Without a doubt, this venue deserves its rightful place among the finest pizza establishments Philadelphia has to offer.

input:
Amazing pizza. AMAZING! After my first bite, I felt like that Oprah Winfrey meme, where her head is thrown back, her mouth is agape and her arms are open wide, and she's screaming, "You get a car!" Except it's not Oprah, it's me. And I don't get a car -- I get a pizza. But I felt that excited.  

This is basically the pizza I have been looking for since moving to the Indianapolis area. It's a whole lot of nothing: It's not cut into square pieces. It's not crispy and thin. It's not redolent of oregano. It's thick and chewy, cheesy, greasy, wonderful -- it tastes the way pizza is supposed to taste! I have found my new pizza home.
Revise this with your best effort: Incredible pizza. INCREDIBLE! With just one bite, I experienced that iconic Oprah Winfrey moment, where her head tilts back, mouth wide open, arms outstretched, and an ecstatic scream of "You get a car!" Only this time, it's not Oprah, it's me. And instead of a car, I've found pure pizza greatness. This is the pizza I've been on a quest for ever since I arrived in Indianapolis. Everything about it is perfection: it's not sliced into squares, it's not paper-thin and crispy, it's not overwhelmed by oregano. It's thick, chewy, cheesy, and delightfully greasy – precisely how pizza should be. I've finally discovered my ultimate pizza haven.

input: Waited 27 minutes for three teas (no one else was in the store when we came in and ordered). NO tea is worth that long of a wait, especially in Chinatown.
Revise this with your best effort: We endured a frustrating 27-minute wait for just three teas, despite being the only customers in the store when we arrived to place our order. Such an extensive delay for a beverage, particularly in Chinatown, completely undermines its value.

input:
I grew up eating beef sandwiches in Chicago, and this place makes the best beef I've ever had outside of the city. 

Couple of suggestions: Offer a third sandwich size option (bigger!), get sweet peppers, serve fries(!!!), keep the main location off of Mass Ave open year-round, and have longer hours!
Revise this with your best effort: Having been raised on beef sandwiches in Chicago, I must say that this place undoubtedly prepares the most exceptional beef outside the city. However, I have a few recommendations that I believe would further enhance the overall experience. Firstly, it would be fantastic if a third sandwich size option, perhaps a larger one, could be introduced to cater to those seeking heartier portions. Additionally, incorporating sweet peppers into the sandwich toppings would undoubtedly add a delightful burst of flavor. Furthermore, offering a side of fries alongside the sandwiches would truly complete the culinary experience. Secondly, to ensure that patrons can enjoy this remarkable establishment throughout the year, it would be greatly appreciated if the main location off of Mass Ave could remain open year-round. Lastly, extending the operating hours would be marvelous as it would accommodate those with varying schedules, allowing them to indulge in the delectable beef sandwiches at their convenience.

input:
We came here for an early mothers day celebration as we were on the quest to find a nail salon that could accommodate 4 pedicures at the same time. They were very friendly and even though they didn't have 4 pedicurists on the schedule that day they added one to accommodate us. That was really nice of them as they could have easily told us no. 

The place itself is decorated very modern and offers a very clean, minimalist atmosphere. Upon walking in we were immediately greeted and after we checked in with the front desk we were asked what we wanted to drink. They had complimentary mimosas, wine and champagne, the perfect way to begin to unwind. Once we picked out our polish colors we were well on our way to getting our pedicures. Everyone was so nice and made us feel comfortable and welcomed. My polish never chipped the whole time I had it on. I will definitely be back. 

The only downside is that its street parking only, which isn't something that they can control. They told us most of their business comes from people who work in the CBD so parking probably isn't an issue for their regular customers. Aside from parking being an issue I would definitely go to Buff again.
Revise this with your best effort:
We visited this place to celebrate an early Mother's Day and were in search of a nail salon that could accommodate four pedicures simultaneously. Despite not having four pedicurists scheduled that day, they kindly added an extra staff member to accommodate us. Their generosity was truly appreciated, as they could have easily turned us away.

The salon itself boasts a modern decor and offers a clean, minimalist atmosphere. As soon as we walked in, we were warmly greeted and promptly checked in at the front desk. To our delight, we were asked about our drink preferences and were offered complimentary mimosas, wine, and champagne, which served as the perfect way to relax and unwind. Once we selected our desired polish colors, we were well on our way to enjoying our pedicures. The staff members were extremely friendly, creating a comfortable and welcoming environment. Remarkably, my polish remained chip-free throughout its entire wear. Without a doubt, I will be returning.

The only drawback we encountered was the limited street parking, which is beyond the salon's control. However, they reassured us that their main clientele comprises individuals working in the central business district (CBD), where parking is likely less of an issue. Apart from this minor inconvenience, I highly recommend visiting Buff.

input: Great spot for pho! Broth is very good. I ordered No. 51 (small) and it was filling. Would definitely come back again when I'm in Philly.
Revise this with your best effort: This place is fantastic for pho! The broth is incredibly flavorful and delicious. I opted for the No. 51 (small) and it surprisingly turned out to be quite filling. Without a doubt, I will make a point to return here whenever I find myself in Philadelphia.

input:
I love the concept of this place. One half of it a café that serves different types of coffees and teas, and breakfast type items, and the other world where it serves bar type apps, salads, and sandwiches,  Can't forget that they also serve a wide variety of beers that they serve on tap, bottled, or in can.  

This place is pretty darn casual, and one can hang out here for hours with their friends.  Reminds me of the good ol' college days when no time could pass especially on a chill out Sunday Fun day.

Bring your four legged friend too.  They are totally welcome.
Revise this with your best effort:
I absolutely adore the concept of this place. It consists of a charming café, offering an array of delectable coffees, teas, and breakfast treats. But that's not all – there's also a delightful world where they serve up bar-style appetizers, fresh salads, and mouthwatering sandwiches. And let's not forget their fantastic selection of beers, available on tap, bottled, or canned.

The atmosphere here is wonderfully laid-back, making it the perfect spot to spend endless hours with friends. It takes me back to those cherished college days when time seemed to stand still, especially on those relaxed Sunday fun days.

Oh, and there's one more amazing thing – you can bring your furry companion along! Their doors are wide open to our four-legged friends.

input: My husband reserved a Corolla-sized car over the internet ten days ahead of time. When we arrived at Avis Rent A Car at the Reno airport I asked if the rental could be upgraded to a Camry-size vehicle. They offered us two different kinds of cars and finally we got the Camry we wanted. The man was very professional and in the end told us the rental would be $800.00 for five days. I felt the price was very high, however we had gone through most of the paperwork. I had already selected to get the $25.00 a day insurance which came to $150.00 with tax. We were very happy with the car and had no problems with it. During our vacation I decided to talk to an Avis representative when we dropped the car off. I asked her if a weekly rate would be less expensive. She said it would be $15.00 more. She said the upgrade cost an extra $20.00 a day. I will not rent from Avis any more. Next time I will go to Hertz or Dollar and make the reservation over the phone. Looking back, i would not have gotten the extra insurance. My personal insurance covers everything.
Revise this with your best effort:
Ten days prior to our trip, my husband made an online reservation for a car the size of a Corolla. Upon arriving at Avis Rent A Car at the Reno airport, I inquired about the possibility of upgrading to a larger vehicle like a Camry. After presenting us with two alternative options, we eventually managed to secure the Camry we desired. The rental agent conducted himself in a highly professional manner and informed us that the cost for the five-day rental would be $800. Although the price seemed steep, we had already completed most of the necessary paperwork. Notably, I had already opted for the $25.00 per day insurance, amounting to $150.00 including tax. In the end, the car exceeded our expectations and caused no issues during our vacation.

However, during our trip, I decided to discuss the rental prices with an Avis representative upon returning the vehicle. The representative informed me that the weekly rate would actually be $15.00 higher than our initial rental cost. Furthermore, it was revealed that the upgrade had incurred an additional charge of $20.00 per day. Dissatisfied with these findings, I have decided to no longer rent from Avis in the future. Instead, I plan to make reservations over the phone with either Hertz or Dollar. In hindsight, I realize that obtaining the extra insurance was unnecessary, as my personal insurance already provides comprehensive coverage.

input: Great customer service! Love my new car! Highly recommend to anyone who's trying to buy a new used car in good shape! Talk to Andy if you want some good help!
Revise this with your best effort: Exceptional customer service! I am absolutely ecstatic about my new vehicle! I wholeheartedly endorse this dealership to anyone seeking a quality pre-owned car. If you are in need of excellent assistance, Andy is the person to see!

input: After moving to the area, Jungle Prada Tavern was one of the first places a friend took me.  The bartender made a great recommendation based on a beer I told her I liked and I loved it!  Now for the food- I LOVE seafood, so I am leary of ordering from places that don't do it justice, but alas, they impressed me thoroughly with all the seafood options I chose!!  The scallops prosciutto app, del mar pizza with crab and scallops, and crab stuffed portabella app (comes with a crab and lobster bisque- YUM) are all delicious!!  I also love the roasted portabella app- for a vegetarian option, it is delicious and was recomended by someone who isn't. I've actually gone back several times since then just to eat (obviously, I also drank ;) and took my sister when she was in town visiting (and is a seafood fanatic).  So all in all, give this place a chance!!  You will not be disappointed with the options!
Revise this with your best effort: After relocating to the area, Jungle Prada Tavern became one of the initial establishments I was introduced to by a friend. The bartender astutely recommended a beer that perfectly matched my preferences, and I was thoroughly impressed! Now, as for the cuisine - being a seafood lover, I am usually apprehensive about ordering from places that fail to do justice to this delicacy. However, Jungle Prada Tavern exceeded my expectations with their remarkable selection of seafood offerings! The scallops prosciutto appetizer, the del mar pizza adorned with succulent crab and scallops, and the crab stuffed portabella appetizer (served with an irresistible crab and lobster bisque) were all absolutely delightful!! Additionally, I found their roasted portabella appetizer, which was recommended by a non-vegetarian, to be equally delectable as a superb vegetarian option. I have actually revisited the establishment numerous times since then, not solely for the exceptional food but also to enjoy their delightful beverages. I even treated my seafood-enthusiast sister to this place when she visited from out of town, and she was equally captivated. So, in conclusion, I strongly encourage you to give this establishment a chance! You will undoubtedly be elated with the diverse array of options it offers.

input: This is one of my favorite bead stores in Nashville, walls and walls of seed beads and glass strands!
Revise this with your best effort: This bead store in Nashville is definitely one of my favorites, boasting an extensive collection of seed beads and glass strands that stretches across its walls!

input: Went here for dinner on opening day and was SO HAPPY I DID!! Great atmosphere, lovely staff, and food on fleek!! Green tea (PHO PHREE) was so satisfying, summer rolls and spicy peanut sauce were DELISH, and pho was PHONOMENAL! Definitely making this one of my regular hot spotz as I eat my way through Fairmount!
Revise this with your best effort: I had the pleasure of visiting this restaurant on its opening day for dinner, and I must say, I was absolutely delighted that I did! The atmosphere was truly amazing, the staff was incredibly friendly and attentive, and the food was absolutely on point! The Green tea (PHO PHREE) provided such a satisfying and refreshing experience. The summer rolls, paired with the spicy peanut sauce, were absolutely delicious. And let me tell you, the pho was simply phenomenal! Without a doubt, I am definitely adding this restaurant to my list of regular hotspots as I continue my culinary exploration through Fairmount!

input:
Don't let the outside fool ya or even the initial impression when you walk in because they food here is really good! When ya walk in this place it's like stepping back into the 1950's.  It's kinda awesome.  Definitely a small-town, homey feel that serves good ole family cookin'.  They had a iceskates up on the wall and a Christmas tree in the corner.  How precious.   
Don't come here expecting the best food in the whole wide world.  It is great for grandma's greasy cooking.  I've only eaten breakfast here but it's been amazing everytime.  I got pancakes and they are so fluffy and light and awesome (esp if you add a little butter).  The bacon was nice, thick, large slices; slightly overcooked maybe but super good cuz I love bacon! :)
The prices are reasonable and the service is great.  This is a great place for a quick delicious home cooked breakfast!
Revise this with your best effort:
Do not be deceived by the exterior or your first impression when entering, because the food at this establishment is truly exceptional! Stepping inside feels like a journey back to the charming 1950s, which is quite delightful. It exudes a small-town, cozy atmosphere, serving wholesome, traditional family cuisine. The decor includes ice skates displayed on the wall and a lovely Christmas tree nestled in the corner, creating an endearing ambiance.

While it may not boast the most extraordinary dishes in the entire world, it certainly excels at offering grandma's beloved, indulgent cooking. Although I have solely experienced their breakfast options, I have been consistently impressed. The pancakes are flawlessly fluffy and light, achieving perfection when paired with a touch of butter. The generous portions of thick-cut bacon, albeit slightly overcooked, pleasantly satisfy my bacon cravings.

Reasonable prices combined with exceptional service make this the ideal spot for a quick yet scrumptious, home-style breakfast.

input: Tried this place out after many suggestions from friends.  We went in one night about an hour or so before closing just to find that they were only serving a partial menu - we're not talking that late, it was like, 9:30 on a weekend.  There was no mention of going down to a bar menu on the website so I was a bit annoyed by that.  Something about 'surprise disappointments that could be totally avoided' really bother me.  So, the dish I had picked out online wasn't available and I ordered a burger instead.  The server seemed to have a very hard time understanding my burger and suggested that modifications couldn't be made?  I told him I'm sure removing a single topping wouldn't cause the kitchen staff any issues...  The rest of the meal we were generally ignored and the service wasn't great.  I found the food to be overpriced for the quality.  Unless there is a special reason to attend, I don't think we'll be going back.
Revise this with your best effort: Following multiple recommendations from friends, we finally decided to give this place a try. We arrived one evening approximately an hour before closing time, only to discover that they were only offering a limited menu. It wasn't even that late, just around 9:30 on a weekend. To my disappointment, there was no mention on their website about transitioning to a bar menu at that hour. It's frustrating to encounter these avoidable surprise disappointments. Moreover, the dish I had specifically chosen online turned out to be unavailable, forcing me to settle for a burger instead. When I requested a minor modification to my order, the server seemed to struggle in comprehending my request, implying that the kitchen staff couldn't accommodate such a simple change. I assured him that removing a single topping shouldn't cause any inconvenience. Throughout the rest of the meal, we felt largely ignored by the server, resulting in subpar service overall. Additionally, considering the quality of the food, I found the prices to be excessively high. Unless there is a compelling reason for us to return, I highly doubt we will revisit this establishment.

input:
Second visit even better than the first!!  Loved the butternut squash and goat cheese Rangoons, and the delightfully filling mushroom yakisoba. Amazing flavor, and a smoky , meaty feel though it is meatless. Then came the coconut curry ramen. Heaven in a bowl. 
My only complaint is when you have to wait for seating there is no way to hang by the bar without constantly feeling you are in The servers' way as they breeze by with deliciousness in bowls and plates. So worth the wait before heading to the theater. Plus, food comes out very quickly so we made the curtain, just barely, but with really happy tummies.
Revise this with your best effort:
The second visit surpassed our expectations and was even more enjoyable than the first! We absolutely adored the flavorful combination of butternut squash and goat cheese in the Rangoons, as well as the satisfyingly hearty mushroom yakisoba. It's incredible how the dish has a smoky and meaty essence despite being meatless. And then we were graced with the coconut curry ramen, which was nothing short of heavenly in a bowl.

If there's one minor issue, it's that when waiting for seating, there's no designated area by the bar where you can relax without feeling like you're in the servers' way as they skillfully transport mouthwatering bowls and plates. However, the wait is absolutely worth it, especially if you're heading to the theater afterwards. Besides, the remarkable thing is that the food arrives promptly, allowing us to make the curtain just in the nick of time, while savoring the contentment of our delighted stomachs.

input: I cannot comment on the food as I had only a couple beers. I did have the white IPA and a red ale which were good but not blow me away. I might be spoiled having 2 friends who brew professionally but the beers were good, not outstanding. The location is kind of far from other stuff which normally wouldn't bother me but everything around is seriously industrial and scenery does make a better place. They do discount the beer $1 when a train comes by and maybe that's the best they can make of a meh location. Probably give it more like a 3.5 stars. It does say something that there was a loyal following at 4pm on a Sunday.
Revise this with your best effort:
I am unable to comment extensively on the food as my experience was limited to a couple of beers. Specifically, I tried the white IPA and red ale, both of which were enjoyable but did not exceed my expectations. It is possible that my perspective may be skewed, as I am fortunate to have two friends who are professional brewers. The beers at this establishment were certainly good, although not exceptional. 

One aspect worth noting is the location, which is somewhat distant from other attractions. Ordinarily, this would not bother me, but the surrounding area is predominantly industrial and lacks in picturesque surroundings, which can enhance the overall ambiance of a place. However, the establishment does offer a $1 discount on beers whenever a train passes by, which could be viewed as their attempt to make the most of a less than ideal location.

In terms of rating, I would lean towards giving it around 3.5 stars. It is worth mentioning that the presence of a devoted following even at an off-peak time, such as 4pm on a Sunday, does speak to the establishment's popularity and appeal.

input:
I first found out about this adorable little salon here on yelp while looking for a place to get a manicure downtown/ CBD.  I visited on 3/8/13 and got their "Mini Manicure"- it's only $15!  I chose an OPI polish and the nail technician did a GREAT job!  So great in fact, that today on Monday, 3/18/13- I did not have ONE CHIP!  This is amazing for polish!  My nails looked fabulous!  The technician was friendly, as were the other stylists.  I'm not sure if it was the manager or the owner that was working the front desk- but she came over as well and was super friendly and welcoming.  The salon looks amazing, trendy, and peaceful.  It has a great vibe.

I was so happy with my first appointment- that I went back today, and left disappointed.  I went to the same nail techinician- and we talked as she worked on my nails.  The person working the front desk (seemed like an owner/ manager- although different from my first visit) was SO  nice, welcoming, and talkative.  This time though I needed a gel manicure, in french- as I am in a wedding this weekend.  I explained that I was in the wedding, assuming the technician would know that this more special than just an everyday manicure  The technician stated after she started my nails, that she did not have the proper brush that she needed in order to do the manicure.  So like most places- they paint the white, and then go back later with a brush to create the crisp, perfect line.  Since she did not have the brush to do that- she used a q- tip.  So obviously the lines are not perfect or even.  Along with the lines being uneven- some are thicker than others, and the edges go up, instead of down.  My nails are not at all filed and shaped pretty either.  For $40 (+ a tip)- I really expect them to look right.  I went during my lunch hour, and it was supposed to be 30 minute appointment, but the appointment took a little bit over an hour.  I understand that french takes a little extra time- but this seemed like quite a bit extra.  I was late for work, and had to hurry out of there when she was finished and did not want to be even more late to work to stay there to make a complaint.  I wish I would have- but I also felt bad because the technician was trying so hard- but they are just not up to par.

I'm conflicted, but I don't know that I'll return.  I loved it to so much the first time, I even sent friends over there.  But after this time- I am not happy with the product.  I wish it wasn't gel- because I can't even take the polish off myself.  So I'm forced to have nails that I am unhappy with, or go to somewhere else and pay to have this taken off, and then pay to have them re done- all before a 6am flight on Wednesday morning, and it's Monday afternoon....
Revise this with your best effort:
I first discovered this delightful salon on Yelp while searching for a manicure place in downtown/CBD. I visited on March 8, 2013, and opted for their "Mini Manicure" which is reasonably priced at $15! I selected an OPI polish, and the nail technician did an impeccable job. To my surprise, even after ten days, my manicure remained chip-free. It was truly remarkable! My nails looked absolutely fabulous, and both the technician and other stylists were friendly and welcoming. There was a manager or owner working at the front desk, who was incredibly warm and hospitable. The salon has a trendy and tranquil ambiance that adds to its overall appeal.

Satisfied with my first appointment, I returned today but left feeling disappointed. I sought out the same nail technician, and we conversed while she worked on my nails. The person at the front desk, who seemed to be an owner or manager (although different from my first visit) was extremely friendly, talkative, and welcoming. However, this time, I needed a gel manicure in French style as I am part of a wedding this weekend. I presumed the technician would understand that this was a more formal manicure than an everyday one since I mentioned the wedding. Regrettably, the technician informed me, after starting on my nails, that she did not have the appropriate brush for the manicure. Typically, salons will paint the white tips and later use a brush to create a neat, defined line. Due to the lack of a brush, she used a q-tip instead. Consequently, the lines are visibly uneven and the thickness varies. Additionally, the edges of my nails are cut unevenly and even facing upward. For a total cost of $40 (plus a tip), I expected a much higher standard of quality. Although French manicures may require extra time, this appointment seemed to take considerably longer than necessary. I came during my lunch hour, expecting a 30-minute appointment, but it ended up taking slightly over an hour. I understand the need for attention to detail, but this delay resulted in me being late for work, and I had to rush out of the salon without the chance to lodge a complaint. I feel conflicted, as the technician was clearly making an effort, but the services provided were subpar.

At this point, I am uncertain whether I will return to this salon. I enjoyed my first experience so much that I even recommended it to friends. However, after this disappointing second visit, I am dissatisfied with the overall outcome. It is particularly frustrating because gel polish cannot be easily removed at home, leaving me with no choice but to either tolerate nails I am unhappy with or go to another salon to have the gel removed and redone, all before my 6 am flight on Wednesday morning—bearing in mind it is currently Monday afternoon.

input:
A bit off the beaten path for most tourists, as it is in the Marigny, but worth the trip. Sure, the place is not perfect, but there are ultra-expensive restaurants in the FQ that are also not perfect. Look, cheap food, especially food this good, gives "wiggle" room for imperfections.

Breakfast served all day is a bonus. Sometimes you just got to have a lox omelet (under $10) late in the day. The restaurant boasts vegetarian and *gasp* vegan dishes, but someone needs to tell them that cheese doesn't fit into either of those categories. That aside, the french fry poboy, and the mac 'n cheese sandwiches are amazing. So is the Saturday Blue Plate of BBQ Chicken legs. 

Every entree is under $10, well except for the Friday Blue Plate, but why quibble? And who can argue with $5 Bloody Mary's, especially ones that are this good?
Revise this with your best effort:
Located in the Marigny, a slightly unconventional spot for most tourists, this hidden gem is definitely worth venturing off the beaten path. Although not flawless, it stands to reason that even pricey restaurants in the FQ aren't perfect either. In fact, the charm of this place lies in its affordability, allowing for the occasional imperfections to be overlooked.

One of the delightful perks is that they serve breakfast all day long, so you can indulge in a mouthwatering lox omelet (for less than $10) even during the later hours. While the restaurant proudly offers vegetarian and even vegan options, it's worth mentioning that cheese doesn't quite fit into those categories. Nonetheless, their french fry poboy and mac 'n cheese sandwiches are truly outstanding. Also, don't miss out on their scrumptious Saturday Blue Plate featuring BBQ Chicken legs.

The best part? Every single entrée on the menu is priced under $10, with the exception of the Friday Blue Plate, but let's not nitpick, shall we? And who can resist the temptation of their delectable $5 Bloody Mary's, especially when they're made to perfection like these?

input: Awesome sangria.  Rotating craft beers. Pizza and calzones keep me coming back
Revise this with your best effort: I can't get enough of the fantastic sangria they serve, wonderfully refreshing and bursting with flavor. And when it comes to their craft beer selection, they always have an exciting rotation of unique and delightful brews. But it's not just the drinks that keep me coming back; their mouthwatering pizzas and calzones are simply irresistible.

input: First off, it is a bar through and through. The alcohol selection is good and the drinks well mixed. It is also a casino bar, so you'll be paying higher than average prices. There is a small food menu, but the selection isn't that great. To add insult to injury the food made me ill. The reviews about service aren't exaggerations. We, too, practically had to tackle our server to order food and drinks many of times. Not my preferred place to go when there are so many better options in Reno.
Revise this with your best effort: First and foremost, it is definitely a bar, offering a wide variety of quality alcoholic beverages, expertly mixed to perfection. Additionally, being a casino bar, it is important to note that prices may be slightly higher than average. While a limited food menu is available, it may not offer a vast selection to suit all tastes. Regrettably, my personal experience with the food was unsatisfactory, as it left me feeling unwell. The remarks regarding the level of service found within the establishment were indeed accurate. On numerous occasions, my party and I faced considerable difficulties in getting our server's attention to place orders for both food and drinks. Considering the abundance of superior alternatives in Reno, this particular venue would not be my preferred choice when seeking a dining or drinking experience.

input: Rude and unprofessional staff. I called today to find out if they had availability over the Thanksgiving holiday and the staff was short and basically said no then hung up the phone. I will take my business elsewhere.
Revise this with your best effort: I had a negative experience with the staff at this establishment, as they displayed rudeness and unprofessionalism. Upon calling to inquire about availability during the Thanksgiving holiday, I encountered a short and dismissive response from the staff, essentially stating that there was no availability, followed by an abrupt hang-up. This kind of treatment is unacceptable, and as a result, I have decided to seek alternative options for my business.

input: Went there due to having a gc, and was suprised at the great food!  Had the sauteed stirfry over spinach, and my gf had the abundant pile of nachos.  They have a pretty decent selection of other delectables, and the day time bartender was very pleasant.  I would recommend to someone who wants a friendly atmosphere with decent food in a sports bar setting.  They actually do have sports playing on the tvs.
Revise this with your best effort: I visited the place thanks to a gift certificate and was pleasantly surprised by the incredible food! I opted for the sautéed stir fry over spinach, while my girlfriend enjoyed a generous pile of nachos. In addition to their mouthwatering menu options, they also offer a decent variety of other delicious dishes. The daytime bartender was extremely friendly, adding to the welcoming atmosphere. I would highly recommend this spot to anyone seeking a friendly sports bar setting with tasty food. They even have multiple TVs playing sports for your entertainment.

input: Horrible experience, pizza was soggy and cold when I received it, took 2 hours until I actually received my order as well. Absolutely no communication on my order, even after calling twice. Once I finally received the pizza I called to get my money back, which was communicated that I would not be charged, soon to find out that I was charged the very next day. I highly recommend never ordering from here, service was horrible and they were extremely rude. I won't be ordering from here again and either should you.
Revise this with your best effort: I had an extremely unpleasant experience with this pizza place. To my disappointment, the pizza I received was both soggy and cold. Moreover, it took an exhausting 2 hours for my order to finally arrive, with absolutely no communication or updates provided throughout the wait, despite me calling twice to check on my order. Even after the long wait, when I called to request a refund as instructed, I was assured that I wouldn't be charged, only to discover the next day that I had indeed been charged. The level of service I received was incredibly poor, and the staff's attitude was outright rude. Based on this experience, I strongly advise against ordering from this establishment. I myself have decided not to order from here in the future, and I suggest you do the same.

input:
Incredible service and incredible food! The black bean ravioli is succulent! The bone-in steak was flavorful and amazingly juicy and delicious. And the best of all, service was perfect. From the friendly hostess to the waiter to the chef who personally came over to make sure we enjoyed our food, everyone really made us feel at home. 

As an added bonus, the ambiance is beautiful. Decor, lighting, and fireplace makes the place very homely. 

Highly recommended. I went as a group of four and had an excellent time.
Revise this with your best effort:
Absolutely outstanding service and absolutely delectable cuisine! The black bean ravioli is simply divine, bursting with succulence! The bone-in steak exudes exceptional flavors, leaving your taste buds in awe of its juiciness and sheer deliciousness. Moreover, the paramount highlight was the flawless service. From the warm and welcoming hostess to the attentive waiter, and even the chef's personal visit to ensure our utmost enjoyment, we felt truly embraced and cherished throughout our dining experience, as if in the comfort of our own home. 

As an added delight, the ambiance captivates with its breathtaking beauty. The exquisite decor, subtle lighting, and inviting fireplace create an incredibly cozy and inviting atmosphere.

I wholeheartedly recommend this establishment. My party of four had an absolutely superb time, and I am confident that you will too.

input:
I've been driving by this location for several weeks anticipating their opening.  With the established Legends Sports Bar directly across the street I thought this place must have something very special to feel they can compete.

They took over the building that was prevriously used by the Ruby River Steakhouse.  The owners apparently opted not to change a thing about the indoor seating.  Gone are all the cowboy boots, up are various team jerseys. It looks like somebody went to Pro Image at the mall to decorate the place.  Nothing appears to be autographed or evoke a sense of authenticity.

Video games are available for the kids, so bring your quarters.  No dart boards, shuffleboard, air hockey or pool tables.  This is pretty much a dine and drink only establishment.

More TV's in the place than I could count (I figure at least 20), all tuned to ESPN or ESPN2.  No clue at this time if they are choosing to use Direct TV, Dish, or Cable One for their service.  However, they already have made one of the biggest mistakes I think most wannabe sports bars make; they broadcast music rather than sound from a live sporting event.  With live sporting events available almost everyday from 12pm - 12am, you would think they would want to try to emphasize that rather than muzak (tuned to a country station; still feels like the Ruby River).

A word of advice here, if you want people to stay and eat and drink, you gotta give them something on which to focus their attention.  The sounds of the game will get their attention.  They came to a sports bar to think about sports, not Conway Twitty.

Typically, when I see the word pub in a restaurant name, I think it is just beer and wine, but it looks like Timeout has a full bar with several specialty drinks.  With a designated driver, it may be fun to experiment.

The food is typical sports bar fare; salads, burgers, pasta.  Most items will cost $9 - $11, with entrees running more.  A few twists on their offerings will ensure that I stop in to try something different, but unless the atmosphere improves, I think I will always leave a little disappointed. 

Those staying at the nearby motel may like the proximity, but I think they might find the walk across the street to Legends worth the extra steps.

Happy Hour 2pm - 6pm Monday -  Friday; Late Happy Hour 10pm - close Monday - Thursday.  Happy Hour all day Sunday.
Revise this with your best effort:
I have been driving past this location for several weeks, eagerly awaiting its opening. Considering the presence of the renowned Legends Sports Bar across the street, I couldn't help but wonder what makes this place stand out.

This new establishment has taken over the building previously occupied by the Ruby River Steakhouse. Interestingly, the owners have chosen to keep the indoor seating exactly the same. The cowboy boots are nowhere to be seen, replaced by various team jerseys. Frankly, it appears as if someone simply decorated the place with items from Pro Image at the mall. Sadly, none of the decorations seem to be autographed or give off a sense of authenticity.

If you're bringing kids along, they'll be pleased to find video games available, so don't forget your quarters. However, if you were hoping for dart boards, shuffleboard, air hockey, or pool tables, you'll be disappointed. This establishment is primarily focused on dining and drinking.
