input: Unfortunately, I'm NOT happy after coming to this salon yet again. I got a message from the owner saying he'd like to have me come in to receive a FREE service because they previously ruined my hair. So, I thought since he's the owner my hair would turn out good but I was wrong. I'm really unhappy with this whole experience. I showed him multiple photos on google of what I wanted done to my hair which was a lot of blonde. I told him I do not want any ORANGE in my hair as I wanted a "white blonde". He said you won't have any orange in your hair. I have a message from him the OWNER saying I would receive a FREE service if I deleted my previous review. He should of NEVER offered a free service if it wasn't really free! So, I said how much because I thought I was getting my hair done for free. He said since your hair is long and thick you'll have to pay for the hair color and "medicine" but he won't charge me for his time. I said ok how much he said $80. He said it would cost me $180 if he didn't give me a discount which is very pricey. He put a lot of highlights on my hair and worked quickly as he seemed to want to rush on my hair which I do not like. My hair is important to me, I don't want my hair to fall out. He said this medicine he's gonna put on my hair is $50 for a treatment and that I needed it because of the blonde going on my hair which I know any coloring is damaging and blonde is very damaging but he said he charges everyone who gets hair color for this so called medicine which they mix into the color you dye your hair. You can purchase the entire set online (3 bottles) for $75 which is supposed to give you like 15 applications so he's definitely charging a lot of money! He only put No.1 on my hair and not No.2 or No.3. He also had a lady (the receptionist) wash out my hair? Ok, even though she was nice why would he have her do that when she said she knows nothing about hair because I asked if she's styling my hair and she said she doesn't do hair and I wouldn't want her to do my hair. As I was waiting there was a lady next to me, she got her hair cut and a perm. She was done but she wasn't happy, she told the lady she didn't like the hair cut and she had her style it more and trim off a little more but the lady still wasn't happy. The girl told the client when she washes her hair it will be better.. um how? I know she left very unhappy! Also the lady behind me was getting her hair cut and when he (the owner) was done cutting her hair she looked in the mirror and wanted it different and styled different so that made me have to wait longer but 2 clients were not happy and also myself. That's not a good look TJ nail and spa! I had a towel on my head and waited about 30 mins just to get my hair blow dried because he was cutting another clients hair. I seen orange roots, I was mad!!! He finally came over and I said I don't like the orange color on my roots, can you put a toner on my hair and he said it's not orange it's the lighting. The lighting?! It wasn't the lighting! He proceeds to blow dry hair and then starts straighten it without asking me if I wanted it straightened or curled, you are supposed to pick how you want your hair styled. At that point I knew my hair wasn't what I wanted and it wasn't gonna be fixed even if I wanted it too. I just sat there in the hair, mad and yet again very disappointed! I looked in the mirror and seen my hair damaged and brittle, orange and brassy and not even close to what I wanted. There goes my money down the drain, yet again. I will not be back to get my hair ruined and he made me delete my previous review which was also 0-1 stars before I left his salon but I had to write this one, this is real, this is honest, beware of getting your hair completely ruined and nothing close to what you want! Like I said I showed the OWNER multiple photos and I stated I did NOT want any orange on my hair but I did have orange on my hair, I didn't get what I wanted like he said, he said he doesn't mess up, he's been doing hair for years. As a salon owner I think he should take the time to really do what the client wants and achieve what the client wants done to their hair, if the workersowner would do that then there shouldn't be any bad reviews but there is so that shows you they do not care, not even the owner cares. They just want to rush and get done to get paid, they don't care if the customer is happy or not. There are more bad reviews from people going to this salon and having horrible experiences but he is bribing people to delete their bad reviews because he told me the bad reviews is hurting his business which is why people do reviews, to let people know this place is awesome or this place is horrible, beware, stay away. I do reviews to let people know the good, the bad and the ugly. I do reviews anywhere and I'm always 100% honest. So, if bad reviews hurt his business that is all on him and his employees not me or anyone else.
Revise this with your best effort:
Unfortunately, my experience at this salon has left me feeling extremely unhappy. Despite receiving a message from the owner offering a complimentary service to rectify a previous hair mishap, my expectations were not met. I made it clear that I wanted a "white blonde" look and showed the owner several reference photos from Google, emphasizing that I did not want any orange tones in my hair. He assured me that there would be no orange. Additionally, he promised a free service if I deleted my previous review, but it turns out that it wasn't really free. I was informed that I would still have to pay for the hair color and a treatment, amounting to $80. The owner claimed that this was a discounted rate and that the original cost would have been $180. 

During the appointment, I noticed the owner rushed through my hair, applying numerous highlights quickly, which made me uncomfortable. He also insisted on using an expensive "medicine" that he said was necessary for the coloring process. Upon further research, I discovered that this product could be purchased online for a fraction of the price he charged. Furthermore, the owner only applied one part of the three-step treatment, neglecting the other necessary steps. 

To my surprise, the receptionist, who admitted to knowing nothing about hair, was tasked with washing my hair. This puzzled me, as it seemed unprofessional to have someone unskilled handle such an important part of the process. 

While waiting, I witnessed another client express dissatisfaction with her haircut and styling. Despite the hairstylist's attempts to fix it, the client remained unhappy. Another client, seated behind me, also expressed dissatisfaction with her haircut and requested further changes. These instances, along with my own disappointing experience, reflected poorly on the salon. 

I experienced a significant delay in having my hair blow-dried because the owner was occupied with another client's haircut. During this time, I noticed prominent orange roots, which infuriated me. When I brought this to the owner's attention, he dismissed it as a lighting issue, even though it was clear to me that the color was not what I desired. 

To make matters worse, the owner proceeded to straighten my hair without consulting me on my preference for styling. This demonstrated a lack of consideration for my personal preferences. At that point, I realized that my hair would not be fixed to my satisfaction, no matter how much I wanted it to be. I walked out of the salon feeling angry and immensely disappointed. 

Upon examining my hair in the mirror, I could see significant damage, brittleness, and an undesired orange, brassy tone. It was far from the result I had anticipated and another waste of my money. I will not be returning to this salon, especially after being coerced into deleting my previous negative review. This review serves as a testament to the truth of my experience and a warning to others to beware of having their hair ruined and their desires disregarded at this establishment. 

Despite showing the owner multiple reference photos and explicitly stating my aversion to any orange tones, my hair still ended up with unwanted orange coloration. The owner claimed to be experienced and never made mistakes, but this experience proved otherwise. As a salon owner, it is imperative that he takes the time and effort to fulfill client expectations and achieve the desired results. Unfortunately, it appears that neither the owner nor the salon's employees genuinely care about customer satisfaction. Frustratingly, there are numerous negative reviews from other dissatisfied customers, yet the owner resorts to bribing people to delete their negative feedback. This behavior demonstrates a lack of concern for the customer experience and only further damages their reputation. I believe in providing honest and accurate reviews to inform others of my experiences, whether positive or negative. If negative reviews harm their business, it is solely a result of their own actions and the poor service they provide.

input:
I am so glad we had our wedding here!!! I cannot say enough what a pleasure it was to work with Breanna, the venue manager and Eli, the food and beverage director. Our wedding here was a destination wedding, so we were very concerned about making sure all of our family and friends that travelled a long way to get to our wedding had a good time. Being a couple straight out of grad school, we were also very concerned with keeping the cost manageable. Everything worked out on all accounts! 

We first picked the venue for two reasons: the price was right and the venue is GORGEOUS. The pricing was very straightforward, which we really appreciated, and when looking at other options in the Santa Barbara area, the Riviera mansion was pretty comparable with other venues which are not all inclusive (ones where you have to find your own caterer, rent linens, etc etc). Planning a wedding without a coordinator and from across the country, it was also definitely worth it for us to go with a venue that minimized the amount of details we would have to think about.

The looks and layout of the place are what sold us though. With people coming from the east coast and middle of the country, we wanted something that would really showcase Santa Barbara's cool architecture and vibe. The mansion is exactly that.  The layout is also pretty perfect for a multigenerational wedding. We were able to enjoy the California weather for our ceremony and cocktail hour outside, then go inside for dinner, avoiding the cooler night air. Later, we could turn up the party in the bar/dance floor area, while the older folks talked and relaxed on the couches in the living room. It really has something for everyone.

What I didn't realize when we picked it was how absolutely awesome all the staff would be to work with. Breanna was super helpful, answering all my questions promptly and pleasantly, and accommodating my sometimes short notice visits to the area. When we did our walkthrough a couple of days before the wedding, Breanna and Eli paid attention to every detail and made sure we were taken care of, as they did the day of the wedding too. Eli was incredibly attentive and easy to work with! My dad is in the restaurant industry and was in charge of setting up desserts (we had family make some traditional desserts, as well as got some cupcakes from Enjoy Cupcakes- also a great idea!). Eli worked with him to get whatever he needed, risers, tablecloths, etc and was really sweet about it. 

The attention to bartending at the Riviera Mansion deserves a paragraph of its own. Breanna worked with me and the bartender (who's name I forget but has worked there for 20 years and is also incredibly awesome) to create a peach moscow mule as our signature drink (our colors were peach and green) and get it to taste just right. She even arranged it so we had fresh peaches! At the wedding, everyone raved about them, even guests who usually prefer something more manly sounding. The staff had all drinks ready to go for our cocktail hour, and also passed trays of drinks, so there was never a line at the bar (something guests also specifically mentioned that they appreciated). Hell, Eli even followed me with my drink for a couple of minutes around dinner since my hands were full of other things! Really spectacular and attentive service.

Five stars all around. It was absolutely a joy to have our wedding here.

input:
Yeah, I know what you're thinking. One Wawa store is pretty much the same as another, so why even bother writing a review? But I think we have a winner here.

When this Wawa store opened for business, gas prices at gas stations all along Concord Pike fell by 30 cents per gallon just to compete with them. Sure, this Wawa store could've followed the general pricing in the area and lowered prices just a few cents, keeping the bulk of the profit. But no, they'll have none of that. I love a store that is on the side of my wallet!

Secondly, I love the automatic start/stop digital air pump. So far, I've only seen that at BJ's Wholesale and Sheetz. It's a snap to use and I get the exact tire pressure every time.

As for service, they seem nice and relatively efficient. The internal layout of the store is the new style that I first saw in Newark. Having separate non-cigarette cashier lines may speed things up in peak periods, although I've never been there during the day, so I wouldn't know.
Revise this with your best effort:
I understand if you're skeptical, but trust me, this Wawa store is worth reviewing. When they opened, gas prices in the surrounding gas stations dropped a whopping 30 cents per gallon just to compete. Instead of pocketing the extra profit, this store decided to prioritize its customers' wallets. Impressive, right?

Another standout feature is their automatic start/stop digital air pump. I have only come across such convenience at BJ's Wholesale and Sheetz. It's incredibly simple to use and provides me with accurate tire pressure readings every time.

In terms of service, the staff appears friendly and reasonably efficient. The store's internal layout follows the new modern style I first saw in Newark. The separate cashier lines for non-cigarette purchases may help expedite transactions during busy periods, although I have yet to visit during peak day hours myself.

input:
For a seafood restaurant at the edge of pear expectations should be set high. My wife and I have come here 3 times now and ordered different plates off the menu each time. This last time we ordered cioppino, clam chowder, and a crab salad sandwich;
*Good - clam chowder (excellent flavor and consistency) would order again.
*Not great - cioppino (lacked flavor & a variety of sea food/lack there of) would not order again
*Pass - crab salad sandwich (lacked flavor, mayo was overpowering, crab flavor was almost non-existent, side of onion rings too greasy) - would not order again 
The overall experience is okay, better if seated outside right on the pear overlooking the ocean, inside is very small. Service is good but be prepared to wait a bit to be seated. 
Is it worth a visit? Yes, but be selective of what you order as the menu tends to be a hit and miss.
Revise this with your best effort:
Expectations for a seafood restaurant on the edge of a pier should be set high. My wife and I have dined here 3 times, trying different dishes each visit. During our most recent visit, we ordered the cioppino, clam chowder, and crab salad sandwich. 
The clam chowder was a standout, boasting excellent flavor and consistency. Without hesitation, I would order it again. 
Sadly, the cioppino fell short. It lacked flavor and a variety of seafood, making it a dish I would not choose again. 
The crab salad sandwich was also disappointing. The lack of flavor, overpowering mayo, and almost nonexistent crab flavor left much to be desired. Additionally, the side of onion rings was overly greasy. This dish is definitely not one I would recommend ordering again. 
The overall experience was satisfactory, especially if seated outside with a view of the ocean. However, the interior of the restaurant is quite small. The service provided was good, although there may be a slight wait to be seated. 
Is it worth a visit? Yes, but it's important to be selective with your order, as the menu can be hit or miss.

input: Chef Kevin Sbraga knows fried chicken. My first exposure to his succulent birds was the hot chicken at The Fat Ham. Lo and behold, his lavender honey fried chicken tops its spicy cousin. The chicken is brined in buttermilk, dredged in seasoned flour and sits for ten minutes. It's then coated with a second round of flour and dropped into the fryer. The chicken (breast, wing, thigh, drumstick) is drizzled with lavender honey and sprinkled with salt and ground pink peppercorns. It comes with a buttermilk biscuit, whipped honey-thyme butter, and red bliss potato salad. It is some of the best fried chicken I've eaten in a long time. Crunchy, crispy coating on the outside with a juicy, moist inside. The sweet honey glaze is truly outstanding and finger lickin' good. The biscuit is awesome. I would definitely order this dish again and again. I got the salty but delicious fried smelts with chili pepper aioli as an appetizer. My friend Chris W got the filet mignon and butter poached king crab surf and turf. For dessert, I had a slice of salted pecan pie and he had the ice cream sundae. Every dish at Juniper Commons was top-notch. Chef Sbraga does it again!
Revise this with your best effort: Chef Kevin Sbraga is undoubtedly a master when it comes to fried chicken. I had my first taste of his delectable poultry at The Fat Ham, where the hot chicken left quite an impression. However, it was his lavender honey fried chicken that truly stole the show, surpassing its spicy counterpart. The process begins with brining the chicken in tangy buttermilk, followed by a dredging in seasoned flour and a brief ten-minute rest. Then, the chicken is coated with a second layer of flour before taking a dip into the fryer. To elevate its flavors, the succulent chicken pieces (breast, wing, thigh, drumstick) are drizzled with lavender honey and sprinkled with salt and ground pink peppercorns. This mouthwatering creation is accompanied by a heavenly buttermilk biscuit, whipped honey-thyme butter, and a side of red bliss potato salad. It's safe to say that this is some of the most exceptional fried chicken I've savored in a long time. The exterior boasts a delightful crunch and crispiness, while the inside remains succulent and juicy. The sweet honey glaze is truly exceptional and leaves you reaching for more. And let's not forget about the incredible biscuit, which deserves its own applause. Without a doubt, I would eagerly order this dish again and again. As an appetizer, I decided to indulge in the fried smelts, which were perfectly seasoned with a touch of saltiness, accompanied by a tantalizing chili pepper aioli. My companion, Chris W, opted for the filet mignon and butter poached king crab surf and turf, a harmonious marriage of land and sea. For the grand finale, dessert was a delightful slice of salted pecan pie for me, while Chris indulged in a heavenly ice cream sundae. Every dish that graced our table at Juniper Commons showcased unparalleled excellence. Chef Sbraga has once again triumphed, demonstrating his culinary prowess.

input:
I really wanted to like Casselli's, but it wasn't in the cards. Maybe I just caught them on a bad night, but I didn't really enjoy much about my visit. The waiter was very unpleasant - was banging down the plates and glasses on the table when he delivered them. Maybe he was having a bad day, but I still would have expected better. 

We had mixed experiences with the food. Mine and our friends' was OK, but my wife's baked ravioli would have been more use to a hockey team for use as pucks. They were really overdone - woefully overdone. 

The worst part was that our table was next to the opera singer guy. He was singing extremely loudly and it was nigh impossible to maintain a conversation - especially coupled with how close we were to the table next to us and their attempts to speak over Opera Guy.

Part of me wants to give them another chance (since I hate writing bad reviews) and the other part is annoyed over the waiter's attitude. I probably will not go back. There are so many good Italian restaurants worth visiting that the opportunity cost of returning to Casselli's seems too high.

On the upside, they have somewhat convenient parking in the lot behind the restaurant (near the Shawmont School).

Note: cash-only.
Revise this with your best effort:
I had high hopes for Casselli's, but unfortunately, it fell short of my expectations. Perhaps it was an off night, but my overall experience left much to be desired. The waiter's demeanor was quite unpleasant, forcefully placing plates and glasses on the table. Even if he was having a bad day, I still expected better professionalism.

The quality of the food varied among our group. While mine and our friends' dishes were just okay, my wife's baked ravioli could have easily doubled as hockey pucks. They were terribly overdone, which was incredibly disappointing.

To make matters worse, our table was situated next to an opera singer, whose excessive volume made it nearly impossible to hold a conversation. The proximity of the adjacent table, along with their futile attempts to speak over the booming opera, added to the discomfort of the situation.

Part of me wants to give Casselli's another chance, as I prefer not to write negative reviews, but the waiter's attitude has left a lasting impression. I highly doubt I will choose to return. The abundance of excellent Italian restaurants in the area outweighs the potential benefits of revisiting Casselli's.

On a positive note, they do offer relatively convenient parking in the lot behind the restaurant, particularly near the Shawmont School.

Please note that Casselli's is a cash-only establishment.

input: I will not return to this location. I contacted the manager in regards to a poorly made pizza I received, he replied to my online inquiry but never followed through on taking care of things. I even sent a photo to prove that the appearance of the pizza was not acceptable, and I never heard back from him.
Revise this with your best effort: After a disappointing experience, I have decided not to revisit this establishment. Despite reaching out to the manager about a subpar pizza I received, his response failed to address the issue. Despite providing photographic evidence of the unacceptable appearance of the pizza, I never received any further communication from him.

input:
Amazing food!! and  the whole experience is great there every time. I suggest going there with a  group of about 6 people so it doesn't totally break the bank but if you've got the money then who cares! Have fun!

First you enter in and select the wine you would like. The staff is helpful and knowledgeable about their stock. (And if for some reason at the end you didn't  finish your bottle they will cork it back up for you to take.) Then select your cheese platter. Lots of yummy stinky cheese to select  from and prosciutto. I wish they had more cured meats but it's all yummy anyway. You pay for the wine and cheese there. Which in a large group one or two people can take care of this  part. 

Then going to get a seat can be difficult but just be patient. There's outdoor seating that's very nice and always a live band playing. Inside upstairs is nice as well. Once you're all set with your wine and group it's time to order. Go to the window and play your order. Definite things you must get.... the bacon wrapped dates stuffed with chorizo and the goat cheese and mushroom dish....AMAZING! Although everything I've ever had here is great. 

Then just wait for your cheese platter, food and enjoy!
Revise this with your best effort:
The food at this place is absolutely amazing, and the overall experience is always exceptional. I highly recommend going with a group of around six people to keep the cost reasonable, but if you're willing to splurge, it's definitely worth it. Get ready to have a great time!

Upon entering, take some time to select the wine you prefer. The staff is incredibly helpful and knowledgeable about their selection. And if, by any chance, you can't finish your bottle, they will kindly cork it up for you to take home. After choosing your wine, it's time to pick out your cheese platter. They offer a variety of delicious and aromatic cheeses, along with prosciutto. While I wish they had a more extensive selection of cured meats, everything on offer is still tasty. You can pay for the wine and cheese right at the counter, and in larger groups, a couple of people can handle this part.

Finding a seat can sometimes be a bit challenging, but just be patient. The outdoor seating is lovely, with a live band always playing. If you prefer indoors, upstairs is also a nice option. Once you're settled with your wine and group, it's time to place your food order. Go to the window and present your order. There are definitely a few must-try items, such as the bacon wrapped dates stuffed with chorizo and the goat cheese and mushroom dish. They are absolutely amazing! However, honestly, everything I've ever had here is great.

Now all you have to do is wait for your cheese platter and food to arrive, and then enjoy!

input: Came to see my son's band Last Frontier. The staff and food here is top notch!   Had the porkbelly and fish nachos.  Awesome.  Great selection of whisky. Great sound system for the band.
Revise this with your best effort: I recently attended my son's band, Last Frontier, and I must say, this place exceeded my expectations. The attentive staff and the incredible quality of food truly made it a memorable experience. I indulged in the delectable pork belly and fish nachos, which were absolutely outstanding. Additionally, the impressive variety of whisky options delighted my taste buds. Not to mention, the sound system provided impeccable clarity and enhanced the band's performance. Overall, it was an exceptional evening that surpassed all my expectations.

input: I have never had any issues with this place and we have been here many times. This is the only paint store I have ever been to besides places like Home Depot or Lowes...so as far as a paint places goes it ranks high on my list. Not only do they sale paint but also everything that you need to get the job done. Everyone is extremely friendly and helpful. They keep your paint information on file so you don't have to remember it if you need to purchase more. I normally go when there is a sale on paint...keep an eye out for 30% off....we buy interior Super Paint which was a part of the deal.
Revise this with your best effort: I have never encountered any issues with this establishment, despite being frequent visitors. This is the sole paint store I have patronized, apart from larger chains like Home Depot or Lowes. In terms of paint stores, it undoubtedly holds a high position on my list. It not only offers a wide range of paint options but also supplies all the necessary tools to complete any paint-related project. The staff here are exceptionally friendly and always willing to lend a hand. One convenient aspect is that they keep a record of your paint preferences, eliminating the need for you to recall specific details when making future purchases. Personally, I often take advantage of paint sales and recommend keeping an eye out for the occasional 30% discount. During one such sale, we acquired interior Super Paint as part of a tempting deal.

input: The food was great, the service excellent.  Had dinner outside on the deck, saw lots of dolphins.  Will come back for sure.
Revise this with your best effort: The dining experience was absolutely extraordinary, with outstanding food and impeccable service. We had the pleasure of enjoying our dinner on the enchanting deck, where we were fortunate enough to witness numerous playful dolphins in the nearby waters. Rest assured, we will unquestionably be returning for this remarkable experience.

input:
I find it hugely ironic that WF is trying to reposition itself as a 'value' food store right now when others (i.e. Trader Joe's up the street) have been doing that for years.  For value, go elsewhere.  For pretty food, lovely store displays and a feeling of smugness, check out Whole Foods.

Despite my snark, I have to admit that it's nice to see an enormous, clean and well stocked yuppie market in Reno finally.  Now that this town has been rated by National Geographic as a top outdoors place to live in, it needs the retail to support that (and I don't mean another REI).  For myself, I'm too cheap to look seriously at this place for my regular shopping needs, but for lunch and the odd stopover, it's awesome.   Beautiful produce, drool inducing cheese selections and a bakery that would break my budget if I bought everything that struck my fancy.

Plus it's proximity to the freeway (for those of us who do our shopping based on distance from the 395 or 80) makes it an ideal stop to/from the airport.
Revise this with your best effort:
It's quite amusing to me that Whole Foods is currently attempting to rebrand itself as a 'value' food store, considering that other places like Trader Joe's have been successfully doing so for years. If you're looking for value, I would recommend looking elsewhere. However, if you're in search of aesthetically pleasing food, delightful store displays, and a sense of self-satisfaction, then Whole Foods is worth checking out.

Putting my sarcasm aside, I must admit that it is refreshing to finally have a large, clean, and well-stocked upscale market in Reno. With the recent recognition by National Geographic as a top outdoors place to live, it's crucial for the town to have retail options that support this reputation (and I don't mean another REI). Personally, I'm too thrifty to consider Whole Foods as my primary grocery shopping destination, but it's certainly a great spot for lunch or the occasional visit. The assortment of beautiful produce, irresistible cheese selections, and a bakery that tempts me to overspend is truly remarkable.

Moreover, its convenient location near the freeway (perfect for those of us who base our shopping choices on proximity to the 395 or 80) makes it an ideal stopover when traveling to and from the airport.

input: Great service and awesome food!!!! We go here all the time. Each time it is excellent! Very very Stellar
Revise this with your best effort: Phenomenal service and exceptional food!!! This is our go-to spot that never disappoints. Every visit is an outstanding experience! Truly exceptional.

input:
Monthly lunch with my fellow colleagues the other day and the person assigned to get lunch ordered from Fresh and had it delivered. 

My selection was the Chopped Italian salad. The salad consists of mixed greens, salami, smoked turkey, tomato, garbanzo beans and parmesan cheese served with the house vinaigrette. The salad was lacking for me. I think such a salad would be so much better with a few more Italian-esque ingredients in it, perhaps a little more anitpasto like. I know, it's not advertised as antipasto but c'mon....this salad was boring.  Throw in a couple of olives, some artichoke hearts, some sliced pepperoncinis. Maybe my tastebuds were having an off day but the salami wasn't very flavorful either. Charge a couple dollars more for a more inventive salad. Please!

I do want to give them another chance since so many reviews on here are glowing. Maybe I need to stick with a panini or something but I really do love salads for summer lunches.
Revise this with your best effort: During our monthly lunch with my fellow colleagues, one of us was assigned to order food from Fresh and have it delivered. On this occasion, I decided to go for the Chopped Italian salad. The salad comprised a mix of greens, salami, smoked turkey, tomato, garbanzo beans, and parmesan cheese, accompanied by the house vinaigrette. However, I found the salad to be lacking. In my opinion, it would have been much better with a few more Italian-inspired ingredients, perhaps incorporating some antipasto elements. I understand that it is not labeled as an antipasto salad, but I couldn't help but feel that it was a bit boring. Adding a couple of olives, artichoke hearts, and sliced pepperoncinis could have made a significant difference. Additionally, the salami itself did not have a very distinctive flavor. I would be willing to pay a couple of extra dollars for a more innovative salad option. Despite my underwhelming experience, I am open to giving Fresh another chance since many reviews are highly positive. Maybe next time, I should stick to a panini or some other dish, although I have always had a preference for salads during summer lunches.

input: Tyson is on point, sharp and follows through on his word. I brought an RV with a ford front end to him not only did he get me in right away but he finished ahead of time. Parts were ordered and in shop and the guys were working on it next day. I had my RV bumper replaced on the ford front end in 3 days and back on the road. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! Only place I will take my vehicles, as a business owner it's important for great service. Manny and Tyson are great!
Revise this with your best effort: Tyson consistently proves to be diligent, reliable, and true to his commitments. When I approached him with an RV featuring a ford front end, he not only ensured that I received immediate attention but also exceeded my expectations by completing the work ahead of schedule. The necessary parts were promptly ordered, readily available at the shop, and the team began working on it the very next day. Within a mere 3 days, my RV's bumper was flawlessly replaced, allowing me to hit the road again with utmost satisfaction. I cannot emphasize enough how highly I recommend their services. As a business owner myself, I greatly value exceptional customer service, making Tyson's Automotive the sole establishment where I entrust my vehicles. Manny and Tyson make an outstanding team.

input: We sat at a pretty hectic lunch at Johnny rockets in the casino. Our server was Lyndel! She was awesome! Helped us at every needy request lol... Good was good, too! I'm too full
Revise this with your best effort: We enjoyed a bustling lunch at Johnny Rockets, located in the lively casino. Our exceptional server, Lyndel, went above and beyond to assist us with every request. The food was also delicious, leaving us feeling pleasantly full.

input: This place is fantastic. The food is exceptional and the service couldn't be better. Very nice and generous people with a cool atmosphere. I eat here almost every weekend. Can't beat the Cuban espresso!
Revise this with your best effort: This place is absolutely amazing. The food here is top-notch and the service is unparalleled. The staff are incredibly friendly and hospitable, creating a cool and inviting atmosphere. I find myself dining here nearly every weekend, and I simply can't resist their unbeatable Cuban espresso!

input:
Great pizza!  The owner Pete is usually there and he's a great guy.  They have lots of fantastic pizzas, but my favorites are the California (white pizza with pieces of breaded chicken cutlet, bacon, and tomatos, and ranch dressing instead of red sauce), Meatlovers (5 meats, but the sausage is the kind that does not have fennel in it, so more points for that), Veggie pizza (they saute the veggies first before they go on the pizza, and instead of using green peppers, they use sweet peppers).  

Unfortunately, the shop was damaged by a fire in the next door laundry mat and they've been closed for a few weeks, but I can't wait for their doors to open again soon. I miss the lunch special, 2 slices and a self serve soda for $3.99.   Best local pizza you'll find in the Hatboro area.
Revise this with your best effort:
Amazing pizza place! Pete, the owner, is always there and he's an absolute gem. Their pizza selection is incredible, but my personal favorites are the California pizza, which is a mouthwatering white pizza topped with breaded chicken cutlet, bacon, tomatoes, and ranch dressing instead of the traditional red sauce. The Meatlovers pizza is another winner with its five different meats, and I especially appreciate that they use sausage without fennel in it – a small detail that makes a big difference. And let's not forget the Veggie pizza, where the veggies are sautéed beforehand and they opt for sweet peppers instead of green peppers, adding a delightful twist to the classic recipe.

Unfortunately, they had a setback recently due to a fire in the neighboring laundry mat, so they've been closed for a few weeks. However, I'm eagerly awaiting the reopening of their doors. I genuinely miss their unbeatable lunch special – 2 slices of pizza and a self-serve soda for just $3.99. Truly, this is the finest pizza joint you'll find in the Hatboro area.

input: Buffalo chicken cheese dip is amazing.  Friendly wait staff and prices are reasonable.
Revise this with your best effort: Buffalo chicken cheese dip exceeds all expectations with its incredible flavors and irresistibly creamy texture. The wait staff, known for their friendliness and warm demeanor, contribute to an overall enjoyable dining experience. Additionally, the prices offered for this delightful dish are fairly reasonable, making it an excellent choice for those seeking both quality and affordability.

input:
Pizza was so good! First time trying today and ordered online. A little mess up with their system so they didn't get my order in time. The guy called me back, told me he was making the pizza in a rush and wasn't charging me for it. 20 minutes later he came to the door himself with my Fresh, hot pizza and 2 brownies all for free. 
He was very apologetic. Customer service was fantastic and food was awesome. This is my new go to delivery joint.
Revise this with your best effort: The pizza I tried today was absolutely delicious! It was my first time ordering online and despite a slight hiccup with their system, they were able to quickly rectify the situation. The person I spoke to on the phone called me back and informed me that he was preparing my pizza on an expedited basis, without any charge at all. I was amazed when just 20 minutes later, the same person arrived at my door with a piping hot pizza and even included two delectable brownies, all as an apology for the inconvenience caused. The level of customer service I experienced was exceptional and the food itself was incredible. From now on, this will be my go-to place for delivery.

input: Came here for my 21st birthday dinner with my family and had a great experience! The food and drinks were to die for, but they were extremely overpriced. Even though the quality of food was good, I still don't think it was worth what we paid for. I recommend getting the lobster mac and cheese as an appetizer, it was probably the best mac and cheese I've ever eaten. At the end of the meal, they gave us some small complimentary desserts, even though we ordered a bunch of desserts to top off our meal. Had a great time, but definitely overpriced.
Revise this with your best effort: I celebrated my 21st birthday at this restaurant with my family and had an overall fantastic experience. The food and drinks provided were exceptional, leaving us absolutely satisfied. However, we found the prices to be excessively high in comparison to the value received. While the quality of the food was undeniably good, the cost did not align with our expectations. Despite this, I highly recommend trying their lobster mac and cheese as an appetizer, as it was easily the most delicious mac and cheese I have ever had. Additionally, towards the end of our meal, the restaurant kindly offered us some complimentary small desserts, despite the fact that we had already ordered multiple desserts to conclude our dining experience. We had a great time overall, but the high pricing did detract from the overall enjoyment.

input:
I like this place a lot. I stopped in once with friends for drinks and was eager to return for food. We finally did over the weekend. 

The ambience is very nice -- somehow ideal for both a fun date as well as for a beer and sports crowd. 

I love the open kitchen. 

Great beer selection. 

I'll definitely return for the rosemary fries, and my fiancée will return for the very good house burger.
Revise this with your best effort:
I am absolutely enamored with this place. After dropping in with some friends for drinks, my anticipation to come back and indulge in their food offerings was insatiable. Needless to say, we finally made it happen this weekend.

The ambiance of this place is simply delightful, striking the perfect balance between a charming spot for a romantic rendezvous and an enticing haven for beer enthusiasts and sports aficionados alike.

Speaking of charms, the open kitchen is an absolute treasure. It adds a touch of excitement and adds to the overall experience.

And let's not forget about the beer selection – it's phenomenal. Their diverse range ensures that every beer lover's taste buds will be satiated.

One bite of the rosemary fries and I am already aching to return for more. The flavor is unparalleled, and it has officially become a must-have for me. As for my fiancée, their house burger has won her over completely.

Without a doubt, another visit is on the horizon for me. This place has won my heart, and I can't wait to create more memorable experiences here.

input:
If you are going for the food, I would give it 5 stars, but since this is a brewhouse, I only gave it 3. 

I ordered the light flight since we went for lunch and I wasn't looking for a heavy meal. The beer was OK at best. It was bland, a little strange in after taste and uninspired. Light beers dont have to equal tasteless. My boyfriend had a "hoppy beer with citrus undertones". He could taste neither the hops or the citrus  (disclaimer - we are from VT and are used to very hoppy beers!)  

Now the food - that was great. We went at lunch time and was able to get a soup and salad for 8.95. We both had the same thing - Chicken Bruchetta salad and French Onion Soup. The portion was fantastic for a lunch size and the soup really flavorful! 

For a lunch downtown it was great, but I would go for the brews...
Revise this with your best effort:
Although the food at this brewhouse deserves a solid 5-star rating, I had to deduct a couple of stars since the main focus is on the beer. My choice for a light flight during lunch was due to my preference for a lighter meal, but unfortunately, the beer fell short of my expectations. It lacked flavor, had an odd aftertaste, and was uninspiring. Light beers can still pack a punch in terms of taste. On the other hand, my boyfriend opted for a "hoppy beer with citrus undertones," but was disappointed to find that neither the hops nor the citrus flavors were apparent (just a heads up - we come from Vermont, where we're accustomed to highly hoppy beers!). 

Now, let's shift our attention to the food - that was a winner. We dined during lunchtime and were delighted to find a soup and salad combo priced at a reasonable $8.95. We both ordered the Chicken Bruschetta salad and French Onion Soup, and were impressed by the generous portion sizes and mouthwatering flavors of the dishes.

Considering it was a downtown lunch spot, the experience was overall enjoyable. However, if you're specifically seeking exceptional brews, there might be better options to explore.

input:
This place just opened up near rivers edge apartments. It's a boutique style taqueria with a menu that anyone can enjoy. The head chef was nominated for a James Beard Award and it shows in his flavorful and diverse menu choices! The restaurant has both an outdoor and indoor setting with double doors that allow access to both, with a bar around the corner. 

I personally have tried every taco on the menu as well as the appetizers! Each taco uses fresh local ingredients with an option for vegetarians and meat eaters like myself. My two favorites are the mushroom taco and the short rib taco, both have unique and fantastic flavors. But I would recommend trying them all, you will not be disappointed! Overall a great place for lunch or dinner! I will definitely be going back soon!
Revise this with your best effort:
A delightful new establishment has recently opened its doors near the picturesque Rivers Edge Apartments - a boutique-style taqueria that is bound to please everyone. With a menu that boasts a myriad of flavors and options, it is no surprise that the head chef has been nominated for a prestigious James Beard Award. 

The restaurant itself offers both indoor and outdoor seating, with convenient double doors that allow easy access to both areas. To top it off, there is a stylish bar tucked around the corner, perfect for those seeking a refreshing beverage to complement their meal.

As an enthusiastic patron, I have had the pleasure of sampling every taco on the menu, as well as the intriguing appetizers. Each taco is crafted with care, using only the freshest local ingredients. Whether you are a devoted vegetarian or a fervent meat eater like myself, there is a delectable taco that caters to your preferences. The mushroom taco and the short rib taco have particularly captured my taste buds with their remarkable and distinct flavors. Of course, I urge you to venture and explore the entirety of the menu, for every offering is a delight that is sure to exceed your expectations.

Whether you are seeking a satisfying lunch or a memorable dinner experience, this taqueria is the perfect destination. Impeccable in every aspect, from the food to the ambiance, I can confidently say that I will be returning soon. Don't miss out on this gem of a restaurant!

input: Originally, our little group headed to Franklin Fountain and the line was around the block-- Capofitto was only a few steps away with no line (and bonus--cheaper/better dessert treat!). We only popped in for gelato, but I would love to come back for the pizza! It looked and smelled really good. Gelato was amazing, as capogiro gelato always is. Highly recommend chocolat scurio and pera as a combo--it was perfect!
Revise this with your best effort: Initially, our small group set off for Franklin Fountain, but we were deterred by the lengthy line that stretched around the block. However, a fortunate turn of events led us to Capofitto, a mere stone's throw away, where we found no line and an added bonus of a more affordable and superior dessert option. Although we only indulged in gelato during our brief visit, the tantalizing sight and aroma of their pizza left me yearning to return. It appeared and smelled exceptionally delicious. As for the gelato, it was truly exceptional, as expected from Capogiro gelato. I highly recommend pairing the sumptuous chocolat scurio and pera flavors together, as they created a harmonious and flawless combination.

input: This hospital is by far the best for families on the East Coast. They make seeing multiple MDs on the same day very easy and the quality of care is incredible. The renovated wing is fantastic with good accommodations for caregivers and friendly and attentive staff. I wholeheartedly recommend A.I. DuPont and will continue to travel from NY for my child's care.
Revise this with your best effort:
A.I. DuPont Hospital, located on the East Coast, undoubtedly stands out as the premier choice for families in need of medical care. Their outstanding ability to facilitate appointments with multiple MDs on the same day has simplified the process for families. Moreover, the level of care they provide is nothing short of exceptional.

One particular highlight of this remarkable hospital is its recently renovated wing. This revamped section offers superb accommodations for caregivers, ensuring their comfort during their loved ones' treatment. Additionally, the staff members at A.I. DuPont are consistently friendly and attentive, creating an atmosphere of warmth and reassurance.

With absolute confidence, I wholeheartedly endorse A.I. DuPont Hospital. Despite residing in New York, I remain committed to traveling the distance to bring my child here for their healthcare needs.

input: I highly recommend this place! This was our first "Chef Tasting"! It was exquisite!! We had 9 courses and all were truly delicious. Wine was amazing. If you are in Philly, I highly recommend Vetri.
Revise this with your best effort: I wholeheartedly recommend Vetri in Philadelphia. Our recent experience with their "Chef Tasting" was an absolute delight! The nine courses we had were nothing short of exquisite, each one bursting with delicious flavors. The selection of wines offered was truly amazing. For anyone in Philly, Vetri comes highly recommended.

input:
I'm pretty sure this place has been open since before I was born and it's no surprise as to why. 

The absolute classic of an American diner, polite and attentive waitresses and most of their food made entirely from scratch. I would definitely say their fried chicken is the best I've had before, and fresh! Bottomless coffee too, for $1.75 which I think is quite reasonable. Nice pie, too :)
Revise this with your best effort: Without a doubt, this establishment has been welcoming patrons long before my existence, and it's easy to see why. It is the epitome of a quintessential American diner, boasting courteous and attentive waitresses who serve up delectable, homemade delights. In particular, their fried chicken reigns supreme, oozing with freshness and flavor. Furthermore, the generous offer of bottomless coffee, priced at a very reasonable $1.75, adds to the overall charm. And let's not forget the delectable pies they have on offer, a delightful treat to complement the experience.

input: Don't go here. They gave me grief over the groupon then didn't bother to actually change my oil filter or tell me that they hadn't changed it so I drove 5k miles on an old filter. Crappy customer service, rude attitude, find somewhere better.
Revise this with your best effort: I strongly advise against visiting this place. Not only did they cause significant hassle with my groupon, but they also failed to perform the necessary oil filter change, without even bothering to inform me. As a result, I unknowingly drove 5,000 miles with an outdated filter. Their customer service is subpar, with a rude attitude to match. I highly recommend finding an alternative establishment that values customer satisfaction.

input: I attended the #welldoneTBO tweet-up at Anthony's Coal Fired Pizza last week and had a great time. The folks at Anthony's were amazing with the customer service. We got to try so many menu items, and all were amazing. The Philly Cheesesteak Pizza was my 10 year old's favorite. I loved the Cauliflower pizza...so buttery and garlicky and delicious (vegetarian). We also got to try the carmelized onion-smothered wings which were out of this world. Also tasted: meatballs, ribs, salad...all very good. We ordered off the menu a half and half pizza with pepperoni, sausage and mushrooms. So good. If they had liquor on the menu I would have given them five stars (I'm just not a beer or wine person). Thanks for a great evening Anthony's! We'll be back.
Revise this with your best effort:
Last week, I had the pleasure of attending the remarkable #welldoneTBO tweet-up at Anthony's Coal Fired Pizza. It was an incredible experience with outstanding customer service provided by the remarkable staff at Anthony's. Throughout the evening, we had the opportunity to sample a wide variety of items from their menu, each of which left a lasting impression.

My 10-year-old child was particularly enamored with the delectable Philly Cheesesteak Pizza, proclaiming it as their absolute favorite. Personally, I was captivated by the delectable Cauliflower pizza, which was rich, buttery, garlicky, and completely satisfying as a vegetarian option. Additionally, we indulged in the unforgettable caramelized onion-smothered wings that were truly out of this world. We were also lucky enough to try their succulent meatballs, mouthwatering ribs, and refreshing salad, all of which were undeniably delicious.

As for our personal order, we opted for a half and half pizza adorned with enticing toppings like pepperoni, sausage, and mushrooms. It was undeniably divine, leaving us longing for more. The only aspect that prevented me from awarding a perfect five-star rating was the absence of liquor options on their menu. Personally, I am not a beer or wine aficionado, and having a liquor selection would have truly elevated the experience for me. Nonetheless, I extend my heartfelt gratitude to Anthony's for providing us with an unforgettable evening. We eagerly anticipate our return in the future.

input: Awesome service and food.  Served with a dry ice fog thing that add a layer of coolness to the whole experience.
Revise this with your best effort: Exceptional service and delectable cuisine. Enhancing the overall experience is the captivating dry ice fog element that effortlessly adds a touch of sophistication and coolness to every moment.

input: Come here for delicious, home style New Orleans cuisine. We went in the afternoon, and although it was full, we were lucky and a table was ready right away. We did the a la carte as opposed to the buffet. It was our favorite meal of the trip!
Revise this with your best effort: Indulge in delectable, authentic New Orleans cuisine at this exceptional establishment. Despite our afternoon visit, the restaurant was bustling, but luckily, we were promptly seated at a table. Opting for the a la carte menu rather than the buffet, we were treated to a truly unforgettable dining experience. Unquestionably, it became the highlight of our entire trip.

input: A great restaurant to take people visiting from out of town. Very popular for breakfast/brunch on the weekends. Should expect to wait at least an hour any time after 9:30 AM and service takes a little while. But great menu options and delicious food. Also a great bakery, coffee and gelato counter that offers instant service or items to enjoy while waiting to get called.
Revise this with your best effort:
If you're looking for an exceptional restaurant to impress out-of-town visitors, this is the place. Our spot is renowned for its irresistible breakfast and brunch, particularly on the weekends. However, do anticipate a wait of at least an hour if you arrive after 9:30 AM, as our popularity is quite evident. While service may be a little slower than desired, rest assured that our menu options and delectable food make it all worth it.

In addition to the remarkable dining experience we offer, we boast a fabulous bakery, coffee, and gelato counter. This allows you to enjoy instant service or indulge in delightful treats while patiently waiting for your table to be called.

input:
The food is really good!! The service is less than average; I felt very rushed, unimportant, and cheated. Was shocked that the waitress withheld my coins when she gave me my change! Do they withhold change from all of their customers?!! Very disappointed.  Would she have done that to a well known food critic?

Will probably go back one more time eventually but will have lots of change with me to pay the EXACT amount! When it came time to give her tip, I applied the coins she withheld from me -they became part of her tip. Also, her tip dropped from my standard 25% to 15%. Flabbergasted.
Revise this with your best effort:
The food at this place is absolutely delicious! However, I have to admit that the service was below average. I felt quite rushed, unimportant, and even a bit cheated. It was a shock to discover that the waitress kept my coins when she returned my change. I couldn't help but wonder if this is a common practice for them with all their customers. Needless to say, I left feeling very disappointed. I couldn't help but think, would she have done the same thing to a well-known food critic?

Despite my dissatisfaction, I might consider giving this place another chance in the future. However, next time I'll be sure to have enough change on me to pay the exact amount. When it came time to leave a tip, I deducted the coins that were previously withheld from me. They became a part of her tip. As a result, her tip dropped from my usual 25% to 15%. I was truly taken aback by the whole experience.

input: Their sushi is pretty good. Mesa rolls are my fav here. They would be 4stars if they gave better estimations for pick ups. It is typical that they lag a lot and they seem to make it after you show up.
Revise this with your best effort: I am quite pleased with the quality of their sushi. The Mesa rolls, in particular, are my absolute favorite at this establishment. However, I would consider giving them a higher rating of 4 stars if they improved their estimation process for pick-up orders. It is a common occurrence that there is significant delay, often resulting in the sushi not being prepared until I arrive at the restaurant.

input: If you want The Best burger in Philly, this is the right place to come. The bread was fresh, meat was nothing but juicy, service was a amiable, price was descent and affordable to everybody!
Revise this with your best effort: If you are in the pursuit of the finest burger in Philly, look no further than this establishment. Here, you will find freshly baked bread, tantalizingly juicy meat, friendly and amiable service, all at a price that is both reasonable and accessible to everyone.

input: Great hangout for wine, cheese, and some music outside.  Tried some of the food - bacon-wrapped dates & brussel sprouts - all unmemorable.  Also tried the sardines which smelled and tasted past their prime - sent back.
Revise this with your best effort: This place is the perfect spot to relax and enjoy some wine, indulgent cheese, and live music in an outdoor setting. However, I must say that my experience with the food was underwhelming. The bacon-wrapped dates and brussel sprouts failed to leave a lasting impression, rendering them forgettable. Additionally, the sardines, unfortunately, emitted an off-putting smell and tasted like they were past their prime. Consequently, I had no choice but to kindly request a replacement.

input:
Excellent tasting Po-Boys but it could have had mire catfish, pretty skimpy.
Service, very good.
Revise this with your best effort: The Po-Boys had a delicious flavor, however, they lacked an ample amount of catfish, which was a bit disappointing. The service, on the other hand, was outstanding.

input:
Define the worst Mediterranean food I have ever had.  The hummus appeared to have a good texture, that is the little bit I could see under the ocean of olive oil.  The pita bread was burned- not just over toasted, but black on the majority of the wedges.  I went home and was sick the rest of the evening from the amount of oil it had in it. 

The manager was probably the worst of the experience. He told my gf he would "upgrade her hummus for no charge, because normally it's $1.00" but said it as if he was doing us this huge favor.  He then continued to yell at us from across the restaurant after we sat down  (instead of coming up to our table and actually having a conversation) and says, "please let me know how your food is because that's the only way I can know if we are doing a good job or not is when customers tell me."  But we agreed that the vibe he gave off would not be that of open mindedness and gratitude if we were to say anything about his plate of olive oil, er I mean hummus.  There is also a sign that advertises the "cleanest bathroom in town".... Ehhhh ok, good to know for our next road trip.
Revise this with your best effort:
Please provide your assistance in reviewing my description of the worst Mediterranean food experience I've had:

My experience with the Mediterranean food at this particular restaurant was far from satisfactory. The hummus had a decent texture, or at least the little that was visible beneath the overwhelming ocean of olive oil. It was apparent that the hummus was drowning in excessive oil, which left me feeling sick for the rest of the evening.

The pita bread was another disappointment. Instead of being lightly toasted, it was burnt to a blackened state on most of the wedges. This not only affected the taste but also made the bread unpleasant to eat.

However, the worst part of the whole experience was undoubtedly the manager. In an attempt to seem generous, he offered to "upgrade" my girlfriend's hummus at no extra charge, as if he was doing us a tremendous favor. Instead of approaching our table and having a genuine conversation, he chose to yell at us loudly from across the restaurant. He then added, "Please let me know how your food is, as that's the only way I can gauge whether we're doing a good job or not." But considering the negative impression he had already given us, we knew that expressing our dissatisfaction with the plate of olive oil disguised as hummus would only lead to closed-mindedness and ingratitude.

To make matters worse, there was a sign proudly advertising the "cleanest bathroom in town." While this might be a useful piece of information for our next road trip, it did nothing to salvage the disappointing dining experience.

input: Great bagels!  I wish they stayed open later in the day though.  Staff not very friendly but the bagels are worth it!
Revise this with your best effort: The bagels are absolutely fantastic! However, it would be even better if the store extended their hours. The staff could use a bit more friendliness, but the unparalleled deliciousness of their bagels makes it all worthwhile.

input:
This hotel was fantastic. I was in town for a week, working at my company's PA office in Wayne. Great location and easy to get in and out. Hotel staff was very friendly. Room was immaculately cleaned and very spacious for just one person. Kitchenette was fully stocked with dishes, silverware, utensils, a small dishwasher and a full size fridge. Windows surrounding the king size bed were great- lots of natural light. I liked that opting out of housekeeping got me a $5 credit at the restaurant. 

The pool is small but no one was there the two times I went to use the hot tub. The bar has a decent drink selection, although I was bummed they were out of mint and couldn't make a mojito (which was on the drink menu). Burger was okay. Dessert was mediocre (but free with my $5 credit, so nbd). Omelet station was a nice touch in the AM. Coffee frequently had coffee grounds in it/was very weak, but the breakfast spread overall was nice.
Revise this with your best effort:
I had an absolutely fantastic experience at this hotel. I had the pleasure of staying there for a week while working at my company's PA office in Wayne. The location was perfect and made it incredibly convenient to come and go from the hotel. Moreover, the hotel staff were incredibly friendly and accommodating.

The room itself was beyond impeccable. It was spotless and spacious, providing more than enough room for just one person. The presence of a well-stocked kitchenette, complete with dishes, silverware, utensils, a small dishwasher, and a full-size fridge, was an added bonus. Additionally, the large windows surrounding the king-sized bed allowed for an abundance of natural light to flood the room.

I was particularly pleased to discover that by choosing to opt out of housekeeping services, I received a $5 credit which I could use at the hotel's restaurant. This added benefit made my stay even more enjoyable and convenient.

While the pool may have been on the smaller side, I was fortunate enough to have it to myself during the two occasions when I wanted to use the hot tub. The hotel's bar had a decent selection of drinks, although I was disappointed to find out they were out of mint and therefore unable to make a mojito, which was on their drink menu. The burger I had was passable, however, the dessert left something to be desired. Nevertheless, the fact that it was free with the $5 credit took away any major concerns.

In the mornings, the omelet station provided a delightful touch to my breakfast experience. However, I did notice that the coffee often contained coffee grounds and was generally quite weak. Nonetheless, the breakfast spread as a whole was still pleasant and satisfying.

Overall, my stay at this hotel was truly exceptional. The combination of its wonderful location, friendly staff, immaculate room, and the added benefits such as the kitchenette and the opt-out housekeeping credit made for an incredibly positive experience. Although there were minor hiccups with the bar and coffee, they did not overshadow the overall excellence of my stay.

input: Decent falafel wrap...but not exactly cheap. And the cave-like sitting area was cold and uninviting. There are better choices in Manayunk.

input: This place was awesome! I am driving cross country and hit a busted tire on the road and something came off the bottom of my car. Definitely recommend this place.

I immediately contacted Brian, who graciously invited me to bring my car in for inspection. The team promptly lifted my vehicle upon arrival and efficiently repaired everything needed. Brian's friendly attitude and professionalism ensured that I was back on the road in no time, all within a remarkable 30 minutes. I wholeheartedly recommend this outstanding establishment without hesitation.

input: Friday, July 22 we decided to give this eatery a try.  It is definitely in a great location especially if you want to explore the Quarter afterwards.  We were a party of 8 people and out of the 8 dishes ordered only 2 were really good --the jambalaya and file gumbo were very tasty.  The other dishes --red beans/rice,  meatloaf, Mac and cheese,  shrimp po boy, and chicken wings were bland and a waste of money.  The staff was nice but overall the food was mediocre.
Revise this with your best effort: On Friday, July 22, we made the decision to try out this eatery, drawn to its excellent location, especially for those looking to explore the Quarter afterwards. Our party consisted of eight people, and unfortunately, out of the eight dishes we ordered, only two stood out as truly delicious - the jambalaya and file gumbo were exceptionally tasty. input: According to my experience, there is just one place in Tokyo at the fish market where you get your seafood a little fresher. Here in Santa Barbara, it does not get any fresher. Right from the fish tank in the cooking pot on your plate. Don't expect a fancy restaurant with a nice ambiance because this is not the reason you come here (though the outside seating has a nice ocean/harbor view). It is the variety of fresh shellfish prepared according to your appetite and taste buds. The wait can be long during peak hours but it is worth it. Put your name down and take a walk on the peer to free-up some extra room in your stomach - you'll need it!
Revise this with your best effort: In terms of my personal experience, there happens to be a solitary spot in Tokyo's fish market where you can find seafood that is marginally fresher. However, here in Santa Barbara, freshness couldn't get any better. You witness it going straight from the fish tank into the cooking pot and onto your plate. While you shouldn't anticipate a high-end restaurant with a luxurious ambiance, that's not the allure of this place (although the outside seating does offer a pleasant view of the ocean/harbor). What draws people here is the assortment of fresh shellfish catered to satisfy your appetite and taste preferences. The waiting time can be lengthy during peak hours, but it is unquestionably worthwhile. Add your name to the list and take a stroll along the pier to make space in your stomach - trust me, you'll need it!

input: I've always had good experiences here. The food is creative and tasty and the house wines are decent. Their cocktails are well made but small. I've never had a problem with service but also haven't been here during a super busy time. The patio is a great spot to hang out with friends.
Revise this with your best effort: I have consistently enjoyed exceptional experiences at this establishment. The culinary offerings are both imaginative and delicious, complemented by a selection of house wines that are more than satisfactory. Although the cocktails are skillfully crafted, it is worth noting that they are served in relatively modest portions. Despite this, I have never encountered any service issues, albeit I have not visited during particularly busy periods. input:
tldr; Huge plates of food. Cheap. Delicious. Get the banana pecan pancakes.

This is the kind of place that you think about when you imagine a local diner (at least my opinion of one). Everything I've eaten has been awesome. The service is good and the coffee keeps coming. 

They have a morning breakfast deal between 7 and 830 am. $2.89 for 5 different combinations such as 2 eggs, pancakes and sausage (when you buy a beverage). I might have to start grabbing a little breakfast before work!

Seriously, though.... get the banana pecan pancakes. You can thank me later.
Revise this with your best effort: TLDR: Skyway Jacks has been renamed Skyway Cafe but still offers the same delicious, affordable, and huge plates of food. The bovine decor adds a cozy touch to this local diner, and the service is great with unlimited coffee. Don't miss their morning breakfast deal, and make sure to try the mouthwatering banana pecan pancakes. Trust me, they're worth it!

input:

I stood in line today for 1 hour and 20 minutes for 1 shot. They the walked up in front of me and closed the line. Told me they were done and leaving. There were 60 people behind me outraged as well. F*** this place

input:
On my first day in New Orleans, I walked to Fair Grinds for a caffeine boost. It was a beautiful afternoon, and a handful of people were scattered around the shop and the outdoor seating area, working on laptops and visiting with friends. 

I ordered a small cold brew with vanilla, easy on the ice. I added a hunk of gluten free zucchini bread (the bread butt; the best part!) to my order and paid with a credit card. They have a fancy touchscreen register that lets you add tip to your card purchase. 

I topped off my drink with whole milk -- which in itself was a real treat. It's so rare to see whole milk at the mixing station! 

Before leaving, I asked what else they had in the way of a GF offering, and the young man behind the counter said "just the zucchini bread." That's a real bummer; the zucchini bread is great but I'd love to have more than one option. 

My drink was smooth and had a perfect flavor. I was happy with my choices. 

If I lived in the neighborhood, I'd be here all the time. I like the hipstery feeling of this place, and everything I've ordered has been delightful.
Revise this with your best effort:
During my inaugural day in New Orleans, I strolled towards Fair Grinds in search of a revitalizing caffeine boost. The afternoon unfolded beautifully, with a gentle scattering of individuals occupying both the shop and the inviting outdoor seating area. Among them, people diligently worked on laptops or engaged in friendly conversations with companions.

I decided to place an order for a small cold brew accompanied by a dash of vanilla essence, and a mindful reduction of ice. To enhance my experience further, I opted for a slice of delectable gluten-free zucchini bread, specifically the coveted bread butt – renowned as the pinnacle of its appeal. Completing the transaction, I conveniently used my credit card through their advanced touchscreen register, equipped with a built-in feature for leaving a gratuity.

As I finalized my concoction, I indulged myself by adorning the drink with wholesome whole milk, a rarity in most establishments. It genuinely delighted me to discover such a luxurious addition available at the mixing station. 

However, before bidding farewell, I inquired about other gluten-free alternatives the cafe could offer. Unfortunately, the young man behind the counter regretfully informed me that only the zucchini bread fit that description. A twinge of disappointment washed over me, yearning for a more extensive selection in this regard.

Nonetheless, the smooth and exquisitely flavorful beverage in my hands rendered me content with my choices. Perhaps, if I were fortunate enough to reside in the neighborhood, I would become a frequent patron of this establishment. Its ambiance exuded a sense of hipster charm, and every item I have sampled thus far has proven to be an absolute delight.

input: This place is so lovely! I went for a sweet and was amazed at the variety. The gooey butter cookies were awesome and the German chocolate cupcake simply amazing!
Revise this with your best effort: I was absolutely captivated by the beauty of this place! I decided to go in for a treat, and boy, was I blown away by the incredible range of options available. input:

input:

input:
Cru is such a cute quaint wine bar! In the front is a wine store and in the back ins the wine bar. The wine bar area is small but had a very modern atmosphere.

I started off with the Vina Vino wine flight and my friends ordered The Bold and the Beautiful. Both came on a cute wood/chalkboard board with the wine written in chalk. All the wines were very tasty but the Vespucci  Primitivo and the Il Fauno di Arcanum were my favorite.

We then ordered the fig jam and prosciutto, bleu cheese, arugula flatbread. A little heavy on the blue cheese for my liking but overall was really good. We also ordered the Farmers Platter. You can choose anything from 1-7 items and build your plate from a variety of cheese and meats. We selected the Brillat-Savarin, Cypress Grove "Purple Haze", Blue Brie, Spressata and the Italian Speck. The farmers plate also came with jam, mustard,  caramelized nuts and crostini. The Farmers plate by far was my favorite!

Overall I really liked CRU. Its cute, quaint and cozy. Can't wait to come back!!
Revise this with your best effort:
Cru is an absolutely adorable and charming wine bar! As you walk in, you are greeted by a lovely wine store situated in the front, while at the back lies the cozy wine bar area. Even though the wine bar is small, it boasts a wonderfully modern atmosphere.

To kick off our evening, I opted for the delightful Vina Vino wine flight, while my friends chose The Bold and the Beautiful. These wine flights were presented on charming wood/chalkboard boards, with the names of the wines elegantly written in chalk. Every single wine we tasted was incredibly delicious, but I found myself particularly drawn to the Vespucci Primitivo and the Il Fauno di Arcanum.

Next, we decided to indulge in the fig jam and prosciutto, bleu cheese, arugula flatbread. While the blue cheese was a bit intense for my personal taste, the overall combination was undeniably tasty. Our adventurous spirits led us to order the Farmers Platter as well. This amazing option allowed us to select anywhere from 1 to 7 items and construct our own perfect plate from a delightful assortment of cheese and meats. We opted for the Brillat-Savarin, Cypress Grove "Purple Haze", Blue Brie, Spressata, and the Italian Speck. In addition, the Farmers Platter came with delectable accompaniments like jam, mustard, caramelized nuts, and crostini. There is no doubt that the Farmers Platter stole the show – it was definitely my favorite!

On the whole, I couldn't have been more pleased with my experience at CRU. The establishment is cute, cozy, and exudes a charming atmosphere. I am already eagerly anticipating my next visit!

input: Great spot I've been coming here for years. Top 3 steaks in the city! Nothing has changed even after the name change. Try a chicken cheesesteak for something different

input:
Pina's is easily one of the mroe underated places to eat in Roxborough. They have great stromboli (which are HUGE) and thier sicilian pie is the best I have every had. Sandwiches and pizza are just ok. 

I stopped ina two occassions for a sit down dinner and came away very stisfied and full. Ordered the chicken park with was a huge chickem covered in cheese and sauce. Excellent.

input: It may be a bit pricey, but it's good food in the cafe and a good selection in the grocery. I love their vegan sandwich and tofu melt and they always have a great selection of vegan sweets.

input:

input:
