input:
First impression:

Home Wine Kitchen's "No Menu Monday" is a must-try for anyone interested in the St. Louis fine dining scene or good food more generally.  We came prepared with reservations, but the restaurant actually began quieting out while our delicious meal was ramping up; the tables offer more elbow room than the photographs online belie.  As the name of the evening suggests, no menu is in play here; you'll let your friendly server know if you have any food allergies or particular preferences, and before long watch your customized meal unfold.  That's a three-course meal, $30, plus $12 for three half-glass wine pairings.

As starters, we were served lamb meatballs -- likely the favorite of the night -- and goat cheese-stuffed poblano peppers.  The peppers had a good bit of spice offset by the chalkiness of the goat cheese, making an excellent pairing for my Soave (white wine).  The mains were a corvina fish delicately cooked in wax paper and a swordfish steak served over asparagus with homegrown tomatoes and "love sauce."  The corvina came out on the rarer side, perhaps a little too complex for this Midwesterner's palate, but the hearty swordfish was some of the best seafood I've tasted in Missouri.  Dessert comprised a champagne gelatin and a chocolate tart, both of which were topped by fluffy homemade whipped cream and quickly eaten.

The staff at Home Wine Kitchen made our visit pleasant, acting casual yet professional during our meal.  The restaurant patrons seemed to be largely industry types that oohed and aahed about the cuisine (perhaps a trifle self-importantly, but this Yelper is no saint himself).  I was surprised to note that other diners were served the same courses as we were (albeit in different configurations), when I was under the assumption there would be a little more variation; however, I can only imagine the challenge such an endeavor would pose to the talented kitchen.  The interior, lighting, and volume here were all very good.

By the end of the evening, we realized that putting yourself in the hands of the chef is not for the faint of heart, as evidenced by one conversation near us during the meal that all but stopped when a beautiful whole fish was served to the table.  Leaving the restaurant, I was glad that I had tried No Menu Monday, but did wonder what the meal would have been like had I ordered off the menu.  I guess that calls for a return visit, don't you?
Revise this with your best effort:
First impression:

If you're interested in exploring the fine dining scene in St. Louis or simply looking for good food, Home Wine Kitchen's "No Menu Monday" is a must-try. We arrived with reservations, but as our delicious meal unfolded, the restaurant started quieting down, providing a more spacious and comfortable dining experience than expected. As the name suggests, there is no set menu for this evening; instead, you'll inform your friendly server about any food allergies or preferences, and then sit back and watch your personalized meal come to life. For just $30, you'll enjoy a three-course meal, with an additional $12 for three half-glass wine pairings.

To begin, we savored lamb meatballs, which quickly became our favorite of the night, and goat cheese-stuffed poblano peppers. The peppers had a delightful hint of spice, balanced by the creamy goat cheese, making it a perfect accompaniment to my Soave (white wine). As for the main courses, we delighted in a perfectly cooked corvina fish prepared in wax paper and a delicious swordfish steak served over asparagus, homegrown tomatoes, and a tantalizing "love sauce." While the corvina was slightly rarer than we preferred, its complex flavors showcased the chef's skill. On the other hand, the swordfish was an absolute seafood delight, possibly the best we've tasted in Missouri. The dessert was a decadent affair, featuring a champagne gelatin and a delectable chocolate tart, both topped with fluffy homemade whipped cream, practically disappearing from our plates in no time.

The staff at Home Wine Kitchen struck the ideal balance between casual and professional, ensuring our dining experience was pleasant from start to finish. The majority of the patrons seemed to be industry insiders, passionately discussing and appreciating the cuisine, though at times it bordered on self-importance (but then again, this Yelper cannot claim to be guiltless in that regard). Interestingly, we noticed that other diners were served the same courses as us, albeit in different arrangements, whereas we had expected more variation. However, we can only imagine the challenges the talented chefs face in executing such a unique concept. The ambiance, lighting, and noise levels inside the restaurant were all spot-on.

As the evening came to a close, it became clear that entrusting the chef with your meal choices is not for the timid, perfectly exemplified by a nearby conversation that came to a halt as a stunning whole fish was presented at a neighboring table. As we left the restaurant, I couldn't help but feel grateful for experiencing No Menu Monday, yet also curious about what the meal would have been like had we ordered from a traditional menu. It seems like a return visit is in order, wouldn't you agree?

input:
Went here with a few friends as the place to have our reunion dinner. We hadn't seen eachother since elementary school and got reacquainted through Facebook so this was a pretty special dinner. 

The restaurant is very swanky and the prices show this. I do think the food was worth the price although all of my party thought it was very expensive. I ordered the lobster bake which was delicious. It was not fantastic and there wasn't alot of seafood but it was adequate for me. I also ordered a Neopolitan Old Fashion which was made perfectly. 

My friends ordered the fritters, carpaccio, crab cake and fries. Plus 2 shots of tequila, a lemonade and 2 more old fashions. Bill was $170 which is not bad but some of my friends weren't expected it. 

And I must say something about our waiter. Unfortunately, I didn't remember his name but he was fantastic! Very attentive, nice and even bought out a dessert because it was also one of my friend's bday. He was just real cool. 

5 stars for service
3 stars for food
4 stars for ambience 
2 stars for price.  

But I was satisfied.
Revise this with your best effort:
I recently had the pleasure of visiting this establishment with a small group of friends for our long-awaited reunion dinner. Our paths hadn't crossed since our elementary school days, and thanks to the wonders of Facebook, we were able to reconnect and make this dinner extra special.

From the moment we stepped into the restaurant, it was evident that we had chosen a truly upscale venue. The prices were reflective of this fact, and while I personally felt that the food justified the cost, my companions found it to be quite expensive. For my own meal, I opted for the lobster bake, which proved to be a delightfully palatable choice. Though not exceptional and lacking in an abundant seafood portion, it indeed satisfied my palate. Additionally, I indulged in a flawlessly concocted Neopolitan Old Fashion, which further enhanced my dining experience.

As for my friends, their orders encompassed a variety of delectable dishes—the fritters, carpaccio, crab cake, and fries—all of which received positive reviews. Alongside these delicacies, we enjoyed shots of tequila, a refreshing lemonade, and two more rounds of the exquisite old fashions. When the check arrived, totaling $170, it was met with some surprise from a few friends who hadn't anticipated the cost.

Finally, I must express my utmost satisfaction with our waiter, whose name regrettably eludes me. He provided impeccable service, demonstrating an unwavering attentiveness and genuine warmth throughout the evening. In fact, he went above and beyond by surprising one of my friends with a complimentary dessert to celebrate their birthday. It is safe to say that he greatly enhanced our dining experience and left a lasting impression on all of us.

In summary, I would rate the service with a well-deserved five stars for its excellence. While the food received a three-star rating due to its lack of standout qualities, the ambiance garners a solid four stars, creating an inviting atmosphere. As for the price, it falls somewhat short with two stars. Regardless, I left the restaurant feeling content and satisfied with my overall experience.

input: My first trip to Susanna Foo was at 6 months old when the restaurant was still a hole-in-the-wall takeout joint owned by Susanna's parents. My parents have been taking my brother and I ever since. I have many fond memories of Susanna fashioning dolls for us out of the linen napkins and preparing Chicken with Cashew Nuts when we refused to eat anything else. The food has always been reliable, but now that I am an adult, I find it lacking excitement. The service is always impeccable and I have never been disappointed by the overall decor or ambience. I'd like to see Susanna improve upon some of her traditional recipes by either adding new flavors or perhaps returning to her Chinese roots with a more ethnic menu. I'm hoping there will be a revitalization and that I will come to love Susanna Foo as much as I did as a child.
Revise this with your best effort: From my very first visit to Susanna Foo at just 6 months old, when the restaurant was a humble takeout place owned by Susanna's parents, my family and I have made it a tradition to dine there. Countless cherished memories flood my mind, such as Susanna's creative napkin dolls and her special preparation of Chicken with Cashew Nuts, which she kindly crafted when we were picky eaters. While the food has always been reliable, as an adult, I yearn for something more thrilling. Thankfully, the service remains impeccable, and the overall decor and ambience consistently impress. To rekindle my love for Susanna Foo, I wish to see an infusion of new flavors into her beloved traditional recipes or a return to her Chinese origins with an enticing and authentic ethnic menu. With a revitalization, I eagerly anticipate falling in love with Susanna Foo all over again.

input: I am from California and was looking for something besides the hotel dining room to have dinner at.  I usually use the Yellow Pages to find restaurants and judge them by the size of their ads.  Spiro's jumped out at me, not because of the size of their advertisement (small) but Greek food just sounded good to me tonight.  I wasn't disappointed at all.  The Greek lemon soup was excellent and I liked the Moussaka, although the waiter suggested the Sea Bass.  All in all, the dinner was terrific and if I am back in this area, I will head to Spiro's again.  Thanks Neil for the wonderful service!
Revise this with your best effort: I am from California and sought an alternative to the hotel dining room for dinner. Usually, I rely on the Yellow Pages to discover restaurants, typically basing my choices on the size of their ads. However, Spiro's caught my attention not because of the magnitude of their advertisement, but rather because Greek cuisine appealed to my taste buds tonight. I was certainly not let down. The Greek lemon soup surpassed my expectations, and although I initially leaned towards ordering Moussaka, the waiter kindly recommended the Sea Bass. In the end, the dinner was exceptional, leaving me with the intention of returning to Spiro's if I find myself in the area again. A special thanks to Neil for the outstanding service provided!

input: I'm a Barbecue judge and this ain't barbecue.  Not in Texas, not in the southeast.  Not in KC.  An earlier reviewer nailed it perfectly.  The brisket is fatty pot roast.  No evidence of smoke.  Mushy texture like long braised  meat.  My sandwich was 75 percent fat.  Big meatless chunks of fat.  Either the owner doesn't care or he's left the place in the hands of employees who don't know any better. Sorry.  But you can do much better elsewhere.
Revise this with your best effort: As a barbecue judge, I must express my disappointment as this does not meet the standards of authentic barbecue, whether it be in Texas, the southeast, or Kansas City. A previous reviewer accurately depicted the situation. The brisket resembles more of a fatty pot roast, lacking any distinct smokiness. Its mushy texture suggests long braising rather than the desired tenderness of smoked meat. Regrettably, my sandwich consisted of a staggering 75 percent fat, with large meatless chunks of it. It seems that either the owner lacks passion for their craft or has entrusted the establishment to unknowledgeable employees. I apologize for the criticism, but I encourage you to explore alternative options where you can undoubtedly find much better barbecue.

input:
Our second favorite place to watch a sunset. It's way north of Tampa, so a bit of a drive. We love to join everyone to clap when the sun goes down...a wonderful way to end the day. 

The music is lively, as are the patrons. Don't expect to swim in the water, it's a rocky beach, not much sand. Have been taking our boys since they were babies...are fifteen now. The food and drinks don't make an impression either way, it's the view and atmosphere that draws you in. 

Never disappoints.
Revise this with your best effort:
One of our top picks for enjoying a breathtaking sunset lies further north from Tampa, making it a bit of a journey to reach. However, the experience is always worth the drive. We delight in participating in the collective applause that reverberates through the crowd as the sun gracefully descends, marking the perfect end to an eventful day.

The ambiance at this place is brimming with life, harmonized by vibrant music and animated patrons. Although swimming may not be possible due to a rocky shoreline offering scarce sand, it has never deterred us from relishing this locale. We have cherished countless memories here, starting from when our boys were mere infants, and now they have blossomed into fifteen-year-olds.

While the fare and beverages do not leave a lasting impression, it is truly the awe-inspiring vistas and the captivating atmosphere that magnetize visitors. Unfailingly, this place charms us, ensuring that disappointment is an emotion rarely encountered.

input:
Obviously they are doing something right since they have been around since 1958. Great soft serve and scooped ice cream cones, boats, floats and sundaes.
Prices great too.  Enjoy!
Revise this with your best effort: It is evident that their success is attributed to their longstanding presence since 1958. With an exceptional range of soft serve and scooped ice cream cones, as well as delightful boats, floats, and sundaes, they have undoubtedly mastered the art of ice cream. Moreover, the prices are incredibly reasonable, adding to the overall enjoyment of the experience. Don't miss out on this delightful treat!

input: I decided to stop by since I was in the area and craving some authentic Mexican cuisine. I was literally by myself (late lunchtime on a tues) and really excited to try the pazole!! It was delicious ( granted my first and only time) I believe it's pork and has hominy, lettuce, radishes,onions and they give you a small container of dried oregano. Not the biggest fan of the lettuce cause it's gets all wilted but add some hot sauce and it's a meal in itself!!! I got also got the taco lunch special (2 pork tacos and rice) and that was good. Besides the amazing service from the sweet lady, the salsa was way sweet! Wasn't the biggest fan but everything is def fresh! And the pineapple water is a must. I don't like pineapples but I read reviews and just had to try it and thank u guys! Great reviews :) I'm excited to come back to try the burritos esp since I come out here for Costco shopping (soooo close by!) pretty dangerous when I find good food cause then I get cravings :/ enjoy this gem and eat up!!!
Revise this with your best effort:
I decided to make a detour and visit this place as I was in the vicinity and had a strong desire for some authentic Mexican cuisine. I happened to be all by myself, visiting during a late lunch hour on a Tuesday. I was filled with excitement to taste their famous pazole, despite it being my first and only time trying it. The combination of pork and hominy, along with lettuce, radishes, onions, and a small container of dried oregano, created a delightful blend of flavors. Although I wasn't particularly fond of the lettuce, as it tended to become wilted, a touch of hot sauce elevated the dish to a savored standalone meal. Additionally, I opted for their taco lunch special, which consisted of two pork tacos and a side of rice, and it turned out to be quite satisfying.

Apart from the impeccable service provided by the kind lady, the salsa, although fresh, had an unexpected sweetness to it that didn't quite appeal to my personal taste. However, I must admit that everything on their menu has a definitive freshness that cannot be ignored. Furthermore, I must highly recommend trying their pineapple water, a drink I initially approached with skepticism, as I am not particularly fond of pineapples. But reading the rave reviews, I couldn't resist giving it a try, and it was absolutely worth it. Thank you to everyone who shared such positive feedback! I am now eager to return and sample their burritos, especially since I often find myself in this area for my Costco shopping trips, conveniently located just nearby. However, I must caution myself, as good food discovered in close proximity tends to ignite cravings that are hard to resist. All in all, I wholeheartedly encourage you to savor this hidden gem and indulge in all its delightful offerings.

input:
by 3 stars, i really mean 3.5-

white brick walls, cool rustic furniture, seasoned, attractive employees. and the lighting is lovely.. nay, PERFECT. probably good for a blind date.  and service is good and timely.

but 3.5 could've been 4 if it wasn't so expensive for what i'm getting. and if the kitchen was more accommodating.

the first time i ever ate there, (around when it first opened), i ordered ravioli and received 3 or 5 pieces for $11-13.  another time i visited, i tried substituting a salad for fries with my burger. and my server said, "no, sorry, the kitchen won't do that." 

are you $^%ER@# kidding me??? it wasn't a super modification. it's not as if i asked for a burger with only one bun, no tomato, half piece of lettuce, two onion rings, and love. it wasn't like i wanted to substitute lobster for fries!!! needless to say, this is the first time i've been unable to substitute. i'm usually really easy to please, but this is the first time i've ever felt difficult. at least in my head. is this in my head?

unforgivable.
Revise this with your best effort:
With a rating of 3.5 stars, this establishment boasts white brick walls, stylish rustic furniture, and a team of charming employees. The lighting, I must add, is not simply lovely, but downright perfect. The ambience makes it an ideal setting for a blind date, and the service is commendably prompt.

However, it must be noted that if not for the steep prices and the lack of kitchen flexibility, this place could have easily earned a four-star rating. Allow me to elaborate. On my initial visit, shortly after their grand opening, I ordered a plate of ravioli, only to be presented with a meager serving of three to five pieces, for which I paid a hefty sum of $11 to $13. Quite disappointing, I must say. Furthermore, during another occasion, I dared to request a simple substitution of fries for a salad alongside my burger, only to be told, rather sharply, by my server that the kitchen would not accommodate such a request. I was astounded. It was not an outrageous modification, as I did not demand a burger with a myriad of specific alterations. I certainly did not ask for a burger sans one bun, tomato, and half a lettuce leaf, with the addition of two onion rings and a sprinkle of love. Surely, it was not as if I were attempting to replace the fries with lobster! To say the least, this incident marks the first time that my request for substitution has been outrightly denied. Normally, I am quite easy to please, but this encounter has left me feeling puzzled. Is it possible that my dissatisfaction lies solely within my own mind?

Regrettably, these shortcomings are unforgivable, in my humble opinion.

input: I would eat here again, but mostly because it is an interesting destination in a town with a lot of bad restaurants. Great decor, noisy atmosphere, and funky vibe. Servers seem hip, but we were rushed through an inattentive service. (One of those dinners where you better ask for the check when you can because you don't know when you will see the waiter again). Note to Gluten Free folks, this place is not completely safe or knowledgeable and the GF buns were awful. The house catsup, which is apparently a thing here, is not GF. Note to anyone with a car: parking sucks.
Revise this with your best effort: I would consider dining at this establishment again, primarily due to its unique charm amidst a town plagued by subpar restaurants. The venue boasts an impressive decor, albeit with a bustling and vibrant atmosphere. The servers exude a trendy aura, yet our experience was marred by rushed and inattentive service. (An occasion where it is prudent to request the check promptly, as encountering the waiter again is uncertain). For those adhering to a Gluten Free diet, it is important to note that this place lacks complete safety measures and knowledge in that regard, as the GF buns were disappointingly dreadful. I should also mention that the signature house catsup, which seems to be a selling point here, is not Gluten Free. Furthermore, if you plan to arrive by car, be prepared for a frustrating parking situation.

input: Good drinks and food. Had the pulled pork and fried chicken po boy. Mac and cheese was amazing. Very reasonable for the price. Great draft list as well. Serves food till1am.
Revise this with your best effort: I thoroughly enjoyed the delicious selection of drinks and food at this establishment. The pulled pork and fried chicken po boy were particularly delectable, complemented perfectly by the amazing mac and cheese. The pricing was quite reasonable considering the quality and portion sizes. Additionally, the extensive draft list was impressive. It's worth mentioning that they also serve food until 1am, allowing for a satisfying late-night dining experience.

input: If you like to wait while several tables are open,  terrible service, a dirty restaurant, and very mediocre food that is overpriced for breakfast then you'll love this place! This was one of the worst breakfasts I've ever had. With First Watch around the corner and Pinky's up the street don't waste your time here. I know what you're thinking...but Todd First Watch and Pinky's are way more expensive....Bullsh#t. don't waste your time on this old broken down dump.
Revise this with your best effort: If you enjoy waiting for tables to open, receiving terrible service, dining in a dirty restaurant, and settling for mediocre overpriced breakfast, then this is the place for you! Without a doubt, this has been one of the most disappointing breakfast experiences I have ever had. In close proximity to both First Watch and Pinky's, there are far better options available, so there is simply no reason to waste your precious time here. I understand the skepticism about First Watch and Pinky's being pricier, but trust me when I say it is worth every penny compared to this rundown establishment.

input:
So, I went back to El Arado on Monday with a group of six people. The staff seemed shocked about our 6 pm arrival, and "sanitized" a large table for us quickly. Yes, the table smelled like dirty sanitized rags, ugh, but, once you got buzzed on...I mean beyond, the smell, your waiter will appear and take your drink orders. 

We got beers and margaritas. The margarita drinker in the group declared that it "was good."  The prices for drinks weren't that bad.  ($2.95 for Mexican beers). 

We all ordered our food, which was brought out at a good time, fresh, and hot. Everyone snarfed - it was good and tasty and all our needs were met attentively by the quiet waiter. 

All of us were let satisfied, and our specific requests (i.e. "no beans" "light on the cheese") were met by the kitchen staff with no problems. We left with full bellies then went to the Red Garter for a mind-numbing strip club experience. 

What a way to wrap up a review..

El Arado has gotten a bad wrap - but, the staff is decent, the food wasn't too shabby and the drink prices are cheap. A good place to start out for affordable and filling eats before a night out in Fountain Square (or to strip clubs).
Revise this with your best effort:
On Monday, I revisited El Arado accompanied by a group of six individuals. To our surprise, the staff appeared taken aback by our arrival at 6 pm, promptly sanitizing a large table to accommodate us. Although the table emitted an unpleasant odor reminiscent of soiled rags, we managed to overlook it once our waiter approached to take our drink orders.

A combination of beers and margaritas were selected, with one member of our party confidently proclaiming the margarita to be "good." The prices for the beverages proved to be quite reasonable, with Mexican beers priced at a mere $2.95.

Moving on to the main course, we all placed our orders, and were pleased to find that the food arrived promptly, served fresh and steaming. Each dish was delectable and satisfied our palates to the fullest extent. The waiter, although soft-spoken, attended to all our needs attentively.

To our delight, the kitchen staff graciously accommodated our specific requests, such as omitting beans or reducing the cheese content, without any issues. Departing with contented stomachs, we decided to conclude the evening with a visit to the Red Garter for an unforgettable strip club experience.

In closing, El Arado has undeniably received unwarranted criticism. The staff proves to be decent, the food surpasses expectations, and the prices for drinks remain remarkably affordable. It is an excellent choice for an economically favorable and satisfying meal prior to a night out in Fountain Square, or even before venturing to various strip clubs in the area.

input: The Loew's hotel is very clean and looks very nice. The service is amazing. My family and I wanted to stay for a whole month. The breakfast there is fantastic! My son said it looked like it was the future. That's how nice it was! The rooms were nice size and the parking is convenient. That's why I give the Loew's hotel 5 stars.
Revise this with your best effort: The Loew's hotel exudes an impeccable level of cleanliness and boasts an exquisite aesthetic appeal. The service we experienced during our stay was nothing short of sensational. In fact, my family and I were so captivated by the exceptional service that we contemplated extending our visit for an entire month. The breakfast offered at this establishment is truly outstanding! To put it in my son's words, it resembled a glimpse into the future, such was its remarkable quality. Moreover, the rooms are generously spacious, ensuring utmost comfort, and the parking facilities are both accessible and convenient. For these remarkable reasons, I wholeheartedly award the Loew's hotel a well-deserved rating of 5 stars.

input:
Yayyy for honeygrow ! I honestly can 't believe it took me so long to try this place. It's awesome ! It is in the same complex as my gym and I always said I would give it a shot but didn't seem to make it over there. 

Well this past Tuesday it happened and I have a new spot to grab a healthy meal. I ordered the Sour Cherry BBQ stir fry with chicken instead of pork and parsley instead of shallots and it was amazing. Low calorie and OO so filling. While the line was long it went very quickly and my food was ready shortly after that. I love that you can order and pay right on the kiosk. 

The employees were friendly and efficient and all went smoothly. I'll definitely go back.
Revise this with your best effort:
I can't contain my excitement for honeygrow! It's mind-boggling that it took me so long to finally give it a try, but boy, am I glad I did. This place is absolutely awesome! Conveniently located in the same complex as my gym, I always had it in the back of my mind to pay it a visit, but for some reason, I never managed to make my way over there.

However, all that changed this past Tuesday, and I am thrilled to have discovered a fantastic spot to grab a healthy meal. I opted for the Sour Cherry BBQ stir fry with chicken instead of pork, and I switched out the shallots for parsley. Let me just say, it was a taste sensation! Not only was it low in calories, but it also left me feeling incredibly satisfied.

Despite the lengthy line, the wait time was surprisingly quick, and my food was ready shortly thereafter. What impressed me the most was their user-friendly self-serve kiosk, allowing me to effortlessly order and pay. The friendly and efficient employees ensured that everything ran seamlessly, enhancing my overall experience. Without a doubt, I will be revisiting honeygrow in the future.

input:
Pros:

-Superb cheeseburger - thick, evenly cooked, (almost) medium rare, nice sauce, soft bun

-Good service

-Cool ambience
-Downstairs from my apartment

Cons:

Cons:

- According to my wife, there may have been an instance where the waitress appeared disappointed that we only ordered cheeseburgers. However, further verification is required to confirm if this truly is a negative aspect.

Overall, I am eagerly anticipating my next visit to this establishment.

input: Smokey (to be expected - minus a star as a non smoker with allergies), several dining options (prices varies), beverages (all sorts for a nominal fee, of course), hotel (pricey), parking (FREE), entertainment (various), ATM (scared for some people who may not have self control), and yes gambling (tip: don't gamble if you're bit willing to lose it). Have fun even if you are an observer (like me).
Revise this with your best effort: Smokey's, a well-known establishment, boasts diverse amenities, albeit with some setbacks like my allergic reactions due to smoke exposure. Notably, there are multiple dining options available, although prices do vary. Additionally, an extensive range of beverages can be acquired for a nominal fee. The hotel, on the other hand, may be considered pricey. However, it does offer the advantage of complimentary parking. It is worth mentioning the presence of an ATM, though I recognize that it may provoke anxiety for individuals lacking self-control. Furthermore, for those inclined, there is gambling available, but it is advisable to approach it with caution and the acceptance of potential losses. Lastly, even as an observer like myself, I encourage you to have a great time at Smokey's.

input: This place is disappointing for a 4.5 star rating. The burgers were so-so. The vibe felt very much like a chain restaurant like Red Robin. We did go on a Tuesday night so perhaps it's better on the weekends? Either way, we won't be back.
Revise this with your best effort: Despite its 4.5 star rating, this place turned out to be quite disappointing. The burgers were just average, failing to impress. The overall atmosphere gave off a generic chain restaurant vibe akin to Red Robin. Granted, we visited on a Tuesday night, so it is plausible that the experience improves during the weekends. Nevertheless, our disappointment was significant enough to confirm that we won't be returning.

input: This is hands down my favorite brewery in The world!! My husband is from STL and every time we go back to visit his family we visit the brewery! Most recently, we didn't"Beer School" with some of our friends and it was AWESOME!! Revise this with your best effort: Without a doubt, this is by far my most cherished brewery in the entire world! My husband hails from STL, and every time we make the journey to visit his family, we make it a point to stop by this remarkable brewery. Recently, we had the incredible opportunity to attend "Beer School" alongside some dear friends, and let me tell you, it was absolutely spectacular! I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone. Witnessing the majestic Clydesdales and unraveling the intricacies of this brewery was a truly awe-inspiring experience! input:
We arrived a few minutes early for a 7pm reservation. When we asked for our table, both hostesses looking at their paper, then said they'd have to go check and would be back. 5 minutes later, they returned and did not acknowledge us. Meanwhile, another large party arrived without a reservation and were told it would be a 40 minute wait. We then heard one hostess say to the other that she didn't want to seat them soon because the kitchen was backed up and people were waiting 40 minutes for their appetizers. So unprofessional.
We walked up again, after they continued to ignore us, and asked about our table. They weren't apologetic when they told us that the girl we spoke to earlier that day was new and never recorded our reservation. They continued to tell us that it would be at least a 20 minute wait before they could put our table together. We got a smug "I'm sorry, but she was new" and they brushed us off.
I really understand that sometimes things just don't go the way they were supposed to and that people make mistakes. However, a little customer service would have gone a long way. Offer us some water, or a seat at the bar or say that you're doing everything you can to get us in as soon as possible. They basically blew us off and blamed it on the new girl. 
Needless to say we left and I will not be returning.
Revise this with your best effort:
We arrived a few minutes early for our 7pm reservation, eager to have a pleasant dining experience. As we politely asked for our table, both hostesses were engrossed in their paperwork and seemed preoccupied. After informing us that they needed to check, they left without any further acknowledgment. A mere five minutes later, they returned, but unfortunately failed to acknowledge our presence. To our surprise, a large party without a reservation arrived shortly after and were informed of a 40-minute wait. Overhearing one hostess confide in the other about the kitchen's delayed appetizer orders, we couldn't help but perceive their behavior as unprofessional.

Feeling neglected and disregarded, we decided to approach the hostesses once more and inquire about our table. Disappointingly, their response lacked any form of apology as they revealed that the new girl we had spoken to earlier failed to record our reservation. They coldly informed us that it would be at least another 20 minutes before our table would be ready, accompanied by a smug "I'm sorry, but she was new," as if that justified their lack of attention.

While I understand that mishaps and human errors can occur, a little bit of customer service and empathy could have made all the difference. They could have offered us some water or even a seat at the bar while assuring us that they were doing everything they could to expedite our seating. However, instead of taking responsibility and attempting to rectify the situation, they chose to dismissively brush us off and shift blame onto the new employee.

Regrettably, we made the decision to leave the establishment that day, and I am left with no desire to return. The overall experience conveyed a total disregard for customer satisfaction, and I am disappointed that such neglectful behavior overshadowed what could have been a memorable dining experience.

input: Food was excellent but when asked to honor their yelp offer of 10% off our bill for checking in and reviewing their business, We were told that they would not honor the deal until our next visit even though the yelp countdown said we had 4 hours to redeem the deal. Great food, but bad business practice :(
Revise this with your best effort: The food at this establishment was truly excellent. However, I was disappointed with their refusal to honor the Yelp offer of 10% off our bill for checking in and reviewing their business. input:
I have only been here on a few occasions, mostly to send the random package, I like that this location has one of the automated machine (the post office closest to me does not...)

But what I wanted to highlight was the fantastic customer service my husband and I experienced when we went here to get our passport applications submitted, the representative we worked with was awesome. She was fast, friendly and knew exactly what needed to be done so we were in and out super quick! She even gave me the follow up forms and explained what I would need to do once I changed my name, perfect. I hope every experience here in the future is just as good. She should train everyone.
Revise this with your best effort:
I have visited this place only a few times, mainly to send the occasional random package. What I particularly appreciate about this location is the presence of an automated machine, which is notably absent in the post office closest to my residence.

However, I would like to emphasize the exceptional customer service my husband and I encountered when we visited this place to submit our passport applications. input: Oh my goodness if you ever want to start on a health "trip" this is the place to start. They have so many different vitamins (hence the name), healthy dietary supplements, beauty products and homeopathic items as well. The staff was super helpful in assisting me find some of the items i needed to make my very own moisturizer. And they accept digital coupons- LOVE THAT TOO!
Revise this with your best effort: If you're looking to embark on a journey towards better health, this is the ultimate starting point! The abundance of vitamins and various health supplements, along with a wide range of beauty and homeopathic products, make this place a haven for health enthusiasts. What impressed me the most was the incredibly helpful staff who guided me in finding the ingredients I needed to create my personalized moisturizer. Not only did they assist me in locating the items they had in stock, but they also offered valuable suggestions for the items they didn't carry. On top of that, their rewards program for frequent shoppers is simply fantastic - definitely something to adore! Additionally, the fact that they accept digital coupons just adds to the convenience and loveability of this place.

input: I love this shoppe. I have been here a few times, but I have been coming more regularly. The staff is AWESOME and the atmosphere GREAT. THey have healthy tasty treats which is nice and a host of croissants and other tasty treats. They also have food for lunch and breakfast. I havent had anything here that wasnt fantabulous.
Revise this with your best effort: I absolutely adore this shoppe. I've visited multiple times in the past, but recently, my visits have become more frequent. The staff is truly amazing, and the ambiance is simply delightful. Not only do they offer delicious and nutritious treats, but their assortment of croissants and other delectable pastries is unparalleled. Furthermore, they provide an extensive menu for both breakfast and lunch. I cannot recall a single item I have tried here that wasn't absolutely fabulous.

input: Great Cranberry Orange Muffin and Caffe Latte on a Saturday morning. Great ambience and fast service.
Revise this with your best effort: Enjoy a delightful Saturday morning with our delectable Cranberry Orange Muffin paired perfectly with a freshly brewed Caffe Latte. Immerse yourself in the warm and inviting atmosphere as our efficient staff ensures prompt and efficient service.

input: My favorite place to eat sushi and the nicest people I know that work there! It'll always be my first choice and they have a great menu! It's always more than just good when you eat from there!
Revise this with your best effort: When it comes to sushi, there's no place I'd rather dine than at my absolute favorite spot. Not only do they serve incredible sushi, but they also employ the most genuinely kind and hospitable individuals. Without a doubt, it remains my top pick, enhanced further by their extensive and delightful menu. Every dining experience goes beyond mere satisfaction; it becomes an exceptional culinary journey.

input: This might be my favorite coffee shop in the city. The food is unbelievable. Anything I have ordered has been fresh, delicious and so enjoyable. The place has a cool edgy vibe and lots of comfy seating and some great seats outside when the weather is nice. Definitely worth checking out especially if you want a some food as well.
Revise this with your best effort: In my opinion, this coffee shop stands out as a personal favorite among the many options available in the city. The food offerings here are truly exceptional, elevating the entire experience to a whole new level. Every dish I've ever ordered has consistently exceeded my expectations, boasting a delightful freshness and flavor that is truly enjoyable. The ambiance of this place is equally captivating, emanating a cool and edgy vibe that adds to its overall charm. With ample comfortable seating indoors and the added bonus of great outdoor seating for pleasant weather days, it provides a perfect setting to savor your meal. Whether you're seeking a delectable meal or simply looking to explore a remarkable coffee shop, this place is definitely worth a visit.

input: I absolutely love this place and think is easily the best burrito shop in town. Great salsas, relaxed atmosphere, excellent service and price,  Most importantly the burritos are delicious. The chicken and chorizo combo is  my personal favorite but the smoked brisket is great as well. The medium burrito is plenty unless you are training for an eating event.  Family owned, not a chain and it shows in the attention to flavor. Highest recommendation if you are interested in good, healthy food (unless you eat yourself into oblivion) at a reasonable price.
Revise this with your best effort: I have an absolute adoration for this establishment and truly believe it to be the premier burrito destination in town. The salsas are outstanding, creating a delightful blend of flavors that perfectly complement the relaxed ambience. Impeccable service and reasonable prices further enhance the overall experience. However, the true star of the show unquestionably lies in the scrumptious burritos. While the chicken and chorizo combo holds a special place in my heart, the smoked brisket option also impresses. Unless you have aspirations of participating in an eating marathon, the medium-sized burrito is more than sufficient. Being a family-owned establishment rather than a generic chain, the meticulous attention to flavor is clearly evident in each bite. Thus, I wholeheartedly recommend this place if you desire tasty, nourishing cuisine (unless, of course, you end up overindulging to the point of oblivion).

input:
This review is for their lunch menu as I have not tried their other offerings yet. If you are lucky enough to have lunch there during their 11-2 sandwich times, you are in for a real treat! The two sandwiches I have tried (the grinder and the southwesterner) were absolutely delicious! There wasn't a single taste bud that wasn't satisfied. It is pricey and sandwiches are a little on the small side but it is well worth it. 

Can't wait to try (afford) their steaks!!

Food: 5/5
Service: 5/5
Price: 4/5 - A little high but great quality
Revise this with your best effort:
I have only had the chance to sample their lunch menu, so this review solely pertains to that aspect. However, I must say that if you happen to find yourself dining at this establishment between the hours of 11 am and 2 pm, when they serve their delectable sandwiches, you are in for quite a treat! The two sandwiches I had the pleasure of indulging in, namely the grinder and the southwesterner, were nothing short of exquisite. Every single taste bud on my palate was thoroughly pleased with the explosion of flavors. Admittedly, the sandwiches are a tad on the smaller side, and the prices might be considered a bit steep. Nevertheless, the high quality of the ingredients and the overall dining experience make it more than worth it. I eagerly await the opportunity to give their steaks a try, once my budget allows it!

Food: 5/5
Service: 5/5
Price: 4/5 - Slightly expensive, but the exceptional quality justifies it.

input:
Tasty selection and very preppy! 

One cannot go wrong with the What's Up Doc omelet. One complaint with the omelets is the actual size, they seem to fluctuate. Clearly a difference in 4-5 extra bits worth of omelet. 

If you have a sweet tooth, any of french toasts are great! Fancy Breakfast Sandwich is great! I substituted the prosciutto with bacon and got great results! Great mimosas!
Revise this with your best effort:
Indulge in a delectable array of dishes that are both scrumptious and undeniably stylish! Embark on a tantalizing journey with the delightful What's Up Doc omelet, a foolproof choice that never disappoints. The only minor setback would be the occasional inconsistency in size, where a variance of 4-5 extra bites of omelet may occur.

For those with a penchant for something sweet, the assortment of French toasts is simply divine! And let's not forget about the Fancy Breakfast Sandwich, a true delight for the taste buds. As a personal touch, I opted for bacon instead of prosciutto and it proved to be a marvelous substitution. Complementing these delectable treats are the superb mimosas, adding an extra touch of magnificence to your dining experience.

input: Great store if you like 50's-Midcentury modern! The prices are a little high compared to my favorite stores in STL, but this store is one of a kind thats for sure!
Revise this with your best effort: If you have a passion for 50's-Midcentury modern, this store is a true gem! While the prices may be slightly higher than my beloved stores in STL, it's undeniable that this store is unparalleled in its uniqueness and charm.

input: STAY AWAY! I am a gold member, so I stay at Hamptons frequently. I have stayed here before, and it seems to be under constant construction. My room was dirty. I came back to give them another chance as it is close to my appointments. I show up for a four night stay, and they send me away because they are booked, but tell me I can come back tomorrow night. Seriously? I couldn't believe that. I wont be back.
Revise this with your best effort: WARNING: AVOID THIS PLACE! As a loyal gold member who frequently stays at Hamptons, I have experienced nothing but disappointment. Despite having visited before, this hotel seems to be perpetually under construction, making for an unpleasant stay. On top of that, my most recent visit was tarnished by a dirty room. Willing to give them another chance due to its convenient location for my appointments, I arrived for a four-night stay, only to be turned away claiming they were fully booked. However, they had the audacity to suggest I return the next night. Seriously? I was utterly shocked and disgusted by their lack of consideration and customer service. Needless to say, I will not be returning.

input: The best fried rice ever! Also the best Pho I had while in Nashville. I'm from Seattle so I'm a little spoiled in that department. If you're looking for a good place to try it for the first time or just looking for a good Vietnamese restaurant, GO!
Revise this with your best effort: You won't believe how amazing the fried rice is here! It truly stands as the best fried rice I've ever tasted. Moreover, while in Nashville, I stumbled upon the most incredible Pho. Being from Seattle, where Vietnamese cuisine is exceptional, I'll admit I'm a bit spoiled. However, this place exceeded all expectations. Whether you're trying Vietnamese food for the first time or simply searching for a remarkable Vietnamese restaurant, this place is an absolute must-visit!

input: Walked here from our condo and found this awesome place! Delicious sliders...donuts...unique drinks... Awesome atmosphere and the staff was sooooooo friendly! Will definitely be back!!!!!
Revise this with your best effort: I walked all the way here from our condominium and stumbled upon this incredible establishment! The sliders were absolutely delicious, accompanied by a delectable assortment of donuts and a selection of unique drinks. The atmosphere was truly awesome, creating such a vibrant and enjoyable experience. Moreover, the staff was extraordinarily friendly, making the visit even more delightful. Without a doubt, I will be returning to this exceptional place in the future!

input: As far as I know, this is the best video rental store in existence.  The staff is knowledgeable and friendly, but the selection really sets it apart.  Suppose you want to rent the newest release and a VHS of the best hockey fights of the 1970s...They would probably have both available at a very low cost.  I only wish that there was a place like Casa Video in Chicago.
Revise this with your best effort: To my understanding, Casa Video is undeniably the ultimate video rental store. Apart from its welcoming and well-informed staff, it's the remarkable selection that truly sets it apart from the rest. Whether you're seeking the latest releases or a nostalgic VHS tape featuring the greatest hockey fights of the 1970s, chances are they will have both options at an exceptionally affordable price. If only there existed a similar haven like Casa Video in the vibrant city of Chicago!

input:
That horrible angst - you want sushi, but you're not SO hungry that you can do AYCE or want to spend $25 for lunch. So we popped in on a weekend for a late lunch and decided to order a la carte.  I ordered a long roll and a hand roll, a drink and a chocolate mochi (OMG, I am officially in love with these things) and the total cost came to just under $20 with tip.  It filled my belly enough so that I was satisfied.  Had I gone for just one more roll, I probably would have broke even with the AYCE, but I probably would've been so stuffed to the point where I wouldn't have needed to eat anything else all day - not the plan for this particular day.

The rolls tasted fresh and delicious, but the surprise was definitely the mochi - so creamy and tasty.
Revise this with your best effort: When the craving for sushi strikes, but you aren't quite ravenous enough for an all-you-can-eat feast or willing to splurge $25 on lunch, a delightful solution presented itself. Opting for a late lunch on the weekend, we chose to go the a la carte route. Indulging in a long roll and a hand roll, accompanied by a refreshing beverage and a mouthwatering chocolate mochi, I discovered a newfound adoration for these delightful treats. The bill, including gratuity, tallied just under $20. This satisfying meal left my hunger satiated without feeling overwhelmingly full. While adding just one more roll would have put me on par with an all-you-can-eat option, it would have left me uncomfortably stuffed for the remainder of the day, which wasn't the intention on this particular occasion. The rolls exhibited a pleasing freshness and delectable taste, but the true surprise of the meal was undeniably the mochi - its creamy and delectable flavor was simply unforgettable.

input: Not too sure why all the negative reviews. I was in and out within 5 mins. Maybe it was because I wasn't looking for something elaborate, who knows. Anyways, I got exactly what I needed and the employees were courteous. The store was organized, well stocked and clean. Unfortunately for this area however, I don't see them staying in business. So many other places near by closed.
Revise this with your best effort: I'm not entirely sure why there are so many negative reviews, as my experience was quite positive. I was able to quickly find what I needed and complete my purchase within five minutes. Perhaps the negative feedback stems from those who were seeking more intricate items or experiences. Regardless, the store had everything I required, and the staff members were friendly and helpful. The overall presentation of the store was impressive, as it was well-organized, sufficiently stocked, and maintained a clean environment. However, it saddens me to observe that numerous nearby establishments have closed down, leading me to question the store's longevity in this area.

input: Best Pizza period. Love the staff and the beer is always cold and the taps are always maintained. If you want fresh beer and a slice it's only 5 bucks.
Revise this with your best effort: Experience the best pizza, period. Our staff offers impeccable service, and rest assured, our beer is refreshingly cold with perfectly maintained taps. Craving a slice with a side of freshly poured beer? Indulge yourself for just 5 bucks.

input:
All of hype about Federal Donuts made me a little worried it wouldn't live up to it's reputation. But, it absolutely did. I'm a vegetarian so I can only personally comment on the donuts and coffee; however, my husband is obsessed with the chicken. His favorite is the buttermilk ranch.

The donuts are pretty amazing. Paired with an iced coffee and it doesn't get any better. The staff couldn't be nicer- even when they're busy.
Revise this with your best effort:
I was initially skeptical due to the tremendous buzz surrounding Federal Donuts, fearing that it might not truly exceed expectations. However, my concerns were swiftly dispelled upon my visit, as it unquestionably lived up to its esteemed reputation. As a vegetarian, my personal appraisal is solely limited to the divine donuts and delectable coffee. Conversely, my husband, a devoted fan, is utterly infatuated with the chicken they offer, specifically favoring the extraordinary buttermilk ranch flavor.

The donuts, oh my, they are genuinely extraordinary. When coupled with an invigorating iced coffee, it creates an unparalleled combination that leaves no room for improvement. Moreover, the warmth and hospitality exuded by the staff, even in the face of a bustling crowd, is truly remarkable.

input:
Three chances and they are out! We tried to like this place as the location is easy and convenient. The bar is great, the staff friendly, but there is not a dish I have tried that is passable (although the asian shrimp wasn't bad, but very sweet). First visit we wrote off as a new restaurant working out the bugs. On our second visit I ordered a turkey burger and received a dry turkey patty. No one informed me that they were out of buns, but they could have at least tried to dress it up. It was seriously a lone piece of ground meat (to their credit, the manager did comp that meal). Today we received fish and chips that had to come out of a box and chicken salad that could have greased my axles!

We won't be back.
Revise this with your best effort:
We were hopeful about this place due to its convenient location and positive aspects like a great bar and friendly staff. However, after giving it three chances, we unfortunately have to conclude that it is not worth another visit. Every dish we've tried so far has been below satisfactory, aside from the relatively decent asian shrimp, although it was overly sweet. The first time we dined there, we were lenient and considered it as a new establishment still working out its kinks. On our second visit, I ordered a turkey burger which turned out to be disappointingly dry. To make matters worse, no one bothered to inform me that there were no buns available, and even a minimal effort to dress it up would have been appreciated. I was served just a plain ground meat patty (at least the manager had the decency to comp that meal). And today, we were served fish and chips that seemingly came straight out of a box, as well as a chicken salad that was excessively greasy. 

Given our consistently unsatisfactory experiences, we have made the decision not to return to this establishment.

input:
I could say that this is a touch of Italy in a strip mall, but even I recognize that is a little too precious. Stepping into the dark, cool interior of Sapore made for a refreshing change after the sweltering July heatwave. It was no problem for our party of three to be seated; the fact that we had a reservation helped, I am sure. We started out with drinks--bellinis for my two dinner companions and a classic vodka martini for me. I appreciated being able to customize my drink with a blue-cheese-stuffed olive and an anchovy. I would never have thought to put an anchovy in a martini, but it looks like this will be a new obsession for me. 

On to the food. We opted to skip the appetizers and go straight to soup/salad and entrees (all the better to save room for dessert). My mom went with the Italian soup and my other dining companion and I split the Caprese salad, a solid presentation that did not blow me away, but certainly does not provide grist for anything like the negative reviews of this establishment that I have seen on yelp. I didn't know what to expect in terms of pasta portions here, so I went with the Chicken Marsala. It might have been nice to have pasta to pick up some of the sauce, but I appreciated that the dish was hot by temperature and I even had enough for leftovers (to which I added pasta, in the comfort and convenience of my home).

The dessert selection was excellent. We went with the tiramisu. I understand Sapore also has an excellent cannoli which I would like to try on a future visit. I would be tempted to come back, if only for another excellent martini, appetizers, and another run through the dessert menu.
Revise this with your best effort:
Sapore offers a touch of Italy nestled in a strip mall, a hidden gem providing a welcome break from the scorching heatwave that July had brought. Despite its popularity, our party of three had no trouble securing a table, thanks to our reservation. As we settled into the dark and cool interior, we indulged in our chosen libations - bellinis for my companions and a classic vodka martini for myself, adorned with a unique twist of a blue-cheese-stuffed olive and an anchovy. Surprisingly, the fusion of an anchovy and a martini intrigued me and ignited a newfound obsession.

Moving on to the main event - the food. We decided to forgo appetizers, saving room for the enticing desserts that awaited us. While my mom opted for the Italian soup, my dining companion and I shared the Caprese salad. Although it didn't astonish me, it certainly didn't warrant the negative reviews I had encountered on Yelp. Unsure of the portion sizes for pasta dishes, I chose the Chicken Marsala. While it would have been delightful to have pasta to soak up the savory sauce, I contented myself with the piping hot dish and was even able to take some home for leftovers, which I transformed into a delightful pasta creation in the comfort of my own kitchen.

The dessert selection was divine. The unanimous choice was the tiramisu, although I couldn't help but be enticed by the rumored excellence of their cannoli, which will certainly beckon me on a future visit. The prospect of returning to Sapore for their remarkable martinis, tempting appetizers, and another indulgence in their dessert menu is undoubtedly tempting.

input:
Due to it's location in a strip mall near Cool Springs, this version of the Twelve South hipster gourmet Burger Up is certainly not as trendy. But it makes up for it by delivering the goods. Awesomely tasty and messy burgers with fresh meat and fixings. The regular fries are delicious... until you try the truffle fries. They are truly outstanding, not greasy and finished with paresan cheese. The metaphorical cherry-on-top was the chocolate milkshake (which actually had no cherry on top). The shake was nothing fancy, but perfectly made, creamy, not too sweet or over-chocolatey. 
If you want your upscale burger experience but still want your burger-fries-shake holy trinity, come here.
Revise this with your best effort:
This particular location of Twelve South's hipster gourmet Burger Up may not boast the same level of trendiness, owing to its placement in a strip mall near Cool Springs. Nevertheless, it compensates admirably by offering delectable, messy burgers that feature fresh meat and top-notch fixings. The regular fries alone satisfy the taste buds, but their truffle counterpart takes things to a whole new level of deliciousness. Remarkably, these fries manage to avoid greasiness and are enhanced with a delectable sprinkling of parmesan cheese. Adding to the delightful experience was the chocolate milkshake, which, despite lacking any adornments, proved to be a sumptuously crafted treat. Creamy, perfectly balanced in sweetness, and not overwhelmed by an excess of chocolate flavor, it exemplified simplicity done right. 

Should you yearn for an elevated burger experience without sacrificing the iconic triumvirate of burger, fries, and shake, look no further than this establishment.

input: I dropped my car off first thing in the morning for a simple "check engine" light appointment. I was told at the end of that day that my car had not been looked at and would not be ready until the following day. What was the point of making an appointment, if they didn't even touch my car? The next evening when I came to pick it up, after they called me to tell me it was ready, I waited for a full hour before my car was given to me. They had parked so many cars in front of it they couldn't get it out. That is an hour of my life I will never get back, all because someone called and told me to come pick up my car (...which was there for two full business days, unnecessarily. For the record, there was nothing wrong with the car. It needed no repair and no maintenance). There was a kind woman who asked how they could make it up to me, but I had to tell her that I will likely never return, so it wasn't worth her time.
Revise this with your best effort: I scheduled an early morning appointment to address a simple "check engine" light issue with my car. However, to my disappointment, by the end of the day, I was informed that my car had not been looked at and that it wouldn't be ready until the following day. I couldn't help but question why I had bothered to make an appointment if they didn't even touch my car. The next evening, when I received a call notifying me that my car was ready, I went to pick it up, only to find myself waiting for a full hour. They had carelessly parked numerous cars in front of mine, obstructing its retrieval. That hour of waiting felt like a complete waste of my time. It's frustrating to think that my car had been sitting there for two full business days, unnecessarily, considering it required no repair or maintenance. While a kind woman inquired about how they could compensate for their mistakes, I regretfully informed her that I would likely never return, making it not worth her time to make amends.

input: For many years, RH&B was the place to go in south Jersey for great BBQ and blues. Sadly, after a recent sale, the restaurant has decided to cancel all live music. The food was decent at best, and in the absence of live music offerings  I can no longer recommend this restaurant. The only aspect I will miss are the people who worked there.
Revise this with your best effort: RH&B has long been renowned as the ultimate destination in south Jersey for an exceptional blend of delectable BBQ and soulful blues. However, it is with sincere regret that I inform you of a recent sale, leading the restaurant to make the distressing decision to discontinue hosting live music performances. Regrettably, this added absence of the captivating live music experiences has greatly diminished my enthusiasm to recommend this establishment, despite its decent culinary offerings. Nevertheless, it is worth mentioning that the departure of live music is overshadowed by the fondness I will undoubtedly hold for the remarkable individuals who contributed their efforts within the restaurant.

input:
This use to be a reliable place for sandwiches but the last two were not good at all.  Cheesesteak was light on the meat.  There are so many good rolls to pick from in the Philly area but this roll was one of the worst and stale.

Hopefully it was just an off night. I'll try again but not for awhile.
Revise this with your best effort:
This place used to be known for its reliable sandwiches, but unfortunately, the last two outings were quite disappointing. The cheesesteak lacked an adequate portion of meat, leaving it lacking in flavor. Moreover, considering the abundance of excellent rolls available in the Philly area, it's disheartening to say that the roll used here was one of the worst, as it was definitely stale. 

Perhaps this was just an off night for them, so I'll give them another chance in the future. However, I think it's best to refrain from revisiting for a while.

input: Maybe I just had bad luck at this property but I am a SPG gold member... quickly approaching platinum and made a reservation at this property. I payed a good amount for my room and when I asked for a larger room they told me they where all the same. I asked did every room have adjoining doors and was told yes. I then told the front desk clerk that I could hear EVERYTHING going on next door including sneezing and even AC talking on CNN 360 very clearly. He told me to come down and get a new key and move to a room there was nobody in. They did not offer to bring me a key or help me move. When I got to the lobby the line was at least 10 people deep and there was only ONE person there. I just gave up and dealt with the noise and a few hours later they finally turned off the TV and I could sleep.  There is nothing fancy about this hotel and the service for sure needs improvement!
Revise this with your best effort: Perhaps I just had the unfortunate experience at this particular property, but as a SPG gold member, and rapidly approaching platinum, I had made a reservation here expecting a certain level of service. Despite paying a significant amount for my room, when I inquired about the possibility of a larger room, I was informed that they were all the same. I further inquired if every room had adjoining doors, to which I received an affirmative response. However, it became evident that this was not the case when I could clearly hear every little sound emanating from the room next door, including sneezing and even the audio from CNN 360 playing on their AC. In an attempt to rectify the situation, the front desk clerk instructed me to retrieve a new key and move to an unoccupied room. Unfortunately, they did not offer any assistance or even offer to bring the key to me. Upon reaching the lobby, I was met with a frustratingly long queue of at least ten people, with only a single staff member present to attend to them. Feeling defeated, I resigned myself to the noise and endured for several hours until the TV was finally turned off, allowing me to get some much-needed sleep. All in all, this hotel lacks any notable elegance, and I strongly believe that their service is in dire need of improvement.

input: Food was fresh and tasted great, nothing amazing but price was fair and staff was very helpful and nice.
Revise this with your best effort: The food offered was fresh and had a delightful taste. While it wasn't extraordinary, the price was reasonable and affordable. In addition, the staff members were tremendously supportive and kind, providing excellent customer service.

input:
Its a hotel and you can stay there.

After a couple of stays here I find it is not bad. 

Its definitely more of a business traveler kind of place than a tourist kind of place.

Pros
The rooms have the essentials. The beds are quite comfortable.
The cafe isn't bad although it is a little foggy as to what comes with the room. Apparently its one entree and one beverage. Not a bad deal.

Cons
Hallways are a bit shaggy. NBD since I am not staying in the hallway.
Room cleaning dropped the ball on my last stay. The room was clean, but I found a bag from BK in my mini fridge ... eeeew!
Revise this with your best effort:
After having stayed at this hotel a couple of times, I must say it's not too bad. It leans more towards accommodating business travelers rather than tourists.

Pros:
The rooms provide all the essentials, and the beds are particularly comfortable.
The café, although slightly unclear about what's included, serves decent food. It seems to offer one entree and one beverage, which is actually a pretty good deal.

Cons:
The hallways could use some maintenance as they appear a bit worn-out. However, it doesn't really affect my stay since I'm not spending much time in the hallway.
Unfortunately, the housekeeping service let me down during my last visit. Although the room itself was clean, I was unpleasantly surprised to find a bag from Burger King in my mini fridge. It left a rather unpleasant impression.

input:
I recently moved in a few blocks away from Henry's and was looking forward to having a neighborhood coffee spot not far from my house. So, on a beautifully humid August morning I walked over to check it. 

1) The atmosphere is pretty standard. Open space with the coffee bar in the back left corner and ordinary tables and chairs scattered throughout. No college coffee shop couches or armchairs but no industrial airbnb chic vibe either. Lacked uniqueness. 

2) The name Henry reminds me of Thomas the tank engine. Was there a train named Henry on there or not? If so, was he chill or not. Could add one star for chill train association. 

3) The coffee was not good. I got an iced coffee (STFU) and it was super bitter. The amount of ice in it wasn't obscene so it had that going for it but other than that idk.

I'm coming back to try some hot coffee or espresso on a cooler day but damn Henry :((( not a great first impression.
Revise this with your best effort:
I recently relocated just a few blocks away from Henry's and was eager to find a nearby coffee spot to frequent. With an August morning filled with gentle humidity, I ventured over to check it out.

1) The ambiance of the place is rather average. It boasts an open space design, with the coffee bar positioned in the back left corner and regular tables and chairs scattered throughout. While it doesn't flaunt any trendy college coffee shop couches or armchairs, it also lacks the impersonal airbnb chic vibe. It could use a touch of uniqueness to stand out.

2) The name "Henry" sparks a nostalgic connection to Thomas the Tank Engine. I can't help but wonder if there was a train named Henry on the show, and if so, was he known for his laid-back demeanor? Perhaps a potential bonus star if there's a chill train association.

3) Unfortunately, the coffee did not meet expectations. I opted for an iced coffee (STFU), and it turned out to be excessively bitter. On the bright side, the proportion of ice was not over the top, but aside from that, I'm unsure. Nonetheless, I plan to return on a cooler day to give their hot coffee or espresso a chance. Disappointing first impression, Henry :(((

input:
We were thoroughly impressed with this hotel! Upon arriving, you are immediately welcomed with the scent of fresh baked cookies. Walking up to the desk we were greeted by Valorie who informed us that cookies and water were complementary to guests and that we were more than welcome. Across from the desk we noticed a book shelf. This is not the kind of book shelf where rejected leftovers were placed but rather, a wide range of books by well known authors. The name of the program was called Read it and Return. In essence, you can borrow a book for the duration of your stay and if you don't finish it you can return it the next time you stay at the hotel at any of the Carlson hotels who have the same program! ( what!?! Cookies and books!?! YES!) Right off the bat, we felt like we were right at home.

   Arriving at our room, we noticed that everything was extremely clean and there was a refrigerator (with a small freezer) , a microwave, a coffee maker, and a well working A.C. (you know, the kind that you don't have to yell over to have a conversation). The bathroom was stocked with brand name shampoo, conditioner, and lotion.

  Our next stop was the smoking area. Normally, smokers feel as though they have been marooned to a small place behind the dumpster...but not here! Provided was 2 sets of swinging benches; set far enough away so that it did not disturb the guests in rooms around the area but no a 10 mile hike for those adults who enjoy the pleasure. Did I also mention they have smoking rooms available?

In the morning, feel free to partake in a complimentary breakfast (NOT CONTINENTAL)-I mean a real breakfast which changes daily; anything from fresh made waffles to eggs, sausage, and bacon! Also, cold cereal, juices, and coffees have options! Coffee is available 24/7 as well! 

The hotel also has a pool and hot tub which I personally observed them clean daily!

On our last night we got back late and I was going to ask the desk for a late check out, but there was no need! Their check out time is 12:00 Pm as opposed to the hotel usual of 11:00 Am. That worked out well for us.

At checkout we were asked if there was anything we would change about the hotel or our stay. I made small suggestions which I thought would help them, but definitely nothing major. The desk person wrote down what I said and said she would pass it on! I was impressed with that, because we've been asked about our stay at other places, but it seemed more out of routine than actual interest. Here, she seemed genuinely interested. We don't usually do reviews, so I'm sorry for the long review. However, we wanted you to get a real feel for this wonderful hotel and hope that you enjoy it as much as we did! Thanks for reading and safe travels. J & Niki.
Revise this with your best effort:
We were incredibly impressed with our experience at this hotel! From the moment we arrived, we were greeted with the delightful scent of freshly baked cookies. Valorie, the receptionist, warmly welcomed us and informed us that cookies and water were complimentary for guests. We were immediately made to feel at home.

As we approached the reception desk, we couldn't help but notice a bookshelf filled with a wide range of books by well-known authors. This unique program, called Read it and Return, allowed guests to borrow books for the duration of their stay and return them during their next visit at any of the Carlson hotels that offer the same program. It was such a pleasant surprise to find this combination of cookies and books!

Entering our room, we were delighted to find a spotlessly clean environment equipped with convenient amenities such as a refrigerator with a small freezer, a microwave, a coffee maker, and an efficient air-conditioning unit that didn't require us to raise our voices to hold a conversation. The bathroom was thoughtfully stocked with high-quality branded shampoo, conditioner, and lotion.

Next, we discovered the designated smoking area, which stood out from the typical cramped spaces found behind dumpsters. The hotel provided two sets of swinging benches, strategically placed far enough away from guest rooms to avoid any disturbances, yet still easily accessible for adults who enjoy smoking. It's worth mentioning that the hotel also offers smoking rooms for added convenience.

In the morning, we indulged in a complimentary breakfast that exceeded our expectations. Unlike the typical continental breakfasts found elsewhere, this hotel served a variety of freshly made options that changed daily. From delicious waffles to eggs, sausage, and bacon, there was something to satisfy every appetite. Cold cereal, juices, and a variety of coffees were also available, providing plenty of choices. For coffee lovers, it was a joy to discover that coffee was available 24/7.

One of the highlights of our stay was the hotel's clean and well-maintained pool and hot tub. It was evident that they were diligently cleaned daily, offering a relaxing and enjoyable experience for guests.

On our last night, we returned to the hotel late and considered requesting a late checkout. However, to our delight, we discovered that the checkout time was already set at 12:00 PM, an hour later than the standard 11:00 AM. This flexibility worked perfectly for us.

During checkout, we were pleasantly surprised when asked if there was anything we would change about our stay. Although we only had minor suggestions, the desk person attentively noted them down and assured us our feedback would be passed on. This level of genuine interest showcased the hotel's commitment to guest satisfaction, far surpassing our previous experiences where inquiries appeared more routine than sincere. 

We rarely write reviews, but we wanted to provide you with a comprehensive account of our wonderful stay at this remarkable hotel. We sincerely hope that you enjoy your time here just as much as we did. Thank you for taking the time to read our review, and we wish you safe travels. 

Sincerely,
J & Niki

input: Let me start by saying buying a car is an intimidating process. I feel like I am playing poker with someone who can see all of the cards while I can only see my cards. Sam Ladd was the salesman who always treated me courteously and let me drive lots of cars while I was deciding what vehicle I wanted. I drove everything from subcompacts to full sized SUVs. I visited many dealerships I chose Toyota of Santa Barbara because they ultimately had the vehicle that I wanted. I bought what I believe will meet my families needs. The negotiation process was business like and I believe that Frank Flores the sales manager was up front with me and answered my concerns. Be prepared and stick to your position throughout the process.

input: Great bar and atmosphere. Bartenders are very friendly as well as the owner. Mixed crowd and staff makes everyone feel welcomed and right at home! The  BBQ truck parked outside is excellent!!

input: Really nice staff but mediocre Italian food served luke warm.   We went here for a large group dinner around Christmas mostly because it was a BYOB and there was no fixed menu for a group of 10.   We ordered numerous appetizers including, fried gnocchi, calamari, garlic pizza bread, fried zucchini.   It was all just ok.   The main courses were unadventurous Italian American selections.  The sauces were just meh.   Three of us ordered 3 different chicken dishes and they all came out with the same sauce.   Boring.  Although the staff was very accommodating, the food was too lack luster to return.
Revise this with your best effort: The staff at this establishment are really nice and accommodating, however, the Italian cuisine leaves something to be desired as it is served lukewarm. We ordered several appetizers, including fried gnocchi, calamari, garlic pizza bread, and fried zucchini, but they were all just okay in terms of taste. input: One of the best and friendliest Chinese places to grab something tasty. Try the double treasure.
