input:
Wildflower is a super scrum, cute little restaurant. I've been here twice now for lunch, unfortunately I am always too late for breakfast. Fortunately though, their lunch is delicious! I took my mum here for her birthday for lunch and we were both so pleased!! 

Sad to say, but due to some health issues, I've had to really change my diet around. This was my first time going out to eat since being on this new regimen. I'm definitely limited, which is too bad, and there was a lot I couldn't have. The menu has good selections, but there is a lot with meat, and I've been a vegetarian for years. Regardless, they serve great food, I just like big menus. Everything is made in house and they use fresh and local ingredients. My mum got the Vermonter salad, which she LOVED!!! It had mixed greens, Vermont cheddar, applewood smoked bacon, pecans, and dried cherries. The dressing was a home made honey vinaigrette I believe. It came with two delicious pieces of muesli bread with a home made honey butter. YUM!! I had the tuna plate, which was great too. It had a very good portion of tuna salad, mixed greens, mixed veggies, and came with a biscuit with that delicious honey butter. It also came with a fresh fruit bowl!!!! I couldn't have the biscuit so I traded for muesli and man that stuff was delicious. My mum loves the biscuit too. Everything is definitely made with love and happiness here!!!

The patio is so cute, 4 tables on a nice little deck with fans and hanging lights. Our server was wonderful, SO kind and adorable. She even brought my mum
a homemade red velvet cupcake with a candle, which LOOKED amazing, and she thought was delicious. Another win at Wildflower, would love to come back for breakfast sometime.
Revise this with your best effort:
Wildflower is an absolutely charming and delightful restaurant, full of scrumptious surprises. Though I've missed out on their breakfast offerings during my visits, I can confidently say that their lunch is a true delight! Recently, I had the pleasure of celebrating my mother's birthday at this lovely establishment, and we were both beyond satisfied with our experience.

Unfortunately, due to some health concerns, my diet has undergone significant changes. This outing marked my first venture into dining out since implementing my new regimen. Despite the limitations I now face, which is a shame, there were plenty of options I couldn't indulge in. The menu boasts an array of tempting choices, but being a vegetarian for several years, I found that many of the dishes revolved around meat. Nevertheless, the food served at Wildflower is exceptional, although I must admit, I am partial to extensive menus. Each dish is carefully crafted with fresh and local ingredients, all prepared in-house.

My mother opted for the Vermonter salad and oh, how she adored it! The intricate combination of mixed greens, Vermont cheddar, applewood smoked bacon, pecans, and dried cherries culminated in a delightful medley of flavors. The homemade honey vinaigrette served as the perfect finishing touch. Alongside the salad, two delectable slices of muesli bread were expertly accompanied by homemade honey butter. A taste sensation, truly! As for myself, I savored the tuna plate, which was equally marvelous. A generous portion of tuna salad, paired with mixed greens and veggies, was accompanied by a biscuit slathered in the same mouthwatering honey butter. The dish also included a palate-refreshing bowl of fresh fruit. Although the biscuit was off-limits for me, I happily traded it for a serving of the divine muesli bread. Trust me, it was beyond delicious, and my mother couldn't resist its charm either. It's evident that love and happiness are the secret ingredients to every dish crafted at Wildflower!

The patio deserves a special mention, as it exudes sheer cuteness. Four tables on a delightful deck, adorned with gentle fans and twinkling hanging lights, create a perfect ambiance for a memorable dining experience. Additionally, our server went above and beyond to ensure our satisfaction, radiating kindness and an undeniable adorableness. To top it all off, she surprised my mother with a homemade red velvet cupcake, complete with a flickering candle. The cupcake looked absolutely stunning, and according to my mother, it was a scrumptious treat.

Wildflower once again surpasses expectations, leaving me yearning to return for a breakfast adventure in the near future.

input: Worst roast pork sandwich I've ever had. The broccoli rabe was lifeless and freezing. It was so cold my cheese didn't melt. The bread was soggy and wet. Horrible. If I wasn't in an airport, I'd bring this back.

Considering each entree costs ~$8, you get what you pay for. I ordered the Pad Thai and it was bad. Way too sweet with no spicy kick to it. We also ordered the Seafood Crispy Noodles, Pearl Noodles, and a Beef rice dish. All were really mediocre. The Indian pancakes and chicken satay apps were great though. Idk why the entrees were so lackluster. I'm sad I didn't enjoy it more but I'm glad the total was cheap for a night out.
Revise this with your best effort:

Considering the cost of each entree at around $8, it is fair to say that you get what you pay for. I opted for the Pad Thai, which unfortunately was disappointing. Though the entrees were underwhelming, I must commend the Indian pancakes and chicken satay appetizers, as they were delicious. input:
Had a great dinner at Spasso. My parents always request Oana and she is an awesome server-- answers questions, gives suggestions, and really knows the menu. We were quoted an hour wait, but were able to grab a high top in the bar area with no wait (they are full service).

Spasso is Italian, but has its own little spin; it's not just the classic dishes of a typical Italian restaurant.

They start you off with bread and this delicious eggplant/pepper topping that is so refreshing. I typically love oil for bread, but love this alternative.

I started with a Caesar salad which was perfect; just enough dressing, super fresh and I love the shaved Parmesan on top. For dinner I had pappardelle porcini which I think is the best item on the menu, it is thick pasta with sundried tomatoes, mushrooms and chicken with light sauce. It is totally delicious, and I had leftovers to have for lunch the next day.

Spasso is definitely recommended for a great dinner in Media!
Revise this with your best effort:
I had an exceptional dining experience at Spasso. Whenever my parents and I visit, we always request Oana as our server, and she never disappoints. Oana goes above and beyond, readily answering our questions, providing helpful suggestions, and demonstrating her extensive knowledge of the menu. Despite being initially quoted an hour wait, we were pleasantly surprised to find an available high top table in the bar area without any delay, as Spasso offers full-service seating.

Spasso offers a unique twist on Italian cuisine, introducing innovative flavors not commonly found in traditional Italian restaurants. To start, they serve warm, crusty bread accompanied by a delightful eggplant and pepper topping that offers a refreshing contrast. While I usually prefer oil with my bread, this alternative proved to be equally enjoyable.

For my appetizer, I opted for the Caesar salad. It struck the perfect balance with just the right amount of dressing, a medley of incredibly fresh ingredients, and a generous sprinkle of shaved Parmesan on top. Moving on to the main course, I delighted in the pappardelle porcini, which is undoubtedly the highlight of the menu. This dish features thick pasta cooked to perfection, complemented by sundried tomatoes, mushrooms, tender chicken, and a delicate sauce. The combination of flavors is simply mouthwatering, and I even had enough for a delectable leftover lunch the following day.

Without a doubt, I highly recommend Spasso for an exceptional dining experience in Media.

For those who relish in succulent meats, a chorizo taco would certainly prove to be an impeccable choice, while the aficionados of oceanic delicacies will find the fish tacos to be truly extraordinary.

input: Wings Wings and more Wings!  Chatham Tap is my favorite place to get wings in the Indianapolis area. On a recent visit with a sizable group, we had the opportunity to try various items from their menu. Initially unsure about Chatham Tap being labeled as a "soccer bar," I was pleasantly surprised by the fantastic atmosphere upon stepping inside. It's bustling with fans of all different sports, and the staff eagerly accommodates your desire to watch any specific game on TV. Their willingness to cater to diverse sporting interests impressed me greatly.

The service we received during our visit was truly exceptional. Without having to ask, our attentive server took care of all our needs, ensuring that we never had to wait or request anything throughout the entire evening. This level of attentiveness made our dining experience truly enjoyable and stress-free.

For anyone seeking a remarkable dining experience, accompanied by top-notch service and a memorable time with friends, I wholeheartedly recommend Chatham Tap. Trust me, you won't be disappointed.

input:
I have been going to this dive bar for years. Jonny's has a great happy hour everyday and it's very laid back. The food is always on point though. You may think that a dive like this wouldn't have the best options but you are wrong my friend. They make all of their dough from scratch and their naked wings keep me coming back every time. Their Jon's salad with grilled chicken is also a staple of mine along with their pizza.
They also offer games such as trivia and even bingo. They are all free to play and you win some great stuff like gift certificates and even 1 cent pitchers of beer! Can't go wrong with that. 
It is a smoking bar so be aware of that and it gets pretty bad when they are busy. It does get  crowded on game days or nights. Overall it's a great place to grab a few cheap beers with friends and a half-price pizza (did I mention they have 1/2 off pizza on certain days?)
Revise this with your best effort:
For years, I have frequented this dive bar called Jonny's, where the daily happy hour never fails to impress and the atmosphere remains relaxed. Surprisingly, the food at this humble establishment is consistently exceptional. Despite initial assumptions, their diverse menu defies expectations with homemade dough and irresistibly delicious naked wings that ensure my frequent return. In particular, their Jon's salad with grilled chicken has become a personal favorite alongside their delectable pizza.

What sets Jonny's apart is the array of games they offer, including trivia and bingo, all of which are absolutely free to participate in. Moreover, the prizes up for grabs range from enticing gift certificates to unbelievable deals like 1 cent pitchers of beer. Truly an unbeatable experience. However, it is essential to note that this is a smoking bar, so caution is advised, and the smoke tends to intensify during peak hours. Furthermore, it can get quite crowded on game days or nights, but despite these minor inconveniences, Jonny's remains an ideal spot to enjoy several budget-friendly beers with friends while indulging in half-price pizza (and did I mention they have 50% off pizza on select days?).

input: Yummy food,  they will veganize things for you as well. The servers are friendly and the restaurant is spacious and has a bar and a stage area. We have had our work Holiday party here for the past couple years, both parties turned out great. The guacamole is awesome!

input:
West Ave. Grill- Its a happy place in Jenkintown with a lot of locals eating outside under umbrellas with their dogs at their feet and kids on their lap.  Inside their is a large and small area with a bar to eat and look past the parking lot to nicer part of Jenkintown town square.  The wait staff is always nice and the owner is often around to talk to.  Free dum dum lolly pops at the counter as you walk out and news papers to read if you are eating alone or want to check in on the Phillies.
Food- always good. Great pancakes that are fluffy and crispy on the edges.  Kansas City  is a great breakfast too- for the most part great.
Big salads could have more Stuff in them- more of the things that are supposed to be there- as described etc.  But a complaint is readily heard and they always try to make you happy.  It's Nice- try it.
Revise this with your best effort:
West Ave. Grill is a delightful spot in Jenkintown bustling with locals enjoying their meals outdoors, shaded by umbrellas, with their furry companions by their side and little ones on their laps. Step inside and you'll find a spacious restaurant filled with a large and smaller dining area, complete with a bar. Through the windows, you can catch glimpses of the charming Jenkintown town square, adding to the pleasant ambiance. The wait staff at West Ave. Grill are consistently friendly, and the owner often makes an appearance, eager to strike up a conversation.

As a delightful touch, you'll be greeted with complimentary dum dum lolly pops at the counter as you bid your farewell. If you choose to dine alone or desire some reading material, they offer newspapers to peruse, providing an opportunity to catch up on the latest news or check in on the Phillies.

Now let's talk about the food - it's consistently good at West Ave. Grill. Their fluffy yet crispy-edged pancakes are a definite highlight, ensuring a delicious start to your day. The Kansas City breakfast is another standout choice, typically succeeding in delivering a delectable meal.

However, the big salads could benefit from an increase in the promised ingredients, ensuring that you receive all the components as described on the menu. However, rest assured that they are receptive to feedback and always strive to satisfy their customers. Overall, West Ave. Grill offers a pleasant dining experience that's worth a visit. Give it a try and discover its charm for yourself.

input:
We found ourselves in South Tucson needing a good meal from somewhere other than the kitchens of the chain hotels surrounding the airport.  Thank you Yelpers for delivering another great place!

A reconverted 1960's era A & W chain fast food stand [I can detect those old bone shards still!], we enjoyed a wonderful meal at a reasonable price.

I had the catfish smothered in poblano sauce and melted cheese.  They told me it was farm catfish but it tasted like the catfish I used to catch out of a lake near my house as a little kid.  Farm fish never tastes this real.

My wife had chile relleno - fresh peppers, not surprising this time of year but definite kudos to the chef.

The late-stage adolescents with us enjoyed their enhiladas and chimichangas too.
Revise this with your best effort:
We found ourselves stranded in South Tucson, desperately craving a satisfying meal that didn't come from the generic hotel kitchens near the airport. Thanks to the trusty recommendations from our fellow Yelpers, we stumbled upon a hidden gem.

Nestled within a refurbished 1960's A & W fast food stand, there was a nostalgia-inducing charm about the place that we couldn't resist. As I savored every bite, I couldn't help but notice remnants of the stand's past, the faint bone shards from their fast food days. Nevertheless, we were pleasantly surprised by the delightful feast we encountered, all at an affordable price.

My taste buds were treated to the enchanting flavors of the smothered catfish, drenched in a tantalizing poblano sauce and topped with melted cheese. While they claimed it was farm-raised, it transported me back to my childhood days, when I would reel in catfish from the nearby lake. It had that genuine, authentic taste that farm fish simply cannot replicate.

My wife opted for the chile relleno, and she was met with delightfully fresh peppers. It was a no-brainer during this time of year, but we must commend the chef for their dedication to quality ingredients.

Even the somewhat-picky late-stage adolescents in our group were pleased with their choices. The enchiladas and chimichangas they devoured proved to be winners, much to our relief.

Overall, our visit to this reimagined A & W fast food stand turned hidden culinary oasis surpassed our expectations. We owe our gratitude to the wonderful Yelpers who led us to this delectable destination.

input:

Revise this with your best effort:

To start off our meal, we indulged in the delightful vegetable pakora, a combination of vegetables and hushpuppies that tantalized our taste buds. It was a harmonious blend of flavors, truly a culinary delight.

For our main courses, we each selected a different dish. The chicken tikki masala, lamb roganjosh, and lamb vindaloo were exceptional choices. Each dish was an authentic representation of its respective flavors and surpassed our expectations. The accompanying sauces were so delectable that I was tempted to savor every last drop. Sadly, there was no room left in my stomach to accommodate this desire.

The prices at this establishment were reasonable, offering good value for the quality of the food. However, the staff and service were only satisfactory, leaving room for improvement.

In conclusion, this restaurant is a welcome addition to Media's diverse dining scene. The enticing lunch buffet also caught our attention, with its promising selection of dishes, and at a reasonable price of $9.95 on weekdays and $10.95 on weekends.

input:
Have only been once a couple of months ago, so maybe this was a one-off experience...Ordered a piece of carrot cake, which tasted fine. Certainly not the best I've ever had but good enough. The to go packaging was a bit overkill just for that one slice of cake, as was the $10 price tag. That being said, I'm sure the "fanciness" of the place is what makes it so appealing to folks. It really is quite unique and cute for our area and would be a good place to go with the gals (rather than my husband who hates all things trendy, lol). 

My problem, though, was with the service. We placed our order for the carrot cake with a nice young teenager, and then waited. And waited. I could see the carrot cake just sitting in the pretty covered cake stand, and I felt really tempted to just slice it myself. After a bit (felt like 10 minutes, although I'm sure it was more like 5 or 6), another employee came and sliced the carrot cake, setting the slice on the back counter with the ticket. And then we waited. And waited some more. After about another 5 to 10 minutes, I flagged the teenager down and asked if he could box up the cake for us. He seemed confused, and it took an awkward minute-long exchange for him to understand we hadn't yet received our order. He did apologize for the wait, which I do appreciate, boxed up the cake, and then we were on our way.

I should clarify that we did not go into the shop at a busy time. It was a relatively cool day and not many people were out. While there were maybe 2 to 3 tables seated, we were the only ones at the counter ordering. And while I'm sure the wait staff who repeatedly walked by our lonely piece of carrot cake sitting on the back counter had many important tasks...I just wanted to eat my $10 cake.

Four stars for the cake. Two stars for the service.
Revise this with your best effort:
I visited this place once a couple of months ago, so it's possible that my experience was just a one-time occurrence. I decided to try their carrot cake, which tasted decent. It wasn't the best I've ever had, but it was satisfactory. However, I was quite surprised by the excessive packaging they used for just one slice of cake, especially considering the $10 price tag. Nonetheless, I understand that the appeal of this place lies in its fancy atmosphere. It's truly unique and charming, a perfect spot for a girls' outing (although not ideal for my husband, who dislikes trendy things, lol).

However, the service was where I encountered some issues. We placed our order for the carrot cake with a friendly teenager and then waited...and waited. I could see the cake sitting in the beautifully covered cake stand, and I grew tempted to just slice it myself. Eventually, another staff member came and sliced the cake, placing the slice on the back counter along with our ticket. Yet, we continued to wait. After approximately 5 to 10 more minutes, I had to flag down the teenager and request the cake to be boxed up. He appeared confused, and it took an awkward exchange lasting about a minute for him to realize that we hadn't yet received our order. He did apologize for the wait, which I appreciate, and proceeded to box up the cake for us before we left.

I want to clarify that we visited when it wasn't a busy time. It was a relatively quiet day with very few people around. Despite there being 2 to 3 occupied tables, we were the only ones ordering at the counter. While I understand that the wait staff had other important tasks to attend to, it was frustrating to see my $10 cake sitting there neglected as they repeatedly walked by.

In summary, I would give the cake four stars for its taste, but the service only warrants two stars.

input:
The gym part of City Fitness is better than most, good equipment, clean, variety, it's a nice gym. I find the rates reasonable and have been a member since they opened and will continue to be a member. So, for the rating I give the gym at CF a 3.5 star, I give MBSC a 1.5 star for an overall 2.5 star rating.

MBSC review: I thought I would kick it up a notch so joined the MBSC thrive program at CF on South Street and tried it for three months. Trainers really aren't "personal" trainers. They have a set program that they put people through and you have very little to say about what you like/don't like. The trainers work with several people in a session so depending on how many people are in a session you could be waiting for the trainer to get back to you or waiting for the person in front of you to finish. One of the things that frustrated me is they want you to push through the routine they have come up for you in the hour's time. The sessions are hard with ropes, sleds, balls, bands, cables, weights and the most uncomfortable stationary bike I've ever had to sit on (and they make you end every session on the thing). No two sessions are alike - so if you like variety then great, if you like consistency or at least enough repetition to get the moves and form down then not so great. I seldom found a session to be fun or enjoyable, rather I often felt like I was a contestant on the Biggest Loser. They also play hip-hop all day long and you either like it or you don't. The environment and training is designed (in my opinion) to appeal to 20-30yo demographic.

If you really want to push yourself beyond your limits and don't care how you get there then you might really enjoy the MBSC program. If you want a professional personal trainer to spend quality time with you in achieving your goals and if you want a training program that you actually learn what muscle groups you are working and not just to be pushed through a routine then you probably won't like MBSC. Definitely do a introductory program because the usual 30 day notice from the contract date applies if you cancel and it's $200+/mo program.
Revise this with your best effort:
The gym section at City Fitness sets itself apart from most others with its excellent equipment, cleanliness, and variety. It is undeniably a great gym to be a member of, and I have personally found their rates to be reasonable. I have been a proud member of City Fitness since they first opened their doors, and I have no plans to leave. Given my overall experience, I would currently rate the gym at City Fitness a solid 3.5 stars.

Now, let's shift our focus to MBSC, a program I decided to give a try at the CF location on South Street. Unfortunately, I was left somewhat disappointed. The trainers at MBSC aren't exactly what I would consider "personal" trainers. They follow a set program with little room for input from the participants. During sessions, trainers work with multiple people at once, which can result in waiting time for assistance or equipment. One aspect that particularly frustrated me was the push to complete their predetermined routine within the hour. The sessions were physically demanding, incorporating exercises with ropes, sleds, balls, bands, cables, weights, and a particularly uncomfortable stationary bike that they insist on ending each session with. Although the variety in sessions could be seen as a positive by some, I personally found it challenging to achieve consistency and master proper form. The experience often felt more like participating in a competitive reality show than an enjoyable workout. Additionally, they exclusively play hip-hop music, which may or may not be to everyone's taste. Overall, the environment and training at MBSC seem to cater predominantly to individuals in the 20-30 age range.

If you thrive on pushing your boundaries and don't mind the manner in which you achieve your fitness goals, the MBSC program may be perfect for you. However, if you prefer a personal trainer who dedicates quality time to helping you reach your objectives and a training program that educates you on the specific muscle groups being targeted, MBSC may not be the best fit. I highly recommend trying their introductory program before committing, as canceling requires a 30-day notice from the contract start date and the program can cost over $200 per month.

input:
Four stars for price. 
I drive truck, so I've eaten bbq all over America. This place is better than most, but it's certainly not 4 star worthy. I'd say the food is more like 2.5 star. 
The cheeseburger was quite large and the meat was tasty. (Be advised: if you don't stop them they'll automatically put that disgusting invention called mayonnaise on it.) I got it plain so I can't comment on their lettuce/tomato game. 
The pork bbq sammich was soggy on the bottom. Moist is good, but this was just plain wet. The meat itself was bland but not bad. 
The bbq sauce is pretty good but not great. 
The Mac & Cheese tasted ok but the noodles were way overcooked. It'd be much better if it were baked and had a little crustiness to it. 

If I lived local I'm sure I'd come here occasionally.
Revise this with your best effort:
I have had the opportunity to try BBQ from various places across America due to my profession as a truck driver. While this establishment is better than most, I personally believe it falls short of deserving a four-star rating. In my opinion, the food here is more accurately equivalent to a 2.5-star experience.

One aspect worth noting is the commendable size of their cheeseburger, and the flavorful meat it contains. However, it is important to mention that they automatically include mayonnaise on the burger unless requested otherwise, which I find to be quite repulsive. I opted for a plain burger, so I cannot provide feedback on their lettuce and tomato toppings.

On the other hand, the pork BBQ sandwich was disappointingly soggy, surpassing the desirable level of moisture and becoming excessively wet. The meat itself lacked significant taste, although it was not necessarily unpleasant.

The BBQ sauce served here is decent, but I would not classify it as exceptional.

The Mac & Cheese had an acceptable flavor, but the noodles were severely overcooked. It would greatly benefit from being baked, yielding a desirable crustiness.

If I were a local resident, I imagine I would visit this establishment occasionally.

input:
So we've been wanting to try the sushiritos since they opened up a location closer to us and we finally tried it last Friday. 

I got the slammin' salmon and my wife got the crunch. I'd say they both definitely had fresh ingredients, and definitely tasted fresh, but I think the balance of flavors wasn't quite right for the slammin' salmon. Way too heavy on the sauce, completely overpowering the crisp fresh veggies and salmon. 

We tried the Japanese fried chicken. Sauce is a little sweet and sour. And the chicken was a little dry. 

We also tried their green tea and lemonade, which were pretty good, but you don't come to a place like this because their green tea and lemonade are their best things on the menu. 

Overall, you pay a high premium for a gimmicky meal. With this location being essentially at a revolving door of new customers on the corner of Penn's campus, I think they have the potential to do well. But I don't think I'll be coming back. We'll take our $34 elsewhere.
Revise this with your best effort:
We had been eager to try the sushiritos ever since a new location opened up closer to us. Last Friday, we finally got the chance to give it a go.

I opted for the slammin' salmon, while my wife went for the crunch. Both rolls undeniably boasted fresh ingredients and had a distinct freshness in their taste. However, I must say the balance of flavors in the slammin' salmon was slightly off. The sauce overwhelmed the crisp, fresh veggies and salmon, leaving an overpowering sensation.

In addition to the rolls, we also sampled the Japanese fried chicken. The sauce had a subtle sweet and sour tang, but unfortunately, the chicken itself was a tad dry.

We also decided to try their green tea and lemonade, which were tasty enough. Nevertheless, one doesn't visit this place for their green tea and lemonade alone; there are better highlights on the menu.

All in all, the sushiritos come at a steep price for what feels like a gimmicky meal. Considering the constant stream of new customers at this location, situated on the corner of Penn's campus, there is potential for success. However, I personally don't foresee myself returning. We'll be taking our $34 elsewhere.

The room itself was spacious and comfortable, which was a definite plus. Unfortunately, I made the mistake of selecting room 263, thinking it would be ideal as it didn't face Conti Street. However, it turned out to be closer to the vending and ice machines, and I could clearly hear conversations in the hallway next to the vending area due to the thin walls. Apart from this drawback, I would have given the hotel a solid 4-star rating.

input: Went to ocharleys on a Sunday afternoon, it wasn't too busy but I guess our server was overwhelmed. He forgot our bread and butter. Forgot my fries multiple times, I was halfway done with my sandwich when my fries finally arrived. We got my son Sprite refilled at the bar after waiting so long for our waiter. We had a coupon that we told the server to add to our bill. Well he forgot to ring it up correctly, he got the manager to fix it. I might give ocharleys another try for lunch instead of dinner.
Revise this with your best effort: On a leisurely Sunday afternoon, my companions and I decided to dine at O'Charley's. Despite the relatively light crowd, it seemed our server was under significant pressure. Regrettably, he overlooked providing us with the customary bread and butter, causing a small disappointment. What followed only heightened this sentiment as my fries were forgotten on multiple occasions. In fact, I was nearly halfway through my sandwich by the time they finally arrived. The service was further delayed when we requested a refill for my son's Sprite, having to resort to the bar as our server was occupied elsewhere. As we handed our server a coupon to apply to our bill, it was disheartening to discover that he had neglected to ring it up correctly. Fortunately, after involving the manager, the issue was resolved promptly. Despite these unfortunate mishaps, I am willing to give O'Charley's another chance, perhaps during lunch service rather than dinner.

input: this place SUCKS. Terrible service and overpriced mediocre food. This is my second time with the same results. I gave them the benefit of the doubt -perhaps having an off night the first time I went, but it was the exact same the second time around. Nothing innovative. They churn tables out and could care less that you are spending upwards of $150 for two. Save this one for the tourists.
Revise this with your best effort: This establishment is highly disappointing. The service is abysmal and the food is mediocre despite being overpriced. Unfortunately, this is not my first encounter with such subpar experiences. I initially thought that my first visit might have been a fluke, but my second visit presented the same exact issues. There is a severe lack of innovation in their offerings and it appears that their primary concern is speedily rotating tables without any regards for the fact that patrons spend a significant amount, sometimes even upwards of $150 for two. I would recommend avoiding this place unless you happen to be a tourist.

input: Is there a 12-step program to help manage a Reanimator Coffee problem? If so please share.

input:
They just opened today and WOW! Aren't we lucky to now have 2 meaderies within a mile or two of each other. 
Mead is a type of fermented honey beverage. The ABV (alcohol percent) is generally 10-14% so more along the lines of wine than beer there. 

We tried Goober Vitis (peanut butter and jelly), Suzy's Cherry Pie, and the coffee one. All were PERFECT. Flavors are pure, beautiful nose, all around great. 

The space is very nice, nice big tables that seat 6-8 easily, an L-shaped bar, a stand-up bar around the tanks, then there are picnic tables outside.
Revise this with your best effort:
Today they have opened their doors and it is truly remarkable! How fortunate are we to now have not one, but two meaderies within such close proximity. Mead, a delightful fermented honey beverage, boasts an ABV (alcohol percentage) ranging from 10-14%, making it more comparable to wine than beer.

We had the pleasure of sampling Goober Vitis, a captivating blend of peanut butter and jelly, Suzy's Cherry Pie, and a delightful coffee-infused mead. Let me tell you, each one surpassed all expectations. The flavors were pure and the aromas were simply beautiful. Overall, a truly exceptional experience.

Moreover, the space itself is absolutely stunning. The large tables easily accommodate groups of 6-8, while an L-shaped bar and a stand-up bar surrounding the tanks add to the vibrant atmosphere. If that isn't inviting enough, there are also picnic tables available outside for a charming outdoor experience.

input: I eat at Pina's or take-out about once a month. My favorites includes their dinner specials, cheesesteaks, calzones, and seafood dishes. The shrimp scampi appetizer (sans linguini) and steamed clams are excellent  inexpensive. Service is always flawless. For casual dining this place is very good.
Revise this with your best effort: I typically dine at Pina's or order take-out approximately once a month. The menu boasts a variety of delectable options, but my personal favorites consist of their mouth-watering dinner specials, tantalizing cheesesteaks, delightful calzones, and delectable seafood dishes. Notably, the shrimp scampi appetizer (without linguini) and the steamed clams are highly recommended for their excellent quality without breaking the bank. Additionally, the service at Pina's is consistently flawless, ensuring a delightful dining experience. When it comes to casual dining, this establishment truly stands out as a top-notch choice.

input: Great place to watch footy.  I was visiting town for work and needed a place to watch my blues take on barfalona and came across Chatham.  It was a Tuesday so they had $4 Guiness and Black and Tans. Had their fish and chips which was new experience for me. Never had fish that was so soft after being fried, but I really enjoyed it, almost the texture of a donut. Saw my team win and had a great time at this pub.
Revise this with your best effort: Chatham turned out to be the perfect spot for me to catch the footy action during my work trip. As I was eager to witness my beloved blues battling against barfalona, I stumbled upon this gem of a place. To my luck, it was a Tuesday, and their offer of $4 Guinness and Black and Tans had me sold. I decided to dive into their fish and chips, which proved to be quite the novelty for me. I was pleasantly surprised by the tender texture of the fish, even after it was fried - it almost reminded me of a donut. Not only did I get to savor this delightful dish, but I also witnessed my team emerge victorious, making the experience even better. Overall, my visit to this pub was nothing short of fantastic.

input: This is the place we have been searching for! We drive almost an hour to get here but it is so worth it! I have had 2 different people who both did exactly what I wanted and are extremely talented! Thank you Pamela and Steven! Revise this with your best effort: This is absolutely the place we have been desperately searching for! After trying out numerous nail salons in Tampa with disappointing results, we stumbled upon this gem on Instagram, and we can confidently say that we will never go anywhere else again! input:
I can't say enough about Belinda and Jerry! They were so helpful and kind. I am a travel nurse and was leaving my car in Boise for the winter. I came in on a snowy December evening and Balinda reassured me that she would stay and wait for me and Jerry even drove me to my storage shed and helped me with my luggage.
I am so happy with storage experiemce here and with the service I received. I highly recommend!!

input: This is our go-to takeout place. It has great food and exceptionally fast service. I live at 2601 Parkway and they deliver right to the door of my condo which many delivery places don't do. Their staff is friendly, make great pizza, and generally run such a business as best you can.
Revise this with your best effort: This is definitely our top choice for takeout. Not only does this place serve delicious food, but their service is impressively prompt. input: Top notch street tacos, great service and hand made horchata made this a top notch stop

input:
I went in for a mani and pedi. My student was a nice person and we chatted. However it took 3 hours and my hands just look terrible. The feet are fine and feel great. Hands, just terrible. No one came and checked in if the work was done properly. I'm fine that it takes longer, they are there to learn. However, I shouldn't have been charged for the manicure (pedicure yes) or at least have someone else redo my nails. See the pictures for yourselves, this is 15 minutes out!

Edit: just wanted to add that when I removed my shoes, my pedi was ruined. I asked if it was ready to put shoes on and I was told yes. 2 stars only because at least my student was nice but 0 for the service (34$!)
Revise this with your best effort:
I went in for a manicure and pedicure, hoping for a relaxing experience. My student, who provided the services, was genuinely nice and we had a pleasant conversation. However, the whole process ended up taking a staggering three hours, and to my disappointment, my hands did not turn out as expected - they looked terrible. On the other hand, the pedicure was satisfactory, leaving my feet feeling great. Unfortunately, no one bothered to check in and ensure that the work was done properly. While I understand that students need time to learn, I believe I should not have been charged for the subpar manicure, or at the very least, there should have been an opportunity for someone else to fix my nails. I urge you to take a look at the attached pictures; these were taken just 15 minutes after leaving the salon.

Additionally, I want to emphasize that when I took off my shoes after the session, I was disheartened to discover that my pedicure had already been ruined. I specifically asked if it was safe to put my shoes back on, and I was assured that it was. Given these circumstances, I can only grant two stars for the pleasant demeanor of my student, but a zero rating for the entire service, especially considering the hefty price of $34.

input: Very nice, quiet and dark restaurant. Chinese and sushi offered. Had szechuan chicken, hot and sour soup, and steamed rice. Hubbie had the prime rib and shrimp hot pot. Just the right amount of food. Didn't have to take any home. Service was excellent.
Revise this with your best effort:
We had the pleasure of dining at a charming and intimate restaurant that exuded a lovely ambiance with its dimly lit and tranquil atmosphere. The establishment served a delectable fusion of Chinese cuisine and sushi. For our appetizers, we savored the tantalizing flavors of the Szechuan chicken alongside a contrasting yet equally satisfying hot and sour soup. Complementing our meal, we indulged in a serving of perfectly steamed rice.

My companion opted for the delightful prime rib and shrimp hot pot, which proved to be a true delight for the senses. The portion sizes were just right, allowing us to relish every morsel without feeling overwhelmed. We were pleasantly surprised that there was no need to take any leftovers home.

Furthermore, the service we experienced throughout our dining experience was nothing short of excellent. The attentive staff went above and beyond to ensure our every need was met, enhancing our overall enjoyment of the meal.

input: Frank is a great dentist and a very nice guy. He has a gentle manner, takes a sincere interest in his patients and in general is a top quality dentist and person. If you are in the market for a dentist he is an excellent choice. I've gone to him for years and know many others who have as well.
Revise this with your best effort: Frank is an exceptional dentist and a genuinely kind-hearted individual. Admirably, he possesses a gentle demeanor that immediately puts his patients at ease. His remarkable commitment to his patients is evident through his sincere interest in their well-being. Undoubtedly, Frank is an exceptional dentist and an outstanding individual. When searching for a dentist, choosing him is an excellent decision. Personally, I have been a loyal patient of Frank's for numerous years, and I am not alone in my admiration for him. Many others, too, have had the privilege of experiencing his exceptional care.

input: This was a nice spot with sidewalk lounge seating. Even had a DJ outside Friday night. There was a walk up bar outside too. The decor inside was pretty sweet. We tried a few appetizers and they were both good! It is located in a trendy waterfront area.

input:
Our office went today for Friday's happy hour special.  Such a great deal, and it wasn't packed.  Didn't expect it, but the food and drinks on their specials-amazing! input: Stopped in tonight for a light bite to eat. I was so impressed! Great service, great fresh, fresh food and beautiful atmosphere- we sat outside in the warm October evening air.  Lisa was a great host, explaining the menu and checked in with us frequently - we ended up chatting with her quite a bit and that only made the whole evening more enjoyable. What a wonderful place- we will certainly be back for more!
Revise this with your best effort: Tonight, I decided to grab a quick bite to eat and ended up being incredibly impressed. The service was outstanding, and the food was absolutely fresh and delicious. The ambiance was simply beautiful, especially as we chose to sit outside and soak in the pleasant October evening air. Lisa, our host, did an exceptional job by not only explaining the menu but also continuously checking in on us. We ended up engaging in delightful conversations with her, which significantly enhanced our overall dining experience. This place truly exceeded our expectations, and it's safe to say that we will definitely be returning for more enjoyable evenings like this one.

input: I've been to Lush in Arizona, S.F., San Jose and Maui. The one in New Orleans is My favorite one. I love how you can smell a Lush store from a block away. :) I've been to this one a few times, Always on Halloween. Always a fun time :)
Revise this with your best effort: I have had the pleasure of visiting Lush stores in various locations including Arizona, San Francisco, San Jose, and Maui. However, my absolute favorite Lush store is the one in New Orleans. What sets it apart for me is the distinctive scent that wafts through the air, making it easily identifiable even from a block away. Every time I have visited, it has been exclusively during Halloween, which adds to the thrill and excitement. Without a doubt, each visit to the New Orleans Lush store has been a delightful and enjoyable experience.

input: Love love love this place for HH n dinner is good too! Its ok for brunch, not as great as what people praise it to be. The Asian Nachos are the dish to get for HH. Its an entree itself! The other HH dishes are great too. The creme brulee is amazing as with their other desserts. The blueberry mojito is awesome along with the mango sling. Great place to celebrate birthdays and such.  Nice feel to it. Bar area gets crowded as it gets later for HH. As usual around the mall, finding parking sux!
Revise this with your best effort: I absolutely adore this place for Happy Hour, and their dinner options are equally fantastic! While I find their brunch to be good, it doesn't quite live up to the high praise it receives. However, I highly recommend the Asian Nachos for Happy Hour – they're practically an entire entree on their own! The other Happy Hour dishes are also exceptional, and their desserts, especially the creme brulee, are absolutely amazing. The blueberry mojito and mango sling are both delicious drink choices. This is a wonderful spot to celebrate birthdays and special occasions, and it has a charming atmosphere. Just be aware that the bar area can get quite crowded as the night progresses during Happy Hour. Unfortunately, like most places near the mall, finding parking can be a hassle.

input: Delicious top shelf pastries. I am outraged at the poor ratings. If you're looking for cheapness over flavor then go to Panera. Service has always been exceedingly pleasent when I go, and I am an obnoxious needy customer. We are so excited to have them make macaroons for our wedding.
Revise this with your best effort: Indulge in our delectable, high-quality pastries that are truly a cut above the rest. However, it deeply disappoints me to see the low ratings they have received. If you prioritize affordability over exquisite flavor, Panera might be a more suitable choice for you. On the contrary, whenever I have visited, I have consistently experienced exceptional service, even as a demanding and somewhat difficult customer. We are eagerly anticipating the pleasure of having them create magnificent macaroons for our upcoming wedding celebration.

input: I could be craving pizza and be walking by and STILL not go in again. I will say the ingredients are definitely fresh and service was great however the pizza is just plain not good. The crust is so thin that the pizza is cold within a few minutes and it was just a little floppy and bland. I wanted to love this place but with so many other pizzerias in the area I won't be going back.
Revise this with your best effort: Even if I find myself craving pizza and happen to pass by this place, I still wouldn't go in again. Although I must admit that the ingredients are undeniably fresh and the service was exceptional, the pizza itself is disappointingly subpar. Its thin crust quickly loses warmth, turning the entire pizza cold within minutes, and its texture is somewhat limp and lacking in flavor. Despite my initial hopes of adoring this establishment, the abundance of other pizzerias in the vicinity makes it clear that I won't be returning.

input: Love the tap room, but I can't seem to get the hours of business right.  My first visit was a kinda a let down.  I had heard that bier was the place to go for great beers in Indianapolis, but I only found 2 that I liked and only 1 was memorable.  However, bier rotates their taps weekly and does not seem to have any regular taps, I like this because it means that they are constantly challenging themselves to create a better beer.   The tap room is a lot of fun too with people constantly revolving around the taps to taste and find their favorite for the week and then relaxing and talking in the lounge area.  I only gave them 3stars this time but I look forward to improving their score after future visits.
Revise this with your best effort:
I have a mixed opinion about the tap room. On my first visit, I was disappointed because I couldn't seem to get the business hours right. However, I had heard that bier was the go-to place for great beers in Indianapolis. Although I only found two beers that I enjoyed, with only one being memorable, I appreciate that bier rotates their taps weekly and doesn't have any regular ones. This shows their commitment to constantly challenging themselves and creating better beers.

The tap room itself is quite enjoyable, with a lively atmosphere of people constantly gathering around the taps to taste and discover their favorite brew of the week. It's a great place to relax and engage in conversations in the lounge area. While I can only give them three stars for now, I'm optimistic about future visits and improving their rating.

input: Beautifully sweet ending to a sweet trip to NOLA with the girls. We stumbled upon this after a delicous savory lunch nearby at Cochon (review to follow). Sweet Confections is on Magazine St, around corner from the art gallery strip on Julia St.   We had a sampling of cupcake (chocolate with mocha filling) and truffles (raspberry, creme brulee, and orange).  Cupcake was good, mocha filling best part. Rasberry truffle was my fav, love the dark chocolate so it's not cloyingly sweet. The coffee was a wonderful chaser, not overly burnt, smoky, or acidic... I usually have coffee with milk n sugar, forgot this time, but I didn't even need it!  Seating was nice, with a few cafe tables inside. Enough for our 6-girl troop. And service was great, helpful with flavor suggestions and labelling.  Gave 4 of 5 stars because maybe they could benefit from one more equally gracious staff person.
Revise this with your best effort:
We had a beautifully sweet ending to our trip to NOLA with the girls at Sweet Confections. After enjoying a delicious savory lunch at Cochon nearby (review to follow), we stumbled upon this delightful bakery on Magazine St, just around the corner from the art gallery strip on Julia St.

At Sweet Confections, we treated ourselves to a mouthwatering selection of cupcakes and truffles. The chocolate cupcake with mocha filling was good, but the mocha filling was the absolute highlight. Among the truffles, my favorite was the raspberry, as I loved the rich dark chocolate that balanced out the sweetness perfectly. The creme brulee and orange truffles were also a treat for the taste buds.

To accompany our delectable treats, we enjoyed a wonderful cup of coffee. Surprisingly, it was not overly burnt, smoky, or acidic, and I usually add milk and sugar to my coffee. However, this time I completely forgot, but to my surprise, it didn't even need it!

The seating at Sweet Confections was cozy, with a few cafe tables inside. It comfortably accommodated our group of six girls. The service was also excellent, with the staff offering helpful flavor suggestions and labeling everything clearly.

Overall, I would give Sweet Confections 4 out of 5 stars. The only suggestion I have is that they could benefit from adding one more equally gracious staff member to enhance the customer experience.

input: Pulled pork sandwich was Delicious .. BUT! The lucky bun (Asian fusion style ) burger . Was a disappointment for the sole purpose of them using a frozen beef patty :/  the bread was good .. The toppings and sauces were great .. But just killed the flavors with a processed frozen beef patty .. If used a fresh ground meat .. It would have been a great gourmet burger ..
Revise this with your best effort: The pulled pork sandwich was savored and deemed delicious. However, the lucky bun burger, which boasted an enticing Asian fusion flair, fell short of expectations due to the unfortunate use of a frozen beef patty. While the bread was commendable and the toppings and sauces were delightful, the infusion of flavor was hindered by the inclusion of a processed, frozen beef patty. With the substitution of a freshly ground meat, the potential for a truly superb gourmet burger would have been realized.

input: This is a great place to bring the kids to. They can have juice, a slice of cake, and homemade popsicles. They think it is a tea party. input: Always awesome!  Best crust ever and super Fresh ingredients and nice staff.  Lots of yummy toppings that aren't offered at other pizza places.   Great salads too! Patio area is a cool place to kick back,have a beer or glass of wine and savor the best pizza in town.

input:

input: I Recently vacationed in St. Petersburg with my family. Dooners was definitely my favorite meal of the trip. Great food and incredibly helpful and friendly staff. Would definitely recommend to anyone, and wouldn't hesitate to go again.
Revise this with your best effort: During our recent family vacation in St. Petersburg, I had the pleasure of dining at Dooners, which undoubtedly became the highlight of our trip. I wholeheartedly recommend Dooners to anyone interested in indulging in a memorable and satisfying dining experience, and I personally am eager to return without any hesitation.

input:
Very cool bar attached to the Alexander Hotel. Several vintage cocktails from pre-prohibition are on the menu. None cooler than "The Elephant in the Room" a bourbon cocktail which comes in its own decanter filled with cherrywood smoke. You decide how long to let it infuse. Lots of comfortable seating and when it warms up a touch a large beautiful deck with seating and heating overlooks the street life. As an added bonus you can relax and watch people work out through the glass of the new CityWay YMCA. 
And yes the truffle oil and sea salt popcorn that greets every patron is as good as it sounds. Get a beer and start collecting bags, once you start you can't stop.
Revise this with your best effort:
Experience the epitome of sophistication at the elegant bar nestled within the Alexander Hotel. This extraordinary establishment boasts an impressive selection of vintage cocktails harking back to the pre-prohibition era. Among them, none shine brighter than the exceptional "The Elephant in the Room" - a tantalizing bourbon concoction presented in a decanter teeming with fragrant cherrywood smoke. The choice is yours to determine the optimal duration for the infusion, ensuring a personalized experience like no other.

Comfort abounds within this extraordinary establishment, with an abundance of plush seating options. As the temperature rises, venture onto the expansive and picturesque deck, complete with ample seating and heating facilities, offering a captivating vantage point overlooking the vibrant street life below. Moreover, an added allure awaits as you unwind and observe individuals engaging in invigorating workouts within the state-of-the-art CityWay YMCA through the impressive glass walls.

To further tantalize your taste buds, delight in the delectable truffle oil and sea salt popcorn that warmly welcomes each guest. Prepare to be mesmerized as you savor this savory treat, for its divine flavor lives up to the utmost expectations. Take the opportunity to pair this delectable popcorn with a refreshing beer of your choice, while simultaneously indulging in the irresistible habit of collecting the accompanying bags. Beware, once you start, the allure of these delicacies is insurmountable, leaving you yearning for more.

input:
This hotel is a gem in the heart of Philadelphia.

It's a cozy, quaint, and charming property. The rooms are spacious, modern and gorgeous. 
The decor is chic and attractive: big wooden desk, hardwood floors, couches and throw pillows: Looks more like a friend's apartment than a hotel. 

Free breakfast is always a plus for those of us with limited time. It's not a hot breakfast (I've had so many mass-produced bad ones, so I'm not complaining) but greek yogurt, a huge croissant, an orange and some cranberry juice hits the spot! They leave it at your door though, instead of ringing your bell to wake you. So if you ask for it to be delivered at 7 a.m., check outside your door; by 7:01 it WILL be there. 

Coffee, a variety of teas, cold and hot water, as well as ice and a bowl of assorted fruit are available 24/7 in the lobby. There are doorbells for each room, and the hotel can only be accessed after hours if you have a key card. Floors are acessible with a keycard as well, for extra protection. The staff is very polite: one of the few places in Philly where someone will actually say "good morning" to you (No, seriously. I lived there for 5 years, so trust me on that). They're also extremely helpful. When I checked in the night before, the gentleman at the reservation desk called to make sure I had a cab waiting for me at 8:15 the next morning so that I could make my speaking engagement on time. While I was getting my clothes ready, my iron was making more wrinkles than it was taking out, so I asked them for a new one and within 30 seconds, I had a brand new model with all the bells and whistles.

I've read a few reviews talking about the noise level of this place. My room was closest to the reception desk and I never heard a peep. There were people out and about, but I didn't hear a thing. And I'm a very light sleeper...

A few things to note:
Its location on a tight, one way street can cause a little difficulty if you're traveling solo, but if you have one person to unload the car while someone else parks, you should be fine. The parking garage they use is about half a block from the hotel, but you have to drive in a big rectangle to get there. 

There's a stand-up shower instead of the traditional bathtub/shower combo. It fits one comfortably enough... provided that you're not too far from average height and build. (My boyfriend is 6'2 with a football player build and he made out okay.)

Don't expect much of a view. The view from our room was of the side of another building. But that's what the city is for... go out there and see something!

Overall, this was an excellent trip and a great find. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone.
Revise this with your best effort:
This hotel is a true gem nestled in the heart of Philadelphia. It exudes a cozy, quaint, and charming atmosphere that immediately makes you feel at home. The rooms are not only spacious but also boast a modern and stunning design. The chic and attractive decor, featuring a large wooden desk, hardwood floors, plush couches, and delightful throw pillows, gives off more of a warm and inviting ambiance found in a friend's apartment rather than a typical hotel.

The best part is that they will discreetly leave the breakfast outside your door, ensuring that you can savor it at your own convenience without any interruptions.

The lobby is a true haven for 24/7 refreshments. You can enjoy a variety of coffee and teas, both hot and cold water, along with ice and a delightful bowl of assorted fruit. Additionally, the hotel ensures top-notch security with keycard access required to enter after hours. The individual doorbells for each room add an extra layer of security and convenience. Only those with a keycard can access the floors, providing peace of mind for guests throughout their stay. The staff at this hotel is exceptional, exuding politeness and warmth. It's a rare treat to find a place in Philly where you're genuinely greeted with a "good morning". Trust me, I lived here for five years.

The level of assistance provided by the staff is commendable. On the night of my check-in, the gentleman at the reservation desk kindly arranged for a cab to be waiting for me at 8:15 a.m. the next morning, ensuring that I made it to my speaking engagement on time. When my iron was failing to perform its duty, they swiftly provided me a brand new model with all the latest features within seconds. Their attentiveness and efficiency truly make a difference.

Regarding the noise level, I was fortunate to have a room closest to the reception desk, and I can confidently say that I never heard a single sound. Despite there being other guests around, the tranquility of the room was impeccable. As someone who is typically a light sleeper, this was a remarkable experience.

A few things to keep in mind are the hotel's location on a tight, one-way street, which may pose a slight challenge if you're traveling alone. However, with someone to help unload the car while the other parks, this shouldn't be a major issue. The parking garage used by the hotel is conveniently located just half a block away, but you may need to navigate a slightly convoluted route to reach it.

Another notable detail is the presence of a stand-up shower instead of the traditional bathtub/shower combination. While it comfortably accommodates one person, it may be a tad snug for individuals who are significantly taller or larger in build. input:

I got the oxtail soup (Sancocho) with extra rice and plantains to see how it would differ from the Korean-style stuff I was used to at home. Aside from a thicker, stew-like broth and beefier potatoes, it was just as delicious. My friend got a flat steak (Carne Asada) that I think he ate in just under 10 seconds. 

Remember Yelp, you're missing out on a lot if you don't visit NE philly once in a while, especially this place.

input:
One of my most favorite Indian restaurants. Nothing fancy but absolutely delicious meals.

Never an issue being seated promptly. A casual dining experience awaits. Service is pleasant. Ambience a bit blahh but still enjoyable.

Now onto the real reason to come here... the FOOD:
Naan is soft. Garlic is tasty but I usually like the original best.  Regardless of your entree of choice, you really cannot go wrong. And although it does not appeal to my level of spiciness preferred (I like it HOT HOT HOT), it has great flavor and is great for the average spicey food eater. My recommendations are the Masala or Vindaloo (Chicken, Shrimp, Lamb... option is yours). Room for dessert? Order the Rice Pudding  and Gulab Jaman, mix together and enjoy the creamy sugary treat.
Revise this with your best effort:
One of my absolute favorite Indian restaurants, this place may not have any frills but it certainly delivers in terms of deliciousness.

Seating is always prompt and the dining experience is casual and relaxed. The service is pleasant, though the ambiance may lack a bit of excitement, it is still enjoyable nonetheless.

But let's get to the real star of the show here... the FOOD:
The naan is delightfully soft and the garlic variation certainly brings some tasty flavor, although I personally tend to prefer the original one. Regardless of your choice of entree, you simply cannot go wrong. While it may not meet my intense preferences for spiciness (I like it really HOT), the dishes here are bursting with amazing flavors and are perfect for those who enjoy a more moderate level of spice. I highly recommend trying the Masala or Vindaloo options, whether you prefer chicken, shrimp, or lamb, the decision is yours.

And if you still have room for dessert, the Rice Pudding and Gulab Jamun are an absolute must-try. Mix them together to create a creamy and sweet treat that will leave you completely satisfied.

input:

You are reviewing the god damn stadium, not that your a Philly fan, and OMG your team won the world series in 08. 

-The food sucks, they do not have enough vendors, So if your enjoying the game, you pretty much have to get up to buy yourself a pretzel or soda. 
-Point out the worst food, the "Hoagies" or whatever are Terrible. Aren't they suppose to be like really good (Believe I'm in Philly). The french fries are mad greasy and no crunch or anything. They were soggy, greasy fries!!!! 
- They have cheap small TVs, that are blurry as hell, so there goes the idea of watching the game while your on line waiting for your food. 
- I would love to understand how the game has just started (3rd inning), and I find empty beer containers everywhere.. 

This is not part of my judgement, but for other people to be aware and be careful 
Philly fans are the RUDEST and NASTIEST people. They are very drunk people, they get in your face, they will spill things on you. Even if your a girl, they have no respect. 

This stadium SUCKS, visit it, knock it off your list, see cheap home runs, since the stadium is built for hitters... 
but we advised...Bring your own food and beware of Philly fans. 
PS: There still are nasty even if you aren't a mets fan...they are just rude people.
Revise this with your best effort:
To the other reviewers,

Please focus your review on the stadium itself rather than emphasizing your personal affiliation with a particular team. Additionally, let's strive for a more professional and objective tone. Here are the revised points:

- The food options at the stadium are limited and there aren't enough vendors available. This can be inconvenient for fans who would like to enjoy the game without having to leave their seats to purchase snacks like pretzels or sodas.
- The quality of the "Hoagies" or sandwiches offered at the stadium falls short. They don't meet the expectations of being delicious, especially considering Philadelphia's reputation for great food. Additionally, the french fries are excessively greasy and lack the desired crunch, making them quite disappointing.
- The TVs provided in the stadium are of poor quality, with blurry screens that make it difficult to enjoy a clear view of the game while waiting in line for food.
- It is disheartening to find empty beer containers scattered around the stadium despite the game being in its early stages (3rd inning), which suggests inadequate cleaning and maintenance.

While this is not a direct critique of the stadium, it's important to note that some Philly fans can exhibit rude and disrespectful behavior. They may be intoxicated, get too close to others, and even accidentally spill things on fellow spectators without showing appropriate respect, regardless of gender or team affiliation.

Considering the stadium's design, it tends to favor home runs due to its dimensions, which may be exciting to some visitors. However, I would advise bringing your own food to ensure a satisfying dining experience and being cautious of the behavior of some Philly fans.

Please remember to maintain a respectful and unbiased tone when reviewing the stadium.

input:
This place is absolutely amazing. A cute little bakery and the employees are super attentive. I walked in and was bouncing around from one dessert to another deciding if I should make a purchase. The employee offered me a sample of the banana puddings - definitely try some! And you know how sometimes when they give you so small of a sample to taste, you can't really make a proper judgment because there isn't enough to judge from? Not the case here!

I got the salted caramel banana, the strawberry banana pudding and the upside pineapple cake.

Thoughts: OMG!! I never crave banana pudding and never really thought anything of the dessert. But man after this, I wanted to go home and make my own banana pudding (Although I highly doubt that I could make it half as good)! Their desserts are crafted perfect - three/four layers depending on what you get. The bottom layer the the pudding, second layer is the nilla wafers or they might even use some sort of pound cake(whatever it was - it was AMAZING), third layer, the strawberry and then the top layer is pudding with a nice whipped creme and topping. The creme has so much flavor and the texture is so smooth. Everything just comes together so nicely! 

The upside pineapple cake was BOMB. the cake wasn't too fluffy but was dense to the perfect amount to Taste like what it's suppose to. The pineapple flavor isn't overwhelming but just right. My only problem was that the pineapple bottom got a little too carameliZed with brown sugar and was a bit hard to chew.

Definitely go to this place! I was so sad that there was no option to leave them a tip. (They use an iPad to ring you up). The service/help was so great and I would have left a tip but I had no cash. Any ways, highly recommend this place for desserts!!
Revise this with your best effort:
I was absolutely blown away by this incredible place. It's a delightful little bakery with exceptionally attentive employees. As soon as I stepped inside, I found myself irresistibly drawn from one delectable dessert to another, struggling to decide which one to indulge in. The kind employee kindly offered me a sample of their divine banana puddings, and I can confidently say that you must give them a try! Unlike other places where the sample size is too small to make an accurate judgment, that was not the case here.

I ended up choosing the salted caramel banana, the strawberry banana pudding, and the upside pineapple cake. Let me tell you, OMG!! I usually never crave banana pudding and usually don't think much of it, but after tasting this, I was tempted to rush home and attempt to recreate it myself (although I highly doubt that mine wouldn't be even half as good as theirs!). Their desserts are masterfully crafted, boasting three or four layers, depending on your selection. The first layer is velvety smooth pudding, followed by nilla wafers or some type of pound cake that simply wowed my taste buds. The third layer features the delightful surprise of juicy strawberries, and the top layer is an indulgent combination of more pudding, heavenly whipped cream, and a delightful topping. The cream has an explosion of flavor, and the texture is incredibly velvety. Every element seamlessly comes together to create a heavenly treat.

Now, let's talk about the upside pineapple cake. It was pure bliss! The cake had the perfect density, not overly fluffy but just right, accurately capturing the true essence of the cake. The pineapple flavor was expertly balanced, not too overpowering but just enough to satisfy my taste buds. My only qualm was that the pineapple bottom had become a bit overly caramelized with brown sugar, making it a tad challenging to chew.

I must insist that you pay a visit to this place! I was truly disappointed when I realized there was no option to leave a tip (as they use an iPad for transactions). The level of service and assistance I received was exceptional, deserving of a generous tip, but unfortunately, I had no cash on me. Regardless, I wholeheartedly recommend this place for anyone with a sweet tooth looking for an unforgettable dessert experience.
