input:
oh Millers, how i wanted to like you.  You are close to my house, have ample parking, and large spacious tables.  you even have a fireplace in the back for a little ambiance. 

friends and i tried to come here 2 or 3 times for a quick/inexpensive* bite to eat and every time there was a 30-60 minute wait. we thought this must mean they are really good.  perhaps it just means that people in Springfield are willing to settle for a less than average dining experience.  *side note- this place is not inexpensive. 

hubby and i ordered apps- he got zinger boneless wings, and i got the guacamole. portion size was ENORMOUS on the guac - it could have served 8 people, seriously.  flavor was meh. apparently the wingz were good.  hard to tell what hubby enjoyed more, the wingz or the scantily dressed hostesses. 

our server was great, attentive and pleasant.  When something went wrong she did her best to fix it. That was much appreciated.   Side salad came out wilted and gross. management offered to take it off the check, would have rather had a decent salad in the first place but i digress.  Dinner was not very flavorful - at all - and portion sizes were okay. i got the quesadilla appetizer (which was plenty for an entree) but it was very sloppily put together and had no seasoning at all.  I have had food that is presented better and tastes better at fast food restaurants, where i am happy to pay $5 for a meal.  

At the end of the meal, i badly wanted dessert but didnt want to risk another poorly flavored dish.  Not to mention, all the dishes were like lunch tray plastic, and i felt that a $50-60 dinner for two was at least worth a nicer presentation. who knows, it may have even made up for the bland flavors. 

perhaps i was let down by the fact that there always seemed to be a wait and i had over hyped it in my head.  Never have i wanted to send back everything i ordered at a restaurant before this night.  i will never be back.  my husband says he will order the wings, but takeout only. no more dining in at this place.
Revise this with your best effort:
Oh, Millers, how I had hoped to enjoy you. With your proximity to my home, plentiful parking, and spacious tables, I thought you would be the perfect dining spot. Your charming fireplace in the back added a touch of ambiance.

My friends and I attempted to dine here on two or three occasions for a quick and affordable meal. However, each time we were faced with a frustrating 30-60 minute wait. Initially, we assumed the long wait meant the food must be exceptional, but in reality, it seemed that people in Springfield settle for a subpar dining experience. Additionally, I must note that this place is not as budget-friendly as one might expect.

My husband and I decided to start with some appetizers; he chose the zinger boneless wings while I opted for the guacamole. The portion size of the guacamole was absolutely enormous, enough to serve eight people. However, the flavor was underwhelming. On the other hand, the wings apparently tasted good. It was hard to determine what pleased my husband more, the wings themselves or the scantily dressed hostesses.

Fortunately, our server was fantastic. She was attentive, pleasant, and made efforts to rectify any issues. Her attentive service was greatly appreciated. Unfortunately, the side salad that arrived was wilted and unappetizing. Though the management offered to remove it from the bill, I would have preferred a decent salad from the start. Moving on to the main course, dinner lacked flavor entirely, and the portion sizes were average at best. I ordered the quesadilla appetizer as my entree, which was more than enough food, but it was carelessly assembled and lacked any seasoning. I have had better-presented and tastier food at fast food joints, which I am content paying $5 for a meal.

By the end of the meal, I had a strong craving for dessert, but I hesitated to risk another disappointing dish. Moreover, the fact that all the dishes were served on flimsy plastic trays did not make up for the fact that a $50-60 dinner for two should warrant a more appealing presentation. Perhaps my high expectations and the constant wait times let me down. This was the first instance where I truly wanted to send back everything I had ordered at a restaurant. Needless to say, I will not be returning. My husband, however, claims he would order the wings for takeout only. No more dining in at this establishment for us.

input: Came back again bc I am stuck with a membership... The facilities are nice but they do NOT do a good job. Been coming here for 6 months because of the membership I bought. Every time I have to have them re-vacuum or wipe everything down again. They don't clean out the cup holders or wipe the door kick panels. So frustrating. Some of them on the vacuum side do not seem to speak English so it's even harder to have to explain I need it re-washed :( too bad... The location is perfect for me, if only the quality was
Revise this with your best effort: I returned once more due to my ongoing membership, but unfortunately, I find myself disappointed with the services provided. Despite the appealing facilities, the staff consistently fails to deliver a satisfactory result. Over the past six months, I have continuously requested them to re-vacuum or re-clean various areas. It's frustrating to see that they don't bother cleaning cup holders or wiping the door kick panels. This lack of attention to detail is quite disheartening. Additionally, communicating my needs becomes even more challenging as some employees on the vacuum side do not appear to speak English. It's a shame because the location couldn't be more convenient for me. If only the quality of their work matched the convenience.

input:
I am sort of a simple man, so I had never been to a liquor bar before. I have been to The Libertine twice and had a good experience both times. They use fresh ingredients all the way down to the crushed ice, which they crush with a mallet right at the bar. 

The biggest problem I ran into was figuring out which restroom was the men's. You have to look at the hair on the dimly lit pictures that indicate which is which, all the faces look the same.
Revise this with your best effort:
As someone who appreciates simplicity, I had never ventured into a liquor bar before. However, I recently had the pleasure of visiting The Libertine on two occasions, and I must say, it was truly delightful. They take great pride in using nothing but fresh ingredients, right down to the meticulously crushed ice, which they skillfully prepare right before your eyes at the bar.

Despite my wonderful experiences there, I did encounter a minor inconvenience when attempting to locate the men's restroom. The dimly lit pictures on the doors depicted individuals with similar hairstyles, making it rather challenging to discern the correct one.

input: Came with the family based on a recommendation and was not disappointed.  I consider myself to be a bit of a Pizza connoisseur and this was right up there.  The staff was friendly and the food came out quick.  Solid experience across the board.  I would come back and recommend it to others.
Revise this with your best effort: My family and I visited this place based on a recommendation and it truly exceeded our expectations. As a self-proclaimed Pizza connoisseur, I can confidently say that the pizza here ranks among the best. The staff was extremely friendly and the service was fast, ensuring a delightful dining experience. Overall, our visit was nothing short of exceptional, and I would gladly return to this place and highly recommend it to others.

input: We tried these at the Collingswood Art Festival this weekend. they are a bit pricey, but worth it. The flavor is perfect. they aren't greasy. I will be seeking them out. Once you try them... you will want to have them again. they are a light cheddar curd, battered and friend. You don't taste grease or batter. the flavor of the cheese is delicious, and so stringy and melty. The sauces are a delicate compliment to the curd. Well worth the splurge.
Revise this with your best effort: We had the pleasure of tasting these delightful treats at the Collingswood Art Festival over the weekend. Although they may come with a slightly higher price tag, they are undoubtedly worth every penny. The flavors are perfectly balanced, and what's even better is that they are not at all greasy. These cheddar curds are incredibly light, coated in a crispy batter and expertly fried. You won't even notice the presence of grease or batter - all you'll experience is the mouthwatering taste of the cheese, which is both stringy and meltingly delicious. Additionally, the sauces provided as accompaniments are a delicate and delightful complement to the curds. This indulgent splurge is definitely a worthwhile and unforgettable experience that will leave you craving more.

input:
Yats rocks. You walk in and they've got 4-6 cauldrons full of your choices...which are written in sidewalk chalk on a blackboard. There's always something vegetarian, and a plate full of any of it costs five fitty. Add a buck and you can get a split plate of 2 delectable cajun creations with rice. But the best part is the ridiculously awesome garlic bread...which you can get a bowl of for like a buck.

Not only is the food awesome, but the owner (Joe Vuskovich) is a local celebrity. He's a famed restaurateur from New Orleans that sells his secret spice to restaurants everywhere. Everybody in town knows him (despite the fact that there are two other locations) and he's highly supportive of local bands and kids that most older people stay away from.
Revise this with your best effort:
Yats is an absolute gem. As soon as you step inside, your senses are greeted by the sight of 4-6 bubbling cauldrons, each brimming with delectable choices, thoughtfully written in vibrant sidewalk chalk on a charming blackboard. You'll find something for every palate, including a delightful vegetarian option, and the best part? A plate full of any of these tantalizing dishes will only set you back five fitty. And if you're feeling extra indulgent, for a mere additional dollar, you can savor a split plate of two mouthwatering Cajun creations served with a generous side of rice. 

But perhaps the pièce de résistance lies in the form of their outrageously incredible garlic bread. A bowlful of this heavenly creation will only cost you a buck, adding an irresistible element to an already exceptional dining experience.

Yet, it's not just the food that makes Yats stand out. The owner, Joe Vuskovich, is a local celebrity, revered for his culinary prowess. Hailing all the way from New Orleans, he has made a name for himself as a renowned restaurateur, even sharing his secret spice blend with eateries far and wide. Despite the presence of two other locations, everyone in town knows Joe, a testament to his passionate dedication. Moreover, Joe's unwavering support for local bands and marginalized youth is truly commendable, showcasing his genuine care for the community and his desire to uplift those who often go unnoticed.

input:
Today after our Ethiopian food fiasco (see Selam review), we literally RAN into Pi after waiting hours to be served at the prior restaurant. We must have looked like a pack of hungry wolves so we told the hostess what had just happened. She seated us right away and sent us two orders of garlic bread (which we later found out were comped!). 

We ordered two pizzas and scarfed it all down. Pi has been consistently good on every visit I have made since I've moved to STL. Service is always excellent. Both the deep dish and thin crust are amazing every time.
Revise this with your best effort:
After enduring a disappointing Ethiopian food experience (as highlighted in our Selam review), fate seemed to have a change of heart as we coincidentally stumbled upon Pi after enduring hours of waiting at the previous eatery. Our collective famished expressions must have screamed desperation, which prompted us to confide in the hostess about our culinary misfortune. To our delight, she promptly seated us and surprised us with not one, but two complimentary orders of delectable garlic bread.

Eager to satisfy our voracious appetites, we wasted no time in ordering two pizzas, and it was as if a symphony of indulgence unfolded before us. The consistency of Pi's exceptional quality has remained steadfast during every visit since my relocation to STL, leaving an indelible mark of satisfaction. The service provided consistently shines in its excellence, ensuring a memorable dining experience. Whether indulging in their tantalizing deep-dish creations or savoring the perfection of their thin crust delicacies, Pi never fails to impress.

input: I went here to get my wisdom teeth out and they did a great job. The only complaint I have is that I never see the same dentist. I've been going here for 5 years.
Revise this with your best effort: I decided to have my wisdom teeth extraction done at this clinic, and I must say they did an exceptional job. However, my only grievance is the lack of consistency with the dentists I see during my visits. Despite having been a loyal patient for the past 5 years, I have yet to receive care from the same dentist consistently.

input:
After hearing about this place from a fellow Yelp Elite, my SO and I decided to try this place! We were warned of possible waiting times so came here on a Saturday around 10:45, and a line was already forming! 

For apps, we ordered the takoyaki and fried octopus. The takoyaki are delicious-an order comes with 5 balls that were perfectly cooked and topped with sauces. Takoyaki are little circular doughs with squid in the middle, topped with sauces and squid flakes (?). I definitely recommend this app. As for the fried octopus, it was just fried without sauces on top and came with mayo on the side, but it didn't come with enough mayo to dip the octopus in.

For ramen, I got the red spicy tonkotsu ramen and my SO got the black garlic tonkotsu ramen. For both ramen, the thin noodles were mushy/overcooked and just didn't quite fit with the ramen. That was the flaw with the dishes, and it tasted like the noodles were overcooked in a pot of flour-y water so it wasn't as clean (which explains the mushy feeling). They should use more bouncy noodles for this.

Now let's talk about the broth. The broth is flavorful, but the red chili broth was a bit too spicy for me and covered up the depth of the broth. I prefer the black garlic tonkotsu broth for that reason.

Overall, delicious food and pricing is reasonable. The decor is very nice as well, but screaming kids that were running around didn't make our meal pleasant.
Revise this with your best effort:
Upon receiving a recommendation from a fellow Yelp Elite, my significant other and I were eager to give this place a try. Aware of potential wait times, we arrived on a Saturday at 10:45 AM, only to find a line forming already!

For our appetizers, we opted for the takoyaki and fried octopus. The takoyaki were absolutely delightful – perfectly cooked, and each order came with five delectable octopus-filled dough balls, generously topped with flavorful sauces and squid flakes (?). I highly recommend giving this appetizer a try. As for the fried octopus, it was simply fried without any accompanying sauces, and unfortunately, the portion of mayo provided was inadequate for dipping.

Moving on to our ramen choices, I selected the red spicy tonkotsu ramen, while my partner settled for the black garlic tonkotsu ramen. Regrettably, both dishes suffered from the flaw of overcooked, mushy noodles that failed to complement the ramen properly. It felt as though the noodles had been excessively boiled in starchy water, resulting in a less refined texture. A firmer, more springy noodle option would greatly enhance the overall experience.

Now, onto the broth. While flavorful in general, the red chili broth proved too spicy for my taste, overpowering the nuanced depth of the broth itself. Consequently, I found myself leaning more towards the black garlic tonkotsu broth, which struck a better balance.

All in all, the food was delicious, and the pricing reasonable. Additionally, the establishment boasted a pleasant decor. Sadly, our dining experience was marred by the presence of unruly children running amok, making it less enjoyable.

input: Hands down best breakfast in Philly!  I've only been here for four months, but I have tried nearly every "Best of" spot in town.  I'm a breakfast fanatic so I get little over critical.  However, this small cafe has managed to create incredible flavor while keeping their dishes fresh and simplistic.  While the actual space is "cozy," this menu could easily keep a place as big as Parc overflowing with patrons.
Revise this with your best effort: Without a doubt, the ultimate breakfast destination in Philadelphia! Despite being a newcomer to the city, I've made it my mission to explore all the top-rated breakfast spots during my four-month stay. Being a breakfast connoisseur, I tend to be overly discerning, but this small cafe has truly impressed me with its ability to strike the perfect balance between mouthwatering flavors and a refreshingly uncomplicated approach to their dishes. Although the physical space may be described as "cozy," the menu is so outstanding that it could effortlessly attract a crowd as large as that at Parc, a renowned eatery in the city.

input: If I could give this place 6 stars I would. Don't let the looks deceive you, great diner food. Biscuits and gravy were incredible. Portions were more than I could eat.
Revise this with your best effort: If I were able to rate this place, I wouldn't hesitate to give it 6 stars. Despite its unassuming appearance, the quality of their diner food is exceptional. The biscuits and gravy truly exceeded my expectations. Not only were they incredibly delicious, but the portions were also incredibly generous, more than I could possibly finish.

input:
This place is hip.  Perhaps too hip for many over 35 but if you can tolerate the boisterous and extremely casually attired youth--I haven't worn a suit in 20 years either but even 20 year olds should have something besides skinny jeans and T-shirts with borderline obscene slogans in their closets--the food is worth it and the staff copes well.   

I had a 6:00 reservation (obtained the day before) but the sky seemed threatening a downpour so I came early to avoid it and was seated 20 minutes or so before the appointed time.  I often don't even make reservations and have no trouble getting seated at popular places by being there when they open or, for those open all day, coming before the popular dinner hour, but that didn't work the day before at Lüke.  Even at 4:30 the place was packed so I did make one for the following day.

My meal started with the crispy Brussel Sprouts.  Even if you hate Brussels sprouts (I like them), don't be afraid to try this dish--if no one told you you might not know what you were eating.  They are in some sort of sweet/sour sauce/dressing and fried both slightly blackened and crispy as advertised . . . tossed with almond slices, small bits of jalapeño and sprinkled with shavings of cheese on top.

Then I had pork schnitzel and "pommes frites" (that's shoestring fries to the Galliphobes).  It came with whitish gravy in a pitcher, I suppose to make it "Southern".  The gravy was good but I skipped eating it, doing that the usual way with a squeeze of lemon.  It was excellent and the fries were fine too.

I finished with some excellent decaf and a glass of Kahlua--I had had iced tea with the meal so some alcohol was not an excess.

A lady who was some sort of hostess dropped by my table while I was eating to make sure everything was OK and when told I needed ketchup (for the fries), went and got me some (in a dainty little single-serve Heinz bottle).  My waiter also checked several times but didn't hover.

I am giving it 4 stars.  The 5th star is withheld because of the crowded dining room and noise level . . . nothing to do with the food which I greatly enjoyed.
Revise this with your best effort:
This establishment is a trendy spot, although it may be too trendy for those over the age of 35. However, if you can overlook the noisy and extremely casually dressed young crowd - I haven't worn a suit in 20 years either, but even 20-year-olds should have more variety in their closets than just skinny jeans and T-shirts with borderline offensive slogans - the food is definitely worth it and the staff handles the chaotic atmosphere well.

I had made a 6:00 reservation (booked the day before), but as the sky seemed threatening a downpour, I arrived early to avoid any potential weather issues. To my surprise, I was seated about 20 minutes before my scheduled time. Typically, I don't bother making reservations and have no trouble getting seated at popular places by arriving when they open or, for those open all day, coming before the peak dinner hour. However, this approach didn't work the day before at Lüke. Even at 4:30, the place was already packed, so I made sure to reserve a table for the following day.

My meal began with the crispy Brussels sprouts. Even if you're not a fan of this vegetable (I happen to enjoy it), I encourage you to give this dish a try - if no one mentioned it, you might not even realize you're eating Brussels sprouts. They are coated in a delicious sweet and sour sauce, fried to a slight crisp and slightly blackened as advertised. Tossed with almond slices, small bits of jalapeño, and topped with cheese shavings, it's a flavorful and unique combination.

Next, I ordered the pork schnitzel with "pommes frites" (shoestring fries for the non-French enthusiasts). It was served with a white gravy in a pitcher, possibly to give it a "Southern" touch. The gravy was tasty, but I opted to skip it and instead enjoyed a squeeze of lemon with my meal. The schnitzel was excellent, and the fries were perfectly fine as well.

To conclude my dining experience, I had some exceptional decaf coffee and a glass of Kahlua. Since I had iced tea during my meal, adding a bit of alcohol was not excessive.

During my meal, a lady who seemed to be a hostess stopped by my table to ensure everything was to my liking. When I mentioned that I needed ketchup for my fries, she promptly fetched a dainty little single-serve Heinz bottle for me. My waiter also checked on me several times but did not hover excessively.

Overall, I would rate my experience 4 stars. I am withholding the fifth star due to the crowded dining room and the high noise level, which had nothing to do with the delicious food that I truly enjoyed.

input: Beers were amazing! I got the porter, the double IPA and the table gutt and they were all fantastic. Food was also killer if you like Russian cuisine. They had a special when I went with a sausage and sauerkraut which was tasty. I also got the pickled everything appetizer, great choice. This place rules.
Revise this with your best effort: The beers at this place were absolutely incredible! I had the pleasure of trying their porter, double IPA, and table gutt, and all of them were nothing short of exceptional. Not only were their drinks top-notch, but the food here is to die for, especially if you're a fan of Russian cuisine. During my visit, they had a special on a mouthwatering sausage and sauerkraut dish that satisfied my taste buds. Additionally, I couldn't resist ordering the pickled everything appetizer, and let me tell you, it was a fantastic choice. Without a doubt, this place is simply phenomenal.

input: There are a ton of good sushi places in Reno and I have tried them all, but it always seems like Rickshaw has the freshest fish. I'm not a big fan of rolls and sauces, and opt mainly for Nigiri or sashimi. You can get some dressed up roll anywhere, hell you can buy them in the store, but if you are a true fan of sushi, just fish is where its at and Rickshaw has some of the freshest in town.
Revise this with your best effort: In Reno, you'll find an abundance of excellent sushi places, yet Rickshaw consistently stands out with their unbeatable freshness of fish. As someone who appreciates simplicity in sushi and prefers Nigiri or sashimi over rolls and sauces, I have tried them all, and Rickshaw truly excels in delivering the pure essence of sushi. While fancy rolls can be found anywhere, even at local stores, true sushi enthusiasts know that it's the quality of the fish that truly matters. When it comes to sourcing the freshest fish in town, Rickshaw takes the lead.

input: This was my 1st visit here.  Overall, not that impressed!  To start with parking was really bad!  There are good choices of beer on draft.  The food was ok.  We split a few appetizers.  The fried olives were very tasty & different!  The rest of the appetizers were ok: the blue cheese chips, calamari, & meat/cheese platter.  I would try this place again, but overall not thrilled!
Revise this with your best effort: This was my first visit to this establishment, and unfortunately, I must say I was not thoroughly impressed. Let's begin with the parking situation, which was genuinely terrible. On the brighter side, they do offer a decent selection of beers on draft. As for the food, it was simply alright. We decided to share a few appetizers, and the fried olives stood out as particularly tasty and unique. However, the remaining appetizers, including the blue cheese chips, calamari, and meat/cheese platter, were average at best. While I might give this place another chance in the future, overall, it did not manage to excite or impress me.

input: Really not sure what the hype was when it opened. It's fine, the ambiance was nice, but the menu is limited and food is nothing to write home about. They are in a nice location so at least if you decide to wait, then you have things to see...
Revise this with your best effort: I wasn't quite sure what all the hype was about when this place first opened. Don't get me wrong, the ambiance was pleasant, but the menu left much to be desired and the food didn't leave a lasting impression. However, I must admit that their prime location offers an advantage. If you find yourself waiting, at least there are plenty of things to see nearby.

input:
This place was amazing! I only tried their ice cream I really wanted to try the hot chocolate but didn't get a chance :(. Well the ice cream was great! The first night I came here I got a brownie sundae all for myself, brownie on the bottom and three scoops of ice cream topped with whipped cream and nuts. I finished it all happily! I chose pumpkin cake flavor which was delicious and smooth. I also got pralines and cream that was better than other praline ice creams. The Tennessee fudge was vanilla with fudge swirled it was good not too special. 

The next time I came I got nutter butter ice cream that was really good had cookie pieces in it! I got the hot fudge topping over it and that was a great combination. 

The service was great the workers were really nice and patient with me haha indecisive! They would joke around with me and let me sample all I wanted. Also no judgement for eating all the brownie sundae alone :) lol
Revise this with your best effort:
This place was absolutely amazing! Although I unfortunately didn't get the chance to try their hot chocolate, the ice cream here was out of this world. On my first visit, I treated myself to a brownie sundae that had a delicious brownie base, three flavorful scoops of ice cream, topped with fluffy whipped cream and crunchy nuts. Every bite brought me pure joy, especially the pumpkin cake flavor which was delightfully smooth. Even the pralines and cream surpassed my expectations, standing out amongst other praline ice creams. As for the Tennessee fudge, it was a tasty blend of vanilla with perfectly swirled fudge, although it didn't completely steal the show.

During my next visit, I couldn't resist trying the nutter butter ice cream that was packed with irresistible chunks of cookie. To enhance the experience, I opted for the hot fudge topping which turned out to be a match made in heaven.

Not only was the ice cream exceptional, but the service was top-notch as well. The staff were incredibly friendly and patient, even humorously accommodating my indecisiveness. They generously allowed me to sample as many flavors as I desired without a hint of judgment. And let's not forget their understanding and lightheartedness when it came to me devouring the brownie sundae all by myself. Their relaxed and welcoming atmosphere added an extra layer of enjoyment to my visits.

input:
My dad and I were here for lunch and after reading some of the reviews, I was excited to check out this restaurant located where an O'Henry's once stood.

The place was fairly empty at 1 on a Friday and we were lead upstairs. Honestly, there's not much going on up there and it was a bit warm, but we decided to stick it out. Everything on the menu looked great and I decided to get the Catfish Acadian, which is catfish topped with crawfish and sauce with a side of vegetables. My dad got the pork chop.

My dish was great! I have no idea what was in the sauce but it was delicious and it was a perfect pairing with the fish. The vegetables were also really good; they were nicely cooked and fresh. My dad wasn't overly blown away by his pork chop, so if you find yourself here you might want to stick to the seafood.

Bria was our waitress and she was wonderful! She was attentive, kept the fresh iced tea coming and she was extremely personable. She was probably the highlight of the visit.

I'm not sure if I would go back. The food was good, but the atmosphere left something to be desired and I feel like I can get good catfish at plenty of places without going out of my way. I might go back at dinner, when the weather is cooler, and sit on the balcony outside as Harry suggested.
Revise this with your best effort:
My father and I came to this restaurant for lunch, intrigued by the previous reviews and its location, which once housed an O'Henry's.

Upon arriving at 1 pm on a Friday, we were led upstairs to a fairly empty dining area. I must admit, there wasn't much happening up there, and it was a bit warm. Nevertheless, we decided to give it a chance. As we perused the menu, every dish seemed enticing, so I couldn't resist ordering the Catfish Acadian, a delectable combination of catfish, crawfish, and a flavorful sauce, served with a side of fresh vegetables. My dad, on the other hand, opted for the pork chop.

To my delight, my chosen dish exceeded expectations! I couldn't pinpoint the exact elements of the sauce, but it was undeniably delicious and complemented the fish perfectly. The vegetables were also impeccably cooked and pleasantly crisp. Sadly, my dad's experience with the pork chop fell a bit short, so if you find yourself at this establishment, it might be wise to stick to the seafood options.

Our waitress, Bria, truly made our visit memorable. She was attentive, ensuring that our glasses were always replenished with refreshing iced tea, and her warm and friendly demeanor was genuinely delightful. She was certainly the highlight of our dining experience.

While I'm uncertain if I would return to this restaurant, as the food was satisfactory but the ambiance left something to be desired, I believe there are plenty of other establishments where I can find equally good catfish. However, Harry's suggestion of returning for dinner, when the weather is cooler, and enjoying the balcony seating does intrigue me. Perhaps a different time of day and setting will offer a more enjoyable experience.

input:
Well, well.... Where do I start with this place? First time experience, went in with my partner.

Walking in at about 7:30 on a Friday night (st paddys day weekend even)  and the  place had about 4 customers. That should have been my first clue as to what our experience was going to be like.

We seated ourselves and the waitress, an older gal maybe mid to late 40's who had greasy stringy unwashed hair and rotting teeth came up and took our drink order. My girlfriend got a Dr. Pepper and I got a water. She brought out Coke instead of DP. No biggie. We let it go, assuming it was an honest mistake. After about 10 minutes she returns and we order a 12 piece "jumbo" wing basket ($11.99), a 6 piece($7.99), and a beer batter sampler($11.99). 20 minutes pass and finally here comes our appetizer. The waitress throws the basket of appetizers on the table  and says "here's your food." Very flat with a big attitude and walks off. The beer battered mushrooms were doughy and undercooked. We had a single half full ranch cup to share between us for the big platter and she avoided our table when she saw we needed more.
***let me note that this waitress is giving the customers at the 3 tables surrounding us WAY better customer service. Even brought their food out in a timely manner with no attitude whatsoever.
I decide to let the mushrooms slide for the moment. I used to work in a restaurant and I understand that mistakes happen, however this far into the experience I'm being mighty generous since it's a first time experience.
We finish our appetizer and we wait and wait and wait and finally she comes by and takes the platter returning 10 minutes later with our wings. She makes no inquiry about the broken open, clearly undercooked, mushrooms still sitting on the platter.
I got the 12 piece with a single half full ranch. Again. Food on the table, doesn't ask if we need anything else which is something she is doing for other customers. at this point we have been here for about 40 minutes.

I got half regular and half thai flavor. The wings were NOT jumbo. They were puny. The flavor was good for the thai, and the waitress even stopped by to check up on us, though I wouldn't consider walking by quickly and saying in your flat attitude tone "youguysdoingalright?okaycool." Really all that helpful since she came and went so fast it took me a second to understand her. I had to reiterate for my girlfriend.  When I started on the regular I bit into my drumstick and had to fish a feather out of my mouth. DISGUSTING. It was that point that the entire experience was completely and thoroughly unacceptable.  The wings were soggy because they batter them or something on top of all that.  At first I had no plans other than to pay for the meal and leave the waitress 2 pennies and be on my merry way. But when the waitress came and asked if we needed a box I said no with 6 wings still on my plate, OBVIOUS SOMETHING WAS WRONG, again. She was going to take my stuff and make no inquiry to right the situation. I asked for the manager. Took a minute but finally the manager came over (mind you it is still pretty dead, what are these people doing I wonder?) I explained the food issues but blew off bringing up our treatment by the waitress. Normally I give the benefit of the doubt on this one but it was blatantly obvious that we were being treated differently with a different attitude than other patrons because we are a same-sex couple. Like our table had a contagious disease that prevented us from getting food in a timely manner, and getting drink and condiment refills too, regardless of the *empty* cups on the edge of the table. It wasn't like we were off in the distance. She had to walk by our table every time to communicate with the surrounding tables.

Anyways. The manager experience wasn't the greatest, but I wasn't going to pay for that meal after the feather thing, and she comped everything. BUT only after slightly arguing with us about the undercooked mushrooms, which by the way come frozen which  makes the fact that they weren't cooked all the way acceptable I guess? Don't know. Don't care. I WILL NOT BE GOING BACK!!!

2 stars because they did comp the meal, the waitress got lucky. If I would have had to pay for anything she wouldn't have gotten a tip due to the attitude but we left her $4 anyway since we didn't have to pay for the meal.  THAT IS THE ONLY REASON.
1 star though for the overall experience. Same-sex couples, steer clear. You aren't welcome there and it's obvious.
Revise this with your best effort:
Well, well... Where do I begin with this establishment? It was our first time visiting, and my partner and I walked in around 7:30 on a Friday night, even though it was St. Patrick's Day weekend. To our surprise, there were only about four other customers present, which should have been a hint about our upcoming experience.

We decided to seat ourselves, and the waitress, who appeared to be in her mid to late 40s with unwashed, greasy hair and decaying teeth, took our drink order. My girlfriend ordered a Dr. Pepper, but the waitress brought her a Coke instead. We brushed it off as an honest mistake and didn't make a big deal out of it. After waiting for about 10 minutes, the waitress returned and we placed our order: a 12-piece "jumbo" wing basket for $11.99, a 6-piece for $7.99, and a beer batter sampler for $11.99.

After waiting for 20 minutes, our appetizer finally arrived. However, the waitress carelessly threw the basket of appetizers on our table while saying, "Here's your food." Her tone and demeanor were quite unpleasant. Moreover, the beer-battered mushrooms were undercooked and doughy. To make matters worse, we were provided with a single half-full ranch cup to share among all the items on the platter. When we tried to get the waitress's attention for more, she conveniently avoided our table.

It is worth noting that the waitress provided much better service to the customers at the surrounding tables. She served their food promptly and without any attitude. This stark contrast only added to our disappointment. Although I tried to overlook the undercooked mushrooms, given my past experience working in a restaurant and understanding that mistakes happen, I was becoming increasingly generous in considering this as a first-time occurrence.

Once we finished our appetizer, we waited and waited for our main course. Finally, after what felt like an eternity, the waitress appeared and took away the empty platter, only to return 10 minutes later with our wings. However, she made no mention of the broken-open and clearly undercooked mushrooms remaining on the platter.

As for my wings, I had ordered a 12-piece and was again given only a half-full ranch cup. The waitress placed the food on the table without asking if we needed anything else, which she seemed to do for other customers. By this point, we had been at the restaurant for about 40 minutes.

The so-called "jumbo" wings were actually puny in size. The Thai flavor was delicious, and the waitress briefly stopped by to inquire if we were doing okay. However, her rushed manner of speaking made it difficult to comprehend her, and she quickly hurried away. I had to repeat her words for my girlfriend. While enjoying the regular-flavored wings, I bit into a drumstick and discovered a feather in my mouth. It was absolutely disgusting, and that moment made the entire experience utterly unacceptable. Additionally, the wings were soggy, perhaps due to some sort of excessive batter coating. 

Initially, I had no intentions other than paying for the meal and leaving a meager tip of two pennies for the waitress. However, when she asked if we needed a box, I declined as there were still six wings on my plate, indicating that something was clearly wrong. She was about to take away the food without attempting to address the issue. That's when I requested to speak with the manager.

After a brief wait, the manager came over. I explained the food problems while neglecting to mention the poor treatment we endured from the waitress. Normally, I give the benefit of the doubt, but it was painfully evident that we were being treated differently because we are a same-sex couple. It felt as though our table had some sort of invisible barrier preventing us from receiving timely service, drink refills, or even condiments, despite the empty cups on the edge of the table. We were not secluded; she had to pass by our table each time in order to interact with the nearby tables.

Although the manager's response was not the greatest, I refused to pay for the meal after finding the feather in my food. Eventually, after a slight argument about the undercooked mushrooms (which we later discovered were frozen, thus somewhat excusable), the manager decided to comp our entire meal. However, this only happened after some resistance. Regardless of the outcome, I have absolutely no intentions of ever returning to this establishment.

I am giving this place two stars solely because of the comped meal. The waitress was lucky that we didn't have to pay, as her attitude alone would have warranted no tip. However, we left her $4 anyway, considering the circumstances. The overall experience, on the other hand, deserves only one star. I strongly advise same-sex couples to avoid this place, as it overtly demonstrates its unwelcoming nature towards such individuals.

input: Why don't we have a Target?  I thought K-Mart was going out of business.  Well not this one, this miserable son of a bitch refuses to die.  They had the audacity to try to update it.  It reminds me of Jack Palance its old, tired, and smells funny, but it ain't going know where.    I wish a shiny new Target would come along and stab this relic of a store through the heart with its superior retail sword.  I have experienced on no less than 5 occasions of a product being labeled as on sale only to be charged full price at the counter.  Then I have to stop the line to back to the aisle and grab the sign to show it to the cashier.  Once I bought a beach chair here, well my wife saw the dopeness of said chair and wanted to copy me.  I return to the store the next day (happened to be 80 degrees and sunny) and those SOB's raised the price of the chair $10.  I was pissed yo.
Revise this with your best effort:
Why don't we have a Target? I remember hearing that K-Mart would be closing down, but apparently not this particular one. It's like this wretched store has a stubbornness to it, refusing to fade away. They had the audacity to attempt an update, but it's reminiscent of Jack Palance; old, worn out, and emitting an unpleasant odor, yet persisting nonetheless. I yearn for a fresh, gleaming Target to arrive and deliver the final blow to this outdated establishment with its superior retail prowess.

To make matters worse, I've experienced multiple instances where products were falsely labelled as being on sale, only to be charged the full price at the checkout counter. It's frustrating to have to halt the line and go back to the aisle to retrieve the sign, just to prove it to the cashier. On another occasion, I purchased a beach chair here, and my wife, impressed by its appeal, wanted to get one as well. However, when I returned the next day (which happened to be a beautiful, sunny day), those sneaky individuals had raised the chair's price by $10. Needless to say, I was extremely infuriated.

input:
Don't let the outside fool you-this place is much cuter and nicer inside than you would expect! 

Food is good and reasonably  priced. We ordered papaya salad, triple flavor duck, and king tofu soup. Papaya salad is always refreshing, but this place overdoes it on the fish sauce. Anything triple flavor is always a safe but delicious choice. I would say their king soup, with choice of protein, is a winner. 

And also, BYO!
Revise this with your best effort:
You'd be pleasantly surprised by the charming and inviting interior of this place, so don't judge it solely based on its exterior. The food here is not only scrumptious but also fairly priced. Our order consisted of the refreshing papaya salad, the delightful triple flavor duck, and the flavorsome king tofu soup. While the papaya salad is typically rejuvenating, this spot tends to go a bit heavy on the fish sauce. Opting for anything with the "triple flavor" label is always a safe and enjoyable choice. However, the real winner is their king soup, which allows you to select your preferred protein. 

Additionally, feel free to bring your own beverages!

input:
I feel so comfortable with the Mazzoni Center.  I, and many others, am incredibly lucky and grateful that these services exist.  Going through all sorts of life challenges can be painful and frightening when you know you're assumed to be a certain way.  Here, there are no assumptions.  They know who they're working with, and they are sensitive without the need to pry for information.  If you're in need of gynecology and you're not a woman, for example, they know exactly how to handle your needs while prioritizing respect for your identity.

My biggest concern is the physical space in which the Mazzoni Center clinic exists.  I feel sort of exposed in the waiting room.  I hope that they someday have the funds to upgrade to a larger, more private space.

If you visit during youth drop-in hours rather than making an appointment, you will probably wait a very long time to see someone.  This is completely understandable, in my opinion.  They'll advise you regarding what time you should show up if you call.

Occasionally, I've noticed lapses in communication; I have been kept waiting in the exam room before with no one around and no idea how much longer I would have to wait.  This is not a common issue, and I find that, overall, I receive more attentive service here than at any other clinic I've visited.

Be aware that the doctor you want to speak with may not always be available over the phone.  Don't be afraid to leave messages with reception.  You'll always receive quick assistance.
Revise this with your best effort:
The Mazzoni Center provides a comforting and inclusive environment that I am grateful for. Its existence is truly fortunate for individuals like myself facing various life challenges who are often assumed to be a certain way. Here, there are no assumptions or prying for information; they respect and understand who they are working with.

However, my main concern lies with the physical space of the Mazzoni Center clinic. I sometimes feel exposed and lacking privacy in the waiting room. I sincerely hope that they can acquire the necessary funds to upgrade to a larger and more private space in the future.

It is important to note that if you decide to visit during youth drop-in hours instead of making an appointment, you may experience a significant wait time. In my opinion, this is understandable and they are willing to provide guidance on the best time to arrive if you reach out to them.

Although rare, I have experienced instances where communication lapses occurred, leading to prolonged waits in the exam room without any updates. However, overall, I must emphasize that the level of attentiveness and care received at the Mazzoni Center surpasses that of any other clinic I have visited.

It's worth mentioning that the doctor you wish to speak with may not always be immediately available via phone. However, there is no need to hesitate in leaving a message with reception as they are very prompt in providing assistance.

input:
If I could give half a star I would, I'm from Tx, and anyone that thinks this is BBQ, I am willing to apologize to you for being led to believe that this is what BBQ is like.
I ordered the sample platter, horrific, the chicken looked and tasted like frozen pressed meat, the ribs.... All cartilage, the sausage, bland.... The sauce.... Walmart basic sauce with cups of sugar thrown in.... Extremely overpriced for ummm.... A child's plate (what it seemed like). I would never recommend this place to anyone.
Revise this with your best effort: If I had the option to give half a star, I certainly would. As a Texan, I feel compelled to apologize to anyone who mistakenly believes that this establishment serves authentic BBQ. I ordered the sample platter and it was an absolute horror show. The chicken had the appearance and flavor of frozen, processed meat, while the ribs were nothing more than chewy cartilage. The sausage lacked any semblance of taste, being completely bland. And don't even get me started on the sauce; it reminded me of a basic sauce you could find at Walmart, with an excessive amount of sugar added. The price was incredibly steep, considering I received what seemed like a child-sized portion. Needless to say, I cannot in good conscience recommend this place to anyone.

input:
Really great place for wine!

Came here with my dining group, there was about 20 of us on a Friday, for their Happy Hour. Excellent wine happy hour where all glasses are $5 or you can take $5 off any bottle of wine, which is a great deal if you're sharing with a few people...great way to try a few bottles.

The food was also great! Cheese plates are the way to go here! Excellent selections! Several of my foodie friends ordered sandwiches, which looked & smelled amazing! They all raved about them!

The ambiance is very warm and inviting! They do a great job decorating, especially around the holidays! My favorite space is the enclosed patio area, adjacent to the main dining area. Super warm and romantic on those cold winter evenings! 

The service is great as well!
Revise this with your best effort:
This place is an absolute gem for wine enthusiasts! I recently visited with a group of 20 people on a Friday and we were blown away by their Happy Hour. The wine happy hour is simply unbeatable, with all glasses priced at $5 or a $5 discount on any bottle of wine. It's an incredible deal, particularly if you're sharing with friends and want to sample multiple bottles.

The food here is equally impressive. The cheese plates are a must-try and offer a fantastic selection. In addition, some of my foodie friends ordered sandwiches, and they were nothing short of amazing. The flavors and presentation were top-notch, and they couldn't stop raving about them.

The ambiance of this place is warm and inviting, creating the perfect atmosphere. The decoration, especially during the holidays, is done exceptionally well. However, my personal favorite area is the enclosed patio, which is adjacent to the main dining area. It's incredibly cozy and romantic, especially on cold winter evenings.

Lastly, the service provided is exceptional. The staff goes above and beyond to ensure a memorable dining experience.

input: Rude staff. Can't even get a salad order right. Overpriced by the slice. When we sat down to wait for our food I thought wow this is taking a long time given the fact we were the only people in there. I guess it should stay that way. Don't waste your money.
Revise this with your best effort: The staff displayed an undeniable rudeness and proved unable to accurately fulfill a mere salad order. Moreover, the prices per slice were exorbitant. As we patiently waited for our food, it became apparent that the service was unreasonably slow, even considering the absence of other patrons. Sadly, this unsatisfactory experience leads me to suggest refraining from spending your hard-earned money at this establishment.

input: Really good, really authentic! This is some of the BEST Mexican cuisine I've tasted since my nana cooked for me; I'm from California so I would know. The enchiladas w/mole are awesome and the carne asada tacos remind me of Rosarito Beach, yummy!
Revise this with your best effort: Truly exceptional and undeniably authentic! This is hands down one of the most remarkable Mexican dining experiences I have savored since my nana's homemade meals. As a California native, I possess a discerning palate, and I can confidently assert that the enchiladas with mole are absolutely phenomenal. Additionally, the carne asada tacos evoke delightful memories of Rosarito Beach. Each bite is a scrumptious journey to flavor town!

input:
You need a Cinnamon Roll from the bake house.  You probably need two; life would have just a little less happiness and light without their Cinnamon Rolls.
The coffee and salads are also excellent, a lovely Saturday morning breakfast treat.
Revise this with your best effort:
Indulge in the heavenly delight of a Cinnamon Roll from the renowned bake house, for it is a necessity that cannot be overlooked. In fact, it is highly recommended that you acquire not just one, but two of these delectable treats, as life would be somewhat diminished without the sheer bliss and radiance they bring.

However, let us not disregard the other remarkable offerings that grace the bake house menu. Delight your palate with their exceptional coffee and delightful selection of invigorating salads, making for a perfect Saturday morning breakfast extravaganza.

input: I had the carrot cake.... Very disappointed tasted like licorice and baking soda cooking powder. It's too bad because everything looks so delicious :( also didn't like the chocolate chips in it either.
Revise this with your best effort: Unfortunately, the carrot cake I tried left me extremely disappointed as it had an unpleasant taste resembling licorice and baking soda. It's truly unfortunate because everything else appeared to be mouthwatering. Additionally, the inclusion of chocolate chips in the cake didn't sit well with my taste buds either.

input: You can't beat the prices for the unlimited food, but I've had better. The sushi is delicious, the salad was subpar and the crab Rangoon was probably the worst I've had. I've been twice and would definitely go again.
Revise this with your best effort: Although the prices for the unlimited food cannot be beaten, I must admit that I have tasted better elsewhere. The sushi is undeniably delicious, yet the salad leaves much to be desired and the crab Rangoon was quite underwhelming, ranking among the worst I have ever had. Despite these drawbacks, I have visited this place twice now and still find it enticing enough to consider going again.

input: Best chicken you could ever hope for in bourbon st. The chicken is good. The sauce is good. Everything is goof
Revise this with your best effort: Experience the pinnacle of chicken perfection at Bourbon St. Indulge in the finest chicken you could ever dream of, prepared to perfection. Not only is the chicken itself absolutely delicious, but the accompanying sauce elevates it to greatness. Every bite promises a divine blend of flavors that will leave you craving more. In short, everything about this chicken experience on Bourbon St. is truly outstanding.

input:
Reviewing the food.
Hard to justify $16 for a burger and fries BUT wowow this burger was so delicious. I'm not sure if I was just starving but ordered the Lama burger and the patty size is quality. They also have random ingredients thrown in that you probably haven't seen before like gruyere stuffed in a pepper on your burger. Fries came out nice and crisp vs. soggy and the bun on that burger was great. You order inside by the Nook and then can sit around. They have tons of craft beer to choose from and I could see this place getting packed on the weekends.
Revise this with your best effort: It is difficult to justify spending $16 on a burger and fries, but boy, was this burger worth it! I might have been famished at the time, but the Lama burger I ordered was absolutely delicious. The patty size was substantial and of excellent quality. Moreover, they had unique ingredients thrown in, like gruyere stuffed in a pepper, which added an interesting twist to the burger. The fries were perfectly crispy, unlike the usual soggy ones you come across. Additionally, the bun on the burger was superb. You place your order indoors by the Nook and then have the option to sit around. The establishment offers an extensive selection of craft beer, and I can foresee it becoming quite crowded on weekends.

input: Stopped in for breakfast on 12/2/17 I used to like it here for breakfast.  Service was slow coffee was not hot, grits were only warm and twenty minute wait for cinnamon biscuit after breakfast was brought to table then ten minutes to pay at counter to get out of the place there are better places to get breakfast in the area.  Should have went with my first choice instead of here.
Revise this with your best effort: On 12/2/17, I stopped by this place for breakfast, which I used to enjoy. However, my recent experience left much to be desired. The service was slow, and the coffee was not hot. Furthermore, the grits served were lukewarm, not up to my expectations. To make matters worse, it took a whole twenty minutes for my cinnamon biscuit to arrive after my breakfast was already served. Additionally, when I went to pay at the counter, I had to wait ten more minutes before being able to leave the place. Considering these disappointments, I now believe there are much better breakfast options available in the area. In hindsight, I should have trusted my instincts and chosen my first pick instead of coming here.

input: simply the best! everything from here is good! I come from a very Italian family and whenever there is a family event, there is always Termini brothers dessert trays! Their cannolis are amazing! Highly recommend.
Revise this with your best effort: When it comes to top-notch desserts, Termini Brothers never disappoints! As someone hailing from a truly Italian family, I can confidently say that their dessert trays are absolutely incredible. However, it is the heavenly cannolis that truly steal the show - they are simply amazing! I cannot recommend them enough, especially for any family gathering or special occasion. Trust me, you won't be disappointed!

input: It's a nice place. Really nice! Great service and awesome restaurants in the hotel. Clean rooms
Revise this with your best effort: The place is exquisite, undoubtedly so! Exceptional service and a plethora of outstanding restaurants within the hotel create an unforgettable experience. Immaculate rooms offer a haven of cleanliness and relaxation.

input:
After our recent trip to New Orleans, I came back to Reno appreciating this place even more than before! 
The shrimp po boy is my favorite thing on the menu! And their corn bread is amazing as well!
Revise this with your best effort: Upon returning to Reno after our unforgettable journey to New Orleans, I found myself developing an even deeper appreciation for this beloved city! Among the myriad of delightful dishes we indulged in, the shrimp po boy undeniably emerged as my absolute favorite on the menu. Furthermore, I must not fail to mention the palate-pleasing corn bread, which left an indelible mark of gastronomic delight on my taste buds.

input: People in this place are generally friendly, but do not make the mistake of going to Katie.  She went through my hair like a bulldozer-- slapped colour on it in less than 5 minutes and cut it in even less time.  I think she was in a rush to get out of there (it was late in the day), but then she shouldn't have agreed to take me on.  The whole thing cost me close to $200, and I was shaken up by the experience.
Revise this with your best effort: The people in this area are typically friendly, however, I strongly advise against visiting Katie. My encounter with her was quite unpleasant as she hurriedly tackled my hair, applying color haphazardly in a mere five minutes and cutting it in an even shorter amount of time. It seemed evident that she was in a rush to finish up and leave as it was late in the day. It's perplexing that she agreed to take me on in the first place if she was so pressed for time. The entire ordeal ended up costing me nearly $200 and left me feeling quite unsettled.

input: Favorite place in Nashville for breakfast!! This is a must go to spot!! Near Vandy and always busy...park in the back lot and be sure to get the parking ticket from the machine so you won't be charged...its free parking for a specified amount of time. My favorite is banana pancakes...think banana bread only in a pancake!! Perfection!!!! I don't leave Nashville until I go here to eat my pancakes!
Revise this with your best effort:
Do you want to know the best spot for breakfast in Nashville? Well, look no further! This place is an absolute must-visit, especially if you're near Vandy. Trust me when I say it's always bustling with eager patrons. Just remember to park in the back lot and make sure to grab a parking ticket from the machine. Don't worry, it's free parking for a certain period of time. 

But enough about parking logistics, let's talk about the real reason why I love this place - the banana pancakes. Picture this: tender, fluffy pancakes infused with the delectable flavors of banana bread. It's an absolute delight! These pancakes are so perfect that I make it a point to indulge in them before leaving Nashville. Believe me, you won't regret it!

input:
Yes, there are vegan options in University City, you just have to know where to look for them. MexiCali has a number of great options.

Many options here can be made vegan by holding the cheese. I absolutely adore the marinated tofu burrito. The tofu has a wonderfully chewy texture, and along with the black beans, the meal packs a protein-filled punch that will leave you full well past dinner-time, should you choose to finish it.  The sweet potato and plantain burrito is purportedly dairy-free, and it's another delicious, filling vegan option. The veggie tacos come with a spicier version of the sweet potato, the marinated tofu and some cabbage on doubled corn tortillas. The tacos are not as filling as the burritos, but they're a delicious lighter option. Finally, a fourth option for vegans: the guacamole burrito. They homemade guac is to-die-for delicious. 

I end up at MexiCali about once a week. I've been going since they were just a lunch truck 8 years back. There's often a line at the restaurant, but this place has been around for years and they have a great system to get you your burrito in a very timely manner.
Revise this with your best effort:
In the heart of University City, vegan options do exist, and with a little insider knowledge, you can easily uncover them. Look no further than MexiCali, a culinary gem boasting a plethora of delightful choices for plant-based enthusiasts.

At MexiCali, many menu items can be transformed into vegan delights by simply excluding the cheese. One standout option that never fails to impress is the marinated tofu burrito. The tofu itself presents a delightful chewy texture, while its pairing with flavorful black beans ensures a protein-packed meal that will keep you satisfied long after dinner. For those who enjoy a touch of sweetness, the dairy-free sweet potato and plantain burrito is a must-try. Bursting with delectable flavors, this filling vegan option is a true crowd-pleaser.

To add a fiery kick to your taste buds, indulge in the veggie tacos, featuring a spicier rendition of the sweet potato, along with marinated tofu and tangy cabbage, all tucked within double layers of corn tortillas. While the tacos may not be as filling as the burritos, they provide a lighter yet equally scrumptious alternative. And let's not forget the guacamole burrito, a heavenly creation that vegans can fully embrace. The homemade guacamole alone is utterly divine, elevating this burrito to absolute perfection.

Personally, I find myself gravitating towards MexiCali on a weekly basis, ever since its humble beginnings as a lunch truck eight years ago. Despite the occasional line, this establishment has honed their operations over the years, ensuring you receive your delectable burrito in a timely manner. So do yourself a delicious favor and embark on a culinary adventure at MexiCali, where vegan options abound and satisfaction is always guaranteed.

input:
Great breakfast fare and all. Eggs provençale was pretty good; all kinds of herbs and seasonings, but cooked inconsistently. Tomato on the side was awesome.

Omelets were executed well, and the pastries were pretty impressive.

But the coffee was horrendously bad. And without good coffee, what's the point of breakfast?

And I still can't trust restaurants that have misspellings on their menus. Even if the misspelling is from another language.
Revise this with your best effort:
The breakfast options were quite commendable, especially the flavorful Eggs provençale with its variety of fragrant herbs and seasonings. However, the preparation consistency could use improvement. The addition of a deliciously fresh tomato on the side enhanced the overall experience.

The omelets were skillfully made, showcasing a mastery of technique, and the pastries were undeniably impressive.

Regrettably, the coffee left much to be desired, falling short of expectations. After all, what is breakfast without a good cup of coffee to accompany it?

Furthermore, it's challenging to fully trust a restaurant that displays misspellings on their menus. Even if the misspelling is in another language, this lack of attention to detail raises doubts in my mind.

input: Another Yelper hit it -- this is a noisy, crowded restaurant with big screen TVs.  I wouldn't call it a sports bar.  Nothing wrong with the place.  Cool location, good beer selection.  The food - delicious, but eliminates itself as a "sports bar". My sons and I wanted to catch some pub grub and the hockey game.  Got the game.  The grub-- eclectic.  Do go here if you want a busy, bustling, energetic, tasty, flavorful, thumping music-beat experience.  Don't go here if you want  a burger, a beer and a hockey game amidst sports conversation.
Revise this with your best effort: Another Yelp reviewer was spot on with their assessment - this restaurant is definitely on the noisy and crowded side, with big screen TVs scattered around. While it may not fit the traditional definition of a sports bar, that doesn't mean there's anything inherently wrong with it. The location is pretty cool, and they have a good variety of beers to choose from. As for the food, it's actually quite delicious, although it might not align perfectly with the typical sports bar fare. My sons and I were looking to enjoy some pub grub while catching a hockey game, and while we did get to watch the game, the food selection turned out to be more eclectic than expected. This place is definitely a go-to if you're seeking a lively and energetic atmosphere, filled with tasty and flavorful cuisine, accompanied by thumping music beats. However, if you're specifically craving a burger, a cold beer, and the chance to engage in sports conversations while watching a hockey game, perhaps it would be best to look elsewhere.

input: Fabulous, quick, stress free windshield repair. .. didnt cost a penny out of pocket. I would definitely use this company again and would recommend to anybody!!
Revise this with your best effort: Exceptional windshield repair service that is efficient, hassle-free, and outstanding. Not only did it not require any out-of-pocket expenses, but it left me completely stress-free. Without a doubt, I would choose this company for any future needs and highly recommend it to anyone seeking top-notch service.

input: I was so excited about this meal, I came home to review it immediately. The service was outstanding and the food I'd say was some of the best in New Orleans. Even the freshly made bread was piping hot and delicious. We started with the oysters good enough, which were four fried oysters with bearnaise sauce and Benton's bacon- a must get. Then we both got scallops and swine with a butternut squash purée and balsamic vinegar. All of the entrees sounded phenomenal, but we both couldn't resist getting that dish. The best part I have to say was the dessert. We got cafe au lait panna cotta with mini glazed donuts, which reminded us of beignets at cafe du monde. Finally, I sampled their house made 'cellos, including ginger and limecellos, and they were unique and delicious. An amazing experience!
Revise this with your best effort: I was absolutely thrilled about this meal, so much so that I immediately came home to write a glowing review. The service was truly exceptional, and I dare say that the food was among the finest I have ever tasted in the whole of New Orleans. Even the freshly baked bread was piping hot and incredibly delectable. To kick off our meal, we indulged in the oysters, which were perfectly fried and accompanied by a delightful combination of bearnaise sauce and Benton's bacon. Trust me, it is an absolute must-have. For our main course, we both opted for the succulent scallops and swine, served alongside a velvety butternut squash purée and drizzled with a tantalizing balsamic vinegar reduction. Though all the entrées were undoubtedly outstanding, we simply couldn't resist the allure of this particular dish. The highlight of the entire experience, however, was unquestionably the dessert. We delighted in the cafe au lait panna cotta, accompanied by miniature glazed donuts that transported us back to the enchanting flavors of the beignets at the iconic Cafe du Monde. And to top it all off, I had the pleasure of sampling their housemade 'cellos, including the wonderfully unique ginger and limecellos, which were nothing short of astonishingly delicious. All in all, this was an extraordinary culinary experience that I will cherish for a long time.

input:
Absolutely amazing!!! My girlfriend and I went on a Wednesday night for Restaurant week and didn't know what to expect but we were overly satisfied. We ordered blood orange margaritas and they were strong and delicious. For our appetizers we had meatballs and let me tell you they weren't your average meatballs. They were veal and beef meatballs that melted in your mouth. Our other appetizer was some sort of grilled cheese that was amazing as well. For our entree we had the fishermen stew that was full of flavor and well balanced. Initially I did not think I was going to like it but it was to die for. Every element of the stew had it's own flavor and it was properly cooked. My girlfriend ordered the steak that came with cauliflower puree and a vegetable medley that was delicious as well. This was the first time we had ever ordered our steak to be medium-well and ever since we've been hooked. The steak was so juicy, tender and seasoned so eloquently and the puree was seasoned beautifully as well. 
The service there was amazing!! I forget the waitors name but he was great with the menu. He helped us order and came back frequently to check on us. 
Overall I think BARRA is amazing. It's not expensive and it is very intimate.  If you are looking for good food and great service at a reasonable price, BARRA is the place to go!!!!
Revise this with your best effort:
Amazing experience! My girlfriend and I decided to try BARRA during Restaurant Week, and we were blown away. We started off with the blood orange margaritas, which were both strong and absolutely delicious. The appetizers exceeded our expectations. The veal and beef meatballs were unlike any we've had before, melting in our mouths with their incredible flavors. The grilled cheese appetizer was also outstanding.

For our main courses, we chose the fishermen stew and the steak. The stew was bursting with flavor and perfectly balanced. Despite having initial doubts, it turned out to be a culinary delight. The steak, cooked medium-well as recommended by the waiter, was incredibly juicy, tender, and expertly seasoned. The cauliflower puree and vegetable medley complemented the steak impeccably.

Speaking of the service, it was exceptional. Though we can't recall our waiter's name, he impressed us with his extensive knowledge of the menu. He assisted us in making the right choices and checked on us regularly throughout the evening.

Overall, BARRA is a fantastic restaurant with an intimate atmosphere and reasonable prices. If you're looking for a place that offers excellent food, impeccable service, and a great value, look no further than BARRA!

input:
We went here hoping for a good breakfast,  and we weren't disappointed.  We went on Valentine's Day, not because we wanted to, but because we had to.  In doing so,  we knew the wait would be long, which it was (an hour and a half), though i hear there's always a wait. 

The place is buzzing with servers and busboys. The tables around the edges of the room are a bit close to one another,  so seating is tight.  The service was though, considering how busy it was.  I ordered the famed cornmeal pancakes with a side of hash browns and a fried egg.  My girlfriend ordered the banana pancakes with a side of bacon.  Everything was amazing.  The pancakes were hearty but fluffy... The side of bacon only comes with three pieces which is disappointing,  but it was cooked to her liking.  The cornmeal pancakes had just the right amount of everything... Bacon,  peppers... Salsa, sour cream,  syrup... Yes,  all of that.  If you're looking for good coffee,  this is not the place, which was surprising. 

The only question is do you go with the homemade syrup or the maple.... Or both
Revise this with your best effort:
We decided to visit this establishment in the hopes of indulging in a delightful breakfast, and we were not let down. Despite our visit taking place on Valentine's Day, not entirely by choice but out of necessity, we braced ourselves for the expected lengthy wait time, which indeed surpassed an hour and a half. However, I have heard that such waits are typical here.

The atmosphere was bustling with a multitude of servers and busboys, and although the tables lining the room's periphery were somewhat cramped together, the service itself was impressive considering the high volume of customers. I opted for the renowned cornmeal pancakes alongside a side of hash browns and a fried egg, while my girlfriend chose the banana pancakes accompanied by crispy bacon. The experience was truly exceptional. The pancakes were robust yet light, achieving the ideal balance... As for the side of bacon, it was a tad disappointing since it consisted only of three pieces, but it was cooked to perfection according to her liking. The cornmeal pancakes were flawlessly composed with just the right combination of ingredients... Bacon, peppers, salsa, sour cream, and even syrup - all present to elevate the dish to majestic heights. Surprisingly, if you are seeking a quality coffee, this establishment may not be your go-to destination.

Now, the only dilemma remains - should one opt for the homemade syrup or the classic maple syrup... or perhaps, one can savor the pleasure of both options simultaneously.

input: My husband son and I went in for dinner last Friday night. Upon entering we were greeted by a friendly hostess. As we stood there waiting for her to grab the menus I couldn't help but to notice a strong dirty mop water stench. Thankfully when we left the entry way it didn't carry into the dining room. The remodel is impressive looking. We were sat at a booth. Looking over the menu I was surprised at how limited it was. As long as you make what you offer well no biggie. I ordered the mushroom swiss burger and a beer. My husband ordered the "knuckle sandwich", ( tri-tip sandwich served French dip style). My son ordered the chicken strips and we all got French fries as our side. Jesse, our server was nice enough but in the loud dining room you couldn't hear a word he said. I was more annoyed that he didn't take the initiative to speak up than about the noise. The beer came out, although tasty it wasn't cold enough at all. The food came out within a reasonable amount of time. My husband's "Knuckle Sandwich" was delicious! That is what the two stars are for. My burger was shockingly small and probably the blandest burger I have ever eaten. My son's chicken strips tasted like they floured them...and that was it... also, no hint of seasoning. The fries are your run of the mill freezer to fryer. I hope they step it up and are successful.
Revise this with your best effort:
Last Friday night, my husband, son, and I decided to have dinner together. Upon entering the restaurant, we were greeted warmly by a friendly hostess. However, I couldn't help but notice a strong, unpleasant odor resembling dirty mop water lingering in the air as we waited for her to grab the menus. Fortunately, as we left the entryway and made our way into the dining room, the smell did not follow us. The restaurant's remodel was impressive, providing a visually appealing atmosphere.

We were seated at a booth and began perusing the menu. To my surprise, the options seemed quite limited, but I figured as long as the restaurant excelled at preparing the dishes they did offer, it wouldn't be a big issue. I decided to order the mushroom swiss burger along with a beer, while my husband opted for the "knuckle sandwich," a tri-tip sandwich served French dip style. Our son chose the chicken strips, and for our sides, we all ordered French fries.

Our server, Jesse, was friendly enough, but due to the loud noise in the dining room, it was difficult to hear anything he said. I found it somewhat frustrating that he didn't make an effort to speak louder, but I understood the challenges of the noisy environment. The beer arrived, and while it had a pleasant taste, it was not adequately chilled. In terms of timing, the food arrived within a reasonable amount of time.

My husband's "Knuckle Sandwich" turned out to be delicious, and for that reason alone, I would give the restaurant two stars. However, I was disappointed with my mushroom swiss burger as it was surprisingly small and lacked any memorable flavor. In fact, it might have been the blandest burger I have ever tasted. Similarly, my son's chicken strips seemed to be coated solely in flour, with no hint of seasoning. The French fries were standard freezer-to-fryer fare, offering nothing extraordinary.

Despite these shortcomings, I do hope that the restaurant can step up its game and find success in the future.

input: I had a delicious breakfast at Tuttini a few months ago.  I went back for lunch recently and was excited by their sandwich offerings, however, I was not served.  It was 1:45 PM, and their sign states that they serve lunch until 2:30 PM.  I waited in line for 7 or 8 minutes before a woman came out to tell me that the kitchen was closing.  Closing over 30 minutes early!  She said she might be able to make something to go.  So, if you can make something to go, doesn't that mean the kitchen is not yet closed?  Besides, I wanted to have a few minutes to relax in the cozy restaurant and enjoy my sandwich, not gulf it down on the street, so I left.  I got a sandwich at North Star Coffee around the corner and gave them my $10 instead.
Revise this with your best effort:
A few months ago, I had the pleasure of indulging in a delectable breakfast at Tuttini. With that delightful experience in mind, I eagerly returned for lunch recently, enticed by their enticing sandwich options. However, to my disappointment, I was not served.
