Resignedly, I patiently waited in line for approximately 7 or 8 minutes before a woman emerged from the kitchen and notified me that they were closing. My astonishment grew as I realized they were closing over 30 minutes earlier than stated. She did mention that she might be able to prepare something for me to take away. This perplexed me since it implied that the kitchen was still operational. Furthermore, my intention was to savor my sandwich while enjoying a few leisurely moments in the cozy ambiance of the restaurant, rather than hurriedly consuming it on the street. Consequently, I made the decision to depart. Instead, I opted for a sandwich from North Star Coffee, a neighboring establishment, and willingly handed them my $10 in place of Tuttini.

input:
I've only eaten here twice and my experience has been great overall. The first time I went, they had just opened. There were some kinks but not anything I would complain about. After all, our group had 8 people so it was understandable. Second time was probably a month later and I noticed they figured out some of the kinks. Their servers are nice and I genuinely felt like they wanted to make my experience great. I know this because every time I made a request the waiter would literally run to get it. I've never seen a server so dedicated, kudos! Honestly most of the stars I'm giving them is because of their genuine service. Added bonus, they were playing Star Trek, hunger games, and iron man. Nice movie selections haha.

The seafood was ok. It's not their fault; it's Tucson so you know you really can't get fresh seafood. That's why I took off a star. They have 1 type of sauce with mild, medium, hot spiciness. It's similar to angry crab's "trifecta" or boiling crab's, "the whole shabang" but with an Asian twist. It was good in my opinion.

Lastly, if anyone has ever gone to angry crab, hot n juicy, boiling crab, should know that the price range is similar. Heck, if anyone has ever bought raw seafood at the store should know that it is on the expensive side. Expensive? Yes. Overpriced? No. I have been to many seafood places similar to this and it's a decent price for what you get. My advice for the Dungeness crab, since it did happen to me at other places and I saw a review on it here, is to share it or get their other selections that they can measure out. The dungeness crab is a full crab so finding a 1 lb dungeness crab is not common. 

Would recommend and go again.
Revise this with your best effort:
I have dined at this restaurant on two occasions and overall, my experience has been excellent. The first time I visited, the establishment had just opened, so there were some minor hiccups, but nothing worth complaining about. Given that our group consisted of eight people, it was understandable. However, when I returned about a month later, I noticed they had ironed out most of the kinks. Their servers were incredibly friendly, and I genuinely felt their dedication to ensuring a wonderful dining experience. I was amazed at how promptly they fulfilled any request I made; in fact, the waiter would literally run to accommodate me. Their exceptional service is the main reason why I am giving them such a high rating. Additionally, it was a pleasant surprise to find that they were playing popular movies like Star Trek, Hunger Games, and Iron Man. The movie selections definitely added to the overall ambiance.

Now, let's discuss the seafood. It was decent, but I must say that it's not entirely their fault. Being in Tucson, it's hard to find truly fresh seafood, which is why I deducted a star from my rating. They offer one type of sauce with varying levels of spiciness - mild, medium, and hot. It reminded me of Angry Crab's "Trifecta" or Boiling Crab's "The Whole Shabang," but with an interesting Asian twist. Personally, I found it quite enjoyable.

Lastly, regarding the price, anyone familiar with establishments like Angry Crab, Hot N Juicy, or Boiling Crab would know that the price range is relatively similar. Even if you have bought raw seafood from a store, you are aware of its expensive nature. Yes, this restaurant can be considered pricey, but it is not overpriced. Having been to many seafood places similar to this, I find that their prices are fair for the quality and quantity of food you receive. For those interested in the Dungeness crab, I would advise either sharing it or opting for their other measured-out selections. Dungeness crabs are typically whole crabs, so finding a one-pound Dungeness crab is not very common.

In conclusion, I highly recommend this restaurant and will definitely visit again in the future.

input:
I moved to Philadelphia from the midwest as a wide eyed 19 year old full of wonder. Yuengling lager was the first beer I've ever truly enjoyed and remains in my top five favorites of all time. Smooth, sweet, cheap, it's like me in a bottle. I love that the bottlecaps can be rusty, I like that the taste varies per batch, I even like its relatively low alcohol content. 

The tour was pretty great, the British tour woman was funny in a non canned way. She took a shine to my grandpa and was constantly begging him to sell her his hat (signed, sports, I haven't a clue). I was amazed at how close they let you get to the active equipment, I could've spit in the mash and no one would've been the wiser. The whole facility reminded me of St. Pete Catholic High, 50's cinderblock with a residue of toil clinging to the walls. 

The tasting, that's what you came for right? Fantastic. They were out of Lord Chesterfield, but who drinks that? I "tasted" the shit out of the lager, probably 6 times. It makes sense, the bar is next to the gift shop and I went a bit insane in there. 

The fact that Dick Yuengling made it a point to hire back the laid off workers after the last closure bumps it up a star. This is a family business, one that deserves support as Inbev has encroached upon everything else.
Revise this with your best effort:
I relocated to Philadelphia from the Midwest as a wide-eyed 19-year-old, filled with awe and curiosity. Yuengling lager emerged as the first beer that truly delighted my senses, and it continues to hold a cherished place among my top five favorites of all time. With its smooth, sweet, and affordable nature, it feels like a true reflection of my own essence encapsulated in a bottle. I even appreciate the rustic charm of its sometimes rusty bottle caps and the delightful variations in taste from batch to batch. Its relatively low alcohol content is also a quality that I find endearing.

The brewery tour proved to be quite remarkable. The British tour guide, unlike the usual scripted speakers, had a genuine sense of humor. She took a liking to my grandfather and amusingly persisted in attempting to buy his signed sports hat (though I had no idea what significance it held). I was astonished by how closely we were allowed to observe the active equipment; I could have easily indulged in childish mischief like spitting in the mash without detection. The overall facility evoked memories of my time at St. Pete Catholic High, with its 1950s cinderblock architecture bearing the tangible marks of hard work etched onto the walls.

Of course, the highlight of the experience was the tasting. Isn't that why everyone comes? And it did not disappoint. Unfortunately, they had run out of Lord Chesterfield, but who really drinks that anyway? I enthusiastically "tasted" the lager numerous times, perhaps to an excessive extent. It's hard to resist when the bar is conveniently located next to the gift shop, and I succumbed to the fervor of the moment.

What truly elevates Yuengling's reputation for me is the fact that Dick Yuengling, the owner, made a deliberate effort to reemploy the workers who were previously laid off during the last closure. This family-owned business deserves all the support it can get, especially considering the encroachment of Inbev into the beer industry.

input:
