input: Try the spinach and feta hummus, it is amazing. I had the chicken caesar pita and if was wonderful. The caesar dressing was very flavorful and the greens (romaine, mixed greens, etc) were good quality and flavorful (not your typical bagged junk). Pulling up the the place I was skeptical (they're in an old garage) but give it a try, well worth it.
Revise this with your best effort: I highly recommend trying the spinach and feta hummus - it truly is an amazing dish. As for my own experience, I had the chicken Caesar pita and it was absolutely wonderful. The caesar dressing had an incredibly rich flavor, and the mix of greens, including romaine and mixed greens, were not only good quality but also packed with delicious flavors, far surpassing your typical bagged greens. Initially, I was a bit skeptical when I saw the restaurant was situated in an old garage, but I assure you it is definitely worth giving it a try.

input: Love this place! Almost all of their menu items can be made vegan. They are super knowledgeable. The Pad Thai with tofu, veggies, and cashews is perfection. The avocado egg rolls are amazing too! A favorite.
Revise this with your best effort: I absolutely adore this place! It's remarkable how they offer vegan options for nearly all items on their menu. The staff here is incredibly well-informed and helpful. I must mention how the Pad Thai with tofu, vegetables, and cashews is an absolute symphony of flavors – perfection at its finest. Additionally, the avocado egg rolls receive nothing but praise, truly a favorite among patrons.

input:
I've often passed this swanky little place in Downtown filled with good-looking professionals laughing over drinks, appetizers and spilling over the sidewalk

NOM NOMS
Although you probably won't get full on the sizes, the food is like little art works of flavor. My bowl of mussels and clams was HUGE and I sopped up the buttery, faintly spiced broth with the accompanying breadstick. Well done. The other appetizers like Tuna Tartare and Coconut Shrimp each had awesome flavor surprises - fresh, melty tuna and a wasabi and jam sauce respectively - both excellent and plated beautifully.

My cocktail "The Tryst" didn't impress. Watery and a strange alcohol after taste. I'll forget it tomorrow. 

SERVICE
Thanks Yelp for introducing me here. It's easy to get overlooked at the bar, but once seated, our server was quick and helpful and was great at lowering my inhibitions by telling me what to expect in a "vegetable" beer they offered--spot on. 

SUMMARY
I'll probably stick to the drinks only here because the food prices are above my range... or go during happy hours. Cool, hip place to bring the girlfriends or if you're looking for impressive, gutsy art dishes with good taste.... and if you have cash to blow (but I won't let that subtract a review star)
Revise this with your best effort:
NOM NOMS
On my frequent journeys through Downtown, I couldn't help but notice this chic establishment bustling with attractive professionals, joyfully indulging in drinks and appetizers that overflowed onto the sidewalk.

When it comes to the food, prepare to be dazzled by the culinary masterpieces that are served here, even if the portion sizes may not leave you feeling completely satisfied. The mussels and clams in my bowl were a grand spectacle, accompanied by a rich and subtly spiced broth that I happily soaked up with a delectable breadstick. Truly impressive. The Tuna Tartare and Coconut Shrimp appetizers offered delightful surprises with their fresh ingredients and exceptional flavors. The melting tuna and the complementing wasabi and jam sauce were divine, and the presentation was simply remarkable.

However, I must confess that my cocktail experience, "The Tryst," was rather underwhelming. It lacked depth, tasted somewhat diluted, and left an unpleasant alcohol aftertaste. I suspect this drink will fade from my memory by tomorrow.

SERVICE
I owe a debt of gratitude to Yelp for leading me to this hidden gem. While initially one may feel a bit neglected at the bar, once seated, our server promptly attended to us, displaying helpfulness and efficiency. They provided valuable insight into the "vegetable" beer on the menu, allowing me to make an informed choice that perfectly aligned with my preferences.

SUMMARY
Considering the slightly steep prices of the food, I will likely limit my visits to enjoying their drinks or take advantage of their happy hour specials. Undoubtedly, this is a trendy and sophisticated spot to gather with friends or venture in search of bold and impressive culinary creations, as long as you're prepared to spend a bit more. However, it would be unfair to deduct a star from this review solely based on the higher prices.

input: The great customer service that you get here, you won't find in another to-go Asian/Thai restaurant. I enjoyed the food! The curry had great flavor and consistency. The shrimp fried rice does not look appealing but it is flavorful and fluffy. I dropped it down to 4 stars because I paid an additional $2.00 for extra egg and it was NOT extra egg. I also called in my order and received a 30 minute wait time. Total wait time was an hour. With all that being said, the ladies won me over with their passion to serve those waiting and making sure each customer was happy!
Revise this with your best effort: You won't find customer service as exceptional as what you experience at this Asian/Thai restaurant. I thoroughly enjoyed the delectable food, particularly the flavorful and well-balanced curry. Despite the visually unappealing appearance, the shrimp fried rice surprised me with its delicious taste and fluffy texture. However, I must deduct a star due to the additional charge for extra egg, which turned out to be nonexistent. Additionally, although I called in my order and was informed of a 30-minute wait time, the total wait ended up being an hour. Nonetheless, the remarkable dedication of the staff, particularly the ladies, in ensuring the satisfaction of each customer pleasantly impressed me.

input: Ordered fresh made pie, not reheated slices.  Some of the best pizza I've had in philly, because of the tasteful and crunchy crust and good amount of toppings.  Had a Cowboy steak with no BBQ sauce and couldn't stop myself at two slices.  Got the same pizza again with bbq sauce and it was just as good so now I do half and half.
Revise this with your best effort:
I had the pleasure of indulging in freshly made, never reheated slices of pie. Undoubtedly, it was some of the most exceptional pizza I have ever had in Philly. What set it apart was the perfect blend of flavors in the tasteful and satisfyingly crunchy crust, coupled with generous toppings that left nothing to be desired.

One particular pizza that stole my heart was the Cowboy steak, minus the BBQ sauce. It was simply irresistible; I couldn't resist devouring two slices in a row. So enamored with its delectable taste, I couldn't help but order it again. This time, however, I decided to experiment and added BBQ sauce to the equation. Surprisingly, it turned out to be just as divine, solidifying my love for this pizza.

Nowadays, I find myself torn between the two variations, opting for a half and half combination that satisfies all my pizza cravings.

input:
It's just a place to get my mail. 
It's about $250.00 per year for a little box.  it makes sense for us because we travel so much.  I don't want any important mail being delivered to my house.  
I have a door key to the store so I can access my letter box after hours.
My larger parcels are kept in the back.  I get a phone call every time I receive one.  
I would rather ship out my parcels using Fed-ex because they are cheaper and more reliable.   
My husband has used their printing services and is happy with them. 
I see packaging materials and other stationary goods for sale, but I prefer to use Canada Post for that.
No problem with the staff.  They are cheerful and helpful.  They know me well.
The strip mall location can be a little sketchy.  Some druggies and homeless people like to hang out at the neighbouring store fronts.
Revise this with your best effort: This is just a convenient spot to receive my mail, priced at approximately $250.00 per year for a small box. Given our frequent traveling, it's practical for us not to have any important mail delivered to our residence. Fortunately, I possess a store key which allows me to access my mailbox even outside of regular hours. Additionally, larger packages are stored in the back and I receive a phone call whenever I receive one. When it comes to shipping out parcels, I prefer utilizing FedEx due to their affordability and reliability. My husband has utilized their printing services and has been quite satisfied. Although I notice packaging materials and other stationery for sale, I personally prefer employing Canada Post for those needs. The staff at the facility pose no issue, as they are always cheerful, helpful, and familiar with me. However, I must admit that the strip mall location can be a bit concerning at times, as there are occasional loiterers and homeless individuals frequenting the neighboring storefronts.

input: I just walked out of Heads and Tails and I can't  say enough about Jenne.  I was quite nervous to have a bikini wax and Jenne talked me though the whole process and it was not bad at all!  If you have sensitive skin and are looking for a clean place with an excellent staff - do not hesitate going here. Will be back!
Revise this with your best effort: I recently visited Heads and Tails and had an exceptional experience with Jenne. My initial apprehension about getting a bikini wax was quickly eased as she patiently guided me through the entire process. To my surprise, it was not as uncomfortable as I had anticipated. If you have sensitive skin and seek a hygienic establishment with a highly skilled team, I wholeheartedly recommend this place. I guarantee you won't regret it; I'm certainly planning to return!

input: Ordered some food at 11:47pm after not eating all day due to airline issues. I was starving. 2 and 1/2 hours later my food was delivered after I called twice looking for it.  When it arrived, there was no utensils or napkins.  I ate my salad with my fingers.  The food is good, the service is horrible.  Never again!
Revise this with your best effort: After enduring a day of airline issues that left me famished, I finally placed a food order at 11:47pm. My hunger was unparalleled. However, my much-needed sustenance arrived a painstaking 2 and a half hours later, only after I made two calls inquiring about its whereabouts. Disappointingly, the delivery lacked essential utensils and napkins, forcing me to resort to eating my salad with my bare hands. While the food itself proved satisfying, the abysmal service has left me with no intention of ever revisiting this establishment.

input: Delicious and very nicely presented. We had J Sushi and Fire Roll and fantastic. Excellent service and great value.
Revise this with your best effort: The food at J Sushi was absolutely delicious, and it was beautifully presented as well. We thoroughly enjoyed the Fire Roll, which was outstanding. Moreover, the service we received was top-notch, and we felt it was an excellent value for the quality of food and experience we had.

input: My wife and I just moved to town and where saddened to have to move away from our local beloved Mexican restaurant.  We passed by this place several times knowing that once we moved in we would have to try it.  And OMG we where floored, the restaurant had great traditional ambiance and the service was top knotch.  They served glass bottle sodas which personally is something I love.  The food was amazing, my wife had the Taco Sombrero and I had the Chimichanga.  Both where amazing.  This place is 6 stars if I could give it.
Revise this with your best effort: My wife and I recently relocated to this town, and it was with a heavy heart that we bid farewell to our cherished local Mexican restaurant. However, as we passed by this new establishment on multiple occasions, we eagerly anticipated the day we could finally step inside and savor its offerings. To say that our expectations were exceeded would be an understatement - we were absolutely astonished by the fantastic traditional ambiance and impeccable service provided by this restaurant. It was delightful to discover that they served glass bottle sodas, a personal preference of mine. Now, let's talk about the food - it was nothing short of extraordinary. My wife savored the Taco Sombrero, while I indulged in the deliciousness of the Chimichanga. Neither dish disappointed; they were both resplendent. In my book, this place deserves a rating of six stars, if only that were possible.

input:
As much as I adore food I am, typically, pretty easy when it comes to food and I forgive a lot. SO...one star means a lot! I haven't been as livid as I was leaving this fiasco of a restaurant in a long while. Reasons:  The server was on her cell phone from the minute we walked in to the minute we walked out (about 90 minutes). She literally had it on her shoulder the entire time except to say, "Please hold" to take our orders. She was also the chef and cooked while talking on her bloody phone, as well. Service:  FAIL.
My pork leg was tender and good which constitutes the lonely little star you see above. My husband ordered the shrimp, which cost $18.99. He received 7 shrimp that would be in a bag of 31-35 count...the size worthy of a salad shrimp. Again, $18.99...and the plantain portion of the meal consisted of 2 plantains the width of a postage stamp. Ridiculous. I then ordered tostones because I knew he would never be full with that quantity of food. I had to get up and find our server to add to my order as she was nowhere to be found.  They were also ridiculously thin, were over salted with an almost breaded and deep fried consistency. Food:  FAIL.
I was going to order a Cuban coffee but the server was so non-existent that I just gave up, finally.  In retrospect, I'm happy I didn't order it because I'm sure it would have been just wrong.
I would not frequent this restaurant again even if I had a free coupon. Don't waste your time or energy.
Revise this with your best effort:
As someone who truly appreciates food, I am usually quite lenient and forgiving. However, this particular dining experience left me absolutely furious and disappointed, a feeling I haven't encountered in a long time. Let me provide you with the reasons behind my frustration: Firstly, our server had her cell phone glued to her shoulder from the moment we stepped foot into the restaurant until we left, which took approximately 90 minutes. Aside from occasionally putting it down to take our orders by saying a mere "Please hold," she shamelessly continued her personal conversations while also attempting to fulfill her role as both server and chef. This level of service was a complete failure.

On a positive note, the only reason I have given the restaurant a single star is because my pork leg dish was somewhat tender and enjoyable. However, my husband's order of shrimp, priced at a hefty $18.99, was an absolute disappointment. He received a pitiful serving of 7 shrimp that belonged in a bag labeled 31-35 count, more suitable for salad shrimp. To make matters worse, the portion of plantains included in his meal consisted of a meager 2 pieces, each as wide as a postage stamp. This was undeniably ridiculous. In an attempt to salvage the meal, I decided to order tostones, knowing very well that the quantity of food provided would not satisfy my husband's appetite. Unfortunately, our server was nowhere to be found, and I had to go out of my way to find her and add the extra side to my order. When the tostones finally arrived, they were disturbingly thin, excessively salted, and possessed an oddly breaded and deep-fried consistency. The quality of the food was undoubtedly a failure.

I had initially planned to conclude the meal with a Cuban coffee, but the server's lack of presence left me no choice but to give up on that idea. Looking back now, I am relieved that I didn't order it, as I can only imagine how disappointingly wrong it would have been.

To put it frankly, I would strongly advise against ever visiting this restaurant, even if you were offered a free coupon. It simply isn't worth your precious time or energy.

input:
Excellent customer service. I wish I could rent from there more often! Had such a great experience verses other car rental services. 

Rent if you can!
Revise this with your best effort: The customer service at this place is truly outstanding. I genuinely wish I could rent from them more frequently! My experience with them far surpassed that of other car rental services. If you have the opportunity, renting from them is highly recommended!

input: Taking over in the spot of the original Benton Park  Cafe is Cafe Piazza.  The atmosphere is really nice and super ST. LOUIS.  The mural on the ceiling is a very eclectic work of art. Ask them how they did it and look under the bar. Great food. Different from your standard breakfast food.  Kinda fancy, but not intimidating.  I would highly recommend this restaurant for three reasons: decor, location, and good, creative food for the price.
Revise this with your best effort: Replacing the original Benton Park Cafe, Cafe Piazza seamlessly takes its place as a charming establishment embodying the heart and soul of St. Louis. Stepping inside, one is greeted by a delightful atmosphere that exudes warmth and character. The pièce de résistance is an eclectic mural adorning the ceiling, an awe-inspiring work of art that warrants inquiry into its creation - and peering under the bar might just reveal the secret. While the food on offer is delectable, it sets itself apart from the mundane breakfast fare typically found elsewhere. With an elegant touch that avoids any hint of pretentiousness, this restaurant is an absolute must-visit. Allow me to present three compelling reasons to indulge in Café Piazza: its captivating decor, prime location, and the delightful fusion of innovation and flavor offered at a reasonable price point.

input:
I am a groupie. He is amazing. I am sad that I got to have his dish only once. Now all construction on market I can't find him!!

His chicken is the most tender and smoky I've ever had. Side dishes are creative and awesome too. 
I hope he is back soon.

His chicken is an unparalleled masterpiece of tenderness and smoky flavors. The accompanying side dishes are a testament to his creativity and are nothing short of remarkable. My anticipation grows as I eagerly await his triumphant return.

input:
Enjoyed a company corporate holiday party with 2K+ people in the Tuscany Ballroom with an overnight stay in the Tuscan Tower.  By far the very best resort in the area delivering a cruise ship like first class experience.  I don't smoke and didn't notice the typical second hand casino smoke.    

Bonus was eating breakfast in the coffee shop with the Peppermill CEO/GM John Hanson pulling up a seat next to me at the counter engaging in friendly conversation about my stay while enjoying his breakfast.   Doesn't get much better than this folks.
Revise this with your best effort:
I had the pleasure of attending the company's corporate holiday party, which took place in the exquisite Tuscany Ballroom, alongside more than 2000 individuals. To top off this exceptional experience, I had the privilege of staying overnight in the luxurious Tuscan Tower, making it unquestionably the finest resort in the entire area, providing a first-class ambiance akin to that of a top-notch cruise ship. Remarkably, despite being a non-smoker, I was pleasantly surprised to find the absence of the usual pervasive secondhand smoke that plagues most casinos.

As an added bonus, I had the opportunity to relish my breakfast in the coffee shop, where I had the unexpected pleasure of sharing a seat at the counter with none other than John Hanson, the esteemed CEO and General Manager of Peppermill. Engaging in warm and friendly conversation about my stay, John made me feel truly valued as a guest while we both enjoyed our morning meals. It goes without saying that this encounter was the epitome of perfection and an experience that one could only dream of.

input:
Wow.  I have to say incredible.  We've driven by the place several times and always had that "meh' attitude because of how the plaza looks.  Since the wife was craving some crispy duck it came up as having the best reviews for it.
  Walking in, was a great traditional indian/thai setting with a comfortable small raunt demeanor.  We tried the mussel appetizer, while the wife got the Tamarind Duck and I tried the Panang Curry with calamari.
  Service was prompt, quick and non invasive.  Mussels were tasty, but the Duck and Curry were to die for!  Portion sizes are definitely reflective of the prices so don't feel like you are going to get gyped.
  We will be back to at least try the sushi or get more duck seeing as they have at least 2 more styles of it.
  Happy tastebuds!
Revise this with your best effort:
I must say, this place is absolutely incredible. Despite our previous indifference towards it, as we drove by the plaza several times, it pleasantly surprised us with its outstanding reviews for crispy duck. 
Upon entering, we were delighted to find a charming traditional Indian/Thai ambiance in a cozy little restaurant. We decided to sample the mussel appetizer, while my wife opted for the Tamarind Duck and I went for the Panang Curry with calamari.
The service was prompt, efficient, and unobtrusive. The mussels were enjoyable, but the Duck and Curry were simply divine! The portion sizes perfectly matched the prices, so you won't feel shortchanged.
We are certainly planning to return, either to try their sushi or indulge in more delectable duck dishes, since they offer at least two additional styles.
Our taste buds were overjoyed!

input:
Went recently for a birthday party and it was certainly worth checking out.   Was my first time there and I was pleased for sure.  

Was nice and quiet as it was a Tuesday and the service was good because of that.  I'm sure it normally is though based on the size of the place.  

I had beef n lobster which both were cooked well and I was happy.  Also the mashed and asparagus that came with it were both very good.  

I wasn't to stoked with the appy we had which was these crab and cheese balls as they were very bland with little crab taste and no real seasoning it seemed.  Maybe just not for me but I wouldn't recommend those. 

Also had Creme Brule which was solid and is get it again for sure.  

Overall I'd say four due to a couple things like the appy and the shaky table, seriously so stupid to have that at a place that nice.  

But I'd gladly go again and would tell friends to try it.
Revise this with your best effort:
I recently attended a birthday party that turned out to be quite an enjoyable experience. It was my first time visiting that particular establishment, and I must say, I was genuinely pleased with the overall experience.

Since it was a Tuesday, the atmosphere was tranquil and serene, adding to the appeal. The service was excellent, most likely due to the smaller crowd. Judging by the size of the venue, I believe the standard of service would be consistently impressive on regular evenings.

For my meal, I opted for the beef and lobster, which were both impeccably cooked and left me feeling content. Accompanying this delightful main course were delectable mashed potatoes and asparagus, both of which were equally satisfying.

However, I must admit that the appetizer we ordered, consisting of crab and cheese balls, failed to amaze me. The flavor was disappointingly bland, lacking the expected essence of crab and any discernible seasoning. While it may simply not resonate with my personal taste preferences, I cannot, in good conscience, recommend that particular dish.

On the other hand, the Creme Brule dessert was an absolute winner, offering a solid and satisfying conclusion to the meal. I would definitely order it again without hesitation.

Overall, my experience warrants a rating of four out of five. A few aspects, such as the underwhelming appetizer and the annoyance of a wobbly table, prevent me from giving a perfect score to such a lovely establishment.

Nevertheless, I would gladly return for another visit and encourage my friends to give it a try.

input: Great ice cream, absolutely terrible service. My son and I went in for ice cream on a Sunday afternoon, so maybe they have their worst staff working on a Sunday. We walked in and were ignored by both people behind the counter. The girl (who seemed drunk) was throwing screwed up napkins around and one of them flew over the counter and hit me. No big deal, but no apology, just more hysterically loud laughter and napkin throwing. The guy noticed my son eyeing the candy and yelled at him not to touch anything. I get it, no one wants sandy little hands in the candy. But he wasn't touching anything, so this was just rude. We stood at the counter and the girl begrudgingly served us, no smile, no greeting, she didn't even look at us. Perhaps she was annoyed we had interrupted her flirting. She ran my card and then turned her back to do some weird dance for her work mate while we stood and waited, more loud shouty laughter. I'm all about a great fun atmosphere and I know I sound like a bore. But when it comes hand-in-hand with a rude attitude towards paying customers, it crosses a line.
Revise this with your best effort:
The ice cream itself was delightful, but unfortunately, the same cannot be said for the service at this particular establishment. On a lazy Sunday afternoon, my son and I decided to treat ourselves to some ice cream. To our disappointment, it appeared that their least capable staff was on duty that day. Upon entering, we were met with complete indifference from both individuals behind the counter. It was as if we were invisible. To make matters worse, the young lady, who seemed to be under the influence, was recklessly tossing crumpled napkins around, one of which landed on me. Though it was a minor inconvenience, instead of offering an apology, she erupted into raucous laughter, completely oblivious to the situation.

To add insult to injury, the gentleman working alongside her admonished my son for merely glancing at the candy display. While I understand preventing the candy from turning into a sandbox for tiny hands, his harsh tone seemed unnecessary since my son hadn't laid a finger on anything. As we patiently waited at the counter, the girl begrudgingly attended to us, displaying no signs of courtesy or professionalism. Both her demeanor and lack of eye contact made it apparent that she resented having to serve us, possibly due to our interrupting her flirtatious interactions. As I handed her my card for payment, she completed the transaction and abruptly turned away to engage in a peculiar dance with her co-worker, leaving us standing there in utter bewilderment and wait. Their boisterous laughter echoed throughout the establishment, further emphasizing their lack of consideration for paying customers.

While I admittedly appreciate a lively atmosphere, it becomes problematic when it comes at the expense of polite and respectful treatment towards customers. The combination of an unpleasant attitude and an unprofessional demeanor takes it one step too far, overshadowing the pleasurable experience of enjoying a delicious ice cream.

input: We visited this place because of its location on the wharf, and because my husband loves seafood. It's tiny, but we were there on a Tuesday evening, and only had to wait a few minutes. We ended up sitting at the bar; it would have been a longer wait for a table outside, since there are so few. Because of its size, it's a little noisy, but not bad. The service was very good. My husband had the crab sandwich, and wasn't impressed. It's served on very uninspiring white bread. I had the fried shrimp, and enjoyed it very much; it was not greasy or heavy, and the shrimp was moist and tasty. There is literally nothing but shellfish on the menu. So, the non-seafood enthusiast (me) was happily surprised to enjoy the shrimp so much (plus good onion rings), but the seafood enthusiast (my husband) didn't love the crab sandwich. If we tried this place again, he would order something else. The location is awesome, so if you like shellfish, definitely give this place a try.
Revise this with your best effort:
We decided to visit this particular establishment due to its prime location on the wharf, and also because my husband has an undying love for seafood. Despite its small size, we were fortunate enough to arrive on a Tuesday evening and only had to wait a brief few minutes. Opting to sit at the bar, as securing a table outside seemed more time-consuming, we embraced the slight noise level that comes with such cozy confines. However, it wasn't overwhelmingly disruptive. The service provided to us was outstanding.

In terms of the culinary experience, my husband ordered the crab sandwich but was ultimately unimpressed. The presentation featured lackluster white bread, leaving much to be desired. Conversely, I selected the fried shrimp and found them to be incredibly pleasing. The preparation was neither excessively greasy nor burdensome, and the shrimp itself was moist and flavorful. It's worth noting that the menu solely focuses on shellfish, which made it even more surprising that as a non-seafood enthusiast myself, I thoroughly enjoyed the shrimp dish. Additionally, the onion rings were commendable. Unfortunately, this did not translate to my seafood aficionado husband, who did not share the same sentiments towards the crab sandwich. If we were to give this place another chance, he would opt for a different selection altogether.

Undoubtedly, the location alone is deserving of praise, making it an ideal destination for shellfish enthusiasts. Should you fall under that category, consider giving this establishment a try, as the overall experience is definitely worthwhile.

input:
If I could give this place zero stars, I would. I had the worst experience when we went today for brunch that I've ever had in a restaurant since I moved to Tucson 7 years ago! First, before even going today, I called to find out what the brunch entailed and when Rosie answered the phone I told her that I had a few questions about brunch, she told me to hold and never came back to the phone. I stayed on hold for 8 minutes at which I called back and spoke to someone else who just seemed like "Oh Well." This brunch was organized by one of my friends, so choice in location was not something I had. We did have a reservation, but were pushed outside because apparently they only planned for one 8 person table and the other table got there a few moments before us and got to choose. The problem with this is that there were two people in our group that are allergic to bees, myself being one of them, and bees were flying all around our table, especially our food. At one point I had to get away from my seat and was not able to return to it for 5 minutes because the one been landed on my waffle and was not leaving. 

At this point my friend and I recognized the danger for the two of us and asked to be moved inside to which we were told "No." When I asked to speak with a manager, I was told "Well, what did you want?" That's when the manager came up, I explained the situation and he was going to put us at one table to which our waitress, gotten by the hostess came up and said to him "I already to her that they could not move in here." What employee talks like that to their boss! The waitress proceeded to run outside and tell the rest of the group that we were moving at which point they decided to stay outside, which was fine by my friend and I, but that meant having to be separated from our friends. This, to me, is deplorable behavior on the side of the the waitress and management. The waitress who was supposed to be our waitress inside as well, never arrived to the table and never checked up on us. Needless to say, I had to get another waiter and he was so appalled with the way that everything was handled he told my friend to not give him a tip. I was so appalled myself, that I did not eat because I just did not want to spend my hard earn money at this establishment any longer. I would never recommend this place to anyone even if they were starving!

input:
I really wanted to like this place and heard about it during lent when I had given up meat. I found myself in the area again and decided to give it a try. I usually don't write reviews until I've been to a place a few times but I think my experience was a complete one. I ordered the special and sampled each type of chicken, the modern BBQ sauce, mac&cheese (which the woman behind the counter was very proud of), 
a bananas foster pie, and the new hope birch beer. After finishing everything, I just wanted my $16.20 back. Individual reviews: 

The chicken: It was very average and that is being generous. It wasn't incredibly flavorful but it wasn't dry so it could have been worse. 

The sauce: It had the tang of a traditional North Carolina BBQ sauce, mustard and vinegar based. I can't eat mayo so I was limited with sauce choices but the mayo sauces were recommended. 

The mac&cheese: Salty and mediocre. It combines all of the things I like but makes a mess doing it. The pasta was well cooked but the cheese and bacon combo made it taste like I just licked salt off of my hand without the nice shot of tequila after. 

The bananas foster pie: The crust of the pie needs no improvement but the filling could use an overhaul. I use the term filling loosely because after biting into the flakey crust, I struggled to find the bananas. There was a thin layer of smashed bananas and cinnamon sugar at the bottom and 75% of the interior was empty space. 

The new hope soda: The birch beer (the actual name of the soda escapes me at the moment but it is birch beer) was the highlight of my meal. Everything you would expect from a Pennsylvania birch beer and very refreshing, which surprised me because I normally don't like fountain sodas and prefer root beer.

I gave this place 2 stars instead of 1 because nothing was horrible.  I think the concept works, the decor is nice, and the menu is good but they need to work on the quality of their food because it currently doesn't match the cost.
Revise this with your best effort:
I had high hopes for this place, especially considering I heard about it during lent when I was abstaining from meat. Finding myself in the area once again, I decided to give it a shot. Although I typically reserve writing reviews until visiting multiple times, my experience here felt complete. I opted for the special, trying out each type of chicken along with the modern BBQ sauce, mac & cheese (which the woman behind the counter seemed particularly proud of), a bananas foster pie, and the new hope birch beer. But after devouring everything, all I craved was a refund of my $16.20. Here's a breakdown of my disappointments:

The chicken: Sadly, it was rather average, to say the least. Lacking in enticing flavors, it managed to avoid being dry, which I suppose is a small consolation.

The sauce: As someone who cannot consume mayo, my options for sauces were limited. However, the mayo-based sauces were highly recommended, so I gave them a shot. The tanginess of the traditional North Carolina BBQ sauce, mustard and vinegar based, was pleasant enough.

The mac & cheese: This dish was just a salty and mediocre mess. While it encompassed all the components I typically enjoy, the combination was executed poorly. The pasta itself was cooked well, but the melding of cheese and bacon left me feeling like I had simply licked salt off my hand, without the desired chaser of tequila.

The bananas foster pie: Crust-wise, this pie was flawless, needing no improvement. However, the filling left much to be desired. I use the term "filling" loosely, as it was a struggle to find any trace of bananas after biting into the flaky crust. The bottom boasted a thin layer of mashed bananas and cinnamon sugar, but a whopping 75% of the interior was an empty void.

The new hope soda: I must say, the birch beer (apologies for momentarily forgetting the actual name of the soda) was the sole highlight of my meal. It delivered everything one would anticipate from a Pennsylvania birch beer – satisfyingly refreshing. This surprised me, as I typically shun fountain sodas in favor of root beer.

I decided to give this place 2 stars instead of 1 because nothing was outright horrible. The concept behind the establishment is appealing, with a pleasant decor and a good menu. However, the food quality falls short of the lofty price tag. Clearly, some work is needed in that department.

input:
Spot on!

I got "the veg" and the spicy fries.  "The veg" is a portabella burger, with grilled mozzarella, picked veg, arugula, and gauc.  Wholly non-cow is this thing spectacular for a bella burger!  The bella is on bottom, then the mozzarella is directly fused on top of that.  I actually thought the cheese was halloumi at first because it wasn't super melted (a good thing). The gauc and pickled veg are slightly citrusy and vinegary, but are contrasted by the bitterness of the arugula.  There's a nice bun to contents ratio, and for bonus points it's a potato bun.

Wasn't sure what to expect with the spicy fries going in - are they hot sauce fries, etc?  Turns out they are of the crab-fries variety with some subtle other spices added in.  Nice portion - not too big.

The atmosphere kind of reminds me of a dive bar - I think that's the best way to describe it.  It's pretty small, so I wouldn't choose to ever eat in most likely.
Revise this with your best effort:
Spot on!

I opted for "the veg," which is a portabella burger topped with grilled mozzarella, pickled vegetables, arugula, and guacamole. Let me just say, this non-cow creation is absolutely phenomenal! Starting with a juicy portabella mushroom as the base, the mozzarella is perfectly fused on top, not overly melted like halloumi. The guacamole and pickled veggies provide a delightful citrusy and vinegary tang, perfectly balanced by the bitterness of the arugula. And to top it all off, the potato bun-to-contents ratio is spot on.

As for the spicy fries, I wasn't quite sure what to expect. Would they be drenched in hot sauce or have other overwhelming spices? Much to my delight, they are reminiscent of crab-fries, with a subtle kick from the added spices. The portion size is just right, not too overwhelming.

Now, let's talk atmosphere. It has an undeniable dive bar vibe, which adds to its charm. It's a bit small, making it less likely for me to choose to dine in, but that doesn't take away from the overall experience.

input:
Being a vegetarian while visiting New Orleans is no easy feat.  However, when I have found eats, they are usually very good.  Tomasito's was below the standard I have gotten used to.  Not to say it was bad, not at all.  I had the chips and a bean and cheese burrito. I would have gotten rice in my burrito but it was not vegetarian (really?).  Service was ok, and the flan was excellent (although "with berries" seems to mean one raspberry).
That being said, at least there was food to eat on the menu, and that is not assumes in New Orleans.
Revise this with your best effort: Being a vegetarian in New Orleans may pose some challenges, but I have managed to find some delicious options during my visits. While I must admit that Tomasito's fell slightly below the high standards I have become accustomed to, it certainly wasn't a bad experience. I opted for the chips and a bean and cheese burrito, though I was surprised to learn that the rice included in the burrito was not vegetarian-friendly (really?). The service was decent, and I must admit, the flan was absolutely excellent, although the description of "with berries" seemed to translate to just one raspberry. Nevertheless, I appreciate the fact that the menu included vegetarian options, as this cannot be taken for granted in New Orleans.
