input:
All I needed was a written estimate.  A rather simple task one would think.  I needed my factory navigation unit in my Denali replaced, and needed to know costs and in writing.  Now this is a normal standard procedure for an auto repair shop.  Let's just assume its bad (it is), so tell me how much it is to remove bad part, and put the new one in.

Jay Fatimo or something like that, said he was very busy, as were the other service writers, so he handed me his card, and said to just email him with what I needed.  Sounded like a good plan, I wasn't in a big rush.  So I did just that, sent a picture of my vin, and the appropriate RPO codes to know what part I needed, and emailed it all to him.  I never got a response.  I tried again about a week or so later, still nothing.  Made sure it is his email at the dealership, etc.  

I guess I have a hard time with taking my car in or trusting a place to do such repairs (3000 dollar job according to Winkel GMC) if they can't even respond to an email.  He knew I would email that day, and I did.  

I guess the GMC dealer right next door gets my money instead.
Revise this with your best effort:
All I needed was a written estimate, a simple task one would expect. I needed my factory navigation unit in my Denali replaced and wanted to know the costs in writing, a standard procedure for an auto repair shop. Assuming it's a bad situation (which it is), I just wanted to know the removal and installation costs for the new part.

A service writer named Jay Fatimo or something along those lines informed me that he was busy, along with the other service writers. He handed me his card and suggested I email him with my requirements. Seemed like a reasonable plan, as I wasn't in a hurry. So I followed his advice, sending him a picture of my VIN and the relevant RPO codes needed to identify the required part. I emailed everything to him, but I never received a response. I tried again after a week or so, but still, no reply. I ensured that I had the correct email address at the dealership and all the necessary details.

It's disheartening to consider trusting a place with such repairs (which Winkel GMC estimated at $3000) or taking my car in when they can't even bother responding to an email. He knew I would email him that day, and I fulfilled my end of the agreement.

I suppose the GMC dealer right next door will be receiving my business instead.

input:
I've been a fan of this place for a long time! Their hazelnut cake is awesome, as are many of their other cakes. I was 'sent' there years ago by recommendation for this signature cake and it more than lived up to it's reputation.

Their butter cookies are awesome -  absolutely love them. I frequently stop in to get cookie gifts to give to family and friends for special occasions - always a huge hit!

I think their prices are right in line with their products. They are always consistently great.

The people that work there are wonderful - friendly and helpful!
Revise this with your best effort:
I have been an avid supporter of this establishment for an extensive period of time! Without a doubt, their hazelnut cake is absolutely incredible, and their assortment of other cakes is equally remarkable. Upon a glowing recommendation from a trusted source, I ventured to this place years ago to indulge in their renowned signature cake, and it unequivocally exceeded expectations.

Furthermore, their butter cookies are truly delectable - I cannot express enough admiration for them. I frequently make a point to visit and procure these delightful treats as gifts for my loved ones during special occasions, and they are always met with resounding appreciation.

In terms of pricing, I find that they strike the perfect balance with their products. Their consistent excellence justifies the cost, making it a fair and reasonable value.

Beyond the delectable treats, the staff members are an absolute delight - embodying warmth, friendliness, and an unwavering willingness to assist. Their presence further enhances the overall experience and perpetuates a sense of belonging.

input:
First time for lunch.  Extensive and flavorful gluten free menu.  

Good lunch and friendly service.
Revise this with your best effort: Experience lunch for the first time at our establishment, where you will be met with an expansive and delectable menu that caters to gluten-free preferences. Indulge in a wide range of flavors that promise to delight your taste buds. Our commitment to providing a satisfying lunch is matched only by our warm and hospitable service, ensuring a pleasant and welcoming dining experience for all.

input:
Service here was excellent. They hosted us for an event and were awesome. 

However, I felt that is where the awesome stopped. The food I had (brisket) was mediocre at best, maybe it had been sitting under lamps all day? The bread it was served on was tough. The mac and cheese was pretty good. My glassware for beer was dirty, chilled, and they were out of everything on draft.
Revise this with your best effort:
The level of service provided at this establishment was truly exceptional. Our event was graciously hosted and I have nothing but appreciation for their efforts. 

Regrettably, my enthusiasm waned when it came to the quality of the food. The brisket I ordered was lackluster, possibly indicating that it had been left under heat lamps for an extended period. Additionally, the bread accompanying the dish was disappointingly tough. On a positive note, the mac and cheese exceeded my expectations and was quite enjoyable. 

To further dampen my experience, the beer glassware provided to me was unclean and improperly chilled. Furthermore, the establishment had run out of every draft option, which was quite unfortunate.

input:
This tour is one to take when you want to have a lazy day, but you want to do a passive activity.  Me & my friends didn't wan the lunch, we just wanted to take a tour of the Mississippi.  The cost was average - around $28.00.  Con:  Remember it is a tour, so they have the typical tourist traps - photographer - me and friends declined that option.  

I would suggest if you aren't going to eat - to pull out your smartphone and research the Natchez Native American Tribe who inhibited the area prior to the colonization of the New Orleans area - interesting "tid bits of rituals", so that made the boat ride more fun because I became the secondary tour leader to my group.  If you are in the mood-go get a drink and this will comfort you as you learn more about the area on a steamboat.  Not a bad way to spend a few hours.
Revise this with your best effort:
This tour is perfect for those seeking a laid-back day with a passive activity. When my friends and I decided to take a tour of the Mississippi, we weren't interested in having lunch. Our main intention was just to enjoy the scenery. The cost of the tour was reasonable, averaging around $28.00. 

One con to keep in mind is that, being a tour, it included the typical tourist traps such as a photographer. However, my friends and I opted out of this option. 

If you choose not to have lunch, I highly recommend using your smartphone to research the Natchez Native American Tribe that inhabited the area before New Orleans was colonized. Their fascinating rituals and tidbits of information added an extra layer of enjoyment to the boat ride, as I became the unofficial tour guide for my group. 

For those interested, grabbing a drink during the tour is a great way to enhance your experience and further immerse yourself in learning about the area while on a steamboat. Overall, spending a few hours this way is definitely a worthwhile experience.

input: Just visited The Fat Ham with my girlfriend about an hour ago. The place is small, but the vibe is nice. Music isn't too loud, the staff welcomed us and the whiskey display is impressive. We couldn't get a table, so we took the two empty seats at the bar. The bartender, Dan, greeted us immediately. Dan was effecient, quick and friendly. Great service. My girlfriend ordered a margarita, which was reasonably priced and tasty. To eat, we ordered the pimento cheese, skillet cornbread, shrimp & grits and the hot chicken. Everything was delicious. The pimento cheese had some heat, and the country bread it is served with gives it a nice touch of salt. The mollases butter on the cornbread was "to die for". The shrimp & grits was my favorite dish. Creamy grits, perfectly cooked and seasoned shrimp. As for the chicken, they do not lie to you. It is hot. The brioche and ranch dressing compliment it well. For desert, we ordered the raspberry cobbler and a coffee. The cobbler was underwhelming. It wasn't bad - just not as great as the previous plates. Elixr coffee was spot on. Overall, I'll be back. Decent price point, high end comfort food and great service.
Revise this with your best effort:
My girlfriend and I recently had the pleasure of dining at The Fat Ham just an hour ago. Although the establishment may be petite in size, it exudes a delightful ambiance. The music played was at a pleasant volume, allowing for easy conversation, and we were warmly greeted by the attentive staff upon arrival. The whiskey display caught our attention with its impressive array of choices.

Unfortunately, we were unable to secure a table, but we were lucky to snag two vacant seats at the inviting bar. It was there that we were swiftly welcomed by the efficient and amiable bartender, Dan. His service was exceptional, as he promptly attended to our needs. My girlfriend opted for a reasonably priced and delicious margarita, while we proceeded to order a medley of mouthwatering dishes.

We indulged in the delectable pimento cheese, accompanied by country bread that provided a subtle touch of saltiness, enhancing the spiciness of the cheese. The skillet cornbread, adorned with molasses butter that was truly heavenly, left us longing for more. The shrimp & grits, however, stole the spotlight as my personal favorite. The creamy grits were flawlessly cooked and paired with shrimp that were seasoned to perfection. As for the hot chicken, it lived up to its fiery reputation. The brioche bun and ranch dressing complemented the spiciness splendidly, creating a harmonious blend of flavors.

For dessert, we opted for the raspberry cobbler, but unfortunately, it left us feeling underwhelmed. While it wasn't terrible, it simply did not reach the same level of greatness as the preceding dishes. However, the Elixir coffee we ordered was a delightful conclusion to our meal, hitting the mark perfectly.

Overall, our experience at The Fat Ham was exceptional, and I can confidently say that I will be returning. The prices were fair considering the high-quality, comforting cuisine offered, and the service was truly top-notch. Do give it a try if you desire a memorable dining experience.

input: When this place first opened we went. We loved the Greek salad and gyros. It was very fresh tasting and the place was cute. We went back last night- the tables were all dirty, lamps full of dirt and dead bugs- so that was a turn off. We got our food and the quality has gone way down. My salad had one bite of potato salad and two items in the salad - tomato and pepper tasted off. I had to spit them out. My daughter got a fajita bowl with chicken. Her tomato was also gross and the chicken was cooked into charred rubber. We ordered baklava and it was stale. I hope they clean and go back to the quality it was when they first opened. It was yummy and clean.
Revise this with your best effort: When this place initially opened, we were thrilled to give it a try. The Greek salad and gyros left a lasting impression on us with their remarkably fresh flavors, and the overall ambiance of the restaurant was pleasant and inviting. However, our recent visit left us quite disappointed. Upon entering, we couldn't help but notice that the tables were visibly dirty, and the lamps were infested with dirt and deceased bugs, which ultimately dampened our enthusiasm. Furthermore, the decline in the quality of the food was apparent. In particular, my salad consisted of only a solitary bite of potato salad and two ingredients - tomato and pepper - both of which tasted peculiar and had to be immediately spat out. Similarly, my daughter's fajita bowl with chicken suffered from a revolting tomato and overcooked, rubbery chicken. To complete our meal, we ordered baklava which turned out to be noticeably stale. It is our fervent hope that the management takes swift action to rectify these issues, restore cleanliness, and reestablish the exceptional quality that the restaurant showcased upon its initial opening. We yearn for the return of the scrumptious cuisine and immaculate hygiene that once defined this establishment.

input: So I hear whispers of a reemergence of brunch I truly believe this is the best brunch spot in New Orleans.  And they only do it once a year. Great local favors. Great service Their so called biscuits and debris should be called the "life changing flavorgasm" at that moment when you realize simplicity and perfection collide; dazed and confused you will awaken your senses at Carrollton market. The oyster good enough French omelet is everything I wanted in life and more. Thank you @Carrolltonmarket I am speechless. And that does not happen often
Revise this with your best effort: I've been hearing whispers about the reemergence of brunch, and I can confidently say that I have found the absolute best brunch spot in New Orleans. This hidden gem only offers brunch once a year, but it is definitely worth the wait. The locally inspired flavors are simply outstanding, and the service is top-notch. One bite of their signature "biscuits and debris" dish will leave you in a state of pure culinary bliss, as the flavors collide perfectly in a symphony of taste. The oyster-infused French omelet is beyond extraordinary; it embodies everything I have ever desired in life and so much more. A heartfelt thank you goes out to Carrollton Market for leaving me utterly speechless with their unparalleled brunch experience. Trust me, it's not often that I am at a loss for words.

input: Great beer selection. Service at the bar was a little slow.
Revise this with your best effort: The beer selection was excellent, offering a wide range of choices. However, the service at the bar could use some improvement as it was a bit slow.

input: Great food... Love the Fish tacos & Nachos are great  it's really a nice atmosphere for family settings and night or dates too.. Music beach bar, home made ice cream  & a little play ground - it's great
Revise this with your best effort: The restaurant offers delicious food, with their fish tacos and nachos being particularly outstanding. Whether you visit with your family or for a romantic date night, the ambiance is perfect. The establishment features a music beach bar, serves incredible homemade ice cream, and even has a charming playground for the little ones. Overall, it's an exceptional place.

input:
O! Wings has the best wings!! Hot momma and the original for the win!! Oh! And the bulgogi wrap. My dad, who's very picky, even praised the wings and wrap! 

Their service and attitude is very very friendly and accommodating. 

I phoned in a to go order originally for 6 people. Later half an hour before the pick up time, I added 10 more entrees. They were very very accommodating and had me ready to go and out the door in 15 minutes! 

Yumm! Can't wait to go back for more!
Revise this with your best effort:
O! Wings undoubtedly reigns supreme when it comes to wings! Their Hot Momma and Original flavors are truly unbeatable, and let's not forget about their incredibly tasty Bulgogi wrap. Even my father, who possesses the most discerning palate, couldn't help but sing praises for their wings and wrap.

On top of their remarkable food, the service and attitude at O! Wings are second to none. The staff exude friendliness and go above and beyond to ensure your satisfaction.

I initially placed a to-go order for a party of six, but as luck would have it, 30 minutes before pickup time, I decided to add an additional 10 entrees. Remarkably, the accommodating staff had my order ready within a mere 15 minutes – talk about outstanding service!

With such delectable offerings and exceptional service, it's safe to say that I cannot contain my excitement to return for more. O! Wings, here I come!

input: Wow!  I just wrote a scathing review about El Patron Pizza in Tampa for leaving unwanted and unwelcome fliers under the door of unsuspecting tourist here in Tampa.  I was going to use a lot of the same issues for this review of New York Pizza Grill, but now I'm not sure what to say, only to say it carefully.  I knew there was something not quite right about the greasy looking punk that was meandering in the hallway of the 4 star hotel where I am currently residing.  As soon as I saw the flier I grabbed my room key and went looking for this person.  In hindsight that was not smart, as soon as I got a look at the guy, I ran for the elevator.  Now, I am no shrinking violet, but this guy looked like he's slap his own mother.  After reading the other reviews on here, I guess I should be happy that this employee didn't turn around and attack!  My biggest issue with this business is that they litter the halls and rooms with these fliers.  They sneak into hotels, a place where you feel safe and after this, I don't.  It doesn't seem to matter where it is a 5 star hotel chain or a family run business.  I did call every one of the pizza place that do this, because I felt bad about complaining to the staff at the hotel, but after yesterdays run in with greasy guy for New York Pizza Grill, I had it.  I do not feel safe and I told management that, and the did call the police.  So, for the employee of New York Pizza Grill, if you get caught stuffing fliers under doors where you are not invited and do not belong, you are more than likely going to be arrested.  So when you are out and about making not enough to keep your car running, ask yourself if your boss will bail you out of jail.  I doubt it, they'll probably just get another less than intelligent person to litter, trespass, annoy and sometimes terrify, hotel staff and their guests.  There are numerous reasons not to eat at New York Pizza Grill, but I'm just tossing out a good reason not to work for them.
Revise this with your best effort: Wow! I must share my displeasure with El Patron Pizza in Tampa for their intrusive flier distribution tactics that have left unsuspecting tourists here feeling unwelcome. I was considering using similar grievances for my review of New York Pizza Grill, but now I find myself unsure of how to approach it delicately. I had an inkling that something was off about the disheveled individual aimlessly roaming the hallway of my four-star hotel where I am presently staying. As soon as the unwanted flier caught my attention, I swiftly grabbed my room key and embarked on a mission to find this person. In hindsight, my actions were not the wisest, as the moment I laid eyes on him, I scurried back to the safety of the elevator. Trust me, I am not easily intimidated, but this individual seemed like he could resort to violence without a second thought. After perusing the other reviews here, I suppose I should be grateful that this particular employee didn't retaliate against me! My major gripe with this establishment lies in their habit of littering the hallways and rooms with these fliers. They surreptitiously infiltrate hotels, which are meant to be sanctuaries, and frankly, I no longer feel secure in this environment. It appears that neither upscale hotel chains nor family-owned establishments are exempt from this invasion. Out of consideration for the hotel staff, I refrained from voicing my complaint directly to them and instead contacted every pizza place engaging in this practice. However, after yesterday's uncomfortable encounter with the greasy individual from New York Pizza Grill, I reached my breaking point. I expressed my concerns regarding my safety to the management, and they took the initiative to involve law enforcement. Therefore, I caution the employees of New York Pizza Grill that if caught trespassing and distributing unwanted fliers, they are likely to face legal consequences. So, the next time you find yourselves struggling to make ends meet, ask yourselves if your employer will come to your rescue when you're behind bars. I highly doubt it; they will probably just find another individual who lacks intelligence to continue littering, trespassing, annoying, and at times, terrifying hotel staff and their guests. While there are numerous reasons to steer clear of New York Pizza Grill as a dining option, I simply present a compelling motive to avoid seeking employment with them.

input:
This was our first time here. I had a coupon so I thought I would try it out. Pulling into the parking lot I noticed it was very busy. I was worried that I would have to wait a long time. I pulled up to the attendant and asked how long it would be for a reg wash. She said each wash takes about 15 minutes. I was surprised since they were busy. I left the car there and proceeded inside. 

The building is huge inside. One side is all windows so you can watch your vehicle move through. They even have a "soap gun" the kids can use to shoot their car. That was a huge hit. 

The cashier greeted me as I walked up to the counter. She took my coupon and handed me a receipt. I walked around while I was waiting. They have drinks she snacks for purchase. They sell lots of greeting cards for every occasion. They have gifts and accessories for your car. The building was cool inside which was great because it was hot the day we came in. I waited about 10 minutes and walked outside. They have a large covered area to wait under. It has some seating so you can sit and wait. After just a few minutes they yelled out my car make to say it was done. I handed the attendant my receipt and tip and I was on my way. Total time was 18 minutes which I think is fair considering they were packed when I arrived. 

The car was clean and vacuumed. Overall they did a great job. The only thing they missed was the front window. It had that haze on it that you notice when the sun hits its. I wiped it off myself. I'm sure they would have fixed it if I noticed before I left. Also, they don't offer free air freshener with the wash like most other places. 

This place was fast and they did a great job. The price was fair and the staff was friendly. I will be coming back soon.
Revise this with your best effort:
This was our first time visiting this establishment, and I decided to give it a try because I had a coupon. As I pulled into the parking lot, I immediately noticed that it was quite busy, which made me concerned about potential wait times. However, upon approaching the attendant, I inquired about the wait time for a regular wash. To my surprise, she informed me that each wash would only take about 15 minutes, despite the high volume of customers. With this information, I left my car with the attendant and proceeded inside.

Inside the building, I was struck by its vastness. One side was adorned with windows, allowing customers to watch their vehicles as they went through the wash. They even had a "soap gun" that children could use to playfully adorn their car, which was a real hit. 

As I walked up to the counter, the cashier warmly greeted me. I handed her my coupon, and she promptly provided me with a receipt. As I waited, I took a stroll around the premises. They offered a range of drinks and snacks for purchase, and I noticed an array of greeting cards suitable for various occasions. Additionally, they had an extensive selection of gifts and car accessories. The building was comfortably cool, which was especially pleasant given the hot weather on the day of my visit. After approximately 10 minutes, I ventured outside to wait in their spacious covered area, complete with seating options. To my delight, after just a few minutes, they called out the make of my car to signify that it was finished. I handed the attendant my receipt and tip, and promptly left. The entire process took a reasonable 18 minutes, considering the establishment was packed when I arrived.

Upon inspecting my car, I found it to be clean and the interior neatly vacuumed. Overall, they did a commendable job. The only minor flaw was the leftover haze on the front window, noticeable when the sun hit it. I took care of it myself, though I'm confident they would have addressed it had I mentioned it before leaving. Additionally, it's worth noting that they don't provide complimentary air fresheners with the wash, unlike most other places.

In conclusion, this establishment proved to be efficient and provided a high-quality car wash. The pricing was fair, and the staff exhibited friendliness throughout. I fully intend on returning in the near future.

input: My go to place in IN when visiting family!  David does the most amazing pink and whites!  The shop is clean and the staff are professional and courteous.  The new management is outstanding (well three years ago but new to me).
Revise this with your best effort: When I visit my family in Indiana, my absolute favorite place to go is David's. Their impeccable pink and white nail services are truly amazing! Not only is the shop exceptionally clean, but the staff also exude professionalism and courtesy. The management, though they have been in charge for three years now (quite new to me), has truly been outstanding.

input:
Ordered curried chicken, teriyaki, and some eggrolls with soup...I never got that order

This was my first and last time ordering food from here. Delivery was quick, I'll give them that, but the order was wrong. When I called in they said I can have a free meal on them for the mistake.

I said, okay "I want that free meal now" (they also offer free delivery for orders over 12.00$) my food came out to 14.87$, 18.87$ with tip.


They refused multiple times (like it'll make a difference if they bring it now or tomorrow, either way it was a lie to get me off the phone). I informed her that if she didn't send her delivery guy back I'll dispute the amount paid to them with my bank, and they'll lose a new customer. 

Normally if one thing in my order was wrong I wouldn't mind at all. It's because my entire order was Wong...
Revise this with your best effort:
Ordered curried chicken, teriyaki, and a side of egg rolls with soup, but unfortunately, my order never arrived as requested. This experience left a lasting impression on me, and I have decided that it will also be my final time ordering from this restaurant. While I must acknowledge their quick delivery service, the fact that they couldn't fulfill my order correctly outweighs any positive aspects.

Upon contacting the restaurant to address the issue, they did offer to provide me with a complimentary meal as compensation for their mistake. I agreed, stating my immediate desire for the free meal. It's worth noting that they also advertise free delivery for orders exceeding $12. However, when they finally provided me with the revised total, it came to $14.87, and after adding a tip, the grand total reached $18.87.

To my disappointment, the restaurant refused my request for the free meal despite their initial offer. Their repeated denial seemed futile, as the timing of their response held no significance. Whether they delivered it immediately or the next day, it appeared to be nothing more than a ploy to get me off the phone.

In response to their refusal, I made it clear that if they didn't send their delivery person back to rectify the situation, I would issue a dispute with my bank to recover the amount paid. I emphasized to them the potential loss of a new customer as a consequence of their actions.

Typically, if only one item in my order was incorrect, I wouldn't mind too much. However, in this case, every single item in my order was wrong. This oversight further intensified my disappointment and highlighted the lack of attention to detail on their part.

input:
A perfect afternoon in the gulch for me would consist of a shopping spree at Blush, a beer at Hops and Crafts and lunch at Turnip Truck.

I mean sure it's an interesting grocery store, but have you tried their ever rotating hot buffet or their made to order sandwiches? 
Tasty!! Or how about some of their all natural beauty products and lip balms? Score!!

You could spend half a day perusing aisle upon aisle of organic fair. This place makes Whole Foods look like Walmart. 

My only complaint: I just wish they would bring back a rewards program of some sort. Guess it was fun while it lasted. 

My usual lunch order; chipotle chicken salad wrap on whole wheat with chipotle mayo.
Revise this with your best effort:
A perfect afternoon in the gulch for me would consist of a delightful shopping spree at the trendy boutique, Blush. After indulging in some retail therapy, I would head over to Hops and Crafts for a refreshing and fulfilling beer. To top off this incredible day, I would treat myself to a scrumptious lunch at the renowned Turnip Truck.

Now, let me tell you about the Turnip Truck - it's not just your average grocery store. While it may first catch your attention with its interesting atmosphere, there's so much more to this place. Have you ever tried their ever-rotating hot buffet? Trust me, each visit is a culinary adventure that will leave you craving for more. And let's not forget their made-to-order sandwiches - a true delight for your taste buds.

But that's not all - the Turnip Truck also offers a range of all-natural beauty products and lip balms. It's a one-stop shop for all your necessities, and you'll be delighted by their quality and selection. Speaking of selection, prepare yourself for an abundance of organic fare as you explore aisle upon aisle. This place makes even the esteemed Whole Foods look like a standard supermarket.

Now, if I were to make a suggestion to the Turnip Truck, it would be to bring back their rewards program. It used to be such a fun perk, and I, along with many others, miss the opportunity to earn some enticing benefits.

As for my go-to lunch order at the Turnip Truck, I can't resist their flavorful chipotle chicken salad wrap on whole wheat, perfectly complemented by their tantalizing chipotle mayo. Each bite is a burst of deliciousness that keeps me coming back for more.

So, if you're seeking the ideal afternoon in the gulch, make sure to include a shopping spree at Blush, a well-deserved beer at Hops and Crafts, and an unforgettable lunch experience at Turnip Truck. You won't be disappointed.

input: Great happy hour.  And brunch.  Only had dinner there once and it was only OK- probably because I ordered something I don't typically eat.  It'll definitely try it again.
Revise this with your best effort: The happy hour at this place is truly fantastic, and they also serve a delightful brunch. While I have only had dinner there once, and it was just alright, I believe that might be because I decided to order something outside of my usual preferences. Nevertheless, I am eager to give it another go soon.

input:
Two co-workers and I came here after flying in from Chicago for an afternoon snack. It was almost 3, so we asked if we could wait until happy hour to order. The place was completely empty while we were there, but the space was well decorated and very open. 

We all ordered cocktails (I got the Mint Julep, which was not great, but then a gin drink that was fantastic), and they were all pretty and tasty. We also ordered Mac and cheese, fries, Brussels sprouts, and a pretzel. I didn't try the sprouts (I really don't like them), but everything else was so good! And the prices during happy hour were a great deal. 

I'll definitely be back next time we go to Reno!
Revise this with your best effort:
After arriving in Reno from Chicago, two of my peers and I sought out a place to grab a quick snack. Since it was nearing 3 o'clock, we kindly inquired if we could hold off our orders until happy hour commenced. Despite the emptiness of the establishment, the ambiance was impeccably adorned and remarkably spacious.

The three of us indulged ourselves with a round of cocktails, of which I opted for the Mint Julep—it failed to meet my expectations. However, my second choice, a gin concoction, exceeded all expectations and left me thoroughly impressed. Alongside our beverages, we delighted in an assortment of delectable dishes, including Mac and cheese, fries, Brussels sprouts, and a pretzel. Regrettably, I abstained from sampling the sprouts due to my personal aversion to their taste, yet every other dish triumphed in terms of flavor and quality. Notably, the prices during the happy hour period provided excellent value for the caliber of food and drinks we enjoyed.

As such, I am already looking forward to my next visit to Reno and would unquestionably revisit this establishment upon returning.

input:
Trying to find a restaurant in The Big Easy that serves vegetarian is not an "Easy" feat

We've encountered many the restaurant who would tell us time & time again that they did not have or *would* not make something to accommodate veggie needs & it was such a letdown.....to this day I still remember 1 guy saying "Vegetarian?  Aww, you gotta get out earrrrrly for *that*".  We still laugh about it....

Well, over the last few years, we're noticing more & more places recognizing veggies like to eat Southern / Cajun comfort food & they are starting to open up their menus to us! ( YAY)

Seeing that Muriel's Jackson Square had such an offering, we made rezzies to ensure we veggies got fed - you'll want to do this too - veggie or not!  They were packed & quoting 2 hr waits & this was at 9pm!

Started w/ drinkys at the bar - Sazerac for the Mr & I had the uber-delish Honey Child cocktail: honey-infused vodka & muddled blackberries.  The Mr liked mine so well that he ordered 1 too, to go w/ dinner & just to be nice, I had another as well so he wouldn't have to drink alone

Their veggie appie had eggplant, of which I'm not a fan so we asked the waitress if they could make their Goat Cheese Crepe, veggie & she said sure.  Since the description said it was topped w/ crawfish, we thought, this would be easy..... but unfortunately, the roulade sauce was made seafood stock. ACK!  Wished you had told us this!  The Mr however, said the crepe was nice & plump, the goat cheese was creamy & smooth & he liked it, barring the sauce

Mains consisted of their Veggie Soiree - this was a sampling of little dollops of veggie tastes - some you'll find on their side dish offerings & some not

Divine beets & roasted acorn squash

Polenta topped w/ chickpeas & a basil sauce - flavorful though those beans were crunchy & could have used a bit more time in the cooker.... same w/ the crunchy wild rice

Yams were very flavorful & had lots of ginger - the Mr got to indulge in both our dollops of chard - I tried a bite & it triggered my dislike for cooked greens

Too full for dessert, we left w/ happy tummies & thankfulness for a nice veggie night out.  A-OK night!
Revise this with your best effort:
Finding a vegetarian restaurant in The Big Easy is no easy feat. We have encountered numerous restaurants that either did not have vegetarian options or were unwilling to accommodate our needs. It was always a disappointment, and we still laugh about the time a guy told us we had to get up early to find vegetarian food. 

However, in recent years, we have noticed a positive change. More and more places are beginning to cater to vegetarians, even offering Southern and Cajun comfort food. One such place is Muriel's Jackson Square, where we made reservations to ensure we would be able to enjoy a meal. We recommend making reservations, regardless of dietary preferences, as they were packed and quoting a two-hour wait at 9pm!

We started our evening with drinks at the bar. My husband had a Sazerac while I enjoyed the delicious Honey Child cocktail, made with honey-infused vodka and muddled blackberries. My husband liked mine so much that he ordered one for himself to accompany dinner. Just to be nice, I had another one so he wouldn't have to drink alone.

We initially asked if their veggie appetizer could be made without eggplant, as it's not my favorite. The waitress kindly suggested their Goat Cheese Crepe, and assured us it could be made vegetarian. However, we were disappointed to find out that the roulade sauce contained seafood stock, even though the description mentioned crawfish. It would have been helpful if they had mentioned this beforehand. Nonetheless, my husband enjoyed the crepe, noting that it was nice and plump with creamy and smooth goat cheese, despite the sauce.

For our main course, we opted for the Veggie Soiree, which consisted of various small servings of vegetarian dishes, including items found in their side dish offerings. We savored the divine flavors of roasted acorn squash and beets. The polenta topped with chickpeas and basil sauce was flavorful, although the beans could have been cooked a bit longer for a less crunchy texture. The same goes for the crunchy wild rice. The yams were bursting with flavor and had a delightful ginger kick. My husband also had the pleasure of enjoying both portions of chard, as I am not a fan of cooked greens.

By the end of our meal, we were too full for dessert, but we left Muriel's with contented stomachs and a newfound appreciation for a satisfying vegetarian dining experience. It was an A-OK night!

input:
I ate at Puckett's yesterday for lunch, and I have to say it was some mighty tasty food for an old-fashioned meat-and-three.  But I actually had a meat-and-two!  Definitely check out the squash casserole.  it was quite the tasty dish.  I'd also recommend their meatloaf, which is what I had.

My only complaint--and it's a minor one--is that they advertise cornbread.  Yes, it's cornbread, but not a slice of cornbread like you typically think of it.  People in the North would call it a corn fritter.  Being from KY, I'd call it a hoe cake.  It's cornbread but more like a cornbread pancake.
Revise this with your best effort:
Yesterday, I indulged in a delightful lunch at Puckett's and I must say, their old-fashioned meat-and-three certainly exceeded my expectations. However, I deviated slightly and opted for a meat-and-two option instead. If you ever find yourself there, don't miss out on their scrumptious squash casserole - it truly left a lasting impression. Another dish I highly recommend is their mouthwatering meatloaf, which happened to be my personal choice.

With regards to my experience, I do have a minor quibble - their advertisement boasts cornbread, but it's not the conventional slice you typically envision. Rather, it leans towards what Northerners would refer to as a corn fritter or, as a Kentuckian like myself would label it, a hoe cake. While it retains the essence of cornbread, it takes the form of a delectable cornbread pancake.

input: I usually stay at The Grand Sierra.  It is where I taught my son to swim years ago, so I have been biased to that property.  However, with it under construction recently, and after they took the horse statues out of the Valet area, and began major construction, I decided to try the Peppermill by a friends suggestion.  The Operations Manager, David Fuller went above and beyond to make my stay unbelievably excellent.  We were met at the hotel and "double" upgraded to a Tuscany Balcony Suite at check-in.  Needless to say, it had a balcony.  Very cool!  The room upgrade started my trip off on a perfect note.  Thank you Peppermill!  I will be back.  My experience was better than expected thanks in part to the staff going the extra mile for us.
Revise this with your best effort: I have typically chosen to stay at The Grand Sierra for many years due to sentimental reasons - it was where I once taught my son how to swim. However, recently, the property underwent construction and significant changes were made, such as the removal of horse statues from the Valet area. Thanks to the staff's willingness to go above and beyond, my experience surpassed what I had anticipated.

input:
Hilton properties are some of the oldest,  most dilapidated properties in the hotel business.  Additionally,  the customer service is the very worst overall with a few exceptions. 
Made a reservation here for 1 bedroom suite.  Suite wasn't ready.  Had a 12:30 lunch mtg  Needed to shower and change but suite booked wasn't ready.  What I thought was a courtesy extend turned out to be bait a D switch.  They gave e me a 'courtesy room' with the understanding that upon my return,  I would get the suite I booked. 
I  returned just to be to told that 'the room I booked had been sold.' Really,???? 
The suite was $250. The downside graded room was $235. I couldn't cancel the room and all of the rooms at a lower rate were 'sold out'  How is that possible so quickly? 
Fake apologies we're given,  but no satisfaction when more could have been done.   Never again.
Revise this with your best effort:
Hilton properties have a reputation for being some of the oldest in the hotel business, potentially in need of renovations. Unfortunately, the overall customer service leaves much to be desired, although there are some exceptions. 

In my recent experience, I had made a reservation for a 1-bedroom suite at a Hilton property. Upon arrival, I was disappointed to find that the suite was not ready, despite having a lunch meeting scheduled for 12:30. I was in desperate need of a shower and a change of clothes, but the suite I had booked was not available.

To my surprise, the hotel offered me a "courtesy room" with the understanding that upon my return, I would be given the suite I had originally booked. However, when I did return, I was informed that the room I had reserved had been sold to someone else. This left me feeling frustrated and incredulous.

The suite I had initially booked was priced at $250, while the inferior room they gave me instead was priced at $235. Strangely, I was unable to cancel the room, and all the other available rooms at a lower rate were supposedly "sold out" in a short span of time, which seemed questionable.

Although the hotel staff offered insincere apologies, their gestures did not bring me any satisfaction. It is clear that more could have been done to rectify this situation, but sadly, it was not. Based on this experience, I have made the decision to never stay at a Hilton property again.

input: Burger was OK, but not at all worth the price. I felt cramped sitting at the long table surrounded by people I did not know. Service was OK. If they brought the prices way down, it would be better. As it is now, it's a really expensive, mediocre burger. There are much, much better places in St. Louis (both in terms of taste and value).
Revise this with your best effort: The burger at this establishment was satisfactory, however, it did not justify the steep price tag. Sitting at the elongated table amidst unfamiliar faces made me feel restricted and lacking in personal space. The service provided was acceptable, but reducing the exorbitant prices would undoubtedly enhance the overall experience. Presently, the burger remains overpriced and merely average in quality. It should be noted that within St. Louis, there exist significantly superior alternatives that excel both in taste and value.

input: We had several quotes, with Pete and Ron's being the best of those I considered reputable. When i told Arbour Bay I was going with Pete and Ron they told me I would be in good hands. Revise this with your best effort: Out of the numerous quotes we received, Pete and Ron's stood out as the most reputable. I was also relieved to observe minimal damage caused by the heavy machinery in my yard. Without hesitation, I will be enthusiastically recommending Pete and Ron's services to my friends and neighbors.

input: I went back here and either I didn't remember the prices  (because someone else had paid last time) or their prices had gone up. It was almost $20 for 2 basic sushi rolls!! While the portions are big, they aren't filling enough to justify such a high price for 2 rolls for lunch. Will not be coming back at those prices.
Revise this with your best effort: Upon returning to this establishment, I was either bereft of recollection regarding the prices (owing to another individual settling the bill previously) or, to my dismay, the prices had indeed escalated. input: Great atmosphere and service! I don't know how often they have live music but the band playing the night we stopped in was very good. Revise this with your best effort: The atmosphere and service at this establishment are exceptional! Regarding the food, it was enjoyable; while I hesitate to claim it as the absolute best burger I have ever tasted, it certainly was not unpleasant. input: We had a 2 1/2 day corporate conference here in the middle of June. The service was excellent, the facilities were very nice and I was fairly impressed with catering. Great spot for conferences or small conventions. Close to the airpor with a complimentary shuttle and complimentary parking.
Revise this with your best effort: In the middle of June, we hosted a remarkable corporate conference at our venue, spanning over 2 1/2 days. input: Yum! input: This is not Middle Eastern food. Side dishes were awfully tasting, including a warmed up rice, which I am sure came from a frozen bag few minutes before it was served.

input:

input:
This place is top notch, with phenomenal service and such fantastic ambiance- how can you go elsewhere? All of the food looked and smelled amazing. I love how creative everything was.
I CANT STOP DAYDREAMING ABOUT THE FOOD. Hands down, best brunch experience of my life. I don't even like french toast usually and theres was by far the most delicious food thats ever entered my mouth. I am literally drooling while writing this.
The chicken and waffles were unreal and standout A++++.

Even the deviled eggs were the best I've personally ever had. They do everything right even when it comes to the music. It was super fun and such a great experience! Ignore any review thats not 4 stars because they must be delusional.

This place is truly exceptional, providing impeccable service and an enchanting ambiance - why would anyone choose to go elsewhere? Every dish presented itself beautifully and emitted irresistible aromas. The sheer creativity displayed in each creation left me captivated.

I find myself incessantly daydreaming about the food, as it was undoubtedly the most remarkable brunch experience I have ever had. Even though I typically do not fancy french toast, their version surpassed any other I have ever tasted, leaving me salivating as I write this.

input: I'm so happy we came upon this place randomly. They have a happy hour 3-8pm everyday:  Half off all beers, $3-$4 glasses of wine & $8 hookah! Their hookah on non-happy hour is $13. They have a wide selection of shisha flavors and even options of an ice chamber or smoking from a fruit bowl (extra charge). They do have a food menu, but I didn't try anything from it. But the plates I saw coming from the kitchen look pretty good. Overall, a really chill place to come and relax with friends. It was definitely an enjoyable experience.
Revise this with your best effort: I am elated that we stumbled upon this hidden gem by chance. What's even better is that they offer a fantastic happy hour from 3-8pm every day. During this time, all beers are half off, glasses of wine range from $3 to $4, and you can indulge in a delightful hookah experience for just $8. On regular hours, the hookah is priced at $13, but fear not, as they offer an array of shisha flavors and the option to enjoy your hookah with an ice chamber or from a fruit bowl, although there may be an additional charge for these enhancements. While I didn't sample anything from their food menu personally, the dishes I observed being served from the kitchen looked incredibly appetizing. As a whole, this establishment provides a relaxing atmosphere that is perfect for spending quality time with friends. Our visit was undoubtedly an enjoyable experience.

input:
I absolutely love this hotel. It is certainly one of my favorites. Upon walking into the building, to your right you will enter the lobby. The lobby is adorable with eclectic decorations and 1 million places to sit that are very comfortable. They serve wine every day from 5 to 6 PM, it's nice to relax down in the lobby with a glass of wine and friendly staff..

Speaking of the staff, they are amazing. Checking in is fantastic, Jasmine and Kayla are the ones I dealt with and they are both wonderful. The hotel concierge Roshid is a very friendly and knowledgeable concierge, they are very lucky to have him on staff. The housekeepers are great, the rooms are immaculate. What I love most about this hotel are the fantastic bathrooms, I'm not sure about the regular rooms, but if you get a king spa room, the bathrooms are absolutely amazing. You have a freestanding tub, and a large shower and you can jump in between the two should you be so inclined ha ha. The decor is so attractive, incredible wallpaper, beautiful rugs, everything seems brand new and they keep it in perfect condition. This hotel is a must for anyone visiting Philadelphia. They make you feel right at home at the moment you step in the door. The pictures that you can get from inside the rooms are enough to make up your whole trip to Philly LOL. But if you want to get out and explore Philly you're only steps away from the Liberty Bell and a historical museum. Right in Center City or the old downtown area, you'll find lots of historical information about Philadelphia.  Definitely stop in and stay at the Monaco, you won't regret it!
Revise this with your best effort:
I absolutely adore this hotel; it is truly one of my favorites. As you walk into the building, you will find the charming lobby to your right. This delightful space boasts eclectic decorations and an abundance of comfortable seating options. To top it off, every day from 5 to 6 PM, they offer a complimentary wine service, allowing guests to unwind and enjoy the company of friendly staff.

Speaking of the staff, they are nothing short of amazing. The check-in process is fantastic, thanks to the exceptional service provided by Jasmine and Kayla. Additionally, Roshid, the hotel concierge, is both knowledgeable and personable, making him a valuable asset to the team. The housekeeping team does a phenomenal job and ensures that the rooms are spotless.

What truly sets this hotel apart, in my opinion, are the stunning bathrooms. While I cannot speak for the regular rooms, the king spa rooms feature absolutely incredible bathrooms. Complete with a freestanding tub and a spacious shower, it is a true luxury to be able to enjoy both at your convenience. The decor throughout the hotel is remarkably attractive, with eye-catching wallpaper, beautiful rugs, and an overall sense of freshness. The dedicated attention to maintaining this level of perfection is commendable.

For anyone planning a visit to Philadelphia, this hotel is an absolute must. From the moment you step through the door, you are made to feel right at home. The photographs captured from inside the rooms alone are enough to make your entire trip to Philly worthwhile, in my opinion. However, if you do decide to venture out and explore the city, you will find yourself just steps away from iconic landmarks such as the Liberty Bell and various historical museums. Situated in the heart of Center City, the old downtown area is also brimming with fascinating historical information about Philadelphia.

Do yourself a favor and make it a point to stay at the Monaco. I assure you, you will not regret it.

input: Love, Love, LOVE this store!!!  I admit, I'm an addict. But where else can you get a Bebe top, a Banana Republic skirt and a BCBG skirt for $4.13?????  The savings are ridiculous!

input: So happy there is a family friendly place to watch football in Carp! Great atmosphere, fast service, delicious pizza.

input: It is what you expect in an Acme, the only thing I found a little different with this one is that it seemed the aisles were a little narrower than in other stores. Store is a little smaller than others so not as wide of a variety, but was fine, looks like they've upgraded some areas like the frozen/refrigerated food sections. Service was fine.

input: We're new to the area, so we're exploring restaurants every weekend. Try the raisin bread or sugar-cinnamon toast. Yum! The cornbread casserole is another dish my wife and I highly recommend. And the service was prompt, attentive and very friendly. Enjoy!
Revise this with your best effort: As newcomers to the area, we've made it a tradition to venture out and discover new restaurants every weekend. In our culinary expeditions, a clear winner has emerged for my wife - The Roost. Her declaration is not taken lightly, as it stems from numerous years of breakfast indulgence, not limited to just this vicinity. The Roost impresses with their masterful baking prowess, crafting delectable breads and pastries in-house. Our personal top picks are the raisin bread and sugar-cinnamon toast, which leave us craving for more. Another standout dish that we enthusiastically recommend is the tantalizing cornbread casserole. To further enhance our dining experience, the service at The Roost is consistently prompt, attentive, and delightfully friendly. Treat yourself and relish in the pleasures this establishment has to offer!

input: Small, crowded and hectic but boy the food was good and plentiful. Wait staff was right on top of the chaos. Great breakfast place.
Revise this with your best effort: Despite its small and crowded setting, the bustling atmosphere at this restaurant was surprisingly lively. However, the real standout of the experience was the impeccable quality and generous portions of the food. The wait staff skillfully managed the chaos, ensuring a seamless dining experience. Without a doubt, this is a fantastic spot for a delicious breakfast.

input: Finally went in after walking by so many times. Glad we did. Small place but IR is pleasing to the eye. One wall cover with wood palates and subtle two tone gray walls. Started with the prosciutto fig arugula Parmesan flatbread appetites. Enough for two people and delicious. Nice mix of flavors. Main dishes were a burger grass fed beef with fries coated with truffles dusting. Burger was humongous!  Looked good smelled good and tasted good. I had a seafood soup with fish ( not sure what it was) shrimp and mollusks in a  coconut/ curry broth. Deliciously spicy but not enough to kill your taste buds. Overall I would recommend this place. We went early as we heard it gets crowded and they do not take reservations.  BYW great wine and craft beer selections
Revise this with your best effort: We finally decided to step inside after passing by numerous times, and we were delighted that we did. Though small in size, the interior design is visually pleasing. One of the walls is covered in wooden palates, complemented by subtly shaded gray walls. To start off our dining experience, we ordered the prosciutto fig arugula Parmesan flatbread appetizer, which proved to be more than enough for two people and absolutely delicious. The combination of flavors was outstanding. For our main dishes, I opted for the grass-fed beef burger served with truffle-dusted fries. The burger itself was incredibly substantial, both in appearance and taste. It looked appetizing, smelled delightful, and certainly lived up to its promising flavors. I chose to have the seafood soup, which consisted of an assortment of fish, shrimp, and mollusks in a delightful coconut and curry broth. The spicy element was just right, providing a tantalizing kick without overwhelming the taste buds. Overall, I confidently recommend this establishment. We arrived early, having heard of its tendency to become crowded, especially since they do not take reservations. Additionally, I must mention their impressive selections of wine and craft beer.

input:
Reading the reviews, I cannot agree with the others which tout the quality of the food. I had the dinner buffet and the food was mediocre at best. The selection was fine, though they do charge a higher price if you want crab legs. BTW- neither Easy Buffet nor Ginger Buffet charge extra for crab legs. The flavors were there, but the meats were dried out, concentrated, and fried foods soggy and tough as if the they hadn't been turned over in hours and were just sitting on the steam table.  

Service was very nice but slow, especially since there were only 3 tables going the whole time we were there.  I think they had him responsible for too many things other that waiting tables.  

There is a slim chance I'll come back since there are 3 other Chinese buffets in the area that I prefer over Dragon.  Perhaps if I do, there will be more guests to turn over the food and I can update my ratings.
Revise this with your best effort:
After reading the reviews, I am unable to agree with the positive comments regarding the food quality. My personal experience with the dinner buffet was disappointing, as the food was, at best, mediocre. While the selection was satisfactory, it should be noted that there is an extra charge for crab legs, contrary to what has been mentioned in previous reviews, both at Easy Buffet and Ginger Buffet. The flavors were present; however, the meats were dry, concentrated, and the fried foods were soggy and tough, as if they had been left untouched for hours on the steam table.

On the plus side, the service was friendly, although quite slow. This was especially noticeable considering there were only three occupied tables during the entirety of our visit. It appeared that the waiter had been assigned numerous tasks beyond waiting tables, which likely contributed to the delays.

Considering there are three other Chinese buffets in the vicinity that I prefer over Dragon, the likelihood of me returning is slim. Perhaps, if I do decide to give it another chance, there will be more guests present to ensure the food turnover is more frequent, allowing me to reassess and update my ratings accordingly.

input: This is our "go to" place! The food is consistently good and we always have friendly attentive waiters to sometimes help with our decisions. One of our favorites is the pasta pockets with pear filling. Really delicious! It's also byob which is always a plus. This is a great restaurant with a real cozy, family atmosphere. Highly recommend.
Revise this with your best effort: This place is undoubtedly our favorite go-to spot! The quality of food is consistently exceptional, and we never fail to receive excellent service from the friendly and attentive waitstaff who are always willing to assist us in making our dining choices. One particular dish that stands out for us is the pasta pockets filled with delectable pear filling – it is truly a mouth-watering delight! Additionally, the fact that it is a BYOB establishment is always a bonus. Without a doubt, this restaurant exudes a warm and inviting family atmosphere, which enhances the overall dining experience. We wholeheartedly recommend this esteemed establishment to anyone seeking a fantastic culinary adventure.

input: To sum it up, it's an average bar with ties to a very well-known TV show - but that fact doesn't make the food or much else better. When I went they had $4 White Rascal's and on top of that I had the normal gravy fries. $11 for fries, steep to say the least. They were steak fries, covered in gravy and mozzarella cheese and while pretty damn good, I would be hesitant to say that they're worth the price. Service was good, sometimes a little slow, but still friendly.
Revise this with your best effort: In summary, this bar is mediocre despite its association with a popular TV show. The quality of the food and other aspects do not improve due to this fact. During my visit, they offered $4 White Rascal's, which was a positive point. Additionally, I tried their regular gravy fries priced at $11, which I found excessively expensive. Although they were tasty with steak fries, gravy, and mozzarella cheese, I question if they truly justify the high price. The service was generally good, albeit occasionally slow, but the staff remained friendly.

input: I went here based on the Yelp reviews and found everything to be true. The staff is extremely helpful and willing to answer all questions. I will continue to bring my bike repair/maintenance needs here.
Revise this with your best effort: I decided to visit this place after reading some positive Yelp reviews, and I must say, everything I read turned out to be absolutely true. The staff here is exceptionally helpful and always ready to assist with any inquiries. I am genuinely impressed with their willingness to answer all my questions. Needless to say, from now on, I will exclusively trust this establishment with all my bike repair and maintenance requirements.

input: A very nice hotel and a good value. ($175/night) The king bed was primo, the room tastefully furnished. The  rotating Carousel bar is fun and the pool at the top of the building is a great way to cool off on a 95 degree day.We stay there given the great location in the French  Quarter, but our room facing Royal St. was very loud, especially on Friday night. Try for a room not facing the street if you are there over a weekend. Make sure they remove the extra $60 per night they tack on to your room charge for incidentals.
Revise this with your best effort:
The hotel presents itself as an exquisite establishment while also offering attractive rates, with a nightly fee of $175. Our experience was further enhanced by the presence of a comfortable king bed and tasteful furnishings that adorned the room. As a delightful addition, the rotating Carousel bar provided an enjoyable atmosphere, and the rooftop pool served as a perfect respite during sweltering 95-degree days.

Undoubtedly, the hotel's location in the vibrant French Quarter made it an ideal choice for our stay. However, it is important to note that our room, overlooking the bustling Royal St., proved to be quite noisy, particularly on Friday nights. If your visit includes a weekend stay, it would be wise to request a room that does not face the street.

Additionally, we must caution against an unexpected charge of an extra $60 per night, seemingly added for incidental expenses. We kindly advise you to ensure its removal from your room bill, as it may come as an unwelcome surprise.

input: the handmade orangina is delicious-better than the bottled version! and the croissant sandwiches are amazing!
Revise this with your best effort: The freshly made Orangina is absolutely delightful - surpassing the bottled variant in taste! Moreover, the croissant sandwiches are simply outstanding!

input: We have great food every time we are here. Great milkshakes, ice cream, Chicago dogs, and cheese fries. Super affordable and delicious!
Revise this with your best effort: Every visit here never fails to offer us delicious food. The milkshakes, ice cream, Chicago dogs, and cheese fries are all exceptionally satisfying. Moreover, the prices are incredibly reasonable without compromising the quality and taste.

input: the foods great, but no buflight on tap.i love the servers there , especially Jamie White, whose the best server. But again. Lack of Bud light is a big negative

input: If I'm basing my rating on the taste and quality of the food, then I must give it a five star rating! I did not mind the atmosphere, which admittedly leaves a bit to be desired. input:
I have been coming here for about a year now and this last week was my 5th visit. I live in the Bay Area. I'm a player card member so they send me free room or discounted room offers all the time. This is a very nice hotel/ casino. Never had a bad experience. Love that I can check in online before getting to to hotel and just use the express kiosk when I get there to get my room keys and avoid the long line,  LOVE THAT! The rooms are always nice and clean and comfortable. The last 2 rooms I have stayed in had views of the pool which was nice! 
The pool is very nice and relaxing and never too crowded. The spa Toscana is very nice but a bit pricey. None of the restaurants I have tried there so far have been great but I haven't tried to steakhouse or Chi yet, so I haven't had the full experience yet. The slots are never too crowded when I go and can usually get on the machines I like to play with little to no delay. 
I enjoy visiting here. I will keep returning as long as they keep sending me sweet offers!!
Revise this with your best effort: I have been regularly visiting this hotel/casino for approximately a year now, and my most recent visit marked my fifth time. As a resident of the Bay Area, I greatly appreciate being a player card member as it allows me to receive frequent complimentary or discounted room offers. This establishment truly lives up to its reputation as a fantastic hotel/casino. Without exception, I have not encountered any negative experiences during my visits. One feature that particularly stands out for me is the convenience of checking in online prior to arriving at the hotel. The express kiosk has been a wonderful addition, as it expedites the process of receiving my room keys and allows me to skip the long line. I absolutely LOVE this aspect! The rooms themselves are consistently delightful, always impeccably clean, and provide a comfortable atmosphere. Moreover, the two recent rooms I stayed in offered beautiful views of the pool, which added to my overall enjoyment. Speaking of the pool, I must emphasize that it is a truly serene and relaxing area that thankfully never becomes overly crowded. On the other hand, the spa Toscana, while undeniably luxurious, can be a bit costly. Regarding dining experiences, I must admit that none of the restaurants I have tried thus far have left a lasting impression. However, I have yet to experience the steakhouse or Chi, so I have not fully explored the culinary offerings. Thankfully, when it comes to the slot machines, I have never faced significant delays or overcrowding, allowing me to easily find and play my preferred games. Overall, I genuinely enjoy my visits here and fully intend to continue returning as long as they continue to extend such appealing offers my way!

input: I had a most-delicious bagel sandwich this morning - pork roll, egg and cheese on an everything bagel. The price was very fair - $4.23 - and the bagels are made on site each day. They seem understaffed so hopefully they get some more staff to keep up with the crowds.
Revise this with your best effort: This morning, I indulged in an absolutely delectable bagel sandwich that left me thoroughly satisfied. Picture this - a tantalizing combination of pork roll, perfectly cooked egg, and a generous amount of cheese, all comfortably nestled within the divine embrace of an everything bagel. Not only was this mouthwatering experience a complete delight, but the cost was also surprisingly reasonable, a mere $4.23. To my utmost pleasure, these delectable bagels are prepared fresh on-site every day, ensuring an unrivaled level of freshness. input: Warning, if you come here on a Sunday there is a set tasting menu.  We were a party of two, they served us with one plate, "family style".  The only problem is the woman next to us was a party of one and had the same size servings.  They are claiming family style but giving the same portions they give to one person to multiple people. My advice, make sure you request being served as one person with separate plates.  The food was delicious but the business aspect was unacceptable.  Will not come back.
Revise this with your best effort: Warning: Please be advised that if you choose to visit this establishment on a Sunday, they offer a fixed tasting menu. During our recent visit as a party of two, we were served a single plate presented "family style." Our unfortunate experience was further compounded when we noticed that the lady seated beside us, dining alone, received equally-sized portions. Despite claiming to follow a family style approach, the restaurant seemed to be providing the same shared portions to both solo diners and groups. It would be prudent to ensure that you explicitly request individual servings on separate plates if you decide to dine here. Although the food itself was undeniably delicious, we found this aspect of their business practice to be completely unacceptable. Consequently, we do not intend to return.

input: Wonderful place, if you haven't checked it out!  Went there for a pizza making class. input: Great vegetarian and organic menu, friendly and helpful staff and delicious coffee! I'm definitely coming back

input: Eh, crust was dry and we got the Delmar which instead of pizza sauce they use bbq sauce however they barely put any on the pizza which caused it to be dry. The server was good. The pizza took forrrevvverrr to come out though we had been done with our salads for 20-30 minutes.

input: Overpriced and underwhelming.  Had the sausage/egg:cheese sandwich this morning on whole grain $4.89. Sausage was cold and the sandwich was about 1/2 the size of the picture on the menu. input:
I came here because of the higher rating and they accepted my insurance. My initial visit went well, no complaints on the staff or the doctor at that time. 

They switched my brand from Acuvue to Air Optix and about 2 weeks after using the contact I started to experience pain, redness and irritation. I took my contacts out that evening and had red rings around both of my eyes. I tried contacting them via telephone and left a message as well as email, I failed to hear back from them in a timely manner so I reached out to them again and got ahold of them. I simply wanted my contacts switched back to Acuvue and they tried to tell me that it was allergies causing my problems and were insisiting on me keeping Air Optix. Eventually I did get them to agree to switch my contacts back to acuvue. 

In march I had another eye irritation and I went to Vanderbilt Eye Institue, they told me it was a continued reaction to the Air Optix lenses because I did not give my eyes enough time to heal before applying my new contacts - which was I was not educated on by Music City Optical when I got my new set of contacts. I then reviewed them on facebook at that time. 

Today (8/30/16) I recieved a response to my review on facebook and a corresponding email stating that I was being slanderous and lying, which was not the case at all. I was simply explaining my experience with Music City Optical.
Revise this with your best effort:
I chose to visit Music City Optical based on their high rating and acceptance of my insurance. During my initial visit, I had no complaints about the staff or the doctor. However, they switched my contact brand from Acuvue to Air Optix, and after about two weeks of using the new contacts, I started to experience pain, redness, and irritation in my eyes. Concerned, I removed the contacts that evening and noticed red rings around both eyes. I tried to contact Music City Optical through phone and email, but unfortunately, they did not respond promptly. Frustrated, I reached out to them again and finally managed to get in touch. All I wanted was to switch back to Acuvue, but they insisted that my problems were due to allergies and tried to convince me to keep using Air Optix. Eventually, I succeeded in persuading them to switch me back to Acuvue.

In March, I experienced another eye irritation and visited Vanderbilt Eye Institute. They informed me that my ongoing reaction was indeed caused by the Air Optix lenses, and the reason for this was that I had not given my eyes enough time to heal before switching to the new contacts. Unfortunately, Music City Optical had not provided me with this information when I obtained the new contacts, leading to my negative experience with them. Consequently, I posted a review on their Facebook page at that time.

Just today, on August 30, 2016, I received a response to my Facebook review and an accompanying email stating that I was making slanderous and false statements, which is not at all the case. I was merely sharing my honest experience with Music City Optical.

input:
This wasn't my first visit to the Italian Centre, but my last visit was many years ago and all I could remember was the huge selection of charcuterie and cheeses. Slightly overwhelming to say the least, meats and cheeses (at the time) I had never even heard of. With some guidance from the staff I was able to select some delights. 

Fast forward a few years... 

My most recent visit was only for some pastries and a quick lunch, so I didn't have time to browse the huge selection of Italian delights. 

I decided to go with the Mossimo pizza. The toppings were fresh the cheese was bubbly! The crust was thin and baked to perfection. I wasn't expecting such a huge pizza- definitely big enough to share! And priced at just $14? A steal if you ask me!

For pastries we chose the Cream Horns; while they were quite pricy, they were certainly delicious. Likely made that day, they were fresh, creamy and flakey! Impossible not to over indulge! 

While visiting the Italian Centre I suggest enjoying a freshly crafted coffee beverage and a pastry. The perfect treat before or after shopping.
Revise this with your best effort:
My previous experience at the Italian Centre wasn't my first, but it had been quite a long time since my last visit. All I could recall from that visit was the overwhelming variety of charcuterie and cheeses. It was a sensory overload with unfamiliar meats and cheeses that I had never even heard of. However, the helpful staff provided guidance and assistance in selecting some delectable options.

Fast forward a few years...

During my most recent visit, I had limited time and was solely focused on getting some pastries and a quick lunch. Consequently, I didn't have the opportunity to explore the extensive array of Italian delights available. Nonetheless, I opted for the Mossimo pizza and it exceeded my expectations. The toppings were incredibly fresh, the cheese melted to perfection, and the thin crust was flawlessly baked. To my surprise, the pizza was massive, easily suitable for sharing! And priced at just $14, it was an absolute steal!

As for the pastries, we decided to indulge in the Cream Horns. Although they were a bit on the pricier side, they were undeniably delicious. It was evident that they were made on the same day, as they were incredibly fresh, creamy, and delightfully flakey. It was practically impossible not to overindulge in these delightful treats!

If you find yourself at the Italian Centre, I highly recommend treating yourself to a freshly crafted coffee beverage alongside a scrumptious pastry. It serves as the perfect indulgence before or after your shopping experience.

input:
It saddens me to say this but I think I need a new nail salon. I have consistently come here for a few years now and the service has never been as bad as it has been the last few times I've been here. Here are my issues:

1) the girl at the front desk never once looked up from her papers while "greeting" me and asking me what I want. She mumbled under her breath to go pick out a color then yelled across the salon that I was getting a mani and pedi. 
2) once I picked out my color I went back to the front and someone who came in after me was seated in a pedi chair, water turned on etc. to get service. Once she saw that I was standing in the front she got a chair going for me. The problem with that is there were no more nail technicians available to work on me.
3) so now I'm sitting in cold water waiting for someone to come and do my feet. 
4) the pedicure started, she painstakingly dug into my toes (which I absolutely hate) and rushed through the Massage part of the pedi
5) after it was all said and done, I find out that their prices have gone up! 

I used to come here because they have later hours and are open on Sunday's but after a 3rd terrible experience here I am not coming back. In the last 3 months, almost the whole staff has changed and these folks are not meeting my needs.
Revise this with your best effort:
Unfortunately, I am saddened to admit that I believe it is time for me to find a new nail salon. Over the past few years, I have been a loyal customer here, but the recent experiences have been consistently disappointing. Here are a few issues that have led me to this decision:

1) Upon entering, the girl at the front desk appeared disinterested, barely acknowledging my presence as she focused on her paperwork. She mumbled instructions to choose a color and loudly announced to the entire salon that I was requesting a manicure and pedicure.
2) After selecting my color, I returned to the front desk only to realize that another customer who arrived after me had already been seated in a pedicure chair with water running. It was only when she noticed me standing there that she hurriedly arranged a chair for me. Unfortunately, this left no available nail technicians to attend to me.
3) Consequently, I found myself waiting in cold water, unsure when someone would finally attend to my feet.
4) The pedicurist, impatiently and uncomfortably dug into my toes, disregarding my dislike for such a treatment, and hurried through the massage portion of the pedicure.
5) Adding to my disappointment, I discovered that the salon had raised its prices without any prior notification.

While I originally chose this salon due to its convenient hours and Sunday availability, the consistently negative experiences I have encountered in the last three months, coupled with the recent high turnover among the staff, have forced me to seek a new establishment that can better cater to my needs.

input: Boulevard Pizza is our go to place in the Sparks/Reno area. It looks like the decor has not changed since 1985, but who cares when they serve you a pizza this delicious! They have some fun arcade games for the kids.

input: I was very impressed! I had a plain glazed and a glazed with a lemon filling. I would go back again if I ever find myself in Indy.

input: Great job first day open packed but well organized me and my family will be back multiple times a week. Thanks for coming to reno.

input: This are awesome and so good! I love the BBQ pork one the best. The staff is so friendly. This is my first dive into Vietnamese cuisine and now I def. want to try more! These jalapenos are fresh, not pickled, and occasionally come with seeds which adds an extra kick of spiciness that I absolutely enjoy. Don't waste any more time, head to Baguette Deli now!

input: I eat here at least once a month, and more often when possible.  The brisket tacos and brisket quesadillas are fantastic.  Happy hour starts at 3 if you're interested in a late lunch for 2-for-1 drinks.
