input:
This place has a great location for the hungry tourist. It manages to be edgy yet chill at the same time. My reason for stopping in was to try the ahi fish tacos with avocado relish, which sounded awesome. At around 3 there was still a healthy amount of people attesting to its popularity and eatability. They had a selection of local microbrews (bottle, not draft) for those interested in getting a taste of Philly in beer form. Alas, I ordered my tacos, but had a little Scooby Doo moment when the arrived. Somehow the chef decided that it was okay to put such a delicate fish in premade taco shells...enough to makes this SoCal girl wince a little and question whether I should consume. Luckily the flavor of the fish was great. I only saw one half inch cube of avocado, but at least the sauce was yummy! 
I got a glimpse of the brunch menu...looks pretty tasty I must say...
Revise this with your best effort: This place is a fantastic spot for hungry tourists, boasting an ideal location. It effortlessly combines an edgy and relaxed atmosphere. My motivation for stopping by was to try their highly anticipated ahi fish tacos with avocado relish, which sounded absolutely amazing. Even at around 3 o'clock, there was still a substantial crowd, demonstrating its popularity and delicious offerings. They also had a noteworthy collection of local microbrews available in bottles, allowing beer enthusiasts to savor the essence of Philadelphia. Unfortunately, when my tacos arrived, I had a moment akin to Scooby Doo's perplexity. The chef surprisingly decided to use premade taco shells for such delicate fish, causing even this SoCal girl to cringe and question whether or not I should proceed. Fortunately, the fish itself had incredible flavor. Although I only found a small cube of avocado, the sauce was delectable. As I caught a glimpse of the brunch menu, my taste buds were enticed by the appealing options it held.

input: OMG! Breakfast pizza and bottomless mimosas and bloody marys. Is there anything better in this world? Even got a handshake on the way out the door. Service like that seems scarce these days

input: I love Bing's boba!!!!!!!!! The Taro snow is my go to drink. Definitely the best boba spot in Tucson! The place is always clean. They have board games for you to play. input: Venus nail is great. I was looking for a new salon and googled some in my area. I've been 3 times now and they've been amazing. Great atmosphere and service. Ask for Ivy she's fantastic. I told her I was going on a trip for my bday and to come up with something. I walked out with this and loved it all.
Revise this with your best effort: Venus Nail is absolutely fantastic! After conducting a thorough search for a new salon in my area, I stumbled across their name and decided to give it a try. I have now been there three times, and each visit has been nothing short of amazing. The salon exudes a wonderful atmosphere, and the service provided is top-notch. input:
Not really the town you would expect to find a great Indian restaurant, but figured I'd give it a shot.
I'm picky about Indian food, and all I can say is WOW it's good!
The Naan with peach chutney was amazing.
The Lamb Korma was perfect. Perfect amount of spice (too many Indian restaurant set your mouth on fire and you can't enjoy the taste). Not too much, not too little.
The rice and lamb was perfectly cooked. Very authentic.

The decor is very nice (those chairs in the front are impressive) and staff very friendly. Service was also very quick.

I'm relocating to Tampa, and might actually have to make the drive from there a few times to come back. Very impressive!

I would definitely recommend this place, even if it's a bit of a drive.  It's worth it.
Revise this with your best effort:
This town may not be the first place you'd think of when looking for a top-notch Indian restaurant, but I decided to take a chance anyway. As someone who is quite particular about Indian cuisine, I was in for a pleasant surprise. The flavors were absolutely delightful!

One dish that truly stood out was the Naan with peach chutney. It was a remarkable combination that left me in awe. The Lamb Korma was also impeccably prepared, with just the right amount of spice. Unlike many other Indian restaurants that overwhelm your taste buds with fiery heat, this place struck the perfect balance. The rice and lamb were cooked to perfection, lending an overall authentic touch to the entire meal.

Moreover, the interior decor was impressive, especially those stunning chairs near the entrance. The staff members were friendly and provided excellent service, ensuring a speedy dining experience.

Even though I will be relocating to Tampa soon, I am seriously considering making the drive back here on multiple occasions. That's how impressed I am with this place!

If you're willing to drive a little bit, I absolutely recommend giving this restaurant a try. Trust me, it's worth the journey.

input:
Have you ever tried a new lunch place and liked it so much that you went back for dinner that night and lunch the next day. I have done the back to back to back only once, at Greko. 

I've love the rotisserie chicken pita with fries. If you are in the mood for something healthier, they have great salads. Definitely try the Horta Greens (you can substitute fries for Horta Greens or have them on the side). The perfectly cooked and seasoned greens are delicious. 
I also love the Athenian Chicken (half a rotisserie chicken). 

As a quick, casual, food-first restaurant, Greko has hit the sweet spot.
Revise this with your best effort:
Have you ever experienced the joy of discovering a new lunch spot that was so amazing, you couldn't resist going back for dinner the very same night and even indulging in lunch the following day? Well, I must confess, I have only experienced this incredible back-to-back-to-back dining extravaganza once, and it was at none other than the fabulous Greko.

Let me tell you, their rotisserie chicken pita adorned with a side of delectable fries has truly captured my taste buds. It is a harmonious symphony of flavors that leaves me craving for more. And for those seeking a healthier alternative, fear not, for Greko offers an array of extraordinary salads. One that particularly stands out is their Horta Greens, which can be marvelously substituted for fries or served alongside. Trust me, the impeccably cooked and spiced greens are an absolute delight to savor.

Moreover, the Athenian Chicken, a mouthwatering half a rotisserie chicken, holds a special place in my heart. Every succulent bite is a testament to Greko's culinary prowess.

Greko, with its emphasis on quick, casual dining while placing food at the forefront of its priorities, has undeniably struck a chord. The charming and laid-back ambiance coupled with the exceptional quality of their dishes makes it a true haven for food enthusiasts like myself.

input:
Brother Rabbit you are young, hip, and tasty!

Met friends for drinks and an early dinner. I was the first to arrive so I sat at the bar and ordered the house cider which is great and I followed that with the Oban 18 which is phenomenal so try it while you're there. 

Our dinner kicked off with the most amazing house biscuits and butter that will have you begging for the recipe.

The rest of our dinner was comprised of several selections from the First course menu. We had the daily oysters which were great. Followed by the Brussels sprouts, delicious but the crispy chicken skins were a bit of a let down, they needed more flavor. 

The smoked tuna tartar is great but the sweet chips can overwhelm the dish. Definitely get the marinated shrimp and jalapeño jus it is a wonderfully fresh and bright dish. 

To close thing up we had the dobeger cake with lemon curd and chocolate ice cream, as if that wasn't enough they pour this amazing chocolate sauce on it when it arrives that will have you just dying as you wait to dig in.

Overall Compere Lapin is a great addition to the New Orleans food scene, great for groups or date night with your significant other.
Revise this with your best effort:
Hey Brother Rabbit, you embody youth, coolness, and deliciousness!

I caught up with some pals over drinks and an early dinner. Being the first to arrive, I settled at the bar and indulged in the fantastic house cider. I then treated myself to the absolutely incredible Oban 18, a must-try if you ever stop by.

Our feast commenced with the most heavenly house biscuits and butter that will make you crave the recipe like there's no tomorrow.

For the remainder of our meal, we dived into various selections from the First course menu. The daily oysters were delightful, followed by the Brussels sprouts which were delicious, though the crispy chicken skins left something to be desired in the flavor department.

The smoked tuna tartar was fantastic, although the sweet chips tended to overpower the dish. Don't miss out on the marinated shrimp and jalapeño jus—it's a wonderfully refreshing and vibrant creation.

To top it all off, we couldn't resist the dobeger cake with lemon curd and chocolate ice cream. As if that weren't enough, they serve it with an irresistible pour of luscious chocolate sauce, leaving you eagerly awaiting your first bite.

All in all, Compere Lapin is an exceptional addition to New Orleans' culinary scene—a perfect spot for group gatherings or a romantic date night with your special someone.

input:
Here for convention and Imo's was suggested as "The Best" St. Louis Style pizza by hotel staff. 

I opted for delivery which was good and efficient. The food arrived still hot. I ordered a medium pepperoni and an order of toasted ravioli. 

Now, I knew the cheese on the pizza was provel so it would taste different. I was really not impressed. It may just be a matter of taste preference. It was hard to separate each piece of pizza too.  Like, it wasn't cut all the way through. Not really a fan. So thumbs down on the pizza. 

What bumps the stars up are the T-Ravs!  I was hoping for cheese ravioli but the staple is a meat mixture. Boy...do they do it justice. They were the bomb!  The sauce with it was too watery but still tasty. I would order just the ravioli next time!
Revise this with your best effort:
While attending a convention, I was recommended Imo's as the epitome of St. Louis Style pizza by the hotel staff. Opting for delivery, I was pleased with the prompt and efficient service as the food arrived still piping hot. My order consisted of a medium pepperoni pizza and a side of toasted ravioli.

Having prior knowledge that the pizza would feature the unique provel cheese, I was prepared for a different taste experience. However, I must admit that I was not particularly impressed. It could be a mere matter of personal preference, but I found it challenging to separate each slice as the pizza was not entirely cut through. This aspect detracted from my overall enjoyment, making me lean towards being unenthusiastic about it. Hence, I would have to give the pizza a thumbs down.

However, the true stars of the meal were the toasted ravioli! Having anticipated a cheese filling, I was surprised to discover a savory meat mixture instead. Let me tell you, they absolutely nailed it. The T-Ravs were simply superb, exceeding my expectations on all levels. The accompanying sauce, albeit a bit watery, still possessed a tasty flavor. If I were to revisit Imo's in the future, I would solely order the ravioli, for they truly stole the show.

input: I have groen up eating Italian food and i have not come across a more legit place than Mazzaros! Love their sauce and meatballs.
Revise this with your best effort: Having grown up eating Italian food, I have yet to discover a more authentic place than Mazzaros! Their sauce and meatballs are absolutely delightful.

input: Okay, so it's a dance club. It's trendy and offers higher-end cocktails and beers while still offering your run-of-the-mill wells and domestic bottles. On certain nights, guys have to pay a door charge (but that's not really uncommon in the industry). There is a huge patio and, even in the winter, almost the entire patio is still available because they enclose it. The music is pretty hit-or-miss...sometimes you're dancing away to classic hip-hop, pop, and even rock, and other times you're standing there while the DJ spins out an un-danceable tune. If you're on the patio, you can chat...but if you're inside it's (not shockingly) too loud to really talk. If you're in the CWE and you're looking to dance, at least give the Mandarin a shot; it's not going to be for everyone, but it's pretty great if you're in the mood for it.
Revise this with your best effort:
The Mandarin is a stylish dance club that caters to a trendy crowd. It offers a wide selection of cocktails and beers, ranging from higher-end options to the more standard wells and domestics. It's worth noting that on select nights, there is a door charge for men, which is fairly common in the industry.

One standout feature of the club is its spacious patio. Even during the winter months, the patio remains almost fully accessible as it is enclosed. Inside, the music can be hit-or-miss. At times, you'll find yourself dancing to classic hip-hop, pop, and even rock, while other times the DJ might play songs that are difficult to dance to.

If you're out on the patio, it provides a more relaxed atmosphere where you can engage in conversation. However, inside the club, the volume is predictably high, making it challenging to hold a conversation. Overall, if you find yourself in the Central West End (CWE) and in the mood for a vibrant dance experience, it's worth giving the Mandarin a try. Keep in mind that while it may not appeal to everyone, it can be a fantastic option for those seeking a specific ambiance.

input:
Another gem on Frenchmen.  We made it in just in time to grab the corner tall table and enjoyed the piano player playing some nice tunes.

Order at the bar and they'll bring you the food.  What we had:
pork pot stickers - pretty good - $4 HH price
smoked hanger steak w/ chimichurri sauce on toastones - tasted much better than it looked - $4 HH price
lobster eggrolls w/ sweet chile lime sauce - $8 - didn't look promising but it was tasty
Hopitoulas - $4.5
UFO - $4.5

One of the owners/chefs is Korean, thus the Asian food.

HH everyday from 4-6:30pm, $4 tapas, $5 wines, $3 beers.

We will definitely return.
Revise this with your best effort:
We stumbled upon another hidden gem on Frenchmen Street. Fortunately, we arrived just in time to snag one of the coveted tall tables in the corner, allowing us to fully immerse ourselves in the ambiance while the talented piano player filled the air with beautiful melodies.

At this establishment, you simply order at the bar and your food is brought directly to you. Our choices included the delectable pork pot stickers, which were surprisingly satisfying for the happy hour price of $4. The smoked hanger steak served on crisp toastones, accompanied by a flavorful chimichurri sauce, exceeded our expectations both in taste and presentation, once again priced at an affordable $4 during happy hour. Although the lobster eggrolls with a sweet chili lime sauce didn't initially captivate us with their appearance, we were pleasantly surprised by their irresistible flavor, despite their slightly higher price tag of $8. To quench our thirst, we indulged in the Hopitoulas and UFO beers, both reasonably priced at $4.5 each.

What sets this place apart is the multicultural influence from one of the owners, who happens to be Korean. This fusion is evident in the Asian-inspired dishes available on their menu.

If you're looking for a good deal, be sure to visit during happy hour, which runs every day from 4-6:30 pm. During this time, you can enjoy $4 tapas, $5 wines, and $3 beers, making it an even more enticing experience.

With such a delightful dining experience, we can confidently say that we will certainly be returning to this establishment in the future.

input: food is ok, felt rushed, too many tables and not enough space.  its very crowded and frequently had other servers and customers bumping into our chairs.
Revise this with your best effort: The quality of the food was satisfactory; however, the overall experience felt rushed due to the excessive number of tables and limited space. input: crappy restarurant with awful service and rude waiter. if you are looking for a GOOD BYO italian restaurant, go to La Baia on 17th and Lombard!

input: After always shopping at the Randall's off Jefferson, it was nice to see West County get their own Randall's. Staff here is uber friendly and helpful. Beer selection is solid here, with plenty of styles to choose from.Prices are competitive with the other beer markets around. Well worth your time and money.
Revise this with your best effort: I was delighted to discover that West County now has its very own Randall's, especially since I had always shopped at the location off Jefferson. What impressed me the most is the solid beer selection offered here, which features an abundance of different styles to cater to various preferences. Moreover, the competitive prices at this store when compared to other beer markets in the area make it a worthwhile destination for both your time and money.

input: Deseree has done my hair for over a decade and I wouldn't trust anyone else. From blonde to brunette, to long or short, she does it all. She's styling my hair for my upcoming wedding plus 6 bridesmaids and I have no doubt it'll be picture perfect. Deseree is accommodating, dependable,and experienced (oh, and hilarious too )!!

input:
Four of us had dinner at the Sockeye Grill this weekend.  Service was terrible.  Super slow.  Salads were warm and tasteless.  Dressing was watered down. 

Salmon was excellent.  Nachos were okay. Finger steaks were mushy and drab. 

Waitress  knew her beer. The dark lager was excellent.  The lighter beers we had were too warm. 

Looks like this restaurant need some fine tuning.  The atmosphere was like a warehouse, more like being in a barn than a restaurant. 

Tvs everywhere but the news was on. Huh? How depressing is that? 

We won't be back.
Revise this with your best effort:
A group of four of us recently dined at the Sockeye Grill, and unfortunately, the service left much to be desired. It was incredibly slow and lacking efficiency. Our salads were disappointingly warm and lacked any flavor. Additionally, the dressing seemed to be diluted and lacked the intended taste.

However, it wasn't all bad. The saving grace of the meal was undoubtedly the excellent quality of the salmon. The nachos were decent, although not outstanding. Unfortunately, the finger steaks were a letdown, as they were mushy and lacking in any vibrant flavors.

On a positive note, our waitress was knowledgeable about the variety of beers offered. The dark lager she recommended was fantastic. However, the lighter beers that we tried were served at a noticeably warm temperature, which was rather disappointing.

It is evident that this establishment could benefit from some fine tuning. The atmosphere felt more like a warehouse or barn rather than a welcoming restaurant. The abundance of TVs placed throughout the venue was a peculiar choice, particularly since the news was playing, creating a somewhat somber ambiance.

Considering our experience, we have made the decision not to return to the Sockeye Grill in the future.

input:
We had a very nice dinner here on St. Patrick's day, which happens to be my sister's birthday.  The server was super sweet and served the cake we brought to celebrate.  The bartender was so kind and gave my sister a complimentary St. Patty's cocktail, which was incredibly yummy.  

We ordered various dishes:  tri-tip, rotisserie chicken, pulled pork and a veggie burrito.  All was wonderful, except for the veggie burrito, which was lackluster (but who orders a veggie burrito at a rotisserie grill???).  My father-in-law has visited many more times, raving about the moist, flavorful rotisserie chicken.  

The prices were reasonable, portions adequate and service super!  We will definitely visit again, minus the resident vegetarian.  :)
Revise this with your best effort:
We had an absolute blast during our St. Patrick's day dinner, which also doubled as a celebration for my sister's birthday. The server we had was incredibly kind and went above and beyond by serving the cake we brought to make the occasion even more special. To top it off, the bartender treated my sister to a delightful complimentary St. Patty's cocktail that was truly scrumptious.

When it came to ordering our dishes, we went for a variety. The choices included tri-tip, rotisserie chicken, pulled pork, and even a veggie burrito (which, let's be honest, was probably not the best choice considering the name of the grill!). While everything we tried was a mouthwatering delight, the veggie burrito fell a bit short, lacking that extra oomph. But hey, who can blame the grill for not excelling in a vegetarian option?

On the other hand, my father-in-law has been to this place several times and can't stop raving about the moist and flavorful rotisserie chicken. It seems to be his go-to favorite.

Overall, the prices were reasonable, the portions were perfectly satisfying, and the service was top-notch. We definitely plan on coming back for another visit, though we might have to leave our resident vegetarian at home this time! :)

input: Went to see Anders Osborne play here & it was a highlight of my trip to NOLA.  Streetcar went straight down to Bourbon after the show but I wish I'd stayed longer! Food smelled awesome, drinks were very reasonably priced  & the crowd was mellow.
Revise this with your best effort: Attending Anders Osborne's performance in this city was undeniably the highlight of my trip to NOLA. Once the show concluded, I hopped onto the streetcar and made my way to Bourbon Street, although in retrospect, I regret not prolonging my stay. The enticing aroma of delectable food permeated the air, the drinks were surprisingly affordable, and the atmosphere exuded a serene and relaxed vibe.

input: I have been told by numerous native philadelphians that Ralph's is one of the best Italian restaurants in the city and is a must to experience. We did not think so. We started off with a grilled calamari appetizer that was soaked in salty red sauce. The amount of sauce overwhelmed the palate to the point where we couldn't even taste the calamari. I got the pasta bolognese with filet mignon tips. Again, the red sauce was very salty. The filet mignon tips was really just average quality beef. My wife ordered the black lobster ravioli which were decent but overly salty. We expected much more from the oldest Italian restaurant in the country.
Revise this with your best effort: I have received feedback from several Philadelphia locals who claim that Ralph's is one of the finest Italian restaurants in the city, insisting it is an essential dining experience. However, our personal experience did not align with these opinions. Our culinary journey began with a grilled calamari appetizer, unfortunately drenched in an excessively salty red sauce. The overwhelming amount of sauce overshadowed the calamari, rendering it virtually tasteless. As for my choice, the pasta bolognese with filet mignon tips, once again the red sauce proved to be overly salted. Moreover, the filet mignon tips themselves were quite ordinary in terms of quality. On the other hand, my wife opted for the black lobster ravioli, which were fairly decent but still marred by an excessive amount of salt. Considering the reputable status of being the oldest Italian restaurant in the country, we held higher expectations for our dining experience at Ralph's.

input: We get high on the beauty of this amazing high desert oasis! Nature's drama in the Catalina Mountains. We come here to run or hike. We're #MCLifeTucson - we love it in the canyon!
Revise this with your best effort: We are captivated by the intoxicating beauty of this remarkable high desert oasis! The Catalina Mountains provide us with an awe-inspiring spectacle of nature's wonders. Whether we come here to run or hike, the allure of this place is undeniable. input:
Beer service was lackluster. The first beer I ordered had an off flavor (sour). I ordered a taste of another similar dark beer to see if the problem was endemic but it wasn't. I would have appreciated it more if the bar tender looked into the off flavor when I sent my beer back. This tells me the bar tender doesn't know beer. I assume that particular draft line needs to be cleaned but maybe the problem was with the keg. 

Another thing that killed me was their use of glassware. They serve beers in the classic American "Shaker" pint glass and serve water in the far superior English Nonic Pint glass. I also saw the bar tender pour a white ale with normal ABV in a stemmed tulip glass.

The shaker pint glasses are kept refrigerated and are too cold in my opinion. I would much rather see them kept at room temp and rinsed in cold water (which they do here). 

All in all, the beer knowledge is not up to par for a place that advertises as a burger joint with a large craft beer selection (30 taps).
Revise this with your best effort:
The beer service provided was disappointing. Upon ordering my first beer, I immediately noticed an unpleasant sour taste, indicating an off flavor. In an attempt to determine if this was an isolated incident, I requested a taste of another dark beer with similar characteristics, only to find that it was not affected. It would have been appreciated if the bartender had looked into the off flavor issue when I returned my beer. This lack of attention suggests a lack of knowledge regarding beer on the bartender's part. I suspect that the draft line in question may require cleaning, although there is a possibility that the issue lies with the keg itself.

Another aspect that left me dissatisfied was their choice of glassware. The use of classic American "Shaker" pint glasses to serve beers seemed inferior to the far superior English Nonic Pint glasses they reserved for water service. Furthermore, I witnessed the bartender pour a white ale with a normal ABV into a stemmed tulip glass, which felt inappropriate.

Moreover, the refrigeration of the shaker pint glasses resulted in them being excessively cold, in my opinion. I would prefer to see them stored at room temperature and rinsed with cold water, which they do here.

In conclusion, the establishment's beer knowledge falls short of expectations for a place that promotes itself as a burger joint with an extensive craft beer selection of 30 taps.

input: Love love live Orangetheory!! Best full body workout ever!!! And so many classes.... always convenient!
Revise this with your best effort: I absolutely adore Orangetheory! It's unquestionably the ultimate full-body workout, hands down! Not to mention, the abundance of classes makes it incredibly convenient!

input: Rons still a regular stop for me.  Usually some good craft beers  (excellent this week) and tasty food  (if you know what to stick with on menu).
Revise this with your best effort: Ron's is still my go-to place. Their selection of craft beers is usually top-notch, and this week in particular, it was excellent. As for the food, it can be hit or miss, but if you know what to stick with on the menu, you're in for a tasty treat.

input: This place is amazing!  They make the donuts fresh with each order.  In fact, I had to wait 10 minutes for them to cool down before I could eat them.  This location is clean and never super busy.  Its a really great addition to the neighborhood and people with cars are sure to appreciate the parking lot.  Best donuts in Philly and the Delaware Valley.
Revise this with your best effort: This place is absolutely fantastic! They create the most delectable donuts, freshly made to order. I was so eager to devour them that I had to exercise patience for a whole 10 minutes as they cooled down. Moreover, this establishment boasts a pristine environment that is never overwhelmingly bustling. Consequently, it serves as a splendid enhancement to the neighborhood, with the added perk of a parking lot that will undoubtedly be cherished by car owners. Undeniably, this spot offers the finest donuts in all of Philly and the Delaware Valley.

input: This is the worst. My first time at an Econo anything. Playing nice for group purposes. We get here. They check us in like the rooms are clean. The rooms are dirty. The lady comes to clean the room because apparently they dont have any others clean or available. Go figure. So the manager comes outside to look as if we are lying about dirty rooms. It's hot as hell outside, wasps everywhere and we're standing here. I asked about other clean rooms and he (a-hole manager) (neil Patel) sarcastically states check in is at 2. It's 1:45 though. If you're going to check guest in at least make sure the rooms are clean or let them know it will be a few. So I'm standing outside in the heat as they apparently clean the room.  They took no cleaner in to clean counters, bathroom, etc. Just nasty. Then they just looked in the microwave & fridge to see if it was clean. They didn't wipe nothing. I would never stay at this filthy mofo or any Econo Lodge. Just nasty. Go w/ a big brand like Marriot, Starwood or Hilton where customer satisfaction is part of their branding scope. This -ish is for the birds and folks who need a place for a quickie.... Not even that.
Revise this with your best effort:
This has been an absolutely terrible experience. It was my first time staying at an Econo Lodge, and I had to pretend to be polite for the sake of the group. When we arrived, the check-in process gave off the impression that the rooms were clean. However, upon entering, it became apparent that they were anything but. We had to wait for the lady to come and clean our room because apparently, there were no others available or in decent condition. It's frustrating and disappointing that we ended up in this situation.

To make matters worse, the manager came outside to inspect the rooms as if we were lying about their cleanliness. Standing outside in the blazing heat, dealing with wasps buzzing around, was certainly not how we envisioned our stay. I inquired about the possibility of getting different, clean rooms, but the manager, who acted like an arrogant jerk (Neil Patel), sarcastically told us that check-in was at 2 PM, even though it was only 1:45. If they insist on checking guests in early, they should ensure the rooms are clean or inform them that it may take a bit longer. It's incredibly frustrating being stuck outside in the sweltering heat while they supposedly clean the rooms.

To our dismay, there seemed to be no effort made to properly clean the room. They merely glanced at the microwave and fridge to see if they were clean, ignoring the rest of the surfaces. It was disgusting and disappointing. Given this experience, I would never consider staying at this filthy establishment or any Econo Lodge in the future. It's far better to opt for a reputable and well-known brand like Marriott, Starwood, or Hilton, where customer satisfaction is a priority within their branding values. This place is no better than a dump and only suitable for those looking for a quick, unsatisfactory stay.

input: Finally got to check out Cafe Soleil. One word: Delicieux!! Being from France, I had high expectations, I don't play with my pastries! Boy do they deliver, the croissants were buttery, nice and flaky, and melt in your mouth...even better then some of the ones I had in France. Not surprisingly, the baker "Nico" is french, and you could taste the difference in the food.  The fact that the products are imported does make a big difference in the taste, it's definitely authentic.  Nico was very personable and friendly, it was fun chatting with an ex-parisian :). The one negative thing is they are too far from me, 45 mins drive, but to satiate my sweet tooth, I will definitely be back! I highly recommend this bakery.
Revise this with your best effort:
I recently had the pleasure of visiting Cafe Soleil and let me just say, it was an absolute delight! As a proud French citizen, I hold the highest standards when it comes to pastries and let me tell you, Cafe Soleil does not disappoint. The croissants were simply divine - perfectly buttery, flaky, and oh-so-mouthwatering. I dare say they surpassed some of the ones I've had back in France.

It comes as no surprise that the talented baker, known as "Nico," hails from France himself. His expertise and passion for flavors shine through in every bite. The fact that the ingredients are imported adds that authentic touch that truly sets this cafe apart.

Not only does the food impress, but Nico himself was an absolute joy. He was personable, friendly, and it was a delight to chat with someone who knows the ins and outs of Parisian culture. However, I must admit, the only downside is that Cafe Soleil is quite a distance from my location, a 45-minute drive. Despite this, my insatiable sweet tooth will surely draw me back time and time again.

In conclusion, I cannot recommend Cafe Soleil enough. It is a haven for pastry enthusiasts like myself, and the dedication to quality and authenticity is evident in every delectable bite. Don't miss out on this hidden gem - you won't be disappointed!

input:
Not mediocre at all IMHO.  Makes me wonder if Daniel O. went to the same place we did.

This is a great neighborhood byob place that provides welcoming service and excellent food at a reasonable price.  We started going here because numerous South Philly friends recommended it.  This is not foo-foo Italian.  This is not pretentious Italian.  This is "let's go back and work our way through the menu" Italian.  We found the specials to be good choices.  My husband's broccoli rabe and sausage was excellent, as was a grilled romaine salad with bleu cheese and pine nuts.  Both were generous enough to share.  Last time, sausage & figs was a hit.  If you are in the mood for a basic plate of macaronis with red gravy, you won't be disappointed either.  We had a great time with the waitress because my BIL brought a bottle of Great Wall wine from China (that was the 2nd bottle we opened) and that started a whole crazy discussion. input:
I must say I'm very disappointed, my two stars are for presentation and prompt delivery. I ordered the rainbow roll, white tuna roll, calamari and chicken lettuce wraps. Where do I begin? ok with the bad. 

I strongly feel that when you are delivering food that should be served cold, you don't put it in a bag with hot food because that equals mushy, warm sushi, which is what I got. The rainbow roll, which normally is topped with raw fish was topped with mushy avocado????? which I ended up peeling off to salvage the sushi. The spicy white tuna roll was very good.

The calamari looked like chicken fingers all the breading was falling off and it was under cooked, I took one bite and tossed it. Now I've had lettuce wraps before but mines came with an actual head of lettuce in a bag and chicken filling in a plate. It was not described this way in the menu at all. All in all I don't think I'll be ordering from here again. I'll stick to Niji's on 5th.
Revise this with your best effort:
I must express my deep disappointment with my recent dining experience. Although I appreciate the presentation and prompt delivery, I am afraid that is where the positives end. I had ordered the rainbow roll, white tuna roll, calamari, and chicken lettuce wraps, and there were quite a few issues that left me dissatisfied.

Firstly, I must address the mishap of packaging the cold items together with the hot ones. This resulted in the unfortunate outcome of mushy, warm sushi. To my surprise, the rainbow roll, which traditionally features raw fish, had been topped with excessively soft avocado. I had to carefully remove the avocado to salvage what was left of the sushi. However, on a brighter note, the spicy white tuna roll was quite delicious.

Moreover, the calamari arrived in a disappointing state. The breading was falling off, resembling more of chicken fingers than calamari. Additionally, the calamari itself was undercooked, leading me to immediately discard it after just one bite.

Lastly, the chicken lettuce wraps I ordered were not as described on the menu. Instead of the advertised plate with chicken filling and a separate head of lettuce, it arrived with both components mixed together in a bag. This discrepancy was quite frustrating and misleading.

Based on this experience, I am reluctant to order from this establishment again. Instead, I will continue to frequent Niji's on 5th, where I have had far more satisfactory dining experiences.

input:
I came in here the other night for a  post-show snack after seeing a ESO performance at the Winspear. The main reason we chose this location was because it was close to the Winspear, and open late (until 11:30pm on Friday and Saturday). I don't have any strong criticisms of the restaurant. I suppose, if anything, the menu may have seemed a little bit over-priced - at least for what I ordered. I had a Caesar salad with three 'jumbo' shrimp on it, which cost $15. The portion size did not seem to justify the cost and the jumbo shrimp were fairly average in their size, but the flavours were good and the ingredients were fresh. My friend had a soup, which looked and smelled absolutely amazing, and at $6 it didn't seem too unreasonable. She also had the smoked salmon Carpaccio, which looked very appetizing with its thick slices of dark rye bread and generous slices of smoked salmon and capers. The also had a couple of interesting beers on their menu that we were keen to try.

I think if you're going to a show in the area and looking for a spot to get a drink or a snack afterward, this is not a bad option. Their menu at that time of night had an interesting mix of appetizers and desserts that seemed to provide something to suit most tastes.

I'm assuming Normand's Bistro must be connected to the Normand's restaurant which is on Jasper Avenue. Of interest, I have heard that Normand's took over the brunch menu that had formerly been offered at the Glenora Bistro.

Normand's Bistro also showcased a selection of intriguing beers on their menu that piqued our curiosity.

If you find yourself seeking a spot for a drink or snack after a show in the vicinity, Normand's Bistro is a decent option. Their late-night menu featured an interesting fusion of appetizers and desserts catering to various palates.

Considering the restaurant's name, Normand's Bistro, it is probable that it is connected to the Normand's restaurant situated on Jasper Avenue. It is worth noting that Normand's apparently inherited the brunch menu formerly offered at the Glenora Bistro, adding an interesting tidbit to its backstory.

input:
I have been a fan of Charlie's for many years and I recently came back because I didn't have any jeans that fit.  I'm so happy I came back.

The girl who helped me was extremely attentive.  She pulled about 20 different pairs for me to try and explained all the nuances in the different fits and washes.  She was very patient despite my incredible indecision.  I ended up purchasing two pairs of Sebastian McCalls and I am really happy that I discovered this brand.  They are super cute and comfortable.  I love this place!
Revise this with your best effort:
For years, I have been a devoted fan of Charlie's, but it was only recently that I found myself returning, driven by the sole reason that I desperately needed a pair of well-fitting jeans. And let me tell you, I am overjoyed that I came back.

Upon entering the store, I was greeted by a girl whose attentiveness was unparalleled. She painstakingly handpicked around 20 pairs of jeans for me to try on, taking the time to guide me through the intricacies of each fit and wash option. Remarkably, she remained patient and understanding despite my immense indecisiveness. In the end, I made the fantastic choice of purchasing two pairs of Sebastian McCalls, a brand I had the pleasure of discovering during my visit. Not only do they possess undeniable cuteness, but they also offer an unparalleled level of comfort. Indeed, I am thoroughly enamored with this brand.

All in all, I cannot express enough my adoration for this establishment. The exceptional service, the incredible selection, and the discovery of a new favorite brand have solidified Charlie's as my go-to place.

input: Went there on a Tuesday with my minivan, which ended up being Senior Discount Day. They didn't tell me before I paid that they won't clean or vacuum 3rd rows on Senior days. I got the Super wash, which included wax. They handed it over with large dirt smudges on the side, like it hadn't been wiped at all. A couple cup holders were barely touched and Some not at all in the front. The rest of the vacuuming wasn't good, with paper scraps still on the floor. I talked with the manager about the 3rd row and why didn't they tell me upfront when I pulled in. He said, "I won't do your 3rd row on Senior Day. That's the way we've been doing it for 15 years." I said I was new to the area and he said, "That's too bad." What kind of customer service is that?!? I usually don't write reviews, but this place was that bad.
Revise this with your best effort: I visited the car wash on a Tuesday in my minivan, unaware that it happened to be Senior Discount Day. Unfortunately, I was not informed beforehand that they do not clean or vacuum the 3rd rows on these days. Opting for the Super wash, which included wax, I was disappointed to find large dirt smudges on the side of my vehicle, as if it hadn't been wiped at all. Additionally, some of the cup holders in the front were barely touched or completely ignored. The overall vacuuming job was subpar, with paper scraps still scattered on the floor. Frustrated, I approached the manager to discuss the issue with the 3rd row and why I wasn't informed upon arrival. Shockingly, he responded, "We don't touch the 3rd row on Senior Day. It's been our policy for the past 15 years." As a newcomer to the area, I expressed my disappointment and he insensitively replied, "That's too bad." This type of customer service is completely unacceptable! I typically refrain from leaving reviews, but my experience at this place was truly appalling.

input: i had the seafood combo-catfish (and im talkin like 5 pounds of it), red beans and rice and coleslaw.  the food was pretty damn good.  well, the real reason we walked in to this place was due to the big sign out front: "happy hour, mon-sat, 4pm-7pm, 2 for 1"  Now THAT is what im talkin about.  i ordered a margarita...and being that i'm from California, i have extremely high standards for marg's.  wasn't bad, but really wasn't great... but food made up for it!
Revise this with your best effort: I thoroughly enjoyed the seafood combo, specifically the generous portion of catfish, weighing in at around 5 pounds. Accompanied by sides of red beans and rice and coleslaw, the meal was quite enjoyable. What prompted our visit to this establishment was the captivating sign displayed outside, boldly advertising a happy hour from Monday to Saturday between 4pm and 7pm, offering a fantastic 2 for 1 deal. Now, that's my kind of offer! Intrigued, I decided to order a margarita, considering myself somewhat of a connoisseur with my California origins. While it didn't quite meet my exceptionally high standards, it was still enjoyable. Nevertheless, the food more than made up for any disappointment.

input:
Have been here many times and always had a great experience. When we moved to Rita Ranch 6 months ago my husband and I did a lot of rehab work on our new house and would go almost once a week to recover from the week's "work-out". It's always clean, they never gyp you on time, take the time to work on problem areas. Felicia is the best. Highly recommend them! 

Update...neck really bothering me so I went in and had the best therapeutic massage with Felicia. It was amazing! She is truly talented.
Revise this with your best effort:
I have visited this place numerous times and have consistently had exceptional experiences. Since my husband and I relocated to Rita Ranch half a year ago, we have been actively engaged in renovating our new home, which often left us exhausted. To rejuvenate ourselves, we frequented this establishment almost every week. They maintain impeccable cleanliness standards, always ensure that the allocated time is utilized effectively, and diligently focus on problematic areas. Among the skilled therapists, Felicia stands out as the absolute best. I wholeheartedly recommend their services.

As an update, I was recently experiencing significant discomfort in my neck, prompting me to seek relief at this establishment. I booked a therapeutic massage session with Felicia, and it was truly exceptional. Her talent and skills are unrivaled, and the experience was nothing short of amazing.

input:
The Sunrise Family Restaurant is an old style diner that has a very small-town, homey feel.   Service is prompt and super friendly.

I had a Monte Cristo sandwich per the waitresses recommendation and I won't lie, it was pretty disappointing.  Take a stack of turkey and a couple thick slices of ham out of their respective industrial packs, microwave them with some swiss cheese on top and serve on limp french toast.  Somebody out there might like it.  I didn't. 

It came with a salad and fries, both of which were good.  The fries were thick steak fries cooked to a perfect golden brown.   

I have a feeling there are some good items on the menu.  I would especially be interested in trying breakfast.  I'll be back.
Revise this with your best effort:
The Sunrise Family Restaurant exudes a charming, cozy ambiance reminiscent of an old-fashioned diner. The service provided is prompt and exceptionally friendly, making guests feel right at home.

Following a waitress' recommendation, I opted for the Monte Cristo sandwich, hoping for a delectable treat. However, I must confess that it fell short of my expectations. The dish consisted of turkey stacked alongside thick slices of ham, borrowed from their respective industrial packs. These ingredients were microwaved together with a layer of Swiss cheese, served on somewhat limp French toast. While it may appeal to some palates, it regrettably did not meet my own preferences.

Nevertheless, the accompanying salad and fries provided a redeeming factor. The fries, in particular, were a delight to behold, boasting a perfect golden brown hue and prepared as thick, steak-cut fries.

Despite my less-than-stellar experience, I hold hope that the menu at Sunrise Family Restaurant contains noteworthy items. Of particular interest to me is their breakfast selection, which I am eager to explore on a future visit.

input: First time at Butcher & Bee with my husband who joined me and my co-workers for lunch one day. I love the place, it so cute with the farmhouse feel. It's really open and cute booths that offers some privacy. We had a group of 7 and it was a bit tight, but we were able to be sat right away. I ordered the pork belly gnocchi, and it was good, but not great. I felt it lacked texture. If the pork belly was crispy, it would have sealed the deal. My husband ordered the trout sandwich, unfortunately, he was disappointed that it was basically a 'tuna salad' sandwich. He did not enjoy it. For dessert, we ordered coconut macaroons, which were good. Co-workers had mixed reviews, but one ordered the KFC (Korean Fried Chicken) sandwich, and he liked it. Will definitely have to give this place another try. Also, the use books for bill holders, so cute!
Revise this with your best effort:
On a certain day, my husband decided to join me and my co-workers for lunch at Butcher & Bee, a place that I had never been before. The moment we stepped foot inside, I instantly fell in love with its charming farmhouse atmosphere. The space was incredibly open, and the adorable booths provided a hint of privacy. Despite being a group of seven, we were promptly seated without any hassle.

To satisfy my craving, I ordered the pork belly gnocchi dish. Although it was tasty, I couldn't help but feel that it lacked a certain texture that would have elevated the overall experience. If only the pork belly had been delightfully crispy, it would have been a perfect match. On the other hand, my husband's choice of the trout sandwich turned out to be a bit disappointing. It essentially resembled a common 'tuna salad' sandwich, and he didn't find it enjoyable at all.

When it came time for dessert, we opted for the coconut macaroons, which proved to be quite satisfying. Among my co-workers, opinions were mixed, but one of them ordered the KFC (Korean Fried Chicken) sandwich and seemed to genuinely enjoy it. Hence, I believe it's worth giving Butcher & Bee another chance to impress us.

Lastly, I must mention the adorable touch of using books as bill holders at the restaurant. It added an extra element of cuteness to an already charming establishment.

input:
This is a really fun event for those who enjoy beer in all its forms. The drinks themselves were relatively cheap ($2-4 for a 4 oz. sample. Most were $2, some were $3, and very few were in the $4 range), however the food was really over priced ($6 for a small cup of fancy macaroni and cheese? really?). For the beer lover, however, there is a wide variety of tried and true along with the new kids on the block from local, national and international lines. Also, if you like what you tasted, you can buy it on site, with a Sobeys/Safeway liquor store right on site doing specials on the sampled brews. 

We went VIP for this event, however I don't think it's worth it. What you get: a glass mug instead of a plastic one, a beer and food class ($2 value) and a beer seminar ($2 value). If you do it all, or really value the glass mug, go for it! But for me, who just did the beer and food class, it wasn't worth it. 

My only complaint is for the venue, but for an event that size, you need the space. $16 for parking on top of your entry fee (though I guess most people would cab or Uber it there so you don't have to have a designated driver), and then you have to buy sample tickets on site. It gets quite expensive.
Revise this with your best effort:
This event is an absolute blast for beer enthusiasts of all kinds. The wide selection of beverages, ranging from local favorites to exciting new brews, make it a truly enjoyable experience. The prices for the drinks themselves are quite reasonable, with most samples priced at $2 and only a few reaching $4. However, the food on offer is disappointingly overpriced. Paying $6 for a small cup of fancy macaroni and cheese is simply outrageous.

For those who relish in the world of beer, this event provides an excellent opportunity to try tried-and-true classics as well as exciting new additions from both local and international breweries. Plus, if you find something you love, you can conveniently purchase it on-site at the Sobeys/Safeway liquor store, which offers specials on the sampled brews.

We decided to go VIP for this event, but to be honest, it didn't quite live up to the hype. The perks of VIP admission include a glass mug instead of a plastic one, a beer and food class (valued at $2), and a beer seminar (also valued at $2). If you're planning to make use of all these benefits or simply highly value a glass mug, then it might be worth it. However, for someone like myself who only attended the beer and food class, it felt like a letdown.

One minor gripe I have is with the venue. To accommodate an event of this scale, ample space is necessary. Unfortunately, this leads to a fee of $16 for parking on top of the entry fee. It can quickly add up, considering you also have to purchase sample tickets on-site. This can become quite costly, although I suppose most people would opt for a cab or Uber to avoid the hassles of finding a designated driver.

Overall, despite a few drawbacks, this event provides a fantastic experience for beer enthusiasts. With its diverse drink selection and potential for discovery, it's definitely worth attending.

input: I've been here a handful of times and it's always because I don't have time to go to VN Nails near Costco where I prefer to go (they get 5 stars from me).  Kiwi Nail has always done a cheap job trying to take shortcuts wherever possible.  But today I've had it and will never go back!  After getting the typical shabby job on a fill with French tips,  I accidentally smudged two nails really badly.  They needed to be repainted and I asked her to do so... I even offered to pay extra.  The nail tech came over to look and she pressed the clumps back down and painted right back over the mess (didn't even keep the paint in the lines) then slathered so much varnish over the train wreck that it was literally dripping down my finger. After my nails were dry enough to leave,  another tech rang me up and the receipt had no place for a tip.  When I asked,  he told me I had to pay tips in cash... Well it's lucky for me I didn't have any cash.  He said I will have to tip her next time.  NEXT TIME??!!  yeah right!  There will be no next time! Save yourself the hassle and don't bother with this d@mn place!
Revise this with your best effort:
I have visited this establishment multiple times, mainly due to time constraints preventing me from going to my preferred nail salon, VN Nails near Costco, which consistently receives a five-star rating from me. Unfortunately, Kiwi Nail has consistently displayed a lack of attention to detail, always attempting to cut corners in their service. However, my patience has reached its limit, and I vow never to return!

During my most recent visit, I received the typical subpar treatment on a fill with French tips. To make matters worse, I accidentally smudged two nails severely and requested that they be repainted, even offering to pay an additional fee. The nail technician simply pressed the lumps back into place and carelessly painted over the mess, without bothering to keep the paint within the lines. Furthermore, she applied an excessive amount of varnish, causing it to drip down my finger, resembling a complete disaster. After waiting for my nails to dry sufficiently, another technician proceeded to ring me up, but to my surprise, the receipt did not provide a space for leaving a tip. When I inquired about this, he informed me that tips could only be given in cash, which was fortunate for me as I did not have any available. He advised that I could tip the nail technician during my next visit. However, considering this dreadful experience, there is absolutely no chance of a "next time."

In conclusion, I strongly urge you to spare yourself the inconvenience and avoid this dreadful place.

input: I'm not really into the fast food scene BUT Chick fil A is a step above. Great quality food! I don't feel like I'm eating a ton of fillers!
Revise this with your best effort: Although I'm not particularly fond of fast food, I must admit that Chick-fil-A stands out from the rest. The quality of their food is exceptional, making me feel like I'm not consuming an abundance of fillers.

input: Square 1682 is a hotel bar I frequent. I've been there for lunch, brunch, dinner and happy hour. The food is great, the service is excellent, and the space is upscale. There is always a nice group of people that go there. Whether they are staying at the hotel or live or work in the area, you'll always find someone nice to chat with at the bar. The very best thing about the bar is the bartender that works on Mondays. His name is Dan and he is the man! He's my favorite bartender in the city and I've been to a lot of places. He always knows just what I want and remembers my name when I go there. The only reason I go to Square 1682 on Monday's is because Dan is working. If I walk by and he's not on, I keep going. He's that good! Love him and have so many great memories at this fine establishment.
Revise this with your best effort: Square 1682 is my go-to hotel bar, frequented by yours truly. I have had the pleasure of indulging in their delectable cuisine during lunch, brunch, dinner, and happy hour. The food is impeccable, the service is top-notch, and the ambiance exudes sophistication. It never fails to attract a delightful crowd, whether they are hotel guests, locals, or professionals in the vicinity. An evening at the bar guarantees delightful conversations with interesting individuals. However, there is one particular gem that sets Square 1682 apart—the exceptional bartender who graces the place every Monday. Enter Dan, a true maestro of mixology. He reigns supreme as my favorite bartender in the entire city, and trust me, I have explored numerous watering holes. Dan possesses an uncanny ability to read my preferences effortlessly, ensuring that my glass is always filled with my desired libation. What's more, he pleasantly surprises me by remembering my name whenever I visit. Such attention to detail is truly commendable. On Mondays, Square 1682 becomes my unequivocal destination solely because of Dan's presence. In the rare event that he is not behind the counter, I carry on, knowing that I would be missing out on an exceptional experience. Dan's exceptional skills and warm demeanor have molded numerous cherished memories within the walls of this exquisite establishment. I hold him in the highest regard and cannot thank him enough for making Square 1682 an unforgettable spot in my heart.

input: This is a must try, we come here frequent and we are never disappointed. Get there early so you get right in and don't have to wait. Decent selection of coffees, they have french press as well. Menu isn't huge which is nice so you can figure out what you want quickly. Food comes how in a decent time. I seem to always get the same thing (wilburt skillet) everytime I go cause it is amazing. Food just seems so fresh as well, friendly staff. You will leave full and a smile on your face.
Revise this with your best effort: You absolutely have to try this place - we visit often and are consistently impressed. Arriving early is essential to avoid any waiting time; fortunately, they offer a delightful variety of coffees, including french press. The concise menu is a breath of fresh air, allowing for quick decision-making. Orders are served promptly, and I find myself returning to the mouthwatering Wilburt Skillet every single time - it's just that good. The food exudes freshness and is accompanied by a friendly and attentive staff. Rest assured, you'll leave feeling satisfied with a radiant smile on your face.

input:
I tried to like this place... I really did. So much so that I went back to try it after a less that satisfactory first wax.

Wax 1- I had Despina, I think her name was. I waited a good 15 minutes after my appointment time for her to come and get me from the front. Ironic they have a 9 minute policy that if you don't show they'll cancel/charge you or whatever. Anyway, as for the experience with Despina, she did not speak to me. Like at all. Made me feel super awkward the whole time, and missed a fair few chunks of hair. She didn't ask me anything about myself, didn't tell me where to sit or how she wanted me positioned etc. Luckily I got this one half price as it was my first time at EWC.

Wax 2- I booked 3-4 weeks later with Amy Jo (based on previous Yelp reviews). She was a lot friendlier (literally the only reason why I'm giving this 1 star) BUT way too sloppy. I think it's safe to say this is the worst wax I've ever had. She left half of my hair on right before Valentine's Day! I understand they can't get all the hairs all the time but a lottttt of hair right on top was left clearly visible to my waxer. My apt was at 3.45, I walked out of the building at 3.53. Really. This includes the time spent undressing, redressing, and paying. 8 minutes is not long enough for all of this. It went so quick that when she said she was done I was actually shocked.  
I'm about to go to CVS and get some at home wax strips to finish the job... For $47+ I expect way way more. 

The staff- Another reason why I won't be returning. The ladies at the front desk are generally rude and disinterested in showing any glimpse of good customer service. ALSO, I don't like being asked if I'm going to tip - can't you give me the card machine so I can do it myself rather than make me announce if I would like to tip and how much? 

The hunt for a decent Brazilian wax in Philly continues- someone help me PLEASE!
Revise this with your best effort:
I made an attempt to like this establishment... I genuinely did. In fact, I even gave it a second chance after my initial unsatisfactory waxing experience.

First experience: The esthetician's name was Despina, if I recall correctly. I had to wait a frustrating 15 minutes past my scheduled appointment time before she finally showed up at the front. Ironically, they have a policy of canceling or charging you if you're more than 9 minutes late. As for Despina's service, she didn't speak to me at all, which made the whole experience incredibly awkward. She also missed quite a few patches of hair and failed to guide me on where to sit or how to position myself. Fortunately, I received a discount on this session since it was my first time at EWC.

Second experience: I decided to book another appointment 3 to 4 weeks later, this time with Amy Jo (based on positive Yelp reviews). To her credit, she was much friendlier (which is the sole reason I'm giving this place one star). However, her technique was incredibly sloppy. I can confidently say that this was the worst wax I've ever had. She left a significant portion of hair untouched, right before Valentine's Day! I understand that not all hairs can be removed every time, but there was a noticeable amount left on the top. My appointment was at 3:45, and I walked out of the building at 3:53. Yes, you read that correctly. This timeframe included undressing, redressing, and payment. Eight minutes is simply insufficient for all of this. It was so unexpectedly quick that I was genuinely surprised when she said she was finished. I'm about to head to CVS to buy some at-home wax strips to complete the job. Considering I paid $47 or more, I definitely expected a much higher level of service.

The staff: Another reason why I won't be returning to this place. The ladies at the front desk are consistently rude and disinterested in providing any form of good customer service. Additionally, I dislike being asked about tipping. Couldn't they simply provide me with the card machine so I can tip myself, rather than putting me in an uncomfortable position of announcing whether or not I intend to tip and how much?

The search for a decent Brazilian wax in Philly continues. I desperately need someone's assistance!

input: Amazing and comfortable atmosphere with extremely unique flavor combinations in the dishes. The Cuban Lamb Frita is a must (add the egg! It's worth it). All of the side items are delicious, you literally can't go wrong. The staff is friendly and they are extremely efficient with the coffee refills. This has quickly become my new regular brunch spot!
Revise this with your best effort: Experience an extraordinary and inviting ambiance complemented by an unparalleled fusion of flavors in their culinary creations. Do not miss out on the delectable Cuban Lamb Frita, enhanced blissfully by the addition of a perfectly cooked egg. Every side item is a tantalizing delight, promising a flawless gastronomic journey. The staff, emanating warmth and amiability, effortlessly ensure prompt coffee refills, elevating the dining experience to new heights. With its remarkable attributes, this establishment has seamlessly assumed the role of my preferred brunch destination.

input:
This place is good. For the lofty prices the proportions were very small. However the drinks were cheap and the service was very good. The piano is a nice touch as well. 

The cheesecake is incredible, just get it and don't look back.
Revise this with your best effort:
This establishment is quite commendable. Although the prices are a bit steep, the portions offered are disappointingly small. Nevertheless, the affordability of the drinks pleasantly surprised me, and the service provided was truly exceptional. Furthermore, the addition of a piano enhances the delightful ambiance of this place.

Now, let's talk about the cheesecake - it is undoubtedly extraordinary! I highly recommend indulging in this delectable treat without any reservations.

input: If you beat the crowd you're in. Small but that's the only negative. Everything I've tried on the menu is AMAZING! They even have vegetarian/vegan items. I always get whatever french toast special they have. I always take people who stay with me for Mardi Gras here for breakfast before we hit the parades.
Revise this with your best effort: When you manage to beat the crowd and secure a seat, you're in for a treat. The only downside is its small size. However, don't let that deter you because everything I've tried on the menu is absolutely phenomenal! Furthermore, they cater to vegetarians and vegans, offering a variety of options. Personally, I'm a huge fan of their french toast specials, and I make it a point to bring my guests for a delicious breakfast before indulging in the Mardi Gras parades.

input: Butch did a great job. The tour was relaxing, informative but 2 good stops to eat and see the cemetery. I recommend going on this trip the beginning of your stay so you know where to go during your trip. He'a also pretty fun.
Revise this with your best effort: Butch did an exceptional job during the tour. It was a truly relaxing and informative experience, with two fantastic stops to enjoy delicious meals and visit the cemetery. I highly recommend embarking on this trip at the onset of your stay as it will provide you with valuable insights on the best places to visit during your entire trip. Additionally, Butch's charming and entertaining personality adds an extra layer of enjoyment to the journey.

input: I love this food truck. They have the tastiest street foods like their captain crunch tilapia burrito. Who would've thought of that? The fried fish is so flakey and delicious, paired with fresh cabbage, tomatoes, avocado and Sriracha mayo. I have also tried their katsu and curry chicken which are so rich in flavor. Their Thai tea is also on point! So much to offer from a small food truck. I live in Jersey and I have driven here many times just to get food. They are so friendly and provide great food at a great price.
Revise this with your best effort: I absolutely adore this food truck! Their street foods are beyond delicious, especially their unexpected creation, the captain crunch tilapia burrito. Who would've imagined such a combination? The fish is perfectly fried, boasting a delightful flakiness and mouthwatering flavor. It's beautifully complemented by the freshness of cabbage, tomatoes, avocado, and a zesty Sriracha mayo. Additionally, I've indulged in their delectable katsu and curry chicken dishes. Each bite bursts with rich and flavorful goodness. And let's not forget about their remarkable Thai tea - it's absolutely on point! It's truly incredible how much this small food truck has to offer. Despite residing in Jersey, I have driven here numerous times solely to savor their exceptional meals. Not only is the food incredible, but the staff is remarkably friendly, providing excellent cuisine at an unbeatable price.

input: I was having an bad migraine and felt terrible. When woke up I had a sinus infection and my day was just going awful. I called a few places to try to get a massage in today because I knew indeed it badly. No one had any availability and I stumbled across massage envy on Google and thought to give them a try. Not only were they able to fit me in with the exact specific type I needed, but they also were able to fit my father in at the exact same time. Jen was understanding and nice, she asked me questions and checked up on me constantly. She even showed me some at home techniques I could use. She took her time, obviously did not rush. Carrie, I believe, was the name of the woman who did a foot massage on my father. He was very pleased and recommended I try it sometime. They also informed me about the membership program which not only is very cost-efficient, but also adheres to my busy schedule. I signed up on the spot with no hesitation. Friendly staff, great atmosphere, comfortable building and very calming environment! Would recommended! I feel so much better already and am going back in a month to get a 90 minute massage.
Revise this with your best effort:
I woke up with a terrible migraine and felt absolutely terrible. Along with that, I discovered that I had a sinus infection, making my day even worse. Desperate for some relief, I called around, hoping to find a place that could squeeze me in for a massage today. Unfortunately, everywhere I called had no availability. However, I stumbled upon Massage Envy during a quick Google search and decided to give them a chance.

To my surprise, not only were they able to accommodate me with the specific type of massage I needed, but they also managed to schedule my father at the exact same time. Jen, the masseuse, was incredibly understanding and pleasant. She took the time to ask me questions about my condition and checked on me frequently. In addition, she even taught me some helpful at-home techniques. It was evident that she didn't rush through the session and genuinely cared about my well-being.

As for my father, he received a foot massage from a skilled woman named Carrie. He was thoroughly satisfied with the experience and suggested that I try it sometime. Moreover, the staff at Massage Envy informed me about their membership program, which not only offers cost-efficient options but also accommodates my busy schedule. Impressed by everything I had experienced, I wasted no time signing up for a membership without any hesitation.

The staff at Massage Envy was incredibly friendly, and the overall atmosphere of the establishment was great. The building itself was comfortable, and the environment inside was calming, allowing me to truly relax. I highly recommend giving them a try. Already, I feel so much better, and I plan on returning in a month for a 90-minute massage.

input: This place is good~  The chicken is moist, the skin is crispy, the flavor is nice and smokey, this is the best kind of roast chicken I have tried. The smells (smokey, bbq) is so good and hypnotizing, just make my mouth water.  I got the double chicken family which is 2 whole chickens, literally a bed of fries underneath them, and cole slaw.  It was more than enough to feed a family of four.  The dipping sauces that come with it are also real good, i really like the mustard base one, its kinda mustardy with a chipotle flair, and there is also a green sauce that is like a salsa.  The fries are wedge fries and they make you real full because there are plenty to go around. We had leftovers because the meal was that big.  I would rather eat here than popeyes or kfc, because you get more, its healthier, and you get better service. The owners are real nice and friendly. I will be back because I know I will be craving this chicken.
Revise this with your best effort: This place exceeds all expectations! The roast chicken here is truly outstanding - succulent, with a perfectly crispy skin and a delightful, smoky flavor. Its mesmerizing aroma filled with smoky BBQ notes never fails to make my mouth water. I opted for the double chicken family meal, which comprised two whole chickens resting on a bed of delectable fries, accompanied by a side of refreshing coleslaw. This generous portion was more than sufficient to satisfy a family of four. The assortment of dipping sauces that accompany the meal also impressed me greatly. The mustard-based sauce, with its subtle chipotle twist, was particularly to my liking. Additionally, there is a vibrant green sauce reminiscent of salsa that adds an extra layer of zestiness to the experience. The wedge fries are so abundant that they leave you feeling gratifyingly full. In fact, the portion size was so generous that we had leftovers. Comparing this establishment to Popeyes or KFC, I can confidently say that this place offers more value, healthier options, and superior service. The friendly and welcoming owners only amplify the wonderful dining experience. Without a doubt, I will return here whenever the craving for this exceptional roast chicken strikes.

input:
This is as close to Japanese cuisine I get! I'm not a big fan of sushi, sashimi or maki, but I really enjoy their rice bowls and tempura. This location is not terribly busy so you won't have to wait in line for too long. 

They also provide catering options so you can have sushi and maki platters at your functions.

The service has always been good, for fast food. And I know I can keep somewhat on my eating plan when I go here. It's a fast lunch or dinner if you're in a hurry to.
Revise this with your best effort:

Additionally, they offer catering services, ensuring that you can enjoy sushi and maki platters at your special events or functions.

The service has consistently been commendable, considering the fast-food nature of the establishment. Moreover, I appreciate that I can somewhat stick to my dietary plan when I dine here. Whether you're in a rush for a quick lunch or dinner, this place never fails to deliver prompt service.

input:
5 STAR FOOD! 
For sure one of if not the best place to get a sandwich on the beach anywhere between St Pete Beach & Clearwater Beach. All orders cooked to order. Super Size, gourmet servings and great very friendly service from the owner. Artison sandwiches for the price of Subway. Great cook with well seasoned sauces and dips usually. I always go for the daily special. Today was 3 Shrimp taco's for $6.00 The shrimp were cooked perfectly and served on fresh corn tortillas with a Kiwi sauce with some fresh peppers. Just enough spice and fruit with the shrimp. DELICIOUS. I could have had 6 they were so good. Only drawback is this place is walk up with only bench seating outside. Not a problem given the food quality for me personally but some may p[refer to sit at a table. It's on the bench or to go. A great place if you are staying at one of the local hotel to walk to. I hear they will start delivering soon. This is a local favorite for me.
The only reason I did not give 5 stars overall as the seating may be an issue for some.
Revise this with your best effort:
5 STAR FOOD!

Without a doubt, this is the ultimate destination for sandwich lovers along the stunning stretch between St Pete Beach and Clearwater Beach. Every order is impeccably prepared to meet your individual preferences. The portions are generously sized, boasting gourmet ingredients that surpass your average fast-food joint. What truly sets this place apart is the incredibly warm and welcoming service provided by the owner. You'll feel like a cherished guest from the moment you step in.

Indulge in their artisan sandwiches, which come at a fraction of the cost you would expect at a typical sandwich chain. The chef here is a true culinary artist, infusing each creation with perfectly seasoned sauces and dips. Be sure to opt for the daily special; today's treat was a tantalizing trio of shrimp tacos for just $6.00. Impeccably cooked and delicately presented on fresh corn tortillas, these shrimp are enhanced by a delectable Kiwi sauce and a touch of fresh peppers. The marriage of flavors, with just the right amount of spice and fruitiness, is unparalleled. In fact, they were so incredible that I could easily have devoured double the amount!

The only drawback to this remarkable establishment is its limited seating arrangements. It's strictly walk-up service with only bench seating available outside. Personally, this doesn't bother me at all, given the outstanding quality of the food. However, for some, the option of sitting at a table may be preferable. No matter what, though, you can enjoy your scrumptious meal either on the bench or take it to go.

Conveniently located within walking distance of many local hotels, this gem is perfect for vacationers seeking an unforgettable dining experience. As an added bonus, I've heard through the grapevine that they will soon offer delivery service, making it even more accessible. Rest assured, this spot holds a special place in the hearts of locals, myself included.

While I hold nothing but praise for this extraordinary eatery, I have opted to give it four stars overall due to the potential seating issue. However, if you prioritize exceptional food over seating arrangements, this outstanding establishment will undoubtedly earn your full five-star rating.
