input:
We had dinner here after a long day at the convention center.  We asked to sit in a quieter area, and they found us a nice table in a side room.  Service was attentive and professional.  Our waiter recommended the aged ribeye steak--"best steak ever."  I didn't think I wanted an entire 18-ounce boneless, so he suggested we split it.  We did--certainly one of the "best steaks ever"--cooked perfectly medium rare and it was plenty for both of us.  Of course, we also had the signature shrimp cocktail (horseradish) and the iceberg lettuce wedge with crumbled bacon (very pancetta-like).   OK, iceberg wedge isn't the most exciting salad, but it's great when done well, which this was.  
   My only disappointment was a wine list that had a very limited choice of medium-priced wines by the bottle, so wine selection took a while.  A small complaint, so I would rate H & I  4.5 stars if possible.
Revise this with your best effort:
After a long day spent at the convention center, we decided to have dinner at this establishment. We requested a quieter setting and were pleased when they accommodated us by offering a lovely table in a side room. The service we received was attentive and professional throughout the evening.

Our waiter, in particular, was exceptional and recommended the aged ribeye steak, confidently claiming it to be the best steak on offer. Initially wary of the hefty 18-ounce boneless serving, he suggested we split it between the two of us. To our delight, the steak lived up to its reputation as one of the best we've ever tasted. Cooked to a perfect medium rare, it proved to be both succulent and plentiful for both diners. Accompanying our main dish were the restaurant's signature shrimp cocktail, with a delightful horseradish kick, and the iceberg lettuce wedge topped with crumbled bacon, resembling the flavors of pancetta. While the iceberg wedge may not be the most adventurous salad choice, it was executed flawlessly, showcasing its potential when prepared with care.

Regrettably, our only letdown was the wine selection. The limited choice of medium-priced wines by the bottle slowed down our decision-making process. Despite this minor setback, it is important to acknowledge that H & I's overall experience deserves a commendable 4.5-star rating, had it been an option.

input: The worst Italian food I have ever tasted!!! I'm far from Italian, but I can make a MEAN lasagna & spaghetti myself compared to this place. 1st of all, we waited 45mins patiently w/ a hungry Hubby, 2yr old, 7yr old, & myself. When we finally got seated, the waitress was very polite, but forgetful at times. Didnt drink any alcohol or sodas but the lemonade was very tart & the garlic bread was not-so-fresh...had to request for some fresh bread after my family devoured the 1st basket from starving & waiting for so long. I ordered the stuffed shells & chicken parmagiana. The salad was very tasty; however, they only have Italian dressing...no ranch or anything else. I am not a picky eater & rarely complain, but the stuffed shells & parmagiana chicken tasted HORRIBLE!! The chicken was very bland & the stuffed shells were hard & overbaked. The meranera sauce tasted like it was old or aged too long (if there's ever such a thing, lol). I could not bring myself to eat my entree. I had to send it back. I heard the lady at the table next to ours say the salmon was good, so I figured the salmon might be safe. It was actually very good! I was still very disappointed after this restaurant was referred to me by many. I felt like they got an easy $50 bucks out of me. I would have rathered gone to the olive garden or macaroni grill. If u r looking for an awesome authentic Italian cusine restaurant in Tucson, I highly recommend Contessa off of Ina Rd. The only reason we didn't go there is b/c it was out of the way from where we were going.  It's pretty far from where we live but always worth the drive. Everything is freshly made & u can definite tell the difference! I'm sorry Caruso, but I don't think my family will be coming here ever again!
Revise this with your best effort:
The Italian food at this place was absolutely terrible! Despite not being Italian myself, I can confidently say that I can make a much better lasagna and spaghetti than what they served here. Firstly, we had to wait for a painstaking 45 minutes with a hungry husband, a 2-year-old, a 7-year-old, and myself. Finally, when we were seated, the waitress was polite, but she seemed to forget things at times. We didn't order any alcoholic beverages or sodas, but the lemonade was ridiculously tart, and the garlic bread was far from fresh. In fact, we had to request for a fresh basket of bread after devouring the first one while starving and waiting for far too long.

I opted for the stuffed shells and chicken parmagiana, but they were an absolute disaster. The salad was the only saving grace as it was quite tasty. However, it was disheartening that they only had Italian dressing and no other options like ranch. Now, I'm not usually a picky eater and rarely complain about food, but the stuffed shells and chicken parmagiana were absolutely revolting. The chicken lacked any flavor or seasoning, and the stuffed shells were incredibly overbaked and hard. To make matters worse, the marinara sauce tasted old or even past its expiration date (if that's even possible, haha). I couldn't even bear to take a bite of my main course, so I had to send it back.

I overheard the lady at the next table praising the salmon, so I figured maybe it would be a safe option. Surprisingly, it was quite good. Nevertheless, I still felt very disappointed since this restaurant had been recommended to me by several people. It seemed like they easily conned me out of $50 without a second thought. I would have much preferred going to Olive Garden or Macaroni Grill instead. If you're on the hunt for an amazing, authentic Italian restaurant in Tucson, I highly recommend Contessa off of Ina Rd. It's a bit of a trek from where we live, but it's always worth it. Everything there is freshly made, and you can definitely taste the difference!

I apologize, Caruso, but it's safe to say that my family will never be returning to your establishment.

input:
If you are looking to be impressed by French-German dishes in New Orleans, please go to Luke Restaurant, I know I was. 

The restaurant is located in the Central Business District, next to the Hilton and in the former Masonic Temple Building, so there is that historic vibe to the restaurant. The front room is a lot more grand than the back room (where we were seated), but that is offset by views of the open kitchen. 

Apparently they only want to seat people with reservations, so since we did not have one, we were refused seating until 9:15pm (it was 6:45pm) but with a little back and forth, we ended up waiting only 15 minutes before we were seated. However, as we walked through the restaurant to the back room, way too many tables were empty that it made no sense that they acted that way. A lot of tables still remained empty throughout the meal.

I decided to start out my meal with a cocktail. I originally wanted the Mint Julep but they were out so I had the Riverbend (vodka, lemon juice, basil syrup, blueberries & ginger ale) at the recommendation of the server. It was a relatively sweet cocktail, with the ginger ale being the most powering flavor, but you could still taste the alcohol.

My friend choose a regular starter and ordered a cup of the Crawfish Bisque. She ate all of it so I am assuming she liked it, but she did complain of a sour aftertaste.

My boyfriend skipped the appetizers and went straight for the entree. He always seems to find the most basic item on the menu and order it. He had the Luke Burger (bacon, caramelized onions, tomatoes, Swiss cheese) and was raving about it. One thing I can tell you, it was a very good size. 

My friend had the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" with lump crab meat, roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausages. She loved it.

I have an obsession with mussels so I had the classic Moules et Frites. Although only having two simply ingredients (garlic & thyme) in the broth, the flavors stood out and the taste was a lot bolder than others I have had with a lot more ingredients. The house-made fries were scrumptious. These are the best kind.

Even with all that food, we still made room for dessert. We first had the Bread Pudding which was delicious but quite sweet. I am also not a fan of over sauced foods.

One wasn't enough so we also ordered the Bourbon Vanilla Bean Creme Brulee. It was superb and not too sweet which is a plus for me. The little cookies on top added nothing to the dessert and if anything could have been left off.

All that good food, I still have to give props to our server. He was amazing and engaging. The front desk soured the mood a little bit a first but he more than made up for it. I couldn't have asked for anyone better.
Revise this with your best effort:
If you're in search of French-German delights that will leave you impressed in New Orleans, do yourself a favor and visit Luke Restaurant. I can personally vouch for it.

Situated in the Central Business District, right by the Hilton and within the historic former Masonic Temple Building, the restaurant exudes a charming, vintage ambiance. Though the front room boasts grandeur, we were seated in the back room, which offered a lovely view of the open kitchen.

Upon arrival, we discovered that reservations were strongly encouraged, and as we hadn't made one, we were initially denied seating until 9:15pm, despite it being only 6:45pm. However, with a bit of negotiation, we managed to secure a table after just a 15-minute wait. Oddly enough, we noticed that numerous tables remained unoccupied throughout our meal, making their strict reservation policy seem rather unnecessary.

To kick off my dining experience, I opted for a cocktail. Although I had my heart set on the Mint Julep, it was unavailable. Nonetheless, our server recommended the Riverbend, a delightful concoction of vodka, lemon juice, basil syrup, blueberries, and ginger ale. This sweet libation leaned heavily on the ginger ale, yet managed to retain a noticeable alcohol kick.

My companion decided to start with a traditional favorite: the Crawfish Bisque. Judging by the fact that she polished off the entire cup, I can safely assume that she thoroughly enjoyed it, despite mentioning a slightly sour aftertaste.

My boyfriend, always one for simplicity, skipped the appetizers and went straight for the main course. True to form, he chose the Luke Burger, topped with bacon, caramelized onions, tomatoes, and Swiss cheese. He was absolutely enthralled by it, and I couldn't help but notice its generous portion size.

Meanwhile, my friend ordered the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" complete with lump crab meat, roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille, and green onion sausages. She couldn't have been happier with her choice.

As for me, I have an unwavering love for mussels, so naturally, I went for the classic Moules et Frites. Despite the simplicity of the broth (featuring only garlic and thyme), the flavors were bold and distinct, surpassing other versions I've tasted with numerous additional ingredients. The house-made fries were an absolute delight as well—their quality unmatched.

Despite our full bellies, we couldn't resist indulging in dessert. First, we savored the Bread Pudding, which, while delicious, leaned toward the sweeter side. Personally, I have a preference for less sauced dishes.

Not satisfied with just one sweet treat, we also ordered the Bourbon Vanilla Bean Creme Brulee. It proved to be simply superb, striking the perfect balance of sweetness. The tiny cookies adorning the top did little to enhance the dessert and could have been omitted entirely.

Despite the outstanding cuisine, I must commend our server for truly elevating the experience. He was exceptional, providing attentive and engaging service. Though our initial encounter with the front desk staff left something to be desired, our server more than made up for it. We couldn't have asked for a better dining companion.

Revise this with your best effort:
This place is absolutely incredible for enjoying cocktails! Admittedly, the prices are a tad steep for my budget, but the unique and visually appealing glassware is worth every penny. Indulging in their delectable concoctions, such as the enticing Dragon's Tear and captivating Blackmail, was an absolute delight. Oh, and there was another delightful drink that slipped my mind momentarily. Even my friends were left craving for more!

The ambiance of the venue is spot on, with the carefully selected music creating the perfect backdrop to the eclectic and relaxed decor. Although I wasn't particularly enthusiastic about their food selection, I am certainly eager to return solely for their exceptional drink offerings.

input:
I love it!  The reviews were great and I was desperate for good carry out, so we decided to try Pizzaville (is anyone else picturing JT singing - Bring it on down to Pizzaville?).  The prices are a bit high, but the quality of the food is great!  The pizza crust is between a hand tossed and thin crust.  Perfectly crunchy ends and just chewy enough in the middle.  Good quality cheese and tangy tomato sauce. I ordered it with just mushrooms and they put on a lot!   I also asked for heavy sauce.  They put extra sauce on the pizza and even gave me an extra container of sauce in case I needed more. 

I can't decide which was better, the pizza or "breadsticks."  I say "breadsticks" because they were really more like garlic bread strips.  So buttery and garlicy, they were great even without sauce.  I'm ashamed to say I ate nearly the entire order myself.  

The employees are very nice and helpful.  The store is clean. I need to go back and try their lunch buffet.
Revise this with your best effort:
I am absolutely thrilled with my recent experience at Pizzaville! After hearing rave reviews and being in dire need of a quality carryout option, my companions and I bravely decided to give Pizzaville a shot (anyone else envisioning JT singing - Bring it on down to Pizzaville?). While the prices leaned towards the higher end, the exceptional food undoubtedly made up for it.

The pizza crust struck the perfect balance between a hand-tossed and thin crust, resulting in delightful crispiness at the edges while maintaining a delectably chewy center. The cheese boasted excellent quality, complemented by a tangy tomato sauce that truly enhanced the overall flavor. Opting for a simple mushroom topping, I was pleasantly surprised by the generous amount of mushrooms added. Additionally, I requested extra sauce, and not only did they oblige by generously spreading it on the pizza, but they also included an additional container of sauce just in case I desired more.

Now, it's nearly impossible for me to pick a favorite between the pizza and what they call "breadsticks." Though I use the term "breadsticks," they were more akin to enticing strips of garlic bread. The sheer buttery and garlicky goodness of these treats made them absolutely satisfying even without any sauce. Embarrassingly enough, I must admit that I indulged in almost the entire order by myself - they were simply irresistible.

Furthermore, the employees at Pizzaville demonstrated exceptional friendliness and willingness to assist. The cleanliness of the store was a pleasant surprise, further proving their commitment to top-notch service. I am already looking forward to revisiting and exploring their highly recommended lunch buffet; I have a feeling it will be just as impressive.

input: The service was good and the staff was polite, but the food was bland and lacked flavor. The drinks were ok about what you would expect of a chain restaurant. If you are looking for somewhere to sit Down for a quick lunch this might be your place.
Revise this with your best effort: The service provided was commendable, and the staff exhibited politeness throughout. However, the food itself unfortunately fell short in terms of taste and lacked the desired flavor. The drinks, while not exceptional, were passable considering the establishment being a chain restaurant. If you are seeking a spot to grab a swift lunch, this particular venue might fit the bill.

input:
I thoroughly enjoyed the ambiance. The decor was modern and cozy. The lighting was appropriate for dinner but terrible for selfies lol. Our waiter was OK. He seemed to be very hyper and impatient. I almost felt like he was rushing to take care of us instead of genuinely trying to give us an experience. I ordered the Shrimp Breaux Bridge and it was tasty. Nothing to phone home about but it was good. My friend ordered the Balsamic Salmon and it was good as well. It kind of reminded me of an Asian dish. Another friend had the Pesto Crusted Idaho Trout. It was cooked and flavored very nicely. 

I also ordered the Zangria White which is a sangria that was supposed to include strawberries, blueberries and diced apples... and i only got apples. IF there is an item on the menu that contains SEASONAL FRUITS AND VEGGIES ETC.... DISCLOSE SOMEWHERE ON THE MENU THAT THOSE THINGS ARE OUT OF SEASON. It definitely wouldve made a difference in my drink order. But overall the sangria was OK. 

I would go back because Im sure the service is better that what I experienced and I have heard amazing things about the menu.
Revise this with your best effort:
I thoroughly enjoyed the cozy and modern ambiance of the restaurant. The decor added a nice touch to the overall atmosphere. The lighting, although suitable for dinner, was not the best for taking selfies, which provided a bit of a humorous moment. As for our waiter, he seemed to be quite hyper and impatient, giving off the impression that he was more focused on rushing through our dining experience rather than sincerely ensuring our satisfaction.

When it came to the food, I decided to try the Shrimp Breaux Bridge, which turned out to be quite tasty. While it wasn't necessarily a dish that left a lasting impression, it was still good. My friend opted for the Balsamic Salmon, which also received positive feedback. Interestingly enough, it had some Asian-inspired elements to its flavor profile. Additionally, another friend ordered the Pesto Crusted Idaho Trout, which was excellently cooked and had delightful flavors.

I also ordered the Zangria White, a sangria that was advertised to include strawberries, blueberries, and diced apples. However, much to my disappointment, I only received apples in my drink. It would have been appreciated if the menu had mentioned that certain ingredients, such as seasonal fruits and veggies, were not available. This information would have influenced my drink order. Nonetheless, the sangria itself was decent.

Despite the shortcomings I experienced, I would be willing to give this place another chance. I'm confident that the service can be better than what I encountered, and I've heard great things about their menu.

input:
Despite being a spin-off at the burgers from Rouge, I actually think that the burgers here are, dare I say it, better then flagship restaurants.
Over the last year they keep expanding their burger and toppings options by editing the little placard next to the registers, instead of changing their giant menuboard every time  they decide to add a new cheese or vegetable you can put on the burger.

I've been here a few times, trying the 500 (lettuce, bacon, cheddar, special sauce) delicious, and also making my own combos with their Kobe Beef burger (I think its worth the extra few bucks). I like it with truffle cheese and grilled onions. The brioche bun also really makes these burgers something special.

Their fries are also extremely delicious. As a huge fan of truffle oil, I can never resist getting their truffle oil fries. When they come warm out of the fryer, coated in truffle oil, there is just no better taste known to man.

Most important of all, they are open late on weekends.
Revise this with your best effort:
Despite being a spin-off of Rouge, I genuinely believe that the burgers here are, dare I say it, even better than those served at their flagship restaurants. What sets them apart is their continuous expansion of burger and toppings options. Instead of constantly changing their giant menuboard, they simply edit the little placard next to the registers whenever they introduce a new cheese or vegetable that can be added to the burger.

I have had the pleasure of visiting this place multiple times and have tried their 500 burger (lettuce, bacon, cheddar, special sauce), which was absolutely delicious. Additionally, I have experimented with creating my own combinations using their Kobe Beef burger, which I believe is worth the slight extra cost. Personally, I enjoy it with truffle cheese and grilled onions. The brioche bun they use adds an extra touch of excellence to these already outstanding burgers.

I must also mention their fries, which are incredibly delectable. As an avid fan of truffle oil, I find it irresistible to not indulge in their truffle oil fries. When these fries come fresh out of the fryer, coated in truffle oil, it creates a taste that is unparalleled and simply divine.

Perhaps the most significant aspect of this place is its late-night availability on weekends. This is a crucial factor for many, as finding a place that serves quality food during late hours can be quite a challenge.

input: Tried this place the other day the pizza was not very good at all the place before this one was so much better all home made food with it would've stuck around
Revise this with your best effort: I recently tried this place, but unfortunately, the pizza was not up to par. I personally found the previous place I visited to be far superior, as they offered a wide selection of homemade dishes. If only I had stuck to that place, I would have been more satisfied.

input: Stopped in for a quick lunch. Jalapeno burger was great.  Sittin' on the patio's pretty cool.  Definitely be back.
Revise this with your best effort: I swung by for a speedy lunch and must say that the jalapeno burger exceeded my expectations. The ambiance of the patio was delightful, adding to the overall experience. I will absolutely make a point to return in the future.

input:
I really, really, really like so much about this hotel. For starters, it's BEAUTIFUL!!  Everytime I go to Reno, this is where I stay and I will continue to stay here when I go!!

PRO's:

1. The Spa is amazing! The staff working there are so friendly and helpful.The pools in the spa area are so clean. There were plenty of towels, water, juice, etc. 

2. The rooms were very clean and organized. 

3. The front desk staff was very nice and helpful. We didnt like the location of our room, so they moved us to another location with no problems.

4. They have a little diner that is there open 24 hours and has good food. Granted its a bit expensive, but it's a casino, what do you expect?


CON's:

1. The bathrooms in the hotel rooms didnt have fans, so when you're in the shower it gets so steamy, so fast!

2. We ordered rooms services and we ordered coffee as well, and they didnt bring creamer.
Revise this with your best effort:
I absolutely adore this hotel in so many ways. Firstly, it is an absolute marvel to behold with its stunning beauty. Whenever I find myself in Reno, this is my go-to accommodation, and I plan on continuing to choose this establishment for all my future visits.

Now, let me elaborate on the pros:

1. The spa here is nothing short of incredible. The staff are exceptionally friendly and always ready to assist. The pools in the spa area are impeccably clean, and I was pleasantly surprised by the abundance of towels, water, and juice provided.

2. The rooms in this hotel are spotlessly clean and thoughtfully organized, creating a truly comfortable atmosphere.

3. The front desk staff deserves applause for their exceptional kindness and helpfulness. When we expressed dissatisfaction with our room's location, they promptly resolved the issue by relocating us. Their professionalism and efficiency were commendable.

4. The presence of a 24-hour diner on-site is undeniably convenient, offering delectable food options. Although the prices may be slightly higher due to the casino setting, it is to be expected and the quality of the food justifies the expense.

In terms of cons, there are a couple of minor inconveniences:

1. The hotel rooms unfortunately lack bathroom fans, leading to quick accumulation of steam while showering. This can be uncomfortable and make it difficult to maintain a pleasant temperature.

2. During our room service experience, we ordered coffee, but were disappointed to find that creamer was missing from the delivery. This oversight, though minor, did detract from an otherwise enjoyable service.

Overall, my affinity for this hotel remains unwavering, and I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone seeking a delightful and awe-inspiring experience in Reno.

input: It was great. The your was interesting if you're in to tours. The beer was good. The atmosphere was the best part. A couple of Tvs for sports, board games, live music, and yours every hours. At times it seems like there's a lot going on but it flowed well. Great spot for a good time with friends or a date.

input:
My personal favorite wine and liquor store in Nashville.  The staff is usually very friendly and helpful without being pretentious.  You can ask for a $10 dollar bottle of wine recommendation without being scoffed at.  The selection is good and the prices are comparable with other liquor stores in town.  

One negative, the curb is a little bit high pulling in.  Don't gun it unless you want to scrape some rust off of the bottom of your car.
Revise this with your best effort:
In Nashville, there is a wine and liquor store that stands out amongst the rest as my personal favorite. The staff consistently exhibits a friendly and helpful demeanor, effortlessly avoiding any air of pretentiousness. Regardless of your budget, you can confidently seek a recommendation for a $10 bottle of wine without facing any judgment or ridicule. input: When my daughter was about a year-and-a-half old, Linda, the owner, helped me out by taking her for a drop in a couple times. My daughter is now four and a half and I have a one-and-a-half-year-old son. I switched school districts from Carson to Washoe and I kept going to all of these other daycare places and not getting a great feel, as well as the fact that they were totally booked for having an infant\toddler. I needed a place for both of my kids and there was just no where for my son..... My gut kept telling me go back to Circle of Friends. I've been extremely happy. Are there always going to be kids who attended daycare that I do not agree with their behavior? absolutely! There is no way to get around that whether it is in school, daycare, or a sports team or some other organized deal. I try the best of my ability to not let those other children's behaviors influence my own and we talk about it. Well the best you can for a 4 year old! I really like Linda and the whole staff. She has a little turnover and I really like that. The first place that my kids were at in Carson had turn over all the time..... The second place was a home daycare so she didn't turn over herself, and the other place was a mother and daughter run joint as well. They had very little turnover. That's important to me that employees stick around. So, my kid has been flourishing both emotionally and academically. She's picking up things that I'm totally surprised about.... Like starfish have two stomachs and octopus have 9 brains.... I didn't believe her and I had to Google them! I didn't read the Yahoo review, but people are always going to have mixed situations with whatever's going on for them. All I know is that Linda and her daughter helped me out greatly when I was in need several years ago, and she helped me out greatly this time and it's been a great fit. I'm very happy and content.
Revise this with your best effort:
When my daughter was around eighteen months old, Linda, the owner, graciously helped me out by looking after her on a couple of occasions. Fast forward to the present, my daughter is now four and a half years old, and I also have a one-and-a-half-year-old son. Due to switching school districts from Carson to Washoe, I found myself searching for suitable daycare options for both of my kids. Unfortunately, I struggled to find a place that not only had availability for my son but also gave me a positive impression.

Despite my endeavors, my gut kept urging me to return to Circle of Friends. And I must say, I have been extremely satisfied with my decision. Of course, like any daycare setting or similar organized activities, there will always be children whose behavior I may not agree with. However, I make a conscious effort to not let those instances affect my own children's behavior. We discuss these situations as best as we can, considering my daughter's age of four.

One aspect I particularly appreciate about Circle of Friends is the minimal turnover of staff. In contrast, the first daycare my kids attended in Carson experienced constant employee turnover. The second place was a home daycare, so the situation remained stable in terms of staffing. The third place, run by a mother and daughter team, also had limited turnover. This consistency is crucial to me, and I find that my child has thrived both emotionally and academically in this environment.

I have been pleasantly surprised by my daughter's newfound knowledge, such as learning that starfish have two stomachs and octopuses have nine brains. Initially, I doubted her claims and had to resort to Googling to confirm her facts! Although I have not read the Yahoo review, it is understandable that people have differing opinions based on their personal experiences.

What matters most to me is that Linda and her daughter came to my aid when I needed help several years ago, and they have once again provided invaluable support. Circle of Friends has proven to be the perfect fit for my family, and I am genuinely happy and content with my decision.

input: Great new location on Central. Great staff and atmosphere! Looks like they have found a place where they will thrive.
Revise this with your best effort: Come discover the incredible new location on Central, boasting a truly outstanding staff and an ambiance that is second to none! It is evident that they have discovered the perfect place where they are destined to flourish.

input: Pretty average take-out chinese. Not bad, not the best, but id definitely eat there again. ***update--- just ate there again and they got our complex delivery perfect and the food was excellent! 5 stars now!!

input:
We've been going to the Rib Cook-Off for a few years now, but apparently I've never taken the time to review it. We have our day pretty much planned out before heading down there. 

We walk to the bus stop by our house, the bus takes us directly to the Sparks bus station for a whopping $2 each. No parking, no driving through crowds, and no paying for parking. Winning.

From the bus station, we head immediately to Great Basin to get a large Icky and Bitchin' Berry. Beer is a must for battling these crowds and the large beers are worth the price!

If you have the JA Nugget mobile app, it will tell you where every vendor is and show it on a map. No more mindless wandering looking for your favorite vendor. I don't have a favorite, but go off of recommendations from friends, co-workers, etc.

Some vendors take cards, but we always make sure to bring plenty of cash. 

Be sure to walk through the non-rib vendors too. We got a couple of hats this year, which are nice to have at the event, but are also great beach hats for next year.

Saturday was a whole day affair and required us taking a cab back home. But because there was practically no crowd on Monday, we were able to get a beer, some food, and still use our bus transfer to get back home. Food stops being served at 5:00 pm on Monday and the vendors also start selling off extra food at crazy cheap prices.
Revise this with your best effort:
Over the past few years, attending the Rib Cook-Off has become a tradition for us, yet I've neglected to review it until now. Prior to heading down there, we meticulously plan our day.

To begin, we walk to the bus stop near our house and take the bus straight to the Sparks bus station, paying a mere $2 per person. This eliminates the hassle of parking, navigating through crowds, and paying for parking. It's a win-win situation.

Once we arrive at the bus station, our first stop is always Great Basin, where we immediately grab a large Icky and Bitchin' Berry. It's essential to have a beer in hand to brave the sea of people, and the generous size of these beers is well worth the price.

For those who possess the JA Nugget mobile app, it conveniently provides information on the location of every vendor, displaying them on a map. No more aimless wandering in search of your preferred vendor. While I don't have a particular favorite, I rely on recommendations from friends and colleagues to guide my choices.

Although some vendors accept cards, we always make sure to bring ample cash. It's wise to explore the non-rib vendors as well. This year, we snagged a couple of hats, which not only serve us well at the event but also make fantastic beach hats for the following year.

On Saturday, we dedicated an entire day to the festivities, necessitating a cab ride back home. However, due to the significantly smaller crowd on Monday, we were able to enjoy a beer, grab some food, and still utilize our bus transfer to return home. It's worth noting that food service ends at 5:00 pm on Monday, and vendors often sell off their remaining food at remarkably discounted prices.

input:
Excellent food and bar. Slow service.

A friend and I stopped here during an evening of bar hopping in the CBD. We were seated promptly and given our menus, which are half-French, half-English. Not a big deal for anyone who can read French and/or has been living in Louisiana for a reasonable amount of time, but definitely something tourists should be wary of. I didn't have any alcohol because I was the designated driver, but I can say that their drink menu is extensive, and the bar was packed from the moment we arrived until the moment we left. 

This restaurant's biggest strength is it's food. I tasted their crab bisque, and had Poulet Grand-Mère as my entrée. Both were excellent. The latter arrived in a wide cast-iron bowl, which I'm sure has a more proper name, but was an interesting touch nonetheless.

The service was why I gave this restaurant 4/5 instead of 5/5. Most of the wait staff seemed to be interns from culinary school. The handful we dealt with were very friendly, but would do well to be a little more attentive. For example, the server who brought us our desserts ran off before we could ask for spoons to eat the dessert with. 

In summary, a good dining experience, but I think I would rather continue exploring new restaurants in the area before returning.
Revise this with your best effort:
My friend and I decided to visit this establishment while bar hopping in the CBD. We were promptly seated and handed menus that were a combination of French and English. While this may not be an issue for those familiar with the language or Louisiana culture, it might be worth noting for tourists. Unfortunately, I was unable to enjoy any alcoholic beverages as I was the designated driver, but their extensive drink menu and bustling bar indicated that they had a lively atmosphere.

Where this restaurant truly shines is in their food. I had the chance to try their delectable crab bisque and opted for the Poulet Grand-Mère as my main course, both of which were outstanding. The latter dish was even presented in a unique cast-iron bowl, adding a touch of novelty to the experience.

However, the service fell short compared to the exceptional food. It seemed that most of the wait staff were interns from culinary school. While friendly, they could benefit from being more attentive. For instance, the server who brought our desserts hurried off before we could request spoons to enjoy them with.

To summarize, it was a satisfying dining experience overall, but I feel inclined to explore other eateries in the area before revisiting this one.

input:
I had just moved to Nashville and one of my friends told me I HAD to come here. We're not both from here originally so technically we were still tourists at this point. Anyways, I went around 9:15 and the line wasn't too bad - I'd say a 5-10 minute wait. The food was awesome. I had the chocolate chip pancakes which were to die for. The sausage side I had didn't rock my world then again it's not the Side Dish Pantry. You don't pay at the table - they ring you up by the door to try and get people in and out fast which seems to work because the line is always moving fairly fast. 


Rip : I drive by it almost every morning - if you want to avoid the line go either RIGHT when they open to around 7:15
Revise this with your best effort:
My recent move to Nashville led me to discover this gem at the recommendation of a friend. Even though neither of us are from the area, we still felt like tourists exploring our new home. Arriving around 9:15, the line was thankfully not too long, only a 5-10 minute wait. Once inside, I was blown away by the amazing food. The chocolate chip pancakes were absolutely divine, but unfortunately, the sausage side didn't quite match up with my high expectations. However, it's worth noting that this place isn't called the Side Dish Pantry for a reason. Rather than paying at the table, the payment process happens by the door, which helps expedite things and keeps the line moving smoothly. 

As a regular passerby, I have noticed that arriving early in the morning, around the time they open or up until 7:15, is a smart way to avoid the usually bustling line.

input:
Came here for Sunday brunch and walked away with a very full belly and a good buzz! 

Their brunch buffet includes tons of seafood, an omelet station, pasta bar, carving station, custom sushi rolls, fresh fruit, salads, and the usually breakfast foods you'd expect at a buffet. I almost forgot dessert...an entire side of the room is dedicated to a table full of desserts AND a chocolate fountain. The brunch price also include bottomless mimosas which were literally bottomless. Our server never let us empty our glasses and  the mimosas were very heavy on the champagne, so we all got a bit tipsy. At least the alcohol let us forget how much weight we gained during this meal.

As if the buffet spread wasn't enough, they also have an a la carte menu with small dishes. The choices included Belgian waffles, french toast, blintzes, Mahi, and a few other savory dishes.  You can order as many of these items as you want, as many times as you want. Our server was sure to remind us of this, she seemed to enjoy watching how gluttonous our table was! 

Unfortunately we were here during Tropical Storm Debby, so we didn't get to enjoy a beautiful view of the bay, Although, being here while the weather was so awful was very cozy with the fireplace and wood interior. Thanks to the weather it wasn't crowded either, so don't write this place off on account of bad weather. 

At $35 a person, the Sunday brunch seems pricey, but if you have no qualms about overeating and overdrinking, you'll definitely get your money's worth.
Revise this with your best effort:
I had the pleasure of indulging in their Sunday brunch and left with a contented stomach and a delightful buzz! The brunch buffet offered an impressive assortment of seafood, an omelet station, pasta bar, carving station, made-to-order sushi rolls, fresh fruit, salads, and all the classic breakfast favorites you would expect. Oh, and let's not forget the desserts! An entire section of the room was dedicated to a tantalizing array of sweets, accompanied by a decadent chocolate fountain. In addition, the brunch price included bottomless mimosas that truly lived up to their name. Our attentive server ensured our glasses were never empty, and the mimosas were generously mixed with champagne, leaving us all happily euphoric. The alcohol served as a convenient distraction from the guilt of indulging in such an extravagant meal.

As if the buffet weren't enough, they also offered an a la carte menu featuring delectable options like Belgian waffles, French toast, blintzes, Mahi, and various savory dishes. Unrestricted by limitations, we were able to order as many of these dishes as our hearts desired, and our server seemed to revel in observing our unabashed gluttony.

Despite being unfortunate victims of Tropical Storm Debby, which cloaked the bay view in inclement weather, the comforting ambiance of the establishment, with its cozy fireplace and inviting wooden interior, made up for the lackluster scenery. The silver lining to the dismal weather was the absence of crowds, proving that one should not dismiss this place solely based on the forecast.

At first glance, the price tag of $35 per person may seem steep for a Sunday brunch, but for those unburdened by concerns of overeating and overindulging, it is undoubtedly a worthy investment that guarantees a lavish experience.

input: We were on our way home from a camping trip and decided to stop in Santa Barbara for some fish taco's last Tuesday!
