We did want to try the shrimp fish taco's and asked if we could get 2 on the side. The kitchen was more than accommodating and gave us a whole platter of delicious battered shrimp. We sat outside on the veranda, enjoying our yummy food and the lovely December weather. The next time we are in Santa Barbara, we will definitely be making a pitstop here again.  The staff is also very friendly.
Revise this with your best effort: On our way back from a delightful camping trip, we made an impromptu decision to make a pitstop in Santa Barbara last Tuesday for some mouthwatering fish tacos! In our pursuit of a great spot, we discovered that this particular place ranked second for its delectable Baja fish tacos. To our pleasant surprise, our expectations were surpassed as we savored every bite of our scrumptious tacos. Intrigued by the shrimp fish tacos, we requested two on the side, and the kitchen graciously fulfilled our request by presenting us with an entire platter of delectably battered shrimp. Taking advantage of the beautiful December weather, we relished our flavorsome meal while basking in the outdoor ambiance of the veranda. Without a doubt, when we find ourselves in Santa Barbara in the future, we will make a point to revisit this gem. Additionally, the staff's warm and amiable nature only added to our memorable experience.

input:
I've been to Mount Laurel's On the Border over 50 times. I used to go to Don Pablo's but I fell in love with On the Border's chips and salsa (their chips are nice and salty, and their salsa is a little spicier).

When I go, 90% of the time I just sit at the bar and drink beer and snack on their chips and salsa. The beer specials are pretty good but could be a little better- weekdays has a happy hour as well as a late night happy hour too.

When I do dine, I often just enjoy a variety of vegetarian sides. Lately, I've grown to enjoy their cheese enchiladas, which I find delicious. Service when dining is usually great.

As for the bartenders, it's really hit-or-miss. Joann is probably my favorite- she's friendly, attentive, funny, and I've really gotten to know her, and I'd give them 5 stars if my experience was with her alone. There is a bartender named Nikki though, and if she's there, I always get the worst service. She barely checks on me/us to see how we're doing, she seems unfriendly, if she actually comes to refill your chips then she will not refill your salsa, she has taken my beer and refilled it without asking (when I was done and trying to leave), and I've had to wait forever to ask her for my check. At least twice, I've had to ask other bartenders to bring my check so that I could finally close out and leave. I'd give them 1 star if my experience was based on her alone.

Overall, good appetizers, cold beer, moderate prices, and usually good service.
Revise this with your best effort:
I have frequented On the Border in Mount Laurel more than 50 times, having switched my loyalty from Don Pablo's due to my adoration of On the Border's delectable chips and salsa. Their chips tantalize the taste buds with a perfect balance of saltiness and their salsa carries a delightful hint of spiciness.

During my visits, I typically choose to occupy a seat at the bar, indulging in their beer selection while relishing the chips and salsa. Although their beer specials are quite enjoyable, I believe they have some room for improvement. Weekdays offer both a happy hour and a late-night happy hour which adds to the appeal.

When I opt for a proper dining experience, I often revel in a variety of vegetarian sides that On the Border offers. Lately, I have developed a deep fondness for their cheese enchiladas as they never fail to satisfy my cravings. The service during my dining experiences has generally been fantastic.

The bartenders, however, have been a mixed bag. Joann stands out as my favorite, with her amiable nature, attentiveness, and sense of humor. If all my encounters were solely with her, I would gladly give them a perfect rating of 5 stars. Unfortunately, Nikki, another bartender, consistently provides the worst service. She rarely checks on me or my companions, seemingly unfriendly, and neglects to refill salsa if she bothers to refill chips. On one occasion, she even took my beer and refilled it without consent when I had finished it and was preparing to leave. Furthermore, I've had to wait excessively to request my check and, on multiple occasions, had to turn to other bartenders for assistance. If my experience was solely based on Nikki, I would reluctantly assign them just 1 star.

To summarize, On the Border excels in the realm of appetizers, offering delicious options, complemented by a refreshing array of cold beers. Their prices fall into a reasonable range, and the service is usually commendable.

input: This was a very busy place. Was told I had to try this place while I was in St Louis.  I was not disappointed. I got a peach shake that was amazing. The rest of my group tried a number of different options that they all enjoyed.  The wait was a little long especially on a very hot date. The prices were very reasonable.  The ordering at the window was confusing. Multiple windows with not a lot of direction of which line to get in and where to wait for the food. It's a great place to stop if you are in the area.
Revise this with your best effort: While I was in St Louis, I was recommended to try this bustling establishment, and it certainly lived up to its reputation. I opted for a peach shake, which was absolutely incredible, and the others in my group explored a variety of options, all of which they thoroughly enjoyed. Although the wait was a bit lengthy, particularly on a scorching hot day, the prices were quite fair. Nonetheless, the ordering process at the window proved to be a bit confusing, as there were multiple windows and a lack of clear guidance regarding which line to join and where to wait for the food. Nevertheless, if you find yourself in the area, this place is a must-visit stop.

input: Delicious food, sub-par service. I stopped into this dessert bar today to grab some dessert and a coffee to-go. While everyone seemed to be very helpful, or at least wanting to be, I'm not sure I received the best possible service. I ordered two slices of cake, one marshmallow chocolate and one cheesecake. Both were DELICIOUS, but it seemed like I waited forever to receive these, and when i did, it was in a cute but inefficient manner. The to-go boxes were stacked one on top of the other, with a loosely tied string around them. While I admire the aesthetics here, I would have much preferred a bag. Though, the worst part of my experience was the barista. I ordered an iced coffee with milk and sugar. First, he put ice in the cup and filled it halfway with coffee. He then asked me to pick and put in my own sugars from a cup of packets as he stated "I wouldn't know what and how much you want, I only drink my coffee black." As I considered this incompetent statement, i expected him to then put more hot coffee in to help the sugar dissolve. But no, he proceeded to fill the rest of the HALF OF THE CUP with milk. And then handing me the drink he told me I'd better stir it to mix the cream and sugar in. Not sure why I'd paid such a high price to practically make my own half-coffee half-mild beverage, I simply smiled and walked away. I ended up throwing out the drink as I could hardly even taste the coffee and I'm not too fond of a lot of milk in my coffee. Nonetheless, the cakes were delicious, and I will be coming back with the hopes that this new business is still in the process of improving itself.
Revise this with your best effort:
Despite the delectable food, the service at this dessert bar fell short of my expectations. While the staff appeared eager to assist, I can't say that I received the utmost level of service. I ordered two slices of cake: a marshmallow chocolate and a cheesecake. Both slices were absolutely scrumptious, but the wait was interminable, and when I finally received them, it was in a charming yet inefficient manner. The to-go boxes were stacked on top of each other, secured only by a loosely tied string—a visually pleasing arrangement, but I would have preferred a more practical bag.

However, the most disappointing aspect of my experience was the barista. I requested an iced coffee with milk and sugar. To my bewilderment, he started by putting ice in the cup and filling it halfway with coffee. Then, instead of adding the sugar himself, he handed me a cup of sugar packets and asked me to do it myself, citing his lack of knowledge of my preference. Astonishingly, he did not even attempt to dissolve the sugar by adding more hot coffee but went on to fill the remaining half of the cup with milk. To top it off, he handed me the drink and advised me to stir it to mix the cream and sugar. Paying a premium price for a beverage only to essentially prepare my own half-coffee, half-milk concoction was disheartening. Despite my disappointment, I smiled politely and walked away. Regrettably, the drink ended up in the trash as the overpowering milk drowned out any semblance of coffee flavor—something I am not particularly fond of.

Nevertheless, I do acknowledge that the cakes were delectable. I remain hopeful that this new establishment is still refining its operations and I will visit again, expecting an improved experience.

input: I cannot say enough about the accommodations at the JW. I was working a trade show in the Grand Ballroom today and needed to pump as I am a new mom. Nathan was so quick to help as I was searching for a location that I could use. He opened up a boardroom for me to use and locked it behind me so I would not be disturbed. I know there was at least one other mom that was accommodated at the same time I was. All of the facilities, as well as the boardroom, were impeccably clean. I am so grateful for how kind and wonderful the staff was. Big kudos to the JW and the staff for making such awesome arrangements to support working moms- totally made my day!
Revise this with your best effort:
I cannot express enough how impressed I am with the accommodations at the JW. Today, while working at a trade show in the Grand Ballroom, I found myself in need of a private space to pump, being a new mom. In my search for a suitable location, I couldn't have asked for a more prompt and helpful staff member than Nathan. He quickly arranged for a boardroom to be opened for me, ensuring that I wouldn't be disturbed by anyone during this important task. It was comforting to know that I wasn't the only mom being accommodated, as there was at least one other individual in a similar situation. Moreover, both the boardroom and all other facilities were impeccably clean, which only heightened my satisfaction.

I am incredibly grateful for the kindness and exceptional service provided by the staff at the JW. Their efforts in making such thoughtful arrangements to support working moms truly brightened my day. My heartfelt appreciation and big kudos go out to the JW and its staff for going above and beyond to create a welcoming and supportive environment.

input:
I visited Joe's on consecutive nights, one with a Living Social coupon.  The beef tacos on the appetizer menu were outstanding, and a great price which will ensure I order them every time I come.  Meatloaf and mashed potatoes were just as I expected; thankfully, no attempt to "fancy them up"; just tasty comfort food.  I asked for French dressing and bleu cheese crumbles on my salad, and they were generous with the cheese.  The salad was cold and fresh and crisp.

The reason I did not give five stars was the service. The first night, we weren't told of specials (ugh, saw them on the way out and would have ordered them!), and my friend's appetizer order was wrong. Drinks were not refilled often enough, and the waitress seemed uninformed about some of the items.  The next night, different waitress. We were one of only two tables, and still waited too long for her to return. She was unable to answer a question about a menu item, as well.

The place is beautiful, and the bathroom was clean and bright.  The menu offers many thoughtfully composed choices. Some of your servers are not up to par.
Revise this with your best effort:
During my recent visits to Joe's, I dined there on consecutive nights, taking advantage of a Living Social coupon on one occasion. The appetizer menu particularly caught my attention, and the beef tacos stood out as exceptional. Not only were they delicious, but the price point was also fantastic, guaranteeing that I will be ordering them every time I return. Additionally, the meatloaf and mashed potatoes lived up to my expectations, providing me with a satisfying and comforting meal. I appreciated that they weren't unnecessarily transformed into something fancy; they remained true to their roots as tasty comfort food. 

When it came to my salad, I requested French dressing and bleu cheese crumbles, and Joe's was quite generous with the cheese. The salad itself was refreshingly cold, fresh, and delightfully crisp.

Regrettably, I must note that I did not give Joe's a perfect five-star rating due to the subpar service. On the first night, we were not informed about the specials, which was disappointing as we noticed them on our way out and would have gladly ordered them. Furthermore, my friend's appetizer order was incorrect, and the frequency of drink refills left something to be desired. The waitress also seemed uninformed about certain menu items, which was disconcerting. The following night, we had a different waitress, but unfortunately, the service did not improve. Despite being one of only two tables occupied, we waited an unacceptably long time for her to return, and she was unable to provide a satisfactory answer to a question about a menu item.

Despite this drawback, I must commend Joe's for its beautiful ambiance. The establishment is aesthetically pleasing, and the clean and bright bathroom experience was appreciated. Additionally, the menu offers a multitude of thoughtfully composed choices for diners. However, it is crucial for Joe's management to address the issue of underperforming servers to elevate the overall dining experience.

input:
Food is excellent!
People are welcoming, choices are long list. Sandwiches have great meat in them. Hand made toasted ravioli is some of the best in town.
Revise this with your best effort: The food quality here is truly exceptional! Not only that, but the warm hospitality of the people is truly welcoming. The array of options available is extensive and diverse. One cannot overlook the sandwiches, which boast succulent cuts of meat that are simply outstanding. Additionally, it's worth mentioning that the handcrafted toasted ravioli offered here is regarded as some of the finest in town.

input: With all the talk of bbq tips, sweetie pie, etc of St. Louis...I decided to try this place after flying in. The customer service was great, they make their own BBQ sauce which is between a sweet, tangy with pinch of spice. It could be considered overpowering if not used to it. The pull pork sandwich was recommended along with beans and Cole slaw. Again, this could be too much for one who has never tried it and/or intake this type of food on a daily basis.
Revise this with your best effort: After hearing all the buzz about St. Louis' barbecue tips and sweetie pies, I made it a point to try out this place upon my arrival. The customer service exceeded my expectations, and what intrigued me even more was their homemade BBQ sauce - a delightful blend of sweetness, tanginess, and a hint of spice. However, for those unaccustomed to these flavors, it might come across as overwhelming. The pulled pork sandwich, accompanied by flavorful beans and refreshing coleslaw, was highly recommended. I must note though, that this combo might be too hearty for someone unacquainted with such cuisine or those not accustomed to indulging in it regularly.

input: They call a chicken salad sandwich two cubes of chicken with mayo in it and a salad with a salad that is a bowl Of lettuce a salad? Hmm left here hungry....
Revise this with your best effort: Is it just me, or is it quite underwhelming to refer to a chicken salad sandwich as merely two cubes of chicken mixed with mayo, and a salad being a bowl of lettuce? It leaves me feeling quite famished, to be honest...

input:
We had a very nice brunch here. The food was consistently quite good and the service was pretty efficient and courteous. The omelets were sumptuous, the beverages fun (including a bloody mary bar.. we did have to ask for fresh bacon as it had run out). 

I did the budget breakfast which hit the spot with scrambled eggs, roaster taters, and a sweet muffin. The fish tacos were also good. Nice al fresco dining on the patio.
Revise this with your best effort:
We thoroughly enjoyed our experience at this establishment, particularly during our delightful brunch. The food consistently exceeded our expectations with its delectable flavors, and the service provided was efficient and filled with cordiality. The omelets were undeniably sumptuous, and we were thrilled by the array of enjoyable beverages, including the enticing bloody mary bar. However, it is worth mentioning that we did have to request fresh bacon since it had momentarily run out.

Opting for the budget breakfast, I found myself wholly satisfied with the scrambled eggs, roasted taters, and a delectably sweet muffin that truly hit the spot. Additionally, the fish tacos proved to be an excellent choice, delivering a satisfying taste. Furthermore, the lovely ambiance of the patio offered a relaxing al fresco dining experience.

input: I would eat anything they served me. I haven't even had the pancakes yet and I'm sold. The line out the front door and down the sidewalk should be an indication that this place is awesome. I just had basic hashbrowns eggs and bacon, but it was so fab and the service was great! I will definitely go back and sit down to eat. Parking is a little difficult around there, but that's to be expected.
Revise this with your best effort: I am willing to indulge in whatever culinary delights they have to offer. Although I have yet to try their pancakes, I am already convinced of their excellence. The lengthy queue extending from the entrance, all the way down the sidewalk, serves as a clear testament to this establishment's incredible reputation. For my first visit, I opted for a simple combination of hashbrowns, eggs, and bacon, yet it proved to be an absolutely fabulous meal accompanied by impeccable service. Without a doubt, I will return to dine in and relish in their offerings. Of course, locating convenient parking in that area can be slightly challenging, but it is to be expected in such a popular spot.

input: I just got C & B's via Order Up Delivery Svc and what a perfect wintry in home dinner. I ordered the Swanky Frank w/ fries and completely enjoyed my loaded up frank. The fries had a little seasoning on them which added a nice touch. I also ordered a lg bowl of beef chili just because I had to have some chili from a chili house. It was nicely pkg'd and I plan on having a late night snack w/some chili later. I requested the sour cream and crackers on the side for warming. I would 100% suggest using Order Up for some cozy chili at home this winter!
Revise this with your best effort:
I just had the most delightful winter dinner at home with C & B's, thanks to Order Up Delivery Svc. Their service was impeccable, and I couldn't be happier with my experience. I decided to try their Swanky Frank with fries, and it exceeded all expectations. The frank was loaded with delicious toppings, and the fries had just the right amount of seasoning to add a delightful touch. 

On top of that, I couldn't resist ordering a large bowl of their beef chili. Being a fan of chili, I had high expectations, and I must say, it didn't disappoint. The chili was carefully packaged, ensuring its freshness upon arrival. I plan on indulging in a late-night snack with some chili later, accompanied by sour cream and crackers that I specifically requested on the side for maximum enjoyment.

If you're looking for a cozy and satisfying chili experience at home this winter, I wholeheartedly recommend utilizing Order Up. Their prompt and reliable service, combined with the mouthwatering dishes they offer, will surely make for an unforgettable dining experience.

input: Great rich food,  but a lil bit pricey.  Everything tastes wonderful but nothing stays the same the menu is always changing.  The most unique donuts you will find.
Revise this with your best effort: While the food is undeniably exceptional and indulgent, it can come with a somewhat high price tag. The ever-changing menu adds an element of excitement to every visit, as you never know what delicious surprises await. Standout among them all are the incredibly distinct and unparalleled donuts on offer.

input:
After visiting with friends and indulging in lots of tastes, consider this my next order at Livery:

(01) Carriage House Margarita with its brandy twist
(02) All of the empanadas because I have no shame
(03) The Red Drum - it's a lovely fish dish, and it's a way to get a taste of the yuca fries.
(04) Churros (Take my advice and don't split 'em with anyone.)

Feel free to copy my order on your visit.
Revise this with your best effort:
After enjoying a delightful time with friends and experiencing a plethora of flavors, I have carefully curated my next order at Livery:

1. The Carriage House Margarita with its delightful brandy twist is an absolute must.
2. Indulge shamelessly in all of the empanadas because they are simply irresistible.
3. Treat yourself to The Red Drum, a delightful fish dish that also offers a wonderful opportunity to savor the delectable yuca fries.
4. Lastly, when it comes to the churros, my advice is to savor them all for yourself and not to share with anyone.

Feel free to follow my recommendation during your visit and enjoy an extraordinary culinary experience.

input:
My son and I went in for burgers after a long day's drive returning him to Nashville for the upcoming semester. We were in need of immediate sustenance after a long fast. What we found was a busy place that actually knew how to operate with a full house. Our need were quickly satisfied with courteous and reasonably priced service. 

Since we were just two, we were quickly seated. We started off with a couple Highland stouts. It was a nice drink and at a reasonable price. Before our entree, we shared a large garden salad. It was fresh and flavorful. The dressing was a bit on the heavy side for a vinaigrette. 

For entrees, I had the Black and Blue burger with fries. The burger was just incredible. It was perfectly cooked. The blue cheese was not overpowering. The bun was soft and fresh. The side of regular fries were crisp and lightly salted. Even better, they went perfectly with the homemade ketchup. I'm not a fan of ketchup, but theirs is very nice since they seem to avoid adding too much sweetness. My son had a basic burger with sweet potato fries. I tried the sweet potato fries and think they might be some of the best I've ever eaten. The burger looked as good as mine and my son concurred. 

The burger was well made and consumed within minutes. No words were spoken as we ate. Always a good sign. We shall return.
Revise this with your best effort:
After a long day's drive returning my son to Nashville for the upcoming semester, hunger struck both of us urgently. Thankfully, we stumbled upon a bustling restaurant that knew how to handle a full house. With efficiency and pleasant service, our needs were promptly satisfied without breaking the bank.

Since our party consisted of just the two of us, we were seated swiftly and wasted no time in ordering a couple of Highland stouts. The drinks, reasonably priced, proved to be a delightful choice. Prior to diving into our main courses, we decided to share a generous portion of fresh and flavorful garden salad. While the vinaigrette dressing leaned towards the heavier side, it was a small critique amidst the overall satisfaction.

As for our entrees, I opted for the Black and Blue burger accompanied by a portion of crispy fries. The burger, an absolute masterpiece, was flawlessly cooked, striking a harmonious balance with the subtly tangy blue cheese. The bun itself was delightfully soft and fresh. The regular fries served as a perfect sidekick, boasting a pleasing crispiness with just the right amount of salt. However, the true revelation emerged in the form of their homemade ketchup, which pleasantly surprised even a non-ketchup enthusiast like myself by avoiding excessive sweetness. On the other hand, my son opted for a classic burger partnered with sweet potato fries. I couldn't resist trying a few of the latter, and I must say they may rank among the best I've ever had. Judging by both appearances and my son's agreement, his burger was just as impeccable as mine.

Within minutes, our burgers were devoured, the silence at our table serving as a testament to their exceptional taste. Without a doubt, this gastronomic experience left us eager to return.

input: Nothing more to say than this is the BEST donut place ever. I literally wished they shipped their products. When I moved to Florida, I missed it so much. It's only in New Orleans... sad face!
Revise this with your best effort: There is truly no better way to describe it than as the ultimate donut haven. This place is unparalleled in its mouth-watering creations, leaving me with nothing more to say than it is the absolute BEST donut place in existence. Every bite is pure bliss, making me genuinely yearn for the ability to have their delectable treats shipped to my new home in Florida. The mere thought of their absence leaves me filled with a deep sense of longing. Alas, this extraordinary establishment can only be found in the enchanting city of New Orleans, and it renders a melancholic expression upon my face.

input: Katie's is a neighborhood restaurant that has existed in one form or another for a few generation.  It's classic New Orleans fare with an Italian-American slant.  Great meatballs.  You'll see all types of classic New Orleans old people dinging before 8pm.   You won't be disappointed if your expectations aren't too high.
Revise this with your best effort: Katie's is a charming neighborhood restaurant that has stood the test of time, serving classic New Orleans cuisine with an alluring Italian-American touch. Their meatballs are simply divine, leaving your taste buds craving for more. As you step into this establishment, you'll be surrounded by the delightful presence of traditional New Orleans locals, who typically arrive early in the evening to enjoy their meals. While it's important to set realistic expectations, you're unlikely to leave disappointed.

input: Excellent service! They were super fast, friendly and professional.  This is now my go to place for oil changes
Revise this with your best effort: Their service was absolutely outstanding! The staff was impressively efficient, welcoming, and displayed utmost professionalism. Without a doubt, this establishment has become my preferred destination for all future oil changes.

input:
If you're a Latino, you're best staying away from this place.
The lady that cut my hair was rude and very unprofessional.
Revise this with your best effort: If you identify as Latino, it is advisable to avoid this establishment. The woman responsible for cutting my hair displayed a discourteous and highly unprofessional demeanor.

input: This place should be on Restaurant Impossible. It's run down, the decor is tacky, beaten up, miss-matched and cheap. It's really dark...probably to hide how dingy it is. Everything was sticky. I ordered a burger medium and got a charred, tasteless hockey puck. My mom and aunt got the baked crab soup, which before we ordered, we misheard each other and called it baked crap soup. It turned out to be a better description. The crab stuffed mushrooms were heavy on the stuff and light on the crab.  The servers were super nice though.
Revise this with your best effort: This establishment desperately needs a visit from the Restaurant Impossible team. Its current state is beyond disrepair, with tacky and worn-out decor that clashes haphazardly and exudes a cheap vibe. The dim lighting seems to serve the sole purpose of concealing its dinginess. To make matters worse, sticky surfaces pervaded the entire place. Despite ordering a medium burger, what I received resembled a charred and flavorless hockey puck. In a comedic miscommunication, my mother and aunt accidentally referred to the baked crab soup as "baked crap soup" beforehand, and unfortunately, it turned out to be a more accurate description. Regrettably, the crab stuffed mushrooms were overwhelmed by excessive filling and lacked sufficient amounts of the anticipated crab. On a positive note, the servers were incredibly friendly and attentive throughout our experience.

input:
What can I say?  I'm a sucker for new american.  The owner is a very nice gentleman who really enjoys food.  

The service was impeccable and the food was Ridiculously good.  We ordered a mixed berry waffle, huevo rancho, traditional breakfast bagel with grits, and best sandwich with fresh fruits.  

I highly recommend the huevo rancho and best sandwich.  The grits was very good as well. 

If you decide to visit this restaurant, say hi to the owner.  He's a great guy.
Revise this with your best effort:
I have a weakness for New American cuisine, so it's no surprise that I found myself thoroughly enjoying this place. The owner, a genuinely kind gentleman, clearly has a passion for food. 

The service was truly exceptional, making the entire dining experience even more delightful. As for the food, it exceeded all expectations – it was simply outstanding. Our order consisted of a mixed berry waffle, huevo rancho, traditional breakfast bagel with a side of flavorful grits, and their renowned best sandwich accompanied by fresh fruits.

Allow me to highly recommend the huevo rancho and best sandwich; they were exceptional. I must also mention that the grits were a delightful surprise. 

Should you choose to pay this establishment a visit, do take a moment to say hello to the amiable owner. He truly adds to the wonderful atmosphere and experience.

input: Great place for happy hour. Oysters were deLISH! My friend and I had 2 dozen and we had some cocktails! The riverbend and champagne au poir we quite tasty. I had a side of fries and she had a side a grits. Best grits I've eaten. Definitely coming back. The server was great too. Just the right amount of attention!
Revise this with your best effort: This place is truly fantastic for happy hour. The oysters were absolutely delicious! My friend and I enjoyed two dozen of them along with some refreshing cocktails. The Riverbend and Champagne au Poire were particularly delightful. On top of that, I decided to get a side of fries while my friend opted for a side of grits. Let me tell you, those grits were the best I've ever tasted. I am definitely planning on returning soon. The server also deserves special mention as they provided just the right amount of attention and excellent service.

input:
The crew at Bella Vista Designs are FABULOUS.  From start to finish, they are professional, conscientious, and innovative (and affordable!).  They never cease to amaze me with their can-do attitude and absolutely gorgeous and creative design. 

The events at Santa Barbara Historical Museum and Goleta Valley Historical Society that I produce attract generous donors and they always say the same thing when they see their work, "Wow!!"  

I can't thank them enough for the hundreds of successful events (and the many magical moments we've seen)!
Revise this with your best effort:
The team at Bella Vista Designs is truly exceptional. Throughout every step of the process, they exhibit professionalism, dedication, and a remarkable ability to think outside the box (all within an affordable budget!). Their unyielding optimism and breathtakingly imaginative designs never fail to impress me.

The events I oversee at both the Santa Barbara Historical Museum and Goleta Valley Historical Society consistently draw in generous donors, who always find themselves in awe when they witness the transformation brought about by Bella Vista's work. Their creations elicit a resounding "Wow!!"

I cannot express enough gratitude for the countless successful events and the countless magical moments we have experienced thanks to Bella Vista Designs.

input: Moved to Tucson and needed a new dentist, everything went great here!
Revise this with your best effort: After relocating to Tucson, I found myself in need of a new dentist, and I couldn't be happier with the experience here!

input: Highly, highly overrated.  The food was a C minus at best.  And the service was so bad that I may never go back.  They screwed up my order completely and my no apologies.  There are a lot of other options around State Street.  Avoid this place like the plague.
Revise this with your best effort: This place is incredibly overrated. The food, to put it mildly, was subpar at best, deserving no more than a C minus. To make matters worse, the service was extremely disappointing, to the point where I have serious doubts about returning. They managed to completely mess up my order without offering any apologies whatsoever. Considering the abundance of alternative dining options available on State Street, it would be wise to steer clear of this establishment.

input:
Couldn't say it better than the below poster. Excellent food, service and prices.

Located where Mugshots used to be (RIP), one of my coworkers had been raving about this place, in particular the falafel and of course the very kind owner.

Went with my pre-wife and we shared beef gyro (carved) pita, falafel pita and hummus plate. Everything was extremely fresh (I concur on the crisp lettuce) well seasoned and just plain delicious.  A lot of food as well and complimentary baklava. We took our leftovers home (I wrapped the two remaining bites of my gyro - it's that good)

I highly recommend this place and you'll definitely walk out with a smile. I think this spot is still relatively unknown and I very rarely post reviews. This is a unique spot to Manayunk and I will be referring all of my friends as I really want the restaurant to succeed - because the owner deserves it and of course for my selfish appetite!
Revise this with your best effort:
I couldn't agree more with the previous reviewer. The food, service, and prices at this restaurant are truly excellent. It's conveniently located where Mugshots used to be, and after hearing rave reviews from a coworker, my partner and I decided to give it a try. We ordered the beef gyro pita, falafel pita, and hummus plate, and were blown away by the freshness and flavorful seasoning of each dish. The portions were generous, and we even received complimentary baklava. We were so satisfied with our meal that we took the leftovers home, carefully wrapping up every last bite of the gyro because it was that good.

I wholeheartedly endorse this place and guarantee that you'll leave with a smile on your face. It seems like the restaurant is still somewhat undiscovered, as I rarely write reviews myself, but I can't help but spread the word about this unique gem in Manayunk. I'll be recommending it to all my friends, not only because the owner truly deserves success, but also because my own appetite selfishly craves more of their delicious offerings.

input: Great food and excellent service. Only knock I would give them was they brought out our entrees about 10 minutes after our apps came so we were still eating that, otherwise great experience
Revise this with your best effort: The dining experience was exceptional, with a delectable selection of dishes and top-notch service. The only minor inconvenience was that our entrees arrived approximately 10 minutes after we started enjoying our appetizers. Nonetheless, overall a truly enjoyable experience.

input:
This is a very mediocre place.  The location itself is in the same dirty strip mall as Mozzarella Pizza. The inside has that "we don't really care about the looks" feel to it.  It's not dirty, per se.  It just doesn't look very clean.  Everything looks like its falling apart.  It probably gets its business from suburbanites like me craving what we think of as Chinese food.

All that said, the food I had was palatable.  Nothing outstanding or amazing: it was just all right.  I won't recommend against it, but it's nothing that you would think of as that great either.
Revise this with your best effort:
This place can be described as quite average. Its location is within a somewhat unkempt strip mall, coincidentally near Mozzarella Pizza. The interior gives off an impression of neglect towards aesthetics; it's not necessarily unclean, but it certainly lacks tidiness. The overall appearance gives the impression that things are falling apart. It likely attracts customers like myself, suburbanites who have a hankering for what we perceive as Chinese cuisine.

Now, considering the food I experienced, it was acceptable. It didn't stand out or leave me in awe; it was simply satisfactory. I wouldn't discourage trying it, but it's also not something you would consider exceptionally remarkable.

input: Phenomenal place to eat. I has the Hickory burger, that was so damn delicious!! Will be coming back for sure!!!
Revise this with your best effort: This place is absolutely incredible for dining. I had the Hickory burger, which was undeniably flavorful and outstandingly delicious! Without a doubt, I will definitely be returning here again in the future.

input: After having been here, I would say that the food had great flavors for the taste buds and it was a unique experience.  Our server, Brian was no doubt a foodie... I've never seen anyone get so excited about food and discuss the ingredients in such detail with so much passion.  The food really was different and had unbelievable flavor.  Anyone who calls themselves a foodie should try this place.  I'm thinking they would be pleased with this place.  But, the portions were small.  And I really didn't like the interior of the restaurant.  I'm more of a booths girl.  Booths can be classy, you know?  All in all, I would say this was an interesting place and I would come back, but the dishes were too complicated for me to want to come back beyond once a year.  Speaking of timing, the chefs change the menu every year.  And these guys really are good at what they do.  The owners actually own the Red Pony and two other restaurants all on the same street!  And they're all doing well.
Revise this with your best effort: Having experienced this place, I must say that the food offered a delightful explosion of flavors for the taste buds, creating a truly unique dining experience. Our server, Brian, unquestionably embodied the essence of a true food enthusiast. I was amazed to witness his unparalleled excitement and passionate discussion about the intricacies of each ingredient. Undoubtedly, the food itself was distinct and boasted an exceptional taste. Any self-proclaimed food aficionado should not miss an opportunity to try this remarkable establishment. I believe they would be thoroughly pleased with the culinary experience it offers. However, it is worth mentioning that the portion sizes were relatively small, and personally, I found the interior of the restaurant to be lacking. As a devotee of booths, I firmly believe they can contribute a touch of elegance to any setting. All things considered, I consider this place to be an intriguing dining spot, and while I would consider returning, the complexity of the dishes might deter me from doing so frequently. Speaking of timing, the menu is refreshed annually by the talented chefs. It is evident that these individuals possess exceptional skills in their craft. Notably, the owners are also the proud proprietors of the Red Pony and two other successful restaurants located on the same street, which further speaks to their proficiency in the industry.

input:
Solid improvement since last visit.  

Service- much improved.  Kid named Dillon gave a great service.  

Ambiance is very casual.  Order and sit, they bring food to you. 

Food- tasty and lots of options.  Not fancy.  Very affordable.  

Family of four for about 30$.  That's a great deal w today's prices. 

If you are looking for a fast, casual Asian option, give this place a try.
Revise this with your best effort:
Significant improvements have been made since my last visit, especially in terms of the service. I must mention the standout service provided by Dillon, a remarkable kid who went above and beyond to ensure an excellent experience.

The ambiance of the place is wonderfully laid-back, allowing customers to simply place their order and take a seat while the attentive staff promptly serves their food.

As for the food, it is both delicious and diverse, offering a wide range of options to satisfy various cravings. While not extravagant, the dishes are prepared with care and are surprisingly affordable. A family of four can enjoy a satisfying meal for approximately $30, which is a tremendous value considering today's high prices.

If you are seeking a quick and uncomplicated Asian dining option, I highly recommend giving this place a try.

input: Use the yelp app to get on the waiting list, we went on a Saturday morning and it was very busy, but the waiting list was cut down significantly by using the app. The menu is expansive, a lot of options. The cinnamon French toast was very good. The traditional breakfast foods were on par with most breakfast joints, but the extras on the menu can keep you busy for many visits trying new things. The strawberry orange juice was excellent so I recommend trying it. It was a little hot in the restaurant, could have been cooled down a lot for a more comfortable experience. The service was very good. There were two places to pay at the counter which I thought was a nice way to speed up the leaving process.
Revise this with your best effort: I highly recommend utilizing the Yelp app to secure a spot on the waiting list as my experience on a busy Saturday morning was significantly improved by doing so. The menu offers a wide variety of options, ensuring that there is something for everyone. One standout dish was the delectable cinnamon French toast, which left a lasting impression. While the traditional breakfast fare was on par with other establishments, the extensive extras on the menu will keep you coming back for more, providing ample opportunity to discover new and exciting flavors. Don't miss out on the delightful strawberry orange juice, as it was truly exceptional. It is worth noting, however, that the temperature in the restaurant was a little too warm, and could have been adjusted for a more comfortable dining experience. On the bright side, the service was top-notch, and I appreciated the convenient presence of two separate payment counters, which efficiently expedited the checkout process.

input:
Visited Shaving Grace on Friday for a hair cut.

Same vibe as my old Barber Shop in Philly. 
Big TV in the waiting area. Plush couch to relax in. Young lady checking me in asked if I wanted water, soda or a beer.
Beer? Need I say more. 

Great cut. Great bunch of guys discussing current events, sports, and what's happening around town.
Found my new spot. 

Will be back.
Revise this with your best effort:
On Friday, I had the pleasure of visiting Shaving Grace for a haircut, and I must say, it felt just like my beloved old Barber Shop in Philly. The atmosphere was welcoming and familiar, with a large TV in the waiting area and a luxurious plush couch to sink into while waiting my turn. As I approached the check-in counter, a friendly young lady asked if I would like water, soda, or even a refreshing beer. The thought of having a cool beer during my haircut experience was an unexpected treat.

Not only was the service top-notch, but the conversations among the talented barbers and other customers were equally enjoyable. Engaging discussions about current events, sports, and the latest happenings in town filled the air, making me feel like I had stumbled upon a community of like-minded individuals. In that moment, I knew I had found my new go-to spot for haircuts.

Without a doubt, I will be returning to Shaving Grace for my future grooming needs. The combination of excellent haircuts, a welcoming atmosphere, and fascinating conversations make it an unbeatable choice.

input: Not only was the food excellent, but the people here are beyond nice-and genuine. I had eggs Benedict. The poached eggs were good but the toast they were sitting on was excellent. We were given a cream pancakes to taste test by our awesome server, Tina. I can honestly say it was the best pancake I've ever tasted. So full of flavour-vanilla, and soft aa pillow.  They melted in my mouth. I didn't even use syrup. Stellar!
Revise this with your best effort: The food at this place was not only excellent, but the people working here were incredibly nice and genuine. I decided to try the eggs Benedict, and while the poached eggs were good, the toast they were served on was truly outstanding. Our incredible server, Tina, even brought us a sample of their cream pancakes to try. Let me tell you, it was hands down the best pancake I have ever had the pleasure of tasting. Bursting with flavors of vanilla and incredibly soft, they practically melted in my mouth. They were so delightful that I didn't even need to use any syrup. Absolutely stellar!

input: Great service. My husband ordered a cheese and bacon burger and I got the crawfish sausage por bo both well made and great tasting.
Revise this with your best effort: The service was excellent. My husband ordered a delectable cheese and bacon burger while I opted for the mouthwatering crawfish sausage po' boy. Both dishes were expertly prepared and packed with fantastic flavors.

input: Had a wonderful experience with JT and Ashley Furniture store!! He was helpful even when I had to change my order.

input:
While at Drexel University, I decided to try a new food truck and go for something that wasn't the typical food truck.  My girlfriend and I always noticed this place was crowded around lunch but never knew why.  After being recommended to try it by a friend, we decided to go ahead and order lunch here.  Cucina Zapata is at the end of the food truck row at the center of Drexel University's campus.  The truck has a graffiti style design which can be easily distinguished from the other food trucks here.

I decided to order (2) thai short rib tacos while my girlfriend got the cap'n crunch tilapia burrito.  The food has a good visual appearance which made us more eager to eat it once we got inside the building.  I really enjoyed the thai short rib tacos even though they put hot sauce on it.  They were definitely better than the typical taco bell food and left me with a 5 star review feeling inside.  My girlfriend also really enjoyed her burrito.

Overall, this food truck provides very good food at a good price.  I recommend this place to anyone looking for a good lunch.
Revise this with your best effort:
During my time at Drexel University, I decided to venture out and try something different from the usual food truck options. My girlfriend and I had always wondered why there was a constant crowd around this particular truck during lunchtime. Upon receiving a recommendation from a friend, we finally mustered up the courage to give it a shot. Cucina Zapata, located at the end of the food truck row in the heart of Drexel's campus, boasted a distinct graffiti-style design that set it apart from the rest.

As we approached the truck, I opted for the mouthwatering Thai short rib tacos, while my girlfriend chose to indulge in the tantalizing Cap'n Crunch tilapia burrito. The food's visually appealing presentation only heightened our anticipation as we made our way back to our dining spot. Despite the added touch of hot sauce, the Thai short rib tacos surpassed our expectations, surpassing the run-of-the-mill offerings found at Taco Bell. With each bite, I found myself experiencing a gratifying five-star sensation. My girlfriend shared a similar sentiment, thoroughly enjoying her burrito.

In terms of both taste and affordability, this food truck undoubtedly delivers. I wholeheartedly recommend Cucina Zapata to anyone seeking a satisfying lunchtime experience.

input: got my haircut here for the first time Jessie Becker took the damaged ends off. She's so sweet and does only what you ask of her. She's also great with kids. come see this place and come see her.

input: Great ramen! I'm really happy to have found this place! The service and food are both wonderful!

input: Cute place, nice servers and good food but dish sizes are waaaaay too small. I left unsatisfied. I don't like it when restaurants are cheap with portions, especially neighborly ones!

input: Just recently ate here for the first time. The hype was real. My girlfriend had the Greek Salad while I ordered the Chickpea Vegetarian Pita and they were kind enough to allow for some substitutions. input: First time here. Great bar and restaurant area. Open floor plan with plenty of TV's to watch the game. Attached to their O'Fallon brewery (in Maryland Heights, Missouri, a suburb of St. Louis). They ranked 2nd in the St Louis area last year for volume of beer sold by a micro brewery. Today, I tried the House Special IPA...a wonderful IPA, not too bitter, just right. Look for Troy behind the bar! (The only reason for 4 stars is no desserts....)
Revise this with your best effort:
This is my first visit here and I must say it's a fantastic bar and restaurant area. With its open floor plan and numerous TV screens, it's the perfect place to catch a game. What's even better is that it's connected to their O'Fallon brewery, located in Maryland Heights, Missouri, a suburb of St. Louis. In fact, they were ranked an impressive 2nd in the St. Louis area last year for the high volume of beer sold as a microbrewery.

Today, I had the pleasure of trying their House Special IPA, and it was truly delightful. It struck a perfect balance, not overwhelmingly bitter but just right. For those who enjoy a well-crafted IPA, this one is a must-try. Additionally, you can expect exceptional service from Troy, who can be found behind the bar.

My only slight disappointment, which is the reason for the 4-star rating, is the lack of dessert options. However, overall, this place is definitely worth a visit.

input: This is a neighbourhood dive bar on the eastern part of Whyte Avenue.  It's in a strip mall on a one way eastbound side street.  I was there on a Saturday night to check it out. Very average decor with a couple pool tables and a foosball table. It's definitely a younger crowd here.  They had a band and a doorman.  Drinks were reasonable.  A few tv screens.  The wings are always really cheap and come with a carrot and celery stick.  They make pizzas which looked good and cheesy but I did not try. Servers were quite young and pleasant.  The owner gal behind the bar was fine.  I gave it an extra star because I found the previous review a little harsh.
Revise this with your best effort:
Located on the eastern part of Whyte Avenue, this neighborhood dive bar presents itself in a strip mall, positioned on a one-way eastbound street. Intrigued, I ventured there on a Saturday night to explore its offerings. While the decor may be considered average, the establishment does provide a couple of pool tables and a foosball table. It became apparent that a younger crowd frequents this place, evident by the energetic ambiance. In addition, there was live music provided by a band, and a doorman ensuring a safe and controlled environment.

One pleasant surprise was the affordability of the drinks, offering a reasonable selection to choose from. Multiple television screens were scattered across the bar, ensuring that patrons could catch their favorite shows or sporting events. The notable feature, however, was their consistently inexpensive wings, which were always accompanied by a carrot and celery stick, providing a satisfying and economical snack. While I did not have the opportunity to taste their pizzas, they were undeniably enticing with their gooey and appetizing appearance.

The servers at the establishment were young yet pleasant, offering friendly and efficient service throughout the night. The owner, a woman managing the bar, also contributed to the positive experience. It is worth mentioning that I have given this place an extra star, as I found the previous review to be somewhat harsh and potentially misleading.

input:

input: I had a small snafu with the Yelp coupon but after that? Food....and it was excellent.  The chicken caeser salad was great and heavy on the chicken.  The subs were fresh and tasty.   And, yes, they have beer!   But I had an old-fashioned Dr. Brown's cream soda because they have all their flavors.   Nicely located.   Just a mile from the Wagon Wheel flea market.

input: I had an amazingly positive experience here. Dr. Neel and Robin were friendly, knowledgable and exceptionally helpful. input: By far the best breakfast I have had in a while. Huge pancakes. Simple home fries with not all the extras. The owner is super sweet and really generous. Deffinetly a new favorite.

input:

Great location, will be going back there for sure next time we are in New Orleans.
Revise this with your best effort:
During our trip to the Big Easy, my family and I had the pleasure of staying at this beautiful and charming establishment for a delightful six-night stay. One experience that we simply cannot forget is visiting the renowned Carousel Bar. It was an absolute must-see, and we were captivated by its unique charm.

Moreover, the location of this place was perfect for exploring New Orleans. Its proximity to various attractions and points of interest made our stay even more enjoyable. This remarkable experience has left a lasting impression on us, and we are already eagerly planning to return here during our next visit to the city.

input: I ordered the chicken stew, it was Tasteless chicken, it was a fried chicken possibly a leftover, that was thrown into a pot and made it into a stew.  If I wanted leftovers, I would have eaten at home.  Gross, still feel like I have to throw up.
Revise this with your best effort: I decided to try the chicken stew, but to my disappointment, the chicken lacked any flavor. It seemed like fried chicken, potentially a remnant from a previous meal, that had been hastily added to a pot to create a stew. Had I desired leftovers, I would have eaten at home. The experience was repulsive, and I still have a nauseating feeling.

input:
I've been having a terrible time in St Louis finding a decent Chinese place that is within delivery or easy take out range of our house. This time I tried Wei Hong. I told my partner it can't be any worse than the other mediocre places we have been going. I was wrong.
The take out service was fast for a Sat night. We were there within 20 minutes of ordering and it was ready. But the dining room was empty. For a Sat night that should have been a big clue. The rest of the places in the neighborhood were busy.
The steamed dumplings could have been great. The tasted homemade and the filling was good. However, they were so doughy with a really thick wrapper too thick that it detracted from the good filling. Everything else went downhill from there. 
The beef and broccoli was inedible. The beef had an awful weird texture. Like it was boiled and was gelatinous.  The sauce on it had off flavors. We literally scraped it off our plates and threw the whole thing out.  The meat in both the general Tao's chicken and the orange beef also had weird textures. It was mushy and the coating was thick on those as well. The flavors in the sauces would have been fine, but they were gloopy.  The fried rice was fair but nothing memorable.
We won't be going back.
Revise this with your best effort:
I have had a truly awful experience trying to find a decent Chinese restaurant that offers delivery or takeout near our house in St. Louis. Hoping for a change, I decided to give Wei Hong a try, thinking it couldn't be any worse than the mediocre places we've been settling for. Unfortunately, I was mistaken.

On a positive note, the takeout service was surprisingly quick for a Saturday night. We arrived at the restaurant within 20 minutes of placing our order, only to find that the dining room was completely empty. This should have been a red flag, as all the other nearby establishments were bustling with activity.

The steamed dumplings had the potential to be great. They had a homemade taste and the filling was flavorful. However, the doughy texture and excessively thick wrapper overshadowed the good filling, making them less enjoyable. Sadly, everything went downhill from there.

The beef and broccoli dish was absolutely inedible. The beef had an odd, gelatinous texture as if it had been boiled, and the sauce itself had off, unpleasant flavors. We couldn't bring ourselves to finish it, scraping off the sauce and discarding the entire dish. Similar issues were found in both the general Tao's chicken and orange beef dishes, with the meat having a mushy texture and the coating also being overly thick. While the flavors of the sauces would have been fine, their consistency was disappointingly gloopy. The fried rice was passable but forgettable.

Needless to say, we will not be returning to Wei Hong.

input: Big shout out to Cecile for helping us load our plywood as we got ready for IRMA. Thanks so much!
Revise this with your best effort: I want to give a huge shout out to Cecile for going above and beyond in assisting us with loading our plywood as we prepared for the arrival of Hurricane Irma. input: The food was outstanding.  I got chicken tagine, with the delicious tender meat falling off the bone, and carrot salad, flavored with mint and cumin.  Service was good, and the inside of the restaurant is cheerful and well-lit.  Total cost was around $13.

input:
After reading a lot of positive reviews, we were really excited to try this place. We were extremely disappointed in the food. I'm going to give the place the benefit of the doubt that it is not always like this as we came in at 10 PM, but if you cannot offer quality food at that hour then don't have your kitchen open. 
All of our food came out within 5 to 10 minutes of ordering which leads me to believe it was not made fresh. The Caesar salad was room temperature and overdressed. The hush puppies were flavorless, and the chicken wings (3 full wings is a serving) were undercooked and barely warm. The only redeeming food item was the chicken and biscuits, which had a nice flavor profile- the biscuit was again, cold in spots. 

On the positive side the place has a nice hip atmosphere and the service is friendly. 

Unfortunately, the food was so sub par we would not consider dining here again.
Revise this with your best effort:
After hearing rave reviews about this place, our anticipation was high. However, our experience with the food left us utterly disappointed. Although we understand that we arrived at 10 PM, we'd like to believe that this isn't a regular occurrence. Nevertheless, if the kitchen cannot deliver quality food during these hours, it would be best to close it altogether.

To begin with, all our dishes arrived suspiciously fast, within a mere 5 to 10 minutes of ordering. This made us question whether everything was prepared fresh. The Caesar salad arrived lukewarm and excessively dressed, lacking the vibrant flavors we had hoped for. The unremarkable hush puppies lacked any discernible taste, while the chicken wings (mind you, a serving consisted of just three full wings) were undercooked and lukewarm, barely meeting the minimum temperature needed for safe consumption. The sole redeeming item was the chicken and biscuits, which boasted a pleasing flavor profile; however, even the biscuit itself had cold spots, dampening our enjoyment.

On a brighter note, the establishment exudes a trendy atmosphere that adds to the overall experience, and the service provided was friendly and attentive.

Regrettably, the underwhelming quality of the food makes us hesitant to consider another dining experience here.

input: For the time and effort I put into ordering online 30 minutes before my pickup, I was pretty disappointed to skip the long line only to be told they 'didn't have anything' in their system. Thanks for nothing.

input:

It comes as no surprise that Joe Bob's is never bustling with customers. The sole priority of the owners and bartenders seems to be catering to the over-indulged gamblers who visit daily. The two women who have built a career within this wretched place rely on the generosity of inebriated individuals who win on the slot machines. This establishment barely qualifies as a chicken joint or a sports bar; a very deplorable rendition indeed. The owners' insatiable greed is glaringly apparent, as they refuse to invest even a nominal amount from their gambling profits toward improving this dump, despite the prevalence of affordable flat screens in today's market. It is disheartening to witness the current owners' blatant disregard for the original founders' commendable efforts, as all they seem to value is the profit generated by the slot machines, even at the expense of serving abhorrent food. The bartenders perpetually exude tension and lack any semblance of friendliness unless, of course, you are a high-stakes gambler who presents the potential of leaving a substantial tip. For a far superior experience, it would be wise to opt for the fast food chicken joint across the street called "El Pollo Loco," where the kitchen is likely to be cleaner, the staff friendlier, and you can safely avoid the daily spectacle of inebriated individuals who drive to and from this establishment. Exercise caution, as this environment can be quite unsettling and alarming.

input:

Great, great experience.

Overall, this was a truly amazing dining experience that we thoroughly enjoyed.

input: Where do I start? Brew D Licious has the very best coffee in town. Hands down. I have tried them all and can say that there isn't another coffee house that even comes close. The minute I met the owner, I knew she was not only very well informed about how to brew a great cup of coffee, but also knows how to make the toughest of customer a repeat patron. This coffee is so good that I buy 5#s at a time from Brigitte. It is always fresh and she has even delivered coffee to me while she is under construction of her new place. Personally, I cannot wait until she opens her new location. I never did care much for the Hollander Hotel and I often felt that she was being stifled by the cramped space she worked in. Also, the hotel has a funky smell (sort of like old socks) so I will be glad when she is at her new location and I can sit and enjoy a good cup of coffee without trying to filter out the bad smell from the hotel. I know it will be a long line at the new location but it will be worth the wait.... Thanks Brigitte for showing St. Petersburg what real coffee tastes and smells like!
Revise this with your best effort:
I don't even know where to begin raving about Brew D Licious. Without a doubt, they serve the absolute best coffee in town, hands down. After tastefully exploring all the other coffee houses around, none even come close to comparing. From the moment I met the owner, her expertise on brewing a flawless cup of coffee and her ability to turn even the pickiest of customers into loyal regulars were abundantly evident.

The coffee from Brew D Licious is so incredible that I don't hesitate to purchase 5-pound bags from Brigitte at a time. Every time I receive my order, the coffee is consistently fresh and vibrant. What truly astounded me was when Brigitte went out of her way to personally deliver coffee to me during the construction phase of her new establishment. Her dedication to ensuring her customers never miss out on their beloved coffee is truly remarkable.

Speaking of her new location, I couldn't be more excited. I must admit, I never truly enjoyed the cramped space of the Hollander Hotel where Brew D Licious was previously situated. The hotel itself had an unpleasant, almost reminiscent smell of old socks, which certainly didn't enhance the coffee experience. Knowing that the new location will provide a spacious and comfortable environment ensures I can savor every sip of my coffee without any distractions.

Undoubtedly, the line at Brew D Licious' new place will be long, but I am willing to wait patiently. The thought of experiencing the exquisite flavors and aromas of Brigitte's coffee in a properly designed space is enough to make the anticipation worthwhile. Thank you, Brigitte, for revolutionizing the way St. Petersburg savors coffee, finally granting us a taste of true excellence.

input:

input:
I think I would've given this place a 4/5 star rating if not for the lackluster service and attitude. The entrees were good, the prices were spot on, and the breadsticks were delicious.

Ahh, the breadsticks. This is where the attitude part kicks in. These things are advertised as "as much as you want for free." However, my buddy heads up to the front counter to request enough for our table of three only to be given a hard time from the manager that we're eating more breadsticks than what we ordered. Even ordering was a chore. It seemed as if they had a new hire manning the register during the lunch hour rush. She was placing orders as to-go for people looking to dine-in and had to have the manager place orders for her. Not a good idea for a Friday lunch rush.

If this Fazoli's location can improve upon these things minor inconveniences, it'd be a great place to grab a quick bite.
Revise this with your best effort:
I would have given this place a 4/5 star rating if it weren't for the lackluster service and attitude. The entrees were enjoyable, the prices were reasonable, and the breadsticks were absolutely delicious.

Ah, the breadsticks. This is where the attitude issue arises. The menu boldly states that they are "unlimited and free," yet when my friend politely approached the counter to ask for enough for our party of three, the manager gave them a hard time, claiming we were eating more than what we had ordered. It felt unfair and it goes against what they advertise.

Even the process of ordering was a hassle. There seemed to be a new employee handling the register during the busy lunch hour. She kept taking orders for takeout instead of dine-in, requiring the intervention of the manager to correct the mistakes. This was definitely not the best decision during a hectic Friday lunch rush.

If this Fazoli's location could address these minor inconveniences, it would definitely be a fantastic place to grab a quick bite.

input:
was on an errand-running run and remembered how ashamed i was at the state of my car the last time i looked at it - five minutes earlier, as i entered said vehicle.

saw the sign as i was about to turn into riverside plaza to make my groceries and decided it was time.  got the basic $12 tchoup and even though there were about 5 cars in the vacuum line ahead of me, my car was ready before i was done checking out the waiting area.  iguanas, parrots, ms. pac man ($1 a game?  the price of nostalgia, i guess).  not to mention the windows that look out into the auto wash system - which is really entertainment enough for me.  i'm not picky.

but then my number was up and i went out and inspected the results.  still some bird poop remnants on the hood and a few bugs didn't give up the ghost on the grill...maybe i am picky after all.  

don't get me wrong - it was better than nothing (which was what my car got in terms of washings since mid-january), but i'm missing my favorite car wash right about now.  their regular automatic wash with vacuum and window cleaning (i.e. the tchoup treatment) is $14, true, but those dudes are much more thorough with the elbow grease post-assembly line washing.

but that place is in los angeles, alas.  which is perhaps the best gauge of how pricey this place is: 85% as expensive as l.a., but 66.67% the quality.  worth it?  you do the math.  i'ma try a completely touchless system next time.  i reckon i'll get about the same results, but with no parrots or ms. pac-man.
Revise this with your best effort:
I was in the middle of running errands when I suddenly remembered how embarrassed I felt about the condition of my car when I last glanced at it just five minutes ago. As I was about to turn into Riverside Plaza to get my groceries, I noticed a sign that made me realize it was time for a car wash. I opted for the basic $12 option, called the Tchoup, and even though there were a few cars ahead of me in the vacuum line, my car was ready before I finished exploring the waiting area. The waiting area was equipped with iguanas, parrots, and even an old Ms. Pac-Man arcade game that cost a dollar per play. I guess nostalgia comes with a price. The entertainment didn't stop there though; the windows overlooked the auto wash system, which was fascinating enough for me. I'm not too picky when it comes to these things.

When it was finally my turn, I went outside to inspect the results. There were still remnants of bird poop on the hood, and a few stubborn bugs refused to leave the grill. Maybe I am a bit pickier than I thought. Don't get me wrong, it was definitely an improvement compared to the zero washes my car had received since mid-January. However, I can't help but yearn for my favorite car wash back in Los Angeles. Their regular automatic wash includes vacuuming and window cleaning, just like the Tchoup treatment, but they pay more attention to detail and give it that extra touch of cleanliness. It costs $14, which is a bit more expensive, but totally worth it in my opinion.

Unfortunately, that amazing car wash is located in Los Angeles, far away from here. That fact alone speaks volumes about how expensive this current place is. It's about 85% as pricey as Los Angeles, but only 66.67% as good in terms of quality. Is it worth it? I'll leave that calculation up to you. Next time, I think I'll give a completely touchless system a try. I assume I'll get similar results, but without the parrots or Ms. Pac-Man to keep me entertained.

input:
This is a great late brunch option during the weekends when the big morning rush dies down after 1 pm. Usually there is no wait or 5 minute wait at this time. One big complaint is that they don't have an organized system for seating guests. The servers don't always greet incoming patrons (which should be required Waffle House-style) and they sometimes tell you to seat yourself (which can lead to one or two people taking up tables for 4) or they'll seat you (whenever they get around to talking to you). 

I've ordered a several different dishes at this point and they have varies from ok to awesome. The chicken wings and onion rings are just ok. The wings are either lightly dredged in flour or not at and then fried whole. They aren't really seasoned so the wings are pretty bland. The "onion rings" made of formed, chopped onions that are breaded. The chicken fingers were a bit over battered and dry. The smashwich (or whatever it's called) was pretty good: your choice of breakfast meat with hash browns and eggs in a hoagie roll, but unspectacular. The club sandwich is classic diner fare that is very well executed. The egg and omelette platters are a very good deal and dang tasty. The best thing on the menu is definitely the waffle. It's gently sweet, very crispy and covered in butter. So good!

The service is generally pretty attentive (once you're seated), the restaurant and bathrooms are very clean, the food is a good, tasty value
Revise this with your best effort:
This is an excellent option for a late brunch on weekends, especially after 1 pm when the busy morning rush has subsided. During this time, there is usually no wait or only a short 5-minute wait. However, a major drawback is the lack of an organized seating system for guests. The servers do not consistently greet incoming patrons, which should be a standard practice akin to Waffle House. Instead, they sometimes tell you to seat yourself, resulting in some individuals occupying larger tables meant for more people, or they seat you whenever they find the time to address you.

Having tried several dishes, I can say that the quality has varied from okay to awesome. The chicken wings and onion rings fall into the okay category. The wings are either lightly coated in flour or not coated at all before being fried whole. Unfortunately, they lack proper seasoning, making them quite bland. The so-called "onion rings" are made from formed and chopped onions that are coated in breading. The chicken fingers were a bit over-battered and ended up dry. On the other hand, the smashwich, which consists of your choice of breakfast meat with hash browns and eggs in a hoagie roll, was decent but not particularly remarkable. The club sandwich, a classic diner offering, was executed exceptionally well. The egg and omelette platters are both tasty and offer great value. However, the standout item on the menu is undoubtedly the waffle. It strikes a perfect balance of gentle sweetness, exceptional crispiness, and is generously covered in butter. It is simply delightful!

In terms of service, once you are seated, the staff is generally attentive. Furthermore, both the restaurant and bathrooms are kept impeccably clean. Overall, the food provides a good value for its taste.

input:

but the reuben's rye bread was disappointing considering that companion is all about the bread.  

However, my fiancee's sandwich(forgot the name) with chicken, bacon, avocado on french bread was amazing!

had their spice chicken soup with their corn bread.  It was great! the soup had tons of vegetables and chicken, just the right amount of heat and the corn bread is pretty big and delicious.  

their chi latte was not impressive.. do not get it. lol 

little pricey but, it's a great place to have a wonderful breakfast/lunch and the workers are nice and friendly. 

check this place out, let me know what you guys think.
Revise this with your best effort:
I would give them a rating of 5, but I was somewhat disappointed by their reuben sandwich. Whenever I visit a new place that offers a reuben on their menu, I feel compelled to try it for some reason. However, the rye bread of their reuben was quite underwhelming, which was surprising considering that the establishment prides itself on its bread.

On a brighter note, my fiancee's sandwich, which consisted of chicken, bacon, and avocado on french bread, was absolutely delightful!

I also had the pleasure of trying their spice chicken soup accompanied by their cornbread, and it was truly delightful. The soup was packed with a generous amount of vegetables and chicken, with just the right level of spiciness, and the cornbread was not only sizable but also delicious.

Unfortunately, their chi latte failed to impress. I would advise against ordering it, as it did not meet expectations.

Although the prices may be a little steep, this place is perfect for a fantastic breakfast or lunch experience. The staff is friendly and accommodating.

I highly recommend giving this place a visit and sharing your thoughts on it.

input:

input:
This is the biggest and best location for HMV in the city. The prices aren't any different from other stores but they do have a larger selection of gifting (figurines,mugs,blankets etc) as well as the largest collection of titles that don't fit into what is new and hot at the moment. Anything that they don't carry can actually be ordered in for you but I have to say staff here are not always the best at phoning customers to let them know when their titles are in so one should definitely keep their number by the phone to check in with them after a week or so.

The biggest selling point for me here besides the selection has to be the staff at the tills. It can get a little busy here but lines are always dealt with quickly and I appreciate that they don't push as hard as other locations to try and sign you up for a pure card. F.Y.I to anybody considering the pure rewards program the redemption items are not that great. It took me about a year of collecting just to accumulate enough points for a true blood key chain and when I got it it was placed in a bubble mailer and not even in it's original packaging. Needless to say when it came time to renew the card I opted out.

Anyways to sum it all up I will say for selection and speedy service these guys get five stars but the prices as well as the sometimes slow ordering process drop it down to a 3. Still worth checking out though if you have been on the hunt at smaller stores for a particular movie or cd.
Revise this with your best effort:
This HMV location in the city is undoubtedly the biggest and best. While their prices may not differ from other stores, they boast an expansive selection of gifting items such as figurines, mugs, and blankets. Additionally, they offer the largest collection of titles that don't align with the current mainstream trends. If by chance they don't carry a desired item, they are more than willing to order it for you. However, it is worth noting that the staff's follow-up communication regarding order availability could be improved. To ensure prompt updates, it is recommended to keep their contact number handy and follow up with them after a week or so.

Aside from the remarkable selection, the standout feature of this location is the efficient staff at the tills. Despite occasional busyness, the queues are always handled swiftly. Furthermore, they refrain from aggressively pushy sales tactics, which is a refreshing change from other locations. Regarding the Pure Rewards program, it's important to note that the redemption items may not be as impressive as one would hope. Personally, I spent a year collecting points before I had enough to claim a true blood keychain. Disappointingly, the item arrived in a bubble mailer without its original packaging. Consequently, when it was time to renew the card, I opted out.

In summary, this HMV branch scores a solid five stars for its extensive selection and efficient service. However, the prices and occasionally slow ordering process detract from its overall rating, bringing it down to three stars. Nonetheless, if you have been searching for a particular movie or CD without success at smaller stores, this location is still worth a visit.

input: Was on a mission trying to find the perfect coat for the Holidays. Found my idea of the perfect coat at Burlington but they did not have my size. Went to Target, bought a coat but ended up taking it bath. Was not my dream coat. Next stop Ross. The only coat in my size was a beautiful Bomber style jacket made of pleather. Bought it right before Christmas. Now it's a few days after Christmas and my husband Guy points out to me that the coat is really wrinkled.
