I go on line and look up every possible hack to get wrinkles out of pleather. They all fail miserably. I just went back to Ross with that coat, no receipt, no tags and asked to speak to the manager. The manager is a young male with dark hair and black framed glasses. I tell him of my plight. He literally says go find what you need, no problem. WOW! You won't believe it, but there was my Camouflage coat, in my size, hanging there waiting for me. Oh the irony! They exchanged my coat and after all that I ended up with my Dream coat after all. Thank you Ross Dress for Less. You will forever be my first choice for now on!
Revise this with your best effort:
I was on a mission to find the perfect coat for the Holidays. After searching high and low, I finally stumbled upon my ideal coat at Burlington. However, my excitement quickly turned to disappointment as they didn't have my size in stock. Determined not to settle, I headed to Target and hastily purchased a coat, only to realize later that it was far from being my dream coat. Feeling discouraged, I decided to give it one last shot and went to Ross.

To my surprise, the only coat available in my size at Ross was a stunning Bomber style jacket made of pleather. Without hesitation, I bought it just before Christmas. However, a few days after the festivities, my husband, Guy, pointed out the noticeable wrinkles on the coat. Desperate to salvage it, I turned to the internet and researched every possible hack to get wrinkles out of pleather. Unfortunately, all my attempts proved futile.

Feeling hopeless, I decided to return to Ross with the coat despite having no receipt or tags. As I approached the manager, a young male with dark hair and black framed glasses, I explained my predicament. Astonishingly, he simply told me to find what I needed without any hassle. Overwhelmed by his generosity, I embarked on a search, praying for a stroke of luck.

And believe it or not, there it was hanging before my eyes - my desired Camouflage coat, in my size, patiently waiting for me. The irony of the situation wasn't lost on me. Ross Dress for Less had exchanged my coat, making all my previous tribulations worthwhile. I am forever grateful to them for making my dream coat a reality. From now on, Ross Dress for Less will forever be my first and only choice.

input: You honestly can't go wrong here. My favorites are the Udon Noodle Salad (a-ma-zing) and the Crispy Hipcity Ranch (so, so good). Friendly staff, fast service. Oh, they deliver too!
Revise this with your best effort: You absolutely cannot make a mistake by choosing any dish on the menu here. Personally, I highly recommend trying the Udon Noodle Salad, which is incredibly delicious. Another standout option is the Crispy Hipcity Ranch, which I must say is absolutely mouth-watering. Additionally, the staff is friendly and the service is prompt. What's more, they even offer delivery services.

input: Philadelphia, I love you.  Places like this remind me why.  We sat at the counter and watched the guys make the pizzas.  Our son hates cheese on a pizza and they had one already on the menu for him: The Marinara (oregano, crushed san marzano tomatoes, garlic, olive oil).  It was simple... but delicious. If you like real wood-fired pizzas that char the crust (a little blackened... in a good way), this is the place to go to.  Our other favorite pizza joints that rival this place are Lombardi's (NYC) and Grimaldi's (Brooklyn).  We all had a slice and were shocked at the lovely simplicity of it. Razor thin slices of garlic dotted the fresh tomato sauce.  My husband and I shared the Salsiccia (fennel sausage, roasted fennel, tomato sauce, mozzarella).  Roasted fennel on a pizza?  Brilliant. I cried a little.  No wait... I REALLY cried when we shared this cocktail: The Brooklyn (Dad's Hat rye, Luxardo cherry, white vermouth).  It says it serves one, but they brought it out in a cute little bottle and gave us each a glass...each with a hand- crafted giant square ice cube (hipster-cool) and Luxardo cherries.  Perfection.  We also shared a Rotolo (pizza dough, mortadella, ricotta, pistacchio pesto).  Those are crazy amazing.  I kept saying my husband could eat the rest... then freaking out and going back for another bite. He's lucky I didn't stab him in the hand with a fork to fight over the last bite (to be fair, he was the smart one who ordered it).  I could've eaten several of those and forgotten the pizza (although that was wonderful too!).  We finished with a little dessert... perfect little Italian cookies ("Cookie Jar" - pignoli, almond cookies, chocolate biscotti, pistacchio gnocchi) and I got an Affogato (fiordilatte soft serve with a shot of espresso).  The soft serve is Italian sweet cream... decadent and lovely... with rich espresso in a pretty little Italian mug.  I'm in Heaven here.  I know nothing about Vetri's other restaurants, but I'm checking them out next time I'm in Philadelphia!  By the way... service was great and friendly.  5 stars all around!
Revise this with your best effort:
Philadelphia, you hold a special place in my heart. This city never fails to remind me why I love it so much. One of my cherished memories was sitting at the counter, mesmerized by the skillful pizza-making happening before my eyes. To my delight, they had a pizza on the menu that perfectly catered to my son's aversion to cheese – The Marinara. With its simple yet delicious combination of oregano, crushed San Marzano tomatoes, garlic, and olive oil, it captured our hearts.

If you have a fondness for wood-fired pizzas that boast a slightly charred crust, this is the ultimate destination for you. As staunch lovers of pizza, we hold Lombardi's in NYC and Grimaldi's in Brooklyn as our other favorites, but this place rivals them both. One bite of their delectable slice, adorned with razor-thin garlic slices atop fresh tomato sauce, had us in awe of its charming simplicity.

My husband and I decided to share the Salsiccia, a pizza topped with fennel sausage, roasted fennel, tomato sauce, and mozzarella. The addition of roasted fennel on a pizza seemed like a stroke of genius, leaving me so moved that tears welled up in my eyes. And don't even get me started on the cocktail we indulged in – The Brooklyn. Despite being advertised as a single serving, it arrived in an adorable little bottle accompanied by two glasses, each garnished with a meticulously crafted, hipster-cool square ice cube and Luxardo cherries. It was a heavenly combination of Dad's Hat rye, Luxardo cherry, and white vermouth – pure perfection.

We couldn't resist the temptation of trying their Rotolo, made with pizza dough, mortadella, ricotta, and pistachio pesto. These indulgent treats drove us to momentarily forget about the pizza itself. I kept telling my husband he could have the rest, only to find myself eagerly grabbing another bite. He was wise to order it, avoiding a potential fork skirmish over the last morsel. The Rotolo was so incredible that I could have devoured several and completely forgotten about the pizza (although it was undeniably wonderful as well).

To cap off our extraordinary meal, we indulged in a selection of perfect little Italian cookies known as the "Cookie Jar," featuring pignoli, almond cookies, chocolate biscotti, and pistachio gnocchi. Meanwhile, I treated myself to the blissful Affogato – a delightful combination of fiordilatte soft serve and a shot of espresso. The Italian sweet cream in the soft serve was decadent and exquisite, perfectly complementing the rich espresso served in an elegant little Italian mug. It truly felt like I was in culinary heaven.

Although I am unfamiliar with Vetri's other restaurants, I am already planning to explore them during my next visit to Philadelphia. And before I forget, let me mention that the service we received was exceptional and friendly. This experience warrants a resounding five-star rating across the board.

input:
This a really price store with great clothes. Mostly high end stuff, everything here is designer. 

The workers here are really friendly and not pushy. They will leave you alone if you just want to be left alone, they are never breathing down your neck trying to make a sale. They carry casual clothing but I think it's much better place for suits and dress shirts and fancy clothing. I think this place stands out in West Edmonton Mall in terms of service and dressy clothing for men. They really do everything to make your shopping experience better. 

Be prepared to spend some coin here, although you won't be disappointed.
Revise this with your best effort:
This store is a hidden gem, offering a magnificent selection of high-quality clothing. Most of the items here are top-tier, designer pieces that are sure to impress. 

What sets this store apart is its delightful staff who are incredibly welcoming and never pushy. If you prefer to browse in peace, they will respect your space without constantly pressuring you to make a purchase. While they do carry casual attire, this establishment truly shines when it comes to suits, dress shirts, and fancy garments. In terms of exemplary service and upscale men's clothing, it is undoubtedly a standout in West Edmonton Mall. 

Keep in mind that shopping here may require a significant investment, but rest assured, the experience will be worth every penny.

input:
The food was pretty tasty. Nothing outstanding though. It reminds me of any Mediterranean food truck that I've been to. It's a nice late night spot. Definitely hits the spot at the end of the night. To me, the amount of food you get for the price could be improved but I would not say that I feel ripped off. The amount of food you get is fair but I think it'd be easier to justify if you got a little more. 

There's plenty of seating. Despite being near a whole bunch of bar/club scenes, once you're inside it's easy to take a break and have a nice conversation. It is all very clean and well kept. The servers are quick and friendly. When I went there were only two guys working but they weren't busy so it didn't take too long. The entire restaurant is very dimly lit and the atmosphere is a bit of a hodgepodge of things. On one wall there is a mural of outer space and the music that plays seems to have no rhyme or reason to it. 

It's a bit of a strange place but I would definitely go back.
Revise this with your best effort:
The food at this place was fairly tasty, although it didn't particularly stand out. It reminded me of the Mediterranean food trucks I've visited before, so nothing extraordinary there. However, it does make for a pleasant late-night option that hits the spot at the end of a long day. In terms of value, the portion size could use some improvement, although I wouldn't go as far as to say that it left me feeling ripped off. The portion size is decent but could be more justifiable if it were slightly larger.

Seating is plentiful, which is a plus considering its proximity to several bar and club scenes. Once you step inside, it's easy to take a break and engage in a nice conversation. The establishment is kept clean and well-maintained, and the servers are quick and friendly. During my visit, there were only two staff members working, but they managed to handle the workload efficiently as they weren't swamped with customers. The ambiance is a bit peculiar, with dim lighting and a mishmash of elements. You'll find a mural of outer space adorning one of the walls, and the music playing lacks a discernible theme or pattern.

Overall, despite its eccentric nature, I wouldn't hesitate to return to this place.

input:
Awesome shop. Everyone is really nice an freely offers suggestions on areas to hit that have been very productive ! The bait is always TOP Notch too. Great supply of tackle an honestly some of the best prices I've seen. I used to buy a lot
Of my tackle at Walmart ( yes I've regretted that ) or dicks. After learning the error of my ways, an seeing the really great prices I've been buying all of my tackle from this shop. You can't go wrong with this bait shop ! The only issue I have is there isn't more of them around town !!!
Revise this with your best effort: This shop is absolutely amazing! The staff members are incredibly friendly and always eager to share productive suggestions on fishing spots. Not to mention, the bait they offer is consistently top-notch. Their wide variety of tackle is exceptional, and I've found their prices to be some of the best in town. In the past, I used to purchase my tackle from Walmart or Dick's, but I've come to regret that decision once I discovered this fantastic shop. From then on, I've exclusively bought all of my tackle from here without any regrets. Trust me, you can't go wrong with this bait shop! The only downside is that there aren't more of them around town.

input:
Nigel's an awesome guy and the candy is amazing it's worth the drive!

Can't believe how much all my friend love and sadly eat all my Bon bons he sells.
Revise this with your best effort: Nigel is truly an exceptional individual, and his delectable candies are simply outstanding; they are unquestionably worth the trip! It is astonishing to witness the immense appreciation of my friends, who regrettably devour all the Bon bons he has to offer.

input:
When giving friends from out of town a tour of the French Quarter, one can only expect they want some classic New Orleans dishes. I've been here a couple of times, but they were the ones that wanted to go, due to their lunch special. It's a nice, well know restaurant that offers a 17.00 lunch special that includes a soup or salad, entree, and the option for a 4.00 Bloody Mary or martini. I got the Bloody Mary and it was a great size for the price. It was spicy and hit the spot.
They text message you when your table is ready, so were able to walk around the quarter while we waited. Thank god a lot of restaurants are getting rid of the those buzzers that make you feel like you are under house arrest. 
We sat down to a beautiful table right by the open shutters. The servers, were ok. They were busy, but forgot a couple of things we asked for. It was still a great experience though!
I got the pork chop with red beans and the turtle soup. The turtle soup was one of the best I have had. The pork chop was cooked to perfection and the read beans were seasoned very well. It came with cornbread, but it was very dry. After this lunch at noon, I didn't find myself hungry till it was basically time for bed. It was a very generous portion and well worth the money.

Muriel's is a great way to get a classic, good quality New Orleans meal at a decent price. The location is spectacular, and the history behind the restaurant made for great conversation at the table.
Definitely check it out if you are in the Quarter!
Revise this with your best effort:
When showing friends from out of town around the French Quarter, it is safe to assume that they will want to taste some authentic New Orleans cuisine. Although I have been to the area a couple of times before, this visit was at the request of my friends who were enticed by the restaurant's lunch special. It is a renowned establishment that offers a $17.00 lunch special, inclusive of a soup or salad, entree, and the choice of a $4.00 Bloody Mary or martini. I opted for the Bloody Mary, which was reasonably priced and satisfyingly spicy. 

While waiting for our table, the restaurant sent us a text message notification, allowing us to explore the Quarter at our leisure. Thankfully, many establishments are now replacing the intrusive buzzer systems that make you feel like you are under house arrest. 

We were seated at a charming table adjacent to open shutters, adding to the ambience of the experience. The servers were adequate, albeit slightly forgetful with a few of our requests due to their busyness. Nevertheless, it did not detract from the overall enjoyment of our time there. 

For my meal, I chose the pork chop accompanied by red beans and turtle soup. The turtle soup surpassed my expectations and can be ranked among the best I have ever had. The pork chop was cooked to perfection, and the seasoned red beans were delightful. Unfortunately, the cornbread served with the meal was rather dry. However, even after indulging in this hearty lunch around noon, I did not feel hungry until bedtime. The portion size was incredibly generous, making it well worth the money spent. 

Muriel's provides a fantastic opportunity to indulge in a classic and high-quality New Orleans meal without breaking the bank. The location of the restaurant is spectacular, and its rich history adds an extra layer of intrigue and conversation to the dining experience. If you happen to find yourself in the French Quarter, I highly recommend giving Muriel's a visit.

input: We stopped here's on the recommendation of our shuttle driver.  The red velvet ice cream is wonderful!! Pieces of cake. Creamy goodness.  Yum!
Revise this with your best effort: We made a pit stop here on the glowing recommendation of our friendly shuttle driver. And let me tell you, the red velvet ice cream they serve is absolutely divine!! Delightful chunks of moist cake perfectly blend with the velvety, creamy goodness of the ice cream. It's a tantalizing treat that definitely leaves you craving for more. Simply put, it's a yum-filled experience!

input:
I ate here for the first time today.  The woman that works behind the counter is really friendly and offered to waive the minimum credit order amount ($7), since I work nearby.

The food itself is pretty average for American-Chinese food.  Nothing great, but not bad either.  My sauce was greasy, but the food in general doesn't seem to be (e.g. fried rice).  They do have some vegetarian options which are of the tofu variety as opposed to fake meat. 

I would go back since they have lunch specials that come with rice and either a drink, soup, or egg roll ($5.75).

EDIT: I got super sick after leaving this review, and I'm 99% sure it was food poisoning.  Will not be returning.
Revise this with your best effort:
Today was my first time dining at this establishment. I was pleasantly surprised by the friendly demeanor of the woman working behind the counter. In a kind gesture, she offered to waive the minimum credit order amount of $7 due to my proximity to the restaurant.

As for the food itself, it can be described as average in terms of American-Chinese cuisine. While not extraordinary, it was also not subpar. Unfortunately, the sauce accompanying my dish was a bit greasy, but in general, the other dishes, like the fried rice, seemed to be less so. I appreciate that they provide vegetarian options, primarily featuring tofu instead of imitation meat substitutes.

Despite the average food quality, the restaurant does offer enticing lunch specials. Each special includes rice and a choice between a drink, soup, or egg roll, all for a reasonable price of $5.75.

However, it saddens me to mention that shortly after leaving this review, I fell seriously ill, strongly suspecting it to be a case of food poisoning. Due to this unfortunate experience, I regret to say that I will not be returning to this establishment.

input:
Delicious! 

I wish they took reservations, but my friend and her fiance go there nice and early so that we could snag a seat inside (it was cold out!). 

We ordered the bianco salad ( to share between 2) and the western addition (to share between 4).

I thought the salad was tasty but nothing special, despite the white chocolate shavings. Cute idea, but not enough crunch or pizazz to make the salad seem really fabulous.

The pizza, however, was pretty darn good. We ordered it deep dish to try their special cornmeal crust and were pretty impressed. 
The crust tastes a little bit like cornbread, a little bit like pizza dough, a tiny bit like grease (the good kind) and a lot like YUM!

I don't know if it was the best pizza I've ever had, but it was very good. It would be even better if it were a tad cheaper, and didn't get so crowded! But definitely worth a visit if you're in the area!
Revise this with your best effort:
Yum! While it would have been nice if they accepted reservations, my friend and her fiancé were wise to arrive early to secure a cozy indoor seat in the chilly weather. With the bianco salad divided between the two of us and the western addition split among the four of us, we eagerly anticipated our meal. The salad, adorned with white chocolate shavings, was tasty but didn't particularly stand out. The concept was adorable, yet the lack of a satisfying crunch and vibrant flavor prevented it from truly dazzling us.

On the other hand, the pizza was downright delicious. Opting for the deep-dish option, we were pleasantly surprised by the specially crafted cornmeal crust. It had hints of cornbread and pizza dough, a touch of delightful greasiness (of the desirable kind), and an abundance of yumminess!

Although I wouldn't label it as the absolute best pizza I've ever tasted, it definitely ranked highly. Perhaps it would be even more exceptional if it were a bit more affordable and didn't get so packed. Nevertheless, if you happen to be in the vicinity, it's certainly worth a visit!

input: A downtown without a bookstore is like a downtown without... I don't know I lost the metaphor. It's just sad is what it is. You need books, you need a place to browse, talk with other book lovers, and listen to book readings. Indy Reads is that place. And it's more than that because all proceeds support a great cause, adult literacy. Most of the books are used so donate a book and pick up a new (used) one. You may be surprised at all the books they have that you didn't even know you wanted. They also have a small selection of new books. If they don't have what you're looking for, you can order it. The one thing I don't really like is that the $1 children's books can be jammed so tightly that it's hard to look through them. The kids books are also arranged by color, which makes it harder for me to distinguish between titles as I glance through. Prices are excellent throughout, and the space is really nice. Check it out!
Revise this with your best effort: A downtown without a bookstore is akin to a desolate landscape, leaving a void that is as disheartening as it is unfortunate. The presence of books is an absolute necessity in any urban center, where the allure of perusing, conversing with fellow book enthusiasts, and immersing oneself in literary events is a cherished pastime. Fortunately, Indy Reads exists precisely for these purposes. Yet it is more than just a bookstore, as its proceeds contribute to a noble cause: adult literacy. Predominantly housing pre-loved books, it encourages patrons to donate their own books while indulging themselves in a new (albeit used) discovery. The sheer variety of unexpected treasures waiting to be unearthed may astound even the most discerning reader. Additionally, a limited collection of new books is available, and special orders can be made upon request. Admittedly, one minor drawback is found in the tightly stacked $1 children's books, which can be challenging to browse. Furthermore, the organizing of kid's books by color might hinder quick identification of specific titles. Nevertheless, Indy Reads offers excellent prices throughout and boasts an aesthetically pleasing environment. Truly, it is an establishment worthy of exploration.

input: Wish I would have came on Yelp and read the previous reviews, it would've saved me a lot of time and frustration. I ran in today to see if someone could take a look at my right passenger front wheel. My tire pressure light was on and I noticed a piece of tire was lifted. I go in and he tells me it's a couple hours wait. Ok, I'll give you that I just showed up so the wait thing is to be expected. I ask the guy if I can make an appointment to come back. He says its first come first serve. Really? When I've made appts previously with other Just Tires? Why not just say you don't want my service? Bottom line? Guy was rude and lacked any customer service. Went down the street to Mr. Tire and was in and out with a replaced new tire in half an hour. Oh, and they appeared WAY busier based on the waiting area and cars in the garage.
Revise this with your best effort: I wish I had checked Yelp and read the reviews before visiting this place. It would have saved me a significant amount of time and frustration. Today, I stopped by to get my right passenger front wheel checked as my tire pressure light was on and I noticed a part of the tire was lifted. Upon entering, I was informed that there would be a wait of a couple of hours. I understand that I had just arrived, so I expected some waiting time. However, when I asked if I could make an appointment for a later time, I was told it's a first-come-first-serve basis. This left me feeling frustrated and made me question if they truly valued my business. The employee I interacted with was not only impolite but also lacked any form of customer service skills. In contrast, I went to Mr. Tire down the street and they promptly replaced my tire within just 30 minutes. To make matters worse for this Just Tires location, Mr. Tire seemed much busier based on the number of cars in their garage and the state of their waiting area.

input: Fantastic experience! I own a flower shop so I am kind of a hard one to please when I send flowers to others but this shop did a GREAT job! I called this afternoon and told the woman that answered the phone to do whatever they would like for x amount of money. My only request was that it was bright and cheery. They hit the nail on the head and delivered it quickly. THANK YOU :)
Revise this with your best effort: Incredibly satisfying experience! As a flower shop owner myself, I tend to be quite discerning when it comes to sending flowers to others, but this particular shop surpassed my expectations completely. Upon calling this afternoon, I enthusiastically conveyed to the warm lady who answered the phone that they were free to exercise their creative expertise within a specified budget. I only made one simple request - that the arrangement exuded brightness and cheerfulness. Without fail, they absolutely nailed it and delivered the stunning bouquet promptly. A heartfelt thank you to the entire team!

input:
I gave it one star because it doesn't give me an option to give it zero. This place sucks. Where should I start?? Okay, arrived at 7 pm with reservations and was seated in the dungeon. Fine. We ordered queso fundido with chorizo and got a weird looking cheese skillet with tortillas NOT chips. Odd! So had to ask for chips. Should've asked for a trash can. So we asked for some salsa to dress it up a bit -- that took an hour and I'm not exaggerating! The salsa was a thick mushy mess. Could turn the bowl upside down and nothng would've come out. Our food took an hour and a half, too. By that time, we were full on chips -- which were the only good thing on the menu! Oh... My favorite part... I ordered a side of beans and rice to go with my carne asada tacos -- which were more like unseasoned beef tips -- and I got a bowl of hard WHITE rice with refried beans on top. WHITE rice??? Seriously?!

Terrible! Dont waste your time. Taco Bell serves better food than this and that isn't saying much! Service was just as bad!!
Revise this with your best effort: I gave this establishment a one-star rating because I am unable to give it zero stars. My experience was highly disappointing. Allow me to elaborate on my grievances. Upon arriving at 7 pm with a reservation, we were seated in an undesirable location. We decided to order queso fundido with chorizo, but instead received a peculiar-looking cheese skillet with tortillas instead of chips. It was an odd choice! We had to specifically request chips, although we should have asked for a trash can instead. Additionally, we waited an hour for salsa to accompany our dish, and when it finally arrived, it was a thick, mushy mess. In fact, the consistency was so thick that if we were to turn the bowl upside down, nothing would have poured out. Our food also took an hour and a half to arrive, during which we filled up on chips - which happened to be the only redeeming item on the menu. Furthermore, I ordered a side of beans and rice to accompany my carne asada tacos, which turned out to be unseasoned beef tips rather than proper carne asada. To make matters worse, the bowl of rice I received was hard and colorless, and it had refried beans on top. White rice is simply unacceptable! Overall, this was a terrible experience. I advise against wasting your time here. Taco Bell, despite its reputation, serves better food than this establishment - and that's not saying much! The service was equally dismal.

input: This is a small coffe place own by Karyn, a blond sweet lady with a big smile! Great coffee and they have drive through
Revise this with your best effort: This quaint coffee spot is owned by Karyn, a delightful blonde lady who greets everyone with a warm smile. Known for their exceptional coffee, this establishment also offers a convenient drive-through service.

input:
This used to be Red's but they knocked of the "R" and re-launched as Ed's, although when I see the sign from outside I keep forgeting it's called Ed's - cause it just looks like part of the sign fell off. Ed's is huge. If you've ever been on a cruise ship, Ed's has a variety of activity spaces, restaurant, bars and lounges under one roof. 

It's endless entertainment. You could probably float around here for a whole week and never get bored. There is a pool room, video games, bowling, a dance area, restaurants, lounges, a stage and much more around every corner you turn. It's a good place for young kids and birthday parties once you're too old for Chucky Cheese. 

Although I've personally never seen a band here my partner has, and it's not that expensive to see good bands like Ween, Jurassic Five or Interpol. The venue's neither big or small, so Ed's can host lesser known but interesting musicians as they can sell upwards of 600 tickets. So for bands that aren't popular enough to fill the Coliseum, Ed's still helps them establish a presence in E-town.
Revise this with your best effort:
This establishment used to be known as Red's until they removed the "R" and relaunched it as Ed's. However, when observing the exterior sign, one can easily forget that it is now called Ed's since it appears as though part of the sign has fallen off. Ed's is an enormous venue that offers a wide array of entertainment options, including various activity spaces, restaurants, bars, and lounges, all located under one roof. 

The entertainment options at Ed's seem endless, as you could spend an entire week here and never tire of the numerous amenities. Whether you are interested in playing pool, video games, bowling, dancing, or simply enjoying a meal and relaxing in one of the lounges, there is something for everyone at Ed's. It is an ideal location for young children and birthday parties, especially as they outgrow places like Chucky Cheese.

While I have not personally had the opportunity to witness a live band performance at Ed's, my partner has and attests to the fact that it is not overly expensive to see talented acts such as Ween, Jurassic Five, or Interpol. The venue is neither excessively large nor small, allowing Ed's to host lesser-known yet intriguing musicians who can still gather a crowd of up to 600 attendees. Therefore, for bands that have not yet garnered enough popularity to fill the Coliseum, Ed's serves as a platform to establish their presence in the E-town music scene.

input: I've had the fortune of eating my way across Asia Pacific, so I might be biased in saying I don't understand the rave reviews. I will say though that the conversation and company I was with more than made up for this!
Revise this with your best effort: Having had the wonderful opportunity to explore the culinary delights of Asia Pacific, I must admit my perspective might be slightly biased when it comes to the rave reviews. However, I cannot deny that the engaging conversations and wonderful company I experienced during my meals more than compensated for any shortcomings.

input: Very disappointed they no longer have the salad & pizza bar! Used to go to other location all the time, moved away & thought they closed. Then I realized they relocated & was excited about having salad there; I loved the salad bar. Was hoping for a piece of pizza for dinner and some salad. Not anymore:-(  Not unless you want to order a whole pizza!
Revise this with your best effort: I am extremely disappointed to learn that they have discontinued their salad and pizza bar. In the past, I used to frequent their other location, but unfortunately, I had to move away. I initially believed that they had closed down, but then I discovered that they had relocated, which sparked excitement in me as I looked forward to enjoying their delicious salads once again. I had always loved their salad bar. Furthermore, I was hoping to indulge in a slice of their scrumptious pizza for dinner accompanied by a refreshing salad. Regrettably, it seems that option is no longer available unless I am willing to order an entire pizza. This unfortunate change has left me feeling quite disappointed.

input:
They used to make an Amiga bowl that had an abundance of shredded grilled chicken on the bottom of a flour tortilla bowl, a layer of rice topped with grilled onions and peppers with a queso sauce drizzeled over the top.
Tonight there was no rice nor any shredded chicken, it had been replaced with chicken crisps. They are the outer parts of a grilled chicken breast with no moisture and very few of them.
Having met the owner in the past and having his wife wait on me I knew something wasn't right.
I explained to the waitress that this dish had changed and wasn't good! She politely offered something else. What to order...if they had modified a basic dish what was next?
To my surprise a male manager came out and "informed" me that this is exactly what they had been serving for 10 years and I must have either special ordered something or was mistaken.
I said this is not what they had served me for the past 5 years and I never had requested a special order before. 
I also asked what they had done to the phenominal soft tacos? They were usually served in a soft warm flour tortilla and had moisture and flavor. Tonight they were stale and crisp and the filing was bland.  Again he informed me I was mistaken while he held my order that had been sent back to the kitchen in front of me.
I apologized and said I didn't wish for anything else, thank you.
Another manager came out a few moments later apologizing and stated that they are unfamiliar with what I had ordered and would "special order" anything I wanted. I declined.
Apparently their cook walked out tonight and they were winging it.
Too bad it was a good place to get a good mexican meal.
Two thumbs down on Poblano's.
Revise this with your best effort:
They used to serve a delicious Amiga bowl at Poblano's. It consisted of a flour tortilla bowl filled with an abundance of shredded grilled chicken, a layer of rice, and topped with grilled onions and peppers, covered in a tasty queso sauce. However, tonight was a disappointment. The usual rice and shredded chicken had been replaced with chicken crisps - dry and scarce. This change in the dish made me suspicious, especially since I had previously met the owner and had his wife wait on me. Something was clearly awry.

I voiced my concerns to the waitress, explaining that the dish had changed and wasn't up to par. She was polite and offered an alternative. However, I couldn't shake the thought that if they had modified a basic dish, what other changes were in store?

To my surprise, a male manager came over to "inform" me that this was exactly how they had been serving the Amiga bowl for the past decade. He suggested that I must have either made a special request or was mistaken. Disappointed, I explained that this was not what I had been served for the past five years and that I had never needed to make a special order before. I also inquired about the soft tacos - they were usually served in a warm, soft flour tortilla with a delightful moistness and flavor, but tonight they were stale, crispy, and lacked any notable taste. Once again, the manager insisted that I was mistaken, holding my returned order from the kitchen right in front of me.

Realizing I wasn't going to get anywhere, I apologized and declined any other options. I thanked him and decided I didn't want to try anything else from the menu. It was clear that their cook had walked out that night, leaving them to improvise.

It's a shame because Poblano's used to be a reliable place to enjoy a delicious Mexican meal. Unfortunately, based on my experience, I have to give them a two thumbs down.

input:
I like Deweys's primary because it's close to my house.  The pizza looks great and the crust is good.  My gripe with Dewey's is that the pizzas are just so salty.  We had the pepperoni, socrates revenge, and bronx bomber.  It's like a eatting a brick of salt.  I'm not sure if it's the amount of salt sauce combined with the salty meat, but the combo so overwhelming, I tastebuds are numb to any other flavor.  Otherwise, if they fix that, I would love it.  

As for the salads, they're a good size, but seems like something you can toss together yourself.  I usually not get because don't want to spend the money on it.
Revise this with your best effort:
I enjoy going to Dewey's primary location due to its convenient proximity to my house. The pizza they serve looks very appealing, and the crust is quite satisfying. However, my only complaint about Dewey's is that their pizzas tend to be excessively salty. We tried the pepperoni, socrates revenge, and bronx bomber, and they all tasted like consuming a block of salt. It is possible that the excessive saltiness is a result of the combination of salt sauce and salty meat, but whatever the cause may be, it overwhelms the palate and prevents the enjoyment of other flavors. Nonetheless, if they were to rectify this issue, I would absolutely adore Dewey's.

Regarding their salads, I find them to be a decent size, but they appear to be something one could easily assemble at home. Consequently, I usually refrain from ordering them as I am reluctant to spend money on something I could make myself.

input:
I came in with high hopes and left with slight disappointment. 

Our server was super attentive, and very friendly; however I feel like the food was disappointing. Our egg drop soup came out right away at a nice piping hot temperature and when the rest of our food came out it was practically room temperature. 

Feeling adventurous, I had ordered the Shrimp with Candied Walnuts entree with brown rice while he ordered the Sesame Chicken platter. I like the idea of sharing food, but my food was too busy all on its own without adding something else to the mix. The brown rice was cold and very bland while the shrimp was overly sweet and I didn't feel like the candied walnuts and melon balls were complementary flavors.

The chocolate cake we had for dessert was amazing though; 6 layers of chocolate on chocolate. It was so sweet and rich, we ended up sharing a slice.

So to sum up, service was great, dessert was great, but the food needs some work. Sorry PF Changs, I just am not impressed.

One thing I will note (that our server told us) is that they are very big on catering to food allergies (especially gluten).
Revise this with your best effort:
I had entered the restaurant with optimistic expectations, but sadly, I departed with a tinge of disappointment. Our server proved to be exceptionally attentive and friendly, providing excellent service. However, the food failed to meet my expectations. Although the egg drop soup arrived promptly at a delightful, steaming temperature, the remainder of our meal was disappointingly lukewarm.

Opting for an adventurous selection, I chose the Shrimp with Candied Walnuts entree paired with brown rice, while my companion ordered the Sesame Chicken platter. Although the concept of sharing appealed to me, my dish felt overwhelming on its own, lacking the need for any additional accompaniments. The brown rice was underwhelming and cold, lacking flavor, while the shrimp was overly sugary. Additionally, the combination of candied walnuts and melon balls failed to harmonize in terms of taste.

Nonetheless, the chocolate cake we indulged in for dessert proved to be a highlight of the evening. Comprising a delectable six layers of velvety chocolate, it boasted an irresistible sweetness and richness, compelling us to share a slice together.

In summary, while the service and dessert were commendable, the restaurant could greatly benefit from improving the quality of their cuisine. Regrettably, PF Changs, I cannot claim to be impressed.

On a positive note, our server did convey the restaurant's strong commitment to catering to various dietary restrictions, particularly those related to gluten allergies.

input: We ordered the rib dinner, pork on a bun, Mac n cheese, baked beans, and cole slaw.  Mac n cheese is worthwhile to prostitute yourself out for! The meat on the ribs had great flavor but was as tender as the bottom of my nikes.  Pulled pork had a sweet taste and was overall very good.  Baked beans were okay, cole slaw was very creamy and I would not gets those again (they have an after taste like lake water). The overall experience of getting BBQ in an abandoned car wash is special, worth a try!
Revise this with your best effort:
We indulged in the rib dinner, pork on a bun, Mac n cheese, baked beans, and cole slaw. Let me tell you, the Mac n cheese is simply irresistible! It's so good, it could make you consider trading it for anything! 

While the rib meat boasted fantastic flavor, unfortunately, it lacked the tenderness one would expect. It was a bit tough, like the bottom of my worn-out Nikes. On the other hand, the pulled pork delighted our taste buds with its delightful sweetness, leaving us thoroughly impressed.

The baked beans were decent, nothing extraordinary, but the cole slaw left much to be desired. Its excessively creamy texture had an unpleasant aftertaste reminiscent of lake water. A definite skip in the future.

Now, let's talk about the overall experience. Dining in an abandoned car wash may not sound conventional, but it added a unique touch to our BBQ adventure. It's definitely worth a try for the novelty factor alone!

input: I love the fries (wow, I'm still thinking about them because they're that good!) but I was not impressed by the beef kebob sandwich.  The sandwich was heavy on the onions and light on the meat, so it could have been better.  I do think that may have been an off sandwich, so I'm thinking of going back to give it a second chance (and to have another helping of fries!).  Smoothies also tasted like syrup and ice.  Prices are fair and service is great.  I love the mom and pop feel of the restaurant :).
Revise this with your best effort: I absolutely adore the fries (I mean, they're so incredible that I can't stop thinking about them!). However, I must admit that the beef kebab sandwich failed to impress me. It seemed to be excessively loaded with onions and the meat portion was disappointingly scarce, leaving room for improvement. Nevertheless, I believe that might have been an isolated incident, so I'm contemplating returning for a second try (plus, an additional serving of those irresistible fries!). On another note, the smoothies had a distinct taste of overly sweet syrup and ice. Despite this, the prices are reasonable and the service is exceptional. Additionally, I am fond of the cozy, family-owned ambiance of the restaurant :)

input: It is under new ownership and now called Taqueria Burrito's Grill. Absolutely delish! I love it! The green sauce rocks! I love it on cheese enchiladas. I'm picky about mexican rice and I love theirs. I recently moved back to New Orleans from Houston and one thing I miss is those little Taquerias that most people don't know about. Truly authentic mexican and they recently moved from Houston as well so I knew I was at the right place. It's the only mexican food that I can find in New Orleans East. I'll be a frequent customer. I think I am going back today! Open 7 days a week. Breakfast served 9a-11a. Open past 5PM. There # is 504-242-0573 to call for take out. YUMMY!!!!
Revise this with your best effort: Under new ownership and sporting a charming new name, Taqueria Burrito's Grill has taken the culinary scene by storm. Let me tell you, the food is simply divine! From the mind-blowing green sauce that elevates their cheese enchiladas to another level, to their delectable Mexican rice that even the most discerning palates would appreciate, this place has it all. As someone who recently relocated back to New Orleans from Houston, I must confess that I've been yearning for those hidden gems known as taquerias. Luckily, Taqueria Burrito's Grill shares my sentiment and their move from Houston cements their authenticity. Unsurprisingly, this is the sole joint in New Orleans East where genuine Mexican cuisine can be found. Needless to say, I'll be a regular patron here. In fact, I might even grace them with my presence once again today! Prepare to be awed by their fare as they welcome you seven days a week, serving breakfast from 9am to 11am and remaining open until after 5pm. Take-out can be arranged by calling 504-242-0573. Trust me, you won't regret it - it's absolutely mouthwatering!

input: Had the Mexican Roll and Philadelphia Roll for take-out. Very disappointed with the portion size of the rolls. There was nothing special with the taste and overall bland.
Revise this with your best effort: I ordered the Mexican Roll and Philadelphia Roll for take-out and unfortunately, I was quite disappointed with the portion sizes of both rolls. Additionally, the taste was rather underwhelming, lacking any distinct flavors and overall found them to be quite bland.

input:
I love going into this place to just browse and see what trendy item I can blow my money on. Living near mass ave shopping can be limited but also very competitive. Between silver in the city, boomerang boutique, global gifts, and homespun you pretty much can find whatever you are looking for as far as gifts go. 

Silver in the city is always my go to first. They are always on top of the newest "it" items for your home and style. They also allow dogs in their store so that's a huge plus because I'm typically walking my dog when I stop in. 

The only reason I am not giving them five stars is that although their employees are super friendly, they definitely watch you. I understand the need for this because they have little items that probably get stolen a lot but I always feel like I have no privacy to browse and debate any purchases. 

Cheers!
Revise this with your best effort:
I absolutely adore visiting this establishment solely for the purpose of leisurely browsing and discovering the latest trendy item that I can happily splurge my hard-earned money on. While residing near mass ave shopping may have its limitations, it also presents a highly competitive atmosphere. Fortunately, with options like Silver in the City, Boomerang Boutique, Global Gifts, and Homespun, one can easily find a plethora of gift options to suit their preferences.

When it comes to my go-to choice, Silver in the City never fails to impress. This remarkable store always manages to stay ahead of the curve, showcasing the most current and sought-after home decor and fashion trends. Moreover, their accommodation of dogs within the premises is an absolute treasure to me since I am often accompanied by my furry friend during my shopping excursions.

Despite my fondness for this establishment, I cannot rate them a full five stars due to one minor inconvenience. While the employees are undeniably friendly, their vigilant eyes seem to be constantly watching every move of the customers. I comprehend the necessity of such surveillance, especially considering the vulnerability of small and easily pilferable items, however, it does impede my sense of privacy and my ability to explore potential purchases with undisturbed deliberation.

Cheers to delightful retail therapy!

input: I had takeout because it was about 45 min prior to closing . I ordered the puttanesca. It was delicious . Perfect combo of salty spiciness. There was such a wide variety of menu combos or you could get the fold and creat your own . Genius ! My only gripe is they need to come up with a gluten free dough option. My tummy will pay for this gluttony later .
Revise this with your best effort: I decided to get takeout since it was only 45 minutes before the restaurant closed. I opted for the puttanesca dish, and it turned out to be incredibly delicious. The blend of savory and spicy flavors was perfect. The menu offered a diverse range of combinations, or you could even create your own, which I found to be a brilliant concept. However, I do have one complaint - they should consider offering a gluten-free dough option. Sadly, I know my stomach will suffer later due to this indulgence.

input: Food was great!!!! I had the crab cake Benedict and it was delicious! Great service and smoothies
Revise this with your best effort: The food at this place was absolutely amazing! I decided to try the crab cake Benedict, and it was a truly delicious choice. Not only was the food great, but the service was exceptional as well. The staff went above and beyond to ensure a pleasant dining experience. Additionally, I highly recommend trying their smoothies, as they were incredibly satisfying.

input:
The one thing I really wanted for breakfast while in New Orleans was Grillades. I have made them at home from a recipe but never had them in a restaurant. When Yelp searching this place popped up so it was a must for breakfast. 

The restaurant has a diner style atmosphere. We were seated by the window so we got to watch traffic pass by on Canal Street. Our service was quick and our server was great. 

Of course I ordered the Grits and Grillades. Slow roasted beef with peppers and onions in a brown gravy over creamy Gouda cheese grits sounded perfect. It did not disappoint as it was so delicious!  I get excited when I go to a restaurant and order something I've cooked before and it tastes better than mine. This will be a must on any future New Orleans trips.
Revise this with your best effort:
During my stay in New Orleans, I had one ultimate breakfast craving – Grillades. Although I had tried making them at home by following a recipe, the allure of experiencing them in a restaurant was irresistible. My quest led me to a highly recommended spot that appeared on my Yelp search, making it an essential stop for breakfast.

Entering the restaurant, I was greeted by a classic diner ambiance that instantly put me in a comfortable mood. With a stroke of luck, we were seated next to a window overlooking the bustling traffic on Canal Street, allowing us to observe the vibrant city awakening. The service was prompt, and our server proved to be exceptional, enhancing our overall dining experience.

My eyes scanned the menu, but my heart was set on the Grits and Grillades. The tantalizing description of slow-roasted beef combined with flavorful peppers and onions simmered in a rich brown gravy atop a bed of creamy Gouda cheese grits tempted my taste buds beyond measure. As I took my first bite, the dish surpassed all my expectations. The harmonious blend of succulent beef and savory vegetables, complemented by the decadent creaminess of the Gouda grits, created a symphony of flavors that left me enchanted. It was a moment of pure bliss when the food I had labored over in my own kitchen tasted even more delectable in a restaurant setting.

Without a doubt, Grillades will forever be a staple during my future visits to New Orleans. The memory of that perfect breakfast, savored amidst the lively ambiance and impeccable service, will always beckon me back to this remarkable restaurant.

input: If I could select less than one star I would. Completely awful. After calling multiple times and no one answering, I finally was able to talk to a very unhelpful employee. He emailed me a specific unit, price, move in date and application. I filled out the paperwork but was unable to find the specific unit he indicated. When trying to call about my problem no one answered for 2 full business days. Then when talking with another very unhelpful employee, she told me that unit was already gone & suggested other units more expensive & not in the move in date discussed. When asking if they would honor the price originally discussed in email correspondence, they would not. Long story shorter, I cancelled my application & just wasted $50. This business only cares about money & does not care about the tenants at all.
Revise this with your best effort:
If I could rate this establishment less than one star, I most certainly would. My experience was absolutely dreadful. Despite making multiple unsuccessful attempts to reach them via phone, I eventually managed to speak with an exceptionally unhelpful employee. This individual provided me with an email containing specific details regarding a unit, its price, move-in date, and an application. I duly completed the paperwork, only to find that the unit in question did not exist as stated. Desperate to rectify the situation, I made countless phone calls over the course of two entire business days, but nobody bothered to answer. Finally, when I did manage to connect with another rather unhelpful employee, she nonchalantly informed me that the unit had already been taken, while suggesting other units that were both pricier and not available on the discussed move-in date.

Inquiring whether they would honor the original price we had agreed upon through our email correspondence proved futile, as they outright refused. To cut a long story short, I ultimately decided to cancel my application, resulting in an unfortunate and unnecessary waste of $50. It is abundantly clear that this establishment solely prioritizes financial gain and demonstrates a complete lack of concern for their tenants.

input: Sierra and her sidekick, India, took impeccable care of my family last weekend during a family reunion.  We came to Santa Barbara from all over the world, and Sierra not only took care of purchasing everything we needed ahead of time, but she also thought of things we didn't think of, and went out multiple times to replenish drinks and food we went through.  They were flexible, fun, thorough and all-around fabulous.  I hope I have another event in Santa Barbara in the future, just so I can use JOTSB!
Revise this with your best effort: Sierra and her trusted sidekick, India, provided unparalleled care and attention to my family during our recent family reunion in Santa Barbara. Despite our diverse origins from various corners of the globe, Sierra's meticulous planning not only ensured the acquisition of all our necessities in advance but also astoundingly anticipated our unspoken needs. She tirelessly made multiple trips to restock our drinks and food, going above and beyond to guarantee our utmost satisfaction. Their adaptable nature, jovial presence, unwavering thoroughness, and overall excellence truly made our experience unforgettable. I earnestly yearn for another opportunity to host an event in Santa Barbara solely to enlist the exceptional services of JOTSB once again.

input: Meh...I wasn't impressed with this spot. Looking past the array of hand written signs and lack of available bagels, the food was ok. I got the pastrami, egg, and cheese. There was hardly any pastrami and the cheese wasn't melted. My wife also had the pleasure of adding spoiled creamer to her coffee. I think we'll just stick with Einstein's or St Pete Bagel.
Revise this with your best effort: I must say, I was underwhelmed by this establishment. Despite the plethora of handwritten signs and the disappointing absence of bagels, the food itself was mediocre at best. Opting for the pastrami, egg, and cheese sandwich, I found it to be lacking in pastrami and the cheese was far from properly melted. To add insult to injury, my wife had the unfortunate experience of discovering spoiled creamer in her coffee. It seems that our allegiance will remain with either Einstein's or St Pete Bagel, as their offerings are far superior.

input: Very nice employes very resonable price. Excellent homemade salad dressing. Good food, an all around good italian resturant.
Revise this with your best effort: The employees at this Italian restaurant are very pleasant, and the prices are quite reasonable. They offer an outstanding selection of homemade salad dressings that enhance the flavors of their delicious dishes. Overall, this is a fantastic Italian restaurant that not only serves good food but also provides a great dining experience.

input: I love their breakfast burritos. I usually get bacon, egg, cheese and potatoes. The potatoes are  well seasoned and cut small, so you don't end up getting a burrito that is about 95% full of overdone, mushy potatoes. You can actually taste the eggs, bacon and potatoes. Could use a bit more cheese, but that's a minor complaint. Nice selection of salsas at the salsa bar and the staff has always been friendly and welcoming. Very glad that they are located about a mile from my house! Hopefully they will be here for a long time.
Revise this with your best effort: I have an immense love for their breakfast burritos, particularly the ones filled with bacon, egg, cheese, and potatoes. The potatoes are expertly seasoned and cut into small, delectable pieces, ensuring that your burrito doesn't end up being overwhelmingly dominated by overcooked and mushy potatoes. Each bite allows you to savor the flavors of the eggs, bacon, and potatoes harmoniously. The only minor complaint I have is that it could benefit from a tad more cheese. Nevertheless, the salsa bar offers a fantastic variety of salsas, adding an extra layer of delight to your meal. Moreover, the staff is consistently warm, friendly, and welcoming, enhancing the overall experience. I am incredibly grateful that this delightful establishment is conveniently located just a mile away from my residence. Here's hoping that they remain a cherished fixture in the neighborhood for many years to come.

input:
I'm still new to Tucson, but having tried a large sample of the various pizza places near the U of A, I have to say that this is the best so far. 

In fact I'd say it's the best I've ever had. Better than the places I tried in NYC even. The crust is just magical. The five alarm (which I tried) is the perfect amount of spicy for those of us who crave that extra spicyness in our food. 

If you decide to try it, I doubt you'll be disappointed.
Revise this with your best effort: Although I'm still a newcomer to Tucson, I've extensively explored the multitude of pizza joints near the U of A, and without a doubt, this particular establishment reigns supreme. I would even go so far as to proclaim it the best pizza I have ever had, surpassing even the renowned pizzerias of NYC. The sheer enchantment lies within the crust, which possesses a mystical quality that transcends ordinary pizza experiences. Notably, their five alarm pizza, which I personally sampled, strikes a harmonious balance of spiciness that caters to the palates of individuals who yearn for that extra fiery kick in their dishes. Should you decide to embark upon this gastronomic journey, I firmly believe you will not be left feeling dissatisfied.

input: I heard alot about Honey's and how the food is so good here. I chose today my birthday to be my first visit .I read earlier reviews about how crowded it gets and they were not lying but I didn't wait no more than 20 minutes. Now let's get down to the food it was delicious. I had french toast, home fries, sausage and for dessert a slice of Jewish apple cake and it was to die for! I will be back most definitely.
Revise this with your best effort: I had heard so much about Honey's and how incredible their food is, so I decided to make my first visit on my birthday. I had read some reviews beforehand mentioning how crowded it can get, and let me tell you, they were not exaggerating. However, I didn't have to wait for more than 20 minutes. Now, let's dive into the food because it was absolutely delicious. I indulged in their mouthwatering French toast, perfectly cooked home fries, flavorful sausage, and to top it off, a slice of their heavenly Jewish apple cake. It was truly to die for! I am definitely planning on returning.

input: Tria's employees are very knowledgeable about the selection of beers and wines they offer. This is probably why I look forward to going to Tria. This location has outside seating during the warmer months and is a real treat if you can get a table out there. It always seems to be busy, which is a good thing. I've never had any of the food items at Tria, because the real treat here are the drinks.
Revise this with your best effort: Tria's employees possess an outstanding expertise when it comes to the exquisite array of beers and wines they offer. It is undoubtedly the remarkable knowledge and passion they exhibit that makes me eagerly anticipate my visits to Tria. Moreover, the establishment's outdoor seating during the delightful warmer months is a genuine indulgence, provided one is fortunate enough to secure a coveted table. The perpetual buzz of activity only adds to the appeal, epitomizing its popularity. Although I cannot personally speak to the quality of their food items, as the primary allure of Tria lies in its exceptional drink selection, known to be an unparalleled pleasure.

input: Mae's is the best Chinese restaurant on this east side. We tried Mae's due to some rude pricks across the street. Lol! But, luckily things happen for a reason. The environment, the decor, the air inside is so much better to start. The food taste so much more fresher, like it was not frozen or reheated. No greasy/oily after taste. The service is very good,  always right there when you need something, staff is very friendly. My family and I love Mae's and what makes it better are the prices. We're large family and we can do really well with just $60. Lunch specials are awesome! I encourage you to try Mae's.
Revise this with your best effort: Mae's is undoubtedly the premier Chinese restaurant located on the east side. Our initial visit to Mae's was a result of some unfavorable experiences with a neighboring establishment. However, as fate would have it, we discovered that Mae's truly excelled in all areas. From the moment we stepped inside, we were enamored by the delightful ambiance, tasteful decor, and refreshing atmosphere. The cuisine itself surpassed our expectations, boasting a noticeably fresher taste that indicated an absence of freezing or reheating practices. Notably, there was no lingering greasy or oily aftertaste, enhancing our dining experience. The service provided by Mae's staff was exceptional, with their attentive presence whenever we required assistance, and their friendly demeanor amplified our enjoyment. It is with great pleasure that my family and I express our fondness for Mae's, and the icing on the cake is the astonishing affordability it offers. Being a large family, we are able to indulge in a satisfying meal with a meager sum of $60. The lunch specials provided are truly remarkable, offering great value for your money. To all those reading this, I wholeheartedly encourage you to embark on your own dining journey at Mae's.

input: This place is my absolute fave! The flavors are spot on, they taste exactly the way you imagine, but better! The strawberries & champagne, toasted marshmallow, and cheesecake  are a few of my personal favorites. I moved to Phoenix a few years back and was ecstatic when I found out they opened locations in the valley. This is a Tucson gem that I will continue to visit over and over!
Revise this with your best effort: This place holds a special place in my heart! The flavors here are truly exceptional, capturing the exact essence you'd imagine and even surpassing expectations! The combination of strawberries and champagne, toasted marshmallow, and cheesecake are just a few of the outstanding flavors that I personally adore. After relocating to Phoenix a few years ago, I couldn't contain my excitement when I discovered they had expanded their reach to the valley. In my eyes, this gem of Tucson is a delightful sanctuary that I plan to frequent time and time again!

input: This location used to be good, several years ago. About 3 years ago it started to go downhill and now it is just terrible. There were 2 people working on a Saturday evening. Nearly all the tables were full and there were people waiting to order and to pay. The sandwich that was made for me was on hard bread, burnt and barely edible. They need to either shape up or ship out.
Revise this with your best effort: This establishment was once commendable, but unfortunately, its quality has significantly declined over the past few years. Around three years ago, a noticeable deterioration began, and presently, it has become abysmal. On a recent Saturday evening, only two staff members were on duty despite the majority of tables being occupied and a queue forming for ordering and payment. Regrettably, the sandwich I was served had hard, burnt bread that was barely palatable. It is imperative for them to promptly rectify their shortcomings, or it may be prudent for them to consider shutting down altogether.

input:
The girly loves this cemetery for photographing angels and such. Personally, I think she's a little creepy.

On the plus side, it's quiet, no zombies and the witches doing spells took time out to photobomb a bit.

So there's that.

Seriously, a well laid out cemetery and some of the better made stones and angels.

And no zombies. Remember that part.
Revise this with your best effort:
The girl truly adores this cemetery as it offers a captivating setting for capturing images of angels and other subjects. However, I must admit that I find her fascination a bit unsettling.

Nevertheless, one cannot deny the tranquility of this place; unlike the typical notion of a cemetery, there are no lurking zombies, and even the witches, engrossed in their spellcasting, managed to amusingly photobomb a few shots.

Concentrating on the positives, it's worth noting that this cemetery is impressively organized, boasting exceptionally crafted tombstones and angelic statues.

And need I mention the absence of zombies? That aspect should not be overlooked.

input:
On a recent trip to Port Richey, I selected Holiday Inn Express for a couple of reasons.  The main reason was the option of two beds (as I was sharing the room with my brother).  The other reasons were:  price, vicinity to my aunt's home and complementary breakfast. 

My family and I typically stay at the Hyatt Place/House when we're traveling.  However, since it was just my brother and I, I figured we'd give Holiday Inn a shot. 

+  The staff were very friendly and helpful.
+  Free wifi.
+  Breakfast was very good, offering both hot and cold entrees. 

-  Sadly, the beds were WAY TOO soft.  It felt as if the mattresses were past their life expectancy.  As a result, I didn't really sleep well for most of my three nights there.
-  The a/c was hit and miss with the lack of reliable thermostat controls. 

There was a pool and hot tub, but since I didn't utilize either, it wouldn't be fair to rate them.  There also a small gym that I didn't use either. 

All in all, it was just ok.  Hyatt has spoiled me.
Revise this with your best effort:
During my recent trip to Port Richey, I opted for Holiday Inn Express for various reasons. Firstly, the availability of two beds was crucial as I was sharing the room with my brother. Additionally, the reasonable price, convenient location near my aunt's house, and the inclusion of a complementary breakfast attracted me to this hotel.

Normally, my family and I prefer to stay at the Hyatt Place/House when we travel. However, since it was just my brother and me, I thought it would be a good opportunity to give Holiday Inn a try.

On the positive side, the staff at the Holiday Inn Express were exceptionally friendly and always ready to assist. The presence of free wifi was also a convenient feature. Moreover, the breakfast offered a wide range of options, including both hot and cold dishes, which were enjoyable.

Unfortunately, there were a couple of downsides to my stay. The beds were surprisingly soft to the point where it felt like the mattresses were well past their prime. As a result, I struggled to get a good night's sleep for most of the three nights I was there. Additionally, the air conditioning in the room was inconsistent due to unreliable thermostat controls.

Although the hotel boasted a pool and hot tub, I didn't have the chance to utilize either, so I cannot provide an accurate rating of these amenities. There was also a small gym available, but I didn't make use of it during my stay.

Overall, my experience at the Holiday Inn Express was just mediocre. The high standards set by the Hyatt hotels have spoiled me, leaving me expecting more from my accommodations.

input: The staff wasn't too interested in helping customers, instead focused on the TV in the lobby, flirting with each other and just standing around. I found the food to be ok, not great, not terrible. I'll round up from the 1.5 I give them.
Revise this with your best effort: The staff seemed disinterested in assisting customers, prioritizing the TV in the lobby, engaging in flirtatious conversations amongst themselves, and generally lingering without purpose. Regarding the food, it was passable but not exceptional. While it didn't impress me greatly, I am willing to give them a rounded-up score of 2 out of 5.

input:
The food is excellent. The customer service and quantity over time has continued to go down. I've been going to this place every couple weeks for two years. The portions over time have continued to gradually get smaller and smaller. I commented on this, because my take out dish is now to the point where it is less then half full when I order, when it used to go to the top. When I commented on this I was told I was wrong.  I proceeded to explain my case. I was told if I didn't want to take the food, I didn't have to pay for it. I said ok, and was the berated for not taking the food I ordered. 

Long story short, these people have lost my business. I am not going back.
Revise this with your best effort:
The food at this place is undeniably exceptional. However, I've noticed a decline in the customer service and portion sizes over time. For the past two years, I have been a regular customer, visiting every couple of weeks. Unfortunately, the portions have gradually decreased in size. It has reached a point where my take-out dish is now less than half full, whereas it used to be filled to the brim. When I brought up this concern, I was met with denial and told that I was mistaken. I tried to explain my case, but was dismissed and told that I didn't have to pay if I didn't want the food. Though I agreed not to take the order, I was then scolded for not accepting the food I had initially ordered.

To sum it up, I have decided to no longer patronize this establishment. They have lost my business and I will not be returning.

input: Food was great. Staff was nice, friendly and helpful with menu suggestions. The Happy Hour is a good deal and the house margaritas tasted better than many other restaurants I've visited. I had the chicken poblano which was great. My friend enjoyed his enchiladas and they allowed him to have 3 different types on one plate.
Revise this with your best effort: The dining experience was exceptional as the food surpassed all expectations. The staff exhibited remarkable qualities of kindness, warmth, and helpfulness, going above and beyond by offering valuable insights and recommendations from the menu. The Happy Hour turned out to be an outstanding deal, and the house margaritas surpassed the standards set by countless other establishments I have patronized in the past. Opting for the chicken poblano dish proved to be an outstanding choice as it delivered a fantastic flavor profile. Moreover, my friend relished his enchiladas, and the accommodating staff graciously fulfilled his request to have three distinctive types impeccably presented on a single plate.

input: Try the salted caramel chocolate cake. It was the best we ever had. I also tried the Apple Brown Betty  - awesome. Good beer selection.
Revise this with your best effort: You should definitely try the salted caramel chocolate cake; it's truly the most exceptional one we've ever had. Additionally, I had the pleasure of tasting the Apple Brown Betty, and it was absolutely awesome. On top of that, they offer a fantastic variety of beers to choose from.

input:
A laid back bar for the college crowd. Cheap drinks.  They have projectors so u can watch the big game that day. However the screen needs to be two feet wider so the picture doesn't go off into the wall.

I came here during the day so it was really spacious, but I can only imagine how it is at night.
Revise this with your best effort: Experience a relaxed bar perfectly suited for the vibrant college crowd, offering affordable drinks that won't break the bank. With the inclusion of projectors, you can enjoy the excitement of watching the big game right on the premises. The only minor improvement required is a two-foot wider screen to ensure that the picture remains uninterrupted, eliminating those moments where it spills onto the adjacent wall. When I visited during the day, I appreciated the ample space available, and I can only envision how thriving and lively it must be during the captivating nights.

input: Terrible service. Called in an order for pick up and completely butchered my order. I asked for a half sausage half cheese pizza and felt like he had no clue what i was saying as i had to constantly repeat myself. i had my boyfriend call back to make sure the order was right and he repeated back the order that i ordered half sausage half BEEF??? So after we corrected him and picked up or pizza, we got back and opened it up and it was ALL SAUSAGE. This is the second time in the past month i have had terrible service. The first time i got there for pickup and they had completely forgotten to put my order in. Terrible.
Revise this with your best effort: Extremely disappointed with the service received. I placed an order for pick-up, specifically requesting a half sausage and half cheese pizza. However, it seemed like the person on the phone had difficulty understanding my order, as I had to repeat myself multiple times. In an attempt to ensure accuracy, I had my boyfriend call back to confirm the order, but to our surprise, he was informed that I had ordered half sausage and half beef instead. After correcting the misunderstanding and collecting our pizza, we returned home, only to discover that it was entirely sausage, not the half sausage and half cheese we had requested. This has unfortunately been the second instance of such terrible service in just a month. The first time, upon arriving for pick-up, they had inexplicably forgotten to prepare my order at all. These repeated disappointments have left me thoroughly dissatisfied.

input:
do not eat here. my husband, two friends and i went out for restaurant week to marmont steakhouse on saturday, january 26, 2013; our experience was horrific.  the four of us ordered the crab bisque soup for our first course, it was cold and we sent it back to be reheated.  my second course was the calamari it was bland, fried too hard and rubbery.  finally two ppl from our party ordered the lobster ravioli for an entree.  it was not lobster ravioli but beef. i asked our waiter and one other waiter to please double check with the chef because this is not lobster, i expressed that i have not eaten beef or pork since 1994, and that it would make me ill. they both came back separately and argued that it was in fact lobster. another party of maybe 6 ppl ordered the lobster ravioli, they had the same problem and sent their dishes back to the kitchen too.  the server finally came over after i'd eaten two of the ravioli to apologize for the kitchens error and telling us that was in fact beef. 
i have been in the bathroom all day with diarrhea from the beef ravioli! the staff was very nonchalant about it and offered an insincere apology.
Revise this with your best effort:
I strongly advise against dining at Marmont Steakhouse. My husband, two friends, and I had a terrible experience during restaurant week on Saturday, January 26, 2013. Our entire meal was a disaster. 

To start, the crab bisque soup we ordered for our first course was served cold. We had to send it back to be reheated. Moving on to the calamari for our second course, it was incredibly bland, over-fried, and had a rubbery texture. 

The worst part came when two members of our party ordered the lobster ravioli as an entrée. Shockingly, what was served to us was not lobster ravioli, but beef. Despite bringing this to the attention of our waiter and another server, they both argued that it was indeed lobster. However, another group of about six people who also ordered the lobster ravioli faced the same issue and returned their dishes to the kitchen. 

Only after I had already consumed two of the ravioli did the server finally come over to apologize for the kitchen's mistake and admit that it was, in fact, beef. As a person who has not consumed beef or pork since 1994, this was extremely concerning and made me ill. I have been dealing with severe diarrhea all day as a result. 

Moreover, the staff displayed an indifferent attitude towards our problem and offered a hollow apology that lacked sincerity. Given this horrific experience, I strongly urge you to avoid dining at Marmont Steakhouse.

input: It simply does not get any better than Tako for sushi. Everything is fresh & delicious. The private rooms are so fun for a festive night out, it's BYO & when my girls get together we enjoy the feast & atmosphere! Some personal favorites are the jalapeño yellowtail(a must!!), kani salad, bird's nest roll & the naruto (served in cucumber instead of rice. Honestly, you can't go wrong when ordering. And so reasonable!! I rarely spend over $35 including tip when we go, and we do not hold back at all when ordering. Highly, highly recommend Tako!
Revise this with your best effort: Tako for sushi is simply unparalleled. The freshness and deliciousness of their offerings surpass any other place. The private rooms add an extra level of excitement for a festive night out. What's more, it's BYO, making it even more enjoyable when my friends and I gather for a feast in a delightful atmosphere. Among the delectable dishes, the jalapeño yellowtail is an absolute must-try, as well as the kani salad, bird's nest roll, and the unique naruto (served in a refreshing cucumber wrap instead of rice). Honestly, there is no wrong choice on the menu. And the best part? It's incredibly reasonable! Rarely do we spend over $35, including a generous tip, and we definitely indulge ourselves. Tako comes highly, highly recommended!
