input: Very good local ice cream. Expresso chip. Moose tracks. Graham Slam are all custom made flavors.
Revise this with your best effort: The local ice cream establishment offers an exceptional range of delicious custom-made flavors. From the indulgent Expresso Chip to the mouthwatering Moose Tracks and the delightful Graham Slam, their ice cream selection is truly top-notch.

input:

(Firemen also get a discount on Mondays) . This isn't a hand-wash, so it's not perfect  but a good $5 carwash if your "baby" needs a quick bath.

They do run a special every now and then on auto detail packages 2 for 1. My husband and I always buy when they're running this special, since they have always done a nice job.
Revise this with your best effort:
My husband and I have been bringing our trucks to this car wash for several years now and we have no complaints whatsoever. It's worth mentioning that on Mondays, firemen are also eligible for a discount. Furthermore, they occasionally run promotions on their auto detail packages, offering a "2 for 1" deal. This is an opportunity my husband and I always take advantage of because they consistently deliver excellent results.

input:
Everything about this place is average. The food is just ok, the service sort of depends on your luck - sometimes good sometimes not so good.

This place doesn't really stand out in any aspect. The food is neither exceptional nor disappointing, just average. The level of service is inconsistent, as it seems to vary depending on chance; at times it can be satisfactory, but there are instances when it falls short.

I've tried their drunken noodles and Thai green curry on separate occasions, and both dishes turned out to be quite average in taste and execution.

input:
This is a milestone review for me on Yelp.  I had been struggling with which one to chhose.  I decidede to make it Redemption.  This was seriously one of the best meals of my ENTIRE life.  

This review was from about 2 months ago.  Sorry it is a little dated.  Such as life.  

The setting is an old church.  It is really a beautiful surrounding for a restaurant.  Although I am an old church architecture nerd.  It was really cool to look around.   

The service was incredible.  I was hear as part of a group of 7 other characters, several were part of the NOLA restaurant scene.  We wanted a good time with the meal and they provided it!   

Paneed smoked soft shell crab a la Christian.  I was not fortunate enough to have enjoyed the original.  I can not comment on the faithfulness to the founders recipe.  I can say this there is no highe calling for a soft shell crab than to be cold smoked and fried in preparation for this dish.  On to your 77 virgins and mecca for you!  But I experienced heaven eating this.  

Seafood stuffed filet of fish a la Christian's - This was superlative.  Again did not try the original, but the mirliton and seafood stuffing was heavenly, and more importantly improved the taste of the fresh flounder rather than competing for the spot light!   

The combination was quite possibly one of the 10 best meals of my life.  If you have been here, you should try it!
Revise this with your best effort:
This is a milestone review for me on Yelp. After much deliberation, I finally decided to choose Redemption, and I must say, it turned out to be one of the most memorable meals I have ever had.

Although this review is from about 2 months ago, please forgive its slight datedness. That's just how life goes sometimes.

The restaurant is located in an old church, creating a beautiful and unique ambiance. Being an old church architecture enthusiast, I found it especially fascinating to explore the surroundings.

The service was absolutely phenomenal. My dining experience took place with a group of 7 other individuals, some of whom were part of the NOLA restaurant scene. We were seeking a good time along with our meal, and the staff delivered beyond our expectations.

Now, let's talk about the food. The Paneed smoked soft shell crab a la Christian was an absolute delight. Although I can't compare it to the original, I must say that there is something truly exceptional about the combination of cold-smoked and fried soft shell crab for this dish. It was like a taste of heaven.

Next up, the Seafood stuffed filet of fish a la Christian's. This dish was beyond superb. While I didn't get a chance to try the original version, the mirliton and seafood stuffing added a heavenly touch to the fresh flounder, enhancing its flavor rather than overpowering it.

In summary, this combination of dishes was easily one of the top 10 meals of my life. If you haven't been to Redemption yet, I highly recommend giving it a try.

input:
I love this place. It's just down the street from me so I'm there probably every other week... don't judge me! They rotate their flavors regularly and if at first you don't see a topping you'd like be sure and ask if they have it because they keep some under the counter!

This place also busts out some pretty intense EDM music over their sound system, which is somewhat bizarre but wholly awesome!
Revise this with your best effort:
I absolutely adore this place! It's conveniently located just down the street from me, so I find myself visiting almost every other week. Please, don't judge me! What sets this place apart is their fantastic variety of flavors that they rotate regularly. If you don't initially see a topping that piques your interest, don't hesitate to inquire if they have it, as they often keep some hidden under the counter for surprises!

input:
Amazing. We had; Steak Tartare, Caribbean Seafood Pepper Pot and the Curried Goat. Everything was really wonderful. Tartare maybe the best i've had. The goat with the sweet curry and gnocchi was very different and I loved it. I had a bite of the lime cheesecake and it was top notch, too. 

No drinks, because it's 2 days after Mardi Gras and I'm still in recovery mode. The service was among the best I've had in this town, which is know for it's hospitality industry. Great great great!

Unfortunately, we refrained from ordering any drinks since it was just two days after Mardi Gras and we were still in recovery mode. input:
I went here on a Wednesday night and, though it wasn't busy, there were no open tables without a reservation,  except the tall tables in the bar area. It still seemed to be a very quiet place anyway. 

The location is not attractive, the street is dark and mostly empty at night, but the inside is stylish in a masculine, refined sort of way; dark wood, low light, maps on the walls and prints of watercolors depicting old Missouri scenes. It was a great place for a quiet, intimate dinner. They've got a couple of TVs up above the bar. 

They seemed very well staffed, as if each table had its own server. 

The menu is one page but very intriguing, I had so many questions for our server about "what is this?" and "what is that?" and he was totally nice and knowledgeable about the menu items. He seemed nervous and unsure at first, but he was friendly and made sure to check on us frequently. 

We decided to split 3 small plates and a side dish between the two of us and, honestly, it was a little too much food for just two people. Perhaps we don't have hearty enough appetites.

Their menu is so varied and interesting, it's really all over the map in terms of seasonings and ethnic origins but the main focus seems to be rustic and warming - at least at this time of year. I have a feeling they may change it up from time to time. I'm sure you'll get things here you won't find anywhere else. The prices are very reasonable, considering the planning and good execution of the food. You'd certainly find more expensive, and less original places in Clayton and down town. 

We ordered the smoked trout, the venison hot dogs, the mini monte cristo sandwiches, and the french fries. 

The venison hot dogs and the smoked trout were fantastic and interesting. The french fries were very well made, and the dipping sauces delicious. I was so impressed with these that I was then a bit underwhelmed by the mini monte cristos. Since everything else there seemed to have a unique spin on it, I expected them to do something original here as well, but they were just like any monte cristo you might have. They were very tasty of course, but nothing new. 

With the food plus two draft beers, our total was $52.05 before tip and we were stuffed and satisfied. I applaud them!
Revise this with your best effort:
On a Wednesday night, I visited this establishment and found that despite it not being busy, all tables were reserved except for the tall ones in the bar area. Nevertheless, the ambiance remained calm and serene.

While the location lacked attractiveness, with a dark and mostly empty street during the evening, the interior exuded a stylish and refined masculinity. The dark wood, dim lighting, and wall decorations consisting of maps and watercolor prints depicting old Missouri scenes created a great atmosphere for a quiet and intimate meal. The bar area featured a few TVs.

The staff appeared to be well-staffed, with each table having its own server.

Although their menu consisted of just one page, it was truly intriguing, leading me to bombard our server with questions regarding the various dishes. He was friendly, knowledgeable, and although initially hesitant, he made sure to check on us frequently.

Opting to split three small plates and a side dish between the two of us, we found that the portion size was slightly excessive for our appetites.

The menu showcased a diverse range of seasonings and ethnic origins, with a particular focus on rustic and comforting dishes, especially during this time of year. I had a hunch that their menu might change periodically. Undoubtedly, this place offers unique culinary experiences that can't be found elsewhere. Remarkably, the prices were reasonable considering the meticulous planning and execution of the food. In comparison, other places in Clayton and downtown charge more for less inventive dishes.

For our order, we selected the smoked trout, venison hot dogs, mini monte cristo sandwiches, and french fries.

The venison hot dogs and smoked trout were truly outstanding and delivered a fascinating flavor profile. The french fries were expertly prepared, and the accompanying dipping sauces were delectable. However, my enthusiasm waned slightly when it came to the mini monte cristos. Given the originality apparent in the other dishes, I anticipated a unique twist here as well. Unfortunately, they tasted like typical monte cristos, albeit still enjoyable.

Our bill, including two draft beers, amounted to $52.05 before tip, and we left feeling stuffed and satisfied. I wholeheartedly commend their efforts!

input: "High Score!"...unfortunately I wasn't playing a video game with my friends, but rather wracked up the highest weight for my frozen yogurt. Revise this with your best effort: "New High Score!"...unfortunately, it wasn't achieved while playing video games with my friends. input: I went last night with a few friends and let me say I was impressed, not necessarily with the quality of the food (nothing wrong with it by any means) or the decor, but the servers: how they don't kill every 4th customer is beyond me. I heard tables on both sides of us giving the most ridiculous of complaints to our/their server. Both tables were demanding as hell and already said loudly to eachother that they weren't tipping because of x, y and z reasons, and then were dumbfounded that there's a gratuity on their bill (it says it in the menu, anything over $50) their server, smaller girl so with purple hair, carried upwards of 4 plates at once, explained the menu perfectly and had an eagle eye for every table in her section and dealt with ridiculous complaints like a true professional. Thumbs up and five stars to the staff, customers, learn how to be basic humans, or stay home.
Revise this with your best effort:
I had the opportunity to dine with a few friends last night, and I must say, I was thoroughly impressed. While it wasn't necessarily the food or the decor that stood out, it was the exceptional service from the servers that truly amazed me. Despite the challenging circumstances, I couldn't fathom how they managed to remain composed and provide excellent service to every customer, especially when faced with unreasonable demands and absurd complaints from neighboring tables.

Both tables on either side of us seemed to be excessively demanding and made it clear that they had no intention of leaving a tip due to various reasons, X, Y, and Z. However, they seemed completely astonished when the gratuity charge appeared on their bill, despite it being clearly indicated in the menu for orders exceeding $50. Our server, a remarkable young woman with purple hair, effortlessly carried numerous plates at once, flawlessly explained the menu, and displayed an exceptional attentiveness to every table in her section. She handled each ridiculous complaint with utmost professionalism.

I cannot praise the staff enough; they truly deserve a standing ovation. As for the other customers, I urge them to learn the basics of being considerate human beings or simply stay at home. The staff deserves nothing less than a five-star rating for their exceptional service.

input:

I found that their list prices were fair and competitive, as well as the certification and warranties on used vehicles - I just chose a different car make/model than I shopped for at Hallmark. Had I liked the car better than what I was comparing it to, I would have likely bought from them. Based on some pretty terrible experiences at other places, I would recommend trying this dealership if you are looking to buy locally.

Although I ultimately did not make a purchase at this particular dealership, I must say that the overall shopping experience exceeded my expectations compared to most other dealerships. I was particularly impressed with the straightforwardness of their process.

If the car had suited my preferences better than the alternative I was considering, I would have highly likely made my purchase from them. Considering the disappointingly negative experiences I have had at other dealerships, I would highly recommend giving this particular dealership a try if you are in the market for a local purchase.

input: Delicious! We had the warm and cold lobster rolls and both were great.  Bread was amazing too!  A little on the expensive side but you get what you pay for and it was quality food.

While it may be slightly pricier, the old saying holds true - you get what you pay for, and in this case, it was undeniably top-notch, high-quality cuisine.

input:

The onion rings are very good also.
Revise this with your best effort:
The Habit Burger is undeniably a fantastic burger joint. It has always been a challenging decision for me to choose between In-N-Out and The Habit Burger. input: My husband and I practically live here, and have through the past 8 years or so.  They have great food, prepared fast, great drink specials.
Revise this with your best effort: My husband and I have practically made this place our second home over the past 8 years or so. Moreover, they offer fantastic drink specials that add an extra touch of delight to our dining experience.

input:
It is typical Broad Ripple charming spot. Small, trendy and bustling with activity. They do not take reservations. Which is somewhat annoying when you are traveling from another part of town. Whatever, we just had to arrange to arrive earlier than we would have liked to hopefully secure a table, which we did. When we arrived it was quiet and only several tables had guests seated. As our dinner progressed it became more crowded until every seat was filled. Nice lively scene except then you can not hear squat! It made dinner conversation difficult. Boo!!!! I think this could be an easy fix for them. 

Meal/Drinks:  The cocktails were creative and tasted wonderful. Our servers suggestions were pretty spot on as we enjoyed most of her suggestions. 

The guacamole was very good with the exception of the fact that my friend has a nut allergy and we asked to have them left off and of coarse they arrived with them on! They really weren't necessary in my opinion either as I don't think they add much to the dish. The reason I wanted to try this restaurant- The Harvest salad! We all split this as well and it was good. The combination of fruit and root vegetables was delish! The figs were so good and the herbed goat cheese mouse was a highlight on this plate!

Two of us ordered the Veracruz Trigger fish and the other ordered the Serrano Scallops and all of it was wonderful. The white sweet mashed potatoes were interesting! I am glad we tried them. The Veracruz sauce was wonderful and full of flavor. It was a lot of food though. Had we known we would have probably skipped one of the first course selections or split an entree. That'a ok though- lunch for today :)

We also tried the Tostones and Stewed Black Beans. Beans were very good, full of flavor! Tostones seemed very dry but maybe that is what they are supposed to be- this is the first time I have had them. BUT, dipped in the Stewed Black Beans they tasted great!

We passed on dessert as they had no gluten free, dairy free options. Delicia offers many options for restricted diets, which we loved. Just no dessert, which is probably better anyway-we were so full! 

Go, you will not be disappointed. Just go before 7pm on a Friday night to ensure a table.
Revise this with your best effort:
This restaurant in Broad Ripple is a typical charming spot that is small, trendy, and always bustling with activity. One downside is that they do not take reservations, which can be annoying if you are traveling from another part of town. Despite this, we made arrangements to arrive earlier than planned to secure a table, which we thankfully managed to do. When we initially arrived, the atmosphere was quiet and only a few tables had guests seated. However, as our dinner progressed, the place became more crowded until every seat was filled. It was a lively scene, but unfortunately, the noise level made it difficult to have a conversation during dinner. This is something that the restaurant could easily fix, and it would greatly enhance the overall experience.

Now onto the food and drinks. The cocktails were creative and tasted wonderful, and our server's suggestions were pretty spot on as we enjoyed most of her recommendations. The guacamole was very good, except for the fact that we specifically requested to have the nuts left off due to a friend's allergy, but they arrived on the dish anyway. Personally, I didn't think the nuts added much to the dish, so they weren't really necessary in my opinion. However, the reason I wanted to try this restaurant was for their Harvest salad, and it did not disappoint. We all shared it, and the combination of fruit and root vegetables was delicious. The figs were particularly good, and the herbed goat cheese mousse was a highlight of the dish.

For our main courses, two of us ordered the Veracruz Trigger fish, while the other opted for the Serrano Scallops, and all of it was wonderful. The white sweet mashed potatoes were an interesting and tasty addition. The Veracruz sauce was flavorful and delicious, although the portions were quite large. If we had known, we would have either skipped one of our first course selections or split an entrée. Nevertheless, that just meant we had leftovers for lunch the next day.

We also decided to try the Tostones and Stewed Black Beans. The beans were full of flavor and quite good. The Tostones, on the other hand, seemed a bit dry, but perhaps that is how they are supposed to be. This was our first time having them, but when dipped in the Stewed Black Beans, they tasted great!

Unfortunately, we had to pass on dessert as they did not have any gluten-free or dairy-free options. However, we were so full from our meal that it was probably for the best. On a positive note, Delicia, another restaurant in the area, offers many options for restricted diets, which we appreciated.

input:
This makes my 6th or 7th time to Jackson's in the last 2 years and I thought that after tonight's visit they deserved a review. 

I had the panini Reuben.  Panini was amazing. Great use of garlic. Loved the cut of the meat. Not stringy but nicely chinked in thin slices. Cheese was well melted throughout the mix of kraut and meat. Rye Bread was wonderful. Would love to have it as a staple in my house. 

Salad came out same time as sandwich which was not good.

Presentation was a little sloppy. 

Like every other place I have had a panini (except Panera where they do it right), the sandwich was served directly on a plate. Why don't they serve on a napkin? Particularly when they bring the salad out at the same time as the sandwich?  If the sandwich sits for more than a few moments, the bread gets soggy from the steam.  Nothing serious, but for the price, which is a little high, it seems lacking.  While the price is a little high, i think it is justified considering the food and drink quality. 

They have a great selection of wines and beers that are likely to fit any palette.  

Wait staff have always been friendly. But you can tell this is a place where people are expected to hustle. Sometimes short or even distracted the service can be lacking. 

The second time I visited was during a medium lunch rush and the wait time was 15 min to get drinks. My trip tonight it was about 8 min. For a sat night this is not bad. But not great either. My bartenders were awesome and never left me wanting (except for getting my salad with the main course).

Overall a good experience and I will be back.
Revise this with your best effort:
This is my sixth or seventh visit to Jackson's in the past two years, and I feel that after tonight's visit, they truly deserve a review.

I ordered the panini Reuben, and it was absolutely amazing. The panini had a great use of garlic, and the meat was cut perfectly - not stringy, but instead thinly sliced and nicely chinked. The cheese was melted perfectly throughout the mix of sauerkraut and meat. Additionally, the rye bread was wonderful, and I would love to have it as a staple in my own house.

However, there was one issue with my experience - the salad came out at the same time as the sandwich, which was not ideal. The presentation was a bit sloppy, especially when compared to other places I've had a panini (except Panera, where they do it right). Usually, the sandwich is served on a napkin to prevent the bread from getting soggy due to the steam. I felt that for the price, which is a little high, this lack of attention to detail was a letdown. That being said, the quality of the food and drinks justifies the price in my opinion.

On the bright side, Jackson's offers a great selection of wines and beers that are likely to satisfy any palate.

The wait staff has always been friendly, although it's clear that this is a place where they are expected to hustle. Sometimes, the service can be a bit short or even distracted, which can be a letdown. During one of my visits, which was during a moderately busy lunch rush, it took about 15 minutes to get our drinks. However, on my most recent visit, on a Saturday night, it only took about 8 minutes. While this isn't terrible, it's not particularly great either. Nevertheless, the bartenders were awesome and never left me wanting (except for when they forgot to bring my salad with the main course).

Overall, I had a good experience at Jackson's and will definitely be back.

input:
I went there for a pedicure and gel manicure.  It was my first time and the reviews was what enticed me. I loved loved Young, who did my pedicure.  She was very friendly and has a very positive attitude.  She took her time with my pedicure and was very thorough with the massaging (which was the best part). 

Unfortunately Young didn't do my manicure.   I had a gel manicure that needed to be soaked off.  The owner did my nails.  She first scraped my nails with the cuticle pusher, but when it wasn't coming off fast enough, she used the drill.  I was really worried as I didn't want my nails to be thin.  But I just let her do her thing.  I'm usually not picky so when she was working on my nails I didn't watch what she was doing until I realized after close examination she didn't fully take the old gel polish off.  
Not only that, the polish didn't go on smoothly, there's are noticeable bumps on my nail bed and the sides of my nails weren't even fully covered.  

I am so disappointed.  I love Young, but I don't know if I'll be going back due to my experience with my gel manicure.
Revise this with your best effort:
I decided to visit this place for a pedicure and gel manicure based on the enticing reviews. It was my first time, and I must say, Young, who performed my pedicure, was absolutely amazing. She displayed a friendly demeanor and radiated a positive attitude throughout. Young took her time with the pedicure, ensuring every aspect was meticulously attended to, especially the fantastic massaging session which I found incredibly enjoyable.

Regrettably, Young didn't handle my manicure. Instead, the owner of the establishment took charge. She began by scraping my nails with a cuticle pusher, but when the process didn't yield satisfactory results quickly enough, she resorted to using a drill. This made me rather apprehensive as I certainly didn't want my nails to become thin and fragile. However, I decided to trust her expertise and allowed her to continue without interfering. Since I generally don't fuss over trivial matters, I didn't pay much attention to her technique until I examined my nails closely and realized that she had failed to completely remove the old gel polish.

To add to my disappointment, the application process of the new polish was far from satisfactory. Not only were there noticeable bumps on my nail bed, but the sides of my nails weren't even fully covered, leaving a rather uneven and unsightly appearance.

Naturally, I am incredibly let down by this experience. While I thoroughly appreciated Young's services, I am uncertain whether I will return to this establishment solely due to my disappointing encounter with the gel manicure.

input:
This is a cool place.  I wonder how many people know that an Ouzaria is?  The ambience here is definitely upbeat - I'd rate it a great place for a group or first date.  They have a couple of semi-secluded tables in the back room that keeps it from getting too loud, but it's not a quiet romantic place.  

We brought my Mother-in-Law, who enjoys good food as long as it's not too weird.  I guess my wife is about the same, now that I think about it.  We tried three tapas plates; a three-cheese sampler, featuring feta, goat cheese and kasseri cheese, greek meatballs and pan-seared scallops.  We liked all three of these dishes.  The scallops were especially good - big and tender.   For tapas, they were pretty big portions, so keep this in mind.  The waitress suggested ordering one thing at a time, but we didn't heed her advice and ordered it all up front.   Two at a time would probably be a good idea.  Along with the tapas, we ordered a traditional Greek salad, which ended up being the lone clunker, surprisingly.  We just didn't like the dressing - too sweet for our tastes.  The gyro meat was fine, though, so maybe we'll just get a gyro next time.   One more thing:  The Spanish granacha (can't remember the label) was excellent for just $6 and a nice pour. 

Okay, now for the belly dancer:  She was cute and a good dancer, but I think this is just something that requires more alcohol on my part.  We did have a few laughs about it, though.  I opted not to get a dollar out to stuff in her skirt or whatever.   Fun but a little awkward. 

I've been to a few other Greek places in town that had better food, but for a night out, Momo's is definitely the choice.  We'll be back.
Revise this with your best effort:
This place is absolutely fantastic. I'm curious how many people are aware of the wonders of an Ouzaria. The atmosphere here is undeniably lively - I would highly recommend it for group gatherings or even a first date. They have a few secluded tables in the back room that prevent the noise from becoming overwhelming, but it's not exactly an intimate and quiet spot for romance.

We decided to bring along my Mother-in-Law, who appreciates good food as long as it's not too unconventional. Come to think of it, my wife shares the same sentiment. We had the pleasure of trying three delectable tapas plates: a three-cheese sampler featuring feta, goat cheese, and kasseri cheese, Greek meatballs, and pan-seared scallops. All three dishes were delightful, but the scallops were an absolute standout - they were impressively large and tender. The tapas portions were quite generous, so bear that in mind. The waitress recommended ordering one dish at a time, but we foolishly ignored her advice and placed the entire order upfront. It would have been wiser to order two at a time. In addition to the tapas, we ordered a traditional Greek salad, which unfortunately fell short of expectations. Surprisingly, we didn't enjoy the dressing, finding it overly sweet for our liking. However, the gyro meat was satisfactory, so perhaps we'll opt for a gyro on our next visit. Oh, and one more thing: the Spanish granacha (I can't recall the label) was simply fabulous, and the fact that it was only $6 and poured generously made it even better.

Now, let's discuss the belly dancer: she was charming and undoubtedly a skilled dancer. Nonetheless, I believe this is an experience that would benefit from a little more alcohol on my part. We did share a few laughs about it, though. I chose not to fish out a dollar to place in her skirt or wherever it is typically done. It was fun but slightly awkward.

I have frequented a few other Greek eateries in town that offered superior cuisine, but for a night out, Momo's is undoubtedly the ultimate choice. We will most certainly be returning.
