input:
This hotel was so terrible and I can narrow it down to 4 things:

1. The price: Expect to pay a lot of money from the second you arrive. They charge $35 per person for a round trip shuttle ride to the airport. Our room was roughly $275 a night. It's an incredibly large hotel that offers a nail salon, a Godiva Chocolate store, about 9 restaurants and a few bars. But you'll pay dearly for any of those things - like $2.50 for a small bottle of soda. The hotel is designed to keep you in there and they charge you $15 for a round trip shuttle ride to the downtown Nashville area. 

2. The service: We called the front desk and were on hold for 20 minutes. We went to the front desk and waited in line for an hour. We waited around to ask the concierge questions. And each time we got, "I don't know" as the usual response. The cleaning staff was extraordinarily loud and they actually shouted as they went down the hall at 6:30 a.m.

3. The name: They call this place a resort but that is, by far, a misnomer. This place is a convention hotel, period. It's horrifically loud at all hours of the day because they host about 3 conventions at one time. Our windows faced one of the courtyards and there is music pumping there 24 hours a day. The walls are thin and you can hear *everything* happening in the neighboring rooms. (eww!) If you want to relax at a resort, don't stay here because with all those convention people, loud cleaning staff, 24 hour music and thin walls you will only end up with more stress.

4. The size: It's no joke that you will get lost in this hotel. It's inexplicably large. And when it hits noon, you should already be in one of the few restaurants because they fill up FAST. With several conventions happening at one time, getting a "quick bite" is not possible here. And there's not really any place close by, either. You can walk over to the mall for some fast food but plan enough time for your walk - getting out of the hotel takes at least 5 minutes.

I'm sure glad I was there for a convention and didn't pay out of my own pocket for this ridiculous hotel.
Revise this with your best effort:
This hotel was an absolute disaster and I can pinpoint four key reasons why it was so terrible.

1. The exorbitant price: From the moment we arrived, we were hit with outrageous costs. They charged a ridiculous $35 per person for a round trip shuttle ride to the airport. On top of that, our room cost a staggering $275 per night. Sure, the hotel boasts an array of amenities including a nail salon, a Godiva Chocolate store, nine restaurants, and a few bars. However, be prepared to empty your wallet for even the simplest things, like a small bottle of soda priced at an exorbitant $2.50. They clearly designed this hotel to keep guests within its premises, as evidenced by the $15 charge for a round trip shuttle ride to downtown Nashville.

2. Abysmal service: We experienced endless frustrations with the hotel's service. After waiting on hold for an excruciating 20 minutes, we decided to approach the front desk in person, only to endure an hour-long wait in line. Each time we sought assistance from the concierge, we were met with unhelpful responses of "I don't know." To make matters worse, the cleaning staff would bellow loudly while going about their duties, making it impossible to enjoy a peaceful stay.

3. Misleading classification: The hotel proudly labels itself as a resort, but that couldn't be further from the truth. In reality, it is nothing more than a convention hotel. The incessant noise from the three simultaneous conventions held within its walls was unbearable, with music blaring 24/7 in the courtyards. Thin walls amplified every sound from neighboring rooms, granting us the discomforting privilege of hearing every intimate detail. If you seek relaxation at a true resort, avoid this place at all costs. The constant presence of convention-goers, loud cleaning staff, non-stop music, and paper-thin walls will only add to your stress.

4. Enormous size: Prepare to get lost in this labyrinthine hotel. Its inexplicable size is mind-boggling. By noon, you must already be seated in one of the scarce restaurants since they become overcrowded in an instant. With multiple conventions concurrently taking place, obtaining a quick meal is an unattainable feat here. To add insult to injury, there are virtually no nearby dining options either. You might consider walking to the mall for some fast food, but be prepared to allocate at least five minutes to navigate your way out of the hotel.

I am incredibly grateful that I attended a convention and did not have to foot the bill for this utterly ludicrous hotel experience.

input:
I waited a long time to finally try this place and I have to say I was let down a bit. I tried the mandatory Dan Dan noodles. They were very flavorful and not too spicy. Nothing mind blowing here just a really good lo mein or spicy pasta dish with virtually no protein more or less. Also had the scallion pancakes. I was just in Chinatown recently at a place I also reviewed (first person from Yelp to do so) and they were way better there. ( I highly recommend you try that place) These were more like quesadillas laying flat where as the other ones jumped off the plate and were so much more crispy and substantial. The last appetizer I had was the Wontons in Chilli oil. These were just not good to me at all and one bite was all I needed. Basically it is steamed Wontons in a bowl with the soup being the chilli oil. Just heavy heavy choking heat with very little substance or taste. Take those same homemade wontons and pan fry them with some chilli peppers and a nice light sauce and you have could a real winner but I digress. Finally we tried the Talapia Medallions . These were fried to perfection but there were some greens mixed in that I could not chew through and had to discard via the old napkin trick which to me is a bit of a deal/star breaker.

The service was very good and the atmosphere very nice but I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here again. All I could think about was how much more I prefer Cantonese style where its all about flavors and you can add heat as you like it. I'm sure I could find better authentic Szechuan cuisine that better suits my taste just not here. It feels very commercialized and Americanized. I prefer the hole in the wall places where I am the only caucasian in the place a heck of a lot more.
Revise this with your best effort:
After patiently waiting for quite some time, I finally decided to give this place a try, but I have to admit, it fell a bit short of my expectations. I couldn't resist ordering the obligatory Dan Dan noodles, which were undeniably packed with flavor but lacked the spicy kick I was hoping for. While they were good, they didn't exactly leave a lasting impression. They reminded me more of a decent lo mein or mildly spicy pasta dish, with minimal protein. 

I also opted for the scallion pancakes, having recently tried them at another Chinatown establishment (which I highly recommend exploring). Unfortunately, this rendition paled in comparison. The ones I had before were crispy, bursting with savory goodness, and simply irresistible. In contrast, the scallion pancakes here resembled flattened quesadillas, lacking the same level of crunch and substance.

Moving on to the Wontons in Chili oil, I can't say they were particularly enjoyable. With just one bite, I knew they weren't for me. The steamed Wontons immersed in a soup-like chili oil lacked flavor and substance. The overwhelming heat made it feel like a heavy, choking experience rather than a satisfying dish. Personally, I believe that pan-frying those homemade wontons with chili peppers and a light sauce would have turned them into a true winner. But, that's just my opinion.

Finally, we ventured into the territory of the Talapia Medallions. They were fried to perfection, but unfortunately, there were some greens mixed in that were incredibly difficult to chew. I had to resort to the old napkin trick of discreetly getting rid of them. It was a bit of a letdown and somewhat affected my overall experience.

On a positive note, I must commend the impeccable service and pleasant atmosphere of the restaurant. However, I wouldn't go out of my way to dine here again. Throughout my meal, all I could think about was how much more I preferred traditional Cantonese cuisine, where the emphasis is on bold flavors and the ability to customize spice levels to one's liking. I am confident that I can find a more authentic Szechuan dining experience that aligns better with my taste elsewhere. This place strikes me as being overly commercialized and catering to a more Americanized palate. Personally, I find the charm and authenticity of "hole in the wall" establishments, where I am typically the only Caucasian customer, much more appealing.

input: "Feather free" in my profile.  "Feather free" in my reservation.  "Feather free" by special request when I called four hours before arrival.  "Feather free" confirmed upon check in.  In the room?  Feathers.  Will Hyatt ever understand how important this is?  Will it take another trip to the emergency room?   And $29/night to park also absurd for St. Louis.  "Sorry about that sir" gets old.
Revise this with your best effort: I clearly and explicitly requested my profile to be "feather free." I reiterated this preference in my reservation and even made a special request over the phone four hours before my arrival. Upon checking in, I was assured that my room would indeed be "feather free." However, to my disappointment, feathers were still present in the room. It is frustrating that Hyatt fails to comprehend the significance of this issue. Will it take another unfortunate trip to the emergency room for them to finally understand? Furthermore, the exorbitant $29 per night parking fee in St. Louis is absolutely absurd. The repeated apologies of "sorry about that, sir" are starting to lose their effectiveness.

input:
A couple months ago we made the mistake of getting there on a weekend around 10am or so and there was over an hour wait. I was too hungry to wait that long and told the bf we HAD to go back but earlier.

Tried again and success!!  Got there right when they opened and there was already people starting to file in.  Managed to get seated and served very quickly.  We both ordered the pancakes.  I had the butter pecan and O.M.G...  His bananas foster pancakes were good too but those butter pecan ones are the best (in my opinion).   The pancakes also come with 2 eggs and a meat.  Big fan of them offering turkey sausage and turkey bacon.   

Go.  It's awesome.  Just get there early and wear loose pants.
Revise this with your best effort:
A few months back, we made the mistake of arriving at the restaurant on a weekend at around 10am, only to find that there was an overwhelming hour-long wait. We were both too famished to endure such a long wait, so I insisted that we come back earlier next time.

We decided to give it another shot and fortunately, we timed it perfectly. Arriving right when they opened, we noticed a few people already making their way inside. We were swiftly seated and served without any delay. We both settled on ordering their famous pancakes. I opted for the butter pecan flavor and oh my goodness, they were heavenly. My boyfriend's choice of the bananas foster pancakes was equally delicious, but in my humble opinion, nothing topped the butter pecan ones. As an added bonus, each pancake plate was accompanied by 2 eggs and a choice of meat. I appreciate that they offered turkey sausage and turkey bacon, as I prefer those options.

I highly recommend visiting this restaurant. It truly is an amazing experience. Just remember to arrive early and wear comfortable, loose-fitting pants.

input:
Food was average at best. As experts on fried green tomatoes, my family was disappointed.  Meatloaf was good and sides average.

Entertainment was disappointing too because they only played a couple songs per hour.
Revise this with your best effort:
The food, unfortunately, was only average at best and left my family, the self-proclaimed fried green tomato experts, feeling disappointed. While the meatloaf was enjoyable, the sides were just average in taste.

Furthermore, our experience with the entertainment was also a letdown, as they only played a minimal number of songs per hour.

input: The service by our server Tina was great..attentive and fast service. The wait was not long at all give it was a Sunday around 10am. 15 wait tops. Now to the food..MUST try the huevos bruncheros!!! Best breakfast item I've had in a long time. I mean I can't really describe just have to try it!
Revise this with your best effort: The service provided by our server Tina was exceptional - attentive and prompt. Despite it being a Sunday morning around 10am, the wait time was minimal, a maximum of 15 minutes. Moving on to the food, I cannot emphasize enough how much I recommend trying the huevos bruncheros. It truly is the best breakfast item I have enjoyed in quite some time. It's difficult to put into words, you simply have to experience it for yourself.

input: When I returned to pick up my new glasses, I realized that they are horribly out of focus. Apparently they don't measure out the position of the pupils in respect to lenses in order to position the center of focus there. The staff member tried to talk me into repositioning the glasses however for me to see, they would have to be floating on my face and you can only look at he bottom most part. Umm no! Then she stated that she did measure but I don't remember such action being taken.  I asked for the lenses to be redone and they promised to send them off as urgent. Well, still no glasses.
Revise this with your best effort: When I returned to pick up my new glasses, I was immediately dissatisfied with them as they were terribly out of focus. It appeared that the opticians failed to properly measure the position of my pupils in relation to the lenses, resulting in an incorrect center of focus. The staff member attempted to convince me to adjust the glasses, but in order for me to see properly, they would have to be positioned in a way that gives the illusion of floating on my face, limiting my field of vision to just the bottommost part. Obviously, this was not a feasible solution for me. Additionally, when I expressed my concerns, the staff member insisted that they had measured correctly, although I have no recollection of such an action being taken. Frustrated, I requested that the lenses be redone, and they assured me that they would expedite the process. However, despite their promises, I am still left without my glasses.

input:
This place is just the greatest.

First, the correct current address is 33 S. 43rd Street, between Chestnut and Walnut. Don't go to the old address like I did!

This place is basically a hole in the wall but they have EVERYTHING, and at great prices. Every time I have called for something they have it. I bought an external hard drive dock that has input for laptop AND desktop, both SATA *AND* IDE, for sixty dollars. It works like a charm.

Today I'm going in for an external CD burner with lightscribe capability, for $40!

Please don't get impatient if there is a language barrier. There seems to be an older Asian man, and a younger one, and the older man may have some communication issues, but you can tell he is trying and if you are patient with him he will be patient with you!!!!!

I can't recommend this place enough when it comes to your computer item needs.
Revise this with your best effort:
I highly recommend this place as it has proven to be exceptional in meeting all my computer item needs. However, please note that the correct current address is 33 S. 43rd Street, situated between Chestnut and Walnut. Avoid going to the previous address, as I unfortunately did.

Although it may appear to be merely a hole in the wall, this place boasts an extensive selection of products, all offered at competitive prices. Every time I have reached out for a particular item, they have consistently had it in stock. For instance, I recently purchased an external hard drive dock for just sixty dollars, which conveniently accommodates both laptops and desktops, featuring compatibility with both SATA and IDE. I must say, it functions flawlessly.

Today, I am excited to acquire an external CD burner with lightscribe capability for a reasonable price of forty dollars.

On a side note, please exercise patience and understanding if there happens to be a language barrier. There are two individuals present, an older Asian man and a younger one. The older man might encounter some challenges with communication, but it is evident that he is making an effort. By demonstrating patience with him, he reciprocates the same level of patience in return.

In conclusion, trust me when I say that this place is truly the best when it comes to fulfilling your computer-related needs.

input: I like the Clue game lookalike of this hotel. Respectful bell boys and valet drivers, bartenders delivering our drinks to our rooms quickly, phone etiquette with nice customer service, and my gf and I would come back to this hotel next year, great area, a little busy streets in downtown Boise. Coming from Cali, this service is phenomenal. Thank you guys. Watch your money spending here. Mine as well walk around and get cheaper foods to eat. The con's is no air vent in bathrooms especially of ours.
Revise this with your best effort: I thoroughly enjoyed the hotel, which gives off a charming Clue game vibe. The bell boys and valet drivers were incredibly respectful, and the bartenders promptly delivered our drinks to our rooms. We were impressed with the phone etiquette and the pleasant customer service provided. My girlfriend and I are already planning to return to this hotel next year, as the location is fantastic, despite the slightly busy streets in downtown Boise. As someone from California, I must say that the service here is truly exceptional. Thank you to the staff for their efforts. While enjoying the amenities, it is important to be mindful of your spending. Consider exploring the area and finding more affordable dining options. One downside, however, is the absence of air vents in the bathrooms, especially in ours.

input:
This review is based on the location in Atlantic city.

Got the strawberry flavor and O.M.G!!! I was not expecting it to be that good. It is not as sweet as others but it's perfect. It had little bits of strawberry in it. The price is really good also $2 for a small I believe. My only regret is not trying all the other flavors. Next time I'm in Philly/AC I will def be getting this!
Revise this with your best effort: Based on my experience at the Atlantic City location, I must say that I am absolutely blown away by the strawberry flavor I tried. Oh my goodness, it exceeded all my expectations. Unlike other options, it wasn't overly sweet but rather had a perfect balance. Moreover, it even had delightful bits of fresh strawberry in it, adding to the overall experience. The price, I should mention, is quite reasonable, as I believe a small size is just $2. However, my only regret is not exploring and trying all the other flavors available. Rest assured, the next time I find myself in Philadelphia or Atlantic City, I will definitely make it a point to indulge in this delightful treat again.

input: I went there for lunch yesterday. It was really good! The staff was very friendly and the portions are almost enough for two people to eat. The recipes are from Mrs. Doll and one of her son's is carrying on the legacy.
Revise this with your best effort: Yesterday, I decided to pay a visit to this delightful eatery for lunch. The experience was truly remarkable, as everything about it exceeded my expectations. From the first interaction with the staff, it was evident that their warmth and friendliness were genuine. As I eagerly awaited my food, I couldn't help but notice that the portion sizes were incredibly generous, practically suitable for sharing between two people. It was truly a testament to the culinary prowess of Mrs. Doll, whose recipes have become the heart and soul of this establishment. Furthermore, it brings me joy to see her son continuing her legacy, ensuring that her culinary brilliance lives on.

input:
I have only ever gotten take-out at the Bridgeport Rib House, so I can only comment on that.  After numerous visits, the short story is that the food is pretty good, the prices are fair, and picking up one's order in the bar is poor.

Barbecue on par with this can be had elsewhere in the area, without the weak service experience.
Revise this with your best effort: Based on my personal experience of solely ordering take-out from the Bridgeport Rib House, I can confidently state that their food is consistently satisfying and reasonably priced. However, I must emphasize that the service for pick-up orders at their bar leaves much to be desired. While their barbecue is undeniably delicious, there are alternative options in the vicinity that offer equally delectable meals without the disappointing service encountered at this establishment.

input: Please, this place makes a semi-new menu and raised their prices. The food is very mediocre. i just started cooking and i make a couple pasta dishes which include spaghetti and lemon chicken piccatta.  As a beginner in cooking I can judge this place's food is horrible. A day after the food looked like it had been out for weeks. Good food can last for a day or two.When i went in there to eat the hostess was nice. first, we ordered a glass a wine. he poured the wine, missed the glass and some spilled on the table and he just ignored it. hello. idiot. waitressing 101. go back. well needless to say. not worth your money at all. ive been there during happy hour with girlfriends and its fine. not a 'high end' restaurant by any means even though they try to make it that way.
Revise this with your best effort:
This place recently introduced a somewhat new menu and decided to increase their prices. Unfortunately, the food they offer is quite mediocre. As someone who has just started exploring the world of cooking, I can confidently say that their dishes, such as spaghetti and lemon chicken piccatta, are of subpar quality. It's astonishing how the food looked like it had been left out for weeks, just a day after it was served. It's common knowledge that good food can last for at least a day or two.

During my visit, the hostess was pleasant, but things quickly went downhill from there. We began by ordering a glass of wine, yet the server clumsily poured it, missing the glass and causing some to spill onto the table. What's worse is that he completely disregarded it, displaying a lack of basic waitering etiquette. It's disappointing to see such incompetence.

In all honesty, this place is simply not worth the money. While I have previously visited during happy hour with my friends and found it tolerable, it is by no means a "high-end" restaurant, despite their attempts to portray it as such.

input: I had acquired a watch when my Grandfather passed and dropped in to get the battery replaced. They noticed one of the pins was missing and went ahead and fixed it on site for free. The wait was a bit for a battery change, but I can't complain because they were extremely nice and didn't charge me for the battery all while fixing the pin. I would definitely look there if I was in the market for some bling.
Revise this with your best effort: I found myself in possession of a watch when my beloved Grandfather passed away, and recently decided to bring it in for a battery replacement. To my surprise, upon inspection, the attentive staff at the watch store discovered that one of the pins was missing. Without hesitation, they kindly offered to fix it on the spot without any additional charge. Although the wait time for the battery replacement was a bit lengthy, I couldn't help but appreciate their exceptional customer service and generosity in not charging me for the battery, especially considering the extra repair they performed. If I ever find myself in need of some quality jewelry, I would unquestionably consider returning to that store.

input: Everything great about a jewish deli, southern comfort joint and a bit of mexican dive restaurant all mixed together. Brisket is good, but don't expect a tomato based sauce. Latke is not a normal round one, but super delicious. I also took the Jewish Apple Cake to go and despite being a little too brown on the bottom, it was delicious even 3 hours later on my flight back to LA.
Revise this with your best effort: Combining the best of a Jewish deli, southern comfort joint, and a touch of Mexican dive, this establishment encompasses all the reasons to fall in love with it. Although renowned for its delectable brisket, do not anticipate a tomato-based sauce as you indulge. The latke here stands out, deviating from the traditional round shape, yet its extraordinary taste makes up for the unconventional presentation. Before my departure to Los Angeles, I couldn't resist taking a slice of Jewish Apple Cake to go. Despite a slight over-browning on the bottom, this dessert remained absolutely delightful even three hours later during my flight.

input: The food is probably one of the more mediocre Chinese food I've had, but the main appeal of this place is renting a karaoke room for a large group of people and BYOing. The restaurant is exceptionally capable of dealing with huge and rowdy groups, and the food comes out to be a decent price and comes out quickly. The karaoke machines all have pretty up to date songs in a variety of languages.
Revise this with your best effort: The cuisine here falls short of my expectations for Chinese food, ranking it among the more mediocre options I've tried. However, the true allure lies in reserving a karaoke room for a sizeable group and bringing your own beverages. Remarkably, this establishment excels in accommodating large and lively gatherings, with prompt service and reasonably priced dishes. Furthermore, the karaoke machines feature an impressive collection of modern songs in multiple languages.

input:
This update (and upgrade) to my review of Khyber is long overdue!

I think the most ringing summary is that I have since moved ~1 mile further away from the Khyber, and I still go there just as often.  I have now sampled most of the menu, but the truly excellent Southern barbecue is what usually calls to me.  You can't go wrong whether you pick the brisket, the ribs, the chicken, the pulled pork or a combo of the above.  Their mac and cheese remains my favorite side, and the addition of the very good coleslaw rounds out the experience.

I love the vibe of Kyber.  It usually pretty full, but they usually seem to have a table available for me (Yay!).  It is often loud, but never quite so loud that I wish it were quieter.  The staff is very knowledgeable, and happy to provide beer recommendations and taste tests of drafts.  They Khyber also manages to hit that sweet spot where I never end up being the most or least intoxicated person there!
Revise this with your best effort:
This overdue update and upgrade to my review of Khyber is long overdue! 

In summary, despite moving approximately a mile further away from Khyber, I still make frequent visits to this fantastic establishment. Having sampled most of their menu by now, it is the Southern barbecue that continually draws me in with its exceptional flavors. Whether it be the delicious brisket, mouthwatering ribs, savory chicken, succulent pulled pork, or a delightful combination of these options, you simply can't go wrong. And let's not forget their mac and cheese, which remains my all-time favorite side dish. The addition of their remarkably tasty coleslaw perfectly complements the whole experience.

The atmosphere at Khyber is absolutely captivating. While the place is usually bustling with people, I have never had trouble finding a table (hooray!). Though the noise level can be energetic, it never reaches a point where I long for a quieter setting. The staff working here is incredibly knowledgeable and always willing to offer beer recommendations and even provide taste tests of their draft options. Additionally, Khyber manages to strike a perfect balance where I never find myself being the most or least intoxicated person in the establishment.

input: Great  breads especially the German rye. My favorite breakfast is the poached eggs, cooked perfectly. For lunch, I go for the eggplant panini or  Laurie's salad.
Revise this with your best effort: One of the highlights is unquestionably the assortment of splendid breads available, with special mention to the exquisite German rye. When it comes to breakfast, my personal preference lies in indulging in flawlessly cooked poached eggs. As for lunch, I often find myself torn between the delectable eggplant panini and the delightful Laurie's salad.

input: Tony's really has surprisingly good Mexican food, which you wouldn't expect to find out here in Chalmette.  It's actually the best Mexican food I've had in Louisiana.  Everything I've tried there is good.  My favorite so far is the chiles rellenos, which are large and excellent.  They also have Mexican Coca-Cola, which is sweetened with actual sugar, rather than the high-fructose corn syrup in the American version.
Revise this with your best effort: Tony's is a hidden gem in Chalmette, dishing out unexpectedly outstanding Mexican cuisine. It's hard to believe, but it truly offers the best Mexican food I have tasted in all of Louisiana. Every dish I have savored there has been top-notch. Among them, the chiles rellenos stand out as my personal favorite. These generously sized delicacies never fail to impress with their exceptional flavors. What sets Tony's apart even more is their inclusion of genuine Mexican Coca-Cola, sweetened with real sugar instead of the ubiquitous high-fructose corn syrup found in its American counterpart.

input: Awful business model it took forever to even figure out where to order. on top of that the workers actually are not professional at all. on top of THAT my other half sandwhich didn't even have sausage covering even half of the bread. easily worst place i've been in a while
Revise this with your best effort: The business model of this establishment is truly disappointing, as it took an excessive amount of time to even locate the ordering area. Moreover, the staff displayed a complete lack of professionalism. To add to my dissatisfaction, my sandwich lacked adequate sausage coverage, with less than half of the bread being filled. Without a doubt, this has been one of the worst experiences I have had in recent times.

input: The staff are friendly and attentive.  They offer a wide variety of quality dancewear products at a decent price, but don't have many options for any one kind of product, at least not for men's dancewear.  The location's convenient if you live in the city, and I always stop by here first if I need something new, but three out of four times I don't find what I'm looking for.
Revise this with your best effort: The staff at this establishment exude friendliness and attentiveness, making for a pleasant shopping experience. Furthermore, they boast a diverse assortment of high-caliber dancewear products at reasonably affordable rates. However, when it comes to men's dancewear, the selection seems to fall a bit short in terms of variety. Nevertheless, the store's central location renders it convenient for city dwellers, prompting me to consistently make it my initial stop whenever I require fresh dancewear. Regrettably, although I frequently patronize this store, four out of five times my search ends without success in finding the desired item.

input: I went here off of a referral. It was great I was done in five hours. I had individuals done, medium size and they cost 150 the hair included. There were three women that are on your head at one time. I will go there again! There very nice as well.
Revise this with your best effort: I visited this place based on a referral, and it exceeded my expectations. I was swiftly attended to and finished within five hours. I got individual medium-sized hair extensions, which cost $150 including the hair. The service involved three talented women working on my hair simultaneously. I was genuinely impressed with their professionalism and kindness. I will definitely return there in the future!

input: Love the lamb gyros plate. It's a distance for me to drive, so sometimes I get an extra order to take back home.  The tiramisu is very good too. The dolmas are good but more vinegary than I prefer.  The Greek salad that comes with the entree' is good also.
Revise this with your best effort: I absolutely adore the lamb gyros plate! Despite being a bit of a drive for me, the deliciousness of it always makes it worth the trip. On occasions when I indulge, I even grab an extra order to bring home and savor later. Additionally, their tiramisu is simply divine, offering a delightful ending to the meal. While the dolmas are quite tasty, I must admit they are slightly more vinegary than my personal preference. However, the Greek salad that accompanies the entree is a definite highlight, bursting with flavors that perfectly complement the main dish.

input: Love the yum yum club and macaroni salad is awesome too!! Sometimes service could be a little more friendly but besides that I continue to go back because price is right and good tastes great
Revise this with your best effort: I thoroughly enjoy the yum yum club, and their macaroni salad is absolutely awesome! Occasionally, the service could benefit from being a bit more friendly. However, disregarding that aspect, I consistently return to this establishment due to its affordable prices and exceptional taste.

input:
This is my husbands and my first time here in Reno. Wow what a great hotel to stay in for your first time. We had a great room with a spa and the shower had a steam room feature. The hotel also offered many places to eat and relax. The casino was very clean and a joy to be in even if you don't gamble like myself. However I did win 41.00 with a 1.00 slot machine :)  we decided to venture out finally to see Reno. However, we weren't impressed with anything else but our great hotel.  Easy checkout right from the room was a time saver. Well now off to explore Reno some more.
If your considering a hotel that is nice, clean, up to date this is the one.
Revise this with your best effort: This is our first time visiting Reno, and I must say, we couldn't have chosen a better hotel to stay in. Our room was incredible, equipped with a spa and a shower that even had a steam room feature. The hotel also provided numerous dining options and areas to unwind. Even for someone like me who doesn't gamble, the casino was exceptionally clean and an enjoyable place to be in. Surprisingly, I even managed to win $41.00 with a $1.00 slot machine! However, when we ventured out to explore Reno, we were somewhat underwhelmed by everything else in comparison to our fantastic hotel. Thankfully, the easy checkout right from our room saved us valuable time. Now, we're excited to embark on further adventures in Reno. If you are looking for a hotel that is nice, clean, and up to date, this is definitely the one to consider.

input: Studying previous  yelp reviews, we decided to take the kids to hibachi and sushi.  This place did not disappoint. The sushi was amazing and the hibachi was awesome. The dessert of fried bananas and ice cream ended a great experience. The service was great and attentive.  Will definitely return for more!
Revise this with your best effort: After carefully examining past Yelp reviews, we made the delightful choice to bring our children to a hibachi and sushi establishment. And boy, were we in for a treat! The sushi surpassed our expectations, leaving us utterly impressed, while the hibachi experience was absolutely mesmerizing. To top it all off, the dessert consisting of luscious fried bananas paired with creamy ice cream brought our extraordinary dining experience to a perfect close. The attentive and exceptional service we received further enhanced our visit, ensuring that we will unquestionably come back for more delightful moments in the future!

input: I Love it here. The pizza is fantastic,  and the staff is very friendly. It's a great place to hang out with friends and family.
Revise this with your best effort: I absolutely adore this place! The pizza here is absolutely fantastic, exceeding all expectations. The staff is extremely friendly, providing exceptional customer service that enhances the overall experience. It's an ideal spot to spend quality time with friends and family, creating cherished memories together.

input: Went here the other day with some friends for a bite and a drink. Service was great as where the drinks ;) Will definitely be back!
Revise this with your best effort: I recently visited this place with a group of friends to enjoy some food and drinks. The service was exceptional, and we were impressed with the quality of the drinks. Without a doubt, we will be returning in the future!

input: This place was on my list for all of the great reviews. The lamb was very flavorful, but the garlic Naan is just frozen from Trader Joe's. Also, the lamb was fairly expensive for the amount you get. Lastly, despite saying they take American Express at the door, the owner would not accept Amex. I will likely not return.
Revise this with your best effort: I chose to visit this place based on its outstanding reviews, but unfortunately, my experience left me underwhelmed. The lamb dish was undeniably flavorful, although it was accompanied by a disappointment - the garlic Naan appeared to be nothing more than frozen bread bought from Trader Joe's. Moreover, the price of the lamb dish seemed rather steep for the portion size offered. Adding to the frustration, despite the assurance at the entrance that American Express was accepted, the owner refused to process my Amex card. Regretfully, I must conclude that this experience falls short of my expectations, and as a result, I am unlikely to dine here again.

input:
This little unassuming shop is tucked away in a strip mall full of furniture stores. Had it not been for Yelp, I would never have known it was here. Now, I won't be taking a trip to Brentwood without stopping for a scoop!

The flavors are quite varied and innovative. I had pumpkin and some sort of whipped cream cheese flavor--both were divine--which when mixed tasted just like pumpkin pie! The owner, Michael, is absolutely a sweetheart and is generous with the samples and the recommendations, and he's always coming up with new flavors to whip up. I can't wait to see what he concocts next!
Revise this with your best effort:
Nestled inconspicuously among a plethora of furniture stores in a strip mall, lies this unassuming little gem. Without the guidance of Yelp, its existence would have remained concealed from my senses. However, now I am forever indebted as I vow to never embark on a Brentwood excursion without indulging in a delectable scoop from this divine establishment!

An enchanting array of flavors awaits the eager taste buds, showcasing an inspiring level of innovation. Among my indulgences were the heavenly pumpkin and a tantalizing whipped cream cheese concoction. When combined, these remarkable flavors harmoniously transformed into a delightful symphony reminiscent of the beloved pumpkin pie! The owner, Michael, personifies the notion of kindness and consistently goes above and beyond by showering patrons with generous samples and invaluable recommendations. Furthermore, his creative genius continuously unveils new and exciting flavors that leave me eagerly anticipating my next visit.

input: Great food and good coffee. Wish they had more of an espresso bar with coffee options, but food and baked goods are spectacular!
Revise this with your best effort: I have to say, the food here is absolutely amazing and the coffee is good as well. My only wish is that they offered a wider range of coffee options, especially with an espresso bar. However, I must admit, the delectable food and freshly baked goods they offer are truly spectacular!

input:
holly grove is the best. I'm consistently impressed with their selection of produce. you can basically get everything (plus more stuff they don't have at the normal grocery store) except it's all local. we are so lucky to live in a place with a year round growing season, and we should really take advantage of that! (I will get off my high horse now lol). 

they also have locally raised meats, bread from local bakeries...it's just a great place to support local growers and makers. also there are always people wandering outside tending to the garden. it's a nice atmosphere. the only thing I dislike is the location - because I'm allll the way across town. that's not their fault, though.
Revise this with your best effort:
Holly Grove undoubtedly stands out as the finest choice. I am consistently astounded by their remarkable array of fresh produce. Not only can you find virtually everything you need, but they also offer an impressive selection of items that you won't find at your typical grocery store. What truly sets them apart is their commitment to sourcing locally. Living in an area blessed with a year-round growing season is a true stroke of fortune, and we should seize the opportunity it presents. Excuse me as I step down from my soapbox now, haha.

Moreover, their dedication to supporting local growers and artisans extends beyond produce. They proudly offer locally raised meats and bread from nearby bakeries. The entire establishment exudes a lovely ambiance with people diligently tending to the garden outside. It truly is a delightful experience that embraces local sustenance and craftsmanship.

If I must pinpoint a drawback, it would be the inconvenient location, as it is situated all the way across town. However, I understand that this is beyond their control and does not diminish the exceptional nature of Holly Grove.

input:
We tried this place for the first time last night. Being a Saturday night during March Madness the service was a bit slow. The complimentary chips took longer to get to the table than my husband's salad did. Thankfully they had one of the nearby televisions playing a kid's movie to keep my 3 year old happy. Back to the chips, they are home made and were fantastic. I went the safe route and ordered a burger with seasoned fries. It was wonderful. My husband ordered the blackened chicken and while it was good it was a little over seasoned making it a tad too spicy. My daughter had the kid's macaroni and cheese. It looked wonderful but she couldn't stop eating the chips, LoL. The seating inside was a bit weird. There is a table about 2ft from the door to the women's bathroom. Maybe I'm weird for thinking it's weird but I ended up waiting until I got home to go. They offer a 15% military discount which was great. 

Overall I'd definitely recommend this place. I would have given it 5 stars if the service had been a little better.
Revise this with your best effort: Last night, we decided to try this place for the first time. It happened to be a Saturday night during March Madness, so the service was a bit on the slow side. Surprisingly, the complimentary chips took longer to arrive at our table than my husband's salad did. However, to our relief, one of the nearby televisions was playing a kid's movie, which kept our 3-year-old entertained. Now, let's talk about those chips. They were homemade, and I must say, they were absolutely fantastic. As for our main courses, I played it safe and ordered a burger with seasoned fries, which turned out to be a delightful combination. On the other hand, my husband went for the blackened chicken. Although it was good, it was slightly over-seasoned, resulting in an unexpectedly spicy taste. Our daughter opted for the kid's macaroni and cheese, which looked delightful, but she couldn't resist munching on the chips instead, and we couldn't help but laugh. Moving on to the seating arrangement inside, there was one peculiar table positioned within about 2 feet of the women's restroom door. Maybe it's just me, but I found it a bit odd, and as a result, I chose to wait until I got home before using the restroom. On a positive note, they do offer a generous 15% military discount, which we appreciated. Overall, I would definitely recommend this place; however, if the service had been a little better, I would have happily given it a perfect 5-star rating.

input: Decent hotel in downtown Tampa. Stayed in the suite with the fold out couch.  This place has a happy hour with FREE drinks, which we missed, but how cool. The complimentary breakfast was awesome.  Made to order omelets, fresh fruit, cereal, toast, bacon, sausage, home fries, juice and pastries.  Did I mention it was complimentary?   Easiest the best free breakfast I've ever had.  Room was nice and modern with two TV's etc.  Clean and a strong shower.
Revise this with your best effort: We had a comfortable stay at a respectable hotel located in downtown Tampa. Opted for a suite that included a convenient fold-out couch. One highlight was the hotel's happy hour, offering complimentary drinks, although regrettably, we missed out on that opportunity. However, the complimentary breakfast made up for it. It was truly impressive, featuring made-to-order omelets, fresh fruit, cereals, toast, bacon, sausage, home fries, juice, and pastries. And yes, I must emphasize that it was all provided at no extra cost. This was undoubtedly the finest complimentary breakfast I have ever experienced. The room itself was tastefully modern, boasting two TV's and other amenities. The cleanliness of the room was commendable, and the shower provided an invigorating experience.

input: Very nice restaurant in the heart of downtown St. Petersburg with a nice homey feel to it. The burgers full of flavor and the arugula is a fine touch to the chicken and potato gratin meal.  I was not a fan of the cheese used in the potatoes gratin but will definitely be. Ack for the burger. Wine was a little high priced so I didn't get any. The atmosphere is very nice and so was our waitress.
Revise this with your best effort: Located in the heart of downtown St. Petersburg, this impressive restaurant offers a delightful and cozy ambiance. The burgers here are bursting with flavor, complemented by a lovely addition of arugula to the mouthwatering chicken and potato gratin dish. While I personally found the cheese used in the potato gratin not to my liking, I will certainly return for another delectable burger. Unfortunately, I refrained from indulging in the wine selection due to its slightly elevated prices. Nevertheless, the overall atmosphere of the establishment is truly enjoyable, and our waitress provided exceptional service.

input: I have been coming to Cd Roma's for over 10 years. I love this place! The old locations was a bit more home style feeling and cozy and the new spot has a more modern vibe to it. I applaud the change in style with the change in times. Too many places get stuck doing the same thing over and over again. I am glad to see that the food is still delicious. The Chicken Parm, Eggplant Parm, house salad and Alfredo are some of my favorites and they have great pizza. The alfredo sauce is made to order and taste amazing with their breadsticks. Some appetizer items leave something to be desired like the frozen cheesesticks or calimari. I would love to see these replaced with better quality items. Overall, I still love this place and would choose it over Olive Garden any day. I do miss the homey old school vibe from the old location but I also miss the good old days when people talked to each other, fragglerock ruled and hip hop was Wu Tang Clan. Oh well....
Revise this with your best effort:
I have been a loyal customer at Cd Roma's for over a decade and I absolutely adore this place! The previous establishment had a delightful homey atmosphere, creating a cozy environment, whereas the new location embraces a more modern ambiance. I truly appreciate the change in style to adapt to the evolving times, as it demonstrates their willingness to innovate. Unlike many other establishments, Cd Roma's does not stick to a monotonous routine, which I find refreshing.

One aspect that has remained consistent throughout the years is the mouthwatering food. The Chicken Parmesan, Eggplant Parmesan, house salad, and Alfredo dishes are among my personal favorites, not to mention their fantastic pizzas. The made-to-order Alfredo sauce serves as a delectable accompaniment to their heavenly breadsticks. However, I must admit that some appetizer choices, such as the frozen cheese sticks or calamari, do not meet my expectations. It would be wonderful to see these items replaced with higher quality alternatives.

Overall, my admiration for Cd Roma's remains unwavering, and I would choose it over Olive Garden any day. Although I do miss the traditional and homely vibes of the old location, reminiscing about the good old days when people engaged in conversation, Fragglerock enjoyed popularity, and Wu-Tang Clan ruled the hip-hop scene. Alas, times change, but my love for Cd Roma's endures.

input:
The Waffle House has consistent quality wherever you go. I'm not really fond of their business model with their yelling and very small dining area, but I get it. 
I still look forward to going for breakfast.
Revise this with your best effort: The Waffle House prides itself on maintaining the same high-quality standards no matter which location you visit. Although not particularly fond of their business model, which includes yelling and a rather compact dining area, I can understand its appeal. Nonetheless, I still eagerly anticipate my visits there for a delightful breakfast experience.

input:
Henry was a rock star  getting us into a storage locker. He was knowledge, professional, courteous and extremely personable. They were gracious to our four legged girl "Marley" who had to check them out, too.
Great experience in obtaining a storage locker!
We recommend!!!
Revise this with your best effort: Henry, the rockstar, effortlessly led us to a storage locker, showcasing his knowledge and professionalism. His courteous and personable demeanor made the experience even more pleasant. Notably, he even took the time to accommodate our four-legged girl, Marley, who also inspected the premises. Overall, it was a truly remarkable experience securing a storage locker with Henry. We highly recommend his services!

input: Phenomenal restaurant. Great location. Great ambience.  Great food and most of all great drinks. If you go, grab a seat at the  bar. Jared is a true mixologist and has created all of the cocktails on the menu. Don't be afraid to challenge him. As for food, I have never had a bad meal and I have had 100's at this point and pretty much everything on the menu. You won't go wrong with anything on the menu. Listen for the specials...they are always wonderful.
Revise this with your best effort: This restaurant truly deserves the title of "phenomenal." Situated in a fantastic location, it boasts an incredible ambience that sets the perfect backdrop for an unforgettable dining experience. The food here is absolutely outstanding, but perhaps the true standout feature is the delightful variety of exceptional drinks on offer. For a truly memorable experience, I highly recommend taking a seat at the bar where you'll have the pleasure of encountering Jared, an extraordinary mixologist. With his creativity and expertise, he has skillfully curated the entire cocktail menu. Don't hesitate to challenge his mixological prowess – he welcomes the opportunity to create something unique just for you. As for the food, having savored countless meals here, it's safe to say that I've never been disappointed. With a wide array of dishes to choose from, you can rest assured that any selection you make will exceed your expectations. Additionally, be sure to keep an ear out for the specials, as they consistently deliver delightful surprises.

input:
I know people RAVE about this place, but frankly I find it A-OK. 

It is a great location, the food is fresh, and they have a great variety of vegan options. But I find it pretty blah otherwise. I've had the crispy ranch and the curry tofu and enjoyed both of them, but I feel like I expect more out of a specialty vegan place. I did really like chick'n in the crispy ranch. The fries are pretty good too. My green lemonade was way too sweet and lemonade-y for me. 

If I were you, I would try it because people love it so much and you get some unique items. But for the $10 range for a lunch item, I wouldn't  say it's nothing AMAZING.
Revise this with your best effort:
Although many people rave about this place, I personally find it to be just average. The location is great, the food is fresh, and they offer a wide variety of vegan options which is commendable. However, aside from that, I find it unremarkable. I've tried their crispy ranch and curry tofu dishes, which were enjoyable, but I can't help but feel that I expected more from a specialty vegan restaurant. The crispy ranch with chick'n was a definite highlight, and their fries are quite good as well. On the other hand, the green lemonade I ordered was overly sweet and heavy on the lemon flavor for my taste. 

If you're curious, I would recommend giving it a try since many people seem to love it, and they do offer some unique items. However, considering the price range of around $10 for a lunch item, I wouldn't classify it as anything extraordinary.

input: Guy at the counter was rude, the place was filthy, and all around horrible! Would/will not recommend this place at all!
Revise this with your best effort: The customer service at the counter was exceedingly rude, and the overall cleanliness of the place was deplorable. In all aspects, my experience was horrendous, and I strongly advise against recommending this establishment to anyone.

input: My last full day in New Orleans and I HAD to come here!! Came in the pouring rain too!! I really wanted some authentic New Orleans style food (yes... it's still authentic if it's vegan, I don't care what you say! Lol!) Jamone was nice enough to give me a little taste of everything, so I could pick. That just made it harder, because I wanted it ALL!!. I'm telling you,  there is no bad choice here. Everything was SO good and flavorful!! And the bread pudding was the topper for me! I would be a regular if I lived out here! Do yourself a favor and come try this place. Come hungry too, so you can have it all, like me!  Oh...and the other great thing.  This is one vegan place where they give you a TON of food without emptying your wallet!!! Amazing food and service!!
Revise this with your best effort: My final day in New Orleans couldn't have been complete without a visit to this amazing place, even in the midst of pouring rain! I was specifically craving some authentic New Orleans style food, and yes, even if it's vegan, it can still possess that wonderful authenticity (no arguments, please!). Jamone, the kind owner, generously allowed me to sample a little bit of everything on the menu, making my decision that much more difficult because honestly, everything was superb! The flavors were so rich and delightful; I couldn't help but indulge in each and every dish. However, the ultimate winner for me was their delectable bread pudding. If I were a local, this would undoubtedly become a regular haunt for me. I wholeheartedly recommend that you treat yourself and visit this place, and make sure to bring along a voracious appetite to truly experience the full offering, just like I did! And here's an additional point worth noting: unlike many other vegan establishments, this place serves generous portions without breaking the bank. The combination of incredible food and outstanding service truly sets this place apart.

input:
Magical vegan heaven. My wife and I stopped here on a detour from our route back home to Boston and she (a non-vegan) devoured their Philly steak. I literally had to pry her away from ordering more; I don't blame her at all though because the food was damn good. I had the curry tofu wrap and it was delicious. The place is pretty small with limited seating so a lot of people were taking (and I'm assuming regularly take) their food to go, so I'd be wary of this if you're wanting to sit in. 

But yeah this place rocks. Their kale lemonade alone is worth the 5 stars. Next time we're in Philly this place will be among the first in which we stuff our faces.
Revise this with your best effort:
My wife and I stumbled upon this magical vegan haven during a spontaneous detour on our way back home to Boston. To our surprise, even my non-vegan wife couldn't resist devouring their delectable Philly steak. I had to practically pry her away from ordering seconds! And I can't blame her, because the food was nothing short of amazing. Personally, I opted for the curry tofu wrap, and it was an explosion of flavors in my mouth.

The only downside was that the place is quite small and has limited seating. Understandably, many people were taking their food to go. So, if you're looking to dine in, I would advise being mindful of the seating situation. However, despite the size constraints, this place truly rocks.

Let me tell you, their kale lemonade alone is worth every single star. Its tangy and refreshing taste is simply unforgettable. So, mark my words, next time we find ourselves in Philly, this enchanting spot will be at the top of our list to indulge in vegan delights.

input: My wife and I LOVE this place. The management is always very attentive and the service is excellent! Things to try: Tiger Roll, Pink Lady Roll, Tornado Roll. Ask for Billy he's our favorite. I highly recommend this place of others in the same area. Enjoy!
Revise this with your best effort: My wife and I absolutely adore this place! The management consistently displays remarkable attentiveness and the service is top-notch. If you're looking for recommendations, we highly suggest trying out the Tiger Roll, Pink Lady Roll, and Tornado Roll. Billy, in particular, is our favorite server, so don't hesitate to ask for him. Without a doubt, we highly recommend this place to anyone in the area. Enjoy your visit!

input: Great place for lunch in NOLA. Love their fried chicken, and the red beans and rice is yummy too. It's a staple on our trips to town. Staff is friendly and attentitve and prices are great.
Revise this with your best effort:
Looking for a fantastic lunch spot in New Orleans? Look no further! This hidden gem not only offers mouthwatering fried chicken but also serves up a delectable bowl of red beans and rice. No trip to town is complete without indulging in these local favorites. 

What sets this place apart is not just the delicious food but also the exceptional service provided by their friendly and attentive staff. They go above and beyond to ensure your dining experience is nothing short of amazing. 

Even better, this incredible eatery offers all of this at affordable prices. You don't have to break the bank to enjoy a satisfying meal here. It's no wonder this place has become a staple for us during our trips to NOLA.

input: I live in the neighborhood so I try to frequent Mint as much as I can. No choice is a bad choice! Also the Taro Tapioca Smoothie is the perfect cure for a sweet tooth.
Revise this with your best effort: Since I reside in the neighborhood, I make it a point to visit Mint as often as possible. Every option on their menu is exceptional, leaving no room for disappointment. Moreover, for those with a craving for something sweet, the Taro Tapioca Smoothie serves as an impeccable remedy.

input: The salsa and guacamole is. Made fresh daily. The chips are home made as well. The shrimp burrito was huge but was tasty and fresh. The wait staff was just average.
Revise this with your best effort: The salsa and guacamole are made fresh daily, ensuring their vibrant flavors. Additionally, the chips are lovingly crafted in-house, resulting in a delightful crunch. The shrimp burrito, although generously portioned, maintains a delectable freshness that enhances its taste. However, the wait staff's performance was merely average.

input:
To be honest, I was kind of disappointed with this place. I really wanted to like it, and it has gotten so many positive reviews, so I thought it was a sure thing, but it was just a little underwhelming. Not bad, just not amazing. I had the costanza, and the fillings were tasty, but the crust was disappointing. It was way too bread-y, as opposed to doughy, and when I think of a calzone, I think of dough like pizza dough- this was not that. The calzones are a good size, but they were a little skimpy with the meat fillings. Probably the most disappointing part was the dessert- we got the apple pie calzone, and it just had a really weird spice to it- something other than cinnamon that I couldn't put my finger on. It also didn't have that many chunks of apples inside- it was almost pureed apple. Meh. 

I like the vibe of this place and it's close and convenient to where i live, so I really want to like it, but I just wasn't thrilled with it the first time. Perhaps I'll give it one more shot, but it seems a little overhyped!
Revise this with your best effort:
To be frank, my initial impression of this place left me feeling rather disappointed. Despite the numerous positive reviews it had received, I was not as impressed as I had hoped to be. While not terrible, it simply fell short of being extraordinary. Opting for the costanza, I found the fillings to be quite flavorful, yet the crust failed to meet my expectations. It was overly bread-like rather than the desired doughy texture that I associate with a calzone. Consequently, the calzones were adequately sized but somewhat lacking in the meat fillings. The most dissatisfying aspect was undoubtedly the dessert. We ordered the apple pie calzone and it had an unusual spice that I couldn't quite identify—definitely not cinnamon. Moreover, there were very few apple chunks present, giving it more of a pureed consistency. All in all, my first experience left much to be desired.

Despite my underwhelming visit, I appreciate the ambiance of this establishment and its close proximity to my residence, which inherently generates a desire for it to be enjoyable. While I may consider giving it another chance, the hype surrounding it seems somewhat excessive.

input:
An amazing view, impeccable professional service great fare,don't  skip a visit to this Philadelphia gem. Nick, who is a stellar, incredible server, recommended a lovely 2010 Bordeaux-Chateau Font Merlet which complemented the Tuna Tartare and Steak Tataki.

This is a must see in Philadelphia. After witnessing a fabulous nighttime view, I can't wait to return to check out the spectacular sunsets.
Revise this with your best effort:
Don't miss the chance to experience this absolute gem in Philadelphia, boasting breathtaking views, outstanding professional service, and delectable cuisine. One cannot overlook a visit to this renowned establishment. Nick, an exceptional and extraordinary server, graciously recommended a delightful 2010 Bordeaux-Chateau Font Merlet, perfectly accentuating the flavors of the exquisite Tuna Tartare and succulent Steak Tataki.

Considered an essential destination in Philadelphia, the awe-inspiring nighttime view left me longing for future visits to witness the captivating sunsets that await.

input: The food is very good but the ability to turnover the tables is a huge problem on busy days. Waited over an hour to be seated today and about an hour to get food. I just do not have 2 hours available to get breakfast. They do not have the proper staffing to quickly get the food out and clear tables in a timely fashion. There were many upset people there due to the time to wait. While we were eating there were 2 empty tables for at least 15 minutes that they did not seat anyone at yet when we left there was a longer line than when I arrived which we waited an hour to be seated. The workers were trying but were simply overwhelmed. Management needs to do a better job handling the staffing schedules. I will not be coming back due to this experience.
Revise this with your best effort: The food at this establishment is undeniably delicious; however, the issue lies in their ability to efficiently turnover tables, particularly on busy days. Today, I found myself waiting for over an hour just to be seated and then another hour for our food to arrive. Unfortunately, I am unable to spare two whole hours for breakfast. The lack of sufficient staffing is clearly evident, causing delays in both food preparation and table clearance. The amount of frustrated customers waiting was quite significant. It was disheartening to witness two vacant tables for at least 15 minutes while we were eating, knowing that they could have accommodated more individuals. Astonishingly, as we departed, the line had grown even longer than when I had initially arrived after an hour-long wait for seating. Although the workers were doing their best, they appeared overwhelmed by the situation. Efficiently managing the staffing schedules is crucial for the management to address. Regrettably, due to this unfortunate experience, I do not plan on returning.

input:
Aside from the occasional Eggs Benny, whenever I go out for breakfast, I always order the same...eggs, bacon, hashbrowns and wheat toast with a side of salsa if they have it. 
And that's exactly what I ordered today.
The hashbrowns were undercooked for my taste, so next time I'll ask for them to be crispy/well done. Everything else was quite good. Better than the Cajun Kitchen on Chapala, but not as good as the CK in Goleta.

Thankfully all of the special requests that I DID make were taken care of.

I'm super picky about my breakfast. 
Who am I kidding...I'm super picky about everything, lol.

Large portions(leftovers for tomorrow), super affordable(more so than CK), and loved sitting on their well shaded patio(no patio at CK).
There was one server taking care of 5 tables, she was great and very cheerful. No complaints about the service.

Terraza means balcony/terrace in Spanish and that's exactly why I would come here instead of other breakfast places that don't have one.

Next on the agenda...
Check out their lunch items.
Revise this with your best effort:
When I go out for breakfast, I typically order the same classic combination of eggs, bacon, hashbrowns, and wheat toast with a side of salsa, if available. And that's exactly what I decided on today. Although everything was delicious, the hashbrowns were slightly undercooked for my liking. Next time, I'll make sure to request them crispy or well done. Overall, the meal was better than what I've had at the Cajun Kitchen on Chapala but not quite as good as the one in Goleta.

Fortunately, all of the special requests I had made were successfully accommodated. I must admit, I can be quite particular when it comes to breakfast. Who am I kidding? I can be picky about everything, lol.

The portions were generous, providing leftovers for tomorrow, and the prices were very affordable, even more so than at the Cajun Kitchen. I especially enjoyed sitting on their well-shaded patio, a feature that the CK in Goleta doesn't have. The service was impeccable considering there was only one server taking care of five tables. She was friendly and cheerful, leaving no room for complaints.

The word "Terraza" translates to balcony/terrace in Spanish, and that's precisely why I prefer coming here over other breakfast spots that lack this feature.

Now, it's time to explore their lunch menu and see what they have to offer.

input:
This is an all you can eat place that at $27/adult isn't bad.  But if you ordered from the regular menu, you come to realize just how mediocre the quality is.  Maki rolls are OK, but mine were so cold they had clearly been premade and sat in the fridge.  Oyster ponzu was missing the ponzu and the coating was really heavy - like an A+W onion ring. 

So if you are really hungry and want to eat several plates of rolls and greasy tempura then this is for you. Granted sometimes that is just what you're craving. But avoid the squid.
Revise this with your best effort:
This all-you-can-eat establishment may seem appealing at $27 per adult, but once you sample items from their regular menu, you'll quickly realize their mediocre quality. While the maki rolls are passable, my personal experience involved receiving cold rolls that seemed pre-made and stored in a refrigerator. Furthermore, the oyster ponzu lacked the essential ponzu flavor and the coating was excessively heavy, reminiscent of an A+W onion ring.

This place may suit individuals with voracious appetites seeking numerous plates of rolls and greasy tempura. Admittedly, there are times when these cravings hit the spot. However, I would caution against ordering the squid as it's best to steer clear.

input: I called them after calling another locksmith who was rude to me on the phone. Anyway I called them in the morning and they sent someone out in 20 min. they were done in less than one hour and I received 4 free keys too. their service can't be beat.
Revise this with your best effort: After experiencing rudeness from another locksmith on the phone, I decided to reach out to this company. I made the call in the morning, and to my surprise, they promptly dispatched a professional to my location within just 20 minutes. Incredibly, the job was completed in less than an hour, and as a bonus, I was also given four complimentary keys. The exceptional service they provided truly surpassed my expectations.

input:
This place is VERY crowded and not in a good way - unless you enjoy smelling other people's BO while you eat and drink. Gag! I guess the smell of the patrons matches the smell of the bathrooms which are also gag worthy and dirty. 

The prices aren't really great for the meh food available. Service was also meh. A few times we wondered if our server was every coming back. There are so many better options in Philly as a foodie city to try, so why waste your time and money here? Pass and head somewhere else.
Revise this with your best effort:
This location is extremely overcrowded, and unfortunately, it does not make for a pleasant experience. Unless you are fond of the overpowering scent of other patrons' body odors permeating the air while you dine and drink, you may want to reconsider. It's truly off-putting! Moreover, the stench seems to match the nauseating state of the restrooms, which are not only unclean but also highly unpleasant.

Considering the underwhelming quality of the food available, the prices offered here are hardly justified. The service, too, leaves much to be desired, as there were instances when we found ourselves wondering if our server had completely forgotten about us. With an abundance of other excellent dining options in Philadelphia, renowned for its culinary prowess, it would be a waste of both time and money to spend it here. My suggestion would be to forgo this place and explore elsewhere instead.

input: Good beer selection, knowledgeable staff. Had I not ordered food here it would have an enjoyable experience. Some how received undercooked inedible Fries, one well done burger and one burger medium rare.... both burgers were served on buns that felt straight out of the refrigerator, slightly hard and cold. If you're drunk the foods good, don't eat it sober, plus add in service that was lackluster at best. We couldn't even eat the food and left it untouched. We told the the bartender no we didn't want it and what was wrong with it. Charged us full price.
Revise this with your best effort: The beer selection here is impressive, and the staff is very knowledgeable. However, my experience would have been much more enjoyable if I hadn't ordered any food. Unfortunately, we were served undercooked and inedible fries, one well-done burger, and one burger cooked medium rare. Both burgers were served on buns that felt like they had just come out of the refrigerator - slightly hard and cold. It's safe to say that the food was not up to par, especially when consumed sober. Additionally, the service was lackluster at best. We couldn't bring ourselves to eat the food and left it untouched. We even informed the bartender of our dissatisfaction, explaining why we didn't want it, but were still charged the full price.

input:
My first experience did mot go well due to the heavy accents of the employees. I called ahead so my order would be ready for me to pick up and it was, it just was not what I ordered. They are nice people and corrected my order but instead of simply picking up my food I had to wait 20 minutes To get my original order. When all was said and done, the food was good.

I was nearby and decided to give them a second chance. This time I ordered a pizza steak and I was really impressed! I need to have a couple more before I can declare them my new favorite pizza steak. Plenty of mozzarella cheese and the roll is stuffed with meat and just enough sauce. It's looking like this place is a lot better than my first impression.
Revise this with your best effort:
My initial experience was not great due to the heavy accents of the employees. However, despite calling ahead and having my order ready for pickup, it was not what I had requested. Although the staff was kind enough to correct it, I ended up waiting an additional 20 minutes for my original order. Nevertheless, once I finally received the food, it turned out to be quite delicious.

Not wanting to write them off completely, I decided to give them another chance since I happened to be in the area. Opting for a pizza steak this time, I was truly impressed! The abundance of mozzarella cheese, perfectly stuffed roll filled with meat, and just the right amount of sauce left me pleasantly surprised. It seems like this place has redeemed itself and I might even consider making it my go-to spot for pizza steaks after trying a few more.

input:
The longest bar in the City!  For as crazy busy as the Happy Hours are, the Friday and Saturday late night crowds are really relaxed and there's always a place to sit.  This is the perfect place on a Saturday night after a show at the Troc if you don't want to go to Chinatown or a Dive bar.   I've been walking over after shows at the Electric Factory lately and it's THE place to unwind after standing up for 3 hours.  

IBP has all kinds of sports packages so it's a great place to go to watch that out of town football or baseball game.  The upstairs bar has pool tables and a separate jukebox.

edit:  RIP IBP
Revise this with your best effort:
Introducing the City's Ultimate Hangout Spot! Despite the bustling Happy Hours, the crowds on Friday and Saturday nights at the longest bar in town exude a relaxed vibe, ensuring you'll always find a comfortable seat. After catching an exciting show at the Troc, this is undoubtedly the go-to destination, sparing you the need to venture out to Chinatown or settle for a run-of-the-mill Dive bar. Lately, I've been strolling over here post Electric Factory gigs, and trust me, it's the perfect spot to unwind after enduring three hours on your feet.

IBP boasts an extensive range of sports packages, making it an ideal spot to catch that eagerly anticipated out-of-town football or baseball game. Additionally, the upstairs bar features enticing amenities like pool tables and a separate jukebox.

Edit: Sadly, bid farewell to IBP as it rests in peace.

input:
Four stars for the beer, atmosphere and usually service. There is a reason this place is always packed! Half price beer during a generous happy hour, a huge deck that welcomes dogs, and delicious key lime pie.   Sadly, said deck allows smoking, and there is usually lots of it. I wish they at least had a nonsmoking side. 

If giving a review just based on the food, I would give it a two. The pretzels are ok, but the cheese dip is Velveeta nastiest. As a native Wisconsinite, I take offense at plastic cheese. Then, there's the pretzel bun sandwiches. I've sampled the chicken, brat and Italian sausage. It's pricey, considering it comes with potato chips (seriously guys?! Get a fryer!) and just ok. The buns were kind of soggy and the overall experience underwhelming, especially knowing the epic sandwiches for sale next door. I wish the Village pub would focus on what it's best that, serving beer, and let us bring Mitchell's sandwiches over.
Revise this with your best effort:
I would give four stars to this place for its beer, atmosphere, and usually good service. It's always packed for a reason! They have a fantastic happy hour with half-price beer and a spacious deck that is dog-friendly. Additionally, their key lime pie is delicious. However, it's worth mentioning that the deck allows smoking, which can be bothersome for non-smokers like myself. It would be great if they had a designated nonsmoking area.

Now, if I were to review the food alone, I would give it a two-star rating. The pretzels are alright, but the cheese dip made with Velveeta is not to my taste. As a native Wisconsinite, I prefer real cheese. The pretzel bun sandwiches, such as the chicken, brat, and Italian sausage options, are overpriced considering they only come with potato chips. It would be much better if they invested in a fryer! The buns tend to be soggy, and overall, the experience falls short, especially when compared to the epic sandwiches sold next door at Mitchell's. I believe the Village Pub would be better off focusing on what they do best, which is serving great beer, and allowing customers to bring in sandwiches from Mitchell's.

input: Could not be more pleased with this establishment. Always clean and has a good feel, like the employees there actually enjoy their job. I didn't think I could like this place anymore and then I tried their fluff and fold service. Immaculate, absolutely perfect. All my clothes were returned perfectly folded and clean like I had just bought them. They even use environmentally friendly detergent! I'm sold! Thanks Modern Laundry now laundry is just one more quick stop on my laundry list of errands.
Revise this with your best effort: I am extremely delighted with this establishment. It constantly maintains a pristine level of cleanliness and exudes a pleasant atmosphere, giving the impression that the employees genuinely take pleasure in their work.
