I express my heartfelt gratitude to Modern Laundry for making laundry just another effortlessly accomplished task on my list of errands.

input: Food and atmosphere is nice. As one should expect in the CBD. Sometimes the back room can be stuffy on a busy day. I recommend the raw oysters and burgers. A few dollars on the high side for lunch.
Revise this with your best effort: The dining experience at this establishment is delightful, offering not only delicious food but also a pleasant atmosphere, as one would naturally anticipate in the central business district (CBD). However, during peak hours, the back room can occasionally become a bit stuffy. When it comes to food recommendations, I highly suggest trying their exquisite raw oysters and flavorful burgers. It's worth mentioning that the lunch prices might be slightly on the higher end, but the quality justifies the expense.

input: Great choice in a small shop. Worth the drive. The wine cakes are excellent! Just went here for first time based on yelp reviews and will definitely be going back
Revise this with your best effort: This small shop is a fantastic option and definitely worth the drive. The wine cakes they offer are truly excellent! After discovering this place through glowing Yelp reviews, I recently visited for the first time and I can confidently say that I will be returning.

input:
I am not known for favorable restaurant reviews.  Most of them below my radar.
The Love is different.  
  We had a Father's Day lunch that was exceptional.
There is little left off the menu and we were hard pressed to make a choice from the wonderful selections listed.  Our waiter was professional and accommodating.  Lovely atmosphere, light and bright.  I was amazed that the inside of my omelet was HOT. A little surprise thrown in with my Potatos..........roasted peppers, and onions.
Greens on every plate. Mine had warm spinach salad as well. My husband had the Belgium waffles made with corn meal and garnished with Blueberry butter.  They use our favorite La Columbe coffee.
Nothing left to wish for.
Revise this with your best effort: I am not typically known for giving favorable restaurant reviews, as most of them do not catch my attention. However, The Love is a pleasant exception. Our Father's Day lunch experience at this establishment was truly exceptional. The menu offers a wide array of delicious options, making it challenging to decide on just one. Our waiter was professional and went out of their way to accommodate us. The atmosphere was lovely - bright and inviting. What surprised me the most was that the inside of my omelet was piping hot, and it came with a delightful addition of roasted peppers and onions. Alongside every plate were fresh greens, and my dish even included a warm spinach salad. My husband opted for the Belgian waffles made with cornmeal, topped with delectable blueberry butter. Additionally, they serve our favorite La Colombe coffee. There was truly nothing more we could have asked for during our dining experience at The Love.

input:
Not bad. Sushi roll was good but options were limited. Hibachi grill: i got steak...chef asked me 2x how i like mine-medium...Still ended up with well done. Rest of my group had chicken which all voiced lacked seasoning. 

Beware they DO NOT have a late happy hour 8-11 as advertised on their website. We asked the staff about it and they claimed 8-11 was for a different location. Their website nowhere indicates the happy hour is for a specific location nor does the website indicate they have multiple locations at all.
Revise this with your best effort:
Pretty decent experience overall. The sushi roll was quite enjoyable, although the menu options were somewhat limited. As for the hibachi grill, I ordered steak and the chef double-checked my preferred cooking temperature, which I specified as medium. However, I ended up receiving a well-done steak instead. Unfortunately, the rest of my group found the chicken lacking in seasoning, as they all voiced their disappointment. 

It is important to note that the advertised late happy hour from 8-11, as mentioned on their website, is not available at this location. When we inquired about it, the staff informed us that the 8-11 happy hour was exclusive to a different branch. It is rather confusing, as their website does not specify that the happy hour is limited to a particular location, nor does it mention the existence of multiple locations at all.

input:
I saw a deal on Groupon for Lee How Fook recently and after I read the reviews on Yelp, I was really excited to check this place out.  Unfortunately, I just didn't enjoy this restaurant and was pretty disappointed.

Lee How Fook is pretty small, but that didn't make it lose any points in my book.  I could see it getting really busy (especially since there are only about 10 tables available), so I would definitely suggest making reservations if you're going on a weekend.  The service wasn't bad, but when I asked some questions about some dishes on the menu, I had a hard time understanding what she was trying to say.  

Okay now to the main course - food!  For appetizers, we ordered the pan seared pork dumplings and sui mai.  Both appetizers were delicious and the dipping sauce was really good.  For the entrees, we ordered the sweet & sour chicken, pan fried noodle with shrimp, and pan fried noodle with beef and black bean sauce.  The sweet & sour chicken was awful - more sweet than sour - and the vegetables in it were really undercooked (pretty much raw).  (I do have to admit that I like things spicy, so maybe this dish just wasn't for me.)  For both pan fried noodle dishes, they were blah with a side of blah.  The beef dish was supposed to be spicy, but I just didn't taste any heat.  I left here full, but unsatisfied.
Revise this with your best effort:
After spotting a deal on Groupon for Lee How Fook, my anticipation grew as I perused the reviews on Yelp. Regrettably, my experience at this restaurant left much to be desired and left me feeling quite disappointed.

Although small in size, the limited seating at Lee How Fook did not detract from its appeal in my eyes. However, it is worth noting that due to its popularity, making a reservation, especially on weekends, is highly recommended as it can get quite busy. The service, while not terrible, had its flaws. I encountered difficulty understanding the server when I sought clarification on certain menu items.

Now let's move on to the star of the show - the food! We decided to start with the pan-seared pork dumplings and sui mai as our appetizers. Both dishes proved to be delectable, and the accompanying dipping sauce added a delightful touch. As for the main courses, we opted for the sweet and sour chicken, pan-fried noodle with shrimp, and pan-fried noodle with beef and black bean sauce. Unfortunately, the sweet and sour chicken was a letdown, leaning heavily towards sweetness with an inadequate sourness, and the vegetables were severely undercooked, bordering on raw. Admittedly, my preference for spiciness may have biased my opinion, but the dish simply did not hit the mark. The pan-fried noodle dishes were equally lackluster, lacking any distinct flavors. Despite leaving the restaurant feeling full, I couldn't shake the feeling of dissatisfaction.

In conclusion, my visit to Lee How Fook did not live up to the positive reviews I had read beforehand. The restaurant's small size did not hinder its appeal, but the service left something to be desired. While some dishes, like the appetizers, showed promise, the main courses failed to deliver in terms of flavor and execution. As a result, I departed feeling satiated but ultimately unsatisfied.

input: The hot chicken is probably one of the best fried chickens I've ever eaten, and I'm from the South/NC and have had quite a bit of it. However, the price for the small portion size is really expensive. The drinks here are fantastic too.
Revise this with your best effort: The hot chicken at this place is hands down one of the most exquisite iterations of fried chicken I've had the pleasure of savoring. And mind you, as a proud Southerner hailing from NC, I dare say I've sampled quite a gamut of fried chicken offerings. Nevertheless, it is with a tinge of disappointment that I must mention the rather exorbitant price tag attached to the small portion sizes. On a positive note, the beverages served here are positively delightful, offering a tantalizing complement to the delectable fare.

input: I could write a lengthy review, persuasive and layered to hit all the right points. But why do that when Lee How Fook makes food that does it for you? Long story short they have some of the best general tso chicken I have eaten to date. Try it for yourself and get back at me. - Coolie
Revise this with your best effort: I can craft an elaborate and thoughtful review, skillfully highlighting all the crucial aspects. However, there's no need for that when Lee How Fook's food speaks for itself. In a nutshell, their General Tso chicken is among the most exceptional I've ever tasted. I highly recommend experiencing it firsthand and sharing your thoughts with me. - Coolie

input:
Thank you Chef John Besh!  My husband and I stayed at the Hilton hotel on St. Charles. One of my main goals was to find some delicious New Orleans grinds.  I was starving when we arrived and didn't want to do any research on Yelp for a place to eat.  Thank God Luke was connected to our hotel!!!  We ended up eating here 3 times over 5 days.  It's usually full of business suits, but that doesn't bother me when the food is so good.

All the traditional dishes were good, but the huge surprise was the burger.  I was against ordering a burger while I was in New Orleans, because I wanted to try as many local eats as possible... and you can find burgers anywhere.  I overheard this lady raving about how delicious her burger was, so I had to order it the next time we ate there.  She was absolutely right!  It was one of the best burgers I've ever had!  It was huge, juicy, and packed with flavor.  I also highly recommend getting their bread pudding a la mode.  It was mouth-watering good and straight out the oven!
Revise this with your best effort:
Dear Chef John Besh, 

I want to express my utmost gratitude to you. My husband and I recently had the pleasure of staying at the Hilton hotel on St. Charles in New Orleans, and I must say, finding delicious local cuisine was high on my list of priorities. 

Upon our arrival, I found myself famished and in no mood for researching restaurants on Yelp. Thankfully, fate intervened and we discovered Luke, conveniently connected to our hotel. To say we were delighted with our dining experience would be an understatement – in fact, we ended up dining there three times over the course of our five-day stay. 

Luke may typically attract business suits, but that didn't detract from our enjoyment as the food surpassed all expectations. While the traditional dishes were undeniably delicious, one particular item left us pleasantly surprised – the burger. Initially, I had reservations about indulging in a burger while in New Orleans, as my aim was to explore as many local delicacies as possible, knowing that burgers can be found anywhere. However, I couldn't resist after overhearing a lady rave about her burger, and decided to order one on our next visit. It turned out to be one of the most exceptional burgers I have ever had the pleasure of devouring. From its generous size to its juicy and flavorful patty, every bite was a sheer delight. 

In addition, I highly recommend indulging in Luke's bread pudding a la mode. Words cannot adequately convey how mouth-wateringly good it was – freshly baked and served warm, it was pure perfection. 

Once again, thank you Chef John Besh for providing an unforgettable culinary experience at Luke. Your dedication to creating exceptional food is truly commendable. 

Warm Regards, 
[Your Name]

input: Came down here for some of their tasty fish tacos to find out that they have closed this location.
Revise this with your best effort: I journeyed down here in search of their delectable fish tacos, only to discover with disappointment that this particular establishment has ceased its operations at this location.

input:
Thanks SO much to Jacob... 
A beautiful day spent skiing at Squaw ended with my realization that I had lost our car keys somewhere on the mountain. I had Security call every lift we'd hit and they took my name in case the keys were turned in. Do I call Toyota? Do I have to tow my car back to SF? I looked up "locksmith" on my phone's Google Maps app and Alpine came up (their Truckee office). Jacob had obviously dealt with the situation before. He gave me a price quote in about 30sec and gave me an accurate time frame as to when he could get to Squaw. He even called when he was running a few minutes late. We enjoyed a nice happy hour in the meantime and when he got to the parking lot, I think it took him less  than 4min to get our key code and create us some new keys. Thanks for saving the day! Honest, quick service. Hope I never need to call them again under the same circumstances, but they'll be the first I call I make if I lose another set of keys. (Alpine accepts AAA).
Revise this with your best effort:
I am extremely grateful to Jacob from Alpine for saving the day. After a wonderful day of skiing at Squaw, I was devastated to realize that I had misplaced our car keys somewhere on the mountain. Worried about the next steps, I asked Security to contact all the lifts we had used and left my name in case the keys were found. Thoughts raced through my mind - should I reach out to Toyota? Would I have to tow my car all the way back to San Francisco? That's when I turned to my phone's Google Maps app and searched for a locksmith. Alpine, with their Truckee office, appeared on the screen, and I decided to give them a call.

Jacob, who clearly had experience handling such situations, promptly provided me with a price quote within 30 seconds. He also gave me an accurate estimate of when he could arrive at Squaw. Even when he was running a few minutes behind, he thoughtfully called to inform me. We decided to make the most of the situation and enjoyed a pleasant happy hour while waiting for him. When Jacob finally reached the parking lot, it seemed like he worked his magic in no more than 4 minutes - he effortlessly obtained our key code and swiftly created new keys for us. His timely and efficient service truly saved the day.

I truly appreciate the honesty and speed displayed by Alpine locksmiths. Although I hope to never find myself in similar circumstances again, if I were to lose another set of keys, Alpine would undoubtedly be the first company I contact. Additionally, it is worth noting that Alpine accepts AAA, which adds an extra layer of convenience.

input:
I finally made it to Farmhaus last Saturday, and it was worth the wait.  

As expected for a weekend, it was crowded.  We arrived about 15 minutes early and had to wait on the bench back by the bathrooms for a few minutes.  However, as I said, we were earlier than they anticipated, and they got us to the bar as soon as seats opened up.  They wisely gave us a copy of the menu to be prepared once we were seated, and we did indeed plan our entire meal in advance.  This was helpful, because we were actually seated about 20 minutes late, and I was about to eat the menu itself as I drooled over the descriptions!  

The smoked fish dip and escolar with prawns were fantastic- the standouts of the meal.  The mushroom salad and tapenade were also very good.  The meatloaf was good, but a little on the dry and bland side.  I wanted to get the nachos, but there were no other takers in my group....next time....

Service was good.  It was a bit shaky at times, but it was slammed the whole time we were there and that small space must be tough to work in.  

I would love to go back and check out their blue place special lunches...I have heard amazing reviews.  I think I will head back for dinner when there is outdoor seating, as I think that would add to the experience.
Revise this with your best effort:
My long-awaited visit to Farmhaus last Saturday was well worth the wait. As expected on a weekend, the restaurant was bustling with people. Arriving a bit ahead of schedule, we had to patiently wait on the bench near the bathrooms for a few minutes. However, the staff efficiently accommodated us at the bar as soon as seats became available, providing us with a menu to peruse in advance. This foresight proved helpful, considering we were eventually seated nearly 20 minutes past our reservation time, leading me to contemplate devouring the menu itself due to its mouthwatering descriptions.

The standout dishes of the evening were undeniably the smoked fish dip and escolar with prawns. These culinary delights were nothing short of fantastic. The mushroom salad and tapenade were also quite enjoyable. While the meatloaf was satisfactory, it veered slightly towards the dry and bland side. Sadly, I was unable to indulge in the nachos, as the rest of my group did not share my enthusiasm. However, that will certainly be on my order list for my next visit.

Given the constant rush of customers, the service was commendable albeit slightly inconsistent. The small, cramped space the staff had to maneuver in must present its fair share of challenges.

I am eager to return and sample their renowned blue plate special lunches, having heard nothing but rave reviews. I believe I will opt for a dinner reservation when outdoor seating becomes available, as I believe it would enhance the overall experience.

input: This restaurant is seriously lacking in customer service!  We have dined many times at Dish.  We like the food.  We made a reservation two weeks ahead for 3 people.  When we arrived we were seated at the smallest table in the restaurant which barely fits two people.  The table next to us had an extra person added at the end, his back was literally a couple of inches from our table.  We asked for a table that would accomdate three people and not involve eating with someone's large back at our very tiny table.  We were rudely informed that it was a take or leave it situation.  It was very frustrating since we booked this as a special night out weeks earlier.  Unfortunately, we are writing this restraurant off our list.
Revise this with your best effort: The customer service at this restaurant leaves much to be desired. Despite being frequent patrons of Dish, the quality of service fell short this time. Although we genuinely enjoy the food, we made a reservation for three individuals; a reservation which we confirmed two weeks in advance. Upon arrival, we were seated at the tiniest table in the establishment, one that could barely accommodate two people comfortably. To make matters worse, an additional person was squeezed into the table next to us, his back practically touching our table. When we kindly requested a table suitable for three, ensuring we wouldn't have to share our dining space with someone's obstructive back, we were met with rude and unwelcoming responses. This entirely contradicted our anticipation for a special night out that we had diligently planned weeks prior. Regrettably, we have decided to remove this restaurant from our list of preferred dining establishments.

input: This restaurant was pretty good; i'll admit it! I went here in the late evening with my boyfriend to have a nice date! He insisted on us ordering a milkshake and i'm SO GLAD that he did. The milkshake was probably one of the best ones i've had in my lifetime. The food was pretty good and so was the service but something was a little off. I couldn't tell what it was but i just got a really strange vibe from the restaurant. Maybe i'm just being crazy!
Revise this with your best effort: I must confess, this restaurant surpassed my expectations. My boyfriend and I decided to visit for a delightful evening date, and I'm genuinely pleased that we did. Against my initial hesitations, he persuaded us to order a milkshake, and boy, am I grateful for his suggestion. Undoubtedly, it was among the finest milkshakes I've experienced in my entire life. The cuisine also impressed us with its quality, and the service was commendable. However, there was an indescribable element that seemed slightly amiss. It could simply be my imagination running wild, but there was an inexplicable oddity that lingered in the atmosphere of the restaurant. Perhaps, I'm just being overly sensitive.

input:
I was so disappointed when this opened; I was hoping for Nashville's first real authentic Greek restaurant (Athens notwithstanding).  This isn't Greek; it isn't even Mediterranean. It's pseudo-Americanized versions of Mediterranean classic cuisine. The corporate chefs got so many things wrong:  Skordalia is a classic Greek dip made out of potatoes and garlic (not bread).  Avgolemono is chicken soup with egg, lemon and rice -- not this thin, awful broth they are currently serving. If one wants true Greek cooking, one should go to Greektown in either Detroit or Toronto. 
Just say no.
Revise this with your best effort: I was extremely let down upon its opening as I had high hopes for Nashville's first truly authentic Greek restaurant (excluding Athens). Unfortunately, this establishment falls short of being truly Greek, or even Mediterranean for that matter. Instead, it offers a watered-down, pseudo-Americanized take on Mediterranean classics. The corporate chefs missed the mark on so many levels here. For example, skordalia, a renowned Greek dip, should be crafted with potatoes and garlic rather than bread as they have done here. Furthermore, their attempt at avgolemono, a delightful chicken soup made with egg, lemon, and rice, is nothing more than a disappointing and watery broth. If you seek genuine Greek cuisine, I highly recommend visiting Greektown in either Detroit or Toronto. Trust me, it's best to steer clear of this place.

input: Best meal in New Orleans!!! I was in a group of 4 and we were served by Travis, Susan & Caroline. I had the set price menu: strawberry salad appetiser, chicken entrée & chocolate cake dessert. The salad was fresh and a great start. The chicken is the best chicken I have ever eaten anywhere. It had crispy skin, but was the meat was extremely moist and the corn bread stuffing was superb. The cake was yummy, but very rich. One of our party is vegetarian and she LOVED her vegetable selection plate. The other 2 members had the pork with sweet potato mash and said it was excellent. The staff were wonderful and very attentive. Excellent location and definitely the best meal we had in New Orleans.
Revise this with your best effort:
The best meal experience in New Orleans!!! Our group of four was impeccably served by the remarkable team of Travis, Susan, and Caroline. Opting for the set price menu, I delighted in the succulent strawberry salad as an appetizer, followed by the most exceptional chicken entrée I have ever had the pleasure of devouring. The chicken boasted a perfectly crispy exterior, while the meat itself remained incredibly moist, effortlessly complemented by the delectable corn bread stuffing. To conclude this extraordinary meal, I indulged in a yummy, albeit rich, chocolate cake dessert.

Amongst our party, one member was a vegetarian and expressed their absolute adoration for the vegetable selection plate. The remaining two individuals opted for the pork with sweet potato mash and unanimously agreed that it was an excellent choice. Throughout our dining experience, the staff proved to be nothing short of exceptional, providing attentive and wonderful service. Additionally, the location of the restaurant was excellent, adding to the overall experience.

Without a doubt, this was the pinnacle of our culinary ventures in New Orleans.
