input:
My girlfriends and I ate at the Creole House for dinner. Our decision to dine here was largely based on the fact that it was pouring raining and this restaurant is next door to our hotel. We started with the bacon garlic oysters and jumbo buffalo wings. The bacon garlic oysters were average, at best. The oysters were overpowered by the cheese and bacon, which was disappointing. The buffalo wings were pretty good and seasoned well. For entrees, we ordered: 1) jumbalaya pasta, 2) blackened red fish and 3) canal street red fish. The jumbalaya pasta lacked flavor and was our least favorite (would not order again). The blackened red fish was just okay and the skimpy side of sautéed veggies (spinach, tomatoes, mushrooms) were VERY salty (would order again as a LAST resort). The canal street red fish wasn't great but my friend would order it again. Her biggest complaint was that it had very little garlic sauce. We also ordered paddle boat drinks, which tasted good but were more juice vs alcohol (had to order an extra shot).

So, overall, we were underwhelmed with the food, making it a solid 3 stars. On a positive note, our server, Alexander, was great...very hospitable and tried his best to make sure we were satisfied.
Revise this with your best effort:
My girlfriends and I decided to have dinner at the Creole House, primarily because of its convenient location next to our hotel and the heavy rain outside. To kick off our meal, we opted for the bacon garlic oysters and jumbo buffalo wings. Unfortunately, the bacon garlic oysters didn't meet our expectations as the flavors of the cheese and bacon overwhelmed the oysters. On the other hand, the buffalo wings were quite enjoyable with their well-balanced seasoning.

For our main courses, we selected the jumbalaya pasta, blackened red fish, and canal street red fish. Regrettably, the jumbalaya pasta lacked flavor and ended up being our least favorite dish, prompting us to not consider ordering it again. While the blackened red fish was decent, the accompanying sautéed veggies (spinach, tomatoes, mushrooms) were excessively salty, leaving us hesitant to order it in the future unless absolutely necessary. On a more positive note, my friend did find the canal street red fish to be acceptable, despite its minor flaw of lacking sufficient garlic sauce.

Additionally, we indulged in paddle boat drinks which were flavorful, but we found them to be more juice than alcohol. We even had to request an extra shot to enhance the overall experience.

Overall, we were left underwhelmed by the food, ultimately awarding the experience a solid three stars. On a brighter note, our server, Alexander, was exceptional, showing great hospitality and making every effort to ensure our satisfaction.

input:
Okay, don't jump on me for this, but its partially my fault because I held them to such high expectations (due to the hype and anticipation of them opening up here) before actually eating at this location. I read so much about it on Facebook and the likes......so reading and seeing the yummy pics; well I just knew it would be all that.....untill yesterday.....

Me and my bf Vince went to BlackFinn for Sunday lunch yesterday. The atmosphere was cool and it was really nice inside. The staff was pleasant as well, so I'm thinking "hum...I like...". We ordered  a couple of mojitos and we also had another drink, which was okay.  Time to order; I ordered the Cuban sandwich, hold the mustard, and add mayo instead....with Black Finn fries and my bf ordered the Prime Rib sandwich with au jus and the same fries.  We got our order, which took a bit of time but it was okay. Everything looked so yummy and I knew they were going to meet my expectations. Now mind ya, my bf put off going to BlackFinn since they day they opened and I've been on him to go here. So anyway, the fries were a bit salty, but good. I had a choice of two dipping sauces, which I believe were ranch and barbeque. Delicious! I bit into the sandwich and what did I taste? A mouth full of mustard!!! Eeewww!! Okay, did I not say "hold the mustard"? So lo and behold, my food had to be returned while my bf ate his food. His beef about his sandwich (no pun intended) was that there was more bread than meat. I looked at it and I noticed the same thing. Also, the au jus was a bit low as well and wasn't enough for the sandwich.  So I'm like the little old lady from the back-in-the-day commercials saying "Where's the beef?" LOL. Wow! 

Finally, after he finishes his sandwich, my food finally comes out and guess what? They left the swiss cheese off the sandwich. WTF! Okay, so at this point I'm like "forget it, just take it back." How many times must I send my sandwich back to get it right? Now I must say that the manager on duty was accommodating and she took care of the check and apolgized for the errors. So for her professionalism and the fact that the staff was very polite, I give them two stars. Will I go back....yes I will give them another chance to redeem themselves, but all in my ear is my bf saying that there must have been a reason why he hesitated to come here and this is why.  Oh well......
Revise this with your best effort:
Please refrain from criticizing me, but I must admit that I hold partial responsibility for my disappointing experience at this establishment. The excessive hype and anticipation, fueled by the constant buzz on Facebook and other platforms, led me to set high expectations before actually dining at this location. Despite this, yesterday's visit to BlackFinn with my boyfriend, Vince, for Sunday lunch fell short of our hopes.

Upon arrival, I admired the trendy atmosphere and inviting interior. The staff members were pleasant, adding a positive element to the initial impression. Feeling optimistic, I ordered a couple of mojitos, along with another drink that was satisfactory. As we started to place our food order, I specified that I wanted a Cuban sandwich without mustard, replacing it with mayo, accompanied by Black Finn fries. Vince opted for the Prime Rib sandwich with au jus and the same fries. Although our order took longer than expected, it was acceptable given the circumstances.

The sight of our plates filled with delectable dishes increased my anticipation, confident that they would surpass my expectations. However, when I tasted my sandwich, to my dismay, my mouth was flooded with an overwhelming taste of mustard. I had explicitly requested for it to be omitted, so this oversight was disheartening. Consequently, my sandwich had to be sent back, leaving me to watch Vince enjoy his meal. He expressed his dissatisfaction as well, stating that his sandwich had an unequal distribution of meat and bread. Observing his plate, I could not help but notice the same imbalance. Additionally, the au jus provided with his sandwich was lacking, insufficient for a proper dipping experience. At that moment, I couldn't help but humorously quote the famous catchphrase, "Where's the beef?" from the commercials of yesteryear.

Eventually, after Vince completed his sandwich, my corrected order finally arrived. However, it had a glaring omission: the Swiss cheese. Frustrated and disheartened, I decided to forgo consuming it altogether. How many times must I send back my sandwich to receive the correct version? Despite this series of disappointments, I must acknowledge the accommodating nature of the manager on duty. She rectified the situation, compensating us and extending her apologies for the errors. Thus, I award this establishment two stars due to her professionalism and the overall politeness of the staff.

Will I give them another chance to redeem themselves? Yes, I will, despite the doubts voiced by Vince. He insists that his initial hesitation to visit this place was justified by our experience today. Regardless, I believe in granting second chances, even though his words continue to echo in my ears.

input:
I have to start out by saying, why do those who like hookah not know about this place?! It was such a wonderful experience! Please hear me out!

My mission on this review is to get the word out! A friend and I went spur of the moment and I'm glad we did. From the outside of the building you wouldn't know it was a hookah bar (except the giant sign of course lol). The moment you open that giant wooden door, the decor and paint color gives it that authentic look. Warm yellow paint with evil eyes and giant metal wall lamps with cutouts shining red surrounding all the walls.
When you go up a few steps there's a gift shop, a table, and the register. They ask you to take a seat upstairs and they follow you shortly after. (There's even another upstairs that I barely peaked at).
This is the amazing part: cushions on the floor with giant metal mandala tables!!!! It was so authentic I could barely handle my excitement. They have a menu with drinks, food and hookah. Water was only a dollar which was amazing because hookah bars are usually pretty pricy.
We smoked "sex on the beach" flavored shisha. It was smooth! Very smooth! We even brought bubbles for the trip to have a little fun :)
What I like about this place compared to other loud hookah bars is that it wasn't even close to being hectic. I felt like I should have whispered at first, but after awhile I was more comfortable. Only one other couple was there and they were very nice to talk to as well. The older man and the young guy was extremely nice. The younger dude checked in on us and was sociable which was really kinda nice but not overbearing. 

If you want a low key, quiet and chill hookah bar, this should be at the top of people's lists.
Revise this with your best effort:
I must begin by questioning why those who are fond of hookah are not aware of this incredible place. It truly surpassed all expectations and I implore you to hear me out!

My primary goal with this review is to spread the word about this hidden gem. A whimsical friend and I decided to visit on a spontaneous whim, and boy, are we glad we did. From the exterior, you would never suspect that it housed a fantastic hookah bar (apart from the conspicuous giant sign, of course). But the moment we pushed open that grand wooden door, the ambiance and color scheme transported us to an authentic realm. The walls were painted with a lovely warm yellow hue adorned with evil eye motifs, and enormous metal wall lamps with intricate cutouts emitted a mesmerizing red glow, enveloping the space.

After climbing a few steps, we encountered a small gift shop, a charming table, and the welcoming register. We were promptly directed to take a seat upstairs, and they soon followed suit. (I must admit, I was too enthralled to properly explore the additional upstairs area).

And now, let me divulge the most remarkable part of our experience: the seating area featured plush floor cushions and colossal metal mandala tables! It was a visual feast of authenticity that left me positively giddy. Their menu boasted an array of beverages, delectable fare, and, of course, hookah. Notably, I was astounded by the reasonable one-dollar price tag on water, as hookah bars tend to be rather lavish in their pricing.

We indulged in the "sex on the beach" flavored shisha, which proved to be an exceptionally smooth and enjoyable smoke. To add an extra element of whimsy, we had brought along bubbles for a playful touch.

One aspect that sets this place apart from the typical bustling hookah bars is its tranquil ambiance. It was so peaceful that I initially felt compelled to whisper, but as time went on, I relaxed and felt more at ease. Only one other couple occupied the space, and they were a delightful pair with whom we struck up a pleasant conversation. The elder gentleman and the younger fellow were incredibly kind, with the younger gentleman periodically checking in on us without being intrusive.

For those seeking a low-key, serene, and utterly chill hookah bar experience, this establishment should undoubtedly top their list.

input:

input:
hmm deep fried balls. This was my first venture with takoyaki and I love Japanese food of any kind, so needless to say I was excited. I ordered the original and was served 6 deep fried balls of goodness. They were tasty, albeit doughy, but left a greasy aching not so fresh feeling. I needed to be drunk to really appreciate the grease. Since it was my first venture I'll say its worth a try, but buyer beware they're super heavy for being small balls of dough. 

The curry chicken I had was a bit disappointing. I scarfed it down thanks to my near state of starvation, but found the roux too rich for my taste. Its worth another trip for japanese fast food- one of my faves and sorely lacking in the city, but its certainly not the best I've had...
Revise this with your best effort:
After hearing rave reviews about deep fried takoyaki balls, I couldn't resist trying them for myself, being a lover of all things Japanese cuisine. With excitement running through my veins, I eagerly ordered the original option and was presented with a plateful of six delectable deep fried balls of goodness. Each bite was undeniably flavorful, although slightly doughy. However, along with the indulgent taste came an unpleasant greasiness that left me feeling less than fresh. It became apparent that to truly savor the grease-laden dish, I needed to be in an intoxicated state. Considering it was my first foray into takoyaki, I believe it warrants a chance, yet caution should be exercised as these small balls of dough can weigh heavily on the stomach.

As for the curry chicken, unfortunately, it proved to be a letdown. With my hunger reaching near-starvation levels, I hastily consumed it, only to find the roux overpoweringly rich for my palate. Despite this disappointment, I am willing to give this establishment another chance, as it offers a convenient option for Japanese fast food, a cuisine I hold dear and which seems to be lacking in the city. However, it falls short of the best Japanese fast food I have experienced thus far.

input:
3.50 stars.  

Gabby's wasn't open.  I knew that.  Neither was Rotier's.  But my handy Yelp app had assured me that Fido's was open.  Imagine the disappointment when I realized there was a very real possibility that no burgers would happen on this trip down to the Deep South.  Would I really have to wait two more weeks when I would find solace in East Texas?   

"We can try Burger up," I mentioned.  

"Why don't you just call them?" hissed the appropriately nicknamed Viper.  

True.  We didn't have to keep driving around aimlessly.  So I call Burger Up, and a very pleasant, sweet voice assures me they are indeed open.  

Viper: "What was her name?  She sounded hot."
  
Me: "Paige."

Viper: "Yeah, she's definitely hot.  Have you ever met an unattractive Paige?"

Me: "Good point.  At least we have that going for us."

Paige was indeed attractive, but this review isn't about a photogenic individual who happens to work at Burger Up.  It's about what ended up being a visit to our fourth choice for burgers in Nashville.  

Burger Up follows a national trend towards upscale burgers.  My particular order consisted of a medium rare patty served with aged cheddar, Benton's bacon (very good), and ketchup served on an artisan bun.  Basically, it was a gussied up bacon cheeseburger, but it was a rather tasty one.  My major complaint is that I wish the actual meat itself exhibited more flavor.  Having said that, the burger was cooked properly and the flavors worked well together.  I ordered some wilted spinach on the side (mediocre) and truffle fries.  Let's talk about those truffle fries for a bit.  I know more people are apparently into the sweet potato fries here, but I think they are missing the boat.  Burger Up's truffle tries have pleasant aroma, taste great, and are the perfect texture for soaking up oil.  If you are on a diet, it is true you should skip these delightful fries.  But if that were the case, why are you at a burger joint in the first place?  Seriously, if you get nothing else out of my review, please do yourself a favor and order the truffle fries.  

Burger Up also boast an interesting beer menu with semi-obscure breweries from the Deep South included in the list.  I tried a pecan-infused amber from Mississippi - not bad.  I could imagine Burger Up could be a decent place to drink for a bit after eating.  

If I attended Vanderbilt, I would probably go here on a moderately frequent basis.  If you want a change from the dive bar hamburger, Burger Up is a decent change of pace.
Revise this with your best effort:
Rating: 3.50 stars

Unfortunately, Gabby's and Rotier's were both closed, leaving us disappointed and uncertain if we would be able to satisfy our burger cravings during our trip to the Deep South. However, after consulting Yelp, we discovered that Fido's was open. Relieved, we decided to give Burger Up a try.

Before heading out, Viper suggested calling ahead to avoid aimlessly driving around. I dialed Burger Up and was greeted by a pleasant and sweet voice confirming that they were indeed open. Viper, ever the charmer, inquired about the name of the woman on the phone, deeming a girl named Paige to be attractive. We joked about the likelihood of an unattractive Paige, but ultimately, our purpose was to review the food.

Burger Up aligns with the national trend of upscale burgers. My order consisted of a medium rare patty topped with aged cheddar, delicious Benton's bacon, and ketchup served on a delightful artisan bun. Essentially, it was an elevated bacon cheeseburger, and it delivered in terms of taste. My only gripe is that I wished the actual meat had more flavor. Nevertheless, the burger was cooked to perfection, and the flavors harmonized well. As a side, I opted for wilted spinach (average) and the star of the show – truffle fries. Let's take a moment to appreciate these fries. While many people might prefer the sweet potato fries here, I believe they are truly missing out. Burger Up's truffle fries have an enticing aroma, fantastic taste, and an ideal texture for soaking up oil. Admittedly, they are not for the health-conscious, but if you're at a burger joint, who cares about a diet? Seriously, if there's one thing you take from my review, make sure to indulge in the truffle fries.

Burger Up also offers an interesting selection of beers, including some from lesser-known breweries in the Deep South. I decided to try a pecan-infused amber from Mississippi, and it didn't disappoint. I can imagine Burger Up being a decent spot to unwind and have a few drinks after your meal.

If I were a student at Vanderbilt, Burger Up would likely become a regular haunt. For those seeking a departure from dive-bar hamburgers, Burger Up provides a refreshing change of pace.

input:
I went to my first BarreAmped class at the Music Row location (I've also been to bounce class - on a trampoline - at the Nations location), and it was a great class: definitely a better workout and a better experience than some of the barre classes I've taken in town since moving to Nashville in July. Had a very family vibe - everyone knew each other in my class except for me (a Class Pass-er trying it out for the first time). Great instructor - very hands on. 

The room is TINY, but luckily there were only six or seven of us in the class (it was a random class in the middle of the day on a weekday). The room is oddly shaped and very small, so if the class was full, I'm sure I would have been hitting everyone else with my arms and legs every 30 seconds. Another frustrating thing? BarreAmped is located within a house on 16th that is also a gym. The building does not say BarreAmped on it! No sign at all! It was my first time coming to this location, and I drove right past it and had to circle around to find it. Then, when I walked inside, no one was at the welcome desk, so I wasn't even sure I was in the right building! Finally someone came in (looked like something using the gym rather than working there), and she told me the BarreAmped room was the up the stairs. A bit confusing. I wish that information had been on Class Pass and that they had a sign on the building.

Still it was a great class, and I think I'd go again!
Revise this with your best effort:
I attended my first BarreAmped class at the Music Row location, and it exceeded my expectations. Compared to other barre classes I've tried in Nashville since moving here in July, it was a superior workout and overall experience. The class had a wonderful family-like atmosphere, with everyone in my class seemed to know each other except for me, as I was just giving it a try through Class Pass.

While the room was quite small and oddly shaped, fortunately, there were only six or seven of us in the class I attended (which happened to be a random one in the middle of a weekday). I can only imagine how cramped it would have been with a full class, as I would likely have been accidentally hitting others with my arms and legs every 30 seconds. Another frustrating aspect was that BarreAmped is located within a house on 16th Street, which is also a gym, but there was no signage indicating this. On my first visit, I actually drove right past it and had to circle around to find the place. Furthermore, upon entering, there was no one at the welcome desk, making me unsure if I was in the correct building. Only when someone who appeared to be using the gym rather than working there arrived did I learn that the BarreAmped room was upstairs. This lack of clarity could easily be resolved by providing such information on Class Pass and by having a visible sign on the building.

Despite these minor inconveniences, I genuinely enjoyed the class and would definitely consider attending again.

Revise this with your best effort: The delivery service was extremely disappointing, as my food order arrived an hour later than initially promised. To make matters worse, upon receiving the order, I discovered that it was incorrect. The biggest letdown, however, was the quality of the food itself. It was evident that all the dishes were either undercooked or overcooked, which left me thoroughly dissatisfied. I can confidently say that I will never be ordering from them again. Needless to say, my experience was quite disheartening.

input: Great spot to come to if your in Nashville. The have one the best drink deals you can find on thursdays and Saturday's and Sunday's. Food is okay.
Revise this with your best effort: If you find yourself in Nashville, this is an excellent place to visit. They offer some of the best drink deals you can find, particularly on Thursdays, Saturdays, and Sundays. The food is decent.

input: I like their salads, tea, and french fries! The servers were great...I've been here a few times and I'd come back!
Revise this with your best effort: I absolutely love their salads, tea, and french fries! The servers here are exceptional, providing excellent service every time I visit. I have frequented this place several times and without a doubt, I would gladly return again!

input: This was a great place to have brunch with the family. It is very clean and the staff were great. I love the decor!! Plus, my four year old actually ate here!!! That is a HUGE deal. He doesn't like anything.
Revise this with your best effort: I had an absolutely fantastic experience having brunch with my family at this wonderful place. From the moment we stepped in, it was evident how immaculately clean the establishment was, and the staff members were truly remarkable, providing exceptional service. The decor was simply fantastic, adding an extra charm to the overall ambiance. What truly amazed me was that even my notoriously picky four-year-old actually enjoyed eating here! This is an extraordinary achievement considering his usual aversion to trying new food.

input: Very cute place with a great selection of loose leaf teas and other tea paraphernalia. The drinks and sweets are delicious and creative. Great relaxing ambience. As a tea lover, I loved reading the books about tea that the owner had. The owner is very nice and is very knowledgeable and passionate about tea. I would love to come back again!
Revise this with your best effort: This charming establishment offers an abundance of adorable charm, accompanied by a superb assortment of loose leaf teas and an assortment of tea-related accessories. Indulging in their delectable and inventive beverages and sweets is an absolute delight. The ambiance is wonderfully serene, making for a truly relaxing experience. As a devoted tea enthusiast, I thoroughly enjoyed perusing the owner's collection of tea literature, which further heightened my appreciation for the art of tea. The proprietor is not only exceptionally amiable, but also incredibly well-informed and zealous about all things tea-related. Needless to say, my desire to revisit this remarkable place is undeniably strong!

input: Great food and service. The antipasto was by far the best that I have ever had.  The pasta is all fresh and full of flavor. The Fisherman's stew was loaded with great tender fish in a saffron sauce.
Revise this with your best effort: The dining experience was exceptional, with outstanding food and impeccable service. The antipasto surpassed all expectations, easily claiming the title of the best I have ever had. The pasta dishes were a true delight, boasting an abundance of fresh ingredients and bursting with delectable flavors. The Fisherman's stew, generously filled with tender fish, immersed in a tantalizing saffron sauce, was an absolute highlight of the meal.

input: Muriel's is a great stop in NOLA. The goat cheese and shrimp crepes are by far the best food I ate in the city (perhaps anywhere ever) and the rest of the meal lived up to the appetizer. Service is great, venue is quintessential French Quarter. It's a little distracting to see ghost tours outside the window at dinner- but the food is so delicious, you won't mind the audience. Rumor has it that Muriel's is haunted, but the only thing other worldly I encountered was the cuisine.
Revise this with your best effort: Muriel's in NOLA is a true gem. Their goat cheese and shrimp crepes are, without a doubt, the most exceptional dish I have ever tasted in the city (and quite possibly anywhere else). Yet, the excellence doesn't end there; the entire meal effortlessly lives up to the outstanding appetizer. The service provided is top-notch, and the ambiance of the venue perfectly embodies the essence of the French Quarter. Although the presence of ghost tours outside the window during dinner may be slightly distracting, the delectable food is so incredibly satisfying that any audience becomes negligible. While rumors circulate about Muriel's being haunted, I can assure you that the only otherworldly experience you'll encounter here is the extraordinary cuisine.

input: Went to this Taco Bell last night.  It was 1 30 and it said 30 minutes to close.  All the lights were on.  We backed up and forward twice and no one would wait on us.  We gave up and pulled up young man was at window closing  register.  Taco Bell was happy to serve us.
Revise this with your best effort: Last night, I visited this particular Taco Bell location. It was around 1:30 in the morning, and the sign displayed that they would close in 30 minutes. To my surprise, all the lights were still on inside the restaurant. We attempted to maneuver our car in the drive-thru line twice, but unfortunately, no one seemed to notice or attend to us. Feeling discouraged, we decided to abandon our attempt and started to drive away. Just as we were about to leave, a young man appeared at the window, closing the register. Surprisingly, Taco Bell was more than willing to finally serve us.

input: Cute place to eat at. Ate breakfast here and was dissappointed after seeing such good reviews. Breakfast menu is very limited. The omlet was just OK.  Biscuit didnt have much flavor to it. We were able to be seated really quick (during the week) but i imagine it getting really crowded during the weekends.
Revise this with your best effort: This adorable eatery seemed promising, but my experience with breakfast left me feeling disappointed despite the glowing reviews. I was disheartened by the limited breakfast menu options. The omelet I ordered was fairly average, failing to impress. The biscuit lacked the desired flavor that I had anticipated. On a positive note, we were promptly seated (owing to the weekday visit), although I can envision this place getting quite crowded during weekends.

input:
Probably the most expensive game in town. But totally worth it for me. I upgraded myself to the executive locker rooms because that gives me zero excuses for why I can't go to the gym before work or after if I am going out later that night. I always have my makeup, hair stuff, etc in my locker. Just getting back to the gym after a long absence due to health issues so I'm taking it slow. I've seen one or two machines that are not quite working right but the facility as a whole is pretty sharp & welcoming. You have tons of options of what to do classes wise, equipment wise...
My only 2 down sides are that I wish they were open a little later on weekends, but that's just me moving slowly on my time off. I wish there was a bit more ritation with the class schedule. There are classes I'd like to take but they always run mid day, never really early, after work or weekends. So no option to try them. I'm sure it's an instructor issue so not likely something that will change. Overall I'm super happy that I joined.
Revise this with your best effort:
Definitely the most luxurious and priciest game in town, but absolutely worth every penny for me. I recently upgraded myself to the exclusive executive locker rooms, eliminating any excuses for not hitting the gym before or after work, even when I have plans in the evening. These top-notch facilities come with a fully stocked locker for all my beauty and grooming essentials. 

After a long hiatus due to health problems, I'm gradually easing back into my workout routine, and although I've noticed a few machines that need attention, the overall condition of the facility is impressive and inviting. The range of classes and equipment available is extensive, giving me endless options to mix up my workouts.

My only two minor drawbacks are wishing for extended weekend hours, but that's purely due to my leisurely pace on my days off. Additionally, I find myself slightly frustrated with the class schedule as some desirable classes are scheduled during mid-day hours, never really early mornings, evenings, or weekends. Unfortunately, it seems to be an issue with the instructors and unlikely to change anytime soon. Despite these minor gripes, I am incredibly content with my decision to join this gym.

input:
A++ 
I have to say, this place is great and one of the biggest reasons why is their bar staff. There is a bartender named "Ally". She is always kind and attentive. Everyone can be crammed at the bar, and the employees running around like their hair is on fire, and Ally still treats you like you're her only customer. 
Cool vibe, great indoor and outdoor seating. Great addition to the Funk Zone.
Definitely go!!
PS: Say hi to Ally for me :-)
Revise this with your best effort:
I must say, this establishment is absolutely fantastic, and one of the key reasons for its greatness is the exceptional bar staff. In particular, there is a remarkable bartender named "Ally" who never fails to impress. She consistently exudes kindness and attentiveness, even when the bar is bustling with patrons and the employees are scurrying around in a frenzy. Ally manages to make you feel like the most valued customer, even in the midst of chaos.

Moreover, the ambiance of this place is undeniably cool, boasting both indoor and outdoor seating options. The addition of this establishment to the vibrant Funk Zone only adds to its allure. It is undoubtedly worth a visit!

P.S. Please convey my warm greetings to Ally.

input: Not to bad. I sat at the bar and the bartender was awesome. The lunch menu here is very decent and the beer is ice cold.  I usually come during lunch when it isn't to congested. So, to get consistent service,  go when it isn't to congested. I will definitely go back?
Revise this with your best effort: Not too bad at all. I took a seat at the bar and was pleasantly surprised by the bartender's awesomeness. The lunch menu offered here is quite decent, and the beer is served perfectly chilled. Normally, I prefer coming here for lunch when it's not too crowded. To ensure consistent service, I would recommend visiting during less busy hours. Without a doubt, I will certainly be returning.

input: The only knock on this place is that they didn't have all the pools open during Memorial Day weekend. Other than that the hotel provides a very friendly environment that's good for adults and families as well plenty of places to eat inside the resort and the atrium was amazing and really fun to explore. Little far from town but a good middle point between music row and the airport. Hotel staff was top notch and the place was clean while still having that old charm. I'd stay here again in a heart beat next time I visit Nashville.
Revise this with your best effort: The only drawback to this establishment is the fact that not all of the pools were open during Memorial Day weekend. However, apart from that, the hotel offers a remarkably welcoming atmosphere that caters to both adults and families. Moreover, it boasts an abundance of dining options within the resort premises. The atrium is particularly noteworthy, as it exudes an incredible ambiance and provides enjoyable exploration opportunities. Although it is a little distant from the city center, it serves as a convenient midpoint between music row and the airport. The hotel staff is exceptional and the cleanliness is maintained without compromising its old-world charm. Without hesitation, I would choose to stay here again on my next trip to Nashville.

input:
Great treat to beat the heat! I stopped in during the Manayunk Arts Festival yesterday to get a cold refreshing treat and I was very pleased with the service and the quality of the fresh frozen yogurt and toppings.

It is a self service fro-yo establishment with countless options of flavors and toppings. I enjoyed the toasted coconut yogurt and topped it with rainbow sprinkles, fresh strawberries, blueberries and raspberries. The fruit was very refreshing but it was hard to select what to put on it because everything looked so yummy. If you are a chocolate lover there are plenty of candy toppings to add to your fro-yo too. 

If you are not sure what flavor you will enjoy best you can sample them with small paper cups that so you don't have to find out if you like the flavor or not after you already purchase! 

Another plus is that the establishment is kept very clean and it still looks as new as it did when it first opening on Main Street just a couple of years ago!
Revise this with your best effort:
Stay cool and indulge in the ultimate summer treat! I made a pit stop at the Manayunk Arts Festival yesterday and stumbled upon a delightful fro-yo haven. The service was top-notch, and the quality of their fresh, frozen yogurt and toppings exceeded my expectations.

This self-service fro-yo joint boasts an impressive array of flavors and toppings. After much contemplation, I settled on the delectable toasted coconut yogurt, complemented by a medley of vibrant rainbow sprinkles, luscious strawberries, juicy blueberries, and tangy raspberries. The fruit added a refreshing burst to the already irresistible concoction. However, the real challenge was choosing amidst the tempting selection of candy toppings, especially if you're a chocolate aficionado.

One thing that truly impressed me was the opportunity to sample the flavors before committing. No more regrets after blindly purchasing! The establishment provides small paper cups for you to explore and decide which flavor will tickle your taste buds.

Moreover, I couldn't help but notice the impeccable cleanliness of the place. Despite having been open for only a few years on Main Street, it still looks as pristine and inviting as ever.

input: I think the trendiness of this chain, in general, has sort of faded and what you have left is the basis of this chain, which is over-priced food of a questionable quality. I wouldn't call it bad, but it's a whole lot of fried food and most of the breadings, whether it's fried pickles or okra or calamari or shrimp, are the same across all of that. The batter is fine, but it gets wearing. The coconut shrimp and hush puppies were definitely overcooked, which was kind of disappointing. Coke Zero on tap, but the mix could be better. For the price, it is also worth nothing there is a ton of food here, definitely quantity over quality. Décor is pretty cool and this is parked right along the Boise river, though it's a bit tucked away and has to be more or less sought out...probably worth hitting at least once, but there are far better local places that are more worthy of attention.
Revise this with your best effort: In my opinion, the previously trendy appeal of this chain has noticeably diminished, leaving behind an establishment characterized by excessively priced food of dubious quality. I wouldn't go as far as labeling it as outright bad, but the menu primarily consists of a plethora of fried dishes, all of which share a similar breading. While the batter itself is satisfactory, its repetitiveness can become tiresome. The coconut shrimp and hush puppies were particularly disappointing as they were clearly overcooked. Although they have Coke Zero on tap, the overall beverage selection could use improvement. It's important to mention that the portions here are generous for the price, prioritizing quantity over quality. The decor is quite pleasant, and the restaurant's location by the Boise river adds to its appeal, although it may require a bit of effort to find. It might be worth visiting at least once, but there are undoubtedly superior local establishments that deserve more attention.

input:
There are bars you can still smoke in?! Yuck. Sorry smokers (I used to be one so I get it) but yuck. The stink of smoke in my hair woke me up in the middle of the night after stopping in here and was so bad I had to get up to wash it before I could get back to sleep. That's not good.

Definitely a dive, this bar is very dim and smokey. The bartender was friendly and came to take my order as soon as I walked up to the bar. The bloody mary I ordered wasn't that great or strong, though.  That's not good either.
Revise this with your best effort:
Are you still allowed to smoke in some bars? Disgusting. I apologize to smokers, as I used to be one, but it's truly revolting. The lingering smell of smoke in my hair abruptly woke me up in the middle of the night after visiting this place, and it was so intolerable that I had to wash it before I could even think of going back to sleep. That is absolutely unpleasant.

This bar can definitely be classified as a dive. It boasts an ambiance characterized by dimness and a cloud of smoke. The bartender, at least, was amiable and promptly attended to me as soon as I approached the counter. However, the bloody mary I ordered failed to impress me with its taste and potency. That too is a disappointing aspect of my experience.

input: Got there mid-morning today, the early rush was over. Two tables were full, each with three people. The family in one of the tables had just walked in ahead of me, so they were being attended to first. Still, I was immediately welcomed, and in a couple of minutes a friendly lady brought the breakfast menu and asked if I wanted coffee. A cup appeared a few moments later, and was kept full throughout my visit. Radio playing golden oldies from the 70s, my kind of music. The ham omelet with home fries and toast arrive a few minutes later, worth waiting for. Done just right and kept me filled for hours. A friendly family restaurant where you feel welcome and appreciated, just north of Gulfport.
Revise this with your best effort:
I arrived at the restaurant mid-morning today, luckily missing the early rush. As I glanced around, I noticed that two tables were already occupied, each with three individuals. The family at one of the tables had just walked in before me, so they were being attended to first. Nonetheless, I received a warm welcome immediately upon entering. Within a couple of minutes, a friendly lady approached me with a breakfast menu in hand, offering to serve me some coffee. Moments later, a steaming cup of coffee appeared before me and remained plentiful throughout my entire visit.

As I settled into my seat, I couldn't help but notice the nostalgic sound of golden oldies from the 70s playing softly on the radio. It was like they knew my taste in music. After a brief wait, my ham omelet with home fries and toast arrived, and let me tell you, it was well worth the anticipation. The omelet was cooked to perfection, and the home fries and toast complemented it wonderfully. My hunger was thoroughly satisfied, leaving me feeling full for hours.

What truly sets this place apart is the friendly and welcoming atmosphere. It truly feels like a family restaurant where every guest is valued and appreciated. Located just north of Gulfport, it's a hidden gem that you won't want to miss.

input: This place is so lovely. It has everything!! Amazing wine selection, hookah's, Lebanese food which I think is the best in the city.
Revise this with your best effort: This place is absolutely delightful! It boasts an incredible array of amenities that cater to various preferences. The wine selection is truly remarkable, offering a wide range of options to satisfy even the most discerning connoisseurs. Additionally, the availability of hookah's adds an exotic touch, creating an ambiance of relaxation and enjoyment. However, the true highlight of this place is undeniably the Lebanese cuisine, which, in my opinion, surpasses any other in the entire city. The delectable flavors and authentic recipes transport you to the heart of Lebanon, leaving a lasting impression on your taste buds.

input: This was recommended by a colleague who is local in the area. A group of us from work decided to go and give it a try.  As soon as we sat down, Chris, took care of us.  He was patient, understanding and extremely knowledgeable of the menu.  Well, our entire party enjoyed every part of the evening while at Red Mess!  From the chips & salsa to the drinks to each of our entrees ... just absolutely DELICIOUS!
Revise this with your best effort: My colleague, who is a local in the area, highly recommended this place and a group of us from work decided to check it out. From the moment we sat down, Chris, our server, provided exceptional service. He was patient, understanding, and had extensive knowledge of the menu. Our entire party had an amazing evening at Red Mess! Every aspect, from the delectable chips & salsa, to the delightful drinks, and each of our mouthwatering entrees, was absolutely delicious.

input: This is my 3rd time and 3rd location at a Brick House across the country. This is by far one of the few chain restaurants I will regularly and happily eat at. The food is very unique and every selection is a good choice. This particular location I received better than average service. Will come back when back in town.
Revise this with your best effort: This is already my third visit to a Brick House location across the country, and I must say it continues to be one of the few chain restaurants where I am genuinely excited to dine at. The food here is exceptionally unique and every item on the menu is a guaranteed winner. During this particular visit, the service surpassed my expectations, exceeding the usual standard. I will definitely make it a point to return to this location whenever I find myself back in town.

input: So... This place is the sh*t. By far the classiest spot on the block, Siam is nudging STL standards up and up. The sashimi:  top grade. The outdoor patio: perfect to enjoy a beer/conversation off the dance floor. The music: something for everyone -- and the last couple nights I've been, the guest dj's we're KILLING some deep house grooves that rival NYC and Miami.  The best thing, though, may be the crowd: a solid mix that don't need labels, don't want pretense, just want a solid, quality night out.  F*ck yeah, Siam!
Revise this with your best effort: This place is absolutely amazing. Without a doubt, it is the most elegant establishment in the neighborhood, raising the standards of St. Louis. The sashimi here is of the highest grade, and the outdoor patio is the perfect setting for enjoying a refreshing drink and engaging in conversations away from the dance floor. The music selection caters to all tastes, and the guest DJs have been absolutely phenomenal, showcasing deep house grooves that can easily rival those in New York City and Miami. However, the standout feature has to be the diverse crowd that frequents this place. They are not concerned with labels or pretending to be something they are not; they simply desire an unforgettable and high-quality night out. Siam, you truly are exceptional!

input:
Worn down signs intrigue me.  I had biked passed 16th Street Seafood a ton of times, always wondering what was going on inside.  Now I know the answer, and the answer is- not much. At least in terms of decor. There is a gumball machine, 2 empty candy machines, plus a counter to order at and that's pretty much it. Also absent was the plethora of seafood over ice you would hope to see at a place specializing in seafood. There were some frozen crab cakes, breaded fish fillets, clams, and crabs- but not else. Still, I threw caution to the winds of Tasker Street and put in an order.

I didn't want to go for fried seafood, so the sandwiches and platters were out.

I got a large order of mussels in butter and garlic sauce ($9.50). Mussels are one of those things I like making at home, but it is way too hot for that right now. . My main complaint is that the order came with an unacceptable amount of closed shells - 9!   It was still a good sized order with a big piece of bread to dip in the unexpectedly spicy, broth. As the place is to-go only- they know how to wrap up messy seafood orders, nothing was spilled.

Remember when I said I didn't want anything fried, well that's not ever actually true. So I ended up sneaking in 2 fried shrimps. Not bad, but not worth $1.25 each.
Revise this with your best effort:
I am always intrigued by worn-down signs that catch my attention. For quite some time, I had pedaled past 16th Street Seafood, wondering what might be happening behind its doors. Finally, the opportunity to uncover the mystery presented itself, and to my disappointment, there wasn't much to see in terms of decor. The interior simply consisted of a gumball machine, two empty candy dispensers, and a modest ordering counter. Considering its specialization in seafood, one would expect an abundance of ice-covered delicacies. However, my hopes were dashed as I discovered a limited selection of frozen crab cakes, breaded fish fillets, clams, and crabs. Nevertheless, undeterred by this underwhelming sight, I boldly ventured forth and placed my order.

Preferring not to indulge in fried seafood, I immediately crossed off sandwiches and platters from my options. Instead, I opted for a generous portion of mussels in butter and garlic sauce, priced at $9.50. Typically, I relish preparing mussels in the comfort of my own home, but the scorching temperatures outside made it an undesirable endeavor. The only qualm I had with my order was the disappointingly high number of closed shells—nine in total. Nonetheless, the serving size remained substantial, complemented by a sizable piece of bread that perfectly complemented the unexpectedly fiery broth. As the establishment exclusively caters to takeaway orders, they demonstrated their expertise in packaging messy seafood without any spills or mishaps.

Now, earlier I may have claimed my aversion to fried seafood, but the truth is, such a sentiment can never be entirely accurate. Failing to resist the temptation, I surreptitiously added two fried shrimps to my order. They were decent, although not worth the steep price of $1.25 each.

input:
we had a groupon and so we went - great lobsters (although they were out of a few sizes this evening) but they were delicious and our waitress Jessica was very attending and nice - made some good suggestions.

not fancy but good lobster.
Revise this with your best effort: We took advantage of a Groupon deal and decided to give this place a try. Despite being slightly limited on lobster size options for the evening, we were pleasantly surprised by the exceptional taste of the lobsters we ordered. Our waitress, Jessica, provided excellent service with her attentive and friendly demeanor. She also offered some great recommendations that enhanced our dining experience. While the establishment may not have a fancy ambiance, the quality of their lobster is undeniably good.

input: Great little upscale but not overpriced cafe. Lots of options, but needs a lox bagel sandwich. :) One of my preferred places to lunch with someone.
Revise this with your best effort: This charming upscale cafe offers a delightful dining experience without breaking the bank. It boasts an extensive menu featuring a wide variety of choices that cater to all tastes. However, it would be even more perfect if it included a scrumptious lox bagel sandwich. Whether enjoying a leisurely lunch alone or in the company of a friend, this place never fails to impress and remains one of my top choices.

input:
Animo juice is the best find in Haddonfield (after the Hadrosaurus, of course!)

I stop at Animo every time I go to Jersey to visit my family; or do I visit my family every time I stop at Animo?  Debatable.

Animo started with juice.  Not frozen juices with sorbet & yogurt added.  Real juice.  

Their menu has expanded & they now call themselves "Animo Juice & Burrito Bar!"  The burrito menu features 10 burritos, all under $10, f my favorite the "Haight & Ashbury" is stuffed with rice, beans, meat/roasted veggies, cheese, lettuce, tomato, guacamole & sour cream.

Not that hungry, have a 'petito', a small version of the burrito, averaging $5.  Porky & Petunia - the name is as cute as the petito is yummy:  shredded lettuce, pulled pork & pineapple salsa.  

A breakfast petito & Animo MD juice destroy any hangover.  The MD is juiced greens, carrot, orange, apple, kiwi, banana & spirolina.   My BF loves the Chilly Palmer:  Acai, apple, banana, yogurt & flax seed.  

For a happy belly add or substitute the perfectly cooked quinoa to any dish.  The Border Salad is a perfect example: lettuce, guac, pico de gallo, cheese, tortilla chips, cilantro lime vin, & sub quinoa for meat.   

Fiber-full signature juices, frozen whipped bananas, sliced fresh wheat grass (cheaper than Jameson!) & yogurt/granola bowls!  

The city's juice bars have something to learn from Animo.
Revise this with your best effort:
Animo juice is the ultimate discovery in Haddonfield, surpassing even the renowned Hadrosaurus. Without fail, I make a beeline for Animo every time I visit my family in Jersey. Or perhaps it's the other way around - I visit my family as an excuse to indulge in Animo's delights. The foundation of Animo lies in their commitment to pure juice, without the inclusion of sorbet or yogurt. Their menu has evolved, earning them the title of "Animo Juice & Burrito Bar!" Adding to their repertoire, they now serve ten delectable burritos, all priced below $10. Personally, my top choice is the "Haight & Ashbury," a heavenly amalgamation of rice, beans, meat or roasted veggies, cheese, lettuce, tomato, guacamole, and sour cream.

For those with a smaller appetite, the 'petito' provides a miniature version of the burrito experience, coming in at a modest average price of $5. The adorable "Porky & Petunia" petito combines shredded lettuce, pulled pork, and pineapple salsa, tantalizing the taste buds with its delightful flavors. When faced with the aftermath of a night of revelry, a breakfast petito and Animo MD juice work wonders in banishing any lingering hangovers. The MD juice itself is an invigorating blend of juiced greens, carrot, orange, apple, kiwi, banana, and spirolina, while my significant other swears by the refreshing Chilly Palmer, comprising Acai, apple, banana, yogurt, and flaxseed.

To enhance satisfaction further, opt to add or replace any dish with their expertly cooked quinoa. The Border Salad stands as an exemplary choice, boasting lettuce, guacamole, pico de gallo, cheese, tortilla chips, a cilantro lime vinaigrette, and the option to substitute meat with quinoa. Additionally, Animo offers fiber-rich signature juices, frozen whipped bananas, sliced fresh wheatgrass (more affordable than a shot of Jameson!), and tantalizing yogurt and granola bowls. Truly, the city's juice bars have much to glean from Animo's pioneering approach.

input: Had a very memorable birthday in SB and was so happy to have Wine Edventures be my gift! Sean picked us up Saturday morning and was super friendly (funny, too). It was just my husband and I along with a group of 10 - who happened to be all guys, having a bachelor party! Haha, so that was pretty funny. We stopped at 3 wineries and 1 brewery. Sean explained where we were as we were driving around and also gave us lessons at the tastings. He provided us with bottled water and souvenir wine glasses. We had lunch at the 2nd vineyard of the day, which was very good - choice of sandwich and a pasta salad side with chips and a cookie (the cookies are awesome). It was a fun day and I'd highly recommend this adventure to anyone looking for a fun day in the SB area.
Revise this with your best effort: I had an incredibly memorable birthday celebration in Santa Barbara, made even more special by the amazing gift of Wine Edventures! Sean, our friendly and humorous driver, picked us up on a delightful Saturday morning. Joining us were my husband and a group of 10 guys who were having a bachelor party. It was quite amusing to have such a diverse group! Throughout the day, we visited three wineries and one brewery. Sean provided insightful commentary as we drove around, enhancing our experience. He also offered valuable lessons during the tasting sessions. To ensure our comfort, he even supplied us with bottled water and souvenir wine glasses. Our second vineyard stop served us an excellent lunch with a choice of sandwich, pasta salad, chips, and a scrumptious cookie. It was a fantastic day filled with laughter and enjoyment, and I wholeheartedly recommend this adventure to anyone seeking a fun-filled day in the Santa Barbara area.

input:
This is my favorite in Delaware.  The menu is simple and perfectly executed.  Rolls are reasonably priced, artfully made and are PACKED with fish!  I do believe they use flash-frozen sashimi grade fish, but the color, texture, taste and smell are perfect.  Easily the best spicy tuna I have ever had.  I think the secret is the kewpie mayo along w/ the right amount of sriracha and sichimi powder.  Frankly, I can't get enough of this place and have at times, eaten it every day for lunch for weeks.  I've gone as far as to pick it up for dinner AFTER having had it for lunch. Their introduction of short-grain brown sushi rice has been great!

The Sushiman, YC Park is amazing to watch.  I've seen him skin a cucumber with a sword-like sushi knife in no time flat, in a single ribbon and then continue to shave it into a nori thin sheet for his tuna naruto roll roll.  The temaki are as big as a carnival iced cream cone.  You can barely finish one of them, there is so much fish in there.  The nigiri are beautiful.  Uniform pieces of fresh fish, perfectly perched on the best sushi rice I've ever had (just the right amount of vinegar and sugar).

Skip the newly opened Kooma.  Save Mikimotos for a night out, but go to Tokyo for lunch!  The owners are lovely, so support them in this tough economy.  If you must eat sushi, eat it here!

Why not 5 stars?  I have to save it for places that serve the local fresh fish, plucked out of the water that morning.  Let me know if you find a place that does!
Revise this with your best effort:
This restaurant in Delaware is undeniably my favorite. Their menu is refreshingly simple yet flawlessly executed. The rolls they offer are reasonably priced, meticulously crafted, and most importantly, bursting with an abundance of delectable fish. Although I suspect they may utilize flash-frozen sashimi grade fish, the color, texture, taste, and aroma are simply impeccable. Their spicy tuna roll, in particular, stands out as the best I've ever had. I believe the secret lies in their skillful combination of kewpie mayo, precisely measured sriracha, and sichimi powder. Honestly, I cannot get enough of this place and have even found myself indulging in their sushi daily for weeks on end. On occasion, I've been tempted to return for dinner immediately after having it for lunch. Their recent introduction of short-grain brown sushi rice has been a delightful addition.

One of the highlights at this establishment is watching the incredible Sushiman, YC Park, in action. I've witnessed him effortlessly skin a cucumber with his sword-like sushi knife, transforming it into a single ribbon before expertly shaving it into a thin nori sheet for his tuna naruto roll. The temaki they serve here are colossal, rivaling the size of a carnival iced cream cone. The abundance of fish packed into each one makes it quite a challenge to finish. The nigiri pieces are a work of art, boasting uniform cuts of fresh fish carefully perched on the most extraordinary sushi rice I've ever tasted, perfectly balanced with just the right amount of vinegar and sugar.

While I suggest skipping the newly opened Kooma and reserving Mikimotos for a special night out, Tokyo is undoubtedly the place to go for a satisfying lunch. The owners of this establishment are delightful individuals, and in these trying economic times, it is crucial to support them. If you have a sushi craving, I implore you to indulge it here.

As for my rating, I reserve five stars for establishments that proudly serve locally sourced, freshly caught fish straight from the morning's catch. If you stumble upon such a place, please do let me know!

input: So I'm super confused as to why everyone rags on this place. They're super nice, quick, and cheap.  People have complained about their chicken fingers being dry but I have no clue what they're talking about. They're great and their honey mustard is delicious. I've had salads from there too and they give you lots of veggies which I love. Their fries are delish as well and I love that they give you cole slaw with the chicken finger platter. All and all, I love that this place is literally a few steps away from my apartment and that they have decent food. I also don't understand the greasy spoon comments... you do realize it's a pizza joint right? You aren't going there for the ambiance, more for the cheap food.
Revise this with your best effort: I am thoroughly perplexed as to why this place constantly receives criticism. In my personal experience, I have found the staff to be exceptionally friendly, service to be prompt, and prices to be reasonable. I cannot comprehend the complaints about their allegedly dry chicken fingers as they have consistently been delightful to me. Additionally, their honey mustard sauce is undeniably delicious. On occasions when I opted for salads, I was pleased to discover generous portions of fresh vegetables, which I thoroughly enjoy. Their fries are also quite tasty, complemented perfectly by the addition of coleslaw that accompanies the chicken finger platter. Overall, I am extremely grateful to have this establishment conveniently located just steps away from my apartment, providing me with decent food. Furthermore, I fail to comprehend the negative remarks labeling it as a "greasy spoon". It is essential to acknowledge that this is primarily a pizza joint, where one does not visit for the ambiance but rather for the affordability of their delectable offerings.

input: Great cheesesteak! Friendly and fast service. Lazo's really made my day.

input: Ambience OK, too bad stuck in a mall in New Hope.  They were very understaffed (which thankfully they kept apologizing for) so there service was definitely slow, however very very pleasant.  We definitely felt it was worth the wait!  Vegetable Samosas were delicious, chicken were slightly dry.  I ordered chicken tikka masala which was so flavorful and rich and my husband had the chicken tagine...amazing!  Has the feeling of a place where "you get what you get and you don't get upset" but when you get it, it is really out of this world!  Loved the mix of cuisines, just enough choices on the menu.  Restaurant is BYOB so we were unprepared, but we will be back!
Revise this with your best effort: The ambiance was alright, although it was unfortunate that we were stuck in a mall in New Hope. The establishment seemed to be understaffed, which they continuously apologized for, resulting in slow service. However, the staff was exceptionally pleasant, making the wait worthwhile. The Vegetable Samosas were delicious, but the chicken was slightly dry. My order of chicken tikka masala was bursting with flavor and richness, while my husband's choice of chicken tagine was simply amazing. The restaurant had a laid-back vibe where you take what you get and don't get upset, but what you receive is truly out of this world. We appreciated the variety of cuisines offered and found the menu to have just the right amount of choices. Unfortunately, we were unprepared for the restaurant being BYOB, but we will certainly be returning!

input: This is the cutest mom/pop local, high-quality ice cream joint in all of Tucson! Delicious... But definitely a bit pricey ($4.50 for a regular single scoop)- hence the 4 stars as opposed to 5.

input: Just found my new favorite place for pizza, didn't get any of the pizzas listed on the menu, built our own. Pepperoni, sliced red onions, roasted garlic. input: What a great place for breakfast!! Healthy options that are yummy, other options that LOOK yummy!! We love the atmosphere, service and food.

input: Great service and body work looked great.  They even vacuumed the inside.  Randy kept me up to date on the status through text so I knew what was going on with my car at all times.

input: I definitely won't be coming back here. Long story short, I scheduled an appointment online to have the transmission and differential fluid changed on my pilot. I arrived on time, and I was told it would take approximately 2 hours for completion, I also said I wanted an oil change, but " full synthetic". He said it would be $20 more, I said okay. When it was finally done and I was ready to check out, my advisor (Brandon) give me the total cost, which was double than what I expected and paid for in the past. I asked him what was all done, he said, "they completed a transmission flush instead of the regular drain and refill". I told him that's not what I wanted or asked for. He went on to say "it was good for the car and whatever", like I'm some kind of idiot. First of all Honda doesn't recommend doing a transmission flush and secondly, its almost triple what you would normally pay for a standard transmission fluid change. On top of that they didn't even do a full synthetic oil change it was just a blend. I didn't have time to argue with him because I was already late for an appointment, but I have the email showing what I originally asked for, so I'll be calling my bank soon.
Revise this with your best effort:
After this unfortunate experience, I have made the decision that I will not be returning to this establishment. To provide some context, I had made an appointment online to have the transmission and differential fluid changed on my pilot. Arriving on time for my appointment, I was informed that it would take approximately 2 hours to complete. Additionally, I requested an oil change, specifically stating that I wanted full synthetic oil. The service advisor informed me that there was an additional cost of $20 for the full synthetic oil, to which I agreed.

Once the work was completed and it was time to pay, I was shocked to hear the total cost from my advisor, Brandon. The amount was double what I had expected and paid for in the past. Sensing the issue, I inquired about the services that had been performed. To my surprise, Brandon explained that they had completed a transmission flush instead of the regular drain and refill that I had requested. This was not what I wanted or had asked for, and I expressed my dissatisfaction. I also mentioned that Honda does not recommend a transmission flush, further emphasizing my concern. Brandon responded dismissively, suggesting that it was beneficial for the car without providing any substantial explanation, making me feel disrespected and belittled.

Firstly, I am aware that Honda does not recommend a transmission flush, and secondly, the cost for this service was almost triple what one would typically pay for a standard transmission fluid change. To add to my disappointment, I discovered that the oil change performed was not even a full synthetic one, but rather a blend. Unfortunately, due to time constraints and an impending appointment, I did not have the opportunity to argue further with Brandon.

However, I do possess an email that clearly outlines my original request, providing evidence of the miscommunication. Given this situation, I will be contacting my bank to rectify the excessive charges.

input: We love, love M.L. Rose! I am a huge beer fan and the flights are so fun to choose and try. I love the neighborhood hangout feel, not too hipster, not too old....just right! We always have awesome service too. My hang up can be the food. Wings not quite crispy enough, burgers not cooked to taste, spinach artichoke dip just meh. The steak and Gouda was flat out gross - big fatty slab of undercooked steak on bread. We were told it is leaving the menu, but they should have removed it long ago. And no visit from the manager when the sandwich was returned, which was a little underwhelming. We will be back, we are big fans, but please get your kitchen together so I can have my fav burger in town cooked just right :-)
Revise this with your best effort:
We absolutely adore M.L. Rose! As a passionate beer enthusiast, I can't get enough of their delightful flights that offer a thrilling variety to choose from. What truly sets this place apart is its charming neighborhood atmosphere - not too pretentious, not too dated - just the perfect balance! Furthermore, we consistently receive exceptional service, which makes our visits even more enjoyable.

However, if I may express a small concern, it would be regarding the food. While the menu has much to offer, there are a few areas that could benefit from improvement. For instance, the wings tend to fall short of achieving the desired crispiness, and the burgers occasionally miss the mark in terms of cooking perfection. Additionally, the spinach artichoke dip, unfortunately, tends to be rather underwhelming.

Nevertheless, the real disappointment arose from the steak and Gouda sandwich, which was quite honestly unappetizing. It consisted of a large fatty slab of undercooked steak on bread, leaving much to be desired. Although we were informed that this particular dish would be removed from the menu soon, it seems it should have been done much earlier. Furthermore, when we returned the sandwich, it would have been nice to receive a visit from the manager, which unfortunately did not occur, leaving us somewhat underwhelmed.

Despite these minor setbacks, we remain loyal patrons and plan on returning in the future. However, we sincerely hope that the kitchen can address these issues, ensuring that I can enjoy my favorite burger in town cooked to perfection.

input:
We went on a non typical day, school year mid week, so we had the luxury of being only a handful of people there  Therefore, my review may not be representative of a typical visit. 
Arrived at opening and found the off season price within reason. Bathrooms and water park were immaculate. The lifeguards were attentive and friendly. 
A star was lost because I found the water and air temp to be a tad too cold. The park was smaller then other indoor water parks I've been to. Only two big slides, one group slide, a couple of younger kids areas, lazy river and a simulated surf area. They would periodically close the big slides in order to open the surf area, for lack of staffing. A minor annoyance since that is why we were there. 
I can see how people  would be upset paying more and sharing the park with hundreds of others. But I think if your timing is right, you could have an enjoyable afternoon.
We did save money by using our AAA card. Could have saved more as it was my sons birthday month, but I didn't have proof on me.
Revise this with your best effort:
We had the opportunity to visit the water park on a non typical day, in the middle of the school year, which meant there were only a few people there. It's important to note that my review may not reflect a typical visit due to this. Nevertheless, we arrived when the park opened and found the off season price reasonable. The cleanliness of the bathrooms and water park area was exceptional, and we appreciated the attentive and friendly lifeguards.

However, I deduct one star from my overall rating because I personally found the water and air temperature to be slightly chilly. Additionally, compared to other indoor water parks I have been to, this park seemed smaller in size. It only had two large slides, one group slide, a few areas designated for younger kids, a lazy river, and a simulated surf area. To my disappointment, they often closed the big slides in order to open the surf area due to insufficient staff, which was a minor inconvenience since that was the main reason we visited.

I can understand how some people might be disappointed if they paid more for their visit and had to share the park with hundreds of others. However, if your timing is right, you could have an enjoyable afternoon with fewer crowds.

On a positive note, we were able to save some money by using our AAA card. It would have been even more cost-effective if I had brought proof of my son's birthday month, but unfortunately, I had forgotten to bring it with me.
