input:
I normally wouldn't think Greek food for brunch or lunch; I'm way more of a traditional American-style brunch kind of guy.  But when my friends suggested to meet them here for brunch this past weekend, I trusted their better judgement.  In the end, I'm glad I did.  This cozy Center City spot not only serves an amazing (and dare I say, a contender for the best) brunch in Philly, the staff really make you feel at home.  They really know how to wow their patrons: fresh food, delightful presentation, and so many delicious sounding choices it's hard to choose which dish you want from their one page menu for mains.

Their specialty, and they're not shy to tell you, is the Cyprus Breakfast.  It's a mediterranean twist on the classic combination of eggs, meat, and starch.  The plate comes out with two sunny-side up eggs, fried in olive oil and garnished with fresh parsely.  It's served alongside a grilled slice of lounza (Greek ham), two pieces of salty, crisp fried halloumi, warm bread, and tomato, cucumber, and onion salad.  The menu also features a spread of other traditional Greek, Mediterranean, and Middle Eastern specialities: Avgolemono, Moussaka, Pastitsio, Shaksouka, and Malohwa to name a few.  They even serve Greek Coffee and Frappes!

The service may be a little over-attentive in an attempt to make you feel more than welcome, but it's much appreciated, especially when other restaurants fail to put as much effort into the service as they do the food.  One other tip: reservations are highly recommended, if not required.  Because of Kanella's small space, getting a table at brunch is nearly impossible if you're not on the list.  But if you can score seats here for brunch, then expect nothing less than a stellar way to start your weekend morning (or recover from last night's activities).  Can't wait to come back and try out the dinner menu.
Revise this with your best effort:
Normally, I wouldn't consider Greek food for brunch or lunch; I tend to lean towards the more traditional American-style brunch. However, when my friends suggested meeting at this place for brunch last weekend, I decided to trust their judgment. Ultimately, I'm really glad I did. This cozy spot in the heart of Center City not only serves an outstanding brunch (which even rivals the best in Philly), but the staff go above and beyond to make you feel right at home. They truly know how to impress their customers with their fresh and beautifully presented dishes, and the menu offers so many mouthwatering options that it's difficult to choose just one main course from their concise one-page menu.

Their specialty, the Cyprus Breakfast, is their pride and joy. It puts a Mediterranean spin on the traditional combination of eggs, meat, and starch. The plate arrives with two sunny-side up eggs, fried in olive oil and garnished with fragrant parsley. Accompanying the eggs is a grilled slice of lounza (Greek ham), two pieces of crispy fried halloumi, warm bread, and a refreshing tomato, cucumber, and onion salad. Additionally, the menu features an array of other traditional Greek, Mediterranean, and Middle Eastern delicacies such as Avgolemono, Moussaka, Pastitsio, Shaksouka, and Malohwa, just to name a few. To top it all off, they even serve authentic Greek coffee and Frappes!

The service can be a tad overly attentive, but I find it quite welcoming, especially when compared to other restaurants that sometimes prioritize food over service. One pro tip: make sure to make a reservation, as it is highly recommended, if not required. Due to Kanella's cozy space, getting a table for brunch without a reservation is nearly impossible. However, if you do manage to secure a seat for brunch, expect nothing less than a fantastic way to kickstart your weekend morning (or aid in recovering from the previous night's activities). I can't wait to return and explore their dinner menu.

input: This place gets two stars from me only because the gravy fries were good. Their sandwiches are awful. Thick slabs of badly sliced, tough, dry meat....gross. I made the mistake of ordering their pork sandwich once and it was inedible. I tried to bite into the sandwich and couldn't even bite through because of how tough and rubbery the pork was. I don't understand why they slice the meat the way they do but it makes for a disgusting sandwich. The people raving on how good this place is are just locals who have never had anything better. You're better off going to Wawa for a sandwich. Seriously. It will at least be edible.
Revise this with your best effort: I can only give this place two stars, mainly due to the delicious gravy fries they serve. However, their sandwiches are simply terrible. The thick, poorly sliced, tough, and dry slabs of meat they use are quite off-putting. It was a mistake for me to try their pork sandwich once, as it was absolutely inedible. Attempting to take a bite, I struggled immensely due to the toughness and rubbery texture of the pork. Their baffling way of cutting the meat ultimately results in an unappetizing sandwich. The individuals praising this place are most likely locals who haven't had the pleasure of experiencing something better. Trust me, your best bet is to head to Wawa for a sandwich. Believe me, it will certainly be more enjoyable to consume.

input:
Be careful.  This place just wants your money, not your business.  They deal only in cash and are very reluctant to take returns.  And I'm sure that they don't only take cash only from the large contractors... probably just the little guys.  
They sell damaged items.  Check your stuff very well before you leave, because you will not be able to bring it back if you discover that they have slipped you the ole' damaged door!

I do not recommend this place.  Don't support them.  Not at all.
Revise this with your best effort:
Exercise caution when dealing with this establishment as their primary focus appears to be on extracting money rather than fostering genuine business relationships. It is worth noting that they exclusively accept cash and are exceedingly unwilling to facilitate returns. Additionally, it is highly likely that their insistence on cash payments applies mainly to smaller contractors, rather than larger ones.

It is important to thoroughly inspect your purchases before leaving their premises as they have been known to sell damaged items. Returning such items will likely pose a challenge, leaving you burdened with a faulty product.

Considering the aforementioned issues, I strongly advise against endorsing or supporting this establishment in any way, as their practices and policies are far from commendable.

input: We stopped here on our way through town and want sure what to expect but we were pleasantly surprised. The service sucked and the staff was rude but the food made up that in the end. We had some pulled pork which was more chopped then pulled, brisket tacos which were define, and pulled chicken which was moist. The sides were pretty good too but nothing to write home about. There were five of us and our bill was close to $60 and one meal was a kids meal. I  really only have two complaints: One, they didn't have ribs for lunch and two, the bathrooms were filthy.
Revise this with your best effort: We made a pit stop in this town unsure of what to anticipate, but ended up pleasantly surprised. Although the service left much to be desired and the staff was impolite, the redeeming factor was definitely the food. The pulled pork, while more chopped than pulled, was enjoyable, and the brisket tacos were truly delightful. Moreover, the pulled chicken had a pleasant moistness to it. The sides were decent, although not extraordinary. Taking into account that we were a group of five, our bill came close to $60, even with one meal being a kids meal. However, I do have two grievances to mention. Firstly, they unfortunately did not offer ribs for lunch. Secondly, the state of the bathrooms was abhorrent, as they were filthy.

input:
Tried dinner there recently and found the quality is very uneven.

While some noodle soup dishes and rice plate dishes are true to authentic Chinese food, others are truly found in only American Chinese restaurants. The duck is very fat and very little meat. The stir fry dishes have weird combo of vegetables that do not go together.

And as a typical Chinese restaurant, service does not come with a smile.
Revise this with your best effort:
I recently dined at that establishment and was disappointed to find a noticeable inconsistency in the overall quality.

While certain noodle soup and rice plate dishes succeeded in capturing the essence of authentic Chinese cuisine, others appeared to be more closely associated with the offerings found in American Chinese restaurants. The duck dish, in particular, was disappointingly excessive in fat content and was lacking in substantial meat portions. Furthermore, the stir fry dishes contained a peculiar combination of vegetables that failed to harmonize with each other.

Additionally, adhering to the stereotype of most traditional Chinese restaurants, the service lacked the warmth and friendliness often associated with a smile.

input:
I have always dreaded going to the hair salon.  I hated the phony atmosphere of most places and I really dreaded the small talk I would be forced to have with my stylist.  Maybe I am unusually insecure, but I always felt intimidated in most salons.  
Then, one day a couple of years ago, I wandered into Andre's salon and I never looked back.  
Andre is warm and personable and made me feel at ease immediately.  Right off the bat, we connected on a topic I care about--dogs--and I didn't feel uncomfortable at all.  Oh, and the cut and color were fantastic!  My highlights last longer than highlights I have received from any other salon.
For the past year or so, Christopher has been styling my hair and I LOVE him to death.  He is incredibly sweet, down-to-earth and talented!  My hair looks amazing for days after he styles it and, try as I might, I can never get it to look as good as he can.
The last time I was at the salon, Christopher, Leah and I had a blast reminiscing about '80s fashion!  I can't remember a time when I enjoyed going to the hair salon (which is probably because I never have!).
Also, back in the spring, I asked Andre if he would be interested in donating a gift for a charity 5K I was helping to organize.  Being the wonderful person he is, Andre didn't hesitate and put together a beautiful basket that was a hit at the race!  Andre has a good heart and that it what I love about going to his salon!
I also love that clients can schedule appointments online through schedulicity!
Great prices, great cuts, great color, great space, convenient scheduling options and, most importantly, great people--you will not regret choosing Andre for your next cut or color!
Revise this with your best effort:

Not to mention, the cut and color I received were absolutely fantastic. The highlights from Andre's salon last longer than any I've had before.

In the past year, Christopher has become my go-to stylist, and I can't praise him enough. He is incredibly sweet, down-to-earth, and supremely talented. Whenever he styles my hair, it looks amazing for days, and I can never recreate the magic he works. Additionally, our recent conversation with Christopher and Leah about '80s fashion during my salon visit was an absolute blast. It's a rare occurrence for me to actually enjoy going to a hair salon, but Andre's salon has changed that.

Furthermore, Andre's generosity shines through. When I approached him about donating a gift for a charity 5K I was involved with, he didn't hesitate. He put together a beautiful basket that was a hit at the race. Andre's kind heart is one of the many reasons I love going to his salon.

Another aspect I appreciate is the ability to schedule appointments online through schedulicity. It makes the process convenient and hassle-free. With great prices, exceptional cuts, stunning color, a welcoming environment, and the added convenience of online scheduling, choosing Andre for your next cut or color is a decision you won't regret. Most importantly, the salon is filled with genuinely great people who make the experience truly enjoyable.

input: Absolutely amazing and unique food. Love their bobba and pork pancake!
Revise this with your best effort: The food here is absolutely outstanding and unlike anything else I've ever tasted. I am absolutely in love with their boba tea and their pork pancake is simply divine!

input:
Nice, old school space with a long bar. It reminded me of some places I've been out west, which might be a little strange in the heart of Philadelphia. 

Not too loud at all - conversations were easy and a lot of the patrons were doing just that. There's a jukebox, so maybe it cranks up later in the evening. We were there pretty early. 

Great service from several people working behind the bar. 

Several beers on tap including a local CCCCC IPA, which was solid. Not many wines, though.

Small menu but very good food. The elote (corn) is quite good, as was the cucumber(?) salad. But the brat plate was the star. Wonderful brat, German potato salad, sauerkraut, pretzel and a hot salsa/relish. Best brat plate ever. Served on a cool wood board.

Prohibition is located in or near a somewhat dicey neighborhood, at least to this non-resident's eye. I may very well be wrong about that. We had to walk a trashy, pissy street past what seemed like skid row coming from the hotel on Race St. If it was later at night we might have chosen not to walk back.
Revise this with your best effort:
The space had a nice, old school charm with a long bar that brought back memories of similar places out west. It was interesting to find such a cozy atmosphere in the heart of Philadelphia.

The volume level was just right, allowing for easy conversations among patrons who seemed to be enjoying themselves. Although there was a jukebox, it remained relatively quiet during our early visit, perhaps waiting to come alive later in the evening.

The service at the bar was exceptional, with multiple friendly staff members attending to our needs.

While the selection of beers on tap was varied and included a solid local IPA, the options for wine were somewhat limited.

Despite having a compact menu, the food exceeded expectations. The elote (corn) and the cucumber salad were both delicious, but the real highlight was the brat plate. It featured a fantastic bratwurst accompanied by German potato salad, sauerkraut, a pretzel, and a delightful hot salsa/relish. It was beautifully presented on a stylish wooden board, adding to the overall experience.

It's worth mentioning that Prohibition is located in, or at least near, a neighborhood that appeared a bit sketchy to an outsider like myself. Walking along a littered and unpleasant street, it felt like we were passing through a rough area similar to skid row. If it had been later in the night, we might have chosen an alternative route back from the hotel.

input:
On the Run is a convenience store chain and BP gas station. It is in a very convenient location for those who are returning rental cars at Lambert-St. Louis International Airport! How many times have you been on the way back into an airport, and not found a gas station nearby? Happens to me to any times - often you have to go out of your way to find one. Not so here!

Paid at the pump - I note that the pump had a hand scrawled note taped to the pumps - requesting you press the appropriate button (credit or debit) before swiping your credit card. Never seen this before - this is the exact opposite procedure of other gas station pumps when using a credit card!

Refueled and was on my way to Hertz!
Revise this with your best effort:
On the Run is a convenient convenience store chain and BP gas station located in close proximity to Lambert-St. Louis International Airport, making it an ideal stop for those returning rental cars. How many times have you found yourself heading back to the airport only to realize there are no gas stations nearby? It has happened to me countless times, often requiring a detour to fill up. However, this is not the case here!

One of the notable features at On the Run is the option to pay at the pump. As I approached the pumps, I couldn't help but notice a hand-scrawled note taped to each one. The note kindly requested customers to press the appropriate button (credit or debit) before swiping their card. This struck me as quite unusual, as it was the opposite procedure compared to other gas stations when using a credit card.

With my car refueled, I promptly continued my journey to Hertz, grateful for the convenient services provided by On the Run.

input:
This is a pretty historical building that is well maintained. When we visited, we were the ONLY people there, which meant the Park Ranger gave us a private tour. Sweet!

Also - if you're into collecting National Park Stamps, you can get a few here! w00t!
Revise this with your best effort:
This building holds great historical significance and is impeccably preserved. During our visit, we had the privilege of being the sole visitors, granting us a personalized tour by the Park Ranger. How wonderful!

Moreover, for enthusiastic National Park Stamps collectors, this site offers the opportunity to obtain a few! Celebratory cheers all around!

input: The service was great and the restaurant was clean, but the food was just okay. We had the linguine with marinara and the rotini primavera. The linguine was fine. The primavera, however, is not something anyone should order!!! The sauce had a great flavor, but the vegetables were actually from frozen. I mean, literally from FROZEN. Go to your local grocery store, look at the bag of Bird's Eye mixed vegetables and you will see what they use... right down to the ruffle cut carrots. There is so much wonderful fresh produce in Tucson, there is absolutely no reason to ever use gross frozen vegetables.
Revise this with your best effort: The service provided at the restaurant was exceptional, and we were pleased with the impeccable cleanliness. However, it is regrettable that the food failed to meet our expectations. Our order consisted of linguine with marinara sauce and rotini primavera. The linguine was satisfactory, but unfortunately, we cannot recommend the primavera dish to anyone. Although the sauce had an appealing taste, it was disappointing to discover that the vegetables used were actually frozen. Yes, frozen, as in the same kind you would find in a bag of Bird's Eye mixed vegetables at your local grocery store, complete with ruffle cut carrots. Given the abundance of fresh and delightful produce available in Tucson, there is truly no justification for using subpar frozen vegetables.

input:
We  heard that Fresh Market was open and since we just got back from vaca we thought we would try it.  First of all, accolades to the staff they could not have been more helpful.  Especially Thomas in the meat section.  For these two things I would give them a five.  However, it does downhill from this point on:  ordered one pound of swiss cheese, after standing there waiting for about 5 minutes, and no one else was on line, the unfriendly clerk waited on us. The imported swiss cheese that we ordered was so poorly cut that in two days we had one clump of swiss cheese, rather than many slices.  I bought ricotta cheese for Easter and went to open it, and it was bad, although it was dated 3/28.  The tomatoes on the vine that I bought on Friday were bad by Sunday.  I have found their prices very high, selection, poor and at this point it is just not worth it. I also bought two pound cakes and their were not up to par.  Very dry and tasteless.. Overall a very disappointing shopping trip 
There is plenty of convenient parking and the store was immaculate, but it is not for me.  The final straw was that I asked for extra cash for Easter gifts, the clerk at the register said there was a $150 limit, the ATM terminal said $100 and the "manager" said $50...I thought they should get their act together.  Best to stay with Weaver's Way... or Whole Foods or Wegmann's.
Revise this with your best effort:
After hearing that Fresh Market had opened, we were eager to give it a try upon returning from vacation. Initially, we were impressed by the exceptional service provided by the staff, particularly Thomas in the meat section. Their assistance alone would warrant a five-star rating. However, our experience began to decline after this point.

When we ordered one pound of Swiss cheese, the disinterested clerk, despite no one else being in line, kept us waiting for approximately five minutes. To make matters worse, the imported Swiss cheese we received was incredibly poorly cut. Instead of receiving several neat slices, we ended up with a clump of Swiss cheese after just two days. Additionally, the ricotta cheese we purchased for Easter turned out to be spoiled, despite being within its expiration date of 3/28. It was disappointing to find that the tomatoes on the vine, bought on Friday, had already gone bad by Sunday. 

Moreover, we have found Fresh Market's prices to be exorbitant, their selection lacking, and it has become evident that the experience is simply not worth it anymore. We also purchased two pound cakes, which were far from satisfactory. They were dry and lacked flavor. Overall, this shopping trip left much to be desired.

Granted, the store does offer ample and convenient parking, and its cleanliness is commendable. However, it is not a store that suits our preferences. The final straw came when we requested extra cash for Easter gifts. The register clerk informed us that there was a $150 limit, yet the ATM terminal displayed a limit of $100, and the so-called "manager" stated a limit of $50. It became evident that Fresh Market needed to establish consistency and improve their organizational skills.

Our advice would be to stick with Weaver's Way, Whole Foods, or Wegmann's instead.

input:
I've only been once, but I'm ready to return.

Since moving to Fletcher Place, I've been looking for a bar near by that's similar to my neighborhood favorite, J Clydes. I think I've found it.

The Dugout is a simple hole-in-the-wall place. They have a decent selection, Sun King for $4.50, happy hour appetizers, and my favorite part: HOT PEPPER CHEESE BALLS! No longer must I wait until my coveted Mug N' Bun trips for these fried morsels of tasty peppery goodness. Had a nice little piece form this joint, too. 

Really excited to return.
Revise this with your best effort:
After just one visit, I can't wait to go back again. Ever since I relocated to Fletcher Place, I've been on the lookout for a nearby bar that can rival my beloved neighborhood spot, J Clydes. And I think I've finally discovered it.

Nestled discreetly, The Dugout is an unassuming gem. It may be a small and unpretentious establishment, but it packs a punch. They offer a respectable selection of beverages, including the popular Sun King for a great price of $4.50. What's more, their happy hour appetizers are a delightful treat. However, the real star of the show, in my opinion, is their HOT PEPPER CHEESE BALLS! These delectable bites of deep-fried, peppery goodness are a revelation. No longer do I have to patiently await my coveted trips to Mug N' Bun to savor these irresistible delights. To top it all off, I even had the pleasure of enjoying a charming little piece of this joint.

All in all, I am genuinely thrilled at the prospect of returning to The Dugout.

input:
I heard this ice cream parlour opened last summer, so upon my first trip home (sometime during the fall) I hustled over to try it. Since Friendly's closed a few years ago, Warminster has sorely needed a new ice cream place (DQ was our last one standing for quite some time). 

Much to my dismay, the Big Scoop had already closed for the season. I marked it in my calendar go return in March, when it reopened. Upon my next trip home in the spring, I was disappointed to see that I was just a few days early for their reopening, and would have to wait until my return in April.

After much anticipation, I made it to Big Scoop last weekend with my sister (who has been before). I was shocked to see what a range of products they serve - hot dogs, funnel cake, onion rings, pizza, you name it! I was tempted at the prospect of waffles and ice cream, but I wasn't that hungry so I settled for a scoop of chocolate chip cookie with hot fudge and whipped cream. The generous scoop of ice cream was tasty and packed with globs of cookie dough! I also tasted the birthday cake, which I enjoyed very much. 

The service was quick, and the shop crowded quickly. The interior was nicely remodeled and looks clean and family friendly. The man who helped me was extremely courteous and seemed to be doing most of the work. 

Especially given the lack of competition around here, the Big Scoop gets an easy four stars!
Revise this with your best effort:

Considering the limited competition in the area, the Big Scoop easily earns a well-deserved four-star rating!

input: Aparently this review is for Saguaro East. I didnt realize there were two separate parks. This park is fine. We planned to do some hiking, but it just looked like flat average desert you can easily see and hike in the Phoenix area. The visitor center and staff were nice.
Revise this with your best effort: Apparently, this review pertains to Saguaro East. I wasn't aware that there were two distinct parks. In terms of this park, it is alright. Although we had intended to engage in some hiking activities, the landscape appeared to be an ordinary, flat desert that one could conveniently witness and explore in the Phoenix area. On a positive note, the visitor center and its staff were pleasant and accommodating.

input:
Staff is amazing!  Coupons on their website are for 40 percent off a regular priced item... so that means... you are always getting something on sale!

We went in one evening at around 15 minutes before closing to grab some things very quickly... and all staff members were very helpful even so close to closing!  

Great store!
Revise this with your best effort:
The staff at this store is truly exceptional! Not only do they offer incredible customer service, but they also provide valuable discounts through their website coupons. With a generous 40 percent off a regular priced item, it's guaranteed that you'll always find something on sale!

On a particular evening, we rushed into the store only 15 minutes before closing time, hoping to grab a few items in a hurry. Despite the late hour, every single staff member went above and beyond to assist us with utmost patience and helpfulness.

This store is truly outstanding, providing an exceptional shopping experience thanks to its incredible staff and fantastic deals.

input:
This is another one of those anytime coffee shops. You can come get some work done, people watch, or just grab a drink to go. Either way, its open early and late.

For the quarter, its "off the beaten path" but in the busy area the locals hang out, and on the way to Fenchmen where everyone goes for good local music, Jazz, et al. 

They have food, not the cheapest, or local, but its better for you than the greasy, salty, fatty foods. Just make sure your service number is visible I got distracted hid my number, and had to stop the guy looking.  

Service varies. Since its a busy sidewalk, people stop in for that pick me up before work or party. One minute there is a like 12 long, and the barista is running ragged, the next its dead. 

Sometimes I'll sit for over an hour working or catching up on email. I'll order something every so often, and its no big deal for me to queue myself if they get busy. After all it helps those stopping in for a quick drink.

p.s. I love there tall cookies

oh and how many coffee shops can you get a shot in your coffee! That's right, its not a bar, but its New Orleans.
Revise this with your best effort:
This coffee shop falls into the category of those convenient establishments that are open at all times. It offers a variety of activities such as working, people-watching, or grabbing a quick drink to take away. The location is slightly off the regular path, but it is situated in a bustling area frequented by locals. It is also en route to Fenchmen, a popular venue for local music, particularly jazz.

The coffee shop serves food, which may not be the most affordable or locally-sourced, but it is undoubtedly healthier compared to greasy, salty, and fatty alternatives. Just remember to keep your service number visible, as I once got distracted and hid mine, resulting in a brief inconvenience while the staff tried to locate my order.

The level of service here can vary due to the constant flow of people dropping by for a little boost before work or a night out. At times, the line can become quite long, with the barista rushing around to keep up, while other moments may be quiet and less demanding.

Personally, I have spent over an hour sitting here, either working on tasks or catching up on emails. Occasionally, I order something to support the establishment, and if it gets busy, I have no problem waiting in line myself. Ultimately, it benefits those seeking a quick beverage.

By the way, I must mention that I absolutely adore their tall cookies. Additionally, how many coffee shops allow you to have a shot in your coffee? That's right, it's not a bar, but we're in New Orleans, where unique experiences like these are the norm.

input: I was on the guest list tonight as my friend from high school was DJing, however, when I got to the front of the line I was unfortunately shoved through the front door before I could show my ID and verify my guest list status. After I was shoved through I tried to explain to the bouncer what had happened so I could properly verify that I was actually on the list. This bouncer then accused me of just trying to sneak in for free without paying even though I went back to him once I was inside. He then proceeded to belittle me and completely disregard the fact that I was allowed to be there. This ended in me being denied total entry, despite the fact that I was on the list, and I will never come here due to how I was treated by this bouncer.
Revise this with your best effort: Tonight, I was excited to be on the guest list at a club where my high school friend was DJing. Unfortunately, as I reached the front of the line, I was forcefully pushed through the entrance before I had a chance to present my ID and verify my status on the guest list. Disturbed by this incident, I immediately sought out the bouncer to explain what had happened, hoping to rectify the situation and confirm my rightful presence on the list. Regrettably, due to the disrespectful treatment I endured from this bouncer, I have made the choice to never patronize this establishment in the future.

input: Salad portions are great. I always go with the Greek. One of the few Nick's spots that serves a rustic roast beef sandwich. Highly recommend that one. Pizza isn't that bad. I'd recommend an XL if having guests over. It's probably there better pizza, surprisingly.
Revise this with your best effort: The salad portions at this place are fantastic, and my personal go-to is always the Greek salad. Another standout menu item is their rustic roast beef sandwich, which is a rarity to find at Nick's spots. I highly recommend giving it a try. As for the pizza, it's actually quite good. If you have guests coming over, I suggest opting for the XL size. Surprisingly, it's probably their best pizza on the menu.

input:
Definitely dug this place...rather hipster-ish and way, way reminiscent of Este Sugarhouse in Salt Lake, but I liked it a lot despite all that...pizza here is definitely a lot better, as is beer selection. This may wind up being one of my more regular haunts as I slog my way through more of their menu (I think I may need to heavily modify next time I'm there), but so far, I have no cause at all for complaint and much to celebrate. It's interesting to me that the environments of the various locations are different, sometimes vastly, yet all have their own unique and innate charm. Whoever is running these is doing a phenomenal job, so props there.

One thing of note here...the ordering system is extremely clunky and seemingly disorganized and I sort of dislike it. Not enough to stop coming here, since I really dig the vibe of these, but on one of my less patient nights, that sort of thing may be enough to cut this out of the running. Definitely a good spot for pizza and a brew (or several), though. I back it.
Revise this with your best effort:
I was really impressed with this place, it had a certain hipster charm to it that reminded me of Este Sugarhouse in Salt Lake. Despite that, I thoroughly enjoyed it, especially the pizza, which was a significant upgrade from other places, and the beer selection was top-notch. I can see myself becoming a regular here as I explore more of their menu, although I might make some modifications next time. Overall, I have no complaints and much to celebrate. It's fascinating how each location has its own unique charm, regardless of their differences. Whoever is in charge of these places is doing an outstanding job, and they deserve recognition for it.

There is one thing worth mentioning though, the ordering system is quite clunky and disorganized, which is something I personally don't like. However, it's not enough to deter me from coming here, as I really enjoy the overall atmosphere. On a night when I'm feeling less patient, it might be a deciding factor, but for now, it's still a great spot to enjoy some delicious pizza and a variety of refreshing brews. I definitely recommend it.

input:
New St. Louis Wok is one of the few local Chinese places that deliver to our area.  Every time (but one), we've ordered, and gotten the food within an house.  In addition, they have a website where you can order the food (avoiding possible language barriers), and then they follow up with a call for your credit card number.

Food wise, it's the best Chinese delivery we've had here.  Nothing too greasy, and everything comes hot...with lots of sauces and fortune cookies.  For our rare Chinese cravings, it's the go-to place.
Revise this with your best effort:
New St. Louis Wok stands out among the limited selection of local Chinese restaurants that offer delivery to our area. Without fail, they have consistently delivered our food within an hour, except for one minor exception. An added convenience is their user-friendly website, which allows for seamless online ordering, thereby avoiding any potential language barriers. Notably, they also take the extra step to follow up with a phone call to securely obtain your credit card information.

When it comes to their cuisine, New St. Louis Wok truly excels in the realm of Chinese delivery. Their dishes are remarkably light and far from excessively greasy, providing a satisfying dining experience. Moreover, each order is delivered piping hot, accompanied by a generous variety of delectable sauces and the customary fortune cookies. Whenever we find ourselves yearning for authentic Chinese flavors, New St. Louis Wok is undoubtedly our go-to establishment.

input: This is my go to sushi place. it's cheap and the rolls are AMAZING. if you want a new sushi place to try i highly recommend osaka
Revise this with your best effort: This is absolutely my favorite sushi spot. Not only is it incredibly affordable, but their sushi rolls are truly exquisite. If you're in the mood to explore a new sushi joint, I wholeheartedly vouch for Osaka as an exceptional choice.

input:
Kelly's has changed hands and the menu has completely changed.  It's clear they've had to defend this and it seems to annoy them.  I mean the menu was epic - why change it?

In response, the new crew touted the place being cleaner and it was.

I got the  classic burger and fries.  I'll be honest, it was the worst $11 burger that I've ever had.  Dry and flavorless and made me envy a $2 McDonalds bacon burger flashing on the TV.  The fries were OK.

I was shocked to just walk in at dinner time.  This wasn't possible before.  Now I know why.

:
Revise this with your best effort:
Kelly's has undergone a recent ownership change, resulting in a complete overhaul of their menu. However, it is evident that they have faced some criticism in defending this decision, which appears to annoy them. The previous menu was highly regarded, making one question the motive behind the changes.

In an attempt to counter the skepticism, the new staff emphasizes the improved cleanliness of the establishment, which does stand out.

My choice for dinner was the classic burger with a side of fries. Truthfully, it was the most disappointing $11 burger I have ever tasted. It lacked moisture and flavor, making me envious of a mere $2 bacon burger shown enticingly on the television screen of a nearby McDonald's. The fries, on the other hand, were decent.

One surprising aspect was that I could easily walk into Kelly's during dinner time, which was previously unheard of. In light of my experience, it now seems apparent as to why this is the case.

input: Great place to go everyday. I saw huge changes in my strength and flexibility there. All of the teachers are unique and teach beneficial classes. I highly recommend a monthly membership!
Revise this with your best effort: Everyday, this place is truly exceptional. It has been where remarkable transformations in my strength and flexibility have unfolded. The instructors, with their distinctive teaching styles, deliver classes that offer incredible value. I wholeheartedly advocate for a monthly membership.

input:
I live in the neighborhood and used to order at least once a week and pick up.  The last last few times I have had to wait from 10 to 15 minutes as the team scrambles around trying to find change. All I wanted to do is pay for my food and take it home.   And tonight after the wait for change. I gave them 2 20's for a 27 dollar check. 
I get home and it is the wrong food. My warm dish was cold and my sushi was wrong.  Lost me as a customer
Revise this with your best effort:
I used to order from this neighborhood restaurant at least once a week and would usually pick up my order. However, during my last few visits, I noticed that I had to wait for about 10 to 15 minutes as the team struggled to find change. All I wanted was to pay for my food and take it home quickly. Unfortunately, tonight was another disappointing experience. After waiting for my change, I handed them two $20 bills for a $27 check. 
Upon arriving home, I discovered that they had given me the wrong food. Not only was my warm dish cold, but my sushi order was completely incorrect as well. This repeated mistake has unfortunately led me to reconsider becoming a loyal customer.

input: Their pizza is pretty good, service is usually cool inside. But today I ordered a delivery for the first time, the driver was very insulting to me. When I open my door she asked me about a car across the street with a guy in the driver's seat. I replied "I don't know," she said "cus I don't wanna be set up to get robbed". Mind you I already paid with my visa when I ordered, her behavior made me feel awkward as if I had done something wrong. I gave her the tip I had in my hand and said thank you, hoping that maybe if I remain polite she'll stop thinking so negative I just wanted some pizza not to be judged because of my surroundings or to be stereotyped.
Revise this with your best effort:
Their pizza is usually pretty good and the service inside is generally cool. However, my experience today with their delivery service left a lot to be desired. The driver that came to my door was incredibly insulting towards me. As soon as I opened the door, she started questioning me about a car parked across the street with a person in the driver's seat. I honestly had no idea about it, and when I responded with "I don't know," she replied with an offensive remark, saying that she didn't want to be set up to get robbed. 

The fact that I had already paid with my visa when I placed the order made her behavior even more perplexing and uncomfortable. I felt as though I had done something wrong, even though all I wanted was some pizza. It was disheartening to be judged based on my surroundings and to be stereotyped just because of where I lived. 

In an effort to diffuse the situation, I handed her the tip I had prepared and thanked her politely, hoping that my kindness would change her negative perception.

input:
First time here and I have to say it's pretty good! The bake shop fits well with the fishtown environment and it's very clean and welcoming inside. The display of beautiful cakes let's you know you have top quality bakers there. 

I got a few items to share such as a Burbon Pecan cookie, chocolate chip cookie, vanilla cupcake with buttercream icing, and a vanilla cupcake with raspberry icing. 

I had a taste of the Burbon Pecan Cookie. It was not too sweet and you get nice bites of pecan; a nice hot coffee is a perfect compliment.The cupcakes were good (cake wise) but, not a huge fan of the icings. The cake itself was sweet and moist. 

Didn't get to try the Chocolate chip cookie but the concensus was that it's delicious. 

I would definitely come back and I have taken a big interest in having Cake Life make a custom order!
Revise this with your best effort:
This is my first visit to this place, and I must say, it's quite impressive! The bake shop blends in perfectly with the fishtown setting, and upon entering, the cleanliness and welcoming ambiance instantly catch your attention. The stunning display of cakes reassures you that their bakers deliver top-notch quality.

During my visit, I ordered a selection of treats to try, including a Burbon Pecan cookie, a chocolate chip cookie, a vanilla cupcake with buttercream icing, and a vanilla cupcake with raspberry icing.

Let me start by discussing the Burbon Pecan Cookie. It struck a perfect balance of sweetness, and the generous pecan pieces provided delightful bursts of flavor. Pairing it with a piping hot coffee was simply heavenly. As for the cupcakes, the cake itself was delectably sweet and moist, truly satisfying. However, I have to admit that I wasn't particularly fond of the icings. Nonetheless, many others vouched for their deliciousness.

Unfortunately, I wasn't able to try the Chocolate Chip Cookie on this occasion, but the consensus among fellow customers indicated that it is an absolute delight.

All in all, I am definitely planning to return, and I have developed a keen interest in placing a custom order with Cake Life.

input:
Went here last Thursday and arrived early enough to take advantage of their $5 domestic pitchers during hh which includes mich golden light, my fave! It did take the server about 10-15 minutes to even notice we were there, but after that service was just fine. 

Started off with the wings which were delicious, although the bf was certain it was not actually a pound of wings which they claim on their menu.

I ordered the gyro and fries which were surprisingly really good! Gyro meat was tasty and the fries were awesome! Bf had the French onion soup and potato skins which he said were good as well.

We stayed for rock n roll bingo (which I guess is every Thursday, and free!) and we had a blast. They also have a pool table and darts in the back which we played while waiting for bingo to start.

We will definitely be back!
Revise this with your best effort:
Last Thursday, my partner and I visited this place and arrived early to take advantage of their happy hour offer, which included $5 domestic pitchers, including my personal favorite, Michelob Golden Light. Although it did take the server around 10-15 minutes to acknowledge our presence, the service afterwards was satisfactory.

To begin our meal, we ordered the wings, which were absolutely delicious. However, my partner suspected that it was not actually a full pound of wings, as advertised on the menu.

I decided to try the gyro and fries, and to my surprise, they were incredibly tasty. The gyro meat was flavorful, and the fries were simply awesome. My partner had the French onion soup and potato skins, which he also enjoyed.

We stayed for the rock n roll bingo, a free event held every Thursday, and had an amazing time. Additionally, they had a pool table and darts in the back, which we played while waiting for the bingo game to start.

We will definitely return to this place in the future!

input: Johnny Tucci and his crew are the absolute best videographers, hands down. They are professional, prompt, and extremely talented. They made our wedding footage look like a movie production and brought everyone to tears that watched it. My advice is that if you are going to splurge in one area for your special day, spend it on a videographer. They do not disappoint.
Revise this with your best effort: Johnny Tucci and his crew truly excel in the field of videography, surpassing all others. Their professionalism, promptness, and exceptional talent set them apart from the rest. With their expertise, our wedding footage was elevated to the level of a captivating movie production, leaving those who watched it in tears. If you are considering where to invest your resources for your special day, I highly recommend indulging in a videographer. Rest assured, Johnny Tucci and his team never fail to deliver a mesmerizing experience.

input:
One of the absolute best places to see a game in the entire country!

Get there early or if it's a blowout, stroll around the park. There are tons of interesting places to eat & drink (including a rooftop bar). Tickets are still amazingly reasonable even after all the success the Phils have had in recent years particularly when compared to the NY parks.

I used to go more often before the team became so prominent (right after the park opened), and I sat all over the joint. Not really anywhere I wouldn't recommend. The outfied is a great option. 

After starting with a 17 game pack many years ago & then buying season tix a few years back (which my company still has), the staff was great about recommending sections that would avoid direct sunlight , etc. (3rd base field level is awesome).

If you are visiting or considering a trip, don't buy the negative publicity about the Philly fans. The crowds are great. Sure, you have idiots and maniacs like you do at any park and for any professional sporting event, but they are by far the minority and Citizens Bank Park is policed pretty well for nonsense. 

I was once with a group of guys & we stood out in one of the open standing areas between 3rd base & the left field wall the whole night. At one point a very nice officer politely asked us not to curse because there were families around. We we were far from out of control, and we all thought that was pretty cool... so we had fun with some occasional lighthearted banter with the officer for the rest of the night.

Don't expect to be sheltered with your kids like you would be in your own living room, but there's no teens running onto the field getting tazed every night nor are there drunk idiots throwing up on people. 

It's a great atmosphere, a wonderful park & still a very fun team to watch.
Revise this with your best effort:
Citizens Bank Park is undeniably one of the premier venues nationwide to catch a game. To fully enjoy your experience, arriving early is recommended, or if the game turns into a one-sided affair, take a leisurely stroll around the park. At this remarkable destination, there is no shortage of intriguing eateries and drink options, including a fabulous rooftop bar. Despite the Philadelphia Phillies' recent successes, ticket prices remain remarkably affordable, especially when compared to the exorbitant prices of New York stadiums.

During the early years of the park, before the team gained widespread prominence, I frequented games more often and explored various seating sections. Frankly, there isn't a single spot I wouldn't recommend. Opting for the outfield is a fantastic choice.

Having started with a 17 game package many years ago and subsequently purchasing season tickets for my company, the staff consistently provided exceptional assistance, recommending sections shielded from direct sunlight, among other considerations. Personally, I find the third base field level to be truly exceptional.

If you're visiting or contemplating a trip to Citizens Bank Park, don't let negative publicity about Philadelphia fans dissuade you. The crowd is tremendous. Although, like any sporting event, you may encounter a few troublemakers or fanatics, they are undoubtedly the minority, and the park is well-regulated to prevent any unnecessary disturbances.

On one occasion, while standing in one of the open standing areas between third base and the left field wall with a group of friends, a kind police officer politely asked us to refrain from using profanity due to the presence of families nearby. Despite us being far from disruptive, we found this interaction to be rather enjoyable. Subsequently, we engaged in occasional light-hearted banter with the officer for the rest of the night.

While you can't expect the same level of sheltering as in the comfort of your own living room when attending with kids, rest assured that instances of unruly teens or intoxicated individuals causing disturbances are exceptionally rare. The atmosphere at Citizens Bank Park is exceptional, the stadium itself is magnificent, and the team's on-field performance guarantees a memorable and enjoyable experience for all.

input: I love Cosi but this Cosi is going down hill fast. I always get a signature salad and lately they are made wrong and no dressing at all. How hard is it to make their own signature salad!? It's practically what they are known for!!! So angry.
Revise this with your best effort: I used to really enjoy Cosi, but lately I've noticed a decline in their quality. Specifically, their signature salads, which have been consistently disappointing. Not only are they being prepared incorrectly, but they often lack dressing entirely. It's frustrating because the signature salad is one of their specialties and should be made perfectly every time. I can't help but feel frustrated with this deterioration in their standards.

input: OMG!! what a disappointment today was, I have been so excited to see Rembrandt's reopen after a few months of remodel, what I was thinking is that the new owners would want to do more restorations of this Beautiful, Cozy, old Church, maybe try to find more space to add Tables, but NO, I walked into a Modern, Cold, Hospital Coffee Shop, the Charm is gone, so so disappointed and sad, we all love the Charm of Eagle, but it seems to be fading fast, Please People talk to all the other Eagle Shop Owners when your visiting them especially the old Original Buildings to keep Eagle's charm and quaintness and restore these Beautiful Buildings.
Revise this with your best effort: Oh my goodness! What a letdown today turned out to be. I was filled with such anticipation to witness the reopening of Rembrandt's after its few months of renovation. I had imagined that the new owners would undertake further restoration of this picturesque, cozy old church. Perhaps they would even find ways to incorporate more tables, enhancing the space. However, as I stepped through the doors, I was met with an impersonal, clinical coffee shop. Gone is the charm that once graced Eagle, leaving me incredibly disappointed and disheartened. It seems that our beloved town's enchantment is rapidly fading away. I implore each and every one of you to engage in conversations with the other owners of shops in Eagle, particularly those housed within the original, historic buildings. Let us work together to preserve Eagle's allure and quaintness. It is vital that we invest in the restoration of these gorgeous structures, for they hold the key to the town's enduring beauty.

input:
The service was lacking. The waiters and waitresses don't know the menu and when you ask for certain things to be brought to your table, it's constantly forgotten. The food is visually appealing but some of the most awkward and distasteful food I've ever had. The waffles are stale, the biscuits are hard as rock and their chorizo is not real chorizo.

The only thing this place has going for it is the atmosphere and their alcohol selection.
Revise this with your best effort:
The overall service at this establishment fell short of expectations. The waitstaff appeared unfamiliar with the menu, frequently forgetting requests for items to be brought to the table. While the presentation of the food was visually impressive, the taste left much to be desired. The waffles lacked freshness, the biscuits were disappointingly hard, and their so-called chorizo did not live up to its name.

However, it is worth noting that the ambiance of the place is commendable, contributing to a pleasant atmosphere. Additionally, their selection of alcoholic beverages stands out as a positive aspect of the dining experience.

input:
This restaurant is a nice place to go and sit down to have something to eat. I've ate just about everything they have on the menu and I'd say their burgers are great. Although their pizza is a bit on the tough side I still manage to eat the crust too. 

Very comfortable dining room area as well!
Revise this with your best effort: This restaurant provides an enjoyable dining experience, where one can relax and indulge in delicious food. Having sampled almost everything on their menu, I can confidently say that their burgers are exceptional. Although their pizza tends to be slightly chewy, I still find myself savoring every bite, including the crisp crust. Furthermore, the dining room area offers a cozy and inviting ambiance, ensuring a comfortable atmosphere for all patrons.

input: We live in the neighborhood and have eaten here many times. I feel as if this restaurant is going downhill. This time we were there for dinner early on a Sunday. The bathrooms were filthy. There are 2 and one was not usable due to all of the paper towels that had been put into the toilet (there was no toilet paper). The other one was usable but also no toilet paper. Our server, Ashley, was not interested in providing any semblance of customer service...RUDE! We had a simple question about the beers on special and she became quite defensive. My daughter spilled her drink, which I realize is a pain in the ass for the restaurant and server (although we were outside so it wasn't that big a deal). We apologized profusely but she didn't even try to hide her annoyance. Finally, the chicken quesadilla should have been labeled the gristle quesadilla....more fat than actual meat...yuck. We love the proximity of this place to where we live and it was great in the past but not anymore...will likely not return...not with so many better quality restaurants in Northern Liberties and Fishtown.
Revise this with your best effort: As frequent visitors to this restaurant in our neighborhood, we are disappointed to observe a decline in its overall quality. Our recent experience occurred early on a Sunday evening, and it raised concerns as we encountered unsanitary conditions in the bathrooms. One of the two restrooms was completely unusable due to an excessive amount of paper towels stuffed into the toilet, while the other lacked essential supplies such as toilet paper. Additionally, our server, Ashley, displayed a blatant lack of interest in providing satisfactory customer service, which left a sour taste in our mouths. When we inquired about the beers on special, she became defensive and unhelpful. We understand that accidents happen, and our daughter spilled her drink. Despite profuse apologies, Ashley made no effort to conceal her annoyance. Lastly, the chicken quesadilla, unfortunately, could only be described as the "gristle quesadilla," as the dish contained more fat than actual meat, which was quite unappealing. While we appreciated the convenience of this restaurant's proximity to our home and had enjoyed it in the past, we are now reluctant to return. With the abundance of higher-quality establishments in the surrounding neighborhoods of Northern Liberties and Fishtown, we feel it is time to explore alternative dining options.

input: Pretty average bar/restaurant with the menu offerings you can expect from a place like this. The food was OK, and the service was excellent.
Revise this with your best effort: This establishment is your run-of-the-mill bar and restaurant, offering a standard array of menu options you'd typically find in a place of its kind. The culinary experience provided was decent, with the food being satisfactory in quality. However, the standout feature was undoubtedly the exceptional service provided by the attentive staff.

input: We came here based on the recommendation we received and from the street it doesn't look like much. But when you sit down and you scan the menu you will come to realize that this place serves nothing but home-cooked comfort food. We had the BLT and it was packed full of flavor, they didn't scrimp on the bacon and the vegetables for very fresh. With the sandwiches came some of the best french fries that we've had, and some of the best coleslaw that I've had in the state of Florida. We took a couple of pies home and they were delicious. We will definitely come back.
Revise this with your best effort: Upon receiving a recommendation, we decided to make our way here, but from the exterior, the place appeared unassuming. However, as soon as we settled down and perused the menu, we quickly understood that this establishment specializes in nothing short of soul-warming homemade fare. Opting for the BLT, we encountered a delightful explosion of flavors, with generous portions of bacon and crisp, fresh vegetables. Accompanying our sandwiches were a plate of impeccably prepared french fries, surpassing any we had ever encountered, alongside some delectable coleslaw that ranked among the best in the entirety of Florida. The remarkable experience prompted us to bring a couple of their tantalizing pies home, which certainly did not disappoint. Without a doubt, a return visit is inevitable.

input: I was greated by a nice friendly staff. There wasnt a long wait for my food. I ordered a chicken bacon croissant with chipolte sauce. They cut it in half as requested and was served in maybe only 20 seconds after the time it took to cook. Food taste great
Revise this with your best effort: I was warmly greeted by a friendly and accommodating staff. The wait for my food was minimal, and I was pleasantly surprised by the efficiency of their service. I ordered a chicken bacon croissant with chipotle sauce, and they kindly cut it in half just as I had requested. The dish was promptly served, taking only about 20 seconds after it was cooked. To my delight, the taste of the food was superb.

input: Excellent food! I am a Thai food junkie, and have travelled to Thailand and throughout Southeast Asia several times. There is ok Thai food in Nashville and then there is Great Thai food. This place was GREAT! The decor is a little dated but who cares...I was there for the food, which is fabulous!!!
Revise this with your best effort: I am an avid lover of Thai cuisine, and my culinary adventures have taken me to Thailand and various parts of Southeast Asia multiple times. Having tried Thai food in Nashville, I can confidently say that there are establishments with decent offerings, but this place surpasses them all. Despite its slightly outdated decor, the reason I visited was solely for the food, and let me tell you, it is absolutely phenomenal!

input: This place is absolutely fantastic. I honesty really don't even like sweets and am not all that into donuts but this place will make you a believer. The apple fritter is amazingly delicious and you can't go wrong with a chocolate long john. Don't even bother with any other donut shops in stl.
Revise this with your best effort: This place is truly amazing. Despite not having a preference for sweets or being particularly fond of donuts, I must admit that this place has the power to convert anyone. The apple fritter is exceptionally mouthwatering, and the chocolate long john is an absolute delight. Any attempt to find a better donut shop in St. Louis would be futile.

input: Of all the restaurants we tried in New Orleans, this was by far our favorite. I had both lunch and dinner on two separate occasions. The service was wonderful, the ambiance is cozy but alive. Make sure to call ahead and get a reservation over the phone if opentable looks booked. Their lunch special spicy fried chicken is a must have! If you are a party of two or three, ask for the corner booth by the window. Best table in the house.
Revise this with your best effort: Out of all the remarkable restaurants we explored in New Orleans, this particular gem unquestionably stole our hearts. To be more precise, I indulged in their delectable offerings for both lunch and dinner on distinct occasions. The service provided was truly exceptional, and the inviting atmosphere exuded a uniquely cozy yet vibrant vibe. It is advisable to prearrange a reservation via phone should OpenTable appear to be fully booked. Without a doubt, their lunch special featuring the tantalizing spicy fried chicken is an absolute must-try! For parties consisting of two or three individuals, I highly recommend requesting the coveted corner booth by the window – undoubtedly the pinnacle of dining experiences at this charming establishment.

input:
City Parkの近くにある激安かき氷屋さん。シェーブドアイスっていったほうがいいね！
特に夏のニューオーリンズはジメジメして暑いから、公園に行った後にここでかき氷とか最高だと思う！

味の種類は半端なく多いです！50以上はあったはず！
そしてなんといっても安い！ぼくは一番安いチョイスのレギュラーかき氷のスモールを頼みましたが、スモールでも結構十分だと思います。そして値段はたったの$1.50. 安い！！

トッピングをしても５ドル以上はいかないはず。
夏のうだる暑さには、最高のチョイスだと思います！
Revise this with your best effort:
There's an inexpensive shaved ice shop near City Park. Shaved ice sounds better, don't you think? Especially in the hot and humid summers of New Orleans, I believe it's the perfect treat after a visit to the park!

They have an incredible variety of flavors! I'm pretty sure there were over 50 options! And the best part is that it's cheap! I ordered the smallest size of the regular shaved ice, called the "small," and it was still quite satisfying. And the price? Just $1.50. So affordable!!

Even with toppings, it shouldn't cost more than $5. I think it's the perfect choice to beat the scorching heat of summer!

input: Mr. X has amazing flavor and overall a pretty friendly staff. The wait time for carry out is on average about 20 minutes, which is way better than a 45 minute wait at chain pizzerias. I get the hand-tossed crust comparable to traditional NY style pizza, and has excellent flavor and texture!
Revise this with your best effort: Mr. X offers an extraordinary dining experience with an exceptional flavor palate complemented by an incredibly friendly staff. Unlike chain pizzerias where one would typically endure a tedious 45-minute wait, the average wait time for carry out at Mr. X is impressively reduced to a mere 20 minutes. Their hand-tossed crust, evocative of the traditional NY style, delivers a delightful combination of delectable flavor and satisfying texture.

input:
First time being here.  It was a nice place but empty.  Had one old man sitting in there, then us two 40 somethings, then another old man.  That was it.   We came during happy hour, basically waiting for Snake and Jakes to open up so we came here to kill some time.  

Beer selection was nice, Magic Hat, Fat Tire, Blue Moon, etc.  Prices were ok too.

Lotsa dark woods and a few TVs and a lonely but attractive bartender that was very nice.  

Nothing bad to say about this place other than it was kinda dead.  It was very clean looking and nicely decorated, just kinda boring.
Revise this with your best effort:
This was my first time visiting this establishment and I found it to be quite pleasant, although it seemed rather empty. Inside, there was only one elderly gentleman occupying a seat, followed by our group of two middle-aged individuals, and another elderly man. That was the extent of the crowd. We had arrived during happy hour, as we were simply waiting for Snake and Jakes to open up, so we decided to pass the time here.

I must commend the establishment on their impressive beer selection, featuring brands such as Magic Hat, Fat Tire, Blue Moon, and more. Additionally, the prices were reasonable, which was quite satisfying.

The ambience of the place consisted of a plethora of dark wooden furniture, a few televisions, and an attractive bartender who, despite the scarcity of customers, displayed excellent attentiveness and friendliness.

In all honesty, I have no major complaints about this place other than the fact that it was somewhat lifeless. The cleanliness and tasteful decoration were noticeable, but it lacked excitement and stimulation.

input:
i dont know what has happened to the in store service in this place!  We have been down here for a few weeks now and have been here 6 times.Only once was the order completed without a screw up!

Today 2 tall decaf coffees took close to 20 minutes.By then our bagels were cold.First i was told the decaf was "brewing' and then i was told there was something 'wrong" with the brewer? After 15 minutes i was offered a decaf americano.
Before we left i politely told a fellow behind the counter the service was abominable and he said 'well we can only store 2 vente size decafs at a time? HUH? I asked if the management knew about this and he just shrugged.
Clearly this staff has never been trained to make it right for the customer.No apology.No coupon.Just a convoluted story.
 
Amazing how you can have numerous people running around a store but you cant get the simplest order straight My next visit to a Starbucks will certainly not be this one.
Revise this with your best effort:
I am extremely disappointed with the in-store service at this particular location. Despite visiting multiple times over the past few weeks, we have only received our order correctly once. Today, it took nearly 20 minutes for our two tall decaf coffees, resulting in cold bagels by the time they arrived.

Initially, I was informed that the decaf was "brewing," but then I was told that there was an issue with the brewer. After 15 minutes, I was offered a decaf americano instead. As we were about to leave, I politely expressed my disappointment to one of the staff members, who nonchalantly mentioned that they can only store two vente size decafs at a time. I was taken aback by this explanation and asked if the management was aware, to which he simply shrugged.

It is evident that the staff at this location have not been properly trained in providing satisfactory customer service. There was no apology or gesture of goodwill, just a convoluted story. It is astonishing that despite having numerous employees bustling around the store, they cannot manage to fulfill a straightforward order. I can assure you that my next visit to a Starbucks will not be to this particular location.

input:
As a double date with a good long lost friend for a relaxing evening dinner, we were surprised in early august to not get reservations until 8. 
So we arrived an hour early and had drinks in the lobby while the piano man played beautifully. The bartender was a bit slow at first but kept us well tended. 
Our table in the corner against the glass was ready early and we enjoyed watching the rays chase fish around the bay as the sun set.  
I started with the tasty crab and corn chowder but was a bit disappointed with al dente potatoes in the bowl. 
Wife ordered the scallops which were superb as was my crab stuffed grouper. But my rice was also inadequately cooked. 
Creve brûlée was excellent as was Tim's attentive service. 
Worth going again, but they need to get all the parts of the dishes correct to get 5 stars.
Revise this with your best effort:
My long-lost friend and I had the pleasure of going on a double date in early August. We were both looking forward to a relaxing evening dinner, but were surprised to find that the only available reservation was at 8 o'clock. Not wanting to waste any time, we decided to arrive an hour early and have some drinks in the lobby. As we sipped our cocktails, the talented piano man serenaded us with beautiful melodies. Although the bartender was a bit slow to serve us at first, he eventually made up for it by ensuring our glasses were never empty.

Luckily, our table in the corner, right by the glass windows, was ready ahead of schedule. As we sat down, we couldn't help but be captivated by the stunning view of the bay. The sun began its descent, casting mesmerizing rays that danced over the water, creating a picturesque scene.

To start off the meal, I ordered the crab and corn chowder, which turned out to be quite tasty. However, I was slightly disappointed by the al dente potatoes in the bowl. On the other hand, my wife made an excellent choice by selecting the scallops, which were cooked to perfection. As for myself, I thoroughly enjoyed the crab stuffed grouper, although the rice accompanying it unfortunately lacked sufficient cooking.

When it came time for dessert, we couldn't resist indulging in the delectable crème brûlée. It was truly a treat for our taste buds. Throughout the evening, our server Tim provided impeccable service, attending to our every need. His attentiveness added to the overall enjoyable experience.

While the restaurant certainly had its highlights, there were a few aspects that could be improved to warrant a perfect rating. Despite this, I believe it is worth returning to in the future. With a little more attention to detail in preparing each component of the dishes, they have the potential to earn a solid five-star status.

input: My wife and I visited this hidden gem today and were not let down. The shop was clean, bright, colorful, and comfortable. We were able to sample all the flavors, listen to the story of how they came about, and walked off with many bags of deliciousness. The owners there were so kind. They took the time to understand exactly what kind of foods we enjoy to match us up with the perfect popcorn. Definitely coming back soon!
Revise this with your best effort:
My wife and I had the pleasure of discovering this hidden gem today, and it surpassed all our expectations. The shop itself exuded a sense of cleanliness, radiating with vibrant colors that immediately caught our attention. It was a delightful and cozy environment to explore. 

One of the highlights of our visit was the opportunity to sample all the intriguing popcorn flavors available. The owners, taking immense pride in their craft, enthusiastically shared the story behind each unique creation. This personal touch added depth to our experience, making it truly memorable. 

Impressed by the array of options, we couldn't resist walking away with numerous bags of these delectable treats. The flavors were simply unparalleled, each bite a symphony of taste and texture that lingered on our palates. 

To our delight, it was evident that the owners genuinely cared about their customers. They invested time and effort to understand our preferences, ensuring that we were matched with the perfect popcorn choice. The kindness and attention to detail they demonstrated further solidified our admiration for this establishment.

As a result of this extraordinary experience, we have already made the decision to return soon. The blend of exceptional flavors, warm atmosphere, and personalized service make this place a true gem amidst a sea of ordinary.

input: A really cute new coffee shop in town. We stopped here in the morning to get a much needed caffeine break. Who's warm day so we opted to get an iced coffee. We had many options on the type of milk and sweetener is available. They had limited food items available being mostly donuts this morning. We opted for a piece of the vegan banana bread to share. Iced coffee came out quickly and are banana bread and we went outside to sit with and realize there is no area connected to this restaurant for outdoor seating. The restaurant next-door however was not yet open so we sat at one of their tables thinking no one would mind. It would be nice if the coffee house itself had its own outdoor seating. Are iced coffee was very good and hit the spot. The vegan banana bread was good but seemed very dense to me. I'll be back another time to try some more of the fancy coffee they have available here. I'm hoping that they will add to the food menu as well as a try to not eat donuts most days. Maybe a breakfast sandwich or some other option than a pastry would be good.
Revise this with your best effort: We stumbled upon a charming new coffee shop in town that had our hearts fluttering. Seeking a much-needed caffeine boost, we ventured inside on a warm day, opting for a refreshing iced coffee. With a variety of milk and sweeteners to choose from, the customization options were plentiful. Unfortunately, the food choices were limited, with only a tempting array of donuts available that morning. Nonetheless, we decided to indulge in a slice of vegan banana bread to share. As the iced coffee arrived promptly, we grabbed our banana bread and made our way outside, only to realize that the shop lacked its own outdoor seating area. However, since the neighboring restaurant was not yet open, we shamelessly occupied one of their tables, hoping nobody would object. It would be delightful if the coffee house provided its own outdoor seating in the future. Nevertheless, our iced coffee hit the spot and proved to be exceptional. On the other hand, the vegan banana bread, while enjoyable, seemed a tad too dense for my liking. Nonetheless, I am eager to return and explore the vast selection of fancy coffees they have on offer. Additionally, I hope that the menu expands to include more than just pastries, perhaps offering a delightful breakfast sandwich or other tasty alternatives. After all, it's always a wiser choice to refrain from indulging in donuts on a daily basis.

input: I went here after a recommendation that this is "the best coffee place in philly" and I'm so glad I checked it out! The cafe area itself is super nice & clean. They also offer tap and sparking water to customers which is awesome. Prices are very reasonable and the staff is super friendly. My friend and I chatted with one of the baristas for a few minutes and he gave us some pro-tips on how to make a killer espresso. I will definitely be coming back here again soon!
Revise this with your best effort: After receiving a commendation dubbing this spot as "the ultimate coffee haven in Philadelphia," I decided to pay it a visit, and it did not disappoint! The ambiance of the café is incredibly inviting and immaculately maintained. To add to that, they even provide complimentary tap and sparkling water to their patrons, which is absolutely delightful. The prices are reasonable, offering excellent value for money, and the staff is exceptionally warm and welcoming. During my visit, my friend and I had the pleasure of conversing with one of the talented baristas, who graciously shared some insider tips on crafting an exemplary espresso. Without a doubt, I will be back here in the near future to relish this delightful experience once again!

input: It's a college-town bar, what do you expect? Lol. Alcohol, pub/bar food, good tap selection, good atmosphere and specials. A Villanova tradition. It's not an upscale bar, or a great place to grab lunch. It is what it is, a bar!
Revise this with your best effort: Welcome to our college-town bar, where expectations are straightforward! With a wide range of alcoholic beverages, delectable pub/bar food, an impressive selection of taps, and an inviting atmosphere, we aim to offer everything you desire for a memorable night out. Consider it a cherished Villanova tradition, embodying the essence of a classic bar experience. While we may not boast an upscale ambiance or specialize in lunch options, we embrace our identity as a quintessential bar that knows exactly what it is all about!

input: Great customer service! Mary was a great help- helped me pick out frames and she was extremely personable! From the time I walked in the store, I was greeted with smiles and hellos! I will be back in the future!
Revise this with your best effort: Outstanding customer service! Mary went above and beyond by assisting me in selecting frames, and her friendly and personable approach greatly enhanced my shopping experience. The moment I stepped into the store, I received warm greetings and hellos from the staff. Without a doubt, I will be returning here for my future needs.

input:
Simply stated...They are true to their word as it relates to having discounted furniture that is less expensive than your name brand furniture stores. The staff was friendly, they definitely don't follow you around the store, however, they get a ding for customer service because they don't seem to be as knowledgeable about the furniture products.

Furniture quality is a mix ranging from low to moderate quality.  

At the end of the day, if you are looking for less expensive furniture or to get a good deal or to find a unique accent pieces this is the place to be!  I mean...I saw "the same" sectional for $1,000 less than the name brand store.   Now that's a deal!!!
Revise this with your best effort: In summary, this store lives up to their promise of offering discounted furniture that is more affordable than traditional name brand stores. The staff is friendly and non-intrusive, although their knowledge about the furniture products could be improved. The quality of the furniture varies from low to moderate. However, if you are searching for affordable furniture, great deals, or unique accent pieces, this store is the ideal place to visit. As evidence, I even found a sectional sofa priced $1,000 less than what the name brand store was offering. That's certainly an extraordinary bargain!

input: I have been here numerous times for brunch, dinner and take out during lunch time hours. Staff is always friendly and the food is delicious.
Revise this with your best effort: I have frequented this establishment on numerous occasions for brunch, dinner, and even takeaway during lunchtime hours. Without fail, the staff consistently exudes friendliness, and the culinary offerings never fail to astound with their delightful flavors.

input: Amazing dinner.  What a unique menu.  The service was top notch.  Adrian was our server and she was a delight.  I had the endive and beet salad - lovely.  And then the tongue.  Not what my grandmother made and that's okay.  This was spectacular.  Good wine list and yummy dessert.  The meal was wonderful and I'll be back next time I'm in town.  Bravo!!!
Revise this with your best effort: The dinner was absolutely remarkable. The menu offered a truly distinctive experience. The service received was nothing short of exceptional, and our server, Adrian, was an absolute delight. I decided to start with the endive and beet salad, which was simply lovely. However, it was the surprising choice of tongue for my main course that truly astonished me. It was far from my grandmother's traditional recipe, yet I found it to be nothing short of spectacular.
