To complement the exquisite meal, the wine list was quite impressive, and the dessert was delectably mouthwatering. Overall, the dining experience was truly wonderful, leaving me eager to return the next time I find myself in town. Bravo to all involved for an outstanding evening!

input: Do not waste your time and money on this place. The "food" is what you might expect from a small town Chi-Chi's.
Revise this with your best effort: Save yourself the disappointment and avoid investing your valuable time and hard-earned money at this establishment. The quality of the food offered here hardly surpasses that of a typical small town Chi-Chi's eatery.

input:
Cozy and family friendly restaurant. I came here for a private engagement party, where the bride and groom to be had arranged for special menus and baked all of their desserts. There were a few booth tables reserved for presents, wine, and desserts. No room for side tables like in an actual special events space.

The wait staff was nice. From the limited menu, I picked the Penne Fellini, which has prosciutto di parma, peas, onions, and light cream sauce. The whole dish was literally this pasta swimming in sauce. It may have had a light cream flavor, but it was ladled heavily onto the pasta. I didn't have a desire to consume an entire meal of this, so I ended up not finishing.

It was a fun celebration, and we were really there for the friends and family, not the food. Oh, and we also had the bruschetta and salad, neither of which was very memorable. I wouldn't be thrilled to come back here, but I think it's awesome that they turned the whole restaurant into a venue for such a special occasion!
Revise this with your best effort:
This charming and family-friendly establishment provided the perfect setting for a private engagement party. The bride and groom had gone to great lengths to organize special menus and even personally baked all the desserts. Although the space did not have separate side tables commonly found in event spaces, a few booth tables were reserved for presents, wine, and desserts.

The wait staff was pleasant and attentive. After perusing the limited menu, I decided to try their Penne Fellini, a delightful combination of prosciutto di parma, peas, onions, and a light cream sauce. However, I found the dish overwhelmed by an excessive amount of sauce, drowning the pasta. While it had a mild cream flavor, the heavy ladling made it less enjoyable, and I couldn't bring myself to finish it.

Despite the underwhelming culinary experience, the celebration itself was a joyful affair, with the focus primarily on the presence of friends and family. The bruschetta and salad that we also indulged in were forgettable, lacking any standout elements. While I wouldn't be enthused about returning to this particular restaurant, I do appreciate the effort made to transform the entire venue into a charming setting for such a remarkable occasion.

input: We are having a recall fixed on our 1999 Nissan Pathfinder. The staff is very friendly and they keep you updated. We were treated the same as somebody buying a new car. Highly recommend!
Revise this with your best effort: We recently took our 1999 Nissan Pathfinder in for a recall repair and had an exceptional experience. The staff at the service center were incredibly friendly and made sure to keep us updated throughout the entire process. What impressed us the most was that they treated us with the same level of care and attention as someone purchasing a brand new car. We highly recommend their services without hesitation!

input:
This place is the epitome of a great hole in the wall find.  From  the  70s vintage floral upholstery  to the back entrance off the alley, it undersells it self and sets you up for a great surprise.  The food is good -- not fancy, not at all pretentious - but good. 

A group from work made the trek on the coldest day of the year and we were rewarded for our efforts -- the chicken hot pot was the best example this dish I have ever had.  The seafood dish with shrimp, scallops and squid was very generous for the price of about $10. The beef in black bean sauce was nice and spicy.  

I will certainly return, but only with adventurous companions.
Revise this with your best effort:
This place is the prime example of an incredible hidden gem. From the retro floral upholstery straight out of the 70s to the inconspicuous entrance through the alley, it downplays its worth and surprises you in the best way possible. The food here is not extravagant or snobbish, but it exceeds expectations with its simplicity.

A group of us from work decided to venture out on the coldest day of the year, and our persistence paid off. The chicken hot pot turned out to be the epitome of this dish, surpassing any other versions I had tried before. The seafood dish, packed with shrimp, scallops, and squid, was an absolute steal at a mere $10. The spicy beef in black bean sauce was a flavorful delight.

Needless to say, I will definitely be returning, but only alongside adventurous companions who are open to new experiences.

input:
I k ow looking at the description, this may seem like a festival you wouldn't want to go to.  But trust me, you really really are missing out on a fun weekend afternoon.  I really enjoyed watching the dances performances - some of the dances were absolutely breathtaking.  This year was the first time I visited, but I'll make a point to go every year I am in town.

The best part of this place was the food - yes the lines are long.  but it is definitely worth the wait.  I remember standing in line waiting in anticipation to be able to order the gyros.  My hungry stomach told me a full eternity had passed before we got to the front, but my watch said it was only a few short minutes.  They serve the food very quickly, so do not be discouraged by a long line.  Also, they have menus that tell you exactly what they serve at each of the stalls.  So make sure you double check because you got end p in a line that only has a couple of options.  My two favorite foods from this place were the gyros and the spankopitas.  Another thing I would suggest is coming with a group that is willing to share - that way you get to try a little of everything.  Definitely a great way to spend Labor Day weekend (and an activity that I think the little ones would enjoy).
Revise this with your best effort:
I understand that at first glance, this festival might not appear to be appealing to you. However, trust me when I say that you are truly missing out on a fantastic weekend afternoon. What stood out to me the most were the dance performances - some of them were truly mesmerizing. Although this was my first time attending, I have decided that I will make it a tradition to come back every year while I am in town.

Now, let's talk about the highlight of this event: the food. Yes, the lines might be long, but I can assure you that the wait is definitely worth it. I vividly remember eagerly standing in line, patiently waiting to order my mouthwatering gyros. Although my stomach rumbled impatiently, it felt like only a few minutes had passed, even though my watch revealed a longer duration. The food is served promptly, so don't let a lengthy queue discourage you. Moreover, each stall has menus that clearly list their offerings, so make sure to double-check to ensure you join the right line. My personal favorites were the gyros and the spankopitas. Additionally, I highly recommend attending with a group of friends who are open to sharing dishes, as it allows you to savor a little bit of everything. This event is undoubtedly a wonderful way to enjoy the Labor Day weekend, and it is also suitable for young ones who will surely find it entertaining.

input: The food here is tasty - love the brisket and the cheese grits. BUT - we have had terrible luck with take out. Tried it three times, and an item was missing every time. A disappointing blemish on an otherwise fine restaurant.
Revise this with your best effort: I am absolutely in love with the delicious food served here, particularly the mouthwatering brisket and delectable cheese grits. However, when it comes to their take out service, we have unfortunately experienced some rather disheartening issues. Despite giving it a shot on three separate occasions, there was an item missing from our order every single time. This consistent letdown is truly disappointing and serves as a regrettable stain on an otherwise exceptional restaurant.

input: Provi is such a wonderful person I came here because of her. The chipotle chicken avocado sandwich and chicken noodle soup is just to die for.
Revise this with your best effort: I was drawn to this place because of the amazing person, Provi. Her warm and welcoming nature made my experience so delightful. Let me tell you, the chipotle chicken avocado sandwich and chicken noodle soup they serve are absolutely incredible and worth raving about!

input:
FOOD REVIEW

If you're looking for quality meal that is quick and affordable, the Fountain has you covered. The menu isn't extensive, but it's got a good amount of inexpensive sandwiches, salads, and soups.  

Their Cuban Sandwich ($10 w/ side) was pretty excellent.  The bread wasn't the traditional panini-style, but a French baguette...it was still great and had a little crispness to it.  All the main ingredients (meat, mustard, pickles, cheese) were in good balance.  As a Florida boy who loves his Cuban sandwiches, I would definitely recommend this.

I also tried a bit of their Royal Grille, a grilled-chese sandwich with several cheeses, as well as apple slices, on whole grain wheat bread ($8.50 w/ side, extra to add ham/turkey).  It was damn good and hit the grilled cheese craving just right.  A side salad was also done well.

For my side, I chose their "spicy carrots" which sounded unique.  It consists of sliced raw carrots that have been marinated in a tangy dressing with crushed red pepper, served in a cup. The carrots were cold and crisp and the flavors were fantastic.  The spice was just enough to be pleasant.  I would definitely get these again.

Our food came out super quick and our service was great.  I'm looking forward to trying a couple more items and bumping this up to 5 stars.
Revise this with your best effort:
FOOD REVIEW

If you're searching for a quick and affordable meal without compromising on quality, the Fountain is the place to go. While their menu might not be extensive, it offers a good selection of inexpensive sandwiches, salads, and soups.

One standout item was their Cuban Sandwich ($10 with a side). Although it deviated from the traditional panini-style by using a French baguette, it was still excellent with a delightful crispness. The combination of meat, mustard, pickles, and cheese was perfectly balanced. As someone from Florida who appreciates a good Cuban sandwich, I highly recommend it.

I also had the opportunity to sample their Royal Grille, a grilled cheese sandwich featuring multiple cheeses and apple slices, served on whole grain wheat bread ($8.50 with a side, with the option to add ham or turkey for an additional charge). It was absolutely delicious and fulfilled all my grilled cheese cravings. The side salad was also well-executed.

For my side dish, I opted for the "spicy carrots," which caught my attention due to its unique description. These were sliced raw carrots marinated in a tangy dressing with crushed red pepper, served in a cup. The carrots were refreshingly cold and crisp, and the flavor combination was simply fantastic. The level of spice was just right, providing a pleasant kick. I would definitely reorder this dish.

To top it all off, our food arrived promptly, and the service was exceptional. I can't wait to explore a few more items on the menu and give this place a well-deserved 5-star rating.

input:
Burger Up is, by far, one of our favorite restaurants in the Nashville area.  It has a cool hipster vibe, without being annoying :)  The burgers are outstanding, and there are endless options, whether you prefer beef, chicken, seafood, or veggie!  I would recommend the Woodstock - the Jack Daniels Maple Ketchup is out of this world, and Benton's bacon is always delicious.  Upgrade to the truffle fries; they're to die for.  Or, if you're a vegetarian, the troyathalon is a great option.  Filling, with great texture and flavor.  As far as drinks go, 12 South Lemonade.

The customer service is also great.  They've always been attentive, but not "on top of you", and they're very knowledgable about their food.  Parking can be a bit difficult at certain times of the day, but it's worth a short walk if necessary.

I would definitely recommend checking it out!
Revise this with your best effort:
Burger Up holds an esteemed place among our cherished dining destinations in the Nashville area. Its attractive hipster ambiance is refreshing, devoid of any bothersome qualities. The burgers presented here surpass all expectations, catering to a diverse array of preferences including beef, chicken, seafood, and veggie options. For an unforgettable experience, the Woodstock burger is an absolute must-try, as the Jack Daniels Maple Ketchup is simply phenomenal, and the Benton's bacon is consistently delightful. You won't regret upgrading to the truffle fries, as they are an unparalleled delight. Vegetarians need not fret as the troyathalon burger offers a remarkable alternative, delivering a satiating experience replete with delightful flavors and textures. For a refreshing sip, the 12 South Lemonade proves to be an excellent choice.

The excellence of their customer service is equally notable. The staff strikes the perfect balance between attentiveness and maintaining a respectable distance, ensuring a seamless dining experience. Their profound knowledge regarding the menu adds an extra layer of enjoyment. It is worth noting that parking can be a bit challenging during peak times, but a brief walk is a small price to pay for the rewarding experience that awaits.

Without hesitation, I strongly urge you to explore what Burger Up has to offer.

input:
I have mix feelings about this place. First, I didn't make a reservation and we waited about 50 minutes to be seated when they told us it will be about 15 to 20 min wait. I probably should'v left and tried the next time since I was not happy when I was seated due to the waiting.

I knew I couldn't eat the full-course meal so we decided to get cheese fondue and one of their entrees. Cheese fondue was delicious. If I go next time, I would probably just get the cheese fondue. =]

And the entree we had.. was some chicken, meat, shrimp, mushrooms, etc. We decided to go with oil instead of broth because that's what our waitress suggested and I didn't really like it. I think I will try the broth next time if I do and see if I like it any better. Except the mushroom with stuffing, others were ok.

We had this private booth which was very romantic and nice. I think this place would be good for people who want privacy and have plenty of time for dinner. We stayed there for 2&1/2 hours excluding the waiting time.
Revise this with your best effort:
I have mixed feelings about this place. Initially, our experience was disappointing as we had not made a reservation and ended up waiting for approximately 50 minutes to be seated, despite being informed that the wait would only be around 15 to 20 minutes. In retrospect, I should have considered leaving and attempting to visit another time, as the frustration from the extended wait lingered even after we were finally seated.

Not wanting to indulge in a full-course meal, we opted for cheese fondue alongside one of their entrees. The cheese fondue surpassed our expectations and left a favorable impression. If I were to revisit in the future, I would likely only order the cheese fondue, as it was truly delightful.

As for the entree, it consisted of chicken, meat, shrimp, mushrooms, and other ingredients. At the recommendation of our waitress, we chose to use oil instead of broth as the cooking medium, but I personally did not find it to my liking. In my next visit, I intend to give the broth a try and see if it better suits my taste. With the exception of the mushroom with stuffing, the other elements of the entree were satisfactory.

We were fortunate enough to secure a private booth, which added a romantic and pleasant touch to our experience. This restaurant would appeal to individuals seeking privacy and those who can allocate ample time for a leisurely dinner. We ended up spending around 2 and a half hours there, excluding the waiting time.

input:
Great Mexican BYOB! I went to Las Cazuelas for the first time for my birthday.  We had a wonderful time.  I was looking for a fun and festive place to go with friends.  This was the perfect choice. We brought our own bottle of tequila, and they made tasty margaritas for the table.  Those were a big hit with my friends, and a cool twist for a Mexican BYOB.  The restaurant is cute.  Plus, the food here is delicious. 

I'm surprised this place doesn't have higher reviews on Yelp, because it far exceeded my expectations... 

The guacamole appetizer was fresh and yummy.  I ordered the shrimp entree with rice and vegetables, and asked for it spicy.  My entrée had an attractive presentation on the plate (i.e. looked classy), and was delicious, well seasoned, and very fresh. On my suggestion, my partner ordered one of their mole sauce dishes (i.e. a sauce usually made from unsweetened chocolate and pureed pumpkin seeds), and it was tasty too. 

I should also note that the waitress was very attentive.  When I placed my order, I explained to her that I have mild lactose intolerance and can't eat much butter or cream (but am okay with cheese), so she had the chef cook the veggies in olive oil, rather than butter.  Thanks for being so cool about accommodating that request!  

The prices are extremely reasonable for fancy and unusual Mexican food, and I love the fact they're a BYOB.  The chef serves creative and inspired cuisine, which has a traditional flair and style to it.  In other words: Don't come here for regular tacos or burritos.  Come here for a fun foodie experience at a reasonable price, and bring tequila for the perk of BYOB Margaritas!
Revise this with your best effort:
Las Cazuelas is an exceptional Mexican BYOB restaurant that left me thoroughly impressed on my birthday celebration. If you're seeking a lively and joyous atmosphere to enjoy with friends, this place is an absolute gem. Our decision to bring our own tequila was a genius move as they concocted delightful margaritas for the entire table, earning rave reviews from everyone. The restaurant itself exudes a charming ambiance, and the food here is simply delectable.

It puzzles me that Las Cazuelas doesn't receive higher ratings on Yelp because it surpassed all of my expectations. The guacamole appetizer was an irresistible combination of freshness and flavor. For my main course, I opted for the shrimp entree accompanied by rice and vegetables, which I requested to be prepared spicy. Not only did it present elegantly, but the flavors were also superbly seasoned and the ingredients showcased remarkable freshness. At my recommendation, my partner ordered one of their signature mole sauce dishes, which proved to be equally delightful.

I must applaud the attentive service of our waitress, who went above and beyond to accommodate my dietary restrictions. When I mentioned my mild lactose intolerance and my aversion to butter and cream (while still being able to enjoy cheese), she ensured that the chef prepared the vegetables using olive oil. Their willingness to accommodate such requests is truly commendable and greatly appreciated.

The pricing at Las Cazuelas is wonderfully reasonable considering the exquisite and unconventional Mexican cuisine they offer. It's important to note that this isn't your typical taqueria or burrito joint. Instead, it's a haven for food enthusiasts seeking an exciting culinary experience at an affordable price. Not to mention, the added bonus of being a BYOB establishment, allowing guests to bring their own tequila for the ultimate margarita experience.

In summary, Las Cazuelas is a fantastic Mexican BYOB restaurant that checks all the boxes for a memorable dining experience. With its charming atmosphere, exceptional cuisine, and attentive service, it's certainly worth a visit. Don't settle for ordinary when you can indulge in extraordinary flavors while experiencing the fun of being able to bring your own beverages.

input: This was one of the greatest meals I have ever had.  The food was delicious and the hospitality was second to none.  The lamb was cooked to perfection, the rice had the perfect amount of spice.  The ability to easily describe the amount of spice made this meal perfect for spicy lovers, but also easy for those with a milder pallet.  All of this is from someone who has historically not been a fan of Pakistani/Indian food.  I would recommend this restaurant to anyone and would encourage a trip to St. Louis just for the food here.
Revise this with your best effort: Without a doubt, this meal has left an indelible mark on my culinary experiences. The exceptional quality of the food exceeded all expectations and the unmatched hospitality provided an extraordinary dining experience. The lamb, meticulously cooked to perfection, exuded unparalleled taste. Furthermore, the rice boasted an ideal blend of spices, striking a harmonious balance that would enthrall even the most zealous spice enthusiasts, while accommodating those with a milder palate. Astonishingly, as an individual who previously held reservations about Pakistani/Indian cuisine, this restaurant has undeniably won me over. I wholeheartedly endorse and suggest this establishment to anyone seeking an exceptional gastronomic experience. In fact, this restaurant's culinary offerings alone warrant a journey to St. Louis.

input: Amazingly awesome! Tried a couple of different things, everything was delicious! Their Bloody Mary was one of the worst I've ever had, but I didn't go there to drink, and besides that not what they are known for. Their mojoto are good tho.
Revise this with your best effort: Absolutely incredible! I had the pleasure of sampling a variety of dishes which were all exceptionally delicious. While the Bloody Mary left much to be desired in my opinion, it's important to note that their main focus is not on beverages. However, their mojitos are absolutely delightful and definitely worth trying.

input:
I'm not really sure why I bother going to other restaurants. 

Every Valentine's Day I try to find some cute, new little BYO for me and my boyfriend to try out and I spend weeks scouring menus and Yelp reviews. 

Every year SOMETHING goes wrong and I get frustrated and pissed off and he always says "Let's go to Jones".

This year was no different. We went out last night (2/12/11...the weekend before Valentines Day) to the BYO I picked out and when I made our reservations, no mention was made that they had a special fixed menu that night consisting SOLELY of seafood, which I am allergic to. As I started to get upset at our table, my boyfriend said "Let's go to Jones".

We got there, were told there was a little bit of a wait, so we sat at the bar for a drink. About 5-10 minutes later they came and got us and sat us at our table. Our waiter (who was WONDERFUL and looked like Jared Leto - extra bonus-) came over and took our order and the food came out perfectly (as usual) and right on time.

We both got the filet, done rare and the spinach it came with was fantastic. The mac and cheese is also an app we get every time and is one of my favorites. I got the deviled eggs for the first time and holy crap they were amazing. I'm gonna say, possibly the best ones I've ever had (sorry, Dad). 

Everything about this restaurant leans towards comfort and it's always done so well. The atmosphere, the staff, the decor, the food, hell even the temperature. I've never had a bad experience at Jones and I don't think I ever will. 

Next year....we'll just go straight to Jones.
Revise this with your best effort:
I have come to the realization that there is truly no point in venturing to other restaurants. Every Valentine's Day, I excitedly explore different cute and charming BYOs for my boyfriend and me to indulge in. I put in weeks of effort, meticulously perusing menus and meticulously analyzing Yelp reviews.

However, without fail, something always manages to go awry, leaving me frustrated and annoyed. Yet, like clockwork, my boyfriend consistently suggests, "Let's just go to Jones."

This year proved to be no exception. Last night (on 2/12/11, precisely the weekend before Valentine's Day), we dined at the BYO establishment I had meticulously selected. Despite making reservations well in advance, they failed to mention their special fixed menu, solely composed of seafood - an allergen for me. Growing increasingly upset at our table, I expressed my disappointment, to which my boyfriend swiftly interjected, "Let's go to Jones."

Our arrival at Jones was met with a brief wait, during which we settled at the bar for a refreshing drink. After a mere 5-10 minutes, they ushered us to our table. Our waiter, who uncannily resembled Jared Leto (an added bonus), greeted us and took our orders. The food arrived flawlessly and punctually, as expected.

Both of us opted for the rare filet, accompanied by delectable spinach. In true tradition, we ordered the mac and cheese as an appetizer, which has always been one of my favorites. This time, I dared to try the deviled eggs, and my goodness, they were absolutely phenomenal - possibly the finest I have ever tasted (apologies to my dad).

Every aspect of Jones exudes a comforting atmosphere, impeccably brought to life through the incredible staff, captivating decor, delectable cuisine, and even the ideal temperature. A negative experience at Jones seems unimaginable, and I genuinely believe it will remain that way.

From now on, let us save ourselves the trouble and head straight to Jones next year.

input: I held my husband's surprise birthday party for about 35 people in the basement bar at Black Sheep. I couldn't have asked for a better experience. From the first call I placed to inquire about hosting the party and spoke with James, the owner, to the night of the party where Adam, our bartender, made sure all went smoothly, everyone I dealt with was fantastic. Overall, a great experience.
Revise this with your best effort: I organized a surprise birthday bash for my husband at the basement bar of Black Sheep, inviting around 35 guests. To say that the entire experience surpassed my expectations would be an understatement. From my very first call to James, the owner, where I inquired about hosting the event, to the actual night of the party where Adam, our dedicated bartender, ensured that everything ran seamlessly, I was consistently impressed with the exceptional service provided by the entire team. Without a doubt, it was an outstanding experience overall.

input: Quack & Cheese is where it is at! We were there for the lunch menu. The duck fries are so delicious. It was my first time there & I ordered the portabello burger. They didn't have the right mushrooms & asked if a substitute was ok. I said sure. But I couldn't eat it. I asked for some kind of sauce & instead they let me order something else. That was so nice. I don't usually complain about anything. I felt like they really catered to our whole party. I would definitely love to come back for a date night.
Revise this with your best effort: Quack & Cheese is the ultimate dining destination! We decided to savor their delightful lunch menu and one dish that truly stood out was the mouthwatering duck fries. Excitement filled the air as it was my first time dining here, and I eagerly opted for the portabello burger. Unfortunately, they were out of the specified mushrooms, but kindly offered a substitute. Despite this effort, the substitute fell short and I couldn't enjoy it. However, when I expressed my disappointment and requested some sauce, they graciously allowed me to order something else instead. This gesture truly impressed me, as I rarely find the level of attentive service they provided. It's evident that they go above and beyond to cater to their guests' needs. I'm already looking forward to returning to Quack & Cheese for a memorable date night experience.

input:
The family and I ate here on Labor Day, 2015.  We wanted to go to another restaurant, but it was closed, so we stopped at Casa Garcia.  The inside of the restaurant is very pleasant.  The fountain is a nice touch.

The chips, salsa and bean dip were very good.  We greatly enjoyed them.  We also all agreed that the tortilla soup was excellent.  It was when the entrees arrived that things went down hill.

The sour cream and guacamole were fresh, but the entrees were just average at best.  The quesadillas had too much cheese and not much else flavor.  

The meal was not bad, but there are better options close by.
Revise this with your best effort:
We dined at Casa Garcia on Labor Day, 2015, after our initial restaurant choice turned out to be closed. Despite our disappointment, we were pleasantly surprised by the ambiance of the restaurant's interior. The addition of a fountain added a nice touch to the overall atmosphere.

Our taste buds were initially satisfied by the delicious chips, salsa, and bean dip. We all thoroughly enjoyed them. Additionally, the tortilla soup surpassed our expectations and left us impressed.

However, our enthusiasm dwindled when our entrees arrived. While the sour cream and guacamole were fresh and satisfying, the main dishes fell short of the mark. The quesadillas were overloaded with cheese, lacking in other flavors that would have enhanced the overall taste.

Overall, our dining experience at Casa Garcia could be categorized as average. Although it did not completely disappoint, we believe there are superior dining options in close proximity worth exploring.

input: Joe's is the place for great seafood! Service was fast and friendly! Clam chowder was great and of course the crab is always amazing! Eat at Joe's!! Love this place!
Revise this with your best effort: Experience the finest seafood at Joe's, where every bite is a delight! The service provided is unparalleled, combining both speed and friendliness. Indulge in the delectable clam chowder, which surpasses expectations. And, as always, the crab offered at Joe's leaves a lasting impression with its unbeatable taste. Don't hesitate to dine at this phenomenal establishment – Joe's is truly a remarkable culinary gem!

input: Nothing makes my busy day easy like my iced coffee at Starbucks and this location botched it up for me:( see my photo yup those are coffee grinds at the bottom a whole bunch of coffee grinds:( yuck yuck!
Revise this with your best effort: My hectic day always finds relief in a refreshing iced coffee from Starbucks, but unfortunately, this particular location completely mishandled my order. Take a look at the photo I captured; it's evident that the bottom of my cup is filled with an unpleasant abundance of coffee grinds. It's truly disappointing and unappetizing.

input:

input: This place was awesome. Clean, beautiful and the food was outstanding. The staff was lovely, very attentive and accommodating. I brought my 11 month old there to meet a friend for lunch and we had a great time and a great meal. This is my new favorite joint.
Revise this with your best effort: I was absolutely blown away by this place. Impeccably clean, exquisitely beautiful, and the food was nothing short of outstanding. The staff went above and beyond, radiating warmth and attentiveness. Despite bringing my 11-month-old along to meet a friend for lunch, the experience was seamless, and we both had a wonderful time enjoying a truly fantastic meal. Without a doubt, this has immediately become my go-to spot, a newfound favorite joint.

input: Awesome experience! Just ate here for the first time and wow it was good. Our meals came very quickly and tasted great! Our waiter, Lyndel, was very amazing and made our experience memorable. The restaurant felt a tad bit cramped, but other than that everything was awesome.
Revise this with your best effort: Absolutely incredible experience! Just had the pleasure of dining here for the first time and I am blown away by the quality. Our meals arrived promptly and were absolutely delicious. Our exceptional waiter, Lyndel, truly elevated our experience and created lasting memories. Though the restaurant was slightly cramped, everything else was phenomenal.

input: I started coming to Moreno when I moved back to Brandon and had an itch for Alessi Bakery but didn't  want to drive too far. Someone told us about Moreno so we gave them a shot! A great, small, FAMILY-OWNED (love it!) bakery right in the heart of Brandon. They make a HUGE variety of baked goods from fresh bread to huge cupcakes to flan and cookies! They also have the best freshly made cuban sandwich with their own special sauce spread! My favorite thing to get here are the almond sticks. I am a huge fan of anything almond, but these are so fresh with loads of almonds and almond flavoring! If you have a sweet tooth, this is DEFINITELY the place to go!
Revise this with your best effort: When I moved back to Brandon and was craving Alessi Bakery, I stumbled upon Moreno and decided to give it a try. To my delight, Moreno turned out to be a fantastic, small, and charming family-owned bakery right in the heart of Brandon. Their extensive range of baked goods, from delectable bread to colossal cupcakes and delightful flan, is truly impressive. Additionally, their freshly made Cuban sandwich, topped with their own special sauce spread, is simply unparalleled. However, my personal favorite at Moreno is their almond sticks. As an avid admirer of everything almond, I can confidently say that these sticks are superbly fresh and bursting with almond flavor, thanks to an abundance of almonds and almond essence. If you have a sweet tooth, a trip to Moreno is an absolute must.

input: I wish I could give this zero stars, this gave my husband and kid a really really bad stomach ache after eating here. This used to be our favorite Chinese restaurant but not anymore. Never eat here. Also on another note the delivery really slow.
Revise this with your best effort: Unfortunately, I cannot give this establishment anything more than zero stars. Regrettably, my husband and child experienced severe stomach discomfort after consuming their food. Previously, this place held a special place in our hearts as our go-to Chinese restaurant; however, our sentiment has dramatically changed. I strongly advise against dining at this establishment. Moreover, I feel compelled to mention that their delivery service is exceptionally slow.

input: I called to get a price on getting a flat fixed $35.99WTH! Is this price legal... Smdh in a city where they don't EVEN pay livable wages.... #tragic ..smdh
Revise this with your best effort: I contacted a shop to inquire about the cost of fixing a flat tire, and I was quoted an astonishing $35.99! Unbelievable! I can't help but question the legality of such a price, especially considering the city's inability to provide livable wages. It's truly disheartening and frustrating. #Tragic! Shaking my head.

input: Good food, great milkshakes!! Loved it! I will definitely be back next time I am in town!!
Revise this with your best effort: The food here is absolutely amazing, and the milkshakes are top-notch! I thoroughly enjoyed my experience and can't wait to revisit when I'm back in town.

input:
I absolutely LOVE the convenience of having a groomer come to me instead of dragging all my dogs to a groomer.  The price of grooming is very competitive to other groomers in the area, if not a bit better.  So, how can you beat that!?!

I pay $60 for my 65lb dog, and $40 for my smaller dogs.  This includes a bath, ear cleaning, nail grind, and anal gland expression if needed.  All of my dogs are short-haired, so nothing too fancy.

My only drawbacks are:  no teeth cleaning; the price is the same regardless if the dog is 5 lbs or 40 lbs; and the feeling of judgement for not taking better care of my dogs (but that could just be me).
Revise this with your best effort:
I absolutely adore the convenience of having a professional groomer come to my doorstep instead of the daunting task of transporting all my beloved dogs to a grooming salon. Not only does this save me time and effort, but the pricing for the grooming services offered is extremely competitive compared to other groomers in the area, if not slightly better. How can one possibly resist such a fantastic deal?

For my 65lb dog, I happily pay a reasonable fee of $60, and for my smaller furry companions, the cost is a budget-friendly $40. This wonderful package includes a thorough bath, meticulous ear cleaning, nail grinding, and even gentle anal gland expression if required. As my furry friends boast short hair, I don't require any extravagant styling or grooming techniques.

While I appreciate the top-notch service provided, it's important to note the limitations. Regrettably, teeth cleaning is not included in the package. Additionally, the pricing remains the same regardless of whether the dog weighs a mere 5 pounds or a substantial 40 pounds. Lastly, there might be a slight feeling of judgment regarding my pet care choices, but I understand this may simply be my own perception.

In conclusion, the convenience, affordability, and comprehensive grooming services offered by this mobile groomer are simply unbeatable. Though there are a few downsides, the overall experience and convenience it provides far outweigh any minor drawbacks.

input: Thursday night and wonderful life music --- James Taylor style. Food is great and service friendly. Yummy red Sangria too!
Revise this with your best effort: Enjoy a delightful Thursday evening immersed in the enchanting melodies reminiscent of James Taylor. input:
I came here for lunch and was very disappointed.  Bland and expensive for the amount and quality of food we received.  Lukewarm, nearly tasteless (how can Mexican food be tasteless???) and a total waste of my lunch hour.

Meh.  Do yourself a favor and support the many authentic, locally owned, non-chain Mexican restaurants.

I was wishing that I had gone to Mi Pueblo instead.......
Revise this with your best effort:
I visited this establishment for lunch and unfortunately, my experience was extremely disappointing. The food was bland and overpriced considering the small portion sizes and lack of quality. Honestly, I suggest that you do yourself a favor and show your support to the numerous authentic, locally owned, non-chain Mexican restaurants instead. Trust me, you won't regret it. In fact, I found myself wishing I had chosen to dine at Mi Pueblo instead...

input: Awesome place. Great beer selection, music and friendly service. Check it out!
Revise this with your best effort: Come and experience an incredible place! It boasts an exceptional variety of beer, a remarkable lineup of music, and a welcoming atmosphere provided by our friendly staff. Don't miss out on this fantastic opportunity! Visit us today and you won't be disappointed.

input: I foresee this bar becoming a new local fav, great spot for amazing cocktails and you must try the bar burger, it's the best burger in town! Brunch is also delicious. I would recommend to anyone, whether you're a local or just passing through!
Revise this with your best effort: I predict that this bar will soon establish itself as a beloved local favorite, offering an excellent atmosphere to enjoy outstanding cocktails. You absolutely must not miss the opportunity to try their exceptional bar burger, widely regarded as the finest in town. Moreover, their brunch menu is simply delectable. I highly recommend this establishment to all, regardless of whether you reside here or are merely visiting passing through.

input:
I am really sorry for writing this, but I have been to this place a couple times in which I had ok experiences. It rarely gives you a good-looking manicure. 
However, today's experience was awful. She gave me 10 different nail shapes, no hand lotion, nothing. I still have my cuticles, and am very upset. I'll stop going to this place. Although it is a beautiful salon with lots of polish options, I don't think they have many professionals.
Revise this with your best effort:
I sincerely apologize for composing this message, but I must express my dissatisfaction with the recurring disappointments I have experienced at this establishment. While my previous visits were somewhat satisfactory, obtaining a well-executed manicure at this place is a rarity. 

Regrettably, today's experience was exceptionally terrible. The technician provided me with an assortment of ten different nail shapes, completely disregarding the use of hand lotion or any other essential treatments. input: Good food excellent service, everything was delicious. We ordered firecracker shrimp which came to us quickly we sat at the bar because it was a 3 hour wait to the formal side of the restaurant. They told us you can eat the full menu in the bar area which was true. There was a really good band playing live music, the servers were attentive and we would definitely go back. We ordered alcohol, appetizer, entree, salad, and dessert. We had the salmon and swordfish both were great! Also had HUGE fish tank from famous tv show tanked. Nice views.
Revise this with your best effort: The dining experience at this establishment was truly exceptional, as we were met with remarkable service and delectable cuisine. One dish that stood out was the firecracker shrimp, which arrived promptly despite us being seated at the bar due to a lengthy wait for a table in the formal dining area. To our delight, we discovered that the full menu was available in the bar, just as we had been informed. Additionally, the live music performed by an incredibly talented band added to the vibrant atmosphere. The attentive servers further enhanced our dining pleasure, leaving us with the certainty that we would eagerly return. Our order encompassed a variety of options, including alcoholic beverages, appetizers, entrees, salads, and desserts. Of particular note were the exquisitely prepared salmon and swordfish dishes, both of which left a lasting impression. Moreover, the presence of a large fish tank, famously featured on the television show, "Tanked," provided an interesting and enjoyable view. Indeed, the overall experience was enhanced by the pleasing aesthetics of the establishment.

input: The atmosphere was nice and small. Very busy for brunch, expect at least a 30-45 minute wait. I recommend the spinach, caramelized onion and goat cheese omelet, but request a little less goat cheese. (this one was way too much, would have been better with 1/2 the amount).  Oh and the fruit was served perfectly ripe. Cash only.
Revise this with your best effort: The ambiance of the place had a pleasant and cozy feel, albeit a bit cramped. The thriving popularity during brunch hours meant a considerable wait of around 30-45 minutes. However, amidst the bustling atmosphere, I highly recommend trying out their delectable spinach, caramelized onion, and goat cheese omelet, albeit with a slight adjustment—asking for a reduced amount of goat cheese. The original serving had an overwhelming quantity, but halving it would have resulted in a more balanced and enjoyable meal. Additionally, the fruit provided was flawlessly ripe, adding a refreshing touch to the dish. Just keep in mind that this establishment operates on a cash-only basis.

input:
I was just passing through Tuscon. Native American inspired breakfast food? I just had to have some :-).  Basically I ended up with amazing and unique food that I wish I could have everyday! Five stars!

It took me while to decide what I wanted because there was so many things I wanted. 

Finally, I ended up with the pueblo, which basically is the green corn waffle with eggs the way you want it and a choice of a side (I got chorizo). The waiter told me how to eat it: put the syrup + hot sauce on the waffle and enjoy. But, instead, I ended up making an awesome syrup, hot sauce, egg, chorizo and red sauce tower on my waffle for each bite. It was delicious - try it!!!
Revise this with your best effort:
While passing through Tucson, I couldn't resist trying some Native American inspired breakfast food. And let me tell you, it was absolutely amazing; a culinary experience that I wish I could indulge in every day! This place had such a vast array of options that it took me quite a while to decide what to order.

After much contemplation, I settled on the pueblo dish, which consisted of a delectable green corn waffle accompanied by eggs prepared to my liking, and I chose to have it served with a side of chorizo. The friendly waiter kindly offered some guidance on how to enjoy this delicious creation - by pouring syrup and hot sauce onto the waffle. However, I decided to take it up a notch and crafted a magnificent tower of syrup, hot sauce, eggs, chorizo, and red sauce for every single bite. The result was mind-blowingly delicious! Trust me, you have to give it a try! With its combination of flavors, it was a breakfast unlike any other. Five stars all the way!

input:
Another wonderful stip mall ethnic restruarant!!! This was my first time at a Veitnamese restuarant and I will say that pho is a little bowl of heaven. It was warm and fragrant and with all the condements they bring on the side, easy to customize. We also got BBQ pork sandwiches and they were very tasty. The meat was tender and flavorful and they had fresh herbs on them and some kind of yummy sauce. They only take cash, so make sure you hit the ATM before you go. The food is very reasonably priced though.

This restuarant started my love affair with pho, but I haven't had any as good anywhere else in Nashville.
Revise this with your best effort: Another exceptional ethnic restaurant in the stip mall! This marked my inaugural visit to a Vietnamese establishment, and I must say, pho is an absolute delight. It exudes warmth and an intoxicating aroma, perfectly complemented by the array of condiments provided on the side, allowing for effortless customization. Additionally, we indulged in their BBQ pork sandwiches, which were truly delectable. The meat boasted tenderness and a burst of flavor, adorned with fresh herbs and a tantalizing sauce. It is worth mentioning that this establishment only accepts cash, so ensure you visit an ATM beforehand. However, the reasonably priced dishes more than make up for this minor inconvenience. I have yet to encounter pho as exceptional as this elsewhere in Nashville, solidifying this restaurant as the catalyst for my unyielding infatuation with this Vietnamese delicacy.

input:
This shop is a slice of Disney beauty and magic hiding on the edge of Broad Ripple, and a MUST stop of sweets, treats, and dreaminess. Your Instagram needs this place. Hands down the ~best~ red velvet cake of my life.

Appearance: The Cake Bake Shop is a beautifully decorated, small white house with a captivating design. The flowers around the sign make it an #instaworthy post for sure, and when the weather is nice, the outdoor seating must be gorgeous.

Inside the Cake Shop will take your breath away, light airy colors and flowers and twinkling lights. This isn't the kind of cake shop you do take-out at, you'll want to sit and enjoy. 

Food: I wanted to try the Raspberry Champagne cake, unfortunately one wouldn't be ready for a little while, so I ordered a slice of the Red Velvet  Cake. The floral icing work was so perfect I didn't want to touch it, but I had to because come on it's cake. What I assume must have been cream cheese filling in the middle was decadent and I never wanted the cake to end. ***I felt one slice was plenty for two people, it's HUGE

I was torn between the Rose Cappuccino and the Lavender Latte. I went with the Lavender Latte, hot, and it was stunning, it was a creamy, smooth, not-at-all bitter latte and the hint of lavender was enough to taste but not over powering, it was probably the most perfect coffee I've ever had in my life. 

Price: the coffee is pricy, $6, so not a regular coffee stop for me, but for #treatyoself it's the way to go. The slice of cake was $12 but like I mentioned, it was enough for two people and for how amazing it was, I think it's so worth it.

Customer Service: I mentioned Disney initially because the friendliness, care, and attention of the staff felt just like Disney. They were kind, they helped me decide what to try, and the barista even offered to make me the rose cappuccino if I didn't like the lavender latte after trying it - how sweet! 

I will most definitely think to come here if anyone visits and wants something sweet. This place has my heart and is a hidden gem to anyone who has a sweet tooth!

Check out my #FirstTimeFriday highlight of my visit to The Cake Bake Shop on my Instagram @jordanqjordanq for pictures of everything mentioned above!
Revise this with your best effort:
In the heart of Broad Ripple, there is a hidden gem of a shop that exudes the enchantment and beauty of Disney. The Cake Bake Shop is an absolute must-visit for anyone seeking a slice of sweetness and a taste of pure magic. Your Instagram feed simply won't be complete without this place. Trust me, their red velvet cake is hands down the best I've ever had.

As you approach the Cake Bake Shop, you'll be greeted by a charming white house adorned with captivating designs. The flowers surrounding the sign make it an instant #instaworthy photo spot. And on a nice day, the outdoor seating must be a sight to behold.

Stepping inside the Cake Shop is like entering a whimsical wonderland. The light and airy colors, the flowers, and the twinkling lights create an atmosphere that will take your breath away. This isn't the kind of cake shop where you grab takeout; you'll want to stay and revel in the dreamy surroundings.

When it comes to the delectable delights at the Cake Bake Shop, the choices are tough. I had initially set my heart on trying their Raspberry Champagne cake, but alas, it wouldn't be ready for a little while. In the end, I settled for a slice of their remarkable Red Velvet Cake. The floral icing work was so impeccable that I hesitated to disturb it, but the temptation of cake overpowered my restraint. The cream cheese filling in the middle was a decadent delight. I never wanted the cake to end – it was truly a massive portion that could easily satisfy two people.

Choosing a beverage was just as delightful as picking out the cake. I found myself torn between the Rose Cappuccino and the Lavender Latte. Ultimately, I opted for the Lavender Latte, served hot. It was a stunning creation – a creamy, smooth, and not-at-all-bitter latte with just the perfect hint of lavender. I can confidently say that it was the best coffee I've ever had in my entire life.

Now, I must admit that the prices at the Cake Bake Shop are on the higher side. The coffee set me back $6, which is a bit steep for my regular caffeine fix. However, when it comes to treating yourself, this is definitely the way to go. The slice of cake came with a price tag of $12, but considering its sheer magnificence and the fact that it can easily be shared between two people, I believe it's worth every penny.

The customer service at the Cake Bake Shop deserves a mention. From the moment you walk in, you'll be greeted with the warmth and friendliness that is reminiscent of the Disney experience. The staff goes above and beyond to assist you in making your choices. The barista even offered to prepare the rose cappuccino if I ended up not liking the lavender latte. Such kindness and attentiveness truly made me feel like a valued guest.

When friends or family visit and crave something sweet, I will without a doubt suggest a visit to the Cake Bake Shop. It has won my heart with its delectable creations and impeccable service. This hidden gem is every sweet tooth's dream come true.

To catch a glimpse of my unforgettable visit to The Cake Bake Shop, be sure to head over to my Instagram @jordanqjordanq and check out the highlights from my #FirstTimeFriday. There, you'll find pictures of everything I've mentioned above, capturing the essence of this extraordinary place.

input:
If you like lobster this is the place. Great prices great service and great food. Very casual dining.

Back again to enjoy the Lobster special w 1  1/4 lb lobster,1 # mussels and 1-2# steamers with corn and potatoes for $19.99. See photo. 
Clam chowder so good as is the Ucon lobster roll covered in melted butter.
Revise this with your best effort:
If you have a fondness for lobsters, then this is certainly the place for you. Here, you can indulge in delectable seafood at fantastic prices, accompanied by impeccable service. The atmosphere is notably casual, making it an ideal spot for relaxed dining.

I must mention that I have returned to this establishment, eager to relish their remarkable Lobster special. It consists of a generous 1 1/4 lb lobster, along with a serving of 1 pound of mussels and 1-2 pounds of steamers. This delightful seafood feast is complemented by corn and potatoes, all for a mere $19.99. I have attached a photo for emphasis.

Their clam chowder is an absolute delight, boasting incredible flavors that will leave you satisfied beyond measure. Additionally, I highly recommend trying their Ucon lobster roll, which is elegantly smothered in melted butter, creating a truly heavenly experience.

input: I've only been here to pick up an outpatient, my father.  I was greeted warmly, right away, and though he has a difficult last name, the receptionist had no problem finding him. He was out in approximately 5 minutes happy and mostly pain-free from the injection he received.  I wouldn't be able to give this facility a full review, but they treated me well while I waited.

input: Their mojo chicken sandwich is the best! It's an intimate restaurant with a hint of carribean and spanish flair. It has a laid back atmosphere and great service. The food is affordable and the staff are super friendly.

input: Not really sure what all the hype is about...wasn't overly impressed with the food. I suppose if you are a beer snob, one may appreciate this place. However, most bars are catering to beer snobs now and nothing about this place truly stands out from the other local bars...

input:
Great brewery, friendly staff, nice area outside to sit
My favorite IPA around

input: Delivery issues caused our pizza to be over 30 minutes later than the estimated delivery date.  Pizza finally arrived and was warm at best.  Won't be ordering from this location again.

input:
This is some good motherfuckin ice cream.

Positive:
+Tell me you're serving bananas foster today!
+Freshly made waffle cones
+Establishment doesn't look like a fucking kindergarden.  I can eat ice cream and still feel like an adult
+Owner is a Harvard grad, but isn't a stuck up asshole.  Actually seems pretty down to earth and can hold a conversation with the layman.

Negative:

The only time I really think about this place is after rolling out of Publix and by then I've already got bags of frozen food thawing out and dont have time for ice cream.  Not even some bad ass ice cream.

Hey... even 5 star joints could use some constructive criticism
Revise this with your best effort:
This ice cream is absolutely delectable and top-notch.

Positive:

-Food not prepared as requested (requested sausage links burnt, even after sending them back still not as requested. Eggs requested as over-medium, whites were runny).
-had to ask for refills on coffee.

Revise this with your best effort:
After enduring a 40-minute wait to be seated, our anticipation for a delightful breakfast was quickly dampened by the disappointing experience that followed. To our dismay, the hot breakfast we eagerly awaited arrived at our table, but unfortunately, it had gone cold. Furthermore, our specific instructions for the preparation of our meal were disregarded entirely. Despite specifically requesting well-done sausage links, they were served to us burnt. Even after returning them to the kitchen for corrections, they still failed to meet our expectations. Similarly, our desire for over-medium eggs resulted in runny whites, which was quite displeasing. 

Regrettably, we were also left to repeatedly request coffee refills as our waitress appeared somewhat indifferent to our needs. Her apparent apathy towards the shortcomings of our meal and service only added to our disappointment. 

To our astonishment, the frustration didn't end there. Upon finishing our subpar meal, we found ourselves waiting for over 10 minutes just to receive our check. This extended delay provided us with ample time to reflect on our experience, compose this review, and ultimately share it with others. 

It is disheartening to note that our simple breakfast for two amounted to a staggering $40, which made the overall experience even more difficult to accept.

input:
I eat at Sukho Thai quite a bit, and I don't really get the negative ratings. Is it the most authentic thai place in the area? No. Sometimes I would say they sometimes substitute certain ingredients. It is however usually pretty consistent as far as quality of food and service. 

I usually get the red or green curry, and almost always get it "native thai hot". I have tried other things on the menu, but they are not quite as good. So I stick with what tastes good and works for me. 

The lady that owns the place is very kind and always very gracious to my wife and I. She always recognizes us and serves us promptly. She not only owns the place, but she waits all of the tables most of the time(which I think is pretty impressive). 
The place is beside a go-cart track, so that makes it a little quirky, but it's something I have grown accustomed to. 

The only thing negative I would say is that I wish they had Kee Mao on the menu, because that's my favorite. I usually go to Siam Cafe or Thai Star for that.
Revise this with your best effort:
I frequently dine at Sukho Thai and I find it puzzling that the restaurant has received negative ratings. While it may not be the most authentic Thai eatery in the area, I admit there are times when they substitute certain ingredients. However, the establishment consistently delivers in terms of food quality and service. 

My go-to choices are the red or green curry, always ordered "native Thai hot". Although I have experimented with other dishes on the menu, none quite compare. I prefer to stick with what I know tastes good and satisfies my cravings. 

The proprietor of Sukho Thai, a lovely lady, consistently exhibits kindness and graciously attends to my wife and me. She never fails to recognize us and promptly serves us. I find it quite impressive that she not only owns the place but also personally waits tables most of the time. 

Admittedly, Sukho Thai's location next to a go-kart track adds a quirky charm to the dining experience, but it has become something I have become accustomed to and even appreciate. 

The only downside I would mention is that my favorite dish, Kee Mao, is not on their menu. For that, I usually visit Siam Cafe or Thai Star.

input:
When you dine at Muriel's, check to see if the 2nd level is open for visitors. If so, you can briefly tour the lounge area upstairs (red couches, decorative pieces). There's a wrap-around balcony where you can get a great view of Jackson Square. 

If you're curious, learn why Muriel's is haunted and find out the story behind why there's a table that is always set for two located near the stairs. 

There are two main dining rooms, a middle section (indoor patio dining area) that I personally prefer because it is quieter, and a bar area located at the back near the restrooms. I love the indoor patio dining area because it brings a bit of the outdoors in a quiet indoor setting. 

On my first visit, I ordered from the dinner pre-fix menu which is a great deal (appetizer or soup + entrée + dessert = $40). The seafood gumbo soup was hearty and delicious. The dijon mustard encrusted salmon was cooked perfectly. The bread pudding was a great way to end a delicious meal.

I returned to Muriel's for lunch on another NOLA trip and tried the wood grilled pork chop. The pork chop was flavorful, tender, and moist. I was not too crazy about the red beans and rice it was served with as I found it a bit bland. The entrée was served in a bowl but should perhaps be served on a plate since it was difficult to slice the pork chop since it kept sinking into the bed of red beans and rice. 

Muriel's is one of the places I would love to return to because of the ambiance and the great food.
Revise this with your best effort:
When dining at Muriel's, don't forget to check if the second level is open for visitors. If it is, take a brief tour of the lounge area upstairs, adorned with red couches and decorative pieces. Don't miss the wrap-around balcony, offering a stunning view of Jackson Square.

For those intrigued by the supernatural, learn about Muriel's haunted tales and discover the story behind the perpetually set table for two near the stairs. It adds a unique element to the dining experience.

Muriel's features two main dining rooms, but personally, I prefer the middle section, an indoor patio dining area that offers a quieter atmosphere. Additionally, there is a bar area located at the back, conveniently close to the restrooms. The indoor patio dining area is particularly enjoyable as it seamlessly combines the outdoors with a serene indoor setting.

During my first visit, I opted for the dinner pre-fixe menu, which proved to be an excellent value at $40. The seafood gumbo soup was hearty and delicious, while the dijon mustard encrusted salmon was perfectly cooked. To end the meal, the bread pudding provided a delightful conclusion.

On another trip to NOLA, I returned to Muriel's for lunch and decided to try the wood-grilled pork chop. The pork chop was packed with flavor, tender, and wonderfully moist. However, I found the accompanying red beans and rice to be a tad bland. It would also be beneficial for the dish to be served on a plate rather than in a bowl, as the pork chop tended to sink into the bed of red beans and rice, making it challenging to slice.

Overall, Muriel's is a place I would love to revisit due to its enchanting ambiance and outstanding cuisine.

input:
I like to make a stop at this Walmart since it's located in Meadowlark where my doctor's office is.  It's smaller than  the supercentre but I find it has a decent selection of items in the food section where the prices are cheaper than the nearby stores.  The produce section can have limited items though with just the basics in stock.  I find the snacks and canned food section are fine with good prices.

As for the rest of the store and items, well it's hit or miss.  I was looking for lightbulbs and they only had one brand of the type I was looking for and it was a energy efficient so pricier than others if they had in stock.  However, the price I paid for the item was probably cheaper than other stores.  

Don't expect much help if you need help finding an item.  Associates seem to be difficult to find unless you count some of the younger staff who like racing shopping carts in the store as they were on my last visit.  

The check outs can have at most 5 cashiers working but I find the time in the line ups is never too long so that's good.
Revise this with your best effort:
I always make it a point to stop by this Walmart conveniently located in Meadowlark, near my doctor's office. While it may be smaller than the supercentre, I appreciate its decent selection of food items that come at more affordable prices compared to nearby stores. However, the produce section can be a bit limited, offering only the basics. Thankfully, the snacks and canned food section make up for it with their good variety and reasonable prices.

Now, when it comes to the rest of the store and its offerings, it's a bit hit or miss. On my search for lightbulbs, I found that they only carried one brand of the specific type I needed, and it happened to be an energy-efficient option, making it pricier compared to other brands. Nonetheless, the overall price was still more budget-friendly than what I've seen elsewhere.

It's important to note that if you require assistance in finding an item, you shouldn't expect much help from the associates. They can be difficult to locate, unless you happen to stumble upon some of the younger staff who seem to be preoccupied with racing shopping carts during my last visit.

On the bright side, they usually have up to five cashiers working at the checkouts, which helps keep the waiting time in line fairly short. That, at least, is something positive to appreciate.
